name: Understanding the Low-Code Development Platform
title: Understanding the Low-Code Development Platform
text:
Understanding the Low-Code Development Platform
 
 
  
  

  
   GDE provides a full-scenario development platform for service developers and a complete asset life cycle tool chain to meet high development requirements and shorten development period, forming a new development mode with service assets as its core and efficient development and reuse.

   
    All-scenario development platform: GDE supports application development and governance, such as simple object orchestration, process orchestration, integration orchestration, data orchestration, RPA orchestration, network operation orchestration, data visualization screen orchestration, mobile app orchestration, trusted development, and asset governance.

    Low learning threshold: The online application development and running platform provides graphical operations and drag-and-drop app design and creation. Common service personnel can start application development after one to two weeks of training.

    Flexible configuration and quick customization: You can modify application elements such as GUIs, service logic, and models as required to shorten the innovation period from idea to production. Developers are free from repetitive works such as adding, deleting, modifying, and querying data in the database. They can focus more on high-level service logics. In addition, the development cycle is not as long as that of the traditional mode.

    Online development and deployment: Online development can be performed in any place and environment. After the development test is complete, the development can be immediately released and take effect as required. Online changes are logged.

    Complete asset life cycle tool chain: provides an asset development, release, and management platform to help business personnel manage and reuse various assets.

   

   You can develop an app in the develop-state environment. Create a project, orchestrate various elements in each type of module, and package and release the project.

   

   
     
    
     
      GDE orchestration help developers create an asset program that can be run on the GDE app execution engine through dragging and dropping orchestration elements and writing basic JavaScript code. Due to its orchestration flexibility, developers can customize code execution, which may cause malicious code execution risks. To securely use the orchestration flexibility, the following requirements must be met:
       
        All developers must strictly follow Knowledge Asset Development Specifications to implement orchestration and development. Any form of malicious code is prohibited, including but not limited to viruses, rogue software, Trojan horses, backdoors, listening programs, and mining programs.

        The system administrator must strictly review the development qualification of developers and assign permissions to developers who have obtained the asset development certification. Assigned permissions cannot be used without control.

       

      The develop-state environment of the low-code platform is used only by developers to develop and debug apps. Sensitive data is not desensitized. Developers are advised not to use real data for debugging in the develop-state environment.

name: Concept Dictionary
title: Concept Dictionary
text:
Concept Dictionary
 
 
  
  

  
   
    
     
      Table 1 Concept dictionary
     
     
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Concept

       
        Description

      

     
     
      
       
        ADC

       
        Application Development Center (ADC) is a low-code and multi-experience development platform.

      

      
       
        GDE

       
        General Digital Engine (GDE) is a digital operation platform. It separates service units with common attributes from front-end applications to form public resources and capabilities that can be shared. It uses the "cloud service + online application development" mode to meet flexible and scalable service requirements of enterprises, decoupling services from platforms and applications from data.

      

      
       
        Tenant

       
        Different tenants can share one environment, in which each tenant is independent and does not affect by others. It is similar to the game Arena of Valor, when you activate account A in a service zone, account A can be used in different service zones. The level and hero of each service are different.

      

      
       
        Develop State

       
        Used to develop apps (including APIs, data orchestration elements, UIs, and processes). The assets developed in the develop-state environment are equivalent to a source program package that does not have running instances. It is also called Studio in develop state (design state).

      

      
       
        Runtime State

       
        The system instantiates and runs the assets developed in the develop-state environment and performs permission control, flow control, and security control during program running.

      

      
       
        Project

       
        In the develop-state environment, you can manage multiple types of assets in a unified manner through projects. A project can contain multiple assets, for example, multiple modules. A project in the develop-state environment corresponds to an app in the runtime-state environment.

      

      
       
        Module

       
        A module is an independent unit in a project. Different modules can be divided based on different orchestration element types.

      

      
       
        Orchestration Element

       
        Elements that are used to form modules, such as models, pages, and services.

      

      
       
        Project Name

       
        Used to isolate project identifiers from orchestration elements. The value can contain 3 to 64 characters, including letters, digits, underscores (_), hyphens (-), and periods (.). It cannot end with [..] and must be globally unique. The project name cannot be changed after submission.

      

      
       
        Module Prefix

       
        Distinguish different modules for easy search. The value can contain lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_). The value is obtained from the Name value by default. A maximum of the first 10 characters can be retained.

      

      
       
        Display Name

       
        The display name is the app name displayed to end users. You can set it to a name that is easy to identify. The value can contain 1 to 100 characters. You can change the value in Settings after submitting the modification.

      

      
       
        One-Click Deployment

       
        Currently, the develop-state environment is separated from the runtime-state environment. After development, a project needs to be packaged and deployed to the runtime-state environment for debugging. The project can be directly packaged as an app and installed in the runtime-state environment. If the configuration in the develop-state environment is updated and needs to be debugged again, you need to deploy it again to debug the updates.

      

      
       
        Hot Deployment

       
        Used to deploy the elements orchestrated in the develop-state environment to the runtime-state environment in real time. The hot deployment function is disabled by default. To use this function, you need to manually enable it. After this function is enabled, you do not need to manually perform one-click deployment when debugging is required.

      

      
       
        Model

       
        Used to store data and provide data APIs. Models are classified into common data models, data source models (used to access external data), and elastic models (used to store and manage a large amount of data).

      

      
       
        Service

       
        Operations on data (also called logic flow).

      

      
       
        Page

       
        Used to design the pages used by users.

      

      
       
        Trigger

       
        Used to configure the triggering action upon data change.

      

      
       
        Data Export

       
        Used to define the capability of exporting data in Excel and CSV formats.

      

      
       
        Data Import

       
        Used to define the capability of importing data in Excel and CSV formats.

      

      
       
        Menu

       
        Pages developed in the develop-state environment can be released as menus for users.

      

      
       
        I18n

       
        Used to configure the multi-language internationalization. The system provides Chinese and English by default.

      

      
       
        Permission

       
        Used to configure permissions for orchestration elements.

      

      
       
        Business Process

       
        Page for managing business processes (also called workflow).

      

      
       
        Inbound REST

       
        Inbound REST API configuration, which is used to configure REST APIs provided for third parties.

      

      
       
        Outbound REST

       
        Outbound REST API configuration, which is used to configure REST APIs for calling third parties.

      

      
       
        Inbound SOAP

       
        Inbound SOAP API configuration, which is used to configure SOAP APIs for third parties.

      

      
       
        Outbound SOAP

       
        Outbound SOAP API configuration, which is used to configure SOAP APIs for calling third parties.

      

      
       
        Asset

       
        Content provided by developers after creation on ADC, such as develop-state projects, runtime-state apps, page templates, and project templates. Such content is accumulated based on developers' wisdom and service experience and has extensive values.

text:
App Development Process
 
 
  
  

  
   The system supports integrated orchestration. That is, in various orchestration scenarios, assets can be orchestrated through the unified entry of project management and follow the unified process covering project management, deployment and debugging, as well as packaging and release.

   This section describes how developers develop assets based on the integrated orchestration capability.

   

   
    
     
      Table 1 Description of the asset development process based on the integrated orchestration capability
     
     
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Development Phase

       
        Description

      

     
     
      
       
        Preparations

       
        Individual developers need to learn about the information in Preparations by Developers.

        Tenant-level or team-level developers also need to learn about the information in Preparations by Tenant Administrators.

      

      
       
        Setting up a project

       
        A project is the basis of integrated orchestration. All development activities start from project creation. For details, see Setting Up a Project.

      

      
       
        Developing a scenario-based app

       
        The orchestration elements to be created during app development vary according to application scenarios. Developers can determine the orchestration elements to be used based on the actual service scenario and refer to the corresponding sections:

        
         Orchestration of Simple Object Management Apps

         Network Operation Automation

         Configuring a Process

         RPA Orchestration

         API Orchestration

         GDELink Mobile App Orchestration

         Data Visualization Screen Orchestration

        

      

      
       
        Deploying and debugging the app

       
        After developing orchestration elements in the develop-state environment, you need to deploy the app in the runtime-state environment and then debug it. For details, see Debugging During App Development.

      

      
       
        Verifying and releasing the app

       
        You can release and put away the app through a pipeline. For details, see Release and Verification.

name: Understanding Developer Roles
title: Understanding Developer Roles
text:
Understanding Developer Roles
 
 
  
  

  
   A role is a group of users with the same responsibilities. Users complete their specified work based on their roles.

   Table 1 lists the default roles provided in the develop-state system. The roles and their responsibilities specified in this document are for reference only.

   The system administrator and developer permissions must be separated for users. You are advised not to assign the administrator and developer roles to the same user.

   The tenant administrator, as an administrator, should not participate in application development. If high-risk operations arise from improper application development by the administrator, the administrator shall bear full responsibility for such operations.

   
    
    
     
      Table 1 Default roles in the develop-state system
     
     
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Role

       
        Description

       
        Default Operation Permission

      

     
     
      
       
        StudioFaaSTenantAdmin

       
        Tenant dependency package administrator in the develop state. Users with this role can query and edit tenant-level dependency packages.

       
        This role has permissions on Tenant Function Dependency Managing and Tenant Function Dependency Query menus.

      

      
       
        StudioDeveloper

       
        Developers. They have the permissions to develop and customize apps and integrate the apps to the system in the develop state. They can only maintain and manage assets such as apps developed only by themselves.

       
        This role has permissions on the following pages:

        
         Menu permissions (runtime state):
          
           Model Management: Model Property Manage, Shard Policy, Data Load Log, Data Dump Log, and Cache Configuration

           Integration Service: FTP Management, Inbound REST Management, Inbound SOAP Management, Inbound Strategy Management, Certificate Management, Outbound REST Management, Outbound SOAP Management, Outbound Strategy Management, and WSSE Signature Management

           Log Management: FaaS Task Run Log (Log query)

           Integration Log: REST Receive Log, REST Send Log, SOAP Receive Log, and SOAP Send Log

           Development State Studio

          

         Shortcut permissions (Portal configuration):
          
           App Shortcuts: Development State Studio

           App Shortcut Category: Common Management

          

         API permissions (develop state):
          
           Asset Management: Category Management, Modify Asset, Import Asset, Delete Asset, and View Asset

           Common operation rights: get user information

           Studio Develop > Common: Develop-State Asset Initialization Logs, Developer Certificate, Menu Unify Func, and Query User info

           Studio Develop > Release Asset: Save asset registration configuration and Viewing asset registration configurations

           Studio Develop > Project Management: Query Remote Deploy Environment, Query Business Field, Create Business Field, Update Business Field, Delete Business Field, Hot Deploy Configuration, Modify personal project members, List Project, Delete Project, Export Project, Import Project, Modify Project, and Create Project

           Studio Develop > Asset Developing: Intg Developing, Workflow Development, Model Develop, Mobile Page Develop, Menu Develop, I18n Develop, Card Develop, Page Develop, Document, PermissionResource, TimerTask, ErrorCode, RolePermission, Permission, Quality evaluation, Custom asset (Import custom asset, Delete custom asset, Query custom asset, update custom asset, Create custom asset, and Export custom asset), Data Import, Data Export, Service Developing, and Network Operation (Command Management, Route Management, Resource Management, Resource Type Management, General Setting, and Script Management)

           Studio Mateline Editor

           Studio UI Editor

           Studio Mateline Editor

           Model Foundry Template Orchestration

          

        

      

      
       
        StudioFaasDeveloper

       
        Preset role of the FaaS service. Users with this role can query and edit project-level dependency packages.

       
        This role has permissions on Tenant Function Dependency Managing and Tenant Function Dependency Query, and Function Developing menus.

      

      
       
        AssetDeveloper

       
        Asset developer, a preset role of the asset services. This role is responsible for asset management operations.

       
        This role can be used only when the StudioDeveloper role is assigned first.

        This role has the following operation permissions:

        
         Menus and operations under Asset Management in the develop-state environment:
          
           Asset Vulnerabilities

           Asset viewing

           Asset deletion

           Asset import

           Asset modification

           Service type management

           Asset deployment

           Deployment environment viewing

           Asset Library

           Asset Approval (only for viewing and no approval-related operation permission)

           Asset Production Environment (only for viewing and using, and no permission to add, delete, or modify the asset production environment)

          

         Operations under API Catalog in the runtime-state environment:
          
           API deletion

           API import

           API modification

           API viewing

          

        

      

      
       
        AssetOperationsAdmin

       
        Asset operations administrator, a preset role of the asset service. Users with this role can approve the asset putaway and remove assets.

       
        This role has permissions to approve and reject asset putaway and remove assets.

      

      
       
        AssetMaintenanceAdmin

       
        Asset O&M administrator, a preset role of the asset service. Users with this role can approve the asset putaway and configure the asset production environment.

       
        This role has permissions to approve and reject asset putaway and add, modify, and delete the asset production environment.

      

      
       
        StudioAssetAnalyst

       
        Develop-state asset analyst, a preset role of the asset service. Users with this role can analyze tenant-level asset dependency and provide analysis suggestions for asset rectification, consolidation, and sunsetting.

        This role must be used together with the StudioDeveloper role. That is, users must be bound to both the StudioDeveloper and StudioAssetAnalyst roles to have the asset dependency analysis permissions. The StudioAssetAnalyst role alone is not enough.

       
        This role has the permission to access the Asset Management > Asset Dependency Analysis menu in the develop state. Users with this role can view the element distribution, element dependency chain, inter-project dependency, and inter-project element dependency of all assets of a tenant.

      

     
    
   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Preparations by Tenant Administrators

name: Understanding the Capabilities of Rights- and Domain-based Management
title: Understanding the Capabilities of Rights- and Domain-based Management
text:
Understanding the Capabilities of Rights- and Domain-based Management
 
 
  
  

  
   ADC supports rights- and domain-based management. Projects are managed by their open levels such as personal, team, and whether the project is public, implementing hierarchical permission control.

   
    Personal: Only the project creator and specified users have the permission to view the project. Other users under the tenant cannot view the project. You can manage members of a personal project and add other members to edit and develop the project.

    Team: Only members in a specified team can access the project. Non-team members do not have the permission to view the project.

    Public: The project can be accessed by all users under a tenant.

   

   
    
     
      Table 1 Rights- and domain-based management description
     
     
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Project Open Level

       
        Permission Description

       
        Member Permission

      

     
     
      
       
        Personal

       
        Only the project creator and specified members can access the project.

        Other personnel of the tenant do not have the permission to view the project.

       
        Member roles of a personal project:

        
         Project Developer: performs orchestration and development only in the project.
          
            NOTE: 
           
            This role provides all capabilities in an AI orchestration project, except Review Labeling Task, View Labeling Task, and Create Labeling Task in the dataset.

           

          

         Project Maintainer: modifies a project and adds, deletes, and changes the personnel who can access the project.
          
            NOTE: 
           
            This role provides all capabilities in an AI orchestration project.

           

          

        

      

      
       
        Team

       
        Only members in a specified team can access the project.

        Non-team members do not have the permission to view the project.

       
        Team member roles:

        
         Team administrator: adds maintenance team members and orchestrates projects in the team.

         Team developer: orchestrates team projects. The role cannot add maintenance team members.

        

      

      
       
        Public

       
        All users in the tenant can use the project.

       
        Member management is not required.

      

     
    
   

   
     
    
     The Develop Asset Management permission is preset in the system. In addition to other necessary orchestration permissions, this permission allows users to perform operations such as project, team, and member management on personal- and team-level projects. That is, the Develop Asset Management permission is beyond the rights- and domain-based management permission.

     
      By default, only the administrator has the Develop Asset Management permission. If the administrator assigns this permission to another role, users of this role share this permission. Therefore, exercise caution when performing this operation.
      
       Figure 1 Asset development and management permissions
       
      

     

    

   

   
    After a project is created, only the following users can modify the project sharing scope and asset sharing scope:
    
     Users who have the Develop Asset Management permission

     Personal project creator

     Personal project manager

     Team creator of a team project

     Team manager of a team project

     Creator of a public project

    

   

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Preparations by Tenant Administrators

text:
Configuring the Tenant-Level Studio Page
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    There are many page elements on the Studio page, such as the logo, menu, navigation, and help menu. These elements can be displayed or not displayed based on user preferences.

    The following table lists the supported configuration methods for Studio elements.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Studio configuration
      
      
       
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Configuration Level

        
         Operator

        
         Configuration Method

        
         Validation Range

       

      
      
       
        
         Tenant

        
         Tenant administrator

        
         Menu configuration

        
         The configuration takes effect within a tenant and takes effect only in projects created using a blank template.

       

       
        
         Template

        
         Template developer

        
         Offline editing of the template definition file

        
         The configuration takes effect only in projects created using this template.

         The priority of the template level is higher than that of the tenant level. That is, during project creation, when the display elements defined in the template are different from those configured using the tenant level configuration method, the project template definition is used.

       

      
     
    

    The following describes how to configure the tenant-level Studio.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the develop-state environment as the tenant administrator of the data zone (that is, the admin user).

     Choose General Settings > Designer Page Configuration.

name: Team Management
title: Team Management
text:
Team Management
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    During team development, administrators can manage teams, such as creating teams and managing team members.

    You can create sub-teams under a team.

    
     Three sub-teams can be created.

     Upper-level team users can manage lower-level teams.

     Upper-level team users can view projects of lower-level teams.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the develop-state environment as the tenant administrator of the data zone (that is, the admin user).

     Choose Team Management on the top menu bar.
      

      
        
       
        
         If a common developer does not have the develop-state administrator permission, the developer does not have the team creation permission. In this case, contact the develop-state administrator.

         On this page, the common developer can view information about the team that the developer belongs to.

        

       

      

      

     Create a team.
      

      
       Click Create. In the displayed dialog box, set related parameters and create a team.
        
         Figure 1 Creating a team
         
        

       Click OK.

      

      

     (Optional) Create a sub-team.
      

      
       In the Operation column of the added team, choose More > Create Sub-team.

       In the displayed dialog box, set the sub-team information.
        
         Figure 2 Creating a sub-team
         
        

       Click OK.

      

      

     Add a team member.
      

      
       In the Operation column of the added team, click Member Management.

       In the displayed dialog box, click Add Member.

       In the displayed dialog box, select a member from the drop-down list.
        If there are a large number of members, it is inconvenient to find them in the drop-down list. You can click  under Team Member. In the displayed dialog box, select the member to be added to the team and click OK.

       Modify permissions for the team member and click OK.
        
         Figure 3 Adding a team member
         
        

        

        Role description:

        
         Team administrator: adds maintenance team members and orchestrates projects in the team.

         Team developer: orchestrates team projects. The role cannot add maintenance team members.

        

       Close the Member Management window.

      

      

     After a team member creates a team project, click the team name to view the created projects.

    

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Preparations by Tenant Administrators

text:
Preparing for App Development
 
 
  
  

  
   Online orchestration is used for GDE asset development. You need to prepare the local environment and online environment.

   
    Context

    GDE consists of the develop-state environment and the runtime-state environment. You can easily switch between them.

    The runtime state is accessed through the unified portal, for example, https://IP address:Port number/portal-web/portal/homepage.html.

    In the runtime-state environment, you can choose Development State Studio from the navigation pane to go to the develop-state environment.

   

   
    Preparing the Local Environment

    To provide better development experience, developers need to prepare a client PC that meets the requirements in the following table.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Client PC requirements
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Constraint Item

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Browser

        
         
          Google Chrome 97 to 130

          Mozilla Firefox 88 to 132

          Microsoft Edge 90 to 130

         

       

       
        
         Resolution

        
         Minimum: 1280 x 1024

         Recommended: 1920 x 1080 or higher resolution; 100% zoom ratio

       

       
        
         Processor

        
         Minimum: single-core 1 GHz

         Recommended: dual-core 2 GHz or higher-level processor

       

       
        
         RAM

        
         Minimum: 2 GB (1 GB free memory)

         Recommended: 8 GB or larger (2 GB or larger free memory)

       

       
        
         Network bandwidth (uplink/downlink rate)

        
         Minimum: 2 Mbit/s/5 Mbit/s

         Recommended: higher than 5 Mbit/s/20 Mbit/s

       

       
        
         Network delay

        
         Maximum: 200 ms

         Recommended: 10 ms or lower

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Preparing the Online Environment

    Developers need to obtain available accounts and passwords from environment installation personnel or administrators and ensure that the obtained accounts have developer permissions.

   

   
    Introduction to the Online Environment

    The online environment provides common shortcut links and various help information.

    
     : Click this icon on the toolbar in the upper right corner to go to the runtime state. The URL in the runtime state supports parameter configuration.

     Recently Viewed Projects: provides the list of recently viewed projects based on the browsing history of the current login user so that developers can quickly access their projects.

     Quick Start in the upper right corner on the home page: provides guidance for beginners to complete the development of a minimum case and help beginners understand the development process.

     Help Center in the upper right corner of the home page: provides guidance documents for asset development.

    

   

   
    Training and Documentation

    Log in to and register with GDE CLOUD. Choose Cloud Academy to enter the developer academy and learn various courses.

    View the guide documents from the Support website.

name: Development Disclaimer Signing
title: Development Disclaimer Signing
text:
Development Disclaimer Signing
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    Before developing an application, you must understand the responsibilities of a developer and sign the development disclaimer.

    The system provides multiple entries for signing the development disclaimer. If a developer does not sign it, the signing page is displayed when the developer performs operations such as project creation.

    Read the development disclaimer carefully and sign it after confirming it. If the developer does not sign the development disclaimer, the developer cannot develop applications.

    The system prompts you to sign the development disclaimer in the following scenarios:

    
     In the runtime-state environment, choose Development State Studio to go to the orchestration home page.

     Manage developer certificates.

     Access the orchestration-related menus, such as Project Management and Team Management.

     Access the menus related to general configuration, such as General Settings > Environment Management, General Settings > Service Domain Management, and General Settings > Quality Evaluation Rule Management.

    

    The following uses the entry for developers to managing certificates as an example to describe how to sign the development disclaimer.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to ADC in develop state as a developer.

name: User Requirements
title: User Requirements
text:
User Requirements
 
 
  
  

  
   Before developing an app, you need to specify the requirements, that is, the type of the app to be developed and the necessary functions.

   
    App Description

    An offering management app is developed to manage offering information.

   

   
    Basic Functions

    
     
      An offering consists of name, price, image, category, and description. The category can be managed separately.

     
      The offering list can be filtered by category and sorted by price.

     
      Offering change information, including the operator and change time, can be recorded during offering operations.

     
      Offering information can be imported from and exported to an Excel file (excluding images).

    

   

   
    Security Requirements

    
     
      Common employees can only add, delete, modify, and query offering information.

     
      Managers can add, delete, modify, query, import, and export offering information and offering category information.

     
      Necessary parameter verification is required before an offering is saved.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Developing an Offering Management App

title: App Requirement Analysis
text:
App Requirement Analysis
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to analyze app requirements.

   
    
     
      Table 1 Requirement analysis
     
     
      
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Category

       
        Item

       
        Implementation Analysis

       
        Orchestration Elements

      

     
     
      
       
        App description

       
        An offering management app is developed to manage offering information.

       
        As a typical information development app, the offering management app can be implemented through the general job orchestration capability of ADC.

        ADC app orchestration is implemented through the Integrated Orchestration module in the develop-state environment. All orchestration resources need to be managed using specific projects and modules. Therefore, you need to create a project and module first.

       
        
         Project

        

      

      
       
        Basic functions

       
        An offering consists of name, price, image, category, and description. The category can be managed separately.

       
        To manage offerings, you need to create data models and tables for offering information. The following tables are involved:

        
         Category information table:
          
           Category ID: unique ID for each offering category.

           Category name: name corresponding to the category ID. For example, DRINK indicates drinks, and FOOD indicates food. The value can be of the text type.

          

        

        
         Offering information table:
          
           ID: offering ID, which is used to uniquely identify and query an offering.

           Name: offering name, which is usually a character string, that is, of the text type.

           Price: offering price. The value can be of the float type, because the value may contain decimal points.

           Image: offering image, which can be managed through file attachments. The value is of the file type.

           Category: Offering categories, for example, food and drinks, can be managed separately. The category information needs to be selected during offering management. Therefore, you need to set the value type of Category to Reference to reference the category information table.

           Description: offering description, which is usually of the text or long text type.

          

        

       
        
         Model

        

      

      
       
        The offering list can be filtered by category and sorted by price.

       
        During offering list query, offerings can be filtered by category and sorted by price.

        In ADC, the offering list query function needs to be implemented through services. Services can be automatically generated through models or modified based on the GetList services. Offerings can be filtered by category and sorted by price.

       
        
         Service

         Page

        

      

      
       
        Offering operation information, including the operator, operation time, change type, and offering name, is recorded.

       
        When creating a model, you can select the preset operator and time.

        Offering addition, deletion, and modification are implemented through services. In services, operation logs can be recorded.

       
        
         Service

        

      

      
       
        Offering information can be imported from and exported to an Excel file (excluding images).

       
        The system supports the import and export of Excel files. When services and pages are automatically generated based on models, the corresponding data import and export capabilities are also automatically generated. You can directly use the default capabilities.

       
        
         Data Import

         Data Export

        

      

      
       
        Security requirements

       
        Managers and common employees can query, create, and delete offerings.

       
        The system supports permission control on app resources such as pages, services, and URLs.

       
        
         Menu

         Permission

        

      

      
       
        Only managers can manage offering category information.

        Only managers can import and export offering information and offering category information.

       
        You can configure the offering management manager role and assign permission items to the role.

       
        
         Permission

         Role

        

      

      
       
        Necessary parameter verification is required before an offering is saved.

       
        In the services used for adding, deleting, and modifying offering information, the parameter validation function needs to be added, which can be implemented through a validator.

       
        
         Service (Service > Validator)

title: Creating an Offering Management Project
text:
Creating an Offering Management Project
 
 
  
  

  
   The orchestration and development of app capabilities must be performed in a project. Therefore, you need to create a project first.

   
    Prerequisites

    Preparations, such as a developer account, have been completed. For details, see Preparations by Developers.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as a user with the StudioDevelper role.

     Choose Products and Services > Development State Studio.

     On the Project Management page, click Create Project.
      

      
        
       
        If you have not signed the developer statement, the system displays a signing page for you. You need to read the statement carefully and sign it after understanding and acknowledging the statement content.

        After the statement is signed, go to the next step.

       

      

      

     The system displays preset templates for project creation. Move the pointer to the required template and click Use.
      

      For simple object management app orchestration, click ADC Common Template. For details about templates and scenarios, see Introducing a Project Template.

      

      

      

     Configure the project parameters, and click Create.
      

      

      

      For details about the parameters, see Table 1.

      
       
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Recommended Parameter Configuration

         

        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Project name that is easy to understand

         

         
          
           Display Name

          
           
              The display name is the app name displayed to end users. You can set it to a name that is easy to identify. The value can contain 1 to 100 characters. You can change the value on the settings page after the creation. In GDE Store, the display name is used to submit the app for release.
             

           For example, set this parameter to Offering Management.

         

         
          
           Tag

          
           Project label, which can be used to query projects by project label

         

         
          
           Service Domain

          
           Service domain to which a project belongs. For details about the application scenarios and creation operations of service domains, see Configuring a Service Domain.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Description of a project. Set this parameter as required.

         

         
          
           Enable Hot Deploy

          
           You are advised to enable this function.

           Hot deployment is to incrementally deploy elements orchestrated in the develop-state environment to the runtime-state environment in real time. Developers do not need to manually perform one-click deployment, which facilitates quick debugging.

           After this function is enabled, a project is deployed at the beginning of the project creation. When you add, delete, or modify orchestration elements in the project, the elements are also deployed.

           This switch is not displayed if the selected template does not support hot deployment.

         

         
          
           Create Module

          
           You are advised to enable this function.

           You need to create modules and then orchestration elements in a project. After this function is enabled, a module with the same name as the project is created by default. Therefore, you do not need to create a module again.

           To customize the name of the module to be created, click Advanced.

           This switch is not displayed if the selected template does not support multiple modules.

text:
Configuring the Page Layout and Uploading Images (Page Components)
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to orchestrate the page based on the page design.

   
    Scenario Description

    According to the description in Configuring Data Models (Offering Category Table and Information Table), the info_goods_create, info_goods_grid, and info_goods_update pages are automatically generated.

    The info_goods_create page is adjusted. After you click info_goods_create and access the page designer, the automatically generated page is shown in the following figure.

    

    

    The automatically generated pages do not fully meet service requirements and need to be adjusted as follows:

    
     The goods_id field is automatically generated and its value does not need to be entered. This field can be deleted from the input parameter. That is, this field is not displayed and its value does not need to be transferred.

     The format and size of the file to be uploaded must be set for goods_picture. In addition, this field is displayed as Offering Image.

     The field sequence is adjusted. The goods_type and goods_name fields are placed in the first row, and the goods_description field is moved to the last row.

     goods_price is displayed as Offering Price. goods_name is displayed as Offering Name. goods_description is displayed as Offering Introduction. goods_type is displayed as Offering Category.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Select the created project and module.

     In the navigation pane, choose Page.

     Click the info_goods_create page.

     In the canvas, select goods_id and delete the goods_id field.
      

      In the Form Panel area, components under the same Layout Col are displayed in the same row in the canvas. Each component is placed in an independent layout column. You can delete the sequence component and the corresponding layout columns used by goods_id.

      

      

     Set the types of files that can be uploaded for the goods_picture field using the File Input component.

text:
Configuring the Category-based Filtering Function (Services and Pages)
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to develop the category-based filtering function based on the solution design.

   
    Scenario Description

    The xxx_get_list service automatically generated based on the model is used to query the result list. By default, data can be filtered only by primary key. To add the category-based (such as goods_type) filtering function, you need to adjust the service.

    In addition, the automatically generated xxx_grid page supports query only by primary key by default. You need to add a page component for category-based query.

   

   
    Procedure (Configuring the Category-based Filtering Function for Services)

    
     Open a created project and module.

     In the navigation pane, choose Service.

     Go to the info_goods_get_list service.

     Adjust the input parameters. Input parameter configuration is the service-level configuration, which is not for performed on the get_list node. You can click the blank area to expand the right pane and configure the parameters.
      

      By default, goods_type is of the string type. To query one or more types at a time, the types of input parameters for goods_type are changed to list.

      

      

     Configure the category-based filtering function.
      

      
       Edit information about the get_list node.
        

       Set the search criteria. Add the goods_type filter criterion to the existing search criteria. Save the configuration.
        

        

        
          
         
          When adding a query criterion based on existing criteria, you need to select a query relationship, for example, and, and then click Add to add the configured criterion to the text box.

          If a variable starts with $!, the expression that contains the variable is invalid when the variable is empty (the logical expression with the smallest logic unit and the variable contained is deleted from the TQL statement), that is, the variable can be empty.

          The query can be performed based on the value of goods_id or goods_type. Multiple values of goods_type can be transferred and values of goods_id and goods_type are allowed not to be transferred. If values of them are not transferred, all data is queried.

         

        

        

      

      

     Save the service.

    

   

   
    Procedure (Configuring the Category-based Filtering Function for the info_goods_grid Page)

    The Select component obtains offering category information from info_category and uses the information as options in the drop-down list. Multiple options can be selected.

    Data in the info_category model is used as the value of goods_type to filter offerings by category.

    
     In the created module, choose Page on the left.

     Click info_goods_grid and access the page designer.

     On the toolbar, add the Select component.
      

      

      

      

     In the property area on the right, configure properties of the Select component.
      

      

      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Key parameters
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           The name must be the same as the service parameter in the query table.

           In this scenario, the offering category needs to be used as the value of the goods_type field for service query. Therefore, set this parameter to goods_type.

         

         
          
           Label

          
           Display name

         

         
          
           Interface Name/Model Name

          
           Selector data, which can be obtained from services or models. The model name info_category is configured, indicating that the options in the drop-down list come from the offering category table.

           
             NOTE: 
            
             Alternatively, you can set the Service field to the info_category_get_list service of the info_category model to achieve the same effect.

             

            

           

         

         
          
           Value Field

          
           Parameter whose value is transferred after this option is selected from the drop-down list. For example, the value of type_id is transferred here.

         

         
          
           Display Field

          
           Field displayed after this option is selected from the drop-down list. For example, type_name is displayed here.

         

         
          
           Multiple

          
           Multiple options can be selected for the selector. For example, select FOOD and DRINKS at the same time.

text:
Configuring the Input Parameter Verification Function
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes the input parameter verification function based on security requirements.

   
    Scenario Description

    Input parameter verification can be classified into front-end page verification and back-end service verification.

    
     With the front-end page verification function, the system can quickly respond to information that does not meet verification rules and report errors.

     The service verification is needed when an interface is provided for an external system.

    

   

   
    Service Input Parameter Verification

    Assume that the price of an offering to be created needs to be verified. For example, all offerings in the inventory are cheap offerings. To avoid errors, you need to set the price to a value less than or equal to 999999.

    
     Open a created project and module.

     In the navigation pane, choose Service.

     Click the info_goods_create service.

     Click the blank area in the canvas.

     Click  on the right and configure a validator for the goods_price field in the Input Parameter Configuration area.
      

      The goods_price property is of the decimal type, so the automatically generated service contains a common validator by default. You need to modify the validator by adding the validation function on the minimum and maximum values.

      

      

      

     Set the validator type.
      

      

      

      

     Click OK and save the service. Then, you can debug the effect through one-click deployment.

    

   

   
    Front-end Web Page Input Verification

    
     Select the created project and module.

     In the navigation pane, choose Page.

     Click the info_goods_create page.

     Set the verification rules for the goods_price field.
      

      

      

      

     Save the page.

name: Configuring Offering Management Permissions
title: Configuring Offering Management Permissions
text:
Configuring Offering Management Permissions
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to configure different roles and permissions based on the solution design.

   
    Scenario Description

    ADC supports multi-layer permission management. You can configure permission items for different orchestration elements, assign permission items to specified roles, and associate roles with users during user creation to implement permission control.

    
     
     
      
       Table 1 Permission configuration analysis
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Orchestration Element Type

        
         Permission Control Mode

       

      
      
       
        
         Model

        
         When Data can be accessed by the frontend is enabled for a model, data permission access control policies need to be configured.

       

       
        
         Service

        
         By default, Authentication Type of the service is Login only, that is, the permission is not controlled. To control the permission, you need to set Authentication Type to Login and authorization, and select the desired permission item. Only the user who has this permission item can access the service.

       

       
        
         Page component

        
         To control the permission of the components on the page, such as the redirection button and window button, you need to obtain and configure the permission URI.

       

       
        
         Menu

        
         A permission item is automatically generated for each menu. The permission item needs to be assigned to a role.

       

       
        
         Import and export services

        
         For data import and export services, configured permission items need to be associated. Otherwise, permission control policies do not take effect.

       

      
     
    

    You need to plan permission items based on permission control requirements.

    
     
      
       Table 2 Permission item planning
      
      
       
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Permission Item Name

        
         Configuration

        
         Description

        
         Role to Which the Permission Is Assigned

       

      
      
       
        
         menu_goods_info

        
         After a menu is created, a permission item with the same name as the menu is automatically generated.

        
         The permission item has been automatically bound to the corresponding menu. After the permission item is assigned to a role, the menu is displayed to the role.

        
         
          staff

          manager

         

       

       
        
         menu_category

        
         After a menu is created, a permission item with the same name as the menu is automatically generated.

        
         The permission item has been automatically bound to the corresponding menu. After the permission item is assigned to a role, the menu is displayed to the role.

        
         manager

       

       
        
         manageCategory

        
         Create a permission item to manage and control the service permission for creating offering categories.

        
         The permission item needs to be bound to the following services of the offering category model:

         
          info_category_update

          info_category_get_list

          info_category_get

          info_category_create

          info_category_batch_update

          info_category_batch_delete

         

        
         manager

       

       
        
         manageGoodsinfo

        
         Create a permission item to manage and control the service permission for querying offering information.

        
         The permission item needs to be bound to the following services of the offering information model:

         
          info_goods_update

          info_goods_get_list

          info_goods_get

          info_goods_create

          info_goods_batch_update

          info_goods_batch_delete

         

        
         
          staff

          manager

         

       

       
        
         importGoods

        
         Create a permission item to manage and control the permission for importing offering information.

        
         The permission item needs to be bound to the data import service info_goods_import for importing offering information.

         In addition, the permission item needs to be bound to the import button on the info_goods_grid page to ensure that the frontend and backend permissions are the same.

        
         manager

       

       
        
         exportGoods

        
         Create a permission item to manage and control the permission for exporting offering information.

        
         The permission needs to be bound to the data export service info_goods_export for exporting offering information.

         In addition, the permission item needs to be bound to the export button on the info_goods_grid page to ensure that the frontend and backend permissions are the same.

        
         manager

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Open a created project and module.

     Configure permission items by referring to Table 1.
      

      
       In the navigation pane, choose Permission.

       Click Add Permission and configure the permission item manageCategory.
        

        

       Click Create.

       Create the manageGoodsinfo, importGoods, and exportGoods permission items in sequence.

      

      

     Configure model permissions.
      

      
       In the navigation pane, choose Model.

       Click Edit in the Operation column of the info_category model to edit the model information. In this model, Data can be accessed by the frontend is enabled to allow data filtering based on offering category during offering information management. Therefore, the offering category model data needs to be accessed.
        

        

        
          
         
          The offering management page references the offering category information model. Therefore, you only need to associate the permission item menu_goods_info of the offering management menu with the data access permission of the info_category model.

         

        

       Click OK.

      

      

     Configure service permissions.
      

      
       In the navigation pane, choose Service.

       Click info_category_create.

       Click the blank area and configure permission items in the property configuration area on the right.
        

        

       Click  to save the settings.

       Repeat the preceding steps to configure permission items of other services.

      

      

     Configure the permissions of the import and export services.
      

      
       In the navigation pane, choose Data Import.

       Select the automatically generated data import service info_goods_import.

       Set Permission Item.
        

        

      

      

     Configure page permissions.
      

      
       In the navigation pane, choose Page.

       Click the info_goods_grid page.

       Set the permission item of the Import button.
        

        

       Click  to save the page.

      

      

     Preset roles staff and manager.
      

      Configure the permissions on the Goods Information Management and Goods Category Management menus, the permissions to add, delete, and query offerings, and the permission to manage offering categories for users with the manager role.

      
       Configure the offering query permission on the Goods Information Management menu for users with the staff role.
       
        In the navigation pane, choose Permission.

        Click the Role Set tab.

        Click Add role, select permissions, and click .

      After the check is complete, if there are element items that do not comply with the rules, you can click the value in the Rule Name column in the list to learn about the rules.

      

     Modify the quality result based on the check result. The following figure shows an example.

name: General Principles
title: General Principles
text:
General Principles
 
 
  
  

  
   General Digital Engine (GDE) provides a secure, reliable, and scalable cloud computing platform and various tools. It regards the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of customer services and data as its first priority for security.

   Currently, GDE is built on Huawei HEC to provide services for tenants. Therefore, HEC, GDE, and tenants jointly build a security framework for cloud infrastructure, platform services, and data. Different from local data centers, when tenants transfer data to the cloud, HEC, GDE, and tenants share the security responsibilities. HEC ensures the security of the underlying infrastructure and basic platform. GDE ensures the security of the public service platform and the services and applications on the platform. Tenants ensure the security of their own accounts, data, and assets after secondary development. This mechanism is called the "Shared Security Responsibility Model".

   
    Figure 1 Shared security responsibility model
    
   

   

   In most cases, GDE and HEC have provided necessary security assurance measures. Tenants do not need to pay more attention to cloud configuration and service security. This reduces operation pressure and enables tenants to focus on their own service operation.

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Shared Security Responsibility Model (OC)

name: HEC's Security Responsibilities
title: HEC's Security Responsibilities
text:
HEC's Security Responsibilities
 
 
  
  

  
   All HEC services run on its global infrastructure, and HEC protects this infrastructure. The infrastructure includes physical data centers, hardware, software, networks, and auxiliary equipment. Protecting the infrastructure is the top priority of HEC. HEC establishes a global infrastructure security protection system in areas such as security organization and personnel, physical and environmental security, business continuity, and security compliance. Based on this infrastructure, HEC uses virtualization technologies to provide basic services for upper-layer services, including network services, computing services, and storage services. HEC is responsible for the security of these basic services. In addition, HEC provides tools and methods to ensure that data and applications on GDE are securely deployed on HEC. HEC isolates customers.

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Security Responsibilities

name: GDE's Security Responsibilities
title: GDE's Security Responsibilities
text:
GDE's Security Responsibilities
 
 
  
  

  
   GDE securely operates the infrastructure provided by HEC. GDE is responsible for the security configuration, security policies, security event handling, and security hardening of the infrastructure.

   GDE is responsible for the security of platforms and services built on the HEC infrastructure. In addition, for HEC products (such as ECS, VPC, and OBS) used by GDE, their security configurations and tasks must be assured by GDE. GDE manages guest OSs (including upgrades and security patches), application software or programs installed on instances, and firewall (security group) configurations provided by HEC on each instance.

   For web applications provided by GDE, their security must be assured by GDE. For web applications developed by tenants using existing resources or microservices, their security must be assured by tenants. GDE provides the security review mechanism and capability.

   For data protection, the tenant is the data controller, and GDE is the data processor. GDE is responsible for security control and protection of data on GDE. In addition, GDE isolates data between tenants.

   GDE provides security capabilities such as account permission minimization and data isolation, provides security regulation enablement, and implements security audit to ensure the security of accounts and permissions. The tenant must ensure the security of their own accounts and data.

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Security Responsibilities

name: Tenant's Security Responsibilities
title: Tenant's Security Responsibilities
text:
Tenant's Security Responsibilities
 
 
  
  

  
   Although the security responsibilities of HEC and GDE cover the overall security framework and GDE has developed some security standards for tenants' reference, tenants (as end users of GDE) still have their own security responsibilities.

   Tenants are responsible for routine security configurations and manage GDE tenant configurations, accounts, permissions, passwords, and activity log recordings, identify sensitive data during these activities, and ensure data security, especially the security of exported data.

   The tenant monitors the security compliance of sensitive data, and GDE provides technical support.

   On GDE, encapsulated module functions are called microservice. Tenants can call microservice in the develop state to perform secondary development. GDE is responsible for microservice security. However, the tenant is responsible for the security of secondary development products and related security configurations of the products in the ecosystem.

   For more security measures, see GDE Security White Paper.

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Security Responsibilities

name: Scenario Examples
title: Scenario Examples
text:
Scenario Examples
 
 
  
  

  
   This topic describes the security responsibilities between GDE and tenants in some typical scenarios. GDE is not responsible for all the example scenarios that are not described. However, you can deduce the responsibility boundary based on typical scenarios. For some controversial scenarios, contact the GDE security SE.

   The selected scenario examples are easy to understand, but it does not mean that GDE or tenants have these problems.

   

  

  
   
    Tenant-Level Security Configuration

name: Tenant-Level Security Configuration
title: Tenant-Level Security Configuration
text:
Tenant-Level Security Configuration
 
 
  
  

  
   
    GDE allows the tenant administrator to manage tenant-level accounts based on the actual status of users in the organization to which the tenant belongs.

   

   Scenario 1: An employee in the organization to which the tenant belongs is transferred, but the permission is not cleared. The employee logs in to GDE to download sensitive data one day after the transfer, leading to data leakage.

   The tenant takes the responsibility. GDE has provided the account and permission control capability. The tenant administrator should revoke the permissions of the employee immediately after the employee leaves the current position (including but not limited to freezing the account, canceling the access permission, and deleting the account).

   Scenario 2: The tenant administrator deletes the account of a resigned employee. One month later, a new employee (with the same name but not the same person) comes. After the administrator creates an account for the employee, the account inherits the permissions of the previous employee.

   GDE takes the full responsibility for data leakage caused by account permission inheritance.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Scenario Examples

name: Tenant Asset Security Development
title: Tenant Asset Security Development
text:
Tenant Asset Security Development
 
 
  
  

  
   1. Tenant developers are responsible for the asset service security governance, and risk and compliance analysis.

   Scenario 1: A tenant developer plans to roll out the newly developed asset at the EU site, but does not perform privacy impact assessment (PIA) properly or use the GDE encryption and anonymization capabilities, leading to privacy violations.

   The tenant developer takes the responsibility to analyze the security of the surrounding environment related to the service and use GDE platform capabilities to follow the compliance requirements.

   

   2. GDE formulates asset development specifications. Tenant developers must develop assets based on the specifications.

   Scenario 1: According to the asset development specifications, the verification of service input parameters is not required. The tenant developer does not verify input parameters during development. The security test team finds that the assets developed by the tenant have XSS injection issues.

   GDE takes the responsibility for not verifying input parameters, which is not required in the specifications.

   Scenario 2: The asset development specifications clearly require verification of service input parameters. However, the tenant developer does not verify them during development. The security test team finds that the assets developed by the tenant have XSS injection issues.

   In this case, the tenant takes the responsibility for not meeting the development compliance requirements specified on GDE.

   

   3. Based on the asset development specifications, GDE develops quality evaluation tools and asset test tools to help developers detect security issues.

   Scenario 1: The asset development specifications clearly require that service input parameters be verified and GDE provides a quality evaluation tool for scanning. The tenant developer does not verify the input parameters during development, and the scanning tool does not detect any issue. The security test team finds that the assets developed by the tenant have XSS injection issues.

   In this case, the tenant takes the responsibility. The tool is only used to assist the tenant developer in detecting issues. No matter whether the tool is available or whether the tool detects issues, the tenant developer is responsible for the development according to the specifications.

   

   4. In the No Code/Low Code scenarios, tenant developers should not introduce open-source or third-party software.

   Scenario 1: A tenant developer copies open-source software codes and pastes them to the GDE develop state page to introduce the open-source software. During penetration test, the security test team finds that the open-source software has known vulnerabilities.

   In this case, the tenant takes the responsibility for the following issues caused by referencing the open-source software fragment: vulnerabilities, intellectual property rights, viruses, malware, and lifecycle management.

   

   5. GDE provides the orchestration capability, which can be maliciously used by some tenant developers to develop malicious codes.

   Scenario 1: A tenant developer develops malicious JavaScript codes and sends the cookies of the login user to an external network. As a result, the user identity is spoofed.

   The tenant takes the responsibility. The orchestration capability provided by GDE cannot be used to develop malicious codes for any purpose, including but not limited to viruses, rogue software, Trojan horses, backdoors, listening programs, and mining programs.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Scenario Examples

name: Tenant Data Protection and Compliance
title: Tenant Data Protection and Compliance
text:
Tenant Data Protection and Compliance
 
 
  
  

  
   1. GDE allows the tenant administrator to configure the anonymization policy to meet data protection and compliance requirements.

   Scenario 1: The tenant administrator does not configure the anonymization policy or the configuration is incorrect. Personal data is not anonymized, leading to privacy violations.

   In this case, the tenant administrator should analyze privacy compliance risks and configure the anonymization policy based on local compliance requirements. Otherwise, the tenant administrator takes full responsibility for the issue that occurred.

   Scenario 2: The tenant administrator correctly configures the anonymization policy, but personal data is still stored or displayed in plaintext, leading to privacy violations.

   In this case, GDE is responsible for not properly implementing system functions.

   

   2. GDE allows the tenant administrator to configure the data access permission to meet data protection and compliance requirements.

   Scenario 1: The tenant administrator does not properly configure the data access permission. Common users have excessive data access permissions, leading to data leakage.

   The tenant takes the responsibility and the tenant administrator should configure the permission based on the minimum permission principle. The tenant is responsible for the issue caused by improper configuration.

   Scenario 2: The tenant administrator correctly configures the data access permission, and the common user role and permission are correctly configured. However, the user accesses unauthorized data, leading to data leakage.

   In this case, GDE takes the full responsibility for the issue that occurs after the tenant administrator correctly configures the permission.

name: Background and Requirements
title: Background and Requirements
text:
Background and Requirements
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Background

    GDE provides a development mode, which helps developers create an asset program that can run on the GDE app execution engine by simply dragging-and-dropping and compiling low-threshold script codes. Different from traditional computer programming, developers can focus on the service design without spending too much time on programming languages.

    GDE lowers the development barrier and the skill requirements for developers who may be inexperience in programming, have no equivalent computer security capabilities, or develop low-quality or insecure assets.

    Based on Huawei's security, reliability, availability, and serviceability baselines, the specifications development team summarizes best practices of asset orchestration and formulates this document to help developers comply with compliance requirements, avoid repeated mistakes, and improve development quality and efficiency.

    General principles:

    
     General development specifications: Excellent codes are not only correct, but also concise, maintainable, reliable, testable, efficient, and portable. Programming is a creative work. Coding specifications are used to instruct developers to form proper programing habits and write high-quality and readable clean codes with consistent styles.

     Security development specifications: Excellent codes should be secure. Security specifications are used to enhance the security awareness of developers in the development process, enable the developers to think as attackers, form the habit of writing codes securely, and write secure and reliable codes.

    

   

   
    Application Scenario and Intended Audience

    This document is used for asset development based on GDE, including GDE ADC common orchestration, data orchestration, and API orchestration.

    This document does not apply to capabilities such as the develop-state environment provided by the product side or provided by the product side after GDE encapsulation. The product side can determine whether to comply with this document or formulate other specifications.

    The specifications are intended for system architects, system engineers, development project managers, development engineers, test engineers, and other readers who are interested in the assets orchestrated on GDE.

   

   
    Implementation Requirements

    This document is released and maintained by Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.

   

   
    Time Requirements

    The specifications take effect as of the date of issuance. Newly developed and changed assets must comply with the specifications.

   

   
    Conventions

    Rule: indicates conventions that must be complied with during development.

    Recommendation: indicates conventions that must be considered during development.

   

   
    Category of Security Specifications

    Security development specifications are classified into bottom-line check items and non-bottom-line check items. Bottom-line check items mainly involve the following aspects:

    
     Sensitive data protection: Do not hardcode or record sensitive data. Encrypt credential data for storage. Do not implement proprietary algorithms.

     Privacy protection: Identify and protect personal data.

     Basic access control: Support authentication on interfaces with external Internet access enabled.

     Prohibition of malicious code: Do not develop, upload, or introduce malicious code in any form.

     Open-source software: Ensure that no open-source software that is not restricted by the GDE sandbox is used in apps.

     Non-query operations must be recorded in logs.

    

   

   
    Issue Feedback

    If you encounter any issue during implementation, discuss it on GDE Cloud at http://gde.huawei.com.

   

   
    Tool Scoring Criteria

    The scanning tool developed on GDE is used to partially test the specifications in this document. The tool adopts a score of the 100-point system. Three points may be deducted for each critical issue, one point for each major issue, and 0.1 point for each minor issue. When the total score is lower than 80 points or a critical issue exists, release is not allowed.

text:
Severity and Tool Description of Specification Items

    Category of Security Specifications

    Security development specifications are classified into bottom-line check items and non-bottom-line check items. Bottom-line check items mainly involve the following aspects:

    
     Sensitive data protection: Do not hardcode or record sensitive data. Encrypt credential data for storage. Do not implement proprietary algorithms.

     Privacy protection: Identify and protect personal data.

     Basic access control: Support authentication on interfaces with external Internet access enabled.

     Prohibition of malicious code: Do not develop, upload, or introduce malicious code in any form.

     Open-source software: Ensure that no open-source software that is not restricted by the GDE sandbox is used in apps.

     Non-query operations must be recorded in logs.

    

   

   
    Severity Ratings

    The severity of each violation is determined based on the consequences. The severity can be critical, major, minor, and suggestion. The determination criteria come from CVSS4.0. For details, see the reference documents in the appendix.

    CVSS score >= 9 points: critical; CVSS score >= 7 points: major; CVSS score >= 4 points: minor; CVSS score < 4 points: suggestion.

    Exclusion Description of Severity Definition

    1. The severity of bottom-line rules is critical.

    2. The severity of all recommendation items is suggestion.

   

   
    Modification Criteria for Issues Detected by Scanning Tools

    GDE provides the AQM scanning tool. The output criteria for scanning issues are as follows: The scanning score is greater than or equal to 80 points, and no minor or major issue exists.
