name: Rule: Ansible, MML, or SSH Cannot Be Used to Run Risky Commands That May Affect the Normal Running of the Target Network
title: Rule: Ansible, MML, or SSH Cannot Be Used to Run Risky Commands That May Affect the Normal Running of the Target Network
text:
Rule: Ansible, MML, or SSH Cannot Be Used to Run Risky Commands That May Affect the Normal Running of the Target Network
 
 
  
  

  
   Description: You can use Ansible, MML, or SSH to orchestrate and execute maintenance commands for the target network. The execution of some maintenance commands may cause running exceptions on the target network, such as configuration deletion and modification, hardware device restart, and software link reset and blocking.

   Check guide: Check whether the Ansible playbook and command activities contain commands that may affect the normal running of devices on the target network by referring to the product manuals of related devices on the target network, and evaluate the risks caused by the execution of the commands. For example:

   
    Check whether Linux service operations include risky operation commands such as reboot, shutdown, halt, poweroff, and rm *.

    Check whether operations on IP routers and switches include risky commands such as shutdown, undo, and reboot.

    Check whether operations on core network and wireless network devices include risky operation commands, such as RST BRD, RMV ***, and DEA ***.

   

   Positive example: You run the display health command through the SSH command activity to query the router health status.

   <HUAWEI> display health

   ----------------------------------------------------------------

   Slot CPU Usage Memory Usage(Used/Total)

   ----------------------------------------------------------------

   9 MPU(Master) 4% 21% 438MB/1995MB

   7 LPU 5% 34% 1147MB/3324MB

   11 SFU 9% 11% 27MB/244MB

   12 SFU 6% 11% 27MB/244MB

   10 MPU(Slave) 2% 17% 347MB/1995MB

   ----------------------------------------------------------------

   Negative example: Run the board slot command through the SSH command to restart the board.

   <HUAWEI> reset slot 1

   Caution!!! Confirm to reset slot 1! Continue? [Y/N]:y

   Warning: Board 1 is being reset.

   Exception scenarios: In the following special scenarios, risky commands may need to be executed. After you fully evaluate the risks, configure a command whitelist to execute risky commands.

   
    The device is not officially brought online. During initial commissioning, risky commands, such as configuration deletion and restart commands, are executed.

    Risky commands, such as configuration deletion and modification commands, are executed on devices during the cutover.

   

   Tool supported or not: yes

   Specification name: Security_MaliciousOperations_Forbid_NetworkDaggerCommand

   Category: non-bottom-line check item

   Severity: minor

   Orchestration scenario: network automation orchestration

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Protection Against Malicious Operations

name: Rule: Unauthorized Operations Cannot Be Performed in Python Scripts
title: Rule: Unauthorized Operations Cannot Be Performed in Python Scripts
text:
Rule: Unauthorized Operations Cannot Be Performed in Python Scripts
 
 
  
  

  
   Description: In Python activities of technical jobs, you can customize Python scripts and encapsulate them into activities. The Python scripts can be used to parse and determine command activity results. You can only write normal service logic in Python scripts. Do not execute invalid logic that is mainly targeted at attacks in Python scripts, for example, CPU and memory resources are consumed by infinite loops or invalid logic, and disk space resources are consumed by writing invalid files.

   Do not use high-risk libraries. Otherwise, an alarm is generated. When an alarm is generated, developers need to confirm the alarm and modify it.

   List of high-risk libraries: subprocess, os.popen, requests, urllib3, os.system, pty.spawan, _posixsubprocess, os.execv, os.execp, os.exece, os.spawnv, os.spawnve,

   os.kill, os.execl, os.execle, os.execlp, os.execvp, os.edecvpe, os.spawnl, os.spwanle, os.popen2(/3/4), pty.fork, exec, and eval

   Check guide:

   1. Check the Python script uploaded to the system to ensure that the Python script contains only proper and correct service processing logic.

   2. Click Project Quality Assessment on the Project Management page to check the project quality.

   Positive example: none

   Negative example:

   
    Invalid service logic. The system CPU resources are consumed by infinite loop or invalid logic.

    Invalid memory operations. Excessive memory resources are requested, consuming system memory resources.

    Invalid file operations. For example, deleting files in the underlying running environment or generating junk files consumes the disk space.

    The script contains more than 1000 consecutive character strings (without spaces).

   

   Exception scenarios: none

   Tool supported or not: yes

   Specification name: Security_MaliciousOperations_Forbid_Python_DaggerCommand

   Category: non-bottom-line check item

   Severity: minor

   Orchestration scenario: all

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Protection Against Malicious Operations

name: Rule: Unauthorized Operations Cannot Be Performed in JS Scripts
title: Rule: Unauthorized Operations Cannot Be Performed in JS Scripts
text:
Rule: Unauthorized Operations Cannot Be Performed in JS Scripts Description: You can customize a JS script and encapsulate it into an activity in the JS activity of the technical operation orchestration service. The JS script can be used to parse and determine the command activity result. You can write only normal service logic in the JS script, and cannot execute invalid logic that is mainly targeted at attacks in the JS script. Check guide: Check the JS script uploaded to the system to ensure that the JS script contains only proper and correct service processing logic. Positive example: none Negative example: Invalid service logic. The system CPU resources are consumed by infinite loop or invalid logic. Invalid memory operations. Excessive memory resources are requested, consuming system memory resources. Invalid file operations. For example, deleting files in the underlying running environment or generating junk files consumes the disk space. Exception scenarios: none Examples of typical invalid JavaScript scripts: Checking whether the script has XSS injection risks Scenarios: The eval command is used to execute variables. The property names of the assignment statement are *url and iframe*, and the U.escapeHtml function is not enclosed in single or double quotation marks. Variables using HTML functions are not escaped using escapeHtml. The variables in the
...
tag are not enclosed in single or double quotation marks. The prepend, promptConfirm, append, attr and before functions use variable parameters. The prepend and append character strings do not contain < and >. The document.write, location.reload and window.open functions use variable parameters. A variable or function is assigned to the right of the innerHTML function, and the function node does not contain escapeHtml. Negative example: if (servicetype === 'host') { txt.innerHTML = data.pa; } else { txt.innerHTML = data; } The div tag contains the html* and url* functions and the functions contain innerHTML. The JavaScript contains a:['target','href','title','class','style'] (the sequence of character strings can be changed). The xssfilter function contains replace, and the replace parameter is concatenated using vertical bars (|) and contains HTML tags. Negative example: function xssfilter(str){ return str.replace(/()/ig, ' ').replace(/(

|

|

)/ig, ' ') } Variables or functions are assigned for location.href and document.form.action. The character string contains href=, and the expression following href= contains variables. Negative example: function func () { key = 'name' value = 'python' url = 'http://www.xxx.com?' + key + '=' + value return '' } The jquery.min.js file whose version is earlier than 3.5.0 exists. The character string dangerouslySetInnerHTML= exists. The value of the property variable (in the +*+ or ${} format) in the
tag is document.location.hash. Negative example: url = document.location.hash function func () { return '
' } Rectification guide: Check whether the code described in the preceding scenarios exists. If yes, modify the code. Checking whether the script has the risk of Trojan horses Scenario: The machine learning model detects that the script has the risk of Trojan horses. Rectification guide: Avoid code confusion. If the character string is too long, a Trojan horse alarm is generated on the web page. Checking whether the script contains suspected mining code Scenario: A mining domain name (such as coinhive.com and minecrunch.co) exists. The machine learning model detects that the script contains mining code. Rectification guide: Check whether the mining domain name exists. If yes, modify it. title: Rule: Open-Source and Third-Party Software Cannot Be Introduced in No Code or Low Code Mode
text:
Rule: Open-Source and Third-Party Software Cannot Be Introduced in No Code or Low Code Mode
 
 
  
  

  
   Description: The improper use of the open-source and third-party software may cause the intellectual property rights (IPR), vulnerabilities, and legal risks. Therefore, in the No Code or Low Code scenario, the open-source or third-party software cannot be introduced through the ways that include but not limited to following:

   
    Overall replication: Developers copy the open-source and third-party software as self-developed assets to the asset package.

    Fragment reference: Developer copy only some code of open-source and third-party software to the asset package.

    External links: Developers reference the external URLs of the open-source and third-party software on pages.
     
       
      
       If developers introduce the open-source or third-party software into the asset package in any form, the mode automatically switches to the Pro Code mode from the No Code or Low Code mode. In the Pro Code mode, developers are responsible for security responsibilities. The quick test process cannot be adapted to. The asset package can be released only after passing the ICSL test.

      

     

   

   Check guide: Check the asset configuration and code.

   Note: For development teams that have deployed CloudDragon, you can integrate FOSSbot with the CloudDragon pipeline to scan the open-source software.

text:
Rule: Do Not Use the MML and TL1 Non-SSL Protocols for Network Automation
 
 
  
  

  
   Description: If an insecure protocol, such as MML or TL1, is used to create a credential, you need to add the SSL configuration to the probe configuration.

   Check guide: Check whether insecure protocols, such as MML and TL1, are used for connection.

   Specification name: General_MCP_InsecureProtocol

   Severity: major

   Orchestration scenario: RPA orchestration

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Others

name: Rule: Personal Data, Sensitive Data, or Project-irrelevant Data Cannot Be Stored in the RPA Project Directory
title: Rule: Personal Data, Sensitive Data, or Project-irrelevant Data Cannot Be Stored in the RPA Project Directory
text:
Rule: Personal Data, Sensitive Data, or Project-irrelevant Data Cannot Be Stored in the RPA Project Directory
 
 
  
  

  
   Description: When a project in Studio is packaged and released, the project directory is compressed into a release package. If personal data or sensitive data is stored in this directory, data leakage risks exist.

   Check guide: Check the project package directory to ensure that there is no personal or sensitive data file.

   Positive example: none

   Negative example: The account password file is stored in the project directory and compressed into a package during release package creation.

   

   Tool supported or not: no

   Specifications name: Security_SensitiveData_RPA_DoNotStoreInProject

   Severity: critical

   Orchestration scenario: RPA orchestration

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Others

name: Suggestion: Do Not Enable Insecure Protocol Options When Using Telnet, HTTP, SMTP, or POP
title: Suggestion: Do Not Enable Insecure Protocol Options When Using Telnet, HTTP, SMTP, or POP
text:
Suggestion: Do Not Enable Insecure Protocol Options When Using Telnet, HTTP, SMTP, or POP
 
 
  
  

  
   Description: During RPA script orchestration, scenarios where the system interacts with external systems through network protocols exist. Insecure protocols such as Telnet and HTTP cannot be used, and secure protocols such as SSH and HTTPS should be preferentially used.

   Check guide: Check whether insecure protocols are used in controls such as Console.login, smtp.sendemail, pop.getemail, and database.connect.

   Positive example: none

   Tool supported or not: no

   Specification name: General_RPA_Use_Secure_Connection_Protocol

   Severity: suggestion

   Orchestration scenario: RPA orchestration

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Others

        Term Involved in this document

        General Digital Engine (GDE)

       
        GDE is a platform+intelligence+agility universal engine that meets GTS service requirements and is provided for services. The engine includes the basic services & framework, data analysis service, AI service, ADC, and O&M operation center.

      

      
       
        Application Development Center (ADC)

       
        ADC is a key product in GDE that enables online orchestration. It provides the no-code/low-code/pro-code approaches for developers to build apps, supporting business scenarios.

      

      
       
        Huawei IT Service (HIS)

       
        Huawei IT service

      

      
       
        HEC (Huawei Enterprise Cloud)

       
        Huawei enterprise cloud

      

      
       
        Data Cube

       
        Data Cube is a big data processing platform of GDE. It provides one-stop data development and operation solutions for GTS solutions, carriers, enterprises, and partners, helping customers build independent and controllable big data platforms and data capability openness centers to maximize data value.

      

      
       
        DataFactory

       
        DataFactory is a big data development platform of Data Cube. It mainly uses the No-Code and Low-Code development modes and uses the Pro-Code development mode as a supplement. DataFactory provides development capabilities in all scenarios (including data access, exploration, modeling, processing, debugging, and governance), depending on the common capabilities of GDE and ADC. DataFactory supports asset accumulation and reuse, and helps business developers efficiently develop data apps to maximize data value.

      

      
       
        Operation Web Services (OWS)

       
        OWS is an online app development platform constructed based on the GDE capability. The online development capability is constructed based on ADC. OWS provides a series of cloud services for fields, such as communications network operation and management, service process management, asset and resource management, and fault and performance management.

      

      
       
        Application (App)

       
        An app is a collection of configurations and codes that are developed on GDE ADC and contain required functions. It can run on one or more servers or VMs.

      

      
       
        BB (Building Block)

       
        BB assets are used for secondary development. For example, common page components, page templates, and project templates are BB assets.

      

      
       
        International Organization for Standardization (ISO)

       
        An international association dedicated to establishing global standards for communications and information exchange. Its main achievement is the widely accepted ISO/OSI model, which defines the standards for the interaction of computers connected by a communications network.

      

      
       
        Robotic Process Automation (RPA)

       
        Record manual actions and develop codes to form a robot. The computer runs the robot to simulate manual operations, improving efficiency.

      

      
       
        Artificial Intelligence (AI)

       
        A technical science that studies and develops theories, methods, and applications for simulating and extending human intelligence.

      

      
       
        User Interface (UI)

       
        Operation interface between the user and system.

      

      
       
        Top Query Language (TQL)

       
        A language developed by Huawei GDE team to query top data, for example, top 10 data records.

      

      
       
        Application Programming Interface (API)

       
        A particular set of rules and specifications that are used for communication between software programs.

text:
Appendix 2: Examples of Personal Data
 
 
  
  

  
   Data is categorized based on the data source, content, and usage.

   
    
     
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Category

       
        Personal Data Type

       
        Remarks

      

     
     
      
       
        Communication related data

       
        Mobile number

       
        Includes the phone number, fax number, and other communication numbers containing the phone number, such as a SIP number or mobile station international ISDN number (MSISDN).

      

      
       
        Email address

       
        Includes the email address and voice mailbox address.

      

      
       
        Address book

       
        Includes the contact list (group names and members), friend group, blacklist group, and address book.

      

      
       
        Communications app account

       
        Includes the instant message (IM) app, social app, and real-name BBS accounts and passwords.

      

      
       
        Terminal device ID

       
        Uniquely identifies a device (such as a computer, network adapter, mobile phone, or smart card), such as the MAC address, international mobile subscriber identity (IMSI), international mobile equipment identity (IMEI), temporary mobile subscriber identity (TMSI), and CDMA mobile equipment identifier (MEID).

      

      
       
        Original content of communication

       
        Includes the actual communication content between two parties (one party is a natural person), including the voice, SMS/MMS, fax, and data service (such as IMs, emails, video communication, and web browsing).

      

      
       
        Personal identity

       
        Authoritative social identity number

       
        Includes the ID card number, social/insurance security number, driver's license, passport number, and visa authorization number.

      

      
       
        Birth information

       
        Includes the birth date, birth place, age, and other information that can be used to deduce a birth (such as constellations and Chinese zodiac). Note: Birth information includes birth-related information calculated through the Gregorian calendar and other common calendars.

      

      
       
        Family information

       
        Includes the marital status, family member information (name), and family composition.

      

      
       
        Others

       
        Includes the name, gender, signature, annuity, personal characteristics, work category, work place, activity type, professional background and achievement, behavior preferences, photos, voice, geographical data, traffic data, race, nationality, ethnicity, political opinions, religious belief, philosophical or moral principles, Trade Union membership, political parties, religious organizations, personal identification numbers, health status (health diagnosis information and disability information), medical record, genetic data, biological feature data (fingerprint and iris), sexual orientation, criminal record, prison record, disciplinary action, military service, SN, UDID, Android ID, and IMSI.

      

      
       
        Location and topology

       
        Logical address

       
        Includes the logical addresses, such as the IPv4 address, IPv6 address, and MAC address of the personal device, base station ID or cell ID (CELL ID), and wireless access point ID, and other open ports.

      

      
       
        Personal location information

       
        Information such as GPS coordinates

      

      
       
        Address and postal code

       
        Includes the family address, temporary address, work address, postal code, and billing address.

      

      
       
        Asset consumption

       
        Asset status

       
        Includes bank deposits, credit limits, credit records, current account balances, and historical balances.

      

      
       
        Asset account

       
        Includes the bank account, ebank account, network virtual asset account (such as Alipay), credit card number, and USERID (corresponding to the account).

      

      
       
        Consumption and payment information

       
        Includes the consumption amount, consumption details (bills and credit card bills), consumption method, and invoice ID.

      

      
       
        Revenue information

       
        Includes the income amount and composition.

      

      
       
        Personal financial information

       
        Includes the fines information, financial status/data, personal asset, and bank account information.

      

      
       
        Historical records

       
        Private browsing history

       
        Includes the browsed URL list, cookies, session IDs, Flash cookies, HTTP logs, and browsing history.

      

      
       
        Operation mode and app usage frequency

       
        Includes the most frequently used apps (for example, website browsing and gaming most accessed by a mobile phone user) and the number of calls per day.

        Note: The app usage frequency is not personal data. However, if it is used together with IMSIs and IP addresses, data subjects can be identified and the involved data is personal data. The operation habits and usage frequency of users are collected for analyzing user behaviors. Generally, the collected information can be used by specific users.

      

     
    
   

   Note: Personal devices refer to devices that are used by individuals and serve individuals.

name: Appendix 3: Three Normal Forms for Data Modeling
title: Appendix 3: Three Normal Forms for Data Modeling
text:
Appendix 3: Three Normal Forms for Data Modeling
 
 
  
  

  
   First normal form (1NF):

   Each specific relationship r in the relational pattern R must have a primary key, and each attribute value is the minimum data unit that is indivisible. In this case, relationship R belongs to the first normal form.

   
    The attribute values displayed in each column are indivisible to ensure the column atomicity.

    For two columns with similar or same attribute values, merge the columns if possible to prevent redundant data.

   

   Second normal form (2NF):

   If all non-key attributes in relational schema R are completely dependent on the primary key, relationship R belongs to the second normal form.

   Each row of data can be related to only one column. That is, a row of data can be used for one purpose only. The table needs to be split as long as duplicate data is found in a data column.

   Third normal form (3NF):

   Non-primary keys in the relational schema R cannot depend on other non-primary keys. That is, there is no function (transfer) dependency among non-primary keys. In this case, relationship R belongs to the third normal form.

title: Appendix 4: Data Classification in the Telecom Field
text:
Appendix 4: Data Classification in the Telecom Field
 
 
  
  

  
   

   
    Data in the BSS domain: refers to data of the customer care and billing, charging, customer service, and settlement systems, such as the real-name authentication data, package data, mobile number, terminal model, traffic consumption data, call duration, bonus points, and complaints.

    Data in the OSS domain: refers to Internet access behavior data, signaling data, and location data. Take data collected over the Gn interface as an example. The data includes web/WAP access log data, URL parsing data, application parsing data, and network track data.

    Data in the MSS domain: refers to ERP data, portal management data, and project management data.

    Data in the virtualization domain: refers to data of the virtual value-added services, including traditional enhanced services and basic services.

        The upgrade packages can be installed.

         The automatic asset archiving function is not supported. By default, only asset packages with up to three versions can be uploaded.

By default, only the latest four asset packages and their corresponding upgrade packages are retained.

        

        

      

      
       
        Asset package version management

       
        
         Asset packages of multiple versions can be concurrently uploaded. The number of versions can be changed by setting the system function parameter number_retained_uninstalled_versions on the GDE App Manager page.

         Asset packages of earlier versions cannot be installed.

name: Format of a GTS Standard Asset Package
title: Format of a GTS Standard Asset Package
text:
Format of a GTS Standard Asset Package
 
 
  
  

  
   
    
     
      Table 1 GTS Standard Package Format
     
     
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Compressed File

       
        Mandatory

       
        Description

      

     
     
      
       
        {Asset package name}.zip

       
        Y

       
        Release package. Compress the files in this directory. There is no root directory.

      

      
       
        ├─meta.json

       
        Y

       
        Asset metadata, which stores asset release information

      

      
       
        ├─release

       
        N

       
        -

      

      
       
        │ ├─quality.json

       
        N

       
        Quality & Trustworthiness Check Result

      

      
       
        │ ├─release_notes.md

       
        N

       
        Description of the version modification point during release. The value is encoded in UTF-8 format and is relative to the image in the pictures/ directory.

      

      
       
        │ ├─pictures

       
        N

       
        -

      

      
       
        │ │ ├─xxx.jpg

       
        N

       
        -

      

      
       
        ├─resources

       
        Y

       
        Directory for storing resource files uploaded by users for asset display on the GDE Store.

      

      
       
        │ ├─logo.png

       
        N

       
        Asset logo displayed on the GDE Store. The pixel must range from 64 x 64 to 90 x 90.

      

      
       
        │ ├─background.jpeg

       
        N

       
        Background image, displayed as the background of the asset logo, 64–96 px, <500 KB

      

      
       
        │ ├─homepage.jpeg

       
        N

       
        Large image on the home page, which is used for asset recommendation display. When the operation personnel recommend the asset to users, the file is zoomed in. The size of the file ranges from 64 px to 96 px and the size of the file is less than 500 KB.

      

      
       
        │ ├─introduction

       
        Y

       
        -

      

      
       
        │ │ ├─summary_zh_cn.txt

       
        Y

       
        Chinese description of the asset, which is encoded in UTF-8 format and contains a maximum of 30 Chinese characters.

      

      
       
        │ │ ├─summary_en_us.txt

       
        Y

       
        English description of the asset, which is encoded in UTF-8 format and contains a maximum of 60 English characters.

      

      
       
        │ │ ├─detail_zh_cn.md

       
        Y

       
        Asset details in Chinese, such as the application scenario, tutorial, and example of the asset. The value is in UTF-8 encoding format.

      

      
       
        │ │ ├─detail_en_us.md

       
        Y

       
        Asset details in English, such as the application scenario, tutorial, and example of the asset. The value is in UTF-8 encoding format.

      

      
       
        │ │ ├─pictures

       
        N

       
        -

      

      
       
        │ │ │ ├─xxx.png

       
        N

       
        detail_en_us.md or detail_zh_cn.md relatively references images in this directory.

      

      
       
        │ │ ├─docs

       
        N

       
        -

      

      
       
        │ │ │ │ ├ ─ {Document name}.{Suffix}

       
        N

       
        detail_en_us.md or detail_zh_cn.md references documents in this directory, such as help documents and third-party open-source software usage instructions. The suffix includes .doc|.docx|.xls|.xlsx|.ppt|.pptx|.zip.

      

      
       
        ├─security

       
        N

       
        -

      

      
       
        │ ├─security.zip

       
        N

       
        Trustworthiness self-check package, such as ICSL test report

      

      
       
        ├─packages

       
        Y

       
        -

      

      
       
        │ ├ ─ {Asset software package name}.{Suffix}

       
        Y

       
        Asset software package. The file name extensions include:

        .zip|.tar|.gz|.gpk|.gdk|.itf|.bpm|.jar|.7z

      

      
       
        {Asset package name}.zip.p7s

       
        Y

       
        Digital signature of the asset package, which is used for asset source tracing

      

     
    
   

   
    
     
      Table 2 meta.json format
     
     
      
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Field

       
        Type

       
        Mandatory

       
        Description

      

     
     
      
       
        id

       
        Character string

       
        Y

       
        Asset ID, which uniquely identifies an asset. It is generated by the asset provider.  UUIDis a number of 16 bytes and 128bits and is usually represented by a character string of 36bytes, for example, 3F2504E0-4F89-11D3-9A0C-0305E82C3301;.

      

      
       
        name

       
        Character string

       
        Y

       
        Asset name, which contains 64 characters, including letters, digits, underscores (_), and hyphens (-).

      

      
       
        version

       
        Character string

       
        Y

       
        Release version, in dotted notation. The content is "V version.R version.C version". For example, 1.4.1 indicates V100R004C01.

      

      
       
        category

       
        Enumeration

       
        Y

       
        Asset category, including App and BuildingBlock and their subcategories. For details about the enumerated values, see the attachment category.xlsx.

      

      
       
        domain

       
        Enumeration

       
        Y

       
        Business domain, which describes the GTS business domain to which the asset is applicable. A business domain has sub-business domains. A maximum of six levels of sub-business domains are supported. For details about the enumerated values, see the attachment domain.xlsx.

      

      
       
        releaseRegion

       
        [Enumeration]

       
        Y

       
        The release area to which the asset is intended. The asset can be used only in these restricted areas. Enumerated value of the list. The options are as follows:

        
         ALL: indicates that the license can be used globally.

         If the document is released for the combination of regions and carriers outside China, use the following code: OC-OP_nnnnn, where OC indicates the combination of regions and carriers outside China, OP_nnnnn indicates the combination of regions and carriers outside China. For details, see the attachment.
          If this parameter is set to OC-ALL, the tool can be used in all regions outside China. If ~ is added before OP_nnnnn, for example, ~OP_nnnnn,, the tool can be used in all regions except this region.

         If the release is a combination of regions and carriers in the China Region, use the following code: CN-Region level-2 code-Region level-3 code-Carrier code. The regional level-2 code and regional level-3 code can be omitted. If the regional level-2 code is omitted, it indicates that the carrier code can be used in the entire China Region. The format of the carrier code is OP_nnnnn, where nnnnn is a number. For details, see the attachment. If ~ is added before an area, for example, ~, the area can be used in all areas except this area. ~ cannot be added before OP_nnnnn.

        

        For details, see the attachment releaseRegion.xlsx.

      

      
       
        eomTime

       
        Numerical value

       
        Y

       
        End of marketing (EOM) time of an asset. The format is MM/DD/YYYY. The time is GMT+00.

      

      
       
        eosTime

       
        Numerical value

       
        Y

       
        End of service (EOS) time of an asset. The format is MM/DD/YYYY. The time is GMT+00.

      

      
       
        developerType

       
        Enumeration

       
        Y

       
        Indicates whether an asset is developed by an individual developer or a team developer. The options are as follows:

        1: individual developer

        2: team developer

      

      
       
        devTeam

       
        Character string

       
        Y

       
        Development team of the asset. The team name contains 64 characters.

        devTeam.xlsx

      

      
       
        techSupport

       
        [Character string]

       
        Y

       
        Technical support contact information, which contains at least the following items: service content, service duration, hotline, and email. A maximum of five items are allowed. The number of characters in each item cannot exceed 300.

        For example:

        Service duration: 9:00–18:00

        Service content: hotline support, remote services, on-site maintenance, and training services

        Service hotline: 123456789

        Service email: xx@xx.com

      

      
       
        otherTags

       
        [Character string]

       
        N

       
        List of asset tags added by developers. Use commas (,) to separate multiple tags. Each tag can contain a maximum of 64 characters. A maximum of 16 tags are supported.

      

      
       
        ootb

       
        Boolean

       
        Y

       
        Out of the Box (OOTB): indicates whether an asset can be used out of the box. The options are True and False. If the value is True, the asset does not require secondary development and customization. If the value is False, the asset can be used only after secondary development and customization.

      

      
       
        platform

       
        Character string

       
        Y

       
        For details, see the Use Platform field in Asset Package Tag.

      

      
       
        platformVersion

       
        Character string

       
        Y

       
        Platform version. The format is V version.R version.C version. For example, 1.4.1 indicates V100R004C01.

      

      
       
        isManaged

       
        Boolean

       
        Y

       
        Indicates whether the modification of an asset is controlled. The value can be True or False.

        True indicates that the asset is controlled, that is, the asset user (including other developers) cannot modify the asset (even if the internal implementation of the asset is visible). False indicates that the asset is not controlled, that is, the asset user can modify the implementation of the asset, enhance or delete the asset, and then release the asset again.

      

      
       
        deploymentMode

       
        Enumeration

       
        Y

       
        Deployment mode. The value can be SaaS or OP.

        SaaS indicates that the service is deployed as SaaS.

        OP indicates that the file needs to be downloaded before being used.

      

      
       
        maturity

       
        Character string

       
        Y

       
        Maturity.

        L1: assets are not mature and are in the exploration/maturity phase. They are for internal use only.

        L5: assets are mature and can be used externally.

        * Other levels can be added as required.

      

      
       
        openness

       
        Enumeration

       
        Y

       
        Mode in which an asset provides capabilities. The options are as follows:

        ServiceAPI: describes APIs of existing services (including SaaS and local services) through asset packages.

        LibAPI: APIs invoked locally. The asset package contains two parts: service capability implementation and service capability API description.

        NonAPI: Capabilities are provided in non-API mode. For example, a specific section is used to describe input parameters in a template, for example, the inputs section in the TOSCA template.

      

      
       
        dependencies

       
        [{}]

       
        N

       
        Definition of dependency on other GTS standard asset packages. Enter the list of dependent assets {name, version}.

      

     
    
   

   The GTS standard asset package consists of two types of software packages: app and BuildingBlock. The standard packaging format of apps is as follows:

   
    
     
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Directory structure

       
        Mandatory

       
        Description

      

     
     
      
       
        {App asset package name}.gpk

       
        Y

       
        The format is gpk, which is essentially zip. Scenario assets that support this format can be installed through GDE AppManager.

      

      
       
        ├─manifest.json

       
        Y

       
        (Mandatory) Asset metadata file, which is used to briefly describe assets

      

      
       
        ├─category.json

       
        Y

       
        Category

      

      
       
        ├─resources

       
        N

       
        (Optional) Asset resource file, such as the registration certificate, birth certificate, icon, and help document

      

      
       
        │├─birth_permit.json

       
        N

       
        Specific module and content of the registration certificate

      

      
       
        │├─birth_certificate.json

       
        N

       
        Specific module and content of the birth certificate

      

      
       
        ├─modules

       
        Y

       
        Asset module folder, which is used for internal asset layering

      

      
       
        │├─module_name

       
        Y

       
        Specific modules are customized by developers as long as they do not conflict with each other in the asset package.

      

      
       
        ││├─module.json

       
        Y

       
        Metadata Description of a Module

      

      
       
        ││├─studio.json

       
        N

       
        Description of the corresponding designer.

      

      
       
        ││ ├ ─ {Orchestration domain}

       
        Y

       
        Orchestration domain, such as common jobs, automatic network orchestration, and data orchestration

      

      
       
        │││├─package.json

       
        Y

       
        Packaging information, including the engine type, engine name corresponding to each package, package file name, and manifest version

      

      
       
        │││├─brief.json

       
        Y

       
        Element name and URI

      

      
       
        │││ │ ─ {Orchestration engine}{.}{zip|tar}

       
        Y

       
        The file or folder of the corresponding engine can be compressed or not. If the file or folder is not compressed, it is automatically compressed into a .zip package.

      

      
       
        ││ ├ ─ {Asset scenario ID}

       
        N

       
        Assets in Multiple Scenarios

      

      
       
        ├─libs

       
        N

       
        Referenced Component Library

      

      
       
        │ ├ ─ {Component type}

       
        N

       
        Component type folder. A maximum of two levels are supported.

      

      
       
        ││ ├ ─ {Component asset category ID}.{gdk|zip}

       
        N

       
        Multiple component assets can be included.

      

     
    
   

   For details, see AssetsPackageFormatV1.3.xlsx.

   

   The format of the BuildingBlock package is not limited. If the BuildingBlock package needs to be added to the integrated orchestration, the middle end needs to parse the package as follows:

   
    
     
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Directory structure

       
        Mandatory/Optional

       
        Description

      

     
     
      
       
        {BuildingBlock asset package name}.gdk

       
        Y

       
        The format is gdk, which is essentially zip. Scenario assets in this format can be imported through tenant assets.

      

      
       
        ├─manifest.json

       
        Y

       
        Asset metadata file, which briefly describes assets. For details about the format, see the app asset package.

      

      
       
        ├─resources

       
        N

       
        (Optional) Asset resource file, such as the registration certificate, birth certificate, icon, and help document

      

      
       
        │├─birth_permit.json

       
        N

       
        Specific module and content of the registration certificate

      

      
       
        │├─birth_certificate.json

       
        N

       
        Specific module and content of the birth certificate

      

      
       
        ├─components

       
        Y

       
        DSL file folder for storing specific building block assets

      

      
       
        │ ├Indicates the metadata of the ─ asset.

       
        Y

       
        DSL file for storing specific building block assets

name: API Fabric Contract Asset Format
title: API Fabric Contract Asset Format
text:
API Fabric Contract Asset Format 
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Schema file naming specifications
     
      
       
        Table 1 Schema file naming specifications
       
       
        
        
        
       
       
        
         
          Protocol

         
          Schema File Naming Specification

         
          Description

        

       
       
        
         
          SOAP

         
          {API name}_{API version}.wsdl

         
          Place the WSDL file and all XSD files used by the WSDL file in the same folder, and compress the folder and the .package file into a ZIP package.

          The following figure shows the ZIP package structure.

          

        

        
         
          REST

         
          
           Cloud Service Engine (CSE) scenario
            
             In the common CSE scenario, the name format is {Microservice name}_{Module ID}.yaml, for example, my_swagger_schemaId.yaml.

             In the scenario where CSE is invoked across apps, the file name must contain App ID. The naming format is [App ID]{Microservice name}_{Module ID}.yaml, for example, [appid]microServiceName_schemaId.yaml.

            

           Non-CSE scenario
            The YAML file name must comply with the API naming specifications.

            The value can contain letters, digits, and underscores (_), and must start with letters. The value can contain 4 to 100 characters.

          

         
          The REST protocol supports the upload of a single YAML or ZIP package. The ZIP package must contain .package.

          The following figure shows the ZIP package structure.

          

        

       
      
     

    The type field in the .package file is mandatory and must be set to schema.
     The following is an example of the .package file:

     spec: "2.0"
packageInfo:
  type: schema
  owner: zhangsan
  timestamp: YYYYMMDD
  tag: first

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Asset Package Specifications

name: API Fabric Extension Plugin Asset Format
title: API Fabric Extension Plugin Asset Format
text:
API Fabric Extension Plugin Asset Format 
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Extension Plug-in Asset Package Description

    The following table lists an example of the aspect plugin package.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Extension Plugin Asset Package Format
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Directory

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         plugin.zip

        
         Overall software package

       

       
        
         |-lib

        
         Stores the Jar compiled by the extended protocol Adaptor. The name of lib can be changed based on service habits.

         If there are two or more JAR packages, compress them into a ZIP package and put the ZIP package to the lib directory.

       

       
        
         |-definition.yaml

        
         Definition file.

         Describes information about the extended aspect, such as the name, version number, aspect name, API policy, and endpoint policy of the extended aspect plug-in.

       

       
        
         |-Package.mf.cms

        
         Signature File

       

      
     
    

    The format and description of the definition.yaml file are as follows:

    
     
      
       Table 2 Extension policy file class definition.yaml
      
      
       
       
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Key Field

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         name

        
         Plug-in name, which must be unique together with version.

       

       
        
         version

        
         Plugin version.

       

       
        
         visible

        
         (Optional) Visibility of the plug-in package after being archived to Catalog.

         The default value is public, indicating that the plug-in is visible to all tenants. Currently, other values cannot be set.

       

       
        
         type

        
         Specifies the type of an extended package.

         
          adaptor: protocol adapter

          aspect: aspect

         

       

       
        
         image

        
         Optional. This parameter is used only for the display image of the plug-in on the catalog.

       

       
        
         description

        
         Description of the plug-in, which is displayed only on the GUI. A configuration example is as follows.

         description:
  zh: ""
  en: ""

       

       
        
         dependency

        
         Version of API Fabric that the plugin depends on, which is the same as that in the pom.xml file of the project during aspect development.

       

       
        
         aspect

        
         -

        
         Asset information about the plugin.

       

       
        
         metadata

        
         Server protocol type, which is the same as that declared in com.huawei.fabric.access.adaptor.server.TcpServer.

       

       
        
         config

        
         -

        
         Describes information about user-extended aspects in the JAR package, including the API policy, endpoint policy, and interceptor. One or more of them can be included during development.

       

       
        
         chains

        
         -

        
         Describe the responsibility chain. The YAML file can contain both api and endpoint, or only one of them.

       

       
        
         api

        
         Information about the API aspect. Multiple API aspects can be configured.

         
          name
           Aspect name, which is the same as the annotation name in the aspect implementation class.

          description
           Aspect description in Chinese and English.

          properties
           The following is an example of the aspect configuration. After the configuration, the value of value can be changed on the API Portal or API Development Tool.

           properties:
            - key: "key1"
              value: "value1"
            - key: "phoneNumber"

//If sensitive information is contained, add the following configuration. The value of value is displayed as * on the GUI. If this parameter is not set, the information is not sensitive by default.
              allowShow: false  
              value: ""

          tables
           The aspect configured in the table format has the same function as the properties.

           tables:
        #table name
        tb1:
          #table column information
          columns:
            - column: "username"
            - column: "age"
            - column: "sex"
            - column: "pass"
              allowShow: false
          #table row information
          rows:
            - username: "aaa"
              age: 18
              sex: "male"
            - username: "bbb"
              age: 22
              sex: "femal"  

          pre
           Location of the aspect in the API responsibility chain.

           
            owner
             Aspect owner, including sys (API Fabric preset aspect) and user (user extended aspect).

            phase
             Phase to which an aspect belongs, including access, mediation, and forward.

            category
             Preset aspect category. For details, see Data Zone Configuration > Data Zone Configuration (default Tenant) > API Integration (API Fabric) > Common Definition > Importing Extension Policies in GDE x.x.x Product Documentation.

           

          scope
           Application scope of the aspect:

           
            global: global application, that is, the application is applied to all published APIs.

            partial: Only the APIs configured with this aspect are applied. APIs of the application aspect are configured using the API development tool.

           

         

       

       
        
         endpoint

        
         Information about the endpoint aspect. The fields and meanings are the same as those of api, but the value of the pre/phase field must be mediation.

       

       
        
         interceptors

        
         (Optional, not recommended) Endpoint interceptor, which is customized for historical versions and is used to be compatible with historical versions. This item can be deleted in other versions.

       

      
     
    

   

   
    
    Adaptor Plug-in Packages

    The following table lists an example of the Adaptor plugin package.

    
     
      
       Table 3 Adaptor plugin package
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         File Name

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         definition.yaml

        
         Information about the extended protocol, such as the name and version of the extended protocol plugin and parameters that can be open to API Portal such as the listening IP address in the Server class.

       

       
        
         lib

        
         JAR package compiled by the extended protocol Adaptor. The name of lib can be changed based on service habits.

         If there are two or more JAR packages, compress them into a ZIP package and put the package to the lib directory.

       

      
     
    

   

   The format and description of the definition.yaml file are as follows:

   
    
     
      Table 4 Adaptor class definition.yaml
     
     
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Key Field

       
        Description

      

     
     
      
       
        name

       
        Plug-in name, which must be unique together with version.

      

      
       
        version

       
        Add-on version.

      

      
       
        visible

       
        Multi-tenant visibility.

        
         public: visible to all tenants.

         private: visible only to the current tenant.

        

      

      
       
        type

       
        Specifies the type of an extended package.

        
         adaptor: protocol adapter

         aspect: aspect

        

      

      
       
        image

       
        Optional. This parameter is used only for the display image of the plug-in on the catalog.

      

      
       
        description

       
        Description of the plug-in, which is displayed only on the GUI. A configuration example is as follows.

        description:
  zh: ""
  en: ""

        Version number of the API Fabric on which the plug-in depends, which is the same as that in the pom.xml file during aspect development.

      

      
       
        metadata

       
        Plug-in metadata path, that is, directory for storing JAR packages developed by users. If there are two or more JAR packages, compress them into a ZIP package in the format of lib/xxx.zip!/JAR package name.

        For example, if the JAR file of an extension protocol is a.jar and the JAR file depends on b.jar, compress a.jar and b.jarzip to c.zip. The path is in lib/c.zip!/a.jar format.

      

      
       
        adaptors

       
        -

       
        Asset information about the plugin.

      

      
       
        name

       
        Server protocol type, which is the same as that declared in com.huawei.fabric.access.adaptor.server.TcpServer.

      

      
       
        description

       
        Detailed description of the server, which is displayed only on the page..

      

      
       
        server

       
        (Optional) Configured if the JAR package contains Server and describes protocol extension information in the JAR package. After the deployment is successful, choose Public Configuration > Extension Management Plug-in Configuration on the API Portal.

        
         channel
          Link configuration. Parameter values can be modified on the API portal.

          Set this parameter based on the reference example in the Adaptor Plug-in Packages. The field names in the example cannot be changed or deleted. Unless otherwise specified, set this parameter based on the example.

          
           port
            Listening port of the server. Port conflicts must be avoided. You can view the list of occupied ports on the API Portal. The value range is [5001, 65535].

           useSsl
            Indicates whether to enable SSL. This parameter can be set to false (disable) or true (enable).

           keepAlive
            Indicates whether the connection is a persistent connection. The value can be false (non-persistent connection) or true.

           maxFrameLength
            Maximum frame length, in bytes.

           maxChannels
            Maximum number of concurrent links allowed. The value range is [1, 65535].

           keepAliveTimeAfterChannelIdle
            Maximum idle time of a link, in seconds.

          

         pool
          Service thread pool configuration. You can change the parameter values on the API Portal.

          Set this parameter based on the reference example in Adaptor Plug-in Packages, unless otherwise specified. The field names in the example cannot be changed or deleted.

          
           corePoolSize
            Number of core threads.

           maximumPoolSize
            Specifies the maximum number of threads.

           keepAliveTime
            Maximum idle time of a non-core thread, in seconds.

           workQueue
            Number of work queues.

           rejectHandler
            Deny policy. The value range is [abort, callerRuns, discard, discardOldest].

          

         userProperties
          If extended configuration is required, set the parameters based on the example in Adaptor Plug-in Packages. If not, retain the userProperties label.

          After the configuration, the value of value can be changed on the API Portal.

        - key: "heartbeat.interval"

          tables:
        #table name
        tb1:
          #table column information
          columns:
            - column: "username"
            - column: "age"
            - column: "sex"
            - column: "pass"
              allowShow: false
          #table row information
          rows:
            - username: "aaa"
              age: 18
              sex: "male"
            - username: "bbb"
              age: 22
              sex: "femal"  

        

      

      
       
        client

       
        (Optional) Required when the JAR package contains northbound clients.

        
         channel
          Link configuration. Parameter values can be modified on the API portal.

          Set this parameter based on the reference example in Adaptor Plug-in Packages, unless otherwise specified. The field names in the example cannot be changed or deleted.

          
           keepAlive
            Indicates whether the connection is a persistent connection. The value can be false (non-persistent connection) or true.

           heartBeatInterval
            Heartbeat interval, in seconds.

           heartBeatMaxLostCount
            Maximum number of heartbeat failures.

           keepAliveSocketNum
            Number of channels that are always in the link state.

           useSsl
            Indicates whether to enable SSL. This parameter can be set to false (disable) or true (enable).

          

         pool
          Parameters related to the connection pool can be modified on the API Portal.

          Set this parameter based on the reference example in Adaptor Plug-in Packages, unless otherwise specified. The field names in the example cannot be changed or deleted.

          
           minIdle

           blockWhenExhausted
            Indicates whether to block a connection when the connection is used up. The value true indicates that the connection is blocked and false indicates that the connection is not blocked.

name: App Development
title: App Development
text:
App Development
 
 
  
  

  
   

  

  
   
    Setting Up a Project
      A project is a basic concept in the develop-state environment. All orchestration elements belong to a project. You can manage these elements by project.

    Orchestration of Simple Object Management Apps
      The simple object management apps are used to orchestrate basic elements, including models, services, events, timers, pages, documents, menus, data processing, and permission management.

    Configuring a Process
      A process is designed for a business object and is operated by different roles in different phases. This helps customers configure and develop processes in graphical mode.

    RPA Orchestration

    API Orchestration

    GDELink Mobile App Orchestration
      To support mobile app development of GDE developers, GDELink provides visualized Web-based orchestration pages, rich orchestration resources, low-barrier drag-and-drop development mode, and flexible and convenient UI customization capabilities. In addition, it has the following advantages: native code expansion of the mobile app, integration of custom plugins, HTML5 apps, and applets, and flexible release and upgrade management modes for mobile apps to achieve custom packaging and release or upgrade management for services. GDELink provides multi-layer orchestration and development capabilities in multiple dimensions and at multiple intervals to enable ecosystem users and partners to quickly build mobile app capabilities and support efficient implementation of various mobile office solutions. This section describes how to orchestrate the GDELink mobile app.

    Data Visualization Screen Orchestration
      This section describes how to orchestrate a data orchestration screen app to dynamically display complex data.

    Network Operation Automation
      This section describes how developers use the orchestration capabilities of the network operation automation module to standardize and automate routine network configuration change actions, including configuring scripts and command-related APIs.

    Configuring the Function Service (Preview)
      This chapter describes how to develop the function service. The permission for function service development is Function Development, and the corresponding role is StudioFaasDeveloper. If the developers do not have this permission, apply for it from the administrator.

    Debugging During App Development

    Feature Description
      This chapter describes how to configure and use a feature.

name: Introduction to Project Concepts
title: Introduction to Project Concepts
text:
Introduction to Project Concepts
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Figure 1 Project concepts
    
   

   

   
    
     
      Table 1 Concept description
     
     
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Concept

       
        Description

      

     
     
      
       
        Develop state

       
        The develop state, also called the design state, is used for app development (including APIs, data orchestration, UI orchestration, and processes). The assets developed in this state are equivalent to a source package that does not have running instances.

      

      
       
        Runtime state

       
        The runtime-state system instantiates and runs the assets developed in the develop state and bears the permission control, flow control, and security issues during program running.

      

      
       
        Project

       
        In the develop state, you can manage multiple types of assets in a unified manner through projects. A project can contain multiple assets, for example, multiple modules. A project in the develop state corresponds to an app in the runtime state.

      

      
       
        Module

       
        A module is an independent unit in a project. Different modules can be divided based on different orchestration element types.

      

      
       
        Orchestration element

       
        Elements used to form a module, for example, pages and APIs.

      

     
    
   

   In the current version, a developer can access the projects and modules created by other developers to collaboratively develop orchestration elements.

   For example, when creating a product management app, you need to create a project and a module, and then develop orchestration elements in this module.

name: Introducing a Project Template
title: Introducing a Project Template
text:
Introducing a Project Template
 
 
  
  

  
   Multiple project templates are preset in the system. After a project is created using a project template, the menus of different orchestration elements are displayed by default.

   
    
     
      Table 1 Template description
     
     
      
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Scenario

       
        Template

       
        Applicable Scenario

       
        Preset Orchestration Menu

      

     
     
      
       
        Common

       
        
         General job orchestration template

         Data visualization template

        

       
        Used to create data models, and add, delete, modify, and query data on a page.

       
        After a project is created using this template, the following menus are displayed by default when the first module is created:

        
         Model

         Service

         Page

         Data Visualization

         Trigger

         Data Import

         Data Export

         Menu

         I18n

         Permission

         Model Archiving

        

      

      
       
        Process

       
        Process template

       
        Used in the scenario where a business object requires a set of processes that are operated by different roles in different phases.

       
        After a project is created using this template, the following menus are displayed by default when the first module is created:

        
         Business Process

         Model

         Service

         Page

         Permission

         I18n

         Menu

         Model Archiving

        

      

      
       
        Network operation automation

       
        Network automation template

       
        Used to develop commands and scripts, change network configurations, and deliver scripts to the network through devices or EMS clients for the scripts to take effect.

       
        After a project is created using this template, the following menus are displayed by default when the first module is created:

        
         Command

         Script

        

      

      
       
        RPA

       
        RPA template

       
        Used to create an asset for automating a robotic process automation (RPA) process.

       
        After a project is created using this template, the following menus are displayed by default when the first module is created:

        
         RPA Script

         RPA Plugin

        

        Related orchestration elements need to be used together with local RPA tools.

      

      
       
        Data orchestration

       
        Data orchestration template

       
        Used during data modeling and data process design and orchestration. It implements one-stop data development during the data life cycle using the metadata management, data computing engine, graphical operators, and operator computing logic.

       
        After a project is created using this template, the following menus are displayed by default when the first module is created:

        
         DataFactory Homepage

         Data Model

         Data Process

         Data Exploration

         Data Source

         Data Integration

         Debug Task Management

         Extended Functions

         Data Quality

        

      

     
    
   

   In a project, after a module is created and the menu is adjusted, if you create a second module, the system creates the second module based on the menu of the current module by default. For example, if a card menu is added to the first module, the card menu is also displayed by default when the second module is created. If multiple modules have been created and different menus have been adjusted, the system creates menus for the new modules based on the menus of the current modules.
