name: Creating a Project
title: Creating a Project
text:
Creating a Project
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    At the service layer, you can orchestrate and develop multiple assets in a project based on ADC and deliver the assets in a unified package.

    You can create a project using a normal template or blank template.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the Project Management page, click Create Project.
      

      
        
       
        If developers have not signed the developer statement, the system displays a dialog box. Developers need to read the statement carefully and sign it after understanding and acknowledging the statement content.

        After the statement is signed, go to the next step.

       

      

      

     Based on different service requirements, create a project using a normal or blank template (no template).
      

      
       (Blank template) Click Create Project Using Blank Template.

       (Template-based creation) The system displays preset templates for project creation. Move the pointer to the required template and click Use.
        

        

      

      

     Configure the project parameters, and click Create.
      

      

      

      For details about the parameters, see Table 1.

      
       
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           
              Project name, which is used to identify a project and must be globally unique. The settings cannot be modified after being submitted.
             

         

         
          
           Display Name

          
           
              App name displayed to end users. You can set it to a name that is easy to identify. You can change the value on the settings page after the creation. In GDE Store, the display name is used to submit the app for putaway.
             

         

         
          
           Tag

          
           Project label, which can be used to query projects by project label

         

         
          
           Service Domain

          
           Service domain to which a project belongs. For details about the application scenarios and creation operations of service domains, see Configuring a Service Domain.

         

         
          
           Share Assets in Inner-Source Repository of GDE Store

          
           This parameter is displayed only in the OC scenario. This parameter controls whether to share assets in the inner-source repository of GDE Store. If Default is selected, the tenant or system configuration is used.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Description of a project.

         

         
          
           Personal Works

          
           Personal works are small plugins, script programs, or tools independently developed by engineers to improve development efficiency. These works must pass basic security scanning before being put away. Personal works are not allowed to access customer networks, and the user shall bear the risks in subsequent deployment and running.

           Projects created in versions before this parameter is set are considered as non-personal works by default. This function is disabled by default.

           The EOS rules for personal works are different from those for non-personal works. EOS date of personal works = min(Asset release time + Days before EOS, EOS date of the develop-state works during packaging). The days before EOS can be configured for personal works at the system level. The default value is six months.

         

         
          
           Enable Hot Deploy

          
           Hot deployment is to incrementally deploy elements orchestrated in the develop-state environment to the runtime-state environment in real time. Developers do not need to manually perform one-click deployment, which facilitates quick debugging.

           After this function is enabled, a project is deployed at the beginning of the project creation. When you add, delete, or modify orchestration elements in the project, the elements are also deployed.

           This switch is not displayed if the selected template does not support hot deployment.

           
             NOTICE: 
            
             If an app fails to pass the quality assessment and code check, and birth certificates, registration certificates, and health certificates of the assets released to the runtime-state environment need to be verified, hot deployment to the runtime-state environment has security risks. In this case, you need to ensure that the risks are acceptable before enabling hot deployment.

            

           

         

         
          
           CreateModule

          
           You need to create modules and then orchestration elements in a project.

           After this function is enabled, a module with the same name as the project is created by default. Therefore, you do not need to create a module again.

           To customize the name of the module to be created, click Advanced.

           This switch is not displayed if the selected template does not support multiple modules.

         

        
       
      

      
        
       
        In earlier versions (1.6.X and earlier versions), you can determine whether a project or app can be customized. Currently, the app and project can be customized by default.

       

      

      

      

     (Optional) If you need to configure more information, click Advanced to configure the logo and service domain.
      

      

      

      
       
       
        
         Table 2 Advanced configuration parameters
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Project

          
           Project information.

         

         
          
           Customer

          
           Customer information.

         

         
          
           Sharing Scope

          
           
            PERSONAL: Only the project creator and specified users have the permission to view the project. Other users under the tenant cannot view the project. If this parameter is set to PERSONAL, you can manage members who have the project permission by referring to Managing a Member.

            TEAM: Only members in a specified team can be opened. Non-team members do not have the permission to view the project.

            PUBLIC: The project can be used by all users under a tenant.

           

           
            After a project is created, only the following users can modify the project sharing scope and asset sharing scope:
            
             Users who have the Develop Asset Management permission

             Personal project creator

             Personal project manager

             Team creator of a team project

             Team manager of a team project

             Creator of a public project

            

           

         

         
          
           Team

          
           When Sharing Scope is set to TEAM, select a created team. If an individual user does not belong to any team, the team cannot be selected. A team needs to create a user who has the develop-state administrator permission. For details, see Team Management.

         

         
          
           Module Name

          
           This field is displayed when CreateModule is enabled.

           The value can contain 1 to 64 characters and start with a letter. Only letters, digits, underscores (_), hyphens (-), and periods (.) are allowed. The value cannot end with [..].

         

         
          
           module Prefix

          
           This field is displayed when CreateModule is enabled.

           Module prefix, which is used to distinguish different modules for easy search.

           The value can contain lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_), and must start with a letter.

           By default, the value is automatically filled. A maximum of the first ten characters of the module name are retained. If the first 10 characters contain uppercase letters, the letters are converted to lowercase letters by default. If the value contains a hyphen (-) or period (.), the hyphen and period are deleted by default and the first 10 characters after the deletion are used.

         

         
          
           Dynamic Permission

          
           This parameter is not displayed by default. This parameter is displayed only when the dynamic permission assignment function is enabled for a master-level system parameter.

           When the dynamic permission assignment function is enabled, resource operation permissions can be dynamically managed in the runtime-state environment.

         

        
       
      

      

     After a project is created, the system redirects you to the project designer where the welcome page displayed by default varies with the selected template.
      

      The following uses ADC Common Template as an example to describe the welcome page. If you select another template during project creation, a different welcome page or even no welcome page is displayed.

      After the welcome page is closed, you can open it by clicking  next to an orchestration element page.

      

      

      
       Orchestration Map: allows beginners to understand the general orchestration procedure and click a phase to quickly access the corresponding task.

       Recently Orchestrated Elements: displays the recently modified orchestration elements of the current login user.

       Shortcut Tools: provides an entry to common functions.

       Learning Resources: provides an entry to learning resources for developers.

       FAQ: provides an entry to common information.

      

      

     Orchestrate and develop the project based on scenario requirements.
      

      Orchestration of Simple Object Management Apps: By dragging and dropping elements, users can add, delete, modify, or query simple objects. In this way, business activities that were originally managed offline can be managed online and in digital mode, making businesses manageable and visible.

      Process Orchestration: Business processes related to organization operations are orchestrated in low-code mode to make business process activities visible and more controllable. Such business processes include approval process, change management, risk management, root cause analysis, and automated diagnosis process.

      RPA Orchestration: Robotic Process Automation (RPA), also called a digital employee, is a software technology that enables software robots to act like humans and perform operations such as data extraction, conversion, verification, and entry between different systems. When an automated business process involves collaboration between multiple systems and no open APIs are available between the systems, the RPA process connects process breakpoints by controlling the mouse and keyboard to simulate human operations on the target system.

      API Orchestration: It aims to integrate existing IT resources of enterprises through APIs, enable siloed apps in enterprise computers to move towards collective collaboration, facilitate data sharing, eliminate information silos, boost service innovation, and maximize resource efficiency.

      GDELink Mobile App Orchestration: With the acceleration of digital transformation of enterprises, mobile apps play an increasingly important role in enterprises. In terms of user experience, business process, and work efficiency improvement, security and privacy protection, data collection analysis, as well as business decision-making, mobile apps are of great help and can bring huge benefits to enterprises.

      Data Visualization Screen Orchestration: With the deepening of digital transformation in the ICT field and enterprises and the development of information technologies, the various business scenarios pose new challenges on data visualization and demands for reducing the development and reuse costs of the data visualization screen. Under this context, the data visualization screen orchestration enables users to quickly orchestrate complex, user-friendly, and professional data visualization screen display effects by dragging and dropping elements.

      Network Operation Automation Orchestration: Network O&M personnel, especially senior network O&M personnel, need to perform routine adjustments to network configurations. They need to modify scripts based on their understanding of network products and deliver the scripts to the network through devices or EMS clients. ADC provides network operation automation modules with the corresponding orchestration capabilities to standardize and automate routine network configuration change actions. This improves the efficiency of network configuration change actions and reduces network failures caused by manual operations.

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    
     After a project is created, if CreateModule is enabled, the project contains a default module. In this case, skip operations in Managing the Module.

     On the Project Management page, click  in the view of the created project.
      

      

      The project configuration page contains the following tab pages and their functions:

      
       Resource Viewing
        Displays the panorama of resources in an existing project. You can view the modules and resources created in the project.

       Project Settings
        Allows you to configure common information such as projects, labels, and dependencies. For details, see Configuring the Common Project Information.

       Project Change History
        Allows you to view the change records of a project. The addition, deletion, and modification operations performed by each user on orchestration elements in the project are recorded and can be queried.

       Indicator White List
        Determines the metrics that can be reported. For details, see Configuring the Project Metric Whitelist.

       Common Parameter Settings
        Allows you to set variables extracted from a project as common parameters. For details, see Configuring the Common Parameters of a Project.

       Privacy Statement Settings
        Allows you to set a privacy statement when an app needs to collect end users' privacy data. For details, see Configuring an App-Level Privacy Statement.

       Member Management
        Allows you to add other members if the project is a personal project. For details, see Managing a Member.

       Data Desensitization Policy Management
        Allows you to mask sensitive data when logs are printed during app running to prevent the leakage of sensitive information. For details, see Configuring a Project Desensitization Policy.

       Description Document
        To facilitate long-term evolution, maintenance, co-construction, and sharing of assets, developers can provide detailed asset description documents for projects. For details, see Configuring Release Information of Inner-Source Assets.

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Setting Up a Project

name: Creating a Project from an Inner-Source Asset
title: Creating a Project from an Inner-Source Asset
text:
Creating a Project from an Inner-Source Asset
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     Interworking with GDE Store has been configured.

    

   

   
    Context

    In the cloud deployment scenario, developers can share assets through GDE Store. For example, developers can upload projects or apps developed by themselves or obtain assets shared by other developers for customized development.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the Project Management page, click Create Project.

     Click the Inner-Source Assets tab.
      

      
        
       
        If the error message "Error Code: 07060002; Description: Failed to obtain cloud GAM authentication token" is displayed, the interworking with GDE Store is not configured in the current environment. Contact the tenant administrator to configure the interworking with GDE Store.

        

       

      

      

     Set filter criteria to search for the required inner-source asset.

     In the inner-source asset list, click the corresponding asset.

     In the displayed Details dialog box, click Create Project.

     In the displayed Project Info dialog box, configure project information and click Create.

     After the project is created, it contains the orchestration elements in the selected shared project. Developers can customize the project by using existing orchestration elements.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Setting Up a Project

name: Managing the Project
title: Managing the Project
text:
Managing the Project
 
 
  
  

  

  
   
    Importing a Project

name: Importing a Project
title: Importing a Project
text:
Importing a Project
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

   

   
    Context

    Projects can be imported and exported in the develop-state environment. The import result varies depending on the package type.

    
     If you choose to pack the project as a project package, export the .gdk project package.
      
       If Read-only is enabled when a project package is exported, you can edit and modify the project after the project package is imported to the develop-state environment again.

       If Read-only is disabled when the project package is exported, you can edit and modify the orchestration elements after the project package is imported to the develop-state environment again.

      

     Export the runtime-state package in .gpk format when the app is selected during packaging. When the runtime-state package .gpk is selected for importing a project, orchestration is not supported in the develop state. By default, the read-only mode is enabled.

    

    In addition, the imported project has different permissions based on the open level.

    
     If a project whose Open Level is set to Public is packaged and imported to another environment, the project remains public.

     If a project whose Open Level is set to Team is packaged and imported to another environment, the project becomes a personal one and can only be used by the user who imports the project. You can change the project open level to Team again by setting the common project information.

     If a project whose Open Level is set to Personal is packaged and imported to another environment, the project remains a personal one and can only be used by the user who imports the project.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Click Import Project.

     Click Add to upload the project package to be imported.
      

      

      

      

     Click OK to start the import as prompted. You can check whether the import is successful in the log import window.
      

      
        
       
        Before a project is imported, the system verifies whether the asset signature certificate of the project is in the signature verification list on the Asset Certificate Management page. If so, the project can be imported. If not, the system determines whether to import the project based on the following logic:

        
         If the user has the asset certificate management permission, the system displays a message showing the certificate information. The user can trust the certificate and import the project.

         If the user does not have the asset certificate management permission, an error message is displayed, and the project cannot be imported.

        

       

      

      

     After the import is complete, view the project in the project list.
      

      For a project in read-only mode, the elements in the project cannot be modified after being imported.

      

      If Read-only in the preceding figure is not displayed, the project is not in read-only mode. You can continue to edit and modify the elements in the project.

name: Backing Up Projects
title: Backing Up Projects
text:
Backing Up Projects
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    During app orchestration, developers usually need to back up projects to avoid data loss.

    On the Project Management page, you can back up all non-read-only projects of the current tenant as project packages in one-click mode.

    Only users with the Develop Asset Management permission can back up projects. By default, only the administrator has this permission.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Choose More > Back Up Projects.

     In the displayed dialog box, click Start Backup.

     After the backup task is successfully started, the Manage Backup Tasks page is displayed. The new backup task is in Running state.
      

      The backup duration varies depending on the project scale of the tenant. You can click  in the upper right corner to refresh the task progress.

      

     Wait until the status of the backup task changes to Succeeded, which indicates that the project backup is complete.
      

      

      

      

     Click Download to download the backup files of all projects in the backup task to the local PC.

     Click View to view task details.
      

      On the task details page, you can download a single project backup file, select multiple projects and download project backup files in batches, or download all project backup files in one-click mode.

      
        
       
        
         By default, backup task records and corresponding backup files are stored in the system for 365 days, which means that the task records and backup files will be deleted if they are stored for more than 365 days.
          The retention period can be configured in the runtime-state environment by performing the following operations: Choose Products and Services > Administration > Archiving Configuration, search for project-backup-package-history on the View Archiving Configuration tab page, click Edit of the found task, and set Retention Period (Days) to a value ranging from 1 to 365 days. You can manually trigger an archiving task to delete backup files that have been retained for more than the value of Retention Period (Days).

         If there are multiple project packages in the backup file, compress the GDK project packages into a ZIP package. If there is only one project package, the GDK project package can be directly used before being compressed into a ZIP package.

         The version of the GDK backup project package is increased by 1 based on the latest packaging version. If there are no packaging records, the default value 0.0.1 is used.

         If a project fails to be backed up in the backup task, you are advised to manually package the project package in the project and view the real-time packaging logs to facilitate fault locating.

         The downloaded project backup files do not contain the projects that fail to be packaged. The backup file is named in the format of GdkGroupTimestamp.zip, for example, GdkGroup1724307021805.zip.

         If the total size of all GDK files to be downloaded exceeds 3 GB, the system automatically downloads the files in batches. As a result, multiple ZIP packages with a size of no more than 3 GB for each package will be obtained.

         To import a project backup file, you need to decompress the ZIP package to obtain the GDK file.

name: Configuring the Common Project Information
title: Configuring the Common Project Information
text:
Configuring the Common Project Information
 
 
  
  

  
   After a project is created, you can modify and maintain the project information.

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     On the Project Management page, click  in the Operation column of the created project.

     On the displayed page, click the Project Settings tab and click Edit on the right of Project Information to modify project parameters.
      

      For details about the parameters, see Table 2.

      

     Configure the project dependency. A maximum of 20 unique dependencies can be added. If a dependency is configured, the dependency will be verified in the runtime-state environment when the project is released to the runtime-state environment.
      

      

      

      

     Configure an app trigger.
      

      Currently, you can specify the service to be triggered before app uninstallation. For example, an interface can be triggered to clear data. The service selected in the trigger must be at the project or public level. The service path starts with / or cse://.

      

      

      
       Service path: /adc-service/rest/v1/services/{project name}/{module name}/{service name}, for example, /adc-service/rest/v1/services/f_test/OWS4ALoginService/serviceValidatea. You can click  and select a service.

       CSE path: cse://xxxx/xxxx

      

      
        
       
        App triggers can be triggered only when apps are uninstalled on the GDE App Manager page. If you need to use the app trigger function, ensure that the trigger has been deployed on the GDE App Manager page in the develop-state environment. For details, see Configuring the Deployment Distribution Mode. In the runtime-state environment, you can install and uninstall apps on the Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager page.

       

      

      

     After the configuration is complete, click Save.

name: Configuring the Common Parameters of a Project
title: Configuring the Common Parameters of a Project
text:
Configuring the Common Parameters of a Project
 
 
  
  

  
   After a project is created, you can configure common parameters of a project.

   
    Context

    The common parameters of a project can be used in multiple scenarios. You can define parameters and use them in development scenarios. You can also configure parameters based on the scenarios provided by the system to implement specified service capabilities.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     On the Project Management page, click  in the Operation column of the created project.

     On the displayed page, click the Common Parameter Settings tab.

     On the displayed page, click Create.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Parameter Name

          
           Parameter name, which can contain letters, digits, underscores (_), and hyphens (-). The value contains 1 to 50 characters.

         

         
          
           Parameter Type

          
           The value can be Number or String.

         

         
          
           Configurable

          
           Whether parameters can be modified after an app is installed and enters the runtime-state environment.

         

         
          
           Encrypt

          
           Whether to encrypt the value.

         

         
          
           Parameter Value

          
           Default value of the parameter.

         

         
          
           DisplayOrder

          
           Sequence of a parameter in the app parameter list in the runtime-state environment. A smaller value indicates a higher sequence. If this parameter is not set, the parameter is displayed at last.

         

         
          
           Parameter Label

          
           Name displayed in Chinese and English.

         

        
       
      

      

     After the configuration is complete, click Save.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After common parameters are configured, they can:

    
     Be called by using the context variable in the script. For example, you can call _context.getAppParameter (connect_address) to obtain the value of the common parameter connect_address.

     Be used in the integration service as the address parameter for calling the outbound APIs.

title: Deleting a Project
text:
Deleting a Project
 
 
  
  

  
   Deleting a project is risky. Exercise caution when performing this operation.

   
    Context

    When a project is deleted, assets released by the project can be deleted in cascading mode. Asset deletion in cascading mode will delete the project packages and app assets released by the project and stored in the local asset library.

    
      
     
      After a project is deleted, all data in the project is deleted and cannot be restored. Therefore, exercise caution when deleting a project.

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     On the project management page, click  in the view of the created project.

     Confirm the options and risks as prompted. If you still want to delete the project, select the check boxes.

     Click OK.

name: Configuring an App-Level Privacy Statement
title: Configuring an App-Level Privacy Statement
text:
Configuring an App-Level Privacy Statement
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    When an app needs to collect end users' privacy data, a privacy statement needs to be provided to declare the user information to be collected, information usage, and protection measures for user information. The app can be used only after users' consent is obtained.

    For example, the member information management system needs to collect member information, the book borrowing registration system needs to collect reader information, and the business trip reimbursement system needs to collect the bank account information and business trip schedule of the reimbursement personnel. Such apps can be used only after the privacy statement is displayed to the user and the user's consent is obtained.

    ADC allows developers to configure privacy statements on the develop-state environment and displays privacy statements to end users on the runtime-state environment.

    
     The privacy statement can be configured on the web client to adapt to the scenario where users use apps on PC web pages.

     The privacy statement can be configured on the mobile client to adapt to the scenario where users use apps through GDELink.

    

    
      
     
      
       If both the web client and mobile client are used, you need to configure privacy statements for the two types of clients separately.

       The privacy statement configured in a project is a part of the tenant privacy statement. Configure the privacy statement only when the project involves user privacy data operations. The privacy statement must accurately describe the types, purposes, handling methods, time limits, and rights of data subjects of all the personal data. Ensure that the privacy statement complies with local laws and regulations and has been reviewed by legal affairs personnel.

      

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     On the Project Management page, click  in the Operation column of the created project.

     On the displayed page, click the Privacy Statement Settings tab.

     Based on the application scenario, click Add in the Operation column of the record whose Client Type is Web or Mobile.
      

      

      

      

     Click Save.

    

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Managing the Project

name: Configuring the Project Metric Whitelist
title: Configuring the Project Metric Whitelist
text:
Configuring the Project Metric Whitelist
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    During app running, app metrics need to be developed to facilitate monitoring and maintenance of app operations. After app metrics are reported to GDE management zone, maintenance and management personnel can learn about the app running status.

    Metrics of counter and gauge types can be reported. Only metrics of the gauge type can be viewed on the WebUI of the GDE management zone. Metrics of the counter type are not displayed.

    To implement the metric reporting capability, you need to perform the following operations:

    
     Define metrics using the Monitor method in a script. The Monitor function supports script engines of V1.5, V1.6, and the latest version. After historical assets are imported, you can define metrics based on historical assets. 
      
       
        
         Table 1 Monitor functions
        
        
         
         
         
        
        
         
          
           API

          
           Description

          
           Example

         

        
        
         
          
           Monitor.gauge(metricName,metricValue[,labels])

          
           Used to report gauge metrics. When this function is used to report metrics, the tenant_id and current_app parameters are contained by default. That is, you do not need to specify the tenant and current app information.

           
            metricName: name of the reported metric. To avoid conflicts between metric names and existing metric names in the system, the reported metric names always start with app_gauge_, for example, app_gauge_user_counts.

            metricValue: reported metric value. The value must be of the Double type.

            labels: Optional. The value is of the Object type. The key is the label name, and the value is the label.

           

           The return value is of the Boolean type.

           
            true: Reporting succeeded.

            false: Reporting failed.

            exception: An exception occurs.

           

          
           
            Example without a label:
             var res =Monitor.gauge("app_gauge_user_counts",12000)
return {"result":res}

            Example with a label:
             var gauge_with_label = Monitor.gauge("app_gauge_test",5.1,{"a":"a","b":"b"})
return {"gauge_with_label":gauge_with_label}

           

         

         
          
           Monitor.counter(metricName,metricValue[,labels])

          
           Used to report counter metrics. When this function is used to report metrics, the tenant_id and current_app parameters are contained by default. That is, you do not need to specify the tenant and current app information.

           
            metricName: name of the reported metric. To avoid conflicts between metric names and existing metric names in the system, the reported metric names always start with app_counter_, for example, app_counter_user_counts.

            metricValue: reported metric value.

            labels: Optional. The value is of the Object type. The key is the label name, and the value is the label.

           

           The return value is of the Boolean type.

           
            true: Reporting succeeded.

            false: Reporting failed.

            exception: An exception occurs.

           

          
           
            Example without a label:
             var res =Monitor.counter("app_counter_user_counts",12000)
return {"result":res}

            Example with a label:
             var counter_with_label = Monitor.counter("app_counter_test",2,{"a":"a","b":"b","c":"c"})
return {"counter_with_label":counter_with_label}

           

         

        
       
      

     Configure a metric whitelist. Only the metrics defined in the project metric whitelist can be reported. A maximum of 50 metrics can be configured for each project.

    

    In addition, in the OC scenario, the master user can configure the metric whitelist function on the Products and Services > ADC System Management > Component Management > System Parameter Configuration page displayed under the master tenant. This function can be enabled only for specified tenants.

    
     
      
       Table 2 System parameters
      
      
       
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Category

        
         Name

        
         Value

        
         Default Value

       

      
      
       
        
         adc-service

        
         app_monitor_enable

        
         Whether the metric reporting capability is enabled for all tenants

         
          true: The project metric reporting capability is enabled for all tenants.

          false: The project metric reporting capability is not enabled for all tenants.

         

        
         true

       

       
        
         adc-service

        
         app_monitor_tenant_whitelist

        
         Whitelist of tenants for whom the metric reporting capability is enabled If app_monitor_enable is set to false, the function is enabled for specified tenants using a whitelist.

         Example: 1002,1003

        
         N/A

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project for which you want to configure a metric whitelist.

     Define metrics using scripts. A new script is used as an example.
      

      
       After entering the project for which you want to configure a metric whitelist, choose Service in the navigation pane.

       Create a service using a blank template.

       Drag RunScript from the left pane.

       Click  to expand the node properties.

       In the Selecting a script area, click Edit.

       In the script box, define metrics and obtain metric values based on service requirements.
        var res = Monitor.gauge("app_gauge_user_counts",12000)
return {"result":res}

       Save the script as prompted and reference it in the service.

      

      

     Configure a metric whitelist.
      

      
       On the Project Management page, click  in the Operation column of the created project.

       On the displayed page, click the Indicator White List tab.

       Click Create and configure the metric information.
        

        

       Click Save.

      

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After the preceding configuration is complete, deploy the app and run the script for verification. Reported metrics need to be viewed in the GDE management zone. You can refer to the following steps to view them. If you do not have the permission, apply for it from the operations personnel.

    
     Log in to the GDE management zone portal as the op_svc_cfe tenant.

     Choose Maintenance > Monitoring > Metric Monitoring.

     Search for adc-service, locate Application: adc-service, expand it, and choose Metric under any instance directory.
      

     Locate the metric based on its name and view the metric reporting result.

name: Configuring a Service Domain
title: Configuring a Service Domain
text:
Configuring a Service Domain
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    Service domains to which projects belong are used in the following scenarios:

    
     Database sharding. The service database is matched based on the configured service domain.
      For example, if Service Domain is set to FM and a secondary database is configured for the FM service domain, the database instance of the project can be created in the secondary database to optimize the performance of the service domain.

     Fine-grained public API control. If an API is set to be public, a public domain whitelist is also set. Only domains in the whitelist can access the API.
      For example, if Service Domain is set to CEAE and the public domain is CEAE for public services of asset domain A, the project can call the corresponding public services.

      For details about how to configure a whitelist for a public API, see Table 1.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the home page of the develop-state system, choose General Settings > Service Domain Management.

     Click Create and set domain parameters.
      

      

      

      

     Click OK.

Configuring a Project Desensitization Policy

text:
Creating a Module
 
 
  
  

  
   In a project, orchestration elements are grouped into modules of different types.

   
    Prerequisites

    A project has been created.

   

   
    Context

    Multiple modules can be created in a project. Module names are case insensitive. For example, if a module named a has been created in a project, you cannot create another module named A.

    If a module has been created by default during project creation and only one module is required in the project, you do not need to create another module.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management. Open a created project.

     In the project module area, click . In the expanded area, click .
      

      
       Figure 1 Creating a module
       
      

      
        
       
        For a new project, if no module is available, the Create Module dialog box is automatically displayed after you click the project.

       

      

      

     Configure the information and click Create Module.
      

      
       Figure 2 Creating a module
       
      

      Table 1 describes the parameters.

      
       
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           The value can contain 1 to 64 characters and start with a letter. Only letters, digits, underscores (_), hyphens (-), and periods (.) are allowed. The value cannot end with [..].

         

         
          
           Prefix

          
           Module prefix, which is used to distinguish different modules for easy search.

           The value can contain lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_), and must start with a letter.

           By default, the value is automatically filled. A maximum of the first ten characters of the module name are retained. If the first 10 characters contain uppercase letters, the letters are converted to lowercase letters by default. If the value contains a hyphen (-) or period (.), the hyphen and period are deleted by default and the first 10 characters after the deletion are used.

text:
Importing Legacy Assets
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    A project has been created.

   

   
    Context

    Legacy assets can be imported to the system. Apps, app groups, interface packages, interface package groups, process packages, and commands of earlier versions (versions earlier than 1.5) can be directly imported and converted into new assets.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Open a created project.

     Click  in the upper right corner.

     Select Import Legacy Asset from the drop-down list. On the displayed page, click Add and upload the legacy assets to be imported.
      

      

      

      
       When importing APP assets, create a module using the app name.

       When importing ZIP and ITF assets, select the module to be imported.

      

      

     Click OK.

     Switch to the imported module and check the imported data.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Managing the Module

name: Managing Element Locks
title: Managing Element Locks
text:
Managing Element Locks
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    When an orchestration element is being edited, it is locked and cannot be modified by other members. In the project designer, you can view the orchestration elements that are being locked.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Access the target module. If there is only one module, it will be accessed by default. If there are multiple modules, manually select one.

     Click Element Lock at the bottom of the project designer, and view the orchestration elements that are being locked.
      

      

      

      
        
       
        If the user have obtained the Develop Asset Management permission or have a role higher than Administrator of the current project, Unlock is displayed in the Operation column. You can unlock orchestration elements.

        The unlocking operation may cause the loss of the content that is being edited by the user. Exercise caution when performing this operation.

       

      

      

    

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Setting Up a Project

name: Managing App Versions
title: Managing App Versions
text:
Managing App Versions
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    In HIS and HEC scenarios, interworking with remote source code repositories is supported for version control and management.

    The app version control capability is opened using a tenant whitelist. Only tenants in the whitelist can use this capability.

   

   
    Prerequisites

    The remote repository has been configured for the current tenant and the tenant whitelist has been enabled. For details, see Data Zone Configuration > Data Zone Configuration (master Tenant) > ADC System Management > Managing the App Development Configuration > Configuring the Remote Repository and Tenant Whitelist in GDE x.x.x Product Documentation.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Access the target module. If there is only one module, it will be accessed by default. If there are multiple modules, manually select one.

     Click Version Control at the bottom of the project designer.

     Click Obtain Latest Changes. The system obtains and displays the element change information in the project.

     Click Submit Current Changes, enter the change reason, and click Confirm.

     Click Version History to view the historical submission information in the version.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Setting Up a Project

Orchestration of Simple Object Management Apps
 
 
  
  

  
   The simple object management apps are used to orchestrate basic elements, including models, services, events, timers, pages, documents, menus, data processing, and permission management.

  

  
   
    Development Process of Simple Object Management Apps
      This section describes the process of developing a simple object management app.

    Model Configuration
      Simple object management apps are mainly used to add, delete, modify, and query data and a model used for storing data is indispensable. Therefore, you need to design a model first and create it based on the plan.

    Configuring Pages

    Configuring Services
      A service is used to orchestrate various operations of a model based on logical conditions.

    Configuring a Model Flow

    Configuring a Trigger
      In the data model, events of specified types, service calling, and data operations can be triggered based on data changes.

    Configuring an Event and an Event Listener
      An event and an event listener are used to define scenarios where specified actions are executed under specific conditions.

    Configuring Data Import and Export Services
      In actual data configuration scenarios, data needs to be imported in batches. This section describes how to configure the data import service.

    Configuring Permissions and Roles

    Configuring a Timer
      A timer is used to define a one-off or periodic job that is executed at specified time.

    Configuring a Customized Asset Package

    Configuring Error Codes

    Configuring the Internationalization Information

    Presetting the App Menu

    Configuring the Markdown Document

Development Process of Simple Object Management Apps
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes the process of developing a simple object management app.

   
    Scenario Description

    Simple object management apps are usually used to model data and allow users to perform operations such as adding, deleting, modifying, and querying data through pages and services in offering, member, and device management scenarios.

    The core functions of such apps are to add, delete, modify, and query data. Therefore, data models need to be designed first and then data can be added, deleted, modified, and queried based on the data models.

   

   
    Development Preparations

    Before developing simple object management apps, you need to create a project and a module by following instructions provided in Setting Up a Project.

name: Model Overview
title: Model Overview
text:
Model Overview
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Introduction to Models

    In ADC simple object management apps, a data model is equivalent to a table created in the database when a service system is developed in traditional mode. The data model is used to store the configuration data and service data required by the service system.

    If you want to develop an offering management system to perform operations, such as adding and querying offering information, you need to create a table to store the offering information, such as offering names and prices. The offering information table is a data model to be planned.

   

   
    Introduction to Model Elements

    Table 1 lists the model types that can be created and managed by the system.

    
     
     
      
       Table 1 Model types
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Name

        
         Element Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Data model

        
         A new relational database model planned in the system, such as an offering information table used for storing offering names and prices.

       

       
        
         Data source model

        
         A model used to access external data sources. For existing data models, data sources can be selected through data source models. This model applies to the scenario in which a database already exists.

       

       
        
         Elastic model

        
         A distributed data model used to store and manage large-scale data.

         For example, if the data model of an offering information table is backed up, the backup data table can be set as an elastic model.

       

       
        
         Vector model

        
         A vector model used to understand data and convert the data into mathematical vectors that carry the meanings or features of the data. Vector models support vectorization of specified fields and vectorized retrieval.

       

      
     
    

    In addition, you can manage proxy and view models under Model, as shown in Table 2. These two types of models are briefly described because they are not used in simple object management apps.

    
     
     
      
       Table 2 Other model types
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Name

        
         Element Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Proxy model

        
         The proxy model is a model that is automatically created when a process is created. The proxy model cannot be created on the Model page and is not displayed in the model view by default. You can view it in the model list. The indexes of proxy models can be added, deleted, and queried.

         For example, when you create a leave e-flow during process orchestration, the system automatically creates a model for storing leave e-flow data. This model is called a proxy model.

       

       
        
         View model

        
         The view model is compatible with the model in 1.0. The view model can be viewed on the Model page only when the imported legacy assets contain model elements.

       

      
     
    

    Table 3 describes the types of property elements supported by a model.

    
     
     
      
       Table 3 Types of model property elements
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Name

        
         Type

        
         Element Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Boolean

        
         boolean

        
         Model property of the Boolean type.

       

       
        
         Text

        
         text

        
         Model property of the text type. You can customize the text length.

         
          Text Type can be set to:
           
            Short Text: defines the short text that contains a maximum of 250 characters.

            Normal text: defines the text that contains a maximum of 1000 characters.

            Long Text: defines the long text. The maximum length can be 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, or No Limit and the unit is KB. You are advised to set this parameter to 256 KB. If No Limit is selected, data query and synchronization may be blocked.

           

          Disallowed Character: indicates the character that cannot be entered in the text.

         

       

       
        
         Integer

        
         integer

        
         Model property of the integer type. Integers ranging from –9007199254740991 to 9007199254740991 can be stored.

       

       
        
         Decimal

        
         decimal

        
         Model property of the decimal (or floating-point number) type. The floating-point number type can only guarantee the precision of decimal numbers of 15 digits.

       

       
        
         Sequence

        
         sequence

        
         Model property of the sequence type. Sequence Type can be set to:

         
          Date time sequence: You need to set the format. The default format is {YYYY}-{MM}-{DD}-{0000}.

          UUID: A universally unique identifier (UUID) is a number generated on a machine and ensures uniqueness for all machines in same spacetime. The default sequence is in UUID format. For example, it can be set to {UUID}.

          Distributed time sequence: This type uses the Snowflake algorithm to generate a distributed time sequence ID of the long type. The ID is unique and the time sequence is ordered. This type applies to division and sharding scenarios.

          Auto-increment sequence: indicates the auto-increment number sequence.

         

       

       
        
         Enumeration

        
         enum

        
         Model property of the enumeration type. You can set the enumerated value and display value.

         
          Enumerated value: actual value

          Display value: The value can be displayed in the TQL drop-down list. If no display value is set, the enumerated value is displayed.

         

       

       
        
         Date

        
         date

        
         Model property of the date type. The default format is yyyy-MM-dd.

       

       
        
         Time

        
         time

        
         Model property of the time type. The default format is HH:mm:ss.

       

       
        
         Date and Time

        
         datetime

        
         Model property of the date and time type. The default format is yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.

       

       
        
         Timestamp

        
         timestamp

        
         Model property of the timestamp type. Timestamp can be set to s or ms.

       

       
        
         Reference

        
         reference

        
         If the field value is synchronized from the model of other type, the Reference property is used. For the reference type, you need to set the following information:

         
          Reference Model: Select the model from which the data comes. For example, if the value of a field in model A comes from model B, model B can be selected for Reference Model.

          Reference Operation: indicates whether to delete the referenced instance when deleting the reference instance.
           
            Forbid Delete: If an instance is referenced by another reference, you cannot directly delete the instance.

            Clean Field: After you delete an instance that is referenced by another reference, the fields in the referenced instance are automatically deleted.

            Cascading Delete: When data of the referenced model instance is deleted, the current model instance is deleted in cascading mode.

           

          Show Property: It is used only to construct TQL statements. You can set this parameter to a mandatory and unique index property in the reference model or do not specify this parameter.

         

       

       
        
         File

        
         file

        
         Model property of the file type. For example, images, ZIP packages, and documents are supported.

         
          File Type: indicates the supported file name extension. Use commas (,) to separate multiple file name extensions. For example, it can be set to zip,txt.
           The basic service has restrictions on the formats of the files to be uploaded. Therefore, when defining the file type in the model, you need to define the file type to values allowed by the basic service.

           The formats of files that can be uploaded for basic services are as follows:

           xml,keystore,bmp,ppt,msg,app,tiff,pptx,bm,jpeg,so,apk,png,avi,docx,xls,mp4,mp3,ico,doc,tar,wsdl,wav,zip,rar,tif,dll,pdf,htm,gz,tgz,html,patch,gif,jks,jar,jpg,data,exe,vsd,itf,spl,keytab,xlsx,xlsm,kml,xps,woff,woff2,ttf,gpk,gdk,wmv,rmvb,mov,type,oft,crl,eml,mdi,mpp,rtf,rdb,pps,swf,mpg,chm,dwg,wps,psd,kmz,jfif,flv,xmind,vsdx,nic,shp,txt,cxv,json,yaml,tmf,rules,properties,groovy,sh,conf,ktr,kjb,ior,lookup,md,tb,asc,keytab,log,csv,tsv,kml,cer,crt,crl,rb,py,sql,ini,cfg,tmp,rpa,tfcpi

          Max. File Size (KB): indicates the maximum size of a file that can be uploaded or stored, in KB. The default value is 100, that is, 100 KB.

          Support Resend: indicates whether to preferentially submit ticket data and retransmit attachments later when attachments fail to be uploaded in Mateline scenarios.

         

       

       
        
         User

        
         user

        
         Model property of the user type.

       

       
        
         User Group

        
         user group

        
         Model property of the user group type.

       

       
        
         Password

        
         password

        
         Model property of the password type.

         
          AES: symmetric encryption algorithm. The encrypted data can be decrypted. This algorithm applies to scenarios where data needs to be decrypted and restored.

          PBKDF2: irreversible encryption algorithm with salt value encryption. The encrypted data cannot be decrypted. This algorithm applies to scenarios where data does not need to be decrypted and restored and provides higher security.

          SHA256: irreversible encryption algorithm without salt value encryption. The encrypted data cannot be decrypted. This algorithm applies to scenarios where data does not need to be decrypted and restored and has good performance.

         

       

       
        
         File List

        
         list:file

        
         Multiple groups of files.

         
          File Type: indicates the supported file name extension. Use commas (,) to separate multiple file name extensions, for example, zip,txt.

          Max. File Size (KB): indicates the maximum size of a file that can be uploaded or stored, in KB. The default value is 100, that is, 100 KB.

          Max. Number: indicates the maximum number of files that can be uploaded. This parameter can be set to a value less than or equal to 300. That is, a maximum of 300 files can be uploaded for a single field. Developers can perform evaluation based on the actual application scenarios and set proper constraints within the scope allowed by the platform.

          Support Resend: indicates whether to preferentially submit ticket data and retransmit attachments later when attachments fail to be uploaded in Mateline scenarios.

         

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Model Inheritance Capability Description

    Model inheritance: During model configuration, if you select an existing model as the parent model, the properties of the parent model are inherited by the current model (child model). The properties of the child model from the parent model cannot be modified. Properties of the parent model will be synchronized to the child model after being modified. Data created in the current model is also created in the parent model at the same time. For example, assume that model A exists and model B is inherited from model A when model B is created (in this case, all fields of model B are from model A). After model B is generated and a data record is created in model B, the same data record is also created in model A. The model inheritance rules are as follows:

    
     You can select a model as the parent model only when Allow Inheritance is set to Yes and Open level is configured for the model.

     The primary key or unique index field of the parent model is of the auto increment or date time sequence type and cannot be inherited.

     A child model inherits all fields from its parent model. The type and constraints of the inherited fields cannot be modified, and additional primary key fields cannot be created for the child model.

     If a field is added to the parent model, this field is automatically added to the child model. If the field to be added to the parent model already exists in the child model, the field cannot be added to the child model.

     If a field is deleted from the parent model, this field is automatically deleted from the child model.

     If a field of a parent model is modified, the corresponding field of the child model is automatically modified.

     Models with sub-models cannot be deactivated or deleted.

     During sub-model export, only the property fields that belong to the sub-model are exported.
      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Model Configuration

text:
Creating a Data Model (Form Mode)
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to create a data model in form mode.

   
    Context

    Different from the canvas mode in which developers orchestrate elements using drag-and-drop operations, the form mode enables developers to create models by setting property fields.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Access the module to be operated. If there is only one module, it will be accessed by default. If there are multiple modules, manually select a module.
      

      
       Figure 1 Selecting a module
       
      

      

     Choose Model.

     On the model list page, click Create to create a data model.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Model Name

          
           The model name has a fixed module prefix. You only need to define the name other than the prefix. The value can contain lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_), and must start with a letter. The value cannot be changed after being submitted.

         

         
          
           Display Name

          
           This parameter is used for WebUI display and can be set to a name that is easy to understand.

         

         
          
           Model Type

          
           
            Data Model: indicates the new relational database model planned in the system.

            Data Source Model: indicates the model used for external data source access. For existing data models, data sources can be selected through data source models.

            Elastic Model: indicates the distributed data model, which is used to store and manage large-scale data. This model can store data replicas of other models and archive data of other models.

           

           Select Data Model.

         

         
          
           Open Level

          
           Open level of a model.

           
            Public: indicates that the model is public and can be used within the system.

            Project: indicates that the model can be used within a project. When there are multiple modules in the project, the model can also be used within the project modules.

            Module: indicates that the model can be used within a module.

           

         

         
          
           Allow Customization

          
           Whether a model can be customized during project customization.

         

         
          
           Allow Inheritance

          
           Whether to allow other models to inherit the model.

         

         
          
           Inherited Model

          
           
            Whether the model inherits other models. To inherit other models, select the inherited model from the drop-down list.
             
              The models can be displayed in the Inherited Model drop-down list only when Allow Inheritance is enabled and the models allowed in Open Level are visible to the current model.

              The maximum inheritance depth of a model is five layers.

             

            If other models do not need to be inherited, do not select this option.

           

         

         
          
           Permission Items

          
           Operations on models can be controlled based on permission items.

           
            Meta Data can be queried by the frontend: Metadata refers to the model definition data. If this permission switch is toggled on, frontend page components (such as TQL components) can use this model to query model metadata.

            Data can be queried by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be queried directly through frontend components.
             For example, the Dropdown component can be used to obtain the value of a field in a model.

            Data can be created by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be created directly through frontend components.

            Data can be modified by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be modified directly through frontend components.

            Data can be deleted by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be deleted directly through frontend components.

           

           These permission items do not need to be enabled when data is added, deleted, modified, or queried through services. They need to be enabled only when metadata or data is accessed directly through the WebUI.

         

         
          
           Permission

          
           When the switch is toggled on, the corresponding permission items are enabled. Therefore, you need to configure the permission items bound to the permission.

           
            If no permission item is configured, all roles can access the model.

            If a specific permission item is configured, only the role with this permission item can access the model.

           

           The corresponding permission items need to be configured after choosing Permission. For details, see Configuring Permissions and Roles.

         

         
          
           Estimated Rows

          
           Select a value based on the enumerated value.

           During quality check, you can determine whether to check low-efficient SQL statements based on the number of estimated lines.

         

         
          
           Default Fields

          
           Select the fields to be preset in the model. The name of a default field cannot be changed.

         

         
          
           Desensitize Switch

          
           After Desensitize Switch is enabled, you can configure desensitization policies for properties in the Property Settings area.

           After a desensitization policy is selected for a property, the policy is used to desensitize model property values in model logs, including O&M logs, operation logs, and backend logs.

         

        
       
      

      

     In the Property Settings area, click Add to add a property and configure the property information. The property name cannot be set to a reserved word. For details about reserved words, see Reserved Words of the Model Property Name.
      

      
       Configure property constraints. In the new property row, click the empty text box in the Property Restriction column. In the displayed dialog box, configure property constraints.
        
         Figure 2 Property Restriction
         
        

        Each property has a different property constraint. For details, see Model Overview.

       Configure a property desensitization policy. The configuration is available when Desensitize Switch is enabled. During log recording, the system desensitizes only the property values for which a desensitization policy is selected. Generally, sensitive information, such as properties related to users' personal data, needs to be desensitized.
        The options in the desensitization policy drop-down list come from the app-level data desensitization policy configuration. For details, see Configuring a Project Desensitization Policy.

        Desensitization policies cannot be configured for model primary key fields and fields added from Default Fields.

      

      

     Click Confirm.

     After a model is created, click Generate Now to generate services and pages for adding, deleting, modifying, or querying model data. For details about the capabilities of the generated services and pages, see Configuring Models to Automatically Generate Services and Pages.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After a data model is created, the model is enabled by default. You can perform more management operations on the model.

    
     Model disabling and enabling: In the model list, choose More > Disable Model in the Operation column of a model to disable the model. A disabled model can be enabled again.

     Model cache: used to store configuration data that is not frequently changed. You can select Enable Caching from the Operation column for this type of data.
      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Configuring a Data Model

title: Creating a Data Model (Canvas Mode)
text:
Creating a Data Model (Canvas Mode)
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to create a data model on the canvas.

   
    Context

    The Model page consists of the element orchestration area on the left, canvas area in the middle, and configuration area on the right. You can drag elements on the left to the canvas area in the middle and modify the detailed information on the right.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Access the module to be operated. If there is only one module, it will be accessed by default. If there are multiple modules, manually select a module.
      

      
       Figure 1 Selecting a module
       
      

      

     Choose Model.

     Click Canvas.

     Click Enter Edit Mode to edit the canvas.

     Create a data model.
      

      
       Drag the Data Model element from the element area on the left to the canvas in the middle.

       In the Create Model dialog box, set the basic model information. 
        
         
          
           Table 1 Parameter description
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Model Name

            
             The model name has a fixed module prefix. You only need to define the name other than the prefix. The value can contain lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_), and must start with a letter. The value cannot be changed after being submitted.

           

           
            
             Display Name

            
             This parameter is used for WebUI display and can be set to a name that is easy to understand.

           

           
            
             Model Type

            
             
              Data Model: indicates the new relational database model planned in the system.

              Data Source Model: indicates the model used for external data source access. For existing data models, data sources can be selected through data source models.

              Elastic Model: indicates the distributed data model, which is used to store and manage large-scale data. This model can store data replicas of other models and archive data of other models.

             

             Select Data Model.

           

           
            
             Permission Items

            
             Operations on models can be controlled based on permission items.

             
              Meta Data can be queried by the frontend: Metadata refers to the model definition data. If this permission switch is toggled on, frontend page components (such as TQL components) can use this model to query model metadata.

              Data can be queried by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be queried directly through frontend components.
               For example, the Dropdown component can be used to obtain the value of a field in a model.

              Data can be created by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be created directly through frontend components.

              Data can be modified by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be modified directly through frontend components.

              Data can be deleted by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be deleted directly through frontend components.

             

             These permission items do not need to be enabled when data is added, deleted, modified, or queried through services. They need to be enabled only when metadata or data is accessed directly through the WebUI.

           

           
            
             Permission

            
             When the switch is toggled on, the corresponding permission items are enabled. Therefore, you need to configure the permission items bound to the permission.

             
              If no permission item is configured, all roles can access the model.

              If a specific permission item is configured, only the role with this permission item can access the model.

             

             The corresponding permission items need to be configured after choosing Permission. For details, see Configuring Permissions and Roles.

           

           
            
             Desensitize Switch

            
             After Desensitize Switch is enabled, you can configure desensitization policies for properties in the Property Settings area.

             After a desensitization policy is selected for a property, the policy is used to desensitize model property values in model logs, including O&M logs, operation logs, and backend logs.

           

           
            
             Open Level

            
             Open level of a model.

             
              Public: indicates that the model is public and can be used by a specific tenant.

              Project: indicates that the model can be used within a project. When there are multiple modules in the project, the model can also be used within the project modules.

              Module: indicates that the menu can be used within a module.

             

           

           
            
             Allow Customization

            
             Whether a model can be customized during project customization.

           

           
            
             Allow Inheritance

            
             Whether to allow other models to inherit the model.

           

           
            
             Inherited Model

            
             
              Whether the model inherits other models. To inherit other models, select the inherited model from the drop-down list.
               
                The models can be displayed in the Inherited Model drop-down list only when Allow Inheritance is enabled and the models allowed in Open Level are visible to the current model.

                The maximum inheritance depth of a model is five layers.

               

              If other models do not need to be inherited, do not select this option.

             

           

           
            
             Estimated Rows

            
             Select a value based on the enumerated value.

             During quality check, you can determine whether to check low-efficient SQL statements based on the number of estimated lines.

           

           
            
             Default Field

       Click  on the canvas to save the settings.

Modifying a Data Model
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    After a model is created in the develop-state environment, you can modify the model on the develop-state page. For example, the property display name of a model can be modified after the model is created, but the property name of a model cannot be modified after the model is created.

    After a model is created in the runtime state, you can modify the model in the runtime state through upgrade after the application is deployed.

    The constraints in the develop-state environment are different from those in the runtime-state environment. When the modification in the develop-state environment is not allowed in the runtime-state environment, the app upgrade may fail in the runtime-state environment.
