name: Configuring a Sharding Policy for the Data Model
title: Configuring a Sharding Policy for the Data Model
text:
Configuring a Sharding Policy for the Data Model
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    You have configured a data model.

   

   
    Context

    Data in a data model is divided into shards based on the value range of a property. Each data model shard is stored in different physical structures (such as MySQL and GaussDB databases). In this way, each physical structure can store a large amount of data in a single model, without undermining the performance.

    After a data model shard is configured, archived data can be deleted based on shard, which improves data deletion efficiency.

    When configuring a sharding policy for the data model, pay attention to the following restrictions:

    
     In the data model for which a sharding policy is to be configured, unique indexes are not supported.

     In the data model for which a sharding policy is to be configured, the primary key of the model can only be the sequence type and multiple primary keys are not supported.

     The data model for which a sharding policy is to be configured does not support the model inheritance function.

     After an app is deployed in the runtime-state environment, you can view the sharding policies of the deployed app on the Products and Services > Administration > Model Management > Shard Policy page but cannot modify the sharding policies in the runtime-state environment.

     After sharding policies are configured, hot deployment to the runtime-state environment is not supported. You need to manually deploy these sharding policies.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Select the module to be operated.

     Choose Model.

     In the row of the data model for which you want to configure a sharding policy, click Manage.

     Choose Shard Policy in the navigation pane, and configure information about the sharding policy.
      

      
       
        
         
          Table 1 Parameter description
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Parameter

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Shard Property

           
            Model property that is used as the sharding property. That is, data is stored in different data shards according to the interval rule of the property value.

            The supported sharding properties of a data model are as follows:

            
             change_time

             _created_time

            

          

          
           
            Shard Period

           
            Set this parameter based on the type of the sharding property.

            
             If the configured sharding property is of the Date and Time type, the sharding period is a time period. Currently, the following values are supported:
              
               One Day

               Seven Days

               Thirty Days

              

              Too many shards will affect the query performance. You are advised to set Shard Period to Thirty Days or a greater value. If Shard Period is set to a small value, the number of shards may be too large. In this case, you can configure shard-based data archiving to reduce the number of shards.

             If the configured sharding property is of the Integer type, the sharding period is a numeric value.

            

          

         
        
       

      

      

     Click Confirm.

     After the configuration is complete, select the sharding policy–based archiving mode during the archiving mode configuration of a data model. For details, see Independent Model Archiving Configuration.
      

      For sharding policies of data models, the following restrictions need to be met: These sharding policies can be used only when independent model archiving is selected; only Retention Day(s) can be set; values of Reserved Row(s) and Data Filter Condition cannot be changed; Archiving Target can only be set to Delete or Dump File Server.

name: Configuring Model Indexes
title: Configuring Model Indexes
text:
Configuring Model Indexes
 
 
  
  

  
   After models are added, you can add indexes to improve model data query efficiency.

   
    Context

    Restrictions on model index configuration:

    
     Indexes can be created only for data models and workflow agent models. Indexes cannot be created for data source models and elastic models.

     Composite indexes are supported. A maximum of five properties can be added to a single index.

     Indexes cannot be created for the following properties: password, user list, user group list, file list, reference list, and enumeration list.

     Indexes cannot be created for primary keys and default fields.

     The model index name must be unique in a single model.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Access the module to be operated. If there is only one module, it will be accessed by default. If there are multiple modules, manually select a module.
      

      
       Figure 1 Selecting a module
       
      

      

     Choose Model.

     (Form mode) In the displayed list, choose More > Model Index in the row where the model needs to be set.

     (Canvas mode) In the canvas area, click  of the model for which you want to set an index and click Model Index.

     Click Create.

     Set the index information, as shown in Figure 2.
      

      
       Figure 2 Creating a property index
       
      

      
       
        
         
          Table 1 Parameters
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Parameter

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Index Name

           
            The index name must start with a lowercase letter and can contain only lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_).

          

          
           
            Property Name

           
            Select a property from the drop-down list box as the index. Properties for which indexes cannot be created are automatically shielded from the drop-down list box.

          

          
           
            Index Type

           
            Index type.

            
             Unique index: The property data used as the index must be unique.

             Ordinary index: The property data used as an index does not need to be unique.

            

          

         
        
       

      

      

     Click Create to submit the information.

name: Creating a Data Source Model (Based on System Data Sources)
title: Creating a Data Source Model (Based on System Data Sources)
text:
Creating a Data Source Model (Based on System Data Sources)
 
 
  
  

  
   System data sources refer to the data sources that can be managed in the ADC system.

   
    Context

    
     
      The table of a data source model is not created by ADC but by external systems or services. The table structure is not defined by ADC. Therefore, the data source model does not support index configuration.

     
      The table location of the data source model is as follows:

      
       
        The table can be in the default data source of the tenant, but the table name must start with t_rt_app_ds_ or t_rt_mod_ds_. Such models correspond to fixed table models of the historical version.

       
        The table can be in the data source configured by the tenant administrator but the data source cannot be the same as that configured by the system administrator. The table name is not limited. Such models correspond to data source models of the historical version.

      

     
      The table data corresponding to the data source model can be directly operated in the database by external systems or services. For example, when an external system or a service directly operates the data in the database:

      
       
        If the model data cache is enabled for the model, the cached data may be inconsistent with the data in the database.

       
        The trigger is not triggered. In the future, the interface for triggering triggers will be opened to external systems. External systems or services need to call this interface to trigger triggers.

      

     
      The table name of the data source model and the field name corresponding to the property can be specified during development.

    

    
     
      Currently, fields of the binary type are not supported.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Access the module to be operated. If there is only one module, it will be accessed by default. If there are multiple modules, manually select a module.
      

      
       Figure 1 Selecting a module
       
      

      

     Choose Model.

     Create a data source model. Click Create and set the basic information about the model.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Model Name

          
           The model name has a fixed module prefix. You only need to define the name other than the prefix.

         

         
          
           Display Name

          
           This parameter is used for WebUI display and can be set to a name that is easy to understand.

         

         
          
           Model Type

          
           
            Data Model: indicates the new relational database model planned in the system.

            Data Source Model: indicates the model used for external data source access. For existing data models, data sources can be selected through data source models.

            Elastic Model: indicates the distributed data model, which is used to store and manage large-scale data. This model can store data replicas of other models and archive data of other models.

           

         

         
          
           Open Level

          
           Open level of a model.

           
            Public: indicates that the model is public and can be used by a specific tenant.

            Project: indicates that the model can be used within a project. When there are multiple modules in the project, the model can also be used within the project modules.

            Module: Indicates that the model can be used within a module.

           

         

         
          
           Datasource Type

          
           
            External Datasource: indicates the external data source accessed through data interworking.

            System Datasource: indicates the data source managed in the system.

           

         

         
          
           Default Fields

          
           Select the fields to be preset in the model.

         

         
          
           Data Source Name

          
           Database where the table that functions as the data source model is located. Select a value from the drop-down list.

           
            Default data source: When a tenant is initialized, the default data source of the tenant is allocated. Default data source corresponds to the fixed table model of the historical versions.

            Extra Data Source: Each tenant can add extra data sources. Extra Data Source corresponds to the data source model of the historical versions. If this parameter is set to Extra Data Source, you need to set Label Value to specify the data source added by the tenant.

           

         

         
          
           Table Name

          
           
            When Data Source Name is set to Default data source, the table name must start with t_rt_app_ds_ or t_rt_mod_ds_.

            When Data Source Name is set to Extra Data Source, the table name can be customized to any value.

           

         

         
          
           Permission Items

          
           Operations on models can be controlled based on permission items.

           
            Meta Data can be queried by the frontend: Metadata refers to the model definition data. If this permission switch is toggled on, frontend page components (such as TQL components) can use this model to query model metadata.

            Data can be queried by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be queried directly through frontend components.
             For example, the Dropdown component can be used to obtain the value of a field in a model.

            Data can be created by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be created directly through frontend components.

            Data can be modified by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be modified directly through frontend components.

            Data can be deleted by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be deleted directly through frontend components.

           

           These permission items do not need to be enabled when data is added, deleted, modified, or queried through services. They need to be enabled only when metadata or data is accessed directly through the WebUI.

         

         
          
           Permission

          
           When the switch is toggled on, the corresponding permission items are enabled. Therefore, you need to configure the permission items bound to the permission.

           
            If no permission item is configured, all roles can access the model.

            If a specific permission item is configured, only the role with this permission item can access the model.

           

           The corresponding permission items need to be configured after choosing Permission. For details, see Configuring Permissions and Roles.

         

         
          
           Estimated Number of Rows

          
           Select a value based on the enumerated value.

           During quality check, you can determine whether to check low-efficient SQL statements based on the number of estimated lines.

         

         
          
           Desensitize Switch

          
           After Desensitize Switch is enabled, you can configure desensitization policies for properties in the Property Settings area.

           After a desensitization policy is selected for a property, the policy is used to desensitize model property values in model logs, including O&M logs, operation logs, and backend logs.

         

         
          
           Property Settings

          
           Click Obtain the table structure to obtain field information from the physical table. In addition, model properties can be configured directly.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Confirm.

text:
Creating a Data Source Model (Based on External Data Sources)
 
 
  
  

  
   External data sources refer to the data sources that are not managed in the ADC system.

   
    Context

    In the data visualization screen scenario or a scenario where a large amount of data exists, developers have to process complex existing data. By using external data sources, developers can effectively manage data in the ADC system at a low cost and develop apps based on the data.

    Developers can manage data sources on the Products and Services > Administration > Model Management > Model External Data Source Management page in the runtime-state environment.

    After a model consisting of external data sources is created, developers can select the automatic generation of services and pages based on the model and add, delete, modify, and query data in the external data sources.

    The restrictions on using external data sources are as follows:

    
     Data model archiving is not supported.

     Indexes cannot be configured.

     Data synchronization configuration is not supported.

     Currently, only GaussDB, MySQL, and PostgreSQL data sources are supported.

     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Access the module to be operated. If there is only one module, it will be accessed by default. If there are multiple modules, manually select a module.

           Set this parameter to the name of the external data source configured in the runtime-state environment.

           Set this parameter to the name of the table in the data source.

         

         
          
           Enable Automatic Table Creation

          
           After this function is enabled, a data table is automatically created if no data table exists in the data source. If a data table exists in the data source, you can add or delete model fields. However, the field type cannot be changed.

            If no permission item is configured, all roles can access the model.

name: Creating an Elastic Model
title: Creating an Elastic Model
text:
Creating an Elastic Model
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    The elastic model is a distributed data model, used to store and manage large-scale data. This model can store data replicas of other models and archive data of other models.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Access the module to be operated. If there is only one module, it will be accessed by default. If there are multiple modules, manually select a module.
      

      
       Figure 1 Selecting a module
       
      

      

     Choose Model.

     Click Create, create an elastic model, and set the basic model information.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Model Name

          
           The model name has a fixed module prefix. You only need to define the name other than the prefix. The value can contain lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_), and must start with a letter. The value cannot be changed after being submitted.

         

         
          
           Display Name

          
           This parameter is used for WebUI display and can be set to a name that is easy to understand.

         

         
          
           Model Type

          
           
            Data Model: indicates the new relational database model planned in the system.

            Data Source Model: indicates the model used for external data source access. For existing data models, data sources can be selected through data source models.

            Elastic Model: indicates the distributed data model, which is used to store and manage large-scale data. This model can store data replicas of other models and archive data of other models.

           

           Select Elastic Model.

         

         
          
           Open Level

          
           Open level of a model.

           
            Public: indicates that the model is public and can be used by a specific tenant.

            Project: indicates that the model can be used within a project. When there are multiple modules in the project, the model can also be used within the project modules.

            Module: indicates that the model can be used within a module.

           

         

         
          
           Update Interval (s)

          
           The default value is 5. You can set this parameter to –1 (indicating no update) or an integer ranging from 5 to 3600.

         

         
          
           Source Model

          
           
            This parameter needs to be set when the elastic model to be created is a replica of another model.
             For example, if the data model A is configured and the new elastic model B is a replica of the model A, set Source Model to the data model A. The properties of the data model A are automatically used as the properties of the elastic model B.

            This parameter does not need to be set when the new elastic model is used for only data storage and management and is not a replica of another model.

           

         

         
          
           Synchronize the metadata model structure

          
           This parameter is displayed only when Source Model is set.

           If this parameter is enabled, all properties of the current elastic model are synchronized from the source model. You do not need to manage properties in the elastic model. The source model modification, such as property addition to the source model, is synchronized to the current elastic model.

         

         
          
           Data Synchronization

          
           This parameter is displayed only when Synchronize the metadata model structure is enabled.

           If this parameter is enabled, data of the current elastic model is automatically synchronized from the source model. All addition, deletion, and modification operations on data instances of the source model are continuously synchronized.

           The elastic model with data synchronization enabled cannot be used as the target model of the dump elastic model.

         

         
          
           Compression Type

          
           Algorithm used for compression.

           
            Default mode: The default compression algorithm of Elasticsearch is used. This algorithm is recommended because of its more stable data query and write performance, but it occupies a large amount of disk space.

            Efficient mode: The efficient compression algorithm (best_compression) specified by Elasticsearch is used. This algorithm has a higher compression ratio but a lower data query and write performance.

           

           After the model is created, this parameter cannot be modified.

         

         
          
           Permission Items

          
           Operations on models can be controlled based on permission items.

           
            Meta Data can be queried by the frontend: Metadata refers to the model definition data. If this permission switch is toggled on, frontend page components (such as TQL components) can use this model to query model metadata.

            Data can be queried by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be queried directly through frontend components.
             For example, the Dropdown component can be used to obtain the value of a field in a model.

            Data can be created by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be created directly through frontend components.

            Data can be modified by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be modified directly through frontend components.

            Data can be deleted by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be deleted directly through frontend components.

           

           These permission items do not need to be enabled when data is added, deleted, modified, or queried through services. They need to be enabled only when metadata or data is accessed directly through the WebUI.

         

         
          
           Permission

          
           When the switch is toggled on, the corresponding permission items are enabled. Therefore, you need to configure the permission items bound to the permission.

           
            If no permission item is configured, all roles can access the model.

            If a specific permission item is configured, only the role with this permission item can access the model.

           

           The corresponding permission items need to be configured after choosing Permission. For details, see Configuring Permissions and Roles.

         

         
          
           Estimated Rows

          
           Select a value based on the enumerated value.

           During quality check, you can determine whether to check low-efficient SQL statements based on the number of estimated lines.

         

         
          
           Desensitize Switch

          
           After Desensitize Switch is enabled, you can configure desensitization policies for properties in the Property Settings area.

           After a desensitization policy is selected for a property, the policy is used to desensitize model property values in model logs, including O&M logs, operation logs, and backend logs.

         

         
          
           Fixed Column

          
           If Fixed Column is enabled, the Elasticsearch index of the model will reuse the index field with the same name as the property. If the index or index field does not exist, the index field with the same name as the property will be created.

         

         
          
           Parameter Configuration

          
           Parameter configuration of the elastic model. For details, see Table 3.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click OK.

name: Configuring a Sharding Policy for Elastic Models
title: Configuring a Sharding Policy for Elastic Models
text:
Configuring a Sharding Policy for Elastic Models
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    You have configured an elastic model.

   

   
    Context

    Data in an elastic model is divided into shards based on the value range of a property. Each elastic model shard is stored in different physical structures (such as MySQL and Elasticsearch indexes). By using filter criteria of data operations, each physical structure can store a large amount of data in a single model, without undermining the performance.

    The elastic model is used for large-scale data management, data archiving, and data replication. Therefore, data scalability and query performance must be considered. The proper sharding policy can improve the query performance of the elastic model.

    After sharding policies are configured, hot deployment to the runtime-state environment is not supported. You need to manually deploy these sharding policies.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Select the module to be operated.

     Choose Model.

     In the row of the elastic model for which you want to configure a sharding policy, click Manage.

     Choose Shard Policy in the navigation pane, and configure information about the sharding policy.
      

      
       Configuring the sharding property of the Numeric type
        

       Configuring the sharding property of the Date and Time type
        
         
         
          
           
            Table 1 Parameter description
           
           
            
            
           
           
            
             
              Parameter

             
              Description

            

           
           
            
             
              Shard Property

             
              A model property, the value range rules of which are used as criteria for storing data into different data shards.

              In the elastic model, mandatory properties of the Date and Time type or Integer type can be used as sharding properties. The configuration items of the two types of properties are different.

            

            
             
              Shard Period

             
              Set this parameter based on the type of the sharding property.

              
               If the configured sharding property is of the Date and Time type, the sharding period is a time period. Currently, the following values are supported:
                
                 One Day

                 One Week

                 One Month

                 One Quarter

                 One Year

                

                Too many shards will affect the query performance. You are advised to set Shard Period to One Month or a greater value. If Shard Period is set to a small value, the number of shards may be too large. In this case, you can configure shard-based data archiving to reduce the number of shards.

               If the configured sharding property is of the Integer type, the sharding period is a numeric value.

              

            

            
             
              Shard Property As Timestamp

             
              For the property of the Integer type, an integer can be used as a timestamp in some service scenarios. Configure different sharding modes depending on whether the sharding property is a timestamp.

              
               Non-Timestamp

               Second

               Milliseconds

              

            

            
             
              Automatically Create Shard

             
              This parameter needs to be configured when the value of Shard Property is of the Date and Time type and Shard Property As Timestamp is set to Second or Milliseconds.

            

            
             
              Automatically Create Shard Period

             
              This parameter needs to be configured only when Automatically Create Shard is set to Yes.

              For example, if the value of Shard Property is of Integer type and is a timestamp, the automatic shard creation is selected, and Automatically Create Shard Period is set to Month, the shard is generated one month in advance after the one-click deployment.

            

           
          
         

        

      

      

     Click Confirm.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Configuring an Elastic Model

text:
Configuring a Vector Model
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to configure a vector model.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     Vector library resources have been configured for the master tenant, and the resources that can be used by service tenants have been specified.

     Embedding models have been configured for service tenants to specify embeddings in vector models.

          Table 2 Parameter description

            Description

            Name of a model. The name has a fixed module prefix. You need to define the name other than the prefix. The value can contain lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_), and must start with a letter. The value cannot be changed after the model is created.

             Public: indicates that the model is public and can be used by any tenant.

             Project: indicates that the model can be used within a project. If your project has multiple modules, the model can be used within the project modules.

             Module: Indicates that the model can be used within a module.

             Data can be queried by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be queried directly through frontend components.

             Data can be modified by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be modified directly through frontend components.

             Data can be deleted by the frontend: If this permission switch is toggled on, model data can be deleted directly through frontend components.

            

            These permission items do not need to be enabled when data is added, deleted, modified, or queried through services. They need to be enabled only when metadata or data is accessed directly through the WebUI.

          

          
           
            Permission

           
            When the switch is toggled on, the corresponding permission items are enabled. Therefore, you need to configure the permission items bound to the permission.

            
             If no permission item is configured, all roles can access the model.

             If a specific permission item is configured, only the role with this permission item can access the model.

            

            The corresponding permission items need to be configured after choosing Permission. For details, see Configuring Permissions and Roles.

          

          
           
            Estimated Number of Rows

           
            Estimated number of rows for quality check. Select a value based on the enumerated value.

            During quality check, you can determine whether to check low-efficient SQL statements based on the number of estimated rows.

          

          
           
            Desensitize Switch

           
            After Desensitize Switch is enabled, you can configure desensitization policies for properties in the Property Settings area.

            After a desensitization policy is selected for a property, the policy is used to desensitize model property values in model logs, including O&M logs, operation logs, and backend logs.

          

          
           
            Property Settings

           
            Parameter configuration of the vector model. For details, see Table 3.

            Vectorization: Each model can be configured with up to three fields for vectorization. Only text fields can be vectorized. Vectorized fields cannot be configured as primary keys.

    Independent Model Archiving Configuration
      For models that do not have dependencies or models depended on the root node, archive them independently. This section describes how to configure independent archiving.

title: Introduction to Model Archiving
text:
Introduction to Model Archiving
 
 
  
  

  
   The system allows you to archive a single model or associated models at a specified time. Archived models can be deleted or dumped.

   
    Model Archiving

    Data models, elastic models, and data source models where default data sources are used support the archiving capability. Data source models where extra data sources are used do not support the archiving capability.

    Model archiving supports the following archiving objectives:

    
     Delete: Data is deleted. If the archived data contains files or file list, files will be deleted.

     Dump Elastic Model: Data is archived to the configured elastic model.

     Dump File Server: Files are archived using the file service.

     Dump SFTP Server: Data is archived to the SFTP server.

    

    
     
      
       Table 1 Archiving capabilities of different models
      
      
       
       
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Model Type

        
         Archiving Target: Delete

        
         Archiving Target: Dump Elastic Model

        
         Archiving Target: Dump File Server

        
         Archiving Target: Dump SFTP Server

       

      
      
       
        
         Data model

        
         Supported

        
         Supported

        
         Supported

        
         Supported

       

       
        
         Elastic model

        
         Supported

        
         Not supported

        
         Supported

        
         Supported

       

       
        
         Data source model

         (default data sources)

        
         Supported

        
         Supported

        
         Supported

        
         Supported

       

      
     
    

    Models can be archived in either of the following methods:

    
     Independent: Used to archive a single model or as the root node model of the dependency tree.

     Associated: Used to archive associated models based on other models.

    

    As shown in the following figure, models B and C depend on model A. If only model A is archived, an error occurs when you query the data of model B and C depended on archived model A. Therefore, you need to configure associated archiving for models B and C. When model A is archived independently, models B and C need to be archived together. Because model D does not depend on other models, archive it independently.

    
     Figure 1 Model diagram
     
    

    If the model uses the database sharding function and the current model is a data model in the model archiving scenario, dependency relationships can be configured only between only data models, data source models, and proxy models in the same schema of the same database.

   

   
    Data Source Model Archiving

    In default data source scenario, when data source models are associated and archived, the associated and archived data source models must be in the same data source.

    Data source models where extra data sources are used do not support the archiving capability.

   

   
    Elastic Model Archiving

    The archiving granularity can be configured for elastic models. By default, data models and data source models are archived by data. However, elastic models support shard configuration and can be archived by shard or data.

    
     Archiving by shard applies only to the scenario where a single model is independently archived. Currently, this function is not applicable to associated archiving (including archiving with other models and triggering archiving of other models).

     Archiving data by shard applies only to models sharded by time. That is, the shard property must be of the date and time type, timestamp type, or integer type and be set to timestamp.

    

    The elastic model supports associated archiving. An elastic model can be archived only by using its dependency relationships. For example, when A depends on B, if A or B is an elastic model, the other must also be an elastic model.

   

   
    Introduction to Proxy Model Archiving

    Data models can depend on proxy models and can be archived with proxy models.

title: Independent Model Archiving Configuration
text:
Independent Model Archiving Configuration
 
 
  
  

  
   For models that do not have dependencies or models depended on the root node, archive them independently. This section describes how to configure independent archiving.

   
    Prerequisites

    You have created a data model.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Select the module to be operated.

     Choose Model.

     (Form) Select the model to be operated, click Manage Model.

     (Canvas) Click Canvas, click Enter Edit Mode, click  next to the model to be archived, and choose Manage Model.

     On the displayed pane, choose Archiving Configuration. On the displayed page, configure the model archiving information.
      

      

      
       
       
        
         
          Table 1 Model archiving parameters
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Parameter

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Archiving Type

           
            
             Independent: Used to archive a single model or as the root node model of the dependency tree.

             Associated: Used to archive associated models based on other models.

            

          

          
           
            Enable Type

           
            This field is displayed only when Archiving Type is set to Independent.

            
             Enable Now

             Enable Later

            

          

          
           
            Archiving Granularity

           
            If this parameter is set to Shard, you need to configure the sharding policy. Otherwise, archiving cannot be performed. For details about how to configure the sharding policy, see Configuring a Sharding Policy for Elastic Models and Configuring a Sharding Policy for the Data Model.

          

          
           
            Retention Day(s)

           
            This field is displayed only when Archiving Type is set to Independent.

            
             On the Archiving Configuration page of the data model and data source model, either Retention Day(s) or Reserved Row(s) must be set. If Retention Day(s) and Retention Row(s) are set and the filter criteria are met, the data with more archived data is used.

             On the Archiving Configuration page of the elastic model, Retention Day(s) is mandatory.

            

          

          
           
            Reserved Row(s)

           
            This field is displayed only when Archiving Type is set to Independent.

            
             On the Archiving Configuration page of the data model and data source model, either Retention Day(s) or Reserved Row(s) must be set. If Retention Day(s) and Retention Row(s) are set and the filter criteria are met, the data with more archived data is used.

             This parameter is not displayed on the Archiving Configuration page of the elastic model.

            

          

          
           
            Minimum Retention Day(s)

           
            This field is displayed only when Archiving Type is set to Independent.

            In the runtime state, the configured minimum retention days must be greater than the configured minimum retention days. This parameter is not displayed on the Archiving Configuration page of the elastic model.

          

          
           
            Minimum Retention Row(s)

           
            This field is displayed only when Archiving Type is set to Independent.

            In the runtime state, the configured minimum retention days must be greater than the configured minimum retention days.

          

          
           
            Data Filter Condition

           
            This field is displayed only when Archiving Type is set to Independent. Archiving is performed when criteria are met.

          

          
           
            Archiving Target

           
            
             Delete: Delete data.

             Dump Elastic Model: Data is archived to the configured elastic model. You can configure the target elastic model and property mapping.

             Dump File Server: Data is archived to the default file server of ADC by using the file service. In this case, you can set File Retention Day(s). If the file storage duration exceeds the configured value, the file is deleted. Within the retention period, you can retrieve the file from the file server. The file storage path can be obtained from the t_rt_mod_archive_file table.

             Dump SFTP Server: Data is archived to the SFTP server. You can configure the SFTP server and the path for storing the data. You can customize the SFTP server and archiving path in the runtime-state environment.

            

          

          
           
            Target Model

           
            This field is displayed when Archiving Target is set to Dump Elastic Model.

          

          
           
            Mapping Mode

           
            This field is displayed when Archiving Target is set to Dump Elastic Model.

            
             Custom: Manually add the mapping between the fields of the current model and those of the target model.

             Auto: Automatically add the mapping between the fields based on the model property name.

            

          

         
        
       

      

      

    

    
     Click Save.

     Configure a dependency. If a model that is independently archived is no dependencies, you do not need to configure a dependency for the model. If the root node of a dependency is depended by other models, you can also configure a dependency for these models.
      

      
       
        
         Table 2 Parameters of a dependency
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Property Name

          
           Select a property in the current model.

         

         
          
           Dependency

          
           Depended by: Configure only the depended relationship between the current model and the target model for archiving independent models.

         

         
          
           Target Model

          
           Configure a target model with a dependency relationship.

         

         
          
           Target Property

          
           Select a property in the target model.

         

        
       
      

      If a dependency of the current model is configured, you can also view the dependency in the target model. For example, if model B depends on model A, a message indicating that model B depends on model A is automatically displayed in model B. In this case, you do not need to configure the dependency again.

name: Configuring Models to Automatically Generate Services and Pages
title: Configuring Models to Automatically Generate Services and Pages
text:
Configuring Models to Automatically Generate Services and Pages
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    Services and pages can be automatically generated based on models. After the generation, if the model is updated, the updates will not be automatically synchronized to the generated services and pages. You need to manually adjust the pages and services or automatically generate the pages and services again.

    If you have decided to generate services and pages during the model creation, skip this section when the model is not modified.

    Services and pages can be generated in either of the following modes:

    
     Generating services automatically: The services, pages, and mobile pages can be automatically generated. To add, delete, modify, or query data on the page, you can call the corresponding service.
      The services have the logic orchestration capability and can translate and convert input and output parameters. For details about the services, see Configuring Services.

      When a service is called on the page, the parameters transferred from the page are used as the input parameters for data addition, deletion, modification, or query.

     Using built-in model services: Only pages are generated. Data operations are not performed using the independent addition, deletion, modification, or query service but by calling the built-in addition, deletion, modification, or query service of a model on the WebUI.
      When built-in model services are used, complex processing, such as translation and conversion of input and output parameters, is not required when you add, delete, modify, or query data in the model.

      When a built-in model service is called on the page, the parameters transferred from the page are used as the input parameters of the built-in service for data addition, deletion, modification, or query.

      Table 1 lists the core differences between the two modes.

      
       
       
        
         Table 1 Differences
        
        
         
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Difference Analysis Item

          
           Service

          
           Built-in Model Service

         

        
        
         
          
           Acceptable to data orchestration and modification

          
           For automatically generated services, the input and output parameters and logic of the services can be adjusted and modified.

          
           For built-in model services, the addition, deletion, modification, or query service cannot be modified again.

         

         
          
           Address format

          
           Format: /adc-service/rest/v1/services/{project}/{module}/{service}

           Example:

           /adc-service/rest/v1/services/equipment/equipment/equipment_baseinfo_get_list

          
           Format:

           /adc-model/web/rest/v1/model-services/{project}/{module}/{model}/{operation}

           Example:

           /adc-model/web/rest/v1/model-services/equipment/equipment/equipment_baseinfo/get_list

         

         
          
           Microservice that is depended

          
           adc-service

          
           adc-model

         

         
          
           Permission control

          
           You can set the permission control mode and permission items during automatic service generation. The permission items can be modified one by one in the service.

          
           You can set the frontend access permission items during model configuration.

         

        
       
      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Access the module to be operated. If there is only one module, it will be accessed by default. If there are multiple modules, manually select a module.
      

      
       Figure 1 Selecting a module
       
      

      

     Choose Model.

     (Form mode) Click Generate Service & Page.

     (Canvas mode) Click Canvas to enter the canvas mode, click Enter Editing Mode, and then click .

     Select the model based on which the service and page are to be generated, and click Generate.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 2 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Select Model

          
           Select a created model or multiple models at a time.

           You can click  to select models whose Open Level is Public from another project. The generated services and pages are saved in the current project and can be used for data addition, deletion, modification, or query on the model under another project.

         

         
          
           Generated Content

          
           Mobile Page: mobile page for adding, deleting, modifying, and querying models, which are used to release GDELink

         

         
          
           Overwrite

          
           Overwrite existing Services pages: If you select this option when the service and page are automatically generated for multiple times based on the same model, subsequent services and pages will overwrite the existing ones. If you do not select this option, a sequence number will be added to the original name of the page or service. For example, if the test_doc_create service has been generated and will be generated for multiple times, the generated services will be named test_doc_create1 and test_doc_create2. The sequence number increases in an ascending order. When the model generates services and pages for the first time, do not select this option.

         

         
          
           Create Enable/Disable Buttons

          
           Whether to create the Enable and Disable buttons on the page. After this option is selected, the automatically-generated page is shown in the following figure. When viewing data, you can select a data record to enable or disable it. If this option is not selected, these buttons are not displayed.

           

           

           

           

         

         
          
           Permission Control Mode

          
           
            If the automatic service generation mode is used, this parameter specifies the permission control mode for the generated services. After this parameter is specified, the automatically generated services and data import and export services are subject to this restriction.

            If the built-in model service is used, the value of this parameter takes effect only for the data import and export services. The built-in data addition, deletion, modification, and query services of a model are controlled by the permission switches on the model configuration page.

           

         

         
          
           Permission Item

          
           You need to associate permission items only when Permission Control Mode is set to Login and authorization. After the association, only users who are associated with the role with this permission item have the permission to access the corresponding service. For details about how to configure permissions, see Configuring Permissions.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Generate. In the Generate Service and Page phase, you can select the generated pages, services, and data import and export services.
      

      On the generated page, you can select the properties to be displayed. Only the selected properties are generated on the corresponding services and pages. {Model name}_grid allows you to select fields to be queried.

      

      

      

     Click Generate.
      

      
       If the automatic service generation mode is used, the orchestration elements listed in the following tables are generated. 
        
         
          
           Table 3 Description of automatically generated services
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Service Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             {Model name}_create

            
             Service for creating model data

           

           
            
             {Model name}_update

            
             Service for updating model data

           

           
            
             {Model name}_get

            
             Service for querying a single data record

           

           
            
             {Model name}_get_list

            
             Service for querying the data list

           

           
            
             {Model name}_batch_delete

            
             Service for deleting data in batches

           

           
            
             {Model name}_batch_update

            
             Service for updating data in batches

           

           
            
             {Model name}_batch_upsert

            
             Service for supplementing data in batches

           

          
         
        

        
         
          
           Table 4 Description of automatically generated pages
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Page Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             {Model name}_create

            
             Page for adding data

           

           
            
             {Model name}_grid

            
             Overall entry of the GUI

           

           
            
             {Model name}_update

            
             Page for modifying data

           

           
            
             {Model name}_import

            
             Page for batch importing data

           

          
         
        

        
         
          
           Table 5 Description of automatically generated data import and export services
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Page Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             {Model name}_import

            
             Batch data import service

           

           
            
             {Model name}_export

            
             Batch data export service

           

          
         
        

        On the automatically generated pages, call the automatically generated services.

        

        

        When the services and pages are automatically generated, data import and export services are also automatically generated and associated with the automatically generated pages. You can batch import and export data on the page.

        The data import and export services can call the automatically generated services.

        When Generated Content is set to Terminal Pages, the automatically generated mobile page is displayed on the Mobile Page menu.

        
         
          
           Table 6 Description of automatically generated mobile pages
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Page Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             {Model name}_create

            
             Page for adding data on the GDELink app

           

           
            
             {Model name}_grid

            
             Overall entry to the GDELink mobile page

           

           
            
             {Model name}_update

            
             Page for modifying data on the GDELink app

           

          
         
        

      

      
       In the built-in model service mode, only page elements and data import and export elements can be generated. Service elements do not need to be generated. Mobile pages cannot be generated.
        Call the built-in addition, deletion, modification, or query service of a model in page elements. The following figure shows examples of called built-in model services on the data creation page.

        

        

        The data import and export services also directly call built-in model services.

name: Configuring Preset Model Data
title: Configuring Preset Model Data
text:
Configuring Preset Model Data
 
 
  
  

  
   In develop state, models support preset data packages, which can be imported and exported with the project package and app package.

   
    Prerequisites

    You have created a data model.

   

   
    Context

    After a data model is created in develop-state environment, you can preset data in the model and import and export the data with the project package and app package as the preset data in the runtime-state environment.

    
     The data template can be automatically generated in CSV or XLSX format based on the selected file format. The template is automatically generated based on model fields. The template header fields are the model field names, excluding the fields such as update_by, create_by, and change_time selected by the user. Only user-defined fields and the active field are included.

     The CSV file must be encoded in UTF-8 format. Data records are separated by commas (,).

     Restrictions on different property types are as follows:
      
       For the file field type, you need to upload the file attachment and data file, set the file field to the relative path of the file to be uploaded, pack the file attachment and data file into a ZIP package, and upload it.

       For the user/user group field type, enter the user name/user group name. Do not use the user ID/user group ID.

       For the date field type, enter values in yyyy-mm-dd format in a CSV file, and enter values in date formats that can be identified by Excel files in an XLSX file.

       For the time field type, enter values in HH:mm:ss format in a CSV file, and enter values in time formats that can be identified by Excel files in an XLSX file.

       For the datetime field type, enter values in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format in a CSV file, and enter values in date and time formats that can be identified by Excel files in an XLSX file.

      

     The size of the preset data package cannot exceed 10 MB. It is recommended that the number of data records do not exceed 1000.

     Model data can be preconfigured across modules and projects. Based on the open level of a model, data can be preconfigured for the model that can be accessed by the current module. For example, if model A is at the public level, data can be preconfigured for model A in any project. If model B is at the project level, data can be preconfigured only in the same project as model B. If model C is at the module level, data can be preconfigured only in the module of model C.

     If the data model needs to be modified after data is preconfigured, refer to Table 2 and Table 3.
      
       For scenarios that can be modified, the preset data is modified synchronously. For example, if a mandatory field is added to a model and the default value is provided, or an optional field is added, the field can be modified, and the preset data is modified accordingly.

       For scenarios that cannot be modified, you need to delete the preset data before the modification. For example, if a mandatory field is added to a model and no default value is provided, the field can be modified only after the preset data is deleted.

      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Select the module to be operated.

     Choose Model.

     (Canvas mode) Click Canvas to enter the canvas mode, click Enter Edit Mode, and click the Preset Data icon .

     (Form mode) Choose  > Preset Data.

     In the displayed dialog box, click Create.
      

      
       In the displayed dialog box, select a model.

       Download a template. You can select an XLSX or CSV template.

       Prepare the data package according to the template. That is, sort out the data according to the template.

       Click Upload to upload the prepared data package.
        

        

       Click OK.

      

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    The uploaded preset data can be deleted. If you import preset data again after importing it once, you can select Update Existing Data or Skip Existing Data in the upload phase.

    To delete existing preset data, click Delete next to the preset data in the Preset Data dialog box.

    
     Figure 1 Deleting the preset data
     
    

    
      
     
      If a model contains fields of the Sequence type and the sequence is of the auto increment type, the auto-increment sequence increases after the preset data is deleted and then preset again. As a result, data cannot be generated based on the preset input values. For example, when the auto-increment sequence field is used as the primary key, data is updated based on the primary key during deployment. However, after the auto-increment sequence value increases, the expected updated data changes to a new data record created based on the auto-increment primary key. In this case, you are advised to preset data using the data import mode. For details, see Configuring the Excel Data Import Service.

     

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Common Model Operations

name: TQL Debugging for Data Models
title: TQL Debugging for Data Models
text:
TQL Debugging for Data Models
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    The data model has been created and deployed.

   

   
    Context

    After data models are created, developers need to perform operations such as data query using these models, and TQL debugging enables them to quickly debug and verify such data models.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Access a created project and module, and choose Model.

     Click Debug TQL Expression.

     In the displayed Debug TQL Expression dialog box, perform TQL debugging.
      

      
       Quick query: Select the first 20 records in the data model.
        You can click  to select a desired data model. After that, choose Insert > Select First 20 Records and then click Execute to query the first 20 records of this data model.

        

        

        

      

      
       Use the TQL function. The Quick Select Function area displays functions supported by TQL. You can use these functions by clicking them. For example, you can click length to add LENGTH() to the TQL. Assume that you want to query the length of the doc_name field, you can add LENGTH(doc_name) to the TQL.
        A maximum of 31 fields can be displayed in the query result in the Debug TQL Expression dialog box. When the number of fields queried by the SELECT clause in the TQL statement exceeds 31, the query result of the excess fields can be returned but cannot be displayed in the Debug TQL Expression dialog box.

       Click  to format the TQL script. For example, the original script is as follows:
        select * from "/office_equipment/office_equipment/office_equ_equipment_mgt" as office_equ_equipment_mgt limit 20
        
         The effect is as follows:
         select
  *
from
  "/office_equipment/office_equipment/office_equ_equipment_mgt" as office_equ_equipment_mgt limit 20
        

       Click  to expand the script editing window and edit the script in full screen.

      

      

     (Optional) Click Execute Plan to view the TQL execution plan. View the TQL execution plan to check whether complex SQL statements need indexes and whether optimization is required.
      

      

      

      The following table describes the parameters in the execution result.

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Bytes

          
           Size of the result set to be returned.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Operation content. The common operations are as follows:

           
            Table data reading methods:
             
              TABLE ACCESS BY INDEX ROWID: Query the table data by the returned row ID of the index.

              TABLE ACCESS FULL: full table scan

             

            Index data reading methods:
             
              INDEX UNIQUE SCAN: scan based on the primary key or unique index

              INDEX RANGE SCAN: index range scan

              INDEX FULL SCAN: full index scan

              INDEX FAST FULL SCAN: quick full-index scan

             

            Methods for connection between tables:
             
              NESTED LOOPS

              HASH JOIN

              SUBSELECT

              KERNEL FILTER

             

           

         

         
          
           Cost

          
           Execution cost of each statement.

         

         
          
           Name

          
           Operation object, such as a table or index.

         

         
          
           Rows

          
           Estimated number of data rows.

name: Importing and Exporting Model Metadata in JSON Format
title: Importing and Exporting Model Metadata in JSON Format
text:
Importing and Exporting Model Metadata in JSON Format
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    After you configure a model in a project, if the same model configuration is required in another project, you can export the model metadata in JSON format and import it to another project.

    The model metadata in JSON format includes the basic model definition, model property configuration, model index, and sharding policy of the model.

    
      
     
      
       You can export the metadata of a maximum of 20 models at a time.

       When you export the model metadata in JSON format, if the exported model metadata file needs to be imported to another project module, you need to modify the file to meet the requirements of the new module.

      

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project and module from which you want to export model metadata.

     Choose Model.

     Export model metadata.
      

      
       Select the model from which you want to export metadata, choose More > Export Model on the right of the Models page, and then click OK.

       Configure the Export data format parameter.
        json: If you select this value, complete model information is exported. This way, you can replicate and migrate the model between different project modules.

      

      

     Import model metadata.
      

      
       Obtain the prefix of the module to which you want to import model metadata.
        
         Click  next to the module name on the top of the page, move the cursor to the name and  of the module, and then select Configure Module.
          

          

         View the module prefix.
          

          

        

       Modify model_name in the JSON file. You need to add the prefix of the current module to the value of model_name to meet the prefix verification requirements during model metadata import.

       Import model metadata.
        
         On the right of the Models page, choose More > Import Model.

         In the displayed dialog box, click Add and select the modified JSON file.

         Click OK.

        

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Common Model Operations

name: Importing and Exporting Model Metadata in XLSX Format
title: Importing and Exporting Model Metadata in XLSX Format
text:
Importing and Exporting Model Metadata in XLSX Format
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    If you want to add multiple properties to a model, use an Excel file to sort out the properties. In this case, using an Excel file is more convenient and faster than using the console. After the properties are sorted out by using the Excel file, use the Excel file to import model metadata. This improves the data import efficiency.

    
      
     
      To use an Excel file to import model metadata, you need to take note of the following items:

      
       The maximum size of the Excel file is 2 MB.

       The Excel file can be used to import metadata of up to 20 models, and each model can contain up to 200 fields.

      

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Select the project and module to which you want to import model metadata.

     Choose Model.

     Export model metadata.
      

      
       Select the model from which you want to export metadata, choose More > Export Model on the right of the Models page, and then click OK.

       Set Export data format to xlsx and save the file to a local path.
        The sheet name of the exported Excel file is the model name. If multiple models are selected, the Excel file contains multiple sheets.

      

      

     Import model metadata.
      

      
       Prepare the file to be imported.
        You can use the Excel file exported in 3, or you can download the metadata template on the page displayed after you choose More > Import Model to prepare an Excel file based on the template.

       Modify the file content. 
        
         
          
           Table 1 Excel file parameters
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             *Operation

            
             Specifies the operation type of a property.

             
              add: Add a property.

              update: Update a property.

              delete: Delete a property.

              skip: Skip a property.

             

           

           
            
             *Property Name

            
             Specifies the name of a property.

           

           
            
             Label Name

            
             Specifies the label name.

           

           
            
             *Property Type

            
             Specifies the property type.

           

           
            
             Primary Key

            
             Specifies whether a property is a primary key.

           

           
            
             Required

            
             Specifies whether this parameter is mandatory.

           

           
            
             Column Name

            
             Specifies the field name. This field is mandatory only for data source models and view models.

           

           
            
             Restrictions

            
             Specifies the property constraints.

           

           
            
             Default Value

            
             Specifies the default value of the parameter.

           

           
            
             Description

            
             Specifies the parameter description.

           

          
         
        

        
         
           
          
           Before you use an Excel file to import model metadata, ensure that the sheet names of the Excel file are the corresponding model names. Otherwise, the properties in the Excel file cannot be imported.

          

         

        

       Import model metadata.
        
         On the right of the Models page, choose More > Import Model.

         In the displayed dialog box, click Add and select the prepared Excel file.

         Click OK.

name: Migrating Model Data
title: Migrating Model Data
text:
Migrating Model Data
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    A model has been configured and the model contains data instances.

   

   
    Context

    The system uses the architecture in which the develop-state environment is isolated with the runtime-state environment, and the model instance data is not carried during app packaging. As a result, the app package does not contain data instances by default.

    In the app development and debugging phase, developers may add some basic data to the design and debugging environment. After the debugging is complete, the basic data needs to be migrated from the design and debugging environment to the production environment when the app is deployed in the production environment.

    
      
     
      
       The difference between model data migration and preset model data is as follows: Preset model data is uploaded and packaged with apps and applies only to a single model. Data involved in model data migration is not packaged with apps and the data needs to be manually imported in the corresponding runtime-state environment. Data migration can be performed on multiple models at the same time. This mode applies to scenarios where associated data is included in multiple models.

       The difference between model data migration and model metadata import or export is as follows: Model metadata refers to the declarative data of a model while data involved in model data migration refers to instances.

       If an associated trigger is configured for a model for data migration, the trigger cannot be triggered during import of the data migration file.

      

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Access the module to be operated. If there is only one module, it will be accessed by default. If there are multiple modules, manually select a module.

     Choose Model.

     On the right of the model page, choose More > Export Model Data.

     In the displayed dialog box, select the model.
      

      

      

      

     Click Export.

     Confirm the security risks of data export as prompted, click Confirm, and save the file.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    Import the exported file to the runtime-state page in the target environment as planned. The page menu path is Products and Services > Administration > Model Management > Model Data Import.
