name: Introduction to Page Designer
title: Introduction to Page Designer
text:
Introduction to Page Designer
 
 
  
  

  
   Page Designer allows you to develop and modify a page.

   The page designer allows you to design and orchestrate web pages by dragging and configuring various components.

   Key capabilities of the page designer are described as follows.

   
    Rapid Reuse of Component Assets

    
     Basic: provides built-in basic components, for example, Layout, Navigator, and Button.

     Extended: provides components that are extended based on basic components and contain certain scenarios and service meanings. Generally, a component is developed and customized by developers using Pro Code.

     Template: provides page template components. Preset and customized page templates are included. When creating a page, you can select a template. After the page is created, the page template can still be used as a component for quick use and reuse.
      

    

   

   
    Quick Reuse of Card Assets

    A card is a combination of page elements and functions with certain business significance. It consists of technical components and business services and is used to display data and information. After a card is created, it can be used as an asset and reused during page creation.

    There are two types of cards:

    
     Project Card: provides card elements that can be obtained from the current module. For example, cards created in the current module, cards created in other modules of the current project with the project-level permission, and cards created in other projects with the public permission.

     Asset Card: provides card assets that can be obtained from the local asset library.
      

    

   

   
    Component Example and Usage Guide

    
     Figure 1 Component usage
     
     
      API Doc: describes the configuration of component property fields and available APIs.

      Example: provides an example to help developers quickly understand how to use the component.

     

    

   

   
    Property Settings

    You can configure properties for the components that have been added to the canvas. The properties that can be configured vary according to components. Developers can view the API document of a component to understand the property configuration information of the component.

   

   
    Event Configuration

    When events such as click, focus, and out-of-focus occur on a component, logical nodes can be configured, such as judgment condition configuration, script execution, service calling, REST API calling, window opening, value setting, and page jumping.

   

   
    Property Variables

    Component properties can be bound as variable data through property data.

   

   
    Script Configuration

    You can use JavaScript and CSS scripts to configure a page.

   

   
    Internationalization Configuration

    By default, inventory assets can directly reference internationalization resource Bundle of ADC, such as bundles in the system/usermgt/aw_schedule directory and process-related apps. In addition, you can add internationalization resource reference relationships to support cross-project reference.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Basic Page Orchestration Guide

name: Configuring a Common Web Page
title: Configuring a Common Web Page
text:
Configuring a Common Web Page
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to configure a common web page.

   
    Context

    The system can automatically generate pages for models. You can adjust effect of the automatically generated pages or create pages.

   

   
    Prerequisites

    A service has been created. For details, see Configuring Services.

   

   
    Scenario

    Create a web page and set member information, including the member ID and member name fields. The two fields are mandatory and the field length cannot exceed 50 characters. After submission, use the member_info_create service to create data in a data model.

    
     Figure 1 Page configuration example
     
    

    This topic uses a simple configuration example to describe the configuration method. The properties and configuration methods vary according to each component. For details, see the API document of the corresponding page component.

    Extended components are usually imported by developers in customized mode. The corresponding usage guide also needs to be provided by the developer of that extended component.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Access the module to be operated. If there is only one module, it is accessed by default. If there are multiple modules, manually select a module.
      

      
       Figure 2 Selecting a module
       
      

      

     Choose Page.

     Click  to create a page.
      

      
       Figure 3 Create New Page
       
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Page Name

          
           The value can contain letters, digits, hyphens (-), and underscores (_).

         

         
          
           Display Name

          
           Page display name, which can be the same as the page name or a name that is easy to understand.

         

         
          
           Label

          
           Custom page label. You can enter a label or select a created one. For details about how to create a label, see Configuring Labels.

         

         
          
           System Template

          
           The system provides various built-in templates, such as charts, forms, and lists. You can use a template to quickly create pages and reuse existing assets.

         

         
          
           Custom Template

          
           Developers can release created pages as templates, which are customized templates.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click OK.

     In the page designer, add the Text Input component.
      

      
       Drag the Text Input component from the Basic tab pane on the left to Component Tree > Pages on the right.

       Set the basic properties of the text input component.
        

        
         
          
           Table 2 Parameters
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Id

            
             Component ID.

           

           
            
             Name

            
             Component name. This parameter is mandatory.

           

           
            
             Label

            
             Component label, that is, the text displayed on the page. Set this parameter based on the site requirements. If multiple languages need to be supported, click  to perform internationalization configuration.

           

           
            
             Placeholder

            
             Text displayed in the text box, which is usually used as prompt message.

             

             

           

          
         
        

        
          
         
          The system provides multiple page components. The parameter settings of each page component are different. For more parameter settings about a component, you can move the pointer to the component in the page designer and select Interface Document in the displayed information. You can also view the interface description about the component.

         

        

       In the property bar on the right, scroll down the mouse to configure the verification condition properties. Set Mandatory to No and Max Length to 200.
        

        

       In the property bar on the right, continue to scroll down the mouse to configure the component style. In the style area, click  to expand the style configuration area.
        

        

        After expansion, configure the style as required.

        

        

       After the style is configured, preview the style to view the configuration effect. For example, after the left spacing is configured, the result is shown in the figure below.
        

        

       Repeat the preceding steps to configure the member name input component.

      

      

     Add the confirmation button component.
      

      
       Drag the Service Button component from the left to the Component Tree > Pages area on the right.

       Configure the button properties.
        

        

        
         
          
           Table 3 Parameters
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Interface

            
             Service to be triggered by clicking a button. Set this parameter to the member_info_create service to be triggered when the submission button is configured.

           

           
            
             Text

            
             Text of a button on a page.

           

          
         
        

       Configure a button event. In the right pane, click the Event tab, click , and configure a click event.
        
         Figure 4 Configuring a button click event
         
        

        Configure the logic content of the corresponding node and click Confirm.

      

      

     Configure internationalization (adding internationalization resources). When a component has properties, such as label and tooltip, the internationalization capability can be used to provide the multi-language function and adapt to the overall language switching capability.
      

      
       Add a page-specific internationalization resource. The icon  indicates that internationalization can be configured for this field.
        

        

        
         
          
           Table 4 Internationalization configuration
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Resource Mark

            
             Resource ID. The value can contain letters, digits, underscores (_), and periods (.).

           

           
            
             Save Bundle

            
             Whether to save a created internationalization resource to a bundle.

             
              Yes: Select the bundle where the created internationalization resource is to be stored. This bundle has been added to the I18n page. After the created internationalization resource is saved to the bundle, the bundle can be reused on other pages based on the openness level of the bundle.

              No: The created internationalization resource is saved in Page Internationalization Resource and can be used only on a specific page.

             

           

          
         
        

       Manage the internationalization resources added to Page Inner Internationalization Resource on the I18n tab page.
        

       Page-specific internationalization resources can be managed and edited in a unified manner.
        

        

      

      

     Configure internationalization (referencing internationalization resource bundles). An internationalization resource bundle has been created on the I18n page.
      

      
       On the I18n page, create an internationalization resource bundle and configure the corresponding properties and multi-language data. For details, see Configuring the Internationalization Information.

       In the right pane, click the I18n tab.

       Click Add to reference internationalization resources. In the displayed dialog box, select the configured internationalization resource bundle and establish a reference relationship so that internationalization resources in the bundle can be referenced on the page. If a bundle is added repeatedly, the reference relationship is established only once.
        
         Figure 5 Referencing internationalization resources
         
        

        Select bundles and click Confirm. The referenced internationalization resource bundles are displayed on the I18n tab page.

        

        

       Click  next to the property for which internationalization needs to be configured. On the Select tab page, select properties from the existing bundles and click Save.
        

        

        
          
         
          
           By default, page-specific internationalization resources can be selected on the Select tab page.

           For a public bundle, you can select it on the Select tab page only when the Quote Internationalization Resource relationship is configured for the bundle.

          

         

        

      

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    
     The page effect can be previewed in the develop-state environment.
      

      

      
        
       
        By default, pages created based on the current version can be previewed directly without being deployed. For pages in the project where legacy assets are imported, click  in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment to deploy the app immediately for the page preview function to take effect. If Enable Hot Deployment has been enabled in the Deployment Configuration dialog box, the system automatically deploys the service after identifying configuration changes.

       

      

     After you choose Page and click , the page list is displayed. You can view and manage the pages in the current module.
      
       You can disable, enable, edit, preview, and copy a page.

       You can manage the customization status. After a page is created, it is in the Non-customizable state by default. To allow page customization, you can manually change Custom Status to Customizable.

Managing Page Templates
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    You can select an existing page template and create a page based on the template.

    Alternatively, you can create a template and use it to create a page. Using a template to create a page can improve the efficiency of creating pages with similarities.

    Page templates are global assets, that is, page templates created in projects. Page templates have a permission system independent from projects.

name: Managing Images
title: Managing Images
text:
Managing Images
 
 
  
  

  
   GDE provides centralized uploading and management of images used for app development.

   
    Procedure

    
     Access a created project and module.

     Choose Page > Orchestration Resource > Image Management.

     (Optional) Click  under Picture Catalog on the left to create an image catalog.
      

      

      

     Click Add to upload an image.
      

      
       Figure 1 Image configuration
       
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Directory

          
           Catalog for storing archived images

         

         
          
           Pictures

          
           Image file you selected. Only the following formats are supported: JPG, GIF, PNG, and SVG.

         

         
          
           File Name

          
           File name automatically generated based on the image file. Additionally, the system automatically generates the image path based on the image name.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Brief description

         

         
          
           Terminal Usage

          
           Whether an image is used on a terminal

         

         
          
           Open Level

          
           Image open level

           
            Module: The image can be used within a module.

            Project: When multiple modules exist in a project, the image can be called across modules.

            Public: The image is opened and can be called in the system.

           

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Submit. You can view the image URL in the list, for example, /adc-static/imagemgt/images/${tenant_id}/test_wc/test_wc/wc/ image 6.png. This address is used when an image is referenced.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    
     For example, you need to set the background image pubu1.png for the text box whose ID is set to text_input1.
     #text_input1{
      background-image:url(${staticContextPath}/${imagePrefix}/${tenant_id}/UItest/test001/pic/pubu1.png);
      background-repeat: no-repeat;
      background-size: cover;}
    

    
      
     
      Because the image is loaded from cache, when the image is deleted and the URL of the referenced image remains unchanged, the display effect cannot be viewed immediately in the develop-state environment. However, the effect is normally displayed in the runtime-state environment.

      If you want to immediately preview the display effect after the image is deleted in the develop-state environment, add t=Timestamp to the URL for accessing the image. Timestamp can be replaced with random digits. The following shows an example:

      #text_input1{

      background-image:url(${staticContextPath}/${imagePrefix}/${tenant_id}/UItest/test001/pic/pubu1.png?t=105234783);}

     

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Basic Page Orchestration Guide

name: Configuring a Custom Theme
title: Configuring a Custom Theme
text:
Configuring a Custom Theme
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    ADC allows you to develop applications for various industries and meets your specific theme color requirements. On ADC, developers can customize application theme colors that meet preferences of target users and industries.

    When the theme switching function is enabled, the four themes that can be switched are Default, Black, Deep Sea Blue, and Moon Shadow Grey. The theme colors have been preset and can be used directly. No color is preset for the Deep Sea Blue theme. You need to define the theme color of the corresponding style.

    Therefore, when customizing a theme, you can set the theme name to Deep Sea Blue and define the theme style for theme switching on the GUI. If the custom theme name is set to a name other than Deep Sea Blue, you need to use scripts to load the theme on the page.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Theme application scope
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Category of GUI Elements

        
         Preset Theme Style

        
         Custom Theme Style

       

      
      
       
        
         Platform pages (such as the Portal Common Configuration and system configuration pages)

        
         Styles of the Default, Black, and Moon Shadow Grey themes are supported.

        
         The theme style cannot be customized.

       

       
        
         Elements at the framework layer (colors of top title bar and menu theme)

        
         Styles of the Default, Black, and Moon Shadow Grey themes are supported.

        
         The style of the Deep Sea Blue theme can be customized. You can select Deep Sea Blue from the Switch Theme drop-down list.

       

       
        
         App orchestration pages (pages generated after orchestration in a project)

        
         Styles of the Default, Black, and Moon Shadow Grey themes are supported.

        
         The style of any theme can be customized.

         
          To customize the style of the Deep Sea Blue theme, you can select Deep Sea Blue from the Switch Theme drop-down list.

          To customize the style of a theme other than Deep Sea Blue, you can use the following scripts to load the theme on the page:
           U.ready(function(){
    U.loadCurrentTheme("newtheme")
});

         

       

      
     
    

    When the theme switching function is enabled for runtime-state deployment, you can switch the themes.

    
     Figure 1 Switch Theme
     
    

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access a created project and module.

     Choose Page > Orchestration Resource > Theme Management.

     (Method 1) Copy an existing theme and modify it.
      

      On the Theme Management page, the system lists the current official themes. If you only need to adjust an existing theme, you can copy the theme and modify it.

      

     (Method 2) In the Custom area, click  and select Custom to create a theme.

     On the theme creation page, view the theme display effect in the middle of the page and configure the theme on the right.
      

      
       Figure 2 Theme configuration
       
      

      

     Complete common configurations.
      

      
       Set the theme color and click OK. You can select a color in the palette or enter the color code in the lower left corner.
        
         Figure 3 Configuring a theme color
         
        

       Confirm the information as prompted.

       After the theme color is adjusted, other colors under the theme are automatically adjusted. Developers can perform secondary adjustment as required.

      

      

     Complete other configurations.
      

      
       Click  next to Common.

       Select the content to be configured.
        
         Figure 4 Switching the configuration
         
        

      

      

     After the configuration is completed, click Save Theme in the upper right corner.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 2 Parameters
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Theme name

         

         
          
           Developer Type

          
           Resource development permission control, that is, developers who have the permission to view, use, and change (activate, deactivate, delete, and edit) resources.

           
            Personal: Grant the development permission only to the individual who creates the asset.

            Team: Grant the development permission to a specified team.

           

         

         
          
           Share Asset

          
           Whether resources can be shared, that is, whether to allow other users except individuals or teams to view, use, copy, and export page templates (excluding change operations). Resource sharing is a restricted disclosure of resource permissions. That is, only the resource usage permission is shared, and the resource change permission is not.

         

         
          
           Whether to push assets at the same time

          
           After being pushed to an asset library, the theme can be used by other apps.

         

         
          
           Version

          
           Updated version when an asset is pushed to the asset library for multiple times.

           
            Major version: The first digit in the version number is updated. For example, if the version number of the first release is later than 0.0.1, the value of Major version after the update is 1.0.1.

            Minor version: The second digit in the version number is updated. For example, if the version number of the first release is later than 0.0.1, the value of Minor version after the update is 0.1.1.

            Patch version: The third digit in the version number is updated. For example, if the version number of the first release is later than 0.0.1, the value of Minor version after the update is 0.0.2.

           

         

         
          
           Business Type

          
           You can view the asset category in the asset library.

         

        
       
      

      

     (Optional) To customize the style of a theme other than Deep Sea Blue, use scripts to load the theme on the page.
      

      
       Under Page, select a configured page.

       On the right of the page designer, click Custom Script.
        

        

       Enter the following scripts in the Script text box, set the script name, and click OK.
        U.ready(function(){
    U.loadCurrentTheme("darkBlue")
});

      

      

     Package the theme into an app. By default, an app contains other orchestration elements such as models, services, and pages. You need to manually add a custom theme.
      

      
       Click  in the upper right corner and select APP from the Packed Into drop-down list.

       Expand the Included Global Assets area and click Add. In the displayed dialog box, add a global asset and click OK.
        

        

        
          
         
          In scenarios such as project packaging into an app or a project package, if a custom theme needs to be packaged, you need to add a global asset to add the custom theme.

         

        

       Click Pack.

       After the packaging is complete, click Download.

      

      

     Deploy the app in the runtime-state environment. Deploy the downloaded app file on the Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager page in the runtime-state environment.

     View the orchestrated page effect in the runtime-state environment.
      

      
       If the custom theme is Deep Sea Blue, you can switch to the theme to view the theme effect.

       If the custom theme is not Deep Sea Blue and the theme loading script has been added to the page, the theme loading effect can be directly displayed on the corresponding orchestration page. In the debugging and development phase, you can preview the effect.

name: Configuring Labels
title: Configuring Labels
text:
Configuring Labels
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    The system allows users to customize labels for orchestration elements such as data visualization screen and page.

    The entry for configuring labels for each orchestration element is different.

    
     Entry path for configuring data visualization screen card labels: Card >  (Card List) > Tag Management

     Entry path for configuring data visualization screen card templates: Card >  (Card List) > Tag Management

     Entry path for configuring data visualization screen page labels: Data Visualization >  (Data Visualization List) > Tag Management

     Entry path for configuring PC page labels: Page >  (Page List) > Tag Management

     Entry path for configuring data visualization screen block labels: Data Visualization > Orchestration Resource > Data Visualization Block Management > Tag Management

     Entry path for configuring data visualization screen template labels: Data Visualization > Orchestration Resource > Data Visualization Template Management > Tag Management

    

    The following procedure uses a page label as an example to describe the configuration method.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project and module to be operated.

     Choose Page.

     Click . The Page List page is displayed.

     Click Tag Management on the right. The Page Tag Management page is displayed.

     Click Create and configure label information.
      

      

      

     Click OK.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    
     You can select the needed label when creating a data visualization screen card, data visualization screen page, or PC page.

     You can select the needed label when saving a data visualization screen page template and block.

     In the page and data visualization screen lists, you can select multiple pages or data visualization screens and click Update Tag to modify labels in batches.

name: Creating a PC Card
title: Creating a PC Card
text:
Creating a PC Card
 
 
  
  

  
   ADC enables you to create cards online. This section describes how to create a PC card.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     A project and a module have been created.

     The Card menu has been added to the navigation pane.

    

   

   
    Context

    A card is a combination of page elements and functions with certain business significance. It consists of technical components and business services and is used to display data and information. A PC card refers to the card used on PCs.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Card.

     Click  to create a card.

     When you create a card, the default card type is PC Card. Set Card Name and click Create Card.

     On the Properties tab page displayed on the right, set card properties.
      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Basic card properties
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Title

          
           Card title.

         

         
          
           Label

          
           Card label. You can select a created label from the drop-down list. For details about how to create a label, see Configuring Labels.

         

         
          
           Display Name

          
           Card display name, which can be set to a name that is easy to understand.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Card description.

         

         
          
           Default Icon

          
           Image displayed in the card list. The recommended size of the image is 36 x 32.

         

         
          
           Key Words

          
           Card label. Multiple labels can be configured for a card.

         

         
          
           Version

          
           Version number, which complies with the semantic version naming specifications, for example, 1.0.0.

         

         
          
           Open Level

          
           Open level of a card.

           
            Public: indicates that the card is public and can be used within the system.

            Project: indicates that the card can be used within a project. When there are multiple modules in the project, the card can also be used within the project modules.

            Module: Indicates that the card can be used within the module.

           

         

        
       
      

      The icon  indicates that internationalization information can be configured for this field. You can click Select to select an existing internationalization resource or click Add to add an internationalization resource. For details, see 9 and 10.

      

     (Optional) Set the card style, including the size, spacing, font, background, and border.
      

      

      

      

     (Optional) Manage internationalization resources.
      

      
       Reference internationalization resources. You can reference the internationalization resources that have been created in a project.

       Manage page-specific internationalization resources. You can manage the internationalization resources that have been added on this page or continue to add internationalization resources on this page.

      

      

     (Optional) Manage scripts.
      

      
       Reference script resources.

       Reference the resource address.

       Manage associated scripts.

      

      

     (Optional) Manage styles.
      

      
       Reference script resources.

       Reference the resource address.

       Manage associated scripts.

      

      

     (Optional) Manage card variables. Add a card variable.

           Name

           Asset name

          
           The value is automatically obtained based on the card name and cannot be changed.

         

         
          
           version

          
           Updated version when an asset is pushed to the asset library for multiple times.

           
            Major version: The first digit in the version number is updated. For example, if the version number of the first release is later than 0.0.1, the value of Major version after the update is 1.0.1.

            Minor version: The second digit in the version number is updated. For example, if the version number of the first release is later than 0.0.1, the value of Minor version after the update is 0.1.1.

            Patch version: The third digit in the version number is updated. For example, if the version number of the first release is later than 0.0.1, the value of Minor version after the update is 0.0.2.

            Team: Grant the development permission to a specified team.

           

         

         
          
           Share Asset

          
           Whether resources can be shared, that is, whether to allow other users except individuals or teams to view, use, copy, and export page templates (excluding change operations). That is, only the resource usage permission is shared, and the resource change permission is not.

    listeners contains the clickMenu property, which is used for configuring report display menus.

text:
Basic Concepts of Page JS
 
 
  
  

  
   
    JavaScript (JS) is a lightweight, interpreted, or just-in-time compiled programming language with first-class functions. It is the most popular script language for developing Web pages. Almost all modern HTML pages and browsers support JavaScript.

    The main functions of the page JS script are as follows:
     
      Embed dynamic text into HTML pages.

      Respond to browser events.

      Read and write HTML elements.

      Validate data before the data is submitted to the server.

      Detect guests' browser information.

     

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Page JS Introduction

Application Scenarios of Page JS
 
 
  
  

  
   On ADC, page JS can be used in the following scenarios:

   
    Operate page objects and components.

    Open a web page or normal page.

    Obtain the web page information.

    Verify the data and process the input data.

    Process page and component events and respond to page operations.

    Call internal and external services.

Creating a JS Script
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    A project, module, and page have been created.

   

   
    Context

    The page JavaScript scripts in ADC are classified into the following types:

    
     Custom script: Developers can customize script files, define the open level, and reference the files on other pages.

     Inline script: An inline JavaScript script can be used only on the current page. It cannot be used as an independent script or referenced by other pages.

     Reference script: Import an external JavaScript script by providing the script resource address. For a third-party script, you need to load a corresponding class on the Page > Orchestration Resource > Third-Party JS Class Libraries page and then reference the class.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access the created page.

     In the right pane, click the Script tab.

     Click  and select the script type to be created.
      

      

      
       Add a custom script, set the script information, and click Save And Close after the script is compiled.

             Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Creation Method

            
             
              Select an Existing Script: Select an existing script, for example, a customized script added in this module.

              Create Script: Create a script.

             

           

           
            
             Public Setting

            
             
              Module: Only pages of the current module can reference this script.

              Project: This script can be referenced by pages of all modules in the project.

              Public: This script can be referenced by all pages of a tenant.

             

           

           
            
             Inline Setting

            
             The parameter is currently not used.

           

          
         
        

        
         In the script editing area, click  to insert a script template.

         Click  to insert the component ID and component name to facilitate quick access to elements.

        

       Add an inline script, set the script information, and click Save And Close after the script is compiled.
        

        

       Create a reference script.
        
         Figure 1 Creating a reference script
         
        

      

      

     Save the page configuration.

name: Basic Concepts of Page CSS
title: Basic Concepts of Page CSS
text:
Basic Concepts of Page CSS
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) is a computer language used to represent web page styles. CSS can statically decorate pages and dynamically format page elements using various scripts. CSS can precisely control the layout of elements on web pages at the pixel level, support almost all font sizes, and edit web page objects and model styles.

    Page CSS has the following features:
     
      Rich style definitions

      Easy to use and modify

      Able to be moved to multiple pages for a unified style

      Separation of the page function and style design, facilitating redesign and replacement

     

    Restrictions on using page CSS are as follows:
     
      Properties can be set only by ID. Class is not supported.

      Only the property whitelist is supported. Other properties are filtered.

     

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Page CSS Description

name: Application Scenarios of Page CSS
title: Application Scenarios of Page CSS
text:
Application Scenarios of Page CSS
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Create a border style for the component, and set the distance between the border and the component and the distance between the border and the content.

    Set the font, color, and size of the text.

    Set the background color or background image.

    Set the length and width of the video frame.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Page CSS Description

name: Common Properties
title: Common Properties
text:
Common Properties
 
 
  
  

  
   
    margin: Outer margin used by most components

    padding: Inner margin used by most components

    color: Color used by components such as the button, text, list view, bulletin, button bar, and collapse bar

    border-radius: Rounded border used by components such as the button, list view, date text box, drop-down list box, and process status.

    background: Background used by components such as the button, date text box, process status, list container, search box, and text box.

    font-size: Font size used by components such as the button, text, list view, bulletin, button bar, collapse bar, search box, and text box.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Page CSS Description

name: Text Effect and Font
title: Text Effect and Font
text:
Text Effect and Font
 
 
  
  

  
   
    CSS provides rich and colorful text processing properties. You can change the color, font, size, direction, alignment, indentation, case, and shadow as required.

    color: Color property, which can be a hexadecimal number (for example, #FF0000), an RGB value (for example, RGB(255,0,0)), or a color name (for example, red) There are only 147 color names.

    direction: Text direction, which is set to ltr by default, indicating from left to right. The value can also be rtl, indicating from right to left.

    text-align: Alignment mode, which is set to left by default. The value can also be center, right, or justify. The value justify indicates that the text is aligned at both ends and the word spacing is the same.

    text-indent: Indentation in the unit of px. The indent direction is the same as the text direction.

    text-transform: Converts between uppercase and lowercase letters. The value can be capitalize, uppercase, or lowercase. This parameter is valid only for letters.

    text-shadow: Shadow, for example, text-shadow: 2px 2px #ff0000. The first parameter indicates the horizontal offset, and the second parameter indicates the vertical offset. There are two options: blurred distance and shadow color.

    text-decoration: Text decoration, which can be underline, overline, or line-through, indicating underscores, hyphens, or strikethrough

    font: defines the font, boldness, size, and style. The values of the following properties can be directly written in the font property:
     
      font-family: specifies the font or font series, for example, times, courier, and arial. Multiple fonts can be entered in parallel and separated by commas (,). You can search for available fonts in sequence. You are advised to use common fonts.

      font-style: Italic fronts can be used.

      font-size: Font size, which is in the unit of px. You can also use in, cm, mm, pt, or pc as the unit.

     

   

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Page CSS Description

name: Buttons
title: Buttons
text:
Buttons
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Button styles include the color, size, border, and shadow.
    
     background-color: Button color. You can define the button color as required.

     color: Color of the button text

     width and height: Width and height of a button, which is in the unit of px or %

     font-size: Font size of the button text. The larger the text, the larger the button. However, the button size is limited.

     border: defines the color, thickness, and line style of the border. Generally, the thickness is in the unit of px. For example, border: red 2px solid.

     border-style: Line style of the border You can define the styles of the four border lines. In this case, the full name of border-style must be used.
      
       dotted: Dotted line

       solid: Solid line

       dashed: Dashed line

       double: Double solid line

       Hidden and none: No border

       You can define the style of the four border lines in the sequence of top, right, bottom, and left. If the left and right lines are the same, the left side can be omitted. If the top, bottom, left, and right lines are the same, the lower left side can be omitted.

      

     border-radius: Rounded corner of the border, which is in the unit of px or %. The maximum value is 50%, which is close to an ellipse.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Page CSS Description

name: Restrictions
title: Restrictions
text:
Restrictions
 
 
  
  

  
   Due to security and trustworthiness requirements, the front-end/terminal-defined CSS may be prohibited from directly depending on the DOM element structure, and some native properties may also be disabled. Do not use complex properties during development to avoid maintenance inconvenience caused by restrictions in the future.

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Page CSS Description

name: FAQs
title: FAQs
text:
FAQs
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Can All Native CSS Properties Be Used?
     No. Due to trustworthiness requirements, the system shields some properties. For details about the available properties, see Common Properties.

   

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Page CSS Description

name: Usage Suggestions
title: Usage Suggestions
text:
Usage Suggestions
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Use the class to customize the HTML template and reduce HTML code changes caused by style changes. For example, you are advised to use the class property in the div label and configure the CSSLIB component compilation style to control the style for HTML template property of the CardGrid component, row template property of the ListView component, and code property of the HTMLPanel component. The style property of div is not recommended, because if style is used, you need to modify the HTML template configuration once style is changed.
     <div class="name_cls" style="font-size:12px;">

    For details about the recommended usage method and properties of each component, click the component in the page designer. In the displayed dialog box, see the property API document and example.

name: Creating a CSS Script
title: Creating a CSS Script
text:
Creating a CSS Script
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    A project and a module have been created.

   

   
    Context

    The page CSS scripts in ADC are classified into the following types:

    
     Custom script: Developers can customize script files, define the open level, and reference the files on other pages.

     Inline script: similar to the inline script in HTML page development. An inline CSS script can be used only on the current page. It cannot be used as an independent script or referenced by other pages.
      
        
       
        The difference between an inline script and a custom script lies in the script compilation and running. An inline script can be embedded in an HTML element so that the script can be automatically executed during page interaction. An inline script can also help simplify code because no additional files are required to store the script. However, an inline script may also affect page loading speed because it needs to be executed immediately.

        You need to decide whether to use inline scripts or custom scripts based on site requirements.

       

      

     Reference script: Import an external CSS script by providing the script resource address. For a third-party script, you need to load a corresponding class on the Page > Orchestration Resource > Third-Party JS Class Libraries page and then reference the class.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project on which you want to perform operations.

     Access the target module. If there is only one module, it is accessed by default. If there are multiple modules, manually select a module.

     Choose Page.
      

      A developer can select a created page or create a page. The following uses a new page as an example.

     Select Text Input: name. On the property page, set ID to projName.

     Select Jump button: cancel. On the property page, set ID to cancelBtn.

     In the right pane, click the Script tab.

     Click  and select the script type to be created.
      

      

      
       Add a custom script, set the script information, and click Save And Close after the script is compiled.

title: Installing the CLI Offline Tool
text:
Installing the CLI Offline Tool
 
 
  
  

  
   Use the CLI offline tool to develop highly complex pages using codes.

   
    Prerequisites

    A Node.js whose version is between v14.17.1 and v18.20.1 has been installed.

    
     To check the Node.js version, open the CMD window on the local PC and run node -v on the CLI to check the node version.

     You can download Node.js from https://nodejs.org/en/download/. If the version of the installed Node.js is too early, download and install it.

     There is a version mapping between Node.js and npm. Ensure that the NPM version matches the Node.js version based on the mapping provided in Nodejs Version Mapping to avoid version mismatch caused by manual npm upgrade.
      Method of checking the NPM version: Open the CMD command window on the local host and run the npm -v command to check the NPM version.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access a created project and module.

     Download the CLI offline tool.
      

      Portal 1:

      
       In the navigation pane, choose Page > Orchestration Resource > Customized Page.

       Click Download in the upper right corner of the page to download the tool package to the local PC.

      

      Portal 2:

      
       In the navigation pane, choose Page > Orchestration Resource > Customized Page Components.

       Click Download CLI in the upper part of the page to download the tool package to the local PC.

      

      

     In a local file directory, hold Shift, right-click in the blank area, and choose Open PowerShell Here or Open PowerShell window here (S) from the shortcut menu.

     Run npm config edit to check the NPM repository configuration. In the displayed .npmrc file, check whether the file contains the following configuration information:
      

      no-proxy=.huawei.com
registry=https://cmc.centralrepo.rnd.huawei.com/npm
@adc:registry=https://cmc.centralrepo.rnd.huawei.com/artifactory/api/npm/product_npm/@adc/
@gde:registry=https://cmc.centralrepo.rnd.huawei.com/artifactory/api/npm/product_npm/@gde/
strict-ssl=false
      If the file does not contain the information, add the information to the file, save the file, and close the file.

      

     Decompress the CLI tool package on the local PC. Double-click the run.bat file to install the CLI offline tool.

     After the installation window is closed, run adc -V in the PowerShell window to view the version. If the correct version information is displayed, the installation is successful.
      

      PS F:\tempfile\procode> adc -V
3.0.28
      The returned version information is only an example. The actual version is subject to the value obtained in 2.

      

     You can run adc --help to learn more about the command usage.
      

      PS F:\tempfile> adc --help
Usage: adc [options] [command]

Options:
  -V, --version                     output the version number
  -h, --help                        output usage information

Commands:
  config <option> [key] [value]     manage the adc configuration files
  init                              init a adc project
  run [command]                     run a local server for development
  install                           install the dependencies declared in adcui.json and package.json
  build [options] [new_version]     build [ <new_version> | major | minor | patch ] and build project or component into a zip file
  upload [options]                  upload to server
  push [new_version]                push [ <new_version> | major | minor | patch ] jslib(javascript library) to server
  pull <type> <resource> <version>  pull < jsLib | component > <name> <version>
  remove <type> <resource>          remove < jsLib | component > <name>
  set-auth                          set adc login auth
  set-cookie                        set adc login cookie
  clear-auth                        clear adc login auth
  migrate                           migrate ADC1.5 to ADC2.0 for Customized Page or Customized Page Components
      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    To uninstall the earlier version, open the Windows CLI (cmd.exe) and run npm uninstall @adc/adc-cli -g. If "removed xxx package in xxxs" is displayed, the uninstallation is successful.

title: Locally Developing a Custom Component
text:
Locally Developing a Custom Component
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Description of the Custom Component Code Project

    Use the scaffolding tool to generate a custom component code project in one-click mode. The project directory is as follows:

    no-code-pkgs //Custom component name
├─.browserslistrc
├─.editorconfig
├─.eslintignore
├─.eslintrc.js
├─.lintstagedrc
├─.prettierrc
├─.stylelintrc
├─adcui.json           //Define the custom component type and the address of the third-party library on which the custom component depends.
├─babel.config.js
├─package-lock.json
├─package.json 
├─postcss.config.js
├─src                 //Main development directory
| ├ ─packages/{Component name}
|  ├─document         //Usage guide in develop state
|    |      |    ├─en.md      //Component usage guide in English
|    |      |    └zh_CN.md      //Component usage guide in Chinese
|    |      ├─config
|    |      |   ├─index.js     //Configuration of open properties of the custom component in develop state
|    |      |   └locale.js      //Internationalization definition of the custom component in develop state
|    |      ├─component       
|    |      |     ├─runtime  
|    |      |     |    └index.vue  // Component definition entry in runtime state
|    |      ├─assets              //Icon used in develop state
|    |      |   └icon.png
├─node_modules                 // 
├─example                //Sample component preset in the custom component
|    ├─example-step
|    |      ├─src
|    |      |  ├─config
|    |      |  |   ├─index.js
|    |      |  |   └locale.js
|    |      |  ├─component
|    |      |  |     ├─runtime
|    |      |  |     |    ├─index.vue
|    |      |  |     ├─designer
|    |      |  |     |    ├─property-editor
|    |      |  |     |     |    ├─custom-editor.vue  //custom-editor.vue //Vue entry file for the custom property. The file name can be customized and can be configured based on the code in the index.js file.
|    |      |  |     |     |    ├─custom-popover-editor.vue  //Vue file for the custom dialog box property. The file name can be customized and can be configured based on the code in the index.js file.
|    |      |  |     |     |    ├─index.js   //Entry file of custom property configurations
├─document               //Open document of the custom component
|    ├─1.designerAndruntime.md
|    ├─2.debuggingAndDevelopment.md
|    ├─3.componentNesting.md
|    └README.md
├─build                  //Package the compilation script.
├─adaptor                //Encapsulated component definition method and constant, which are used by compilation developers
    
     Description of the adcui.json file
      {
  "type": "nocode", //Custom component that is identified
 "javascriptLibraryDependencies":[{"src":"xxxx"}]  //Depended third-party component, which is associated with the third-party library provided by the UI
}

     Configuration description of open properties of custom components in develop state (path: src/packages/{Component name}/config/index.js)

     Internationalization definition of the custom component displayed in develop state (path: src/packages/{Component name}/config/locale.js)

     Entry for defining components in runtime state (path: src/packages/{Component name}/component/runtime/index.vue)
      
       The scoped style is strongly recommended to avoid affecting other components.

       The component must support internationalization switching.

       Currently, the development of custom components mainly depends on the Vue custom component capability. Based on the encapsulation of custom component capabilities, the intuitive configuration and dynamic loading of custom components are provided. For details, see Vue official website. The difference between the custom component and Vue custom component is that global custom components, for example, Vue.component("custom-component",componentConfig), are dynamically registered using the framework during running

      

    

   

   
    Open Property Configuration of Custom Components

    The native Vue component provides custom properties for other developers to use. Similarly, the properties provided on ADC must be configurable in the designer. The development procedure is as follows:

    
     Define the props property for the custom component. You are advised to name the property in lower camel case. The following uses the custom date range component as an example:
      

      props: {
    id: String,
    label: String,
    readOnly: {
      type: Boolean,
      default() {
        return this.readOnly == "" ? false : false;
      }
    },
    showStyle: {
      type: String,
      default: "yyyy-MM-dd"
    },
    convenientPick: {
      type: Boolean,
      default: false
    },

    /**
     *Initial value of the component
     */
    value: [String, Number, Object]
}
      

     Configure external properties of the page designer.
      

      
       Type of the provided configuration property 
        
         
          
           Table 1 External property configuration
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Property Field

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             name

            
             Property name

           

           
            
             type

            
             Property type. For details, see the INPUT_TYPE property defined in adaptor/config-creator/consts.js.

           

           
            
             category

            
             Type of a property. The common types are as follows:

             For details, see the PROPERTY_TYPE property defined in adaptor/config-creator/consts.js in Table 2.

           

           
            
             options

            
             Only the property type is SELECT, which is similar to the following:

              options: [
          { name: "yyyy/MM/dd", value: "yyyy/MM/dd" },
          { name: "yyyy-MM-dd", value: "yyyy-MM-dd" },
          {name: "yyyy-MM-dd", value: "yyyy-MM-dd"}
        ]
             

           

           
            
             defaultValue

            
             Default values:

             
              If type is set to BOOLEAN, defaultValue can be set to defaultValue:"true" or defaultValue:true and defaultValue:"false" or defaultValue:false.

              If type is set to SELECT, set the value field in options.

             

           

           
            
             forceSelection

            
             Whether to forcibly select a value. This parameter is valid only when type:QUERY_SELECT is used. In other scenarios, the default value is true.

           

           
            
             parameters

            
             This parameter is valid when type is set to QUERY_SELECT. Currently, the configurable parameters are fixed capabilities of the platform. For details, see Table 3.

           

          
         
        

        
         
         
          
           Table 2 PROPERTY_TYPE property definition
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Type Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             PROPERTY_TYPE.PROPERTY

            
             Properties of property category. If this parameter is not set, the property category is used by default.

           

           
            
             PROPERTY_TYPE.STYLE

            
             Property of style category

           

           
            
             PROPERTY_TYPE.VALIDATION

            
             Property of verification category

           

          
         
        

        
         
         
          
           Table 3 Examples of parameters
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Example

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             basic({ name: "label", value: "label", type: "QUERY_SELECT", parameters: { queryBean: "imageIconQueryer" } })

            
             Address of the selected icon

           

           
            
             basic({ name: "label", value: "label", type: "QUERY_SELECT", parameters: { queryBean: "permissionQueryer" } })

            
             List of selected permissions

           

           
            
             basic({ name: "label", value: "label", type: "QUERY_SELECT", parameters: { queryBean: "foregroudPageServicesQueryer" } })

             basic({ name: "label", value: "label", type: "QUERY_SELECT", parameters: { queryBean: "pageModelsQueryer" } })

             URI of the page opened at the frontend

           

          
         
        

       Property type description 
        
         
          
           Table 4 Property types
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Type

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Text

            
             Text input component

           

           
            
             NUMBER

            
             Digital input component

           

           
            
             QUERY_SELECT

            
             Drop-down list box for dynamically loading data from the backend. This parameter needs to be set when type:"QUERY_SELECT" is required.

             Parameters property. For details, see the parameters property configuration.

           

           
            
             JSON_MAP

            
             Character string configuration, for example, {"key1":"value1","key2":"value2"}. For details, see the data mapping configuration of the Column component.

           

           
            
             JSON_ARRAY

            
             Array

           

           
            
             RICH_TEXT

            
             Rich text configuration

           

           
            
             TEXTAREA

            
             Multi-line text boxes that can be configured

           

           
            
             JSON_ANY

            
             Any JSON format that can be configured by modifying codes

           

           
            
             COLOR_PICKER

            
             Color selector

           

           
            
             ICON_PICKER

            
             System icon selector

           

           
            
             SELECT

            
             Drop-down list box that can be configured with fixed options

           

           
            
             BOOLEAN

            
             Drop-down list box that can be configured with Yes or No

           

           
            
             HTML

            
             HTML editor

           

           
            
             CUSTOM_PROPERTY

            
             Custom property. When configuring custom basic properties, you need to configure the parameters property which must contain the following fields:

             
              The name field indicates the component name of the custom property, which must be the same as the value of name in the corresponding Vue component file for the custom property.

              Developers can transfer other custom parameters and obtain the custom parameters from the custom component.

             

           

           
            
             CUSTOM_POPOVER_PROPERTY

            
             Custom dialog box property. When configuring custom dialog box properties, you need to set the parameters property which includes the following fields

             
              name: indicates the component name of the custom property. This field is mandatory. The value must be the same as the value of name in the corresponding Vue file. The custom property component is registered globally. Therefore, ensure that the name is unique.

              promptWidth: indicates the dialog box width. This parameter is valid for the dialog box property editing box.

              promptMaxHeight: indicates the maximum height of a dialog box. This parameter is valid for the dialog box property editing box. If the height exceeds the value of this parameter, a scroll bar is displayed.

              showPromptButton: indicates whether to display the default button in the dialog box. This parameter is valid for the dialog box property editing box. The default value is true.

              Developers can transfer other custom parameters and obtain the custom parameters from the custom component.

             

           

          
         
        

       Configure the validator of the property. The properties are described as follows:
        validation({ maxLength: 5, required: true }))​
        
         
          
           Table 5 Validator properties
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             required

            
             Whether a parameter is mandatory. The options are true and false. required:true indicates that the parameter is mandatory.

           

           
            
             specialChars

            
             Whether special characters exist, for example, specialChars: "\\/:*?\"'<>|"

           

           
            
             maxLength

            
             Maximum length of a character string. For example, "maxLength": 255 indicates that the maximum length is 255.

           

           
            
             minLength

            
             Minimum length of a character string. For example, "maxLength": 1 indicates that the minimum length is 1.

           

           
            
             maxLongNumber

            
             Maximum value. This parameter is valid only when the property field type is Number. "maxLongNumber":255 indicates that the maximum value is 255.

           

           
            
             minLongNumber

            
             Minimum value. This parameter is valid only when the property field type is Number. "minLongNumber":1 indicates that the minimum value is 1.

           

           
            
             checkRules

            
             Verification rule preconfigured in the system, for example, checkRules:["url","HTML"]. The options are as follows: url, HTML, dateTimeInput, dateInput, and colorInput.

           

          
         
        

      

      

     Configure the internationalization capability of configurable properties.
      

      For details, see the definition in src/config/locale.js in the example. This file defines the internationalization configuration of the custom component displayed in the designer, including the custom component name and properties. For details, see the comments in the example.

      module.exports = {
 en-US: {
    component: {  
      //Sample name of the component displayed in the designer
      label:"Select Time Period",
      //Description of the component example displayed in the designer
      tips:"Select Time Period"
    },
    childNode: {
      panel: {
        label:"Panel"
      }
    },
    property: {
      name: {
        //The label corresponding to the name property is displayed in the designer.
       label:"Name",
       //Tips corresponding to the name property are displayed in the designer.
        tips:"Name Property"
      }
    }
  },
  en_US:{
    component: {
      label: "Time Range Picker",
      tips: "Time Range Picker"
    },
    childNode: {
      panel: {
        label: "Panel"
      }
    },
    property: {
      name: {
        label: "name",
        tips: "Name Property"
      }
    }
  }
};

text:
Debugging a Custom Component
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Procedure

    
     Debugging a local custom component depends on the online environment. You can log in to the online develop-state environment first.

     The developed custom component needs to be debugged locally. You need to modify the envs.js file. The code path is /build/wepack/envs.js. The following is an example:
      

      module.exports = {
  serverAddr: "https://10.10.10.100:38443/",
  auth: "",
  cookies: "locale=zh_CN;MATEINFO_SESSION_ID=de1be14a-6a45-4fbb-adea-906a7f3d1e20;tenant_id=2000;"
};
      The fields are described as follows. If you log out of the online environment and log in again, you need to update the configuration file in env.js.

           Name

          
           Description

           Copy the address from the obtained online environment address according to the format.

         

         
          
           cookies

          
           Construct cookies for verification, including language settings. Generally, you do not need to change the language.

title: Packaging a Customized Component
text:
Packaging a Customized Component
 
 
  
  

  
   Use the CLI offline tool to generate a customized page project package.

   
    Procedure

    
     In the VSCode-huawei tool, choose View > Terminal on the toolbar.

     In the displayed window at the bottom, enter adc run to perform local debugging.

     In the displayed window at the bottom, enter adc build to run the packaging command. You can run the adc build major, adc build minor, or adc build patch command to automatically change the version of a customized component.

     Verify that the message "Build successfully!" is displayed, and the packaging is successful.

     In the local code directory, obtain the compressed package xxxxxx.zip.

text:
Internationalization Information Calling in a Script
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Scenarios

    After internationalization information is configured, if the information needs to be referenced in component configuration, you can directly select this function on the WebUI. However, if the information needs to be referenced in a script, how can we implement this function?

   

   
    Implementation Method

    The page calls the configured internationalization resource using Nf.res (Property key).

   

   
    Implementation Process

    
     Configure the corresponding internationalization information.
      

      

      

      

     Import the internationalization language package to the corresponding script page.
      

      

      

      

     Reference the internationalization property key in the script that needs to reference the internationalization information.
      

      U.promptError({    
    message: Nf.res("demo.error.message"),
    height: 200,
    width: 300,
    title:Nf.res("demo.error.title"),
    showCancelButton:false,
    showConfirmButton:true,
    handler: function (btn) { 
      alert('ok')
    }
});

text:
Preparations
 
 
  
  

  
   A service is used to define the processing logic and how we perform various operations on a model.

   Therefore, before configuring a service, you need to understand the concepts of model and configure a model. For details, see Model Configuration.

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Configuring Services

name: Service Orchestration Elements
title: Service Orchestration Elements
text:
Service Orchestration Elements
 
 
  
  

  
   This topic describes the orchestration elements involved in services.

   The service orchestration page consists of the element area on the left, canvas area in the middle, configuration area on the right, and debugging area at the bottom.

   You can click  in the configuration area on the right to display more parameters.

   You can expand the debugging area at the bottom to debug the service.

   
    
     
      Table 1 Description of service information
     
     
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Service Element

       
        Description

      

     
     
      
       
        Service Property

       
        Properties, such as input parameters, output parameters, and public levels, can be configured for each service. These properties are service properties.

      

      
       
        Service Node

       
        Nodes contained in services. You can drag and drop nodes to orchestrate them. Properties can be configured for each node, such as associating models, calling APIs, and setting input and output parameters. Parameters can be transferred between service nodes.

      

     
    
   

   
    
     
      Table 2 Model operations
     
     
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Orchestration Element

       
        Element Description

      

     
     
      
       
        Create

       
        The Create operation is used to create data of specified models. After you configure the mapping between service input parameters and model data, the system can create model data using the input parameters.

      

      
       
        Update

       
        The Update operation is used to update data of specified models. After you configure the mapping between service input parameters and model data, the system can find the corresponding existing model data and update the model data.

      

      
       
        Delete

       
        The Delete operation is used to delete the corresponding model data based on the input primary key.

      

      
       
        Supplement

       
        The system checks whether the entered data exists. If no, the system creates the data. If yes, the system updates the data.

      

      
       
        Get

       
        The Get operation is used to query a unique model data record based on input parameter conditions and return the data.

      

      
       
        GetList

       
        The GetList operation is used to query model data based on input parameter conditions and return all model data that meets the conditions.

      

      
       
        BatchCreate

       
        The BatchCreate operation is used to create data in batches.

      

      
       
        BatchUpdate

       
        The BatchUpdate operation is used to update data in batches. That is, calling a service once can change multiple model data records to the same value in a unified manner.

      

      
       
        BatchDelete

       
        The BatchDelete operation is used to delete data in batches. That is, calling a service once can delete multiple data records at a time.

      

      
       
        Batch Supplement

       
        The Batch Supplement operation is provided for data provided in batches. If a record does not exist in the data table, the operation inserts the record. If the record exists in the data table, the operation updates the record.

      

      
       
        TQLQuery

       
        The TQLQuery operation provides a service for querying complete TQL configurations so that you can configure complex reports or query operations.

      

     
    
   

   
    
     
      Table 3 Common Operations
     
     
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Orchestration Element

       
        Element Description

      

     
     
      
       
        ServiceInvoke

       
        Call other APIs. Specifically, you can configure the mapping between input parameters of the current service and those of the called service to call another service, including translating or validating some fields.

      

      
       
        RunScript

       
        The RunScript operation is used when a single service cannot meet requirements. For example, when a submit button on a page applies to two models, or when the operation execution logic is complex, you can configure services using RunScript.

      

      
       
        FireEvent

       
        The FireEvent operation provides the function of triggering events. You can configure events and decision-making rules to complete a series of actions after an event is triggered.

      

      
       
        BatchOperation

       
        The BatchOperation operation provides the function of performing operations in batches on a service.

      

      
       
        Mapping

       
        Parameter processing node, which does not contain any operations and is used only for parameter mapping. For example, if the input and output parameters of the last two operations do not match, you can add a mapping node to process parameters.

        The assign operation is used to define a global context variable and assigns a value to the variable.
