name: Creating a Service (Blank Template)
title: Creating a Service (Blank Template)
text:
Creating a Service (Blank Template)
 
 
  
  

  
   The empty template indicates that no template is used when a service is created.

   
    Context

    ADC provides services for performing data operations. A service can connect multiple operations on data and execute the operations based on logical conditions.

    Basic orchestration operations of services are as follows:

    
     Drag

     Link

     Move

    

    You can create a service by using a template such as Create or Update, or by using an empty template.

    This section describes how to create a service based on an empty template and configure basic service information.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the required project.

     Choose Service.

     Click  to create a service. Set the service name.
      

      

      

      

     Configure the service level information. When you click the blank canvas, the global properties of the service are displayed in the property area on the right.
      

      
       Configuring basic service information 
        
         
         
          
           Table 1 Server configuration description
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Service Name

            
             This parameter is set during creation, and does not need to be modified.

           

           
            
             Service Access Address

            
             The value is automatically generated based on the app and service name, and does not need to be modified.

           

           
            
             Service Type

            
             
              Common: indicates that the service is created normally.

              Customized: indicates that the service is customized based on other services.

             

           

           
            
             Customizable

            
             Whether the current service can be customized.

           

           
            
             Open level

            
             Open level of the service

             
              Module level: A service can be accessed only within a module.

              Project level: When multiple modules exist in a project, a service can be called across modules.

              Public: A service is opened and can be accessed in the system.

             

           

           
            
             Synchronized

            
             Whether to enable synchronization. If this function is enabled, the calling party returns a response only after the service execution is complete. Otherwise, results are returned immediately after the calling triggered.

           

           
            
             Open Business Field

            
             This parameter is displayed when Open level is set to Public and Register with API Catalog is disabled.

             This parameter is used to control the whitelist of public services.

             If this parameter is not set, it is open to all business fields.

             If a business field is set, only projects in the business field can call this service.

           

           
            
             Register with the API directory

            
             This parameter is displayed only when Open level is set to Public.

             After a service is registered with the API catalog, the service can function as an API. That is, you can view the description of the API on API Catalog.

           

           
            
             API Catalog

            
             This parameter is displayed only when Register with the API directory is enabled.

             If you select a catalog from the API Catalog drop-down list, the API is registered with the API catalog. You can query the API in the catalog contained in the API Catalog drop-down list.

           

           
            
             Page Access

            
             Whether to enable the front-end service. If this function is enabled, the service is a front-end service. Otherwise, the service is a back-end service.

           

           
            
             Operation log

            
             Whether to record operation logs.

           

           
            
             App Log Record Parameters

            
             After this function is enabled, parameters will be recorded in logs. If the parameters contain sensitive information, such information will also be recorded after this function is enabled.

           

           
            
             App Desensitize

            
             After this function is enabled, you can configure desensitization policies for input and output parameters of a service.

             In scenarios in which the input and output parameters of the app log printing service and services in the runtime state are debugged, if you configure data desensitization policies for the parameters, the sensitive information of the parameters is protected based on the data desensitization policies. The intermediate node parameters in the debugging scenario are desensitized by default.

           

           
            
             Page Access Address

            
             The value is automatically generated based on the app and service name, and does not need to be modified.

           

           
            
             Permission Control Mode

            
             Permission

             
              Logged-in: Users who have logged in to the system can access the service regardless of their role permissions. The permission control capability is weak. Exercise caution when you configure this parameter.

              Logged-in and Authorized: Only users who have logged in to the system and obtained role authorization can access the service. For details about permission and role configuration, see Configuring Permissions and Roles.

              Customized Service: The permission is controlled based on the customized service. If this parameter is set to Customized Service, Customized Service Name needs to be set to the name of the service whose permission needs to be controlled.

              Permission Compatibility: This option is available only for legacy asset services and is unavailable for services created based on ADC 2.X or later. When this option is selected for a legacy asset service, refer to Configuring the Permission Compatibility Function to configure the corresponding permission items.

             

           

          
         
        

       Configure service parameters.
        Different from the input and output parameters of a node, the input and output parameters at the service level determine the input and output parameters of the service.

        You can import the input and output parameters from a model, set Related Model, configure the parameters, or use all of these methods.

        For example, if Related Model is set to um_role and the more_info field is configured, the final input parameter is the union set of the um_role model field and more_info field, and perform deduplication.

        

        

        
         
          
           Table 2 Parameter description
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Element

            
             In the Input Parameter Configuration area, the root node Input is provided in the Element column. The root node name can be changed. Only one root node is allowed.

             Select the row of the root node, and click  to add a sub-node.

           

           
            
             Type

            
             Node data type. The validator and translator types vary depending on the node type. For details, see Configuring the Element Validator and Configuring the Element Translator.

             Sub-nodes can be added to Object and Array->Object. Other types can only be used as sub-nodes.

           

           
            
             Related Model

            
             Associated model. That is, all parameters of this model are added to the input parameters.

           

           
            
             Mandatory

            
             Specifies whether this parameter is mandatory.

           

           
            
             Default Value

            
             Default value of the parameter. If the parameter is left empty or is not transferred, the default value is used.

           

           
            
             Validator

            
             The validator is commonly used in the input parameters. For details, see Configuring the Element Validator.

           

           
            
             Translator

            
             The translator is used in the input parameters. After the input parameters are converted and translated by the translator, specific operations such as data creation can be performed.

           

           
            
             Desensitize Policy

            
             The configuration is available when App Log Desensitize is enabled.

             The options in the desensitization policy drop-down list come from the app-level data desensitization policy configuration. For details, see Configuring a Project Desensitization Policy.

           

          
         
        

        Under the Output root node of the output parameters of the entire service, if no subnode parameter is set, all output parameters of the previous node are output. If a subnode parameter is set, only the subnode parameter that is set is output.

        

        

        
         
          
           Table 3 Parameter description
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Element

            
             In the Output Parameter Configuration area, the root node Output is provided in the Element column. The root node name can be changed. Only one root node is allowed.

             Select the row of the root node, and click  to add a sub-node.

           

           
            
             Type

            
             Node data type. The translator type varies depending on the node type. For details, see Configuring the Element Translator.

             Sub-nodes can be added to Object and Array->Object. Other types can only be used as sub-nodes.

           

           
            
             Related Model

            
             Associated model. That is, all parameters of this model are added to the output parameters.

           

           
            
             Path

            
             Path for obtaining parameters. Click the empty text box in the Path column. In the displayed Edit TEL Expression dialog box, click  on the left to expand the variable directory. Double-click a variable to select it and obtain the parameters.

             

             

             
              _context: context variables

              _current: variables that can be obtained on the current node

              _global.node: variables on a specified node

             

           

           
            
             Default Value

            
             Default value of the parameter. If the output parameter is not transferred, the default value is used.

           

           
            
             Translator

            
             The translator is used in the output parameters to translate the output parameters into the value type required by the target system.

           

           
            
             Desensitize Policy

            
             The configuration is available when App Log Desensitize is enabled.

             The options in the desensitization policy drop-down list come from the app-level data desensitization policy configuration. For details, see Configuring a Project Desensitization Policy.

           

          
         
        

      

      

     Drag a node from the left pane to the canvas, and configure the node information. The following uses the Create node as an example. For details about how to configure each type of node, see the following sections.
      

      
       Drag the Create node from the left pane to the arrow between the Start and End nodes. When the arrow turns blue, place the Create node. If the following figure shows an example.
        
         Figure 1 Adding a node
         
        

       Click the Create node to view the node details on the right. In this case, the information on the right is at the operation node level, which is different from the information at the service level.

       Configure the basic information. You need to configure an associated model for the Create node to store data.
        
         Figure 2 Basic node information
         
        

       Configure the node input parameters.
        
         By default, the root node Parameters is provided. Select the root node and click  to add a subnode. Click  to add a node of the same level. You are not allowed to add the same-level node when the root node is selected. Only one root node is allowed. Select the added subnode and click  or  to move the subnode up or down.

         If the parameter filtering function is disabled, all output parameters of the previous node are used as the input parameters of this node by default. If other parameters are added, the union set of the new parameters and all output parameters of the previous node is used as the input parameters.

         If the parameter filtering function is enabled, the configured field is used as the input parameter. That is, if a field is configured, only the configured field is transferred. When no field is configured, the parameter is transparently transmitted. In scenarios where the filtering function is enabled, when you add a RunScript validator or translator to the input parameter node (Parameters), all fields must be listed in compiling scripts. In some scenarios, only specified fields can be entered to the node for security purposes. In this case, you can enable the parameter filtering function and configure the node to be transferred.

         The Path column in the input parameter element can be used to specify the path for obtaining the input parameter value.
          Click the empty text box in the Path column. In the displayed Edit TEL Expression dialog box, click  on the left to expand the variable directory. Double-click a variable to select it and obtain the parameters.

          

          
           _context: context variables

           _current: variables that can be obtained on the current node

           _global.node: variables on a specified node

          

        

       Understand the node output parameter information. By default, the output parameters are the output information of this node and do not need to be configured.

      

      

     Save the canvas.

    

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    
     After the develop-state configuration is complete, click  in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment for the app to take effect immediately. If Enable Hot Deployment has been enabled in the Deployment Configuration dialog box, the system automatically deploys the service after identifying configuration changes.

     When a service is being edited in the canvas, the system locks the service to avoid conflicts caused by multi-person editing. That is, when member A edits a service, member B cannot edit the service at the same time.
      In some exception scenarios, for example, the service is locked after member A is editing a service and the lock cannot be released in time but member B needs to edit the service immediately, member B can apply to the administrator for unlocking the service for member A using the canvas lock management function.

      
       Log in to the as a user with administrator permissions, for example, admin.

       Access the current project and module, choose Service, and click .

       Click Canvas Lock Management, select the service whose lock needs to be released, and click Unlock.
        

        
         
         
           
          
           Only users with administrator permissions can unlock services. Unlocking services will discard the editing and modification of the current member. Therefore, exercise caution when performing this operation.

          

         

        

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Creating a Service (Blank Template)

name: Configuring Operation Nodes for Adding, Deleting, Modifying, and Querying Models
title: Configuring Operation Nodes for Adding, Deleting, Modifying, and Querying Models
text:
Configuring Operation Nodes for Adding, Deleting, Modifying, and Querying Models
 
 
  
  

  
   You can configure operation nodes to create, update, delete, and query a data model or the model list in a batch. In addition, you can batch supplement models and batch query TQL statements.

   
    Context

    
     Model operations include creating, updating, deleting, querying a single data record or the data list in a batch. You can select a template when creating a service to quickly create a model.

     You can create, update, and query a single data record or a list, and create, update, and supplement them in a batch using the service automatically generated by a model.

     In complex service scenarios, you can drag and drop different orchestration elements based on service requirements. If you do not use a template to create a service, manually set the input and output parameters of the service.

     On each operation node, you can customize the input parameter filtering function. If the filtering function is enabled, only the parameters configured on this node are transferred. If the filtering function is disabled, all output parameters of the previous node are used as input parameters for the current node.

    

   

   
    Creation Operation

    Associated model: Model object for which the creation operation is performed. Select a model from the configured ones.

    Input parameter configuration: The root node is Parameters. By default, the parameters of the previous node are used as input parameters. You can enable the filtering function to filter parameters and configure them as required.

    Output parameter configuration: Result, which automatically contains the associated model properties. The return value also contains id of the created data. The id parameter can be used to specify the data to be deleted when the data is deleted.

   

   
    Update Zone

    Associated model: Model object to be updated. Select a model from the configured ones.

    Input parameter configuration: The root node is Parameters. By default, the parameters of the previous node are used as input parameters. You can enable the filtering function to filter parameters and configure them as required. The input field must contain the primary key field of the model instance.

    Output parameter configuration: Result, which automatically contains the associated model properties. The success node can be used to determine whether the execution is successful.

   

   
    Deletion Confirmation

    Associated model: Model object to be deleted. Select a model from the configured ones.

    Input parameter configuration: The root node is Parameters. By default, the parameters of the previous node are used as input parameters. You can enable the filtering function to filter parameters and configure them as required. The input field contains the primary key field or id field of the model instance.

    Output parameter configuration: Result, which automatically contains the associated model properties. The success node can be used to determine whether the execution is successful.

   

   
    Single Data Record Query

    Associated model: Model object for querying a single data record. Select a model from the configured ones.

    Search criteria: Set data filter criteria.

    Input parameter configuration: The root node is Parameters. By default, the parameters of the previous node are used as input parameters. You can enable the filtering function to filter parameters and configure them as required.

    Output parameter configuration: Result, which automatically contains the associated model properties. Records that meet the search criteria are returned.

    Model replica configuration

    
     Replica: specifies the replica generation mode. If static is selected, the replica name is specified in the service. If dynamic is selected, the replica name is specified by the service input parameter.

     Replica Name: If Replica is set to static, enter a replica name, indicating the replica to be operated on the service. If Replica is set to dynamic, enter a parameter name in the input parameter configuration area. When the service is called, the replica name is specified by the parameter.

    

    Read/Write separation acceleration: To improve the data query speed, you can create a data source for reading data, that is, enable the read/write splitting function. After the data source for reading data is configured and this function is enabled, the data source for reading data is preferentially used for data query.

   

   
    List Query

    Associated model: Model object for which the list query operation is performed. Select a model from the configured ones.

    Search criteria: Set data filter criteria.

    
     Input parameter configuration: The root node is Parameters. By default, the parameters of the previous node are used as input parameters. You can enable the filtering function to filter parameters and configure them as required. The query list operation must contain the following fields:
     
      start: start line number

      limit: number of records to be queried

      sort: field to be sorted. Multiple fields are supported. Use commas (,) to separate them. For example, in a user list query scenario, users can be sorted by name and age. In this case, set sort to name,age.

      dir: sorting mode of the field to be sorted. The options are true (ascending order) and false (descending order). By default, the ascending order is used. If there are multiple fields to be sorted, the sorting mode can be configured in a different way. For example, to sort users by name in ascending order and by age in descending order, set dir to true,false when sort is set to name,age.

     

    

    Output parameter configuration: Result, which automatically contains the associated model properties. Records that meet the search criteria are returned.

    Model replica configuration

    
     Replica: specifies the replica generation mode. If static is selected, the replica name is specified in the service. If dynamic is selected, the replica name is specified by the service input parameter.

     Replica Name: If Replica is set to static, enter a replica name, indicating the replica to be operated on the service. If Replica is set to dynamic, enter a parameter name in the input parameter configuration area. When the service is called, the replica name is specified by the parameter.

    

    Read/Write separation acceleration: To improve the data query speed, you can create a data source for reading data, that is, enable the read/write splitting function. After the data source for reading data is configured and this function is enabled, the data source for reading data is preferentially used for data query.

   

   
    Batch Creation

    Associated model: Model object for querying a single data record. Select a model from the configured ones.

    Input parameter configuration: The root node is Parameters. By default, the parameters of the previous node are used as input parameters. You can enable the filtering function to filter parameters and configure them as required. _values is in array format, indicating the input for batch creation. Debug the input style of the _values field.

    "_values": [{"memberId":"111","name":"aaa"},{"memberId":"222","name":"bbb"},{"memberId":"333","name":"ccc"}]

    Output parameter configuration: Result, which automatically contains the associated model properties.

    Restriction on the number of batch operations: This function is enabled by default when service nodes involved in a batch operation are added. After this function is enabled, it cannot be disabled.

    Number of batch operations: The default value is 1000. The value ranges from 100 to 5000. If this parameter is not configured in historical assets, the default value 1000 is used.

    
      
     
      You are advised not to change the input parameter _values that is used for batch creation. If you need to change the parameter _values (as shown in Figure 1), add a parameter mapping on the batch_create node, and set the input parameter for the mapping configuration to _values (as shown in Figure 2). This restriction also applies to other batch operations, such as batch update, deletion, and supplement.

      
       
        Figure 1 Service input parameters
        
       

      

      
       
        Figure 2 Node input parameters
        
       

      

     

    

   

   
    Batch Update

    Associated model: Model objects to be updated in a batch. Select a model from the configured ones.

    Input parameter configuration: The root node is Parameters. By default, the parameters of the previous node are used as input parameters. You can enable the filtering function to filter parameters and configure them as required. _values is in array format, indicating the input for batch update. The input field must contain the primary key field of the model instance.

    Output parameter configuration: Result, which automatically contains the associated model properties. The success node can be used to determine whether the execution is successful.

    Restriction on the number of batch operations: This function is enabled by default when service nodes involved in a batch operation are added. After this function is enabled, it cannot be disabled.

    Number of batch operations: The default value is 1000. The value ranges from 100 to 5000. If this parameter is not configured in historical assets, the default value 1000 is used.

   

   
    Batch Deletion

    Associated model: Model object to be deleted. Select a model from the configured ones.

    Input parameter configuration: The root node is Parameters. By default, the parameters of the previous node are used as input parameters. You can enable the filtering function to filter parameters and configure them as required. _values is in array format, indicating the input for batch deletion. The input field contains the primary key field or id field of the model instance.

    Output parameter configuration: Result, which automatically contains the associated model properties. The success node can be used to determine whether the execution is successful.

    Restriction on the number of batch operations: This function is enabled by default when service nodes involved in a batch operation are added. After this function is enabled, it cannot be disabled.

    Number of batch operations: The default value is 1000. The value ranges from 100 to 5000. If this parameter is not configured in historical assets, the default value 1000 is used.

   

   
    TQL Query

    Input parameter configuration: The root node is Parameters. By default, the parameters of the previous node are used as input parameters. You can enable the filtering function to filter parameters and configure them as required.

    Query condition: You can use the TQL function and expression to define query conditions.

    Output parameter configuration: Result, which is required for output parameter customization. The output parameter of TQL query is an array object _values.

    For details about the syntax and examples of RunScript, see TQL Syntax Reference.

    Read/Write separation acceleration: To improve the data query speed, you can create a data source for reading data, that is, enable the read/write splitting function. After the data source for reading data is configured and this function is enabled, the data source for reading data is preferentially used for data query.

   

   
    Batch Supplement

    Associated model: Model object to be supplemented in a batch. Select a model from the configured ones.

    Input parameter configuration: The root node is Parameters. By default, the parameters of the previous node are used as input parameters. You can enable the filtering function to filter parameters and configure them as required. _values is in array format, indicating the input for batch supplementation. The input field must contain the primary key field of the model instance.

    Output parameter configuration: Result, which automatically contains the associated model properties. The success node can be used to determine whether the execution is successful.

    Restriction on the number of batch operations: This function is enabled by default when service nodes involved in a batch operation are added. After this function is enabled, it cannot be disabled.

    Number of batch operations: The default value is 1000. The value ranges from 100 to 5000. If this parameter is not configured in historical assets, the default value 1000 is used.

name: Configuring the Node for Calling a Service
title: Configuring the Node for Calling a Service
text:
Configuring the Node for Calling a Service
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    Various types of interfaces can be called through service calling.

    
     Service: You can call other services in a service.

     Model: built-in model interfaces for data addition, deletion, modification and query.

     SOAP: Outbound SOAP interface, which is called by the integration service.

     REST: Outbound REST interface, which is called by the integration service.

     Function: Function service to be called.

     Outbound API: Outbound interface introduced through API Fabric (on the Outbound API tab page).

     API: Public API asset registered with API Catalog.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    For details, see Creating a Service (Blank Template). The following steps describe only key configurations.

    
     Drag ServiceInvoke from the left pane.

     Click  to edit node properties.

     In the Invoke Interface area, click .

     Select the required interface based on site requirements, and click OK.

     Click Load Params and click OK as prompted. The input and output parameters of the operation node are loaded to the running node based on input and output parameters of the called interface.

     Click  to save the canvas data.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After develop-state configuration is complete, click  in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment for the app to take effect immediately. If Enable Hot Deployment has been enabled in the Deployment Configuration dialog box, the system automatically deploys the service after identifying configuration changes.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Creating a Service (Blank Template)

name: Configuring the Node for Executing a Script
title: Configuring the Node for Executing a Script
text:
Configuring the Node for Executing a Script
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    By running the script node, you can use JavaScript to implement some complex business scenarios. For details about the syntax, see Service JavaScript Syntax and API Reference.

   

   
    Procedure

    For details, see Creating a Service (Blank Template). The following steps describe only key configurations.

    
     Create a service using a blank template.

     Drag RunScript from the left pane.

     Click  to edit node properties.

     In the Selecting a script area, click Editing a script.

     In the displayed dialog box, select an existing script or add a script. The script engine is compatible with historical engines. The engine versions are as follows:
      

      
       Latest: indicates the latest version, which is also the default version. The latest version is used by the current product and document by default.

       1.6: Not displayed by default and displayed only when the tenant system parameter support-engine-js-v16 is set to true. Version 1.6 is a transition version. It is used to be compatible with existing assets, instead of developing new assets. For details about the differences between versions 1.6 and the latest version, see Comparison Among Multi-Version APIs. The engine of version 1.6 can be replaced by the latest version. After the replacement, the rolled back is not supported.

       1.5: Not displayed by default and displayed only when a historical version of 1.5 has been imported and displayed. It is used only to be compatible with existing assets. There are great differences between versions 1.5 and the latest version. Obtain the documents of these two versions, respectively. The engine of version 1.5 can be replaced by the latest version. After the replacement, the rolled back is not supported.

      

      

     Write a script in the window. Use either of the following methods to quickly obtain the script segment:
      

      
       Inserting an API (): You can select a service, built-in model service, SOAP API, REST API, function, API, or connector to quickly generate a code segment for API calling.

       Inserting a script template (): You can select a script sample to quickly obtain the script segment of the sample scenario.

       Inserting a function (): You can select a common function to quickly obtain the calling script of the function. For details about the functions and scripts, see Managing Service Scripts and Functions.
        
         Figure 1 Script example
         
        

      

      

     Click OK, set the script name, and save the settings.

     (Optional) Run or debug the script. After a script is saved and deployed, you can run and debug the script step by step.
      

      
       Click  to start the debugging.

name: Configuring the Yacht Data Query Node
title: Configuring the Yacht Data Query Node
text:
Configuring the Yacht Data Query Node
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    The application scenario of DataService Query under Platform Services is different from that of Get, GetList, and TQLQuery under Model Operations.

    

    

    
      
     
      This node is not displayed by default. To display this node, set integration_yacht to true at the master level.

     

    

    This node is used for data exchanges between ADC and Data Cube. The following query modes are supported:

    
     TQL mode: Data can be queried using TQL syntax or TQL scripts. For details about the syntax and examples, see TQL Syntax Reference.
      An example is as follows.

      select * from #table where name = $name and age > $age limit #start,#limit order by #orders #asc_desc

     Yacht SQL mode: The SQL editor for Yacht service is provided to edit SQL statements for accessing Data Cube data through Yacht, implementing flexible development of data access functions. For details about the SQL syntax supported by Yacht, see SQL Syntax of the Yacht Service.
      Before configuring this item, you are advised to prepare a runtime-state environment where Yacht has been installed and understand the data source to be queried under Products and Services > Data Cube > Data Opening > SQL Editor.

      

      

      An example of Yacht SQL statements is as follows:

      yacht_sql: select * from #table where name = ? and age > ? order by #orders #asc_desc limit #start,#limit

    

    Take the preceding statement as an example. You need to set the input parameters listed in the following table in the service.

    
     
     
      
       Table 1 Input parameters for DataService Query
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Parameter

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         table

        
         Table name. If the table name has been specified in the SQL statement, for example, select * from cfg.BAT_IMP_RELATION_D, you do not need to set the table name again.

         If no table name is specified in the SQL statement, you need to transfer the table name using a parameter. For example, if select * from #table is used, you need to transfer the specified table name using a parameter.

       

       
        
         start

        
         Start row number of the query

       

       
        
         limit

        
         Number of query records

       

       
        
         orders

        
         Field to be sorted. Multiple fields are supported. Use commas (,) to separate them.

       

       
        
         asc_desc

        
         Sorting mode of the field to be sorted. The options are true (ascending order) and false (descending order).

       

       
        
         yacht_database

        
         Yacht data source for the specified query. By default, if this parameter is not transferred, the query data source is physical-MetaOne. That is, you do not need to specify this parameter when querying physical-MetaOne.

         To query other data sources, such as data in physical-MONITOR_PT, transfer this parameter and specify the data source.

       

       
        
         Other parameters

        
         Parameter used as the query input, for example, a field in a data table

       

      
     
    

    The following uses the Yacht SQL mode as an example to describe how to configure the DataService Query service.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Create a service using a blank template.

     Configure service input parameters.
      

      
       Click the blank area in the canvas and click  on the right to expand the service property configuration window.

       Select the text box on the left of Input and click Subnode to add parameters to the root node. For details about the parameters, see Table 1.

       Click OK to save the settings.

      

      

     Configure the DataService Query node.
      

      
       Drag DataService Query from the left pane.

       Select the DataService Query node and click  in property box on the right.

       In the displayed dialog box, set basic information.
        

        

       In the Query Condition area, compile SQL statements.
        

        

       Click OK to save the node property configuration.

      

      

     Click  to save the service configuration.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    The debugging of the Yacht DataService Query depends on the deployment of the Yacht service in the runtime-state environment. Otherwise, the debugging cannot be performed.

    
     After the configuration is complete, click , select APP, package as an app, and download the app package.

     In the runtime-state environment where the Yacht service is deployed, switch to the master tenant, choose Products and Services > ADC System Management > Component Management > System Parameter Configuration, and configure the Yacht parameter.
      

      
       
        
         Table 2 Yacht parameter
        
        
         
         
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Category

          
           Parameter Name

          
           Default Value

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           adc-service

          
           integration_yacht_db_address

          
           None

          
           Yacht SQL execution link address

           
            If a unique link address is used globally, set this parameter to the link address.

            If different link addresses need to be defined for multiple tenants, specify the tenant address and default address in the format {"Tenant ID":"Link address 1","default":"Link address 2"}.
             Example: {"2000":"BBB","default":"CCC"}

text:
Configuring an Abnormal Process
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    Exception handling: On the model operation and common operation nodes, you need to configure Exception Handling to determine whether to ignore exceptions.

       Abnormal branch: For a node that has been connected, drag the edge point again and add a node branch to connect to the node. If an exception occurs on a node that has an exception branch, the exception branch is preferentially used.

       Exception process: process started from the exception node, which is similar to try catch in the code to capture exceptions. name: Creating a Service (Based on a Preset Template)
title: Creating a Service (Based on a Preset Template)
text:
Creating a Service (Based on a Preset Template)
 
 
  
  

  
   When you use a template to create a service, the system automatically generates corresponding operation nodes based on the selected template type and imports the model data to the service parameters based on the associated model.

   
    
     
      Table 1 Template types
     
     
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Template Name

       
        Template Description

      

     
     
      
       
        Create

       
        Service template for creating a model instance. The Create model operation node is automatically added, and fields of the associated model are used as the input and output parameters of the service.

      

      
       
        Update

       
        Service template for updating a model instance. The Update model operation node is automatically added, and fields of the associated model are used as the input and output parameters of the service.

      

      
       
        Delete

       
        Service template for deleting a model instance. The Delete operation node is automatically added, and the primary key and ID of the associated model are used as the input parameters for query. The deletion result is provided.

      

      
       
        Get

       
        Service template for querying a single data record. The Get operation node is automatically added, and the primary key and ID of the associated model are used as the input parameters for query. The model instance is used as the output.

      

      
       
        Get List

       
        Service template for querying the list. The GetList operation node is automatically added. The start, limit, sort, and active fields and model fields are used as the input parameters, and the start, limit, and total fields and model instance are used as the output parameters. There can be multiple model instances.

      

      
       
        Batch Create

       
        Service template for creating model instances in batches. The BatchCreate model operation node is automatically added.

      

      
       
        Batch Update

       
        Service template for updating model instances in batches. The BatchUpdate model operation node is automatically added.

      

      
       
        Batch Delete

       
        Service template for deleting model instances in batches. The BatchDelete model operation node is automatically added.

      

      
       
        Batch Upsert

       
        Service template for adding model instances in batches. The Batch Upsert model operation node is automatically added.

      

      
       
        TQL Query

       
        Service template for querying data using TQL. The TQL Query node is automatically added. The data query TQL statements are automatically generated based on the selected model.

      

     
    
   

  

  
   
    Creating a Service (Create Template)
      The Create template is used to configure the service used for creating data. When you use the template to create a service, the system automatically imports model data to the service parameters based on the associated model.

    Creating a Service (Get List Template)
      The Get List template is used to configure the service used for querying the list. When you use the template to create a service, the system automatically imports model data to the service parameters based on the associated model.

   

   
    
     Parent topic: Configuring Services

name: Creating a Service (Get List Template)
title: Creating a Service (Get List Template)
text:
Creating a Service (Get List Template)
 
 
  
  

  
   The Get List template is used to configure the service used for querying the list. When you use the template to create a service, the system automatically imports model data to the service parameters based on the associated model.

   
    Context

    After a Get List template is selected and is associated with a model, the generated service automatically generates input and output parameters based on the model.

    There is a property type conversion from model fields to service input and output parameters. By default, the conversion is performed based on the following rules:

    
     The output for the field of the reference type on the model side is an ID, which is translated into a key code on the service side.

     The output for the field of the file type on the model side is a token, which is translated in to a JSON array on the service side. The JSON array contains detailed information about each file.

     The output for the field of the password type on the model side is ciphertext, which is translated into an empty string on the service side.

     The output for the field of the user and user group type on the model side is user:id group:id, which is translated to user:name group:name on the service side.

    

    You can modify the conversion rules through configuration.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Service.

     Click  to create a service. For example, to create the Get List service, select the Get List template and select the data model corresponding to the service. Click OK.
      

      

      

      

     Go to the service editing page and orchestrate the service. When the Get List template is selected, the GetList node is automatically displayed on the service editing page and the selected model is associated.

     (Optional) Set the search criteria. Select the get_list node, and click  to expand the configuration window.
      

      
       The template contains "active is $!active" and input parameters of the primary key as the query criteria. If other fields need to be added as input parameters for the query, you can set the query criteria as follows:
       
        Figure 1 Adding query criteria
        
       

      

      When adding a query criterion based on existing criteria, you need to select a query relationship, for example, and, and then click Add to add the configured criterion to the text box.

      If a variable starts with $!, the expression that contains the variable is invalid when the variable is empty (the logical expression with the smallest logic unit and the variable contained is deleted from the TQL), that is, the variable can be empty.

      For example, if doc_id=$!doc_id and active=$!active and doc_name=$!doc_name is configured in the query list condition and the associated model is demo/demo/demo_test, the whole query statement is select * from demo/demo/demo_test where doc_id=$!doc_id and active=$!active and doc_name=$!doc_name.

      If active=1 is entered and doc_id and doc_name are left blank during service execution, doc_id=$! doc_id and doc_name=$! doc_name does not take effect and the statement that is actually executed is select * from demo/demo/demo_test where active=1.

      

     (Optional) Set input parameters. Input parameters are resources at the service level. After the Get List template is used to generate a service, the common input parameters start, limit, sort, active, and dir and model fields are automatically set as input parameters. You can add other fields as filter criteria.

     (Optional) Set output parameters. Output parameters are resources at the service level. After the Get List template is used to generate a service, the common output parameters start, limit, total, and results are automatically set as output parameters. The results field contains the model fields.

     (Optional) Click  in the Service area on the right to configure more parameters, such as the validator and translator.

     Save the canvas.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After develop-state configuration is complete, click  in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment for the app to take effect immediately.            Name

          
           Setting Method

         

        
        
         
          
           Validator Type

          
           For text validation, set this parameter to text.

         

         
          
           Terminate Session Upon Failure

          
           When this function is enabled, if the number of consecutive verification failures exceeds 15 during service calling, the session will be terminated.

         

         
          
           Maximum Length

          
           Maximum text length.

         

         
          
           Disabled Characters

          
           Special characters that are not allowed. For example, if the special characters ($%) are not allowed, set this parameter to $%.

           The regular expression is used to restrict the input text. The value is a character string of digits and 26 English letters, for example, ^[A-Za-z0-9]+$.

           Error information displayed when an input parameter does not comply with the regular expression.

           For example, the message similar to the following is displayed: The parameter you entered does not comply with the rule. The input element can contain only digits and 26 letters.

name: Configuring TQL Expression Verification
title: Configuring TQL Expression Verification
text:
Configuring TQL Expression Verification
 
 
  
  

  
   TQL statements are used to perform operations on data. TQL expression verification provides a mechanism to verify the TQL format. This verification mode is used only when the TQL expression is stored in a field.

   
    Context

    During TQL expression verification, the length and the left and right values of the TQL query statement can be verified.

    For example, the TQL statement "xxx is yyy" is stored in a field. When left value verification is configured, "xxx" is verified. If "xxx" is not a field in the left value model, the verification fails.

    If right value verification is configured, the system verifies "yyy". If "yyy" is not a field in the right value model, the verification fails.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access a created project and module, and choose Service.

     On the editing page of Service, click the blank area on the canvas, the service configuration is displayed on the right. Click  on the right to expand the service configuration area.

     In the Input Parameter Configuration area, add a node of the string type and select Common verification from the Validator drop-down list box.
      

      
       Figure 1 Common verification
       
      

      

      

     Configuring TQL expression verification
      

      
       Figure 2 TQL expression verification
       
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 TQL expression verification parameters
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Maximum Length

          
           Maximum length of the TQL expression.

         

         
          
           Terminate Session Upon Failure

          
           When this function is enabled, if the number of consecutive verification failures exceeds 15 during service calling, the session will be terminated.

         

         
          
           TQL Query Expression

          
           Only the length of the TQL query expression is verified. If you select this option, you do not need to configure other information.

         

         
          
           lvalue model

          
           Model of the left value in the TQL comparison expression. If the corresponding model is selected and the left-value parameter is not in the model field, an error is reported during verification.

         

         
          
           rvalue model

          
           Model of the right value in the TQL comparison expression. If the corresponding model is selected and the right-value parameter is not in the model field, an error is reported during verification.

         

        
       
      

      

     Save the settings.

     Save the canvas.

name: Configuring Existence Verification
title: Configuring Existence Verification
text:
Configuring Existence Verification
 
 
  
  

  
   Data existence verification provides a mechanism to check whether the content of an input element exists in a model or service. If yes, the verification succeeds.

   
    Context

    For input parameter of the string type, the existence of the parameters can be verified.

    Data existence verification: If the value of the text1 field to be created is aaa, the value of the corresponding field configurations queried in the corresponding model or service must contain aaa. Otherwise, the creation fails.

    For example, when creating the member information, the system needs to check whether the member type exists.

    
     If the value of member_type is vip and vip exists in member_type during the verification, the verification is successfully.

     If the value of member_type is vvip and vvip does not exist in member_type during the verification, the verification fails.

    

    
     Figure 1 Existence verification using a model
     
    

    
     Figure 2 Existence verification using a service
     
    

    If the data existence verification fails, the service returns a failure message.

    Both the model and service can be used for verification in the preceding scenario. In the actual development, there are more complex scenarios. You can select a proper method based on site requirements.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access a created project and module, and choose Service.

     On the editing page of Service, click the blank area on the canvas, the service configuration is displayed on the right. Click  on the right to expand the service configuration area.

     In the Input Parameter Configuration area, add a node of the string type and select Existence verification from the Validator drop-down list box.
      

      
       Figure 3 Existence verification
       
      

      

     Optional: Configure the model existence verification The following describes how to configure a verification using a model and service. In the actual scenario, you need to select a proper mode based on the data.
      

      
       Figure 4 Model existence verification
       
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Model

          
           Target model for existence verification, that is, the model in which data is to be verified.

         

         
          
           Terminate Session Upon Failure

          
           When this function is enabled, if the number of consecutive verification failures exceeds 15 during service calling, the session will be terminated.

         

         
          
           Replica Name

          
           If the replica archiving is configured for model data, you can set the replica name of the model.

         

         
          
           Field

          
           Fields in the model.

         

         
          
           Condition

          
           Matching condition to be executed when model data needs to be verified. For example, if only the data in Enabled state needs to be matched, set active to true.

         

        
       
      

      
       Figure 5 Service existence verification
       
      

      
       
        
         Table 2 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Service

          
           Target service for existence verification, that is, the service in which data is to be verified.

         

         
          
           Terminate Session Upon Failure

          
           When this function is enabled, if the number of consecutive verification failures exceeds 15 during service calling, the session will be terminated.

         

         
          
           Field

          
           Fields in the service output parameters.

         

         
          
           Condition

          
           Input parameters of the service. Configure the input parameters based on the actual service in the format of {"name1":"value1","name2":"value2"}.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click OK to save the validator.

     Click OK to save the configuration.

     Save the canvas.

name: Configuring Run Script Verification
title: Configuring Run Script Verification
text:
Configuring Run Script Verification
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    The Run Script validator supports more flexible validation modes through scripts. For details about the syntax and examples of Run Script, see Service JavaScript Syntax and API Reference.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access a created project and module, and choose Service.

     On the editing page of Service, click the blank area on the canvas, the service configuration is displayed on the right. Click  on the right to expand the service configuration area.

     In the Input Parameter Configuration area, add the Run Script validator to the node that requires script verification.
      

      
       Figure 1 Run Script verification
       
      

      

     In the displayed dialog box, select an existing script or add a script. The script engine is compatible with historical engines. The engine versions are as follows:
      

      
       Latest: indicates the latest version, which is also the default version. The latest version is used by the current product and document by default.

       1.6: Not displayed by default and displayed only when the tenant system parameter support-engine-js-v16 is set to true. Version 1.6 is a transition version. It is used to be compatible with existing assets, instead of developing new assets. For details about the differences between versions 1.6 and the latest version, see Comparison Among Multi-Version APIs. The engine of version 1.6 can be replaced by the latest version. After the replacement, the rolled back is not supported.

       1.5: Not displayed by default and displayed only when a historical version of 1.5 has been imported and displayed. It is used only to be compatible with existing assets. There are great differences between versions 1.5 and the latest version. Obtain the documents of these two versions, respectively. The engine of version 1.5 can be replaced by the latest version. After the replacement, the rolled back is not supported.

      

      

     Optional: Edit the script. After the editing is complete, click Save, set the name of the script to be saved, and click OK. The script name is automatically displayed in the Script List area.
      

      
       Figure 2 Configuring Run Script
       
      

      

     (Optional) Run or debug the script. After a script is saved and deployed, you can run and debug the script step by step. For details, see 8.

name: Configuring the Element Translator
title: Configuring the Element Translator
text:
Configuring the Element Translator
 
 
  
  

  
   The element translator provides a mechanism to convert the input and output elements of a service to store or return the converted elements.

   

  

  
   
    Introduction to Element Translator Capabilities

    Common Functions
      The Common functions translator provides common translation functions.

    Date Time Converter
      The Date Time Converter translator is used to convert the time in the character string format based on the time zone.

    Merging Information
      The Merging Information translator provides a mechanism for combining data of multiple elements.

    Simple Data Mapping
      The Simple data mapping translator provides the simple data mapping function to map the source value to a translated value.

    Searching for Related Models
      The Searching for Related Models translator translates elements from related data models.

    UI Component Display Value Translation
      The Radio box, Check box, Datetime, and Select person components contain two parts: values stored in the system and values displayed on the GUI. The value returned by a service is used as values stored in the system of the component. When the component assigns values using values stored in the system, a query request is sent to obtain values displayed on the GUI. This deteriorates page performance. The UI Component Display Value Translation translator is used to translate the values returned by the service to two parts: values stored in the system and JSON object of the values displayed on the GUI.

    Internationalization Translatori18n translator allows a service to display its contents in the language the same as the browser language. In the output parameter configuration of the service, a field returned by the service is an internationalization key value, which is then translated into the corresponding language by the internationalization translator.

    File Permission Translator

    Run Script Translator

    Attachment Translator

name: Common Functions
title: Common Functions
text:
Common Functions
 
 
  
  

  
   The Common functions translator provides common translation functions.

   
    Context

    Table 1 describes the methods and functions of the Common functions translator.

    
     
     
      
       Table 1 Description of methods of the Common functions translator
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Method Name

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         result()

        
         Returns the result.

       

       
        
         xmlToJson()

        
         Converts XML objects of input/output elements into JSON objects.

         For example, if the XML object is <abc><name>jack</name><sex>boy</sex></abc>, the JSON object is {"name":"jack","sex":"boy"}.

       

       
        
         safeHtml()

        
         Securely filter the input HTML.

       

       
        
         empty()

        
         Returns an empty value.

       

       
        
         currentUser()

        
         Returns the current login user.

       

       
        
         currentTime()

        
         Returns the current time.

       

       
        
         userGroupAllInfoTranslator()

        
         Converts fields of the user group type, including all user group fields.

       

       
        
         userGroupDisplayTranslator()

        
         Convert the user group field type to the name display type.

       

       
        
         UserIdToUserAccount()

        
         Converts the user ID into the user name.

       

       
        
         utc2Local()

        
         Converts the UTC time into the local time.

       

       
        
         Local2utc()

        
         Converts the local time into the UTC time.

       

       
        
         utc2LocalWithDST()

        
         Converts the UTC time to the local time and marks the DST. After the DST starts, the UTC time is converted to the local time to differentiate the DST. After the time conversion, the DST suffix is used for the DST time.

       

       
        
         utc2Long()

        
         Converts the UTC time into a timestamp of the long integer type.

       

       
        
         aesDecrypt()

        
         Decrypts the input/output element of the service using the AES algorithm.

       

       
        
         aesEncrypt()

        
         Encrypts the input/output element of the service using the AES algorithm.

       

       
        
         copyFile()

        
         Copies files.

       

       
        
         UserIdToUserAccountWithoutException

        
         Converts the user ID to the user name. If an exception occurs during the conversion, the user name is displayed as unknown.

       

       
        
         long2utc

        
         Converts a timestamp of a long integer type to the UTC time.

       

       
        
         long2local

        
         Converts a timestamp of a long integer type to a local time.

       

       
        
         toPinyin()

        
         For the string type, Chinese characters can be converted to Chinese pinyin. The pinyin translator supports only basic Chinese characters, that is, Chinese characters ranging from 19968 to 40869 (Unicode code 4E00 to 9FA5). Custom separators are supported.

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access a created project and module, and choose Service.

title: Simple Data Mapping
text:
Simple Data Mapping
 
 
  
  

  
   The Simple data mapping translator provides the simple data mapping function to map the source value to a translated value.

   
    Context

    By using the Simple data mapping translator in input parameters, the input character string mbb is mapped to m to store it in the database.

    By using the Simple data mapping translator in output parameters, the returned information m can be mapped to mbb and then returned.

    For example, if the following mapping is required for the element, you can configure the mapping by referring to the procedure in this topic.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Mapping relationship

name: Searching for Related Models
title: Searching for Related Models
text:
Searching for Related Models
 
 
  
  

  
   The Searching for Related Models translator translates elements from related data models.

   
    Context

    During the data query, multiple data models need to be queried to obtain corresponding data.

    For example, in a member information system, there are two tables storing the member information, one is a basic information table baseinfo that is used to store names, and the other is a contact information table contact that is used to store phone numbers and email addresses.

    When a query service needs to be provided and all information needs to be queried, you can search for the related model. When the information in baseinfo is matched, contact_code is returned based on baseinfo. In this case, the contact information can be obtained from the contact table.

    
     Figure 1 Example of searching for related models
     
    

    In the actual scenario, such information is encrypted. This is only an example and does not involve encryption and decryption conversion.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access a created project and module, and choose Service.

     On the editing page of Service, click the blank area on the canvas, the service configuration is displayed on the right. Click  on the right to expand the service configuration area.

     In the row that contains the parameter node for which a translator is to be configured, click  on the right of the Translator box and configure the value translation mode.
      

      
       Figure 2 Value translation mode
       
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Correlation Model

          
           Target model to be searched for. Note that this model is not the model associated with the service.

         

         
          
           Condition

          
           Matching condition for querying data in the related mode. The static and dynamic conditions are supported.

           
            For static condition, you can set a specific value for matching.

            For dynamic condition, you can set a parameter in the related model to match the output parameters of the node.

           

           For example, you need to match contact_code in the contact model with contact_code in the baseinfo table to find the required data.

         

         
          
           Default Mapping

          
           Mapping between the parameter to be translated in the Output Parameters area and the parameter value obtained through the related model. The mapping is used to transfer the values obtained from the related model to the output parameters.

           
            Element Name: The options in the drop-down list are the parameters to be translated in the output parameters.

            Property Name: Property name of the related model.

           

         

        
       
      

      

     Click OK to save the translator configuration.

     Click OK to save the node property configuration.

     Save settings of the service on the canvas.

    

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    Deploy the service that has been configured with a translator to the runtime state in one-lick mode.

name: UI Component Display Value Translation
title: UI Component Display Value Translation
text:
UI Component Display Value Translation
 
 
  
  

  
   The Radio box, Check box, Datetime, and Select person components contain two parts: values stored in the system and values displayed on the GUI. The value returned by a service is used as values stored in the system of the component. When the component assigns values using values stored in the system, a query request is sent to obtain values displayed on the GUI. This deteriorates page performance. The UI Component Display Value Translation translator is used to translate the values returned by the service to two parts: values stored in the system and JSON object of the values displayed on the GUI.

   
    Context

    The UI Component Display Value Translation translator can be used only in front-end services to query the return value and display value of data.

name: Internationalization Translator
title: Internationalization Translator
text:
Internationalization Translator
 
 
  
  

  
   i18n translator allows a service to display its contents in the language the same as the browser language. In the output parameter configuration of the service, a field returned by the service is an internationalization key value, which is then translated into the corresponding language by the internationalization translator.

   
    Prerequisites

    You have configured the required model and service.

   

   
    Context

    When a user queries the data, if the fields in the data need to be internationalized, the internationalization translator is required.

    For example, if the queried member information contains the member type data in different languages, the internationalization display on the page is required.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Member information
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Member Name

        
         Member Type

        
         Member Type (in English)

       

      
      
       
        
         David

        
         vip

        
         VIP Member

       

       
        
         Bob

        
         normal

        
         Normal Member

       

      
     
    

    If the internationalization conversion is not performed on the page, the value stored by the data is displayed, as shown in the following figure.

    
     Figure 1 Display of non-internationalized data
     
    

    vip and normal can be internationalized using the internationalization translator.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Configure the internationalization resources.
      

      
       Choose I18n.

       Add a bundle and configure the internationalization properties.
        
         Figure 2 Internationalization properties
         
        

      

      

     On the Service page, select the service for which the internationalization translator needs to be configured, for example, the member information query service member_info_get_list.

     Click  in the Properties area on the right, and configure the output parameters of the service.

     In the row that contains the parameter node for which a translator is to be configured, click  on the right of the Translator box and configure the value translation mode.
      

      
       Figure 3 i18n translator
       
      

      
       
        
         Table 2 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Bundle Name

          
           Click , select the configured internationalization bundle, and select the bundle from the drop-down list. The bundle must contain the internationalization resources to be internationalized.

         

         
          
           The data contains the bundle name.

          
           Select this parameter based on whether the actual name contains the bundle name.

           For example, if the bundle name is type, the internationalization resource properties are vip and normal, and the data to be internationalized is vip and normal (that is, the data does not contain the bundle name), you do not need to select this parameter.

           If the stored data is type.vip and type.normal, you need to select this parameter.

         

         
          
           Auto Match Bundle

          
           If this parameter is selected, you do not select the bundle name. The system dynamically queries and matches the internationalization information based on the non-translated data (in the format of "Bundle.Property").

           In this scenario, the data format must be "Bundle.Property", that is, the data must contain the bundle name. Otherwise, the internalization information cannot be automatically matched.

           For example, if the bundle name is type, the internationalization resource properties are vip and normal, and the data to be internationalized is vip and normal, the bundle cannot be automatically matched. Only the data type.vip and type.normal can be automatically matched.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click OK to save the translator configuration.
      

      
       Figure 4 Output parameters of the internationalization translator

name: File Permission Translator
title: File Permission Translator
text:
File Permission Translator
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    The apps provided by the developers can be used by multiple users. For example, if user A uploads a file and there is no special permission control, user B can view and download the file.

    The file permission translator is only used to the Get and Get List services.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access a created project and module, and choose Service.

     On the editing page of Service, select get or get_list in the canvas.

     Click  of the property window on the right.

     In the Output Parameter Configuration area, select the field whose Format is file, and click  in the drop-down list of Translator.
      

      
       Figure 1 Output Parameter Configuration
       
      

      

     Configure the file permission translator, as shown in Figure 2. The translator for the field of the file type is File Permission Translator by default and cannot be changed.
      

      
       Figure 2 Configuring the file permission translator

            Figure 3 Viewing the permission path
            
           

         

         
          
           Update

          
           Permission item to update the file.

           The permission Update depends on the permissions Create and Delete. That is, if Update is selected for a permission, Create and Delete are also added. If Update is selected, Create and Delete cannot be deselected.
