           Name of an export template.

         

         
          
           Service

          
           Service (such as the GetList service) that corresponds to each row of data in an Excel file.

           The selected service must be able to receive start and limit as input parameters, and return the actual value of total. The limit parameter is used only to limit the handling batch.

           The following is an example of the return value format for the service:

           {
  "start": 0,
  "limit": 1000,
  "total": 1,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "095adb8b-f7d8-11ee-b749-0255ac12016c",
      "keycode": "AB10000",
      "equipment_code": "AB10000",
      "active": true,
    }
  ]
}

         

         
          
           Service Method

          
           The system orchestration service supports only POST requests.

         

         
          
           Open Level

          
           Open level of the service.

           
            Module Level: Only the orchestration elements in the current module can call this service.

            Project Level: In the current project, orchestration elements in different modules can call this service.

            Public: Orchestration elements of all projects can call this service.

           

         

         
          
           Template settings

          
           Excel Template

          
           Template file used for data export.

           The Excel template takes effect only when Skip Setting Headers is enabled.

           
            If Skip Setting Headers is enabled and a template file is uploaded, you can export data using this template file.

            If Skip Setting Headers is enabled but no template file is uploaded, the exported data does not contain table headers and data is written from the defined start row number.

           

           If both Skip Setting Headers and Support Internationalized Template are enabled, templates in Chinese and English can be provided separately.

         

         
          
           Sheet

          
           Name of the sheet in the exported Excel file. If an Excel template is uploaded, you can select a sheet in the template from the drop-down list box. If no Excel template is uploaded, you can enter a sheet name. The sheet in the exported Excel file is named based on the entered name.

         

         
          
           Support Internationalized Template

          
           When this function is enabled, the sheet name and column name of the worksheet can be internationalized.

         

         
          
           (Displayed when Support Internationalized Template is enabled)

           Template Language

          
           Set the language of the template to be uploaded.

         

         
          
           (Displayed when Support Internationalized Template is enabled)

           Select Bundle

          
           Click  and select an internationalization bundle resource. For details about how to create an internationalization bundle resource, see Configuring the Internationalization Information.

         

         
          
           Export settings

          
           Start Row Number

          
           Row in an Excel file from which data is exported. The first row is Column. Therefore, data is exported starting from the second row.

         

         
          
           Export File Name

          
           Name of an exported file

         

         
          
           Advanced settings

          
           Check Download User

          
           When this function is enabled, only the user who creates the task can download error logs.

         

         
          
           Skip Setting Headers

          
           When this function is enabled, the exported file does not contain table headers. That is, the column name in the field mapping is skipped and data is directly written from the start row.

         

         
          
           Auto Mapping

          
           Automatically map the exported fields based on the model.

         

         
          
           Front Access

          
           Whether the front end is allowed to call the service.

         

         
          
           (Displayed when Front Access is enabled)

           Permission Items

          
           When Front Access is enabled, you need to configure the front-end access permissions. For example, if permission item A is configured, only users with permission item A can access the service. For details about how to configure permission items, see Configuring Permissions.

         

         
          
           (Displayed when Auto Mapping is enabled)

           Model

          
           Model that corresponds to each row of data in a CSV file.

         

         
          
           Filter Page

          
           Whether to enable page-based data export by filter criteria. If this parameter is selected, page-based data export by filter criteria is enabled.

         

         
          
           Encrypt

          
           Whether data is encrypted before being exported.

         

         
          
           (Displayed when Encrypt is enabled)

           Manual Input

          
           
            When this function is enabled, you need to manually enter the password for exporting data.

            When the function is disabled, the password is generated randomly. When Manual Input is disabled, Send Email is automatically enabled and cannot be disabled, indicating that the randomly generated password is sent through an email.

           

         

         
          
           (Displayed when Encrypt is enabled)

           Send Email

          
           Sending passwords through emails depends on the deployment of the email service.

           When this function is enabled, the manually entered or automatically generated passwords can be sent based on the configuration of Manual Input.

         

         
          
           Excel field mapping

           
             NOTE: 
            
             In the Fields area, you can click Load from Template to upload a template file for quick configuration of field mappings.

            

           

          
           Message Element

          
           Output parameter of the data export service.

         

         
          
           Column

          
           Column No. in the Excel file, for example, A, B, and C.

           
             NOTE: 
            
             In the Fields area, when you move a field up or down, the column No. is automatically updated. Click Column Refresh to update the column No. sequence.

            

           

         

         
          
           Header

          
           Column name, which corresponds to the table header in the Excel file.

           When Support Internationalized Template is enabled, the column name can be configured as an internationalization property. For example, if the internationalization bundle i18n_member_info is selected and the bundle contains member_id and member_name, the property name in the column name (for example, the part except the prefix in the Property Name column in the following figure) does not need to contain the prefix. When the service is called on the page, the template obtained by the user can be adapted to the language environment selected by the user.

         

         
          
           Type

          
           Type of the field to which the exported data is written into an Excel file. For details about the field types, see Table 1.

           When Type is set to Hyperlink, the called service needs to be configured as follows.

           
            Service output parameter. The corresponding message element must be of the Object type and contain the address and text fields. The value of address is the hyperlink address, and the value of text is the hyperlink display text.
             

            In the service, you need to use a script to assign values to the address and text fields. For example, after data is obtained through the get_list node, you need to add a script node to map the obtained parameter values to the address and text fields.
             _context.message._values[0].hyperlink = { "address":_context.message._values[0].address,"text":_context.message._values[0].textview};
return _context.message;

            The hyperlink fields (fields of the Object type) in the service output parameter need to be configured in the Excel Field Mapping area as follows.
             

           

         

         
          
           Format

          
           Format in which the exported data is written into an Excel file.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Field description.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Submit.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After develop-state configuration is complete, click  in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment for the app to take effect immediately. If Enable Hot Deployment has been enabled in the Deployment Configuration dialog box, the system automatically deploys the service after identifying configuration changes.

text:
Configuring the CSV Data Export Service
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    Services have been configured. For details, see Configuring Services.

   

   
    Context

    When a user views data on the front end, there is a scenario where the user needs to export the data as an offline file and store or transfer the file locally.

    Therefore, data export is supported during app development. The overall data export capability is implemented through configuring the data export service, associating the configured service used for querying the list, and using the export button for page development.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Select the module to be operated.

     Choose Data Export.

     Click Create. Set Export to CSV.

     Configure parameters as required.
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters of the CSV export template
        
        
         
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter Type

          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Basic settings

          
           Name

          
           Name of an export template.

         

         
          
           Service

          
           Service (such as the GetList service) that corresponds to each row of data in a CSV file.

         

         
          
           Service Method

          
           The system orchestration service supports only POST requests.

           Open level of the service

           
            Module Level: Only the orchestration elements in the current module can call this service.

            Project Level: In the current project, orchestration elements in different modules can call this service.

            Public: Orchestration elements of all projects can call this service.

           

         

         
          
           Template settings

           When this function is enabled, the template column names can be internationalized.

         

         
          
           (Displayed when Support Internationalized Template is enabled)

           Select Bundle

          
           Click  and select an internationalization bundle resource. For details about how to create an internationalization bundle resource, see Configuring the Internationalization Information.

         

         
          
           Export settings

          
           File Zip Type

          
           Format of the exported file. Currently, csv and tsv are supported.

         

         
          
           File Compression Type

          
           The file is compressed into a ZIP or GZ package.

         

         
          
           Export File Name

          
           Name of an exported file

         

         
          
           Advanced settings

          
           Check Download User

          
           When this function is enabled, only the user who creates the task can download error logs.

         

         
          
           Auto Mapping

          
           Automatically map the exported fields based on the model.

         

         
          
           (Displayed when Auto Mapping is enabled)

           Model

          
           Model that corresponds to each row of data in a CSV file.

         

         
          
           Front Access

          
           Whether the front end is allowed to call the service.

         

         
          
           (Displayed when Front Access is enabled)

           Permission Items

          
           When Front Access is enabled, you need to configure the front-end access permissions. For example, if permission item A is configured, only users with permission item A can access the service. For details about how to configure permission items, see Configuring Permissions.

         

         
          
           Filter Page

          
           Whether to enable page-based data export by filter criteria. If this parameter is selected, page-based data export by filter criteria is enabled.

         

         
          
           Encrypt

          
           Whether data is encrypted before being exported.

         

         
          
           (Displayed when Encrypt is enabled)

           Manual Input

          
           When this function is enabled, the password is entered by the user. When this function is disabled, the password is randomly generated and sent by email.

         

         
          
           (Displayed when Encrypt is enabled)

           Send Email

          
           Sending passwords through emails depends on the deployment of the email service.

           When this function is enabled, the manually entered or automatically generated passwords can be sent based on the configuration of Manual Input.

         

         
          
           Excel field mapping

           
             NOTE: 
            
             In the Fields area, you can click Load from Template to upload a template file for quick configuration of field mappings.

            

           

          
           Message Element

          
           Output parameter name in a service.

         

         
          
           Column

          
           Column number exported to the CSV file, for example, A, B, and C.

           
             NOTE: 
            
             In the Fields area, when you move a field up or down, the column No. is automatically updated. Click Column Refresh to update the column No. sequence.

            

           

         

         
          
           Header

          
           When Support Internationalized Template is enabled, the column name can be configured as an internationalization property.

           For example, if the internationalization bundle i18n_member_info is selected and the member_id and member_name properties are contained, the property name entered in the column name does not need to contain the prefix. When the service is called on the page, the template available for the user can be adapted based on the selected language.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Field description.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Submit.

    After develop-state configuration is complete, click  in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment for the app to take effect immediately. If Enable Hot Deployment has been enabled in the Deployment Configuration dialog box, the system automatically deploys the service after identifying configuration changes.

title: Configuring the Page for Data Importing
text:
Configuring the Page for Data Importing
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    After the template for importing and exporting data is configured, a page for importing and exporting data needs to be provided for users. In this way, users can use page components to call data import and export services.

    When a model is created based on ADC and services and pages are automatically generated, the automatically generated xx_xx_grid page contains the Import button by default and can call the automatically generated xx_xx_import page.

    This section describes how to assemble and configure a page when a developer needs to create a page to call the Excel service.

    
     Figure 1 Importing configurations
     
    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Select the module to be operated.

     Create a blank page for importing attachments.
      

      
       Choose Page.

       Click  to create a page.

       Set Page Name to import_goods_info, select Blank Template, and click OK.

       In the left pane, search for Excel Import Panel and drag it to the canvas.
        
         Figure 2 Dragging the Excel Import Panel component to the canvas
         
        

       Configure the properties of the component on the right.
        
         Figure 3 Configuring properties of the Excel Import Panel component
         
        

       Save the page.

      

      

     Add a button on the info_goods_grid page to link to the import_goods_info page.
      

      
       Choose Page, and select the existing info_goods_grid page.

       Search for the Window button on the left, and drag it to the toolbar in the canvas.
        
         Figure 4 Window button
         
        

       Configure the properties of the window button.
        
         Figure 5 Window button properties
         
        

       Save the page.

      

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    Preview and debug the info_goods_grid page.

    
     Figure 6 Previewing the page
     
    

    
     Figure 7 Viewing the data import result
     
    

    To view Excel import operations, choose Products and Services > Log Management > Data Import Logs to check the import logs in the runtime-state environment. If the import fails, you can view the details to locate the fault.

    
     Figure 8 Importing log using an Excel file

name: Configuring Page-based Data Export
title: Configuring Page-based Data Export
text:
Configuring Page-based Data Export
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    Data can be exported based on page. In actual application scenarios, data may be frequently added. As a result, duplicate data may be exported. This problem can be resolved through the pagination configurations.

    This section describes how to modify the configurations of the data list query service and data export service automatically generated after the model creation.

    Assume that the data model info_goods has been created and services and pages are automatically generated. The following elements are automatically generated:

    
     info_goods_get_list

     info_goods_export: The data export service info_goods_export calls the data list query service info_goods_get_list.

     info_goods_grid: Click Export on the page to call the data export service info_goods_export to export data.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the project to be operated.

     Select the module to be operated.

     Select Service and select a created data list query service or a data list query service automatically generated after the model creation, for example, info_goods_get_list.

     Configure extended conditions for the get_list node.
      

      
       Select the get_list node and click  to edit it.
        

       In the Input Parameter Configuration area, select Add ext_condition_tql.
        

        

       Click OK.

      

      

     Set the input parameters of the service.
      

      
       Click the blank area in the canvas and click  in the property area on the right.

       In the Input Parameter Configuration area, select the root node, click it, and add the input parameter ext_condition_tql.
        

        

       Click OK.

      

      

     Click  in the canvas to save the service configuration.

     Select Data Export, click the automatically generated data export service info_goods_export, enable Filter Page, and click Submit.
      

      

      

      

     Configure the page.
      

      
       Choose Page and click info_goods_grid. The page designer is displayed.

       Select the Export component. By default, the Export component calls the info_goods_export service to export data. You need to add the input parameter configuration of the service.
        

       In the displayed dialog box, click Save.

       Click  in the page designer to save the configuration.

      

      

     Deploy the app in one-click mode and build data for verification.

name: Configuring Permissions
title: Configuring Permissions
text:
Configuring Permissions
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     The menu Permission has been displayed in the navigation pane.

    

   

   
    Context

    During app development, if developers need to differentiate permissions for different functions in the app, they can configure permissions. For example, in a document management system, the document administrator can view, add, edit, and delete documents, and common users can only view documents. In this case, you need to set different permissions for different functions in the app and assign the permissions to corresponding roles. If you select different roles when creating a user, the roles will have different permissions.

    After a permission item is configured, select the permission in the related resource configuration.

    

    
     
      
       Table 1 Right configuration
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Orchestration Element Type

        
         Authentication Type

        
         Configuration

       

      
      
       
        
         Model

        
         The metadata and data of models are controlled based on the menu permissions.

        
         Configure the permission in the Properties area on the right. If the related parameters are not configured, the permission is not controlled.

         

         

       

       
        
         Service

        
         By default, Authentication Type of the service is Logged-in, that is, the permission is not controlled. To control the permission, you can set Authentication Type to Logged-in and Authorized, and select the corresponding permission item. Only the user who has this permission item can access the service.

        
         

       

       
        
         Page component

        
         To control the permission of the components on the page, such as the redirection button and window button, you need to obtain and configure the permission URI.

        
         The value of Permission URI of the components on the page is the configured permission of the current module. You can select the required permission from the drop-down list.

         

       

       
        
         Menu

        
         A permission item is automatically generated for each menu. The permission item needs to be assigned to a role.

        
         

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Permission.

     On the Permission Tree tab page, click Add Permission to configure permission properties.
      

      

      
       
       
        Display Name: name displayed when a permission is assigned to a role. Multiple languages are supported.
         
          If only one language needs to be configured, directly enter the text and select the entered text.

          If multiple languages need to be configured, ensure that the internationalization configuration has been completed. For details, see Configuring the Internationalization Information. Click  next to the Display Name area, select the i18n bundle, and select the configured i18n bundle property from the drop-down list.

         

        Add Parent Permission: category of a permission item. Click  next to Add Parent Permission and select a created permission item as the parent permission of the permission item.

       

      

      

     Click Create.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After develop-state configuration is complete, click  in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment for the app to take effect immediately. If Enable Hot Deployment has been enabled in the Deployment Configuration dialog box, the system automatically deploys the service after identifying configuration changes.

    
     Select permissions in the specific resource. For example, for service permission configuration, Permission items is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to Logged-in and Authorized. You only need to select the configured permission items.
     
      Figure 1 Configuring service permission
      
     

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Configuring Permissions and Roles

name: Configuring Roles
title: Configuring Roles
text:
Configuring Roles
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    In a same app, you can use roles to differentiate permissions for different users.

    For example, a common user can only view pages and services. The administrator can add, delete, modify, and query pages and services.

    In this case, you can create a common user role and only assign the role the permission for viewing pages and services. Create an administrator role and assign permissions for adding, deleting, modifying, and querying pages and services.

    When creating a user, you can select different roles for the user to obtain different permissions.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Permission.

     On the Role Set tab page, click Add role.

     Set the role name and add permissions to the preset role. You can directly enter the description or select an internationalization bundle and then select the corresponding internationalization resource.
      

      

      

      

     Click Create to save the settings.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After develop-state configuration is complete, click  in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment for the app to take effect immediately. If Enable Hot Deployment has been enabled in the Deployment Configuration dialog box, the system automatically deploys the service after identifying configuration changes.

    Permission Compatibility is available only when historical legacy assets are imported. If a project is created based on ADC 2.X or later, skip this section.

    The permission compatibility function can be used for historical legacy assets to manage permission items in a unified manner. The logic for managing permission items is the same as that in earlier versions but different from that in the current version.

           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Name of a resource that requires permission control. For example, if permission control is required for a service, set this parameter to the service name.

         

         
          
           Type

          
           Type of the resource that requires permission control.

           
            service

            data_import: data import service

            data_export: data export service

            model

            page

           Full path of the permission. The format is "/{Project name}/{Module name}/{Permission item name}". Set Project name and Module name based on the project and module where current operations are performed, and set Permission item name as required.

Configuring a Timer
 
 
  
  

  
   A timer is used to define a one-off or periodic job that is executed at specified time.

  

  
   
    Introduction to Timers

    Configuring a Repeat Timer
      A Repeat timer is used to configure jobs that are executed at a fixed interval and number of times.

name: Introduction to Timers
title: Introduction to Timers
text:
Introduction to Timers
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Basic Concepts

    Timer: indicates the automatic jobs created by the user to periodically call ADC services. The Job page is displayed for users on ADC. Users can periodically call interfaces or services to execute jobs in feature scenarios.

   

   
    Timer Types

    
     Repeat: used to configure jobs that are executed at a fixed interval and number of times.

     Cron: used to configure complex cron jobs. Scheduling can be defined using the cron expression.

    

   

   
    Execution of Cron Jobs

    After a job is configured in the develop-state environment, deploy it in the runtime-state environment. Then, the job enters the execution state based on rules.

    You can view the execution information about the scheduled jobs on the Products and Services > Administration > Cron Jobs page in the runtime-state environment.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Configuring a Timer

name: Configuring a Repeat Timer
title: Configuring a Repeat Timer
text:
Configuring a Repeat Timer
 
 
  
  

  
   A Repeat timer is used to configure jobs that are executed at a fixed interval and number of times.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     A project and a module have been created.

     The Job menu has been displayed. For details, see Configuring the Module Navigation Menus.

     The service to be called by the scheduled job has been configured.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access a created project and module.

     Choose Job.

     Click  to create a scheduled job.
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Job Name

          
           Job name. The value can contain only lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_). In the runtime-state environment, you can search for tasks by setting Job Name and Job Label.

         

         
          
           Job Label

          
           Job label. The value can contain Chinese characters, English letters, digits, and symbols. You are advised to set this value to characters that can be easily identified. In the runtime-state environment, you can search for tasks by setting Job Name and Job Label.

         

         
          
           Status

          
           
            Enabled: The timer is available. After the deployment, the timer starts to run based on the configurations.

            Disabled: The timer does not start after the deployment.

           

         

         
          
           Job Type

          
           
            Repeat: A Repeat timer is used to configure simple jobs that are executed at a fixed interval. Select Repeat.

            Cron: A Cron timer is used to customize complex scheduled jobs.

           

         

         
          
           Periods

          
           This parameter is displayed when Job Type is set to Repeat. This parameter indicates the number of repetition times of the job interval. For example, if Interval is set to hour and Periods is set to 1, the execution period is 1 hour.

           The execution period of a job is the product of the number of periods and the interval. The minimum value is 30 seconds.

         

         
          
           Interval

          
           This parameter is displayed when Job Type is set to Repeat. This parameter indicates the unit of the interval for executing a scheduled job. The options are second, minute, hour, day, and month.

         

         
          
           Repetitions

          
           Number of execution times, which can be calculated by using the following formula: Number of execution times = Number of repetition times + 1. 0 indicates that the job is executed once, and -1 indicates that the job is executed permanently.

         

         
          
           Start Time

          
           Time when the scheduled job starts.

         

         
          
           End Time

          
           Time when the scheduled job ends.

         

         
          
           Time Zone ID

          
           Time zone to which the start time and end time belong. The UTC time is used by default.

         

         
          
           Forbid Concurrent Execution

          
           Whether to forbid concurrent execution. If this parameter is set to Yes, the next job will not be scheduled on time if the current job is not complete.

         

         
          
           Interface

          
           API used to execute scheduled jobs.

         

         
          
           Request Type

          
           Job request type.

         

         
          
           Interface Parameters

          
           Input parameters for the service selected from the Interface drop-down list. The value is in JSON format.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Timer description.

         

         
          
           Advanced Settings

          
           
            Perform Callback as System User: execution user displayed in the callback service job record. If this parameter is set to Yes, the execution user in the job record is the system user.

            Callback Language: language set for the callback service. By default, the language of the user who creates the scheduled job is used.

           

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Create.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After develop-state configuration is complete, click  in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment for the app to take effect immediately. If Enable Hot Deployment has been enabled in the Deployment Configuration dialog box, the system automatically deploys the service after identifying configuration changes.

    After the deployment is complete, choose Products and Services > Administration > Cron Jobs in the runtime-state environment to check the execution status of the scheduled job.

name: Configuring a Cron Timer
title: Configuring a Cron Timer
text:
Configuring a Cron Timer
 
 
  
  

  
   A Cron timer is used to configure scheduled jobs with complex time rules.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     A project and a module have been created.

     The Job menu has been displayed. For details, see Configuring the Module Navigation Menus.

     The service to be called by the scheduled job has been configured.

    

   

   
    Context

    A Cron timer is used to configure scheduled jobs with complex time rules based on the Cron expression. Table 1 describes the syntax rules of the Cron expression.

    
     
     
      
       Table 1 Cron expression description
      
      
       
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Location

        
         Time Domain

        
         Allowed Value

        
         Special Value

       

      
      
       
        
         1

        
         Second

        
         0-59

        
         , - * /

       

       
        
         2

        
         Minute

        
         0-59

        
         , - * /

       

       
        
         3

        
         Hour

        
         0-23

        
         , - * /

       

       
        
         4

        
         Date

        
         1-31

        
         , - * ? / L W C

       

       
        
         5

        
         Month

        
         1-12

        
         , - * /

       

       
        
         6

        
         Day-of-week

        
         1-7

        
         , - * ? / L C #

       

       
        
         7

        
         Year (optional)

        
         1-31

        
         , - * /

       

      
     
    

    Table 2 describes the guidelines for use of special values.

    
     
     
      
       Table 2 Description of special values
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Special Value

        
         Name

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         *

        
         Asterisk (*)

        
         It is used in all fields, indicating every time point in the corresponding time domain. For example, it indicates every minute in the minute field.

       

       
        
         ?

        
         Question mark (?)

        
         It is used only in date and day-of-week fields. It usually indicates a meaningless value and is equivalent to a dot.

       

       
        
         -

        
         Minus sign (–)

        
         It indicates a range, for example, the value 10–12 used in the hour field indicates 10:00 to 12:00, that is, 10:00, 11:00, and 12:00.

       

       
        
         ,

        
         Comma (,)

        
         It indicates a list value, for example, the value MON, WED, FRI used in the day-of-week field indicates Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

       

       
        
         /

        
         Slash (/)

        
         For example, x/y indicates a sequence with the same steps, in which x is the start step value and y is the incremental step value. For example, 0/15 used in the minute field indicates 0s, 15s, 30s, and 45s, and 5/15 used in the minute field indicates 5s, 20s, 35s, and 50s. You can also use */y, which is equivalent to 0/y.

       

       
        
         #

        
         Pound sign (#)

        
         It is used only in the day-of-week field, indicating a workday in the current month. For example, 6#3 indicates the third Friday in the current month (6 indicates Friday and #3 indicates the third sequence), and 4#5 indicates the fifth Wednesday in the current month. If the current month does not have the fifth Wednesday, the timer will not be triggered.

       

       
        
         L

        
         Last

        
         It is used only in the date and day-of-week fields, indicating Last. However, it has different meanings in the two fields. In the date field, L indicates the last day of a month, for example, January 31 or February 28 February in a non-leap year. If L is used in the day-of-week field, it indicates Saturday, which is equivalent to using 7 in the day-of-week field. However, if L is used in the day-of-week field and a number X is followed by L, it indicates the last X day of this month. For example, 6L indicates the last Friday of this month.

       

       
        
         W

        
         Workday

        
         This character is used only together with the date field, indicating the workday nearest to the date. For example, 15W indicates the workday nearest to the fifteenth day of this month. If the fifteenth day of this month is Saturday, the fourteenth day which is Friday in this month is matched. If the fifteenth day of this month is Sunday, the sixteenth day which is Monday in this month is matched. If the fifteenth day of this month is Tuesday, this day is matched. Ensure that the matched date is in the same month as the specified day. For example, 1W indicates that if the first day of this month is Saturday, the third day which is Monday in this month rather than the last day of the last month is matched. W can specify only a single date but not a date range.

       

       
        
         LW

        
         Last Workday

        
         It is used in the date field, which indicates the last workday of the current month.

       

       
        
         C

        
         Calendar

        
         It is used only in the date and week fields, indicating Calendar. It indicates the date associated as planned. If the date is not associated, all dates in the calendar are associated. For example, 5C in the date field indicates the first day after the fifth day in the calendar. In the week field, 1C is the first day after Sunday in the calendar.

       

      
     
    

    The Cron expression is case-insensitive to special characters and English abbreviations that represent the days of the week. Table 3 describes the Cron expression examples

    
     
     
      
       Table 3 Examples of the Cron expression examples
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Expression

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         0 0 12 * * ?

        
         The timer is triggered at 12:00 every day.

       

       
        
         0 15 10 ? * *

        
         The timer is triggered at 10:15 every day.

       

       
        
         0 15 10 * * ?

        
         The timer is triggered at 10:15 every day.

       

       
        
         0 15 10 * * ? *

        
         The timer is triggered at 10:15 every day.

       

       
        
         0 15 10 * * ? 2008

        
         The timer was triggered at 10:15 every day in 2008.

       

       
        
         0 * 14 * * ?

        
         The timer is triggered once every minute from 14:00 to 14:59 every day.

       

       
        
         0 0/5 14 * * ?

        
         The timer is triggered once every 5 minutes from 14:00 to 14:55 every day.

       

       
        
         0 0/5 14,18 * * ?

        
         The timer is triggered once every 5 minutes from 14:00 to 15:00 and once every 5 minutes from 18:00 to 19:00 every day.

       

       
        
         0 0-5 14 * * ?

        
         The timer is triggered once every minute from 14:00 to 14:05 every day.

       

       
        
         0 10,44 14 ? 3 WED

        
         The timer is triggered at 14:10 and 14:44 on Wednesday of March every year.

       

       
        
         0 15 10 ? * MON-FRI

        
         The timer is triggered at 10:15 from every Monday to Friday.

       

       
        
         0 15 10 15 * ?

        
         The timer is triggered at 10:15 on 15 of each month.

       

       
        
         0 15 10 L * ?

        
         The timer is triggered at 10:15 on the last day of each month.

       

       
        
         0 15 10 ? * 6L

        
         The timer is triggered at 10:15 on the last Friday of each month.

       

       
        
         0 15 10 ? * 6L 2007-2009

        
         The timer was triggered at 10:15 on the last Friday of each month in 2007, 2008, and 2009.

       

       
        
         0 15 10 ? * 6#3

        
         The timer is triggered at 10:15 on the third Friday in every month.

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access a created project and module.

     Choose Job.

     Click  to create a scheduled job.
      

      
       
        
         Table 4 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Job Name

          
           Job name. The value can contain only lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_). In the runtime-state environment, you can search for tasks by setting Job Name and Job Label.

         

         
          
           Job Label

          
           Job label. The value can contain Chinese characters, English letters, digits, and symbols. You are advised to set this value to characters that can be easily identified. In the runtime-state environment, you can search for tasks by setting Job Name and Job Label.

         

         
          
           Job Type

          
           
            Repeat: A Repeat timer is used to configure simple jobs that are executed at a fixed interval.

            Cron: A Cron timer is used to customize complex scheduled jobs. Select Cron.

           

         

         
          
           Status

          
           
            Enabled: The timer is activated. After the deployment, the timer starts to run based on the configurations.

            Disabled: The timer does not start after the deployment.

           

         

         
          
           Cron expression

          
           It is displayed when Job Type is set to Cron. Set this parameter to a Cron expression.

         

         
          
           Start Time

          
           Time when the scheduled job starts.

         

         
          
           End Time

          
           Time when the scheduled job ends.

         

         
          
           Time Zone ID

          
           Time zone to which the start time and end time belong. The UTC time is used by default.

         

         
          
           Forbid Concurrent Execution

          
           Whether to forbid concurrent execution. If this parameter is set to Yes, the next job will not be scheduled on time if the current job is not complete.

         

         
          
           Interface

          
           API used to execute scheduled jobs.

         

         
          
           Request Type

          
           Job request type.

         

         
          
           Interface Parameters

          
           Input parameters for the service selected from the Interface drop-down list. The value is in JSON format.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Timer description.

         

         
          
           Advanced Settings

          
           
            Perform Callback as System User: execution user displayed in the callback service job record. If this parameter is set to Yes, the execution user in the job record is the system user.

            Callback Language: language set for the callback service. By default, the language of the user who creates the scheduled job is used.

           

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Create.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After develop-state configuration is complete, click  in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment for the app to take effect immediately. If Enable Hot Deployment has been enabled in the Deployment Configuration dialog box, the system automatically deploys the service after identifying configuration changes.

    After the deployment is complete, choose Products and Services > Administration > Cron Jobs in the runtime-state environment to check the execution status of the scheduled job.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Configuring a Timer

name: Configuring a Customized Asset Package
title: Configuring a Customized Asset Package
text:
Configuring a Customized Asset Package
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    
     A project and a module have been created.

     The Data Package > Customized Asset menu has been displayed. For details, see Configuring the Module Navigation Menus.

     The service to be called by the scheduled job has been configured.

    

   

   
    Context

    A customized asset package is used to introduce data maintained in other forms. For example, if data is maintained using an Excel file, import the Excel file to the model in the app when importing an app to initialize data.

    Therefore, the system allows users to complete the data initialization configuration task using an attachment when importing an app.

    Customized assets can be imported in the following modes:

    
     Excel file import:
      You can import data in Excel format by using an Excel file. In this mode, you need to select the configured Excel import template. For details about how to configure the Excel import template, see Configuring the Excel Data Import Service.

      This mode supports only asset files in .xlsx format.

     Service:
      You can import data through a service. In this mode, you need to select a configured service. For details about how to configure a service, see Configuring Services.

      This mode supports asset files in .xlsx, .xls, .csv, .zip, .json, .kjb, .ktr, .properties, .groovy, .rb, .xml, .png, .pmd, .asc, .txt, .app, or .tsv format.

      
       The service is implemented through the RunScript script. Parameters configured on the GUI, such as the asset file to be uploaded, triggering scenario, and installation parameters, are transferred through _message.
       console.info("_message is ", JSON.stringify(_message));
var batchId = _message.batchId; //File token, which is transferred from the uploaded asset file.
var event= _message.event; //Triggering scenario, which is transferred from Trigger Scenario set on the GUI.
var parameters= _message.parameters; //Parameters, which are transferred from Installation Parameter configured on the GUI.
var name= _message.name; //Name, which is transferred from Asset Name configured on the GUI.
var appName= _message.appName; //App name. The value is the module name for legacy assets.

//Obtain the corresponding parameters for customized asset services using the preceding commands. After obtaining the parameters, execute its own service logic. The following is an example of importing a template by calling the adc-batch service:
var param = {"fileToken": batchId, "type": "excel" ,"templates": ["quxw/common/common_model_import"], "truncateModel": false, "parameters": {}}
var response = ServiceInvoker.post("/adc-batch/rest/v1/import-tasks/actions/create", param);

console.warn(JSON.stringify(response))
var result = {}
result.taskId = response.taskId
return result
      

     CSE:
      Asset files are imported through a CSE interface developed by microservices. This mode can be used if the service scenario is complex. In this mode, microservice development is required. For details, see CSE Microservice Development Guide.

      In this mode, a CSE interface needs to be specified. For example, use the CSE interface cse://portal/rest/v1/i18nResource/create, which is used to add i18n resources in batches.

      This mode supports asset files in .xlsx or .zip format.

      
        
       
        It is recommended that the number of initialization data records in the Excel file imported through customized asset does not exceed 1000. If there are more than 1000 records, manually import them using a customized Excel file. For details about how to import an Excel file, see Configuring the Excel Data Import Service. In addition, you need to configure the web page. Use the Excel import panel to import data page, and release the page as a runtime-state menu. For details, see Configuring the Page for Data Importing.

       

      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Data Package > Customized Asset.

     Click  on the right of Customized Assets to create a customized asset and configure the asset information.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Trigger Scenario

          
           Scenario where the import of customized assets is triggered.

           
            Initial app installation: The asset is imported only when the app is installed for the first time.

            App upgrade: The asset is imported when only the app is upgraded. App upgrade includes overwriting installation of an app with the same version and app upgrade from an earlier version to a later version.

            Each import: The asset is imported when the app is installed or upgraded for the first time.

           

           
             NOTE: 
            
             When an app is installed on the Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager page in the runtime-state environment, you can select initial installation or overwriting installation.

             
              Initial installation indicates the scenario where the app status is Not Installed after an app package is imported and installed for the first time. If an app needs to be installed again after it is uninstalled and the app status is Not Installed after the app package is imported, the installation can still be considered as initial installation.

              Overwriting installation indicates the scenario where the app status is Installed, Can be started, or Running if an app package already exists. In this case, you need to install the app package of the same version again and the installation operations can be regarded as app upgrade operations.

             

            

           

         

         
          
           Asset Type

          
           Type of the external access asset specified by the user.

           
            Customization Type: Assets of this type can be installed and uninstalled with apps.

            If assets of other types are added by clicking Create, they are not installed or uninstalled with the app, and asset data is not processed through services or CSE interfaces. Instead, assets are managed by AppManager. Click Manage to delete the created asset type.

           

           Other options are restricted and not described here. For details, contact Huawei engineers to obtain the orchestration document of the trial version.

         

         
          
           Installation Service Type

          
           Service type used for data import.

           
            Excel Import Template: When this parameter is set to Excel Import Template, select the configured Excel template.

            Service: When this parameter is set to Service, select a configured service. In most cases, the service script is used to check, install, and uninstall assets.

            CSE: When this parameter is set to CSE, the CSE interface is used to check, install, and uninstall assets.

           

         

         
          
           Import Template

          
           Excel import template. For details about how to configure the Excel template, see Configuring the Excel Data Import Service.

         

         
          
           Installation Service

          
           Select the configured service or enter the CSE interface based on the type of the service to be installed.

           CSE interface format: cse://xxxx/xxxx

         

         
          
           Pre-installation Check Service

          
           Select the configured service or enter the CSE interface based on the type of the service to be installed.

           CSE interface format: cse://xxxx/xxxx

         

         
          
           Uninstallation Service

          
           Select the configured service or enter the CSE interface based on the type of the service to be uninstalled.

           CSE interface format: cse://xxxx/xxxx

         

         
          
           Installation Parameter

          
           Parameters in JSON format are supported.

         

         
          
           Asset Version

          
           Asset version information.

         

         
          
           Upload Asset File

          
           Upload the asset file.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Save.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After develop-state configuration is complete, click  in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment for the app to take effect immediately. If Enable Hot Deployment has been enabled in the Deployment Configuration dialog box, the system automatically deploys the service after identifying configuration changes.

name: Configuring an Internationalization Resource
title: Configuring an Internationalization Resource
text:
Configuring an Internationalization Resource
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     The I18n menu display has been adjusted.

    

   

   
    Context

    Internationalization resources can be managed by bundle, that is, an internationalization resource package. Each internationalization resource package can be configured with multiple property resources.

    An internationalization resource package can be opened at different levels to control the scope of pages that reference this internationalization resource package. Currently, the following openness levels are supported:

    
     Module Level: Only resources in the current module can reference the internationalization resource package (that is, internationalization resource bundle).

     Project Level: Resources in all modules in the current project can reference the internationalization resource package (that is, internationalization resource bundle).

     Public: Resources in all projects in the system can reference the internationalization resource package (that is, internationalization resource bundle).

    

    After internationalization resources are configured, reference the internationalization resource bundles in a page instance. For details, see Configuring a Common Web Page.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose I18n.

     On the Bundle tab page, click Add Bundle.
      

      
       Figure 1 Creating an internationalization bundle
       
      

      

     Click Confirm And Complete. The internationalization resource package configuration page is displayed.

     Create internationalization resource properties.
      

      
       Click create and add internationalization resource properties.
        
         Figure 2 Configuring an internationalization resource
         
        

       Click OK.

       The name of the created property is the name of the added bundle prefix. When using the property, you need to use the displayed value of Property Name after configuration, that is, the property name that contains the bundle name prefix.
        

      

      

     (Optional) Export the internationalization resource properties. Click export on the right to export the internationalization resource properties.
      

      
       Figure 3 Exporting the internationalization resource properties
       
      

      

     (Optional) Import the internationalization resource properties. When there are many internationalization resource properties, the efficiency is low if you create one by one. You can prepare data in an Excel file and import the data at a time. For details about the format of an imported file, see the exported attachment.

    

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After configuring internationalization resources, you can reference the configured internationalization resources in the planned internationalization display. For example, reference the internationalization resources in menu internationalization.

name: Presetting the App Menu
title: Presetting the App Menu
text:
Presetting the App Menu
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    For apps that contain operation pages, you need to mount the pages to the menu path to facilitate user operations. Menu names can be translated into multiple languages. External URLs can be integrated to the system through menu configuration.

    
      
     
      If no menu is preset for the page, no visible entry is available for users after the app is installed, which affects user experience.

     

    

    For example, in the offering management system, the offering information management page is mounted as the Offering Information Management menu. Users can click the menu to access the corresponding page.

    If an application has multiple menus, you can plan multi-level menus. For example, two-level menus listed in the following table are planned based on the functions of the offering management system.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Menu
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Level-1 Menu

        
         Level-2 Menu

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Offering Management System

        
         Offering Information Management

        
         
          Level-1 menu: directory menu. No URL or page needs to be mounted.

          Level-2 menu: pages orchestrated in the app are mounted.

         

       

       
        
         Offering Category Management

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Menu.

     Set the information about the level-1 menu.
      

      
       In the Menu area on the left, click  to create a level-1 menu.

       Configure the menu information.
        

        

        
         
          
           Table 2 Parameter description
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Menu Name

            
             Menu name. This name is not the displayed name of the menu.

           

           
            
             Parent Menu Name

            
             Upper-level menu of the current menu. A menu can be set as a parent menu only when Menu Type is set to Contents.

             The value of this parameter can be copied from the Menu Name field of the parent menu.

             When a submenu is created by clicking , the parent menu name is automatically displayed.

             If the current menu is a level-1 menu, you do not need to set the parent menu.

           

           
            
             Menu Label

            
             Menu internationalization name. You can enter a single language or configure multiple languages through an internationalization file.

             
              Method 1: You can directly enter a value.

              Method 2: Select a configured internationalization resource from the drop-down list.

              Method 3: If no internationalization resources have been configured, click  to add one.

             

           

           
            
             Sort

            
             Position sequence of menus deployed to the runtime-state environment.

             A smaller value indicates a higher sequence. For the menus with the same value of Sort, an earlier the modification time indicates a higher sequence.

           

           
            
             Configure Icon

            
             Menu icon. The size of an icon image file must be less than 1 MB.

           

           
            
             Menu Type

            
             
              Page: page developed in the project or module specified by the system.

              Url: URL of a menu, that is, the menu of a leaf node.

              Contents: Set it to a directory as the menu node of a directory. You can add a specific URL menu to the node.
               
                 NOTE: 
                
                 When multi-level menus exist, Menu Type of non-leaf menus must be set to Contents. For example, if a level-3 menu exists, the level-3 menu is a leaf menu, while the level-1 and level-2 menus are non-leaf menus and Menu Type needs to be set to Menu Type.

                

               

              Custom Page: page developed using a Pro Code project.

             

           

           
            
             Open Level

            
             Public level of a menu in the develop-state orchestration element

             
              Public: indicates that the menu is public and can be used by a specific tenant.

              Project: indicates that the menu can be used within a project. When there are multiple modules in the project, the menu can also be used within the project modules.

              Module: indicates that the menu can be used within a module.

             

             
               NOTE: 
              
               The public level of the develop-state menu is irrelevant to the access permission in the runtime-state environment. The Open Level parameter is used only for access and call between orchestration elements in the develop-state environment. The access permissions in the runtime-state environment are still controlled by the permission and role configuration. For details, see Configuring Permissions and Roles.

              

             

           

          
         
        

       Click Add.

      

      

     Set the information about the level-2 menu.
      

      
       In the level-1 menu on the left, click  to create a submenu.

       Configure the submenu information. By default, the parent menu information is displayed in the submenu.
        

        
         
         
          
           
            Table 3 Parameter description
           
           
            
            
           
           
            
             
              Parameter

             
              Description

            

           
           
            
             
              Menu Name

             
              Menu name. This name is not the displayed name of the menu.

            

            
             
              Parent Menu Name

             
              Upper-level menu of the current menu. A menu can be set as a parent menu only when Menu Type is set to Contents.

              The value of this parameter can be copied from the Menu Name field of the parent menu.

              When a submenu is created by clicking , the parent menu name is automatically displayed.

              If the current menu is a level-1 menu, you do not need to set the parent menu.

            

            
             
              Menu Label

             
              Internationalized name of a menu.

              
               Method 1: You can directly enter a value.

               Method 2: Select a configured internationalization resource from the drop-down list.

               Method 3: If no internationalization resources have been configured, click  to add one.

              

            

            
             
              Sort

             
              Position sequence of menus deployed to the runtime-state environment.

              A smaller value indicates a higher sequence. For the menus with the same value of Sort, an earlier the modification time indicates a higher sequence.

            

            
             
              Configure Icon

             
              Menu icon. The size of an icon image file must be less than 1 MB.

            

            
             
              Menu Type

             
              
               Page: page developed in the project or module specified by the system.

               Url: URL of a menu, that is, the menu of a leaf node.

               Contents: Set it to a directory as the menu node of a directory. You can add a specific URL menu to the node. For example, Portal Management is a directory node. The Customized Menu URL node exists under this directory node.

               Custom Page: page developed using a Pro Code project.

              

            

            
             
              Open Method

             
              Configure the menu opening mode.

              
               Tab: Open a tab in the current browser.

               New Page: Open a new browser tab.

              

              This parameter is displayed when Menu Type is set to Contents.

            

            
             
              Url

             
              Specify a URL for a specific menu when Menu Type is set to Url.

              For example: /portal-web/portal/defaultApplication.html

              The URL can be an absolute path or a relative path.

              
               Absolute path: for example, https://www.huawei.com

               Relative path:
                
                 /xxx/xx.html. The URL is https://ip:port/xxx/xx.html after supplementation.

                 portal/xxx.html. The URL is https://ip:port/portal-web/portal/xxx.html after supplementation.

                

              

            

           
          
         

        

       Click Add.

       If there are multiple level-2 menus, repeat the preceding steps to add submenus.

      

      

     Deploy and debug the menu and view the menu mounting effect in the runtime-state environment.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    A permission item is generated for each menu. You can query the permission item on the Permission page of the develop-state menu and assign the permission item to a role based on requirements. For details, see Configuring Permissions and Roles.

    After develop-state configuration is complete, click  in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment for the app to take effect immediately. If Enable Hot Deployment has been enabled in the Deployment Configuration dialog box, the system automatically deploys the service after identifying configuration changes.

    During development and debugging, if you need to delete a menu in the runtime state, delete it in the develop state. After the deployment, the menu is deleted from the runtime state.

name: Configuring the Markdown Document
title: Configuring the Markdown Document
text:
Configuring the Markdown Document
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    
     A project and a module have been created.

     The Document menu has been displayed. For details, see Configuring the Module Navigation Menus.

     The service to be called by the scheduled job has been configured.

    

   

   
    Context

    Markdown is a markup language that can be edited by the common text editor. It can format the common text through a simple markup syntax.

    The developers can use the Markdown document to provide the description and help document for the developed apps.

    The Markdown document needs to be provided through the document package. You need to prepare the Markdown document to be provided offline, compress it into a ZIP file, and upload it to the system.

    In the project in the develop-state environment, click Template Download on the Document page to obtain the ZIP package template.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Directory and file description
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Directory/File

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         images

        
         Directory sample

       

       
        
         markdowns

        
         Directory sample. The directory and level for storing the MD file can be customized.

       

       
        
         binding_page_config.xlsx

        
         Configure the mapping between the page and help documents to implement the page-level help function. For example, the help document of the developed page A is A.md.

         Fill in the template. The parameters in the template are as follows:

         
          App Name: Name of the app to which the page belongs.

          Module Name: Name of the module to which the page belongs.

          Page: Page name. For example, the page testx_model_grid added by the developer to Page.
           
             NOTE: 
            
             The relative directory of the customized page can be configured. That is, the developer adds the customized page to Page > Orchestration Resource > Customized Page and configures it in the format of "Customized page name/Version/Location and name of the page help document", for example, procode1/1.0.2/dist/index.html. To obtain the relative address of the customized page, choose Page > Orchestration Resource > Customized Page, and click  on the left of the name of the imported project to expand the project information. Click View, and obtain the text of the customized page in the resource path column.

             

            

           

          Help Url: Relative directory of the help document, for example, markdowns/demo-md1.md.

         

         The mapping between Page and Help Url is automatically recorded on the Products and Services > Administration > Portal > Online Help Management page after the deployment to implement the page-level help.

       

       
        
         README.md

        
         Document sample

       

       
        
         SUMMARY.md

        
         Markdown document directory tree file

       

      
     
    

    
      
     
      The restrictions on the document page are as follows:

      
       The size of the ZIP package cannot exceed 150 MB.

       The maximum number of files in the ZIP package is 1000.

       The file directory can contain a maximum of five levels.

       The binding_page_config.xlsx file can contain a maximum of 5000 data records.

      

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Document.

     Click Create.

     Set the document information and upload the attachment.
      

      
       Figure 1 Setting document information
       
      

      

     Click OK.

     (Optional) When you configure a multi-language document, you need to add multiple records to configure the document of the corresponding language.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After the develop-state configuration is complete, click the icon in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment for the app to take effect immediately. Currently, the hot deployment is not supported.

    After the deployment is complete, click the help icon in the upper right corner in the runtime state, and check whether the displayed help document is correct.

name: Configuring a Process
title: Configuring a Process
text:
Configuring a Process
 
 
  
  

  
   A process is designed for a business object and is operated by different roles in different phases. This helps customers configure and develop processes in graphical mode.

  

  
   
    Process Development Overview
      Before using a process, you are advised to understand the basic concepts, permission description, and process designer of the process.

    Creating a Project
      This section describes how to create a project required by a process on the Project Management page.

    Non-Automated Process Development
      This topic describes how to create, configure, and debug a non-automated process.

    Automated Process Development
      An orchestrated API can handle a specific process. The input and output parameters, conditions, and phases of an API are set when it is developed. This ensures that phases are triggered when this API is applied to generate desired results.

    Development Guide of Introductory Processes
      This section describes how to create an introductory non-automated process using a simple process template. The introductory non-automated process contains common process components and can directly run the game of displaying all the prime numbers between one start number and end number.

    Process Designer Configuration Description
      This section describes the components and component properties in the process designer in detail and provides configuration examples.

    Custom Process Component Development Guide
      A custom process component provides the capability of developing the process component and can be directly used in the process designer.

    Common Operations for Process Configuration
      After developing a process, you can configure more properties for the process.
