name: Basic Concepts of a Process
title: Basic Concepts of a Process
text:
Basic Concepts of a Process
 
 
  
  

  
   Before using a process, you are advised to understand the basic concepts of the process.

   A process is a set of business operation rules and mechanisms designed under specific conditions to create value for customers or achieve business objectives. On a graphical process orchestration engine. In addition to traditional user interaction processes, API processes orchestrated based on app services, service catalogs, and JavaScript nodes are supported. You can quickly develop and deploy processes through online orchestration.

   ADC supports the following processes:

   
    Non-automated process: applies to various manual tasks. Forms are used as data interaction interfaces between users and the system.

    Automated process: applies to automatic tasks. No form is required as human-machine interaction interfaces.

   

   The ADC process consists of the following parts:

   
    Diagram: defines the logical sequence to be followed and the organizations or individuals involved in completing a business in a diagram

    Form: includes PC forms, mobile forms, and GDELink forms that support data interaction between users and the system. Users can enter information and perform operations on the designed page.

    Rule: refers to rules and mechanisms that support the effective operation of the process.

   

   
     
    
     To better be compatible with historical assets, you can import the SEP process package orchestrated in ADC 1.0 to 2.0 through the legacy assets.

     
      When importing historical assets, you can import customized service task, intermediate events, and nodes that call sub-processes.

      Historical asset process packages can be converted to the new asset package format when being exported in 2.0.

      The properties (class fields) of SEP customized components can be modified online.

      The properties of the time event component can be modified.

      The properties of the component that calls a sub-process can be modified.

     

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Process Development Overview

name: Process Permissions
title: Process Permissions
text:
Process Permissions
 
 
  
  

  
   After a process is created, ticket permission items are automatically created. Permission elements are deployed and installed together with the project package in the runtime state environment.

   All processes under the default role are bound to the default operation permission. For details, see Table 1. Each role in the system has different permissions. If a function or role is added, the administrator needs to assign operation permissions and menu permissions to the role.

   
    
    
     
      Table 1 Default roles in processes
     
     
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Role

       
        Default Permission

       
        Description

      

     
     
      
       
        TicketCreator

       
        Cancels tickets, displays process status diagrams, urges tickets, views ticket operation details, copies tickets, supplements suspension and resumption records, associates tickets, deletes ticket association relationships, queries ticket association relationships, handles associated tickets in batches, re-dispatches tickets, creates work logs, updates work logs, and queries the process list, attachments, rule logs, SLA details, and work logs.

       
        Role preconfigured in the process orchestration service. This role is used in process orchestration.

        
          NOTE: 
         
          You can log in to the Role Management page in the runtime-state environment as the current tenant administrator to customize the permission items.

         

        

      

      
       
        TicketProcessor

       
        Cancels tickets, displays process status diagrams, escalates tickets, handles tickets, creates sub-tickets, associates tickets, transfers tickets, urges tickets, modifies tickets, suspends tickets, resumes tickets, exempts tickets, views ticket operation details, queries attachments, views SLA details, re-assigns tickets, creates work logs, queries work logs, and updates work logs.

text:
Diagram Designer
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes the page layout of the diagram designer.

   

   

   
    
     
      Table 1 Description of the diagram designer page
     
     
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Category

       
        Function

      

     
     
      
       
        Top - toolbar

       
        Shortcut tools used for editing a diagram, including tools used for searching for nodes, saving, debugging, generating menus, undoing, redoing, deleting selected items, automatic layout, aerial view, zooming in, zooming out, and restoring the page, as well as selecting proportions.

      

      
       
        Left - component bar

       
        Components required for editing the diagram. For details, see Diagram Components.

      

      
       
        Middle - work area

       
        Work area for editing a diagram, which functions as a canvas.

        
          NOTE: 
         
          By default, the system generates three simple user tasks. You can edit the tasks directly or delete the tasks and edit them as required.

         

        

      

      
       
        Right - property bar

       
        
         Property of the configured flow component. Select the component to be configured from the work area and set the corresponding property parameters in the property bar.
         
          Primary Property: core configuration items of a component.
           
            Non-automated process: includes properties such as process name, label, model, type, multi-instance type, default handler, filter handler, skip expression, condition, policy configuration, and rule.

            Automated process: includes properties such as process name, label, type, service task parameter, and script.

           

          More Properties: common properties (such as the style) in most cases, which are optional. You can retain the default values for them.

name: Diagram Components
title: Diagram Components
text:
Diagram Components
 
 
  
  

  
   The diagram designer allows users to drag various components to draw diagrams.

   
    Components provided by the process designer include extended components and common process components. On the APIs and Activity tab pages, extended components including custom APIs and activities are provided for customizing orchestration elements. The dragging method of these extended components is the same as that of common process components.
    
     Custom APIs, including APIs registered in the automated process and APIs in the runtime-state environment, can be filtered by permission. In addition, service task parameters can be configured.

     Custom activities can be directly registered with the process management module to implement activity orchestration.

    

   

   Static operation items are displayed based on the phase type of the process. Recommended Action is displayed only when there is no egress connection line in the current phase. That is, the possible next action is predicted based on the current user behavior on the canvas.

   
    The following tables list the common process components. 
    
     
      
       Table 1 Event components
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Event

        
         Description

        
         Operation Item

       

      
      
       
        
         Start Event

        
         Indicates the start phase of a process.

        
         
          Recommended Action

          Change Task

         

       

       
        
         Scheduled Start Event

        
         Starts a clock task.

       

       
        
         End Event

        
         Indicates the end phase of a process.

        
         -

       

      
     
    

    
     
      
       Table 2 Activity components
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Activity

        
         Description

        
         Operation Item

       

      
      
       
        
         User Task

        
         Used for tasks participated by users. This component is unavailable in an automated process.

        
         
          Recommended Action

          Form

          Mobile Form

          Handler

          Process Rules

          Skip Expression

          Change Task

         

       

       
        
         Service Task

        
         Used to call an encapsulated service interface.

        
         
          Recommended Action

          Service Task Parameter

          Change Task

         

       

       
        
         Script Task

        
         Used to call a script task.

        
         
          Recommended Action

          Script

          Change Task

         

       

       
        
         Manual Task

        
         Used to define external tasks of the process engine. Manual tasks are handled as transfer activities.

        
         
          Recommended Action

          Change Task

         

       

       
        
         Redirection Task

        
         Used to specify a follow-up phase to improve user experience if there are multiple phases and complex connections.

        
         
          View Redirection Task

          Change Task

         

       

       
        
         Call SubProcess

        
         Used when a process contains multiple subprocesses.

        
         
          Recommended Action

          Parameter

          View Sub Process

         

       

       
        
         RPA Task

        
         Used to execute an RPA script. For details, see Development of a Hyper-Automation Process for RPA.

        
         
          Recommended Action

          Change Task

         

       

      
     
    

    
     
      
       Table 3 Gateway components
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Gateway

        
         Description

        
         Operation Item

       

      
      
       
        
         Exclusive Gateway

        
         The exclusive gateway defines a unique decision for a set of branches. All outgoing branches are evaluated in sequence, the branch whose first condition is evaluated as true is executed, and the subsequent branches are not evaluated further.

         For example, in the reimbursement review scenario, if the review is successful, the subsequent reimbursement process is executed. If the review fails, the ticket is returned to the creator for information modification.

        
         
          Recommended Action

          Change Task

         

       

       
        
         Inclusive Gateway

        
         Inclusive gateways are the combination of exclusive and parallel gateways. During decision-making, all subsequent branches whose condition is true are executed, which is different from that of exclusive gateways.

       

       
        
         Parallel Gateway

        
         The parallel gateway unconditionally creates or reclaims branches based on the preceding or subsequent connection lines.

         For example, the ETM ticket process needs to be checked by the back-end operation (BO) manager, front-end operation (FO) manager, and field maintenance engineer (FME). After a ticket is created, three parallel tasks are generated based on the reviewer. After the BO manager, FO manager, and FME review the ticket, the ticket is submitted to the project director (PD) for final review. The BO manager, FO manager, and FME can review tasks in any sequence. Three parallel tasks can be generated by using the parallel gateway.

       

      
     
    

    
     
      
       Table 4 Connection components
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Connection

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Sequence Flow

        
         Used to connect processes and configure process directions.

       

       
        
         Association

        
         Used to mark the association between elements.

       

      
     
    

    
     
      
       Table 5 Swimlane components
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Swimlane Diagram

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Pool

        
         Used to carry swimlanes.

       

       
        
         Lane

        
         Used to represent responsibilities of an activity in a process. A lane can be an organization, a role, or a system.

       

      
     
    

    
     
      
       Table 6 Mechanical part components
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Mechanical Part

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Group

        
         Group of process elements, which is used to identify the group relationship between elements.

       

       
        
         Text

        
         Text description of a group.

name: Drawing Method
title: Drawing Method
text:
Drawing Method
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes the common methods of drawing a diagram.

   
    Method 1 (drag-and-drop mode): Drag the required component from the component bar to the work area, as shown in the following figure.
     

     

     
       
      
       
        If a user task is to be dragged, you need to initialize the task before drawing the process diagram.

        Activities, gateways, and components under Activity support quick insertion of a third node between two nodes.

        If a single node exists in the process canvas or the connection line between nodes is incomplete, the node is highlighted in red.

       

      

     

    Method 2 (shortcut mode): Select a process component (for example, User Task) in the workspace, choose Change Task from the shortcut menu, and select the desired task, as shown in the following figure.
     

     

   

   
     
    
     
      Use sequence flows to connect components. If necessary, you can move components to check whether the sequence flows are successfully connected. Pay attention to the following skills for line connection s and shapes:
      
       Line connection (drag-and-drop mode): Drag a sequence flow component from the left component bar to the canvas, and drag the start or end node of the line to the area around the component to be connected. When a green line () appears around the component, release the mouse.

       Line connection (shortcut mode): Click the start component to be connected in the work area, select the sequence flow from the shortcut menu, and drag the line to the area around the target component. When a green line () appears around the target component, release the mouse.

       Line shape change: Click a line (sequence flow component). Folding points appear on the line. Move the pointer to a folding point. When a cross appears, drag the line to change its shape ().

name: Creating a Project
title: Creating a Project
text:
Creating a Project
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to create a project required by a process on the Project Management page.

   
    Context

    The project template provides a project template. You can create a project based on this template or using a blank template.

    
     When a process is created based on a process template, the menus required by the process are automatically displayed for new modules.

     When a project is created based on an existing project or using a blank template, you need to manually adjust the menus to be displayed.

    

    The following shows how to create a project and project using a process template.

    
      
     
      You can import or export a process by importing or exporting a project or module. If you create a project or process by importing a project or module, pay attention to the following points:

      
       Hot deployment cannot be directly enabled for the project imported with a process.

       Hot deployment cannot be enabled for the existing project to which a compatible process is imported.

      

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the Project Management page, click Create Project.

     In the navigation pane, choose Business Process.

     Hover the cursor over Business Process Template and click Use.

     Configure the project information.
      

      
       For details about parameter settings, see Table 1. 
       
        
        
         
          Table 1 Parameter description
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Name

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Name

           
            
               Project name, which is used to identify a project and must be globally unique. The settings cannot be modified after being submitted.
              

          

          
           
            Display Name

           
            
               App name displayed to end users. You can set it to a name that is easy to identify. You can change the value on the settings page after the creation. In GDE Store, the display name is used to submit the app for putaway.
              

          

          
           
            Tag

           
            Project label, which can be used to query projects by project label

          

          
           
            Service Domain

           
            Service domain to which a project belongs. For details about the application scenarios and creation operations of service domains, see Configuring a Service Domain.

          

          
           
            Share Assets in Inner-Source Repository of GDE Store

           
            This parameter is displayed only in the OC scenario. This parameter controls whether to share assets in the inner-source repository of GDE Store. If Default is selected, the tenant or system configuration is used.

          

          
           
            Description

           
            Description of a project.

          

          
           
            Personal Works

           
            Personal works are small plugins, script programs, or tools independently developed by engineers to improve development efficiency. These works must pass basic security scanning before being put away. Personal works are not allowed to access customer networks, and the user shall bear the risks in subsequent deployment and running.

            Projects created in versions before this parameter is set are considered as non-personal works by default. This function is disabled by default.

            The EOS rules for personal works are different from those for non-personal works. EOS date of personal works = min(Asset release time + Days before EOS, EOS date of the develop-state works during packaging). The days before EOS can be configured for personal works at the system level. The default value is six months.

          

          
           
            Enable Hot Deploy

           
            Hot deployment is to incrementally deploy elements orchestrated in the develop-state environment to the runtime-state environment in real time. Developers do not need to manually perform one-click deployment, which facilitates quick debugging.

            After this function is enabled, a project is deployed at the beginning of the project creation. When you add, delete, or modify orchestration elements in the project, the elements are also deployed.

            This switch is not displayed if the selected template does not support hot deployment.

            
              NOTICE: 
             
              If an app fails to pass the quality assessment and code check, and birth certificates, registration certificates, and health certificates of the assets released to the runtime-state environment need to be verified, hot deployment to the runtime-state environment has security risks. In this case, you need to ensure that the risks are acceptable before enabling hot deployment.

             

            

          

          
           
            CreateModule

           
            You need to create modules and then orchestration elements in a project.

            After this function is enabled, a module with the same name as the project is created by default. Therefore, you do not need to create a module again.

            To customize the name of the module to be created, click Advanced.

            This switch is not displayed if the selected template does not support multiple modules.

          

         
        
       

      

      

     (Optional) If you need to configure more information, click Advanced to configure the logo and service domain.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 2 Advanced configuration parameters
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Project

          
           Project information.

         

         
          
           Customer

          
           Customer information.

         

         
          
           Sharing Scope

          
           
            PERSONAL: Only the project creator and specified users have the permission to view the project. Other users under the tenant cannot view the project. If this parameter is set to PERSONAL, you can manage members who have the project permission by referring to Managing a Member.

            TEAM: Only members in a specified team can be opened. Non-team members do not have the permission to view the project.

            PUBLIC: The project can be used by all users under a tenant.

           

           
            After a project is created, only the following users can modify the project sharing scope and asset sharing scope:
            
             Users who have the Develop Asset Management permission

             Personal project creator

             Personal project manager

             Team creator of a team project

             Team manager of a team project

             Creator of a public project

            

           

         

         
          
           Team

          
           When Sharing Scope is set to TEAM, select a created team. If an individual user does not belong to any team, the team cannot be selected. A team needs to create a user who has the develop-state administrator permission. For details, see Team Management.

         

         
          
           Module Name

          
           This field is displayed when CreateModule is enabled.

           The value can contain 1 to 64 characters and start with a letter. Only letters, digits, underscores (_), hyphens (-), and periods (.) are allowed. The value cannot end with [..].

         

         
          
           module Prefix

          
           This field is displayed when CreateModule is enabled.

           Module prefix, which is used to distinguish different modules for easy search.

           The value can contain lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_), and must start with a letter.

           By default, the value is automatically filled. A maximum of the first ten characters of the module name are retained. If the first 10 characters contain uppercase letters, the letters are converted to lowercase letters by default. If the value contains a hyphen (-) or period (.), the hyphen and period are deleted by default and the first 10 characters after the deletion are used.

         

         
          
           Dynamic Permission

          
           This parameter is not displayed by default. This parameter is displayed only when the dynamic permission assignment function is enabled for a master-level system parameter.

           When the dynamic permission assignment function is enabled, resource operation permissions can be dynamically managed in the runtime-state environment.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Create.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Configuring a Process

name: Non-Automated Process Development
title: Non-Automated Process Development
text:
Non-Automated Process Development
 
 
  
  

  
   This topic describes how to create, configure, and debug a non-automated process.

  

  
   
    Analyzing the Business Logic
      Business logic analysis converts customer requirements into a process.

    Creating a Non-automated Process
      This section describes how to create a simple non-automated process, so that users can understand its basic configuration.

    Managing a Diagram
      This topic describes how to use the process diagram designer to configure, describe, and beautify a process diagram.

    Configuring Process Form Pages
      This section describes how to use the form editor to configure form pages.

    Configuring the Ticket Operation Button Components
      This section describes how to customize ticket operation button components using the form editor.

    Configuring Transfer Conditions
      This section describes how to configure transfer conditions for sequence flows.

    Configuring the Default Process Handler
      This section describes how to configure the default process handler.

    Configuring a Process-Level Filter Handler
      This section describes how to configure a process-level filter handler.

    Configuring a Global Exception Handling Policy

    Configuring Withdrawal Rules
      By default, non-automated processes cannot be withdrawn. You can configure withdrawal rules to configure the initiation node to support withdrawal.

    Configuring Handlers for Process Phases
      This section describes how to configure handlers for process phases.

    Configuring Process Rules
      This topic describes how to configure process rules. Process rules provide assistance in process instance operations to improve O&M efficiency.

    Debugging Process Rules
      On the Rule Management page, you can use the debugging function to obtain the process rule items that can be matched.

    Debugging a Non-Automated Process
      This topic describes how to debug a non-automated process.

   

   
    
     Parent topic: Configuring a Process

title: Process Design
text:
Process Design
 
 
  
  

  
   Key elements of the design for non-automated processes are listed based on the requirement analysis.

   The following uses a trouble ticket dispatching process as an example to describe the key elements that need to be analyzed in the customer process:

   
    Trouble ticket dispatching process (for example, user task process)

    Three process activity phases, including CreateTask, ProcessTask, and ConfirmTask

    Handler of each phase

    Branch and judgment conditions of each phase

name: Form Design
title: Form Design
text:
Form Design
 
 
  
  

  
   Key elements of the form design are listed based on the requirement analysis.

   Taking a trouble ticket dispatching process as an example, the key elements that need to be analyzed on the process form page are as follows:

   
    Sorting of business data objects, which refer to the data sources that need to be maintained on the processing page of each process phase and property types of these data sources

    Selection items of some information in the business data objects (drop-down lists on the form page), for example, options of Fault Level.

    Association between data sources. For example, when Operation Mode is set to Reject, associate the rejection reason.

   

   
     
    
     To use the function of reassigning a ticket, you need to orchestrate the Reassign Order component in the process form by dragging the Window Button component. When a ticket is reassigned, that is, when a non-automated process is handled, the handler can specify a handler of the current phase or handler of the next manual task phase. After the handler of the next phase is selected, the process directly goes to this phase and the handler is changed to the specified handler.

name: Rule Design
title: Rule Design
text:
Rule Design
 
 
  
  

  
   This section lists key elements of the rule design based on the requirement analysis.

   The following content uses a trouble ticket dispatching process as an example to describe the key elements that need to be analyzed in custom process rules:

   
    Other activities triggered by the current activity (for example, status change and message sending)

    Rules to be triggered for the current activity of each phase and the trigger conditions

   

   
    Event

    
     
      
       Table 1 Rule event description
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Rule Event

        
         Whether the Event Is Related to the Process Phase

        
         Event Trigger Condition

       

      
      
       
        
         Ticket Deleted

        
         Irrelevant to process phases. This event can be selected when Process Phase is set to All.

        
         This event is triggered when a ticket is deleted.

       

       
        
         Ticket Completed

        
         This event is triggered when a ticket is handled.

       

       
        
         Ticket Canceled

        
         This event is triggered when a ticket is canceled.

       

       
        
         Ticket Modified

        
         This event is triggered when a ticket is modified.

       

       
        
         Ticket Participant

        
         This event is triggered when a ticket handler is modified.

       

       
        
         Ticket Recalled

        
         This event is triggered when a ticket is withdrawn.

       

       
        
         Ticket Resume

        
         This event is triggered when an SLA resumes a ticket.

       

       
        
         Ticket Suspend

        
         This event is triggered when an SLA suspends a ticket.

       

       
        
         Before Task Completed

        
         Relevant to process phases. This event can be selected when a specific process phase is selected.

        
         This event is triggered before a task is handled.

       

       
        
         Subticket Updated

        
         This event is triggered when a sub-ticket is updated.

       

       
        
         Task Completed

        
         This event is triggered when a task is handled.

       

       
        
         Task Reassigned

        
         This event is triggered when a task needs to be reassigned.

       

       
        
         Task Started

        
         This event is triggered after a task starts.

       

       
        
         Task Transferred

        
         This event is triggered when a task is transferred.

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Association Between Events and Activities

    Activities vary with events.

    
     
      
       Table 2 Association between events and activities
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Event

        
         Activity Type

       

      
      
       
        
         Ticket Canceled

        
         
          Invoke service

          Send messages

          Update business status

         

       

       
        
         Ticket Completed

        
         
          Invoke service

          Send messages

          Update business status

         

       

       
        
         Ticket Deleted

        
         
          Invoke service

          Send messages

         

       

       
        
         Ticket Modified

        
         
          Invoke service

          Send messages

         

       

       
        
         Ticket Participant

        
         Invoke service

       

       
        
         Ticket Recalled

        
         
          Invoke service

          Send messages

          Update business status

         

       

       
        
         Ticket Resume

        
         
          Invoke service

          Send messages

          Update business status

         

       

       
        
         Ticket Suspend

        
         
          Invoke service

          Send messages

          Update business status

         

       

       
        
         Before Task Completed

        
         Update fields

       

       
        
         Subticket Updated

        
         
          Automatically submit

          Invoke service

          Update business status

         

       

       
        
         Task Completed

        
         
          Create subticket

          Invoke service

          Send messages

          Update business status

         

       

       
        
         Task Reassigned

        
         
          Invoke service

          Send messages

         

       

       
        
         Task Started

        
         
          Automatically submit

          Create subticket

          Invoke service

          Send messages

         

       

       
        
         Task Transferred

        
         
          Invoke service

          Send messages

         

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Activity

    
     
     
      
       Table 3 Rule activity description
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Rule Activity

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Invoke service

        
         Calls services required for ticket handling.

       

       
        
         Send messages

        
         Sends notifications during ticket handling.

       

       
        
         Update business status

        
         Automatically updates the business status of a ticket during ticket handling.

       

       
        
         Update fields

        
         Updates ticket fields during ticket handling.

       

       
        
         Automatically submit

        
         Automatically submits a ticket in a phase. This activity is mainly used in ticket automation scenarios.

       

       
        
         Create subticket

        
         Automatically creates sub-tickets of the corresponding process type. This activity is mainly used in ticket automation scenarios.

       

      
     
    

    
     
     
      
       Table 4 Rule action parameters
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Parameter

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         When Rule Action is set to Update fields, configure the following parameters.

       

       
        
         Mode

        
         The options are Default and Customize.

       

       
        
         Input Parameter

        
         If Mode is set to Default, configure this parameter.

         
          Click the text box. The Input Parameter dialog box is displayed.

          Configure input parameters.

          Click Save.

         

       

       
        
         Update Field Service

        
         If Mode is set to Customize, configure this parameter.

         Select the service whose fields need to be updated from the drop-down list.

       

       
        
         When Rule Activity is set to Create subticket, configure the following parameters.

       

       
        
         Subprocess

        
         Select a required sub-ticket from the drop-down list.

       

       
        
         Mode

        
         The options are Default and Customize.

       

       
        
         Ticket Creation Param

        
         If Mode is set to Default, configure this parameter.

         
          Click the text box. The Input Parameter dialog box is displayed.

          Configure input parameters.

          Click Save.

         

       

       
        
         Service

        
         If Mode is set to Customize, configure this parameter.

         Select a desired service from the drop-down list.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           After selecting a service, you can click  next to the drop-down list to edit the service.

          

         

       

       
        
         When Rule Activity is set to Invoke service, configure the following parameters.

       

       
        
         Service

        
         Select a desired service from the drop-down list.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           
            After selecting a service, you can click  next to the drop-down list to edit the service.

            When the service is executed, the value of current_phase obtained from the process rule context is the value of current_phase_id instead of current_phase_name.

           

          

         

       

       
        
         Input Parameter

        
         
          Click the text box. The Input Parameter dialog box is displayed.

          Configure input parameters.

          Click Save.

         

       

       
        
         Exclude Ticket Context

        
         Specifies whether to exclude the ticket content. This function is disabled by default.

         
          Disabled: indicates that the ticket content and parameters configured in the Input Parameter dialog box need to be input for service call when a service is executed.

          Enabled: indicates that only the parameters configured in the Input Parameter dialog box are input for service call when a service is executed.

         

       

       
        
         When Rule Activity is set to Send messages, configure the following parameters.

       

       
        
         Message Type

        
         Message type. Multiple options are supported. The options are as follows:

         
          SMS

          Email

          MateLineMessage

          Custom message notification type. For details, see Adding an SMSGW Configuration.

          Extended type of the custom message notification mechanism

         

       

       
        
         Message Receiver

        
         Message recipient. Multiple recipients are supported.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           You need to select at least one recipient from Message Receiver or Specified Receiver. An external user can be selected as the specified message recipient.

          

         

       

       
        
         Specified Receiver

       

       
        
         Cc

        
         CC recipient.

         This parameter is displayed only when Message Type is set to Email.

       

       
        
         BCC

        
         BCC recipient.

         This parameter is displayed only when Message Type is set to Email.

       

       
        
         Email Server

        
         Select an email server from the drop-down list.

         This parameter is displayed only when Message Type is set to Email.

       

       
        
         SMS Sender

        
         Select an SMS server from the drop-down list.

         This parameter is displayed only when Message Type is set to SMS.

       

       
        
         Include recipient subgroups

        
         Specifies whether the recipient subgroup is included.

       

       
        
         Message Title

        
         Message title.

         This parameter is displayed only when Message Type is set to Email.

         To automatically generate a message title, perform the following operations:

         
          In the first drop-down list, select a variable.

          Click Add.

         

       

       
        
         Message Content

        
         Content of an email or message.

         To automatically generate the message content, perform the following operations:

         
          In the first drop-down list, select a variable.

          Click Add.

         

         
           NOTE: 
          
           You can switch between rich texts and simple texts only when the message type is Email. Rich texts are used to send emails.

          

         

       

       
        
         Delay

        
         Specifies whether to delay the message sending.

       

       
        
         Delay Time

        
         Delay for sending messages.

         This parameter is displayed only when Delay is selected.

       

       
        
         Cycle

        
         Specifies whether to send messages cyclically.

       

       
        
         Cycle Interval

        
         Interval for resending a message, in minutes.

         This parameter is displayed only when Cycle is selected.

       

       
        
         Repeat Count

        
         Number of times that a message is sent repeatedly.

         This parameter is displayed only when Cycle is selected.

       

       
        
         Auto Escalate

        
         Specifies whether to automatically escalate a ticket.

         This parameter is displayed only when Delay is selected.

       

       
        
         Escalation Level

        
         Escalation level.

         This parameter is displayed only when Auto Escalate is selected.

       

       
        
         Record in Work Log

        
         Specifies whether to record messages in work logs.

       

       
        
         When Rule Activity is set to Automatically submit, configure the following parameters.

       

       
        
         Delay

        
         Specifies whether to delay the automatic submission. The options are Yes and No.

       

       
        
         Mode

        
         The options are Default and Customize.

       

       
        
         Type

        
         When Delay is set to Yes, configure this parameter.

         Calendar day type of the delay duration.

       

       
        
         Days

        
         When Delay is set to Yes, configure this parameter.

         Enter the number of delayed days.

       

       
        
         Hours

        
         When Delay is set to Yes, configure this parameter.

         Enter the delayed hours.

       

       
        
         Minutes

        
         When Delay is set to Yes, configure this parameter.

         Enter the delayed minutes.

       

       
        
         Input Parameter

        
         If Mode is set to Default, configure this parameter.

         
          Click the text box. The Input Parameter dialog box is displayed.

          Configure input parameters.

          Click Save.

         

       

       
        
         Execute Custom Service

        
         If Mode is set to Customize, configure this parameter.

         Select a custom service from the drop-down list.

       

       
        
         When Rule Activity is set to Update business status, configure the following parameters.

       

       
        
         Update Type

name: Creating a Non-automated Process
title: Creating a Non-automated Process
text:
Creating a Non-automated Process
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to create a simple non-automated process, so that users can understand its basic configuration.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     A project and a module have been created.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access a created project and module.

     In the navigation pane, choose Business Process.
      

      

      

     Access the page for creating a process.
      

      
       Method 1
        On the displayed Business Process tab page, click  in the upper right corner.

      

      
       Method 2
        
         On the displayed Business Process tab page, click  in the upper right corner.

         On the displayed page, click Create

        

      

      

     Set the parameters related to the non-automated process.
      

      

      
       
       
        
        
         
          Table 1 Parameters for creating a process
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Parameter

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Process Type

           
            Select a value from the drop-down list. The options are as follows:

            
             Automated process: corresponds to the API process in version 1.0. In an automated process, the user task node cannot be used.

             Non-automated process: corresponds to the business process in version 1.0. In a non-automated process, the user task node can be used.

            

            By default, Non-auto process is selected.

          

          
           
            Display Name

           
            The process display name must be unique and entered manually.

          

          
           
            Process Abbreviation

           
            Used to distinguish processes for easy search.

            The value contains a maximum of 5 characters, including letters, and digits.

          

          
           
            Process Name

           
            The process name must be unique and entered manually.

            The value can contain lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_), and must start with a lowercase letter.

          

          
           
            Open Level

           
            The following levels are supported during process creation:

            
             Public

             Project

             Module

            

            The default value is Module.

            
              NOTE: 
             
              During process configuration, if other orchestration elements (such as services, processes, pages, and events) are needed, the restrictions on the orchestration elements and processes are as follows:

              
               If orchestration elements and the process belong to the same project and module, the open level of the orchestration elements is not limited.

               If orchestration elements and the process belong to different modules of the same project, the open level of the orchestration elements must be Public or Project.

               If orchestration elements and the process belong to different modules in different projects, the open level of the orchestration elements must be Public.

              

             

            

          

          
           
            Business Type

           
            The business type can be configured during process creation. By default, this parameter is left empty. You can select one of the following types from the drop-down list or enter a type.

            
             Hyperautomation

             Other

             SDM

             WFM

            

          

          
           
            Data Model

           
            The name of a data model can contain lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_), and must start with a lowercase letter.

            This parameter needs to be set only when Non-auto process is selected for Process Type.

          

          
           
            Sequence Format of Process Instance

           
            When creating a process, you can specify the sequence format of the process instance.

            This parameter needs to be set only when Non-auto process is selected for Process Type.

            
              NOTE: 
             
              
               The value of Sequence Format of Process Instance is in the format of Process abbreviation+connector+sequence number.

               You can log in as a tenant user to the GDE data zone portal and choose Products and Services > Administration > System Settings to restrict the connector. The configuration method is as follows: On the System Settings page, click Create. On the displayed page, set Name to order_seq_split_symbol, Category to adc-bpm, and Value to - or _. The default value is -. If the value is not specified, no connector is used. If an invalid value is entered, the default value is used.

              

             

            

          

          
           
            Customize Process Forms

           
            Whether to enable the process form customization capability during process creation.

            
             Enabled

             Disabled

            

            This function is disabled by default.

            This parameter needs to be set only when Non-auto process is selected for Process Type.

            
              NOTE: 
             
              
               After this function is enabled, properties can be customized for process models, log models, and process phase pages. When a page is created based on customizable properties, Custom Type can only be set to Override.

               After customizing a process form page, you need to customize the workflow_detail page. That is, if any modification is made on the customized process form page, the modification must be synchronized to the workflow_detail page. Otherwise, the customization content does not take effect on the transfer details page.

               After customizing a process form page, you need to customize services related to process creation and transfer. For details, see Customizing Services.

              

             

            

          

          
           
            Process Template

           
            The system provides process templates during process creation:

            
             If Non-automated process is selected: simple process template and default non-automated process template

             If Automated process is selected: default automated process template

            

          

         
        
       

      

      

     Click Submit.
      

      
       After the process is created, the process diagram designer page is displayed. By default, the page is in view mode.

       Click Enter Editing Mode to edit the process diagram.
        
          
         
          
           When the process canvas is locked or in view mode, you can drag the canvas and view the process and process property configuration.

           If you cannot enter the editing mode and the current user is an administrator or the same user who is editing the information, click Forced Entry.

          

         

        

      

      

      According to the process diagram, you can understand that:

      
       The default process created by the system consists of three task phases.

       Non-automated process: Operation items are displayed on the right of each task phase.

      

      
        
       
        The mobile form designer includes the Mateline designer and GDELink designer.

       

      

      

     (Optional) If hot deployment is disabled, click  in the upper right corner of the page and select One-Click Deployment.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After creating a process, you can perform the operations listed in the following table.

    
     
      
       Table 2 Operations after creating a process
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation

        
         Description

        
         Procedure

       

      
      
       
        
         Editing a process

        
         You can edit a process.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           When editing a process, you can change its open level, which will make some functions unavailable. Perform this operation when absolutely necessary.

          

         

        
         
          On the Business Process page, click Edit in the Operation column.

          On the displayed page, modify the values of Display Name and Open Level.

          Click Submit.

         

       

       
        
         Copying a process

        
         You can copy an existing process.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           
            You can copy processes and the internationalization information of forms across projects.

            Only incompatible non-automated processes of the source project can be copied to the target project.

            You can copy processes of a read-only project an external project only.

           

          

         

        
         
          On the Business Process page, choose More > Copy in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, configure the process.
           The values of Open Level, Process Type, and Business Type are inherited from existing processes and cannot be changed.

          Click Submit.

         

       

       
        
         Disabling a process

        
         You can disable an enabled process.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           When disabling a registered automated process, the registered APIs of the process will also be deleted.

          

         

        
         
          On the Business Process page, click Disable in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Enabling a process

        
         You can enable a disabled process.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           
            By default, the newly created process is enabled.

            Only one version of a process can be enabled.

           

          

         

        
         
          On the Business Process page, click Enable in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Deleting a process

        
         You can delete a process only when it is disabled and no longer used.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           
            When deleting a registered automated process, the registered APIs of the process will also be deleted.

            When a process is deleted, if multiple versions exist, the process itself and the copied elements are successfully deleted, but the shared elements are not deleted.

           

          

         

        
         Method 1:

         
          On the Business Process page, choose More > Delete in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

         Method 2:

         
          On the Business Process page, select one or more processes.

          Click Delete in the upper part of the page.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Debugging a process

        
         You can debug an enabled and deployed process.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           A process that is enabled or not deployed cannot be debugged.

          

         

        
         
          On the Business Process page, choose More > Debug in the Operation column.

          On the displayed page, debug the process.
           
            To debug a non-automated process, see Debugging a Non-Automated Process.

            To debug an automated process, see Debugging an Automated Process.

           

         

       

      
     
    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Non-Automated Process Development

name: Managing a Diagram
title: Managing a Diagram

text:
Drawing a Diagram for the Non-Automated Process
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to use the process diagram designer to draw a diagram for the non-automated process.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     You have obtained the process configuration permission.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Business Process.

     On the displayed Business Process tab page, click  in the upper right corner.

     On the business management page, click the created process.
      

      By default, the page is in view mode.

      

     Click Enter Editing Mode in the upper left corner of the page.

     Draw a non-automated process by referring to Process Design and Introduction to the Diagram.
      

      

      

      
        
       
        Process orchestration supports the draft capability. If a process diagram is modified, the diagram is automatically saved as a draft every minute. When you enter the editing mode again, if a draft already exists, the system displays a message asking you whether to restore the draft.

        

        

        
         If you click Cancel, the system automatically clears the draft.

title: (Optional) Describing a Process Diagram
text:
(Optional) Describing a Process Diagram
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes the process configuration in a process diagram.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     You have obtained the process configuration permission.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Business Process.

     On the displayed Business Process tab page, click  in the upper right corner.

     On the business management page, click the created process.
      

      By default, the page is in view mode.

      

     Click Switch to edit mode in the upper left corner of the page.

     Edit the process diagram.
      

      Describe the process with the following process components:

      
       Group

       Text Annotation

       (Optional) Association

      

      
       Drag and drop the Group component to the canvas to enclose the components to be described.
        

        

       Drag the Annotation component and place it next to the Group component. Set the Text field on the Main attributes tab page in the right Property pane. For example, set it to Process test.
        

        

        You can also set the color and thickness for the Annotation component in the Property pane.

       (Optional) Drag the Association component to connect it to the Group and Annotation components.
        

        

        You can also set the color and thickness for the Association component in the Property pane.

       View the effect.

name: (Optional) Beautifying a Process Diagram
title: (Optional) Beautifying a Process Diagram
text:
(Optional) Beautifying a Process Diagram
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to beautify a process diagram.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     You have obtained the process configuration permission.

    

   

   
    Context

    Most process diagrams are simple and look tidy and neat. If a process diagram has too many branches, sequence flows overlap with other sequence flows and components regardless of adjustment. This makes it difficult to see clearly the logical relationship in the process diagram. The Redirection Task component can be used to simplify a process diagram.

    In the following example, the Redirection Task component is used to replace the sequence flows of the Reject branch of the gateway of the ConfirmTask phase.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Business Process.

     On the displayed Business Process tab page, click  in the upper right corner.

     On the business management page, click the created process.
      

      By default, the page is in view mode.

      

     Click Enter Editing Mode in the upper left corner of the page.

     Drag the Redirection Task component and drop it to the gateway.
      

      

      

      

     Connect the sequence flow of the original Reject branch to the Redirection Task component.
      

      

      

     Set the properties of the Redirection Task component.
      

      

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Managing a Diagram

name: Configuring Process Form Pages
title: Configuring Process Form Pages
text:
Configuring Process Form Pages
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to use the form editor to configure form pages.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     You have obtained the process configuration permission.

    

   

   
    Context

    Assume that the design information in a process form is as follows:

    
     
     
      
       Table 1 Form of the CreateTask phase
      
      
       
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Property Name

        
         Property Type

        
         Mandatory (Yes/No)

        
         Data Source

       

      
      
       
        
         First Occur Time

        
         Date and time input

        
         Yes

        
         Selected or input by the event proposer.

       

       
        
         Attachment

        
         File input

        
         No

        
         Input by the event proposer.

         Multiple types of input materials, such as PDF, Excel and Word files and JPEG and PNG image files, are supported.

       

       
        
         Description

        
         Text input

        
         No

        
         Input by the event proposer.

       

       
        
         Assign To

        
         Handler selection

        
         Yes

        
         Selected by the event proposer.

       

      
     
    

    
     
     
      
       Table 2 Form of the ProcessTask phase
      
      
       
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Property Name

        
         Property Type

        
         Mandatory (Yes/No)

        
         Data Source

       

      
      
       
        
         Operation Mode

        
         Radio group

        
         Yes

        
         Resolved, Update

       

       
        
         Radio option (Update)

       

       
        
         Assign To

        
         Handler selection

        
         Yes

        
         Selected by the event proposer.

       

       
        
         Radio option (Resolved)

       

       
        
         Description

        
         Text box

        
         No

        
         Input by the event handler.

       

      
     
    

    
     
     
      
       Table 3 Form of the ConfirmTask phase
      
      
       
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Property Name

        
         Property Type

        
         Mandatory (Yes/No)

        
         Data Source

       

      
      
       
        
         Operation Mode

        
         Radio group

        
         Yes

        
         Accept, Reject

       

       
        
         Description

        
         Text box

        
         No

        
         Input by the personnel who confirms the event.

       

      
     
    

    
      
     
      
       The manual task phase in the non-automated process supports the following form designers: PC designer, Mateline designer, and GDELink designer. The Mateline designer and GDELink designer depend on the configuration item for which Name is mobile_engine_type and Category is adc-mobile on the Products and Services > Administration > System Settings page in the runtime-state environment. The Mateline designer takes effect only when Value of this configuration item is mateline and the Status is Enabled. Otherwise, the GDELink designer is used.

       The process form template in the manual task phase can be a simple phase template and default phase template.

       You can customize process form pages automatically generated by the system. If the pages are modified, check whether the corresponding model contains the corresponding fields. If no, manually add the fields to implement related functions.

       The process form page can be quickly orchestrated. When the page is saved, the corresponding model and service are updated synchronously. The mandatory properties of the component will be synchronized to the input parameter properties of the service. After a mandatory component is deleted, the historical input parameter property of the mandatory component in the service is changed to optional.

       When you configure a process form page, do not use project_name and role_project_name as the component name.

       Projects that contain mobile pages can be released to GDELink. In this document, the mobile page refers to the GDELink page.

      

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Business Process.

     On the displayed Business Process tab page, click  in the upper right corner.

     On the business management page, click the created process.
      

      By default, the page is in view mode.

      

     Click Enter Editing Mode in the upper left corner of the page.
      

      The PC form is used as an example.

      

     Configure a form for the CreateTask phase.
      

      According to the plan, Template/Draft and Title have been preconfigured in the system. You only need to configure other components.

      
       Select the CreateTask phase and click Form in the operation item.

       Configure the First Occur Time field.
        Search Basic on the left for Date Time Input and drag and drop it to Region Panel of the workspace or component tree.

        
          
         
          
           Different processes require different types of data and controls. Get familiar with the functions and application scenarios of controls on the control bar. For details, see the online help.

          

          
           The effect of dragging and dropping the required components to the component tree is the same as that of dragging and dropping the components to the workspace, but the former one is more accurate. Practice more to get proficient at dragging and dropping components.

          

         

        

       Configure the First Occur Time field.
        
         Name: Only lowercase letters, digits, hyphens (-), and underscores (_) are allowed.

         Label: indicates a field label. If the internationalization function is enabled in the system, this parameter is used to bind languages.

         Mandatory: If the field is mandatory, select Yes.
          

        

       Click  in the center of the form editor to save the settings.

       Repeat the preceding steps and configure the Attachment field with the File Input component, the Description field with the Text area component, and the Assign To Create field with the Person Select component by referring to Table 1.
        

        
          
         
          
           The Submit button has been preconfigured in the process form editor.

          

          
           The Assign To field exists in both the CreateTask and ProcessTask phases. To differentiate them in the TQL condition configuration, do as follows. Set name of the field for the CreateTask phase to assign_to_create and set that of the field for the ProcessTask phase to assign_to_process. Set the label of the field for the CreateTask phase to Assign To Create, and set that of the field for the ProcessTask phase to Assign To Process.

           For the Person Select component, set Value Type to name.

          

         

        

      

      

     Configure a form for the ProcessTask phase.
      

      
       Select the ProcessTask phase and click Form in the operation item.

       Use the required basic components to configure the ProcessTask page.
        

        

        

        The basic components used in the ProcessTask form are as follows:

        
         Radio group

         Option button group box

         Handler selection

         Text box

        

       Configure form field properties based on Table 2.
        
          
         
          
           The Operation Mode field exists in both the ProcessTask and ConfirmTask phases. To differentiate them in the TQL condition configuration, set name of the field for the ProcessTask phase to operation_mode_process, and set that of the field for the ConfirmTask phase to operation_mode_confirm.

           The Assign To field exists in both the CreateTask and ProcessTask phases. To differentiate them in the TQL condition configuration, do as follows. Set name of the field for the CreateTask phase to assign_to_create and set that of the field for the ProcessTask phase to assign_to_process. Set the label of the field for the CreateTask phase to Assign To Create, and set that of the field for the ProcessTask phase to Assign To Process.

          

         

        

       Click  to save the settings.

      

      

     Configure the ConfirmTask form.
      

      No component needs to be added. You only need to open the page, configure form field properties based on Table 3, and click  to save the settings.

Configuring the Ticket Operation Button Components
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to customize ticket operation button components using the form editor.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     You have obtained the process configuration permission.

    

   

   
    Context

    For a process created using a default template for non-automated processes on the pages of the ProcessTask and ConfirmTask phases, the following ticket operation buttons are provided by default: Cancel Ticket, Associate Ticket, Transfer Ticket, Remind Ticket, Pause Ticket, Resume Ticket, and Process Status Diagram. The following describes how to add the Escalate Ticket button in the ProcessTask phase. You can configure other ticket operation buttons as required.

     Drag Window Button from the Basic tab page to the Ticket Operation area.

name: Configuring Transfer Conditions
title: Configuring Transfer Conditions
text:
Configuring Transfer Conditions
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to configure transfer conditions for sequence flows.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     You have obtained the process configuration permission.

    

   

   
    Context

    The transfer conditions are required only for the sequence flows after a gateway. Based on the planned process diagram, the sequence flows to be configured are as follows.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the created process.
      

      By default, the page is in view mode.

      

     Click Enter Editing Mode in the upper left corner of the page.

     Configure a transfer condition for the Resolved sequence flow in the ProcessTask phase.
      

      
       Select the sequence flow after the gateway and click the editing box of the Condition property.
        

        

       Configure transfer conditions.
        Configure a condition based on the options on the form page of the previous phase.

        

        

        
          
         
          A process supports the following conditions: TQL, Script (JUEL), and Script (TEL). TEL is a new condition added in version 2.1. JUEL and TEL on the page are adapted and displayed based on the old and new processes.

          
           Only TQL and TEL can be used by new processes. JUEL cannot be used.

           TQL, JUEL, and TEL can be used by historical processes.

          

          For details, see Guidance for the Conditional Expressions.

         

        

       Click Submit.
        The configuration is finished, as shown in the following figure.

        

        

      

      

     Similarly, configure transfer conditions for other sequence flows.

name: Configuring the Default Process Handler
title: Configuring the Default Process Handler
text:
Configuring the Default Process Handler
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to configure the default process handler.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     You have obtained the process configuration permission.

    

   

   
    Context

    
     If no handler is matched for a manual phase, the default process handler is used as the handler of the corresponding phase.

     Default process handlers, which can be specific personnel or groups, can only be configured for non-automated processes.

     Handler rules are matched in the following sequence: Process phase handler > Default handler for the process phase > Default process handler

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the created process. By default, the page is in view mode.

     Click Enter Editing Mode in the upper left corner of the page.
      

      

      

      

     In the Default Handler area, click  on the right of the selection box.
      

      

      

      

     In the Select a person dialog box, select required personnel or groups from the Available area and add them to the Selected area.
      

      

      

      

     Click OK.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Non-Automated Process Development

name: Configuring a Global Exception Handling Policy
title: Configuring a Global Exception Handling Policy
text:
Configuring a Global Exception Handling Policy
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    A global exception handling policy can be configured for non-automated processes. If an exception occurs in the Service Task or Script Task node in a non-automated process, you can configure a global exception handling policy, including the following options:

    
     Terminate Exception: The process ticket of the current service task or script task is terminated unexpectedly, and the ticket status changes to Completed.

     Abort Exception: The process ticket of the current service task or script task is stopped unexpectedly, and the ticket status changes to Running.

     Ignore Exception: The process ticket of the current service task or script task ignores the exception and the ticket continues to be transferred.

    

    
      
     
      The exception handling policy at the process node level has a higher priority than that at the global level.

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the process to be configured.
      

      By default, the page is in view mode.

      

     Click Enter Editing Mode in the upper left corner of the page.

     In the Fault Handling Policy area on the right, select the exception handling policy of the service task or script task based on site requirements.
      

      

      

     Click  to save the settings.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Non-Automated Process Development

name: Configuring Withdrawal Rules
title: Configuring Withdrawal Rules
text:
Configuring Withdrawal Rules
 
 
  
  

  
   By default, non-automated processes cannot be withdrawn. You can configure withdrawal rules to configure the initiation node to support withdrawal.

   
    Context

    After withdrawal rules are configured, the withdrawal operation has the following restrictions by default:

    
     Only the ticket creator can withdraw a ticket to the ticket creation phase. After the withdrawal, the current handler of the task is the ticket creator.

     If a ticket has been withdrawn once, it cannot be withdrawn again after being submitted again.

     Tickets that have been approved cannot be withdrawn.

     Tickets cannot be withdrawn if an automatic node such as service node exist after the creation phase and tickets are transferred.

     If the approval phase after the ticket creation phase contain multiple instances and some tasks have been approved in the approval phase, the ticket cannot be withdrawn.

     Historical data is retained after the withdrawal, and the withdrawal operation is recorded in work logs.

     After a ticket is withdrawn, the SLA/OLA calculation continues. If the ticket is submitted again, the SLA/OLA recalculation is not automatically started.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the process to be configured.
      

      By default, the page is in view mode.

      

     Click Enter Editing Mode in the upper left corner of the page.

     In the Recall Configuration area on the right, set the parameters.
      

      
       Recall not supported: This is the default value. If this parameter is not set, the withdrawal function is not supported by default.

       Initiating node supports Recall: After the ticket creator initiates a task, the ticket creator can withdraw the task if the task is not approved.

      

      

     Click  to save the configuration rules.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Non-Automated Process Development

         FO

        
         Operator in the step of Create Task

       

       
        
         7

        
         End

        
         Close

        
         N/A

        
         N/A

       

      
     
    

    From the planning and design perspective:

    
     In the CreateTask phase, set Processor to Creator to represent the original ticket initiator. It needs to be configured only if the ticket is rejected to the ticket creation phase.

     In the ProcessTask phase, configure the handler based on the sequence flows of the transfer conditions and the person specified in the form of the previous phase.

     In the ConfirmTask phase, configure the handler to the operator in the Create Task phase because transfer conditions are set but the handler is empty in the form of the previous phase.

    

    
      
     
      
       Handler rules are matched in the following sequence: Process phase handler > Default handler for the process phase > Default process handler

       Handlers vary depending on process phases and logical relationships. You can select the default group as the handler based on site requirements.

       The Multi-Instance type property on the Main attributes tab page applies to the multi-person approval scenario. The options are as follows:
        
         None: If at least one person approves or rejects the ticket, the non-automated process continues.

         Parallel: The next phase can start only if multiple persons approve or reject the ticket and specific conditions are met. For example, the next phase can start only after everyone approves the ticket, more than three persons approve the ticket, or 50% of them approve the ticket.

         Sequential: The Accept phase can start only after all persons approve the ticket in sequence. If one person rejects the ticket, the Reject phase starts. The approval sequence is random.

        

       The approval conditions for the Multi-Instance type property are configured in the Assignments property. When Multi-Instance type is set to Sequential or Parallel, the Multi-Instance Completion Condition area appears in the Assignments dialog box.

      

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

      By default, the page is in view mode.
