               Specified Cc handler required in the process phase.

               TQL expression. It can be left blank, indicating that all conditions are met.

             

            
           
          

         Click Submit.

        

       Click Submit.

      

      

     Configure a handler for the ProcessTask phase.
      

      
       In the ProcessTask phase, choose Handler from the shortcut menu or click the text box of Handler.

         In the Default Handler area, click  on the right of the selection box.

             The effective scope of the handler depends on the parameter whose Category is adc-bpm and Name is tenant-jump-policy on the Products and Services > Administration > System Settings page of the runtime-state environment. If the value of this parameter is set to match_assign_to and its Status is set to Enabled, only the handler specified by Handler can handle the ticket. Otherwise, other handlers with the ticket handling permission can also handle the ticket.

         Configure a handler for the ProcessTask phase in which Reject is selected, and click Submit.
          

        

       Click Submit.

      

      

     Similarly, configure a handler for the ConfirmTask phase.

         Configure handler rules.
          

         Click Submit.

title: Configuring Status Change Rules
text:
Configuring Status Change Rules
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to configure status change rules for process phases.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     You have obtained the process configuration permission.

    

   

   
    
    Context

    This section uses the planning and design in the following table as an example to describe the status change rules in each phase.

    
     
      
       
       
       
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         No.

        
         Process Phase

        
         Rule Event

        
         Rule Condition

        
         Business Status

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         1

        
         CreateTask

        
         Task Completed

        
         N/A

        
         In Process

        
         Create Task to Process Task

       

       
        
         2

        
         ProcessTask

        
         Task Completed

        
         Operation Mode(Process Task)=Resolved

        
         Pending for requester confirm

        
         Process Task to Confirm Task on Resolved

       

       
        
         3

        
         ProcessTask

        
         Task Completed

        
         Operation Mode(Process Task)=Update

        
         In Process

        
         Process Task to Process Task on Update

       

       
        
         4

        
         ConfirmTask

        
         Task Completed

        
         Operation Mode(Confirm Task)=Reject

        
         In Process

        
         Confirm Task to Process Task on Reject

       

       
        
         5

        
         ConfirmTask

        
         Task Completed

        
         Operation Mode(Confirm Task)=Accept

        
         Closed

        
         Confirm Task to Closed on Accept

       

      
     
    

    From the planning and design perspective:

    
     In the CreateTask phase, after a ticket is submitted, the ticket status changes to In Process.

     Configure the status change rules for the ProcessTask and ConfirmTask phases based on the sequence flows and the options in the form of the previous phase. (Two status change rules are required because two transfer conditions of sequence flows exist.)

    

    
      
     
      Status change rules vary depending on process phases and logical relationships.

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Click a project on the Project Management page.

     In the navigation pane, choose Business Process.

     On the displayed Business Process tab page, click  in the upper right corner.

     Access the Rule Management page.
      

      
       Method 1:
        On the Business Process page, choose More > Manage Rule in the upper right of the page.

       Method 2:
        On the Business Process page, choose More > Manage Rule in the Operation column.

       Method 3:
        
         On the Business Process page, click the process to be configured.

         Click Enter Editing Mode in the upper left corner of the page.

         Select a process phase to be configured.

         Click  under Rule Info in the lower right corner.

        

      

      

     Click Create.
      

      
        
       
        If the Rule Management page is accessed using method 3, you can also click  in the Rule Info in the lower right corner to create a rule.

       

      

      

     Configure a status change rule for the CreateTask phase by referring to the planning and design in Context.
      

      
       Click Create.

       Configure a rule.
        
         Figure 1 Status change rule for the CreateTask phase
         

         
          
          
           
            
             Table 1 Rule parameters
            
            
             
             
            
            
             
              
               Parameter

              
               Description

             

            
            
             
              
               Rule Name

              
               Rule name.

             

             
              
               Process Display Name

              
               Display name of the process corresponding to the rule.

               
                 NOTE: 
                
                 
                  If the Rule Management page is accessed using method 1, you can select the required process display name. If you set this parameter to All, the Process Phase is also All.

                  If the Rule Management page is accessed using method 2 or 3, the value of this parameter is the display name of the current process and cannot be changed.

                 

                

               

             

             
              
               Process Phase

              
               Default process phase for which the rule is configured:

               
                CreateTask

                ProcessTask

                ConfirmTask

                All

               

             

             
              
               Rule Event

              
               Event for which the rule is configured.

               
                When Process Phase is not set to All, the options are as follows:
                 
                  Before Task Completed

                  Subticket Updated

                  Task Completed

                  Task Reassigned

                  Task Started

                  Task Transferred

                 

                When Process Phase is set to All, the options are as follows:
                 
                  Ticket Canceled

                  Ticket Completed

                  Ticket Deleted

                  Ticket Modified

                  Ticket Participant

                  Ticket Recalled

                  Ticket Resume

                  Ticket Suspend

                 

               

             

             
              
               Synchronize

              
               Specifies whether synchronization is supported during rule execution. The options are as follows:

               
                Yes: Rules are executed synchronously.

                No: Rules are executed asynchronously.

               

               
                 NOTE: 
                
                 When Rule Activity is set to Send messages, this parameter can only be set to No and cannot be modified.

                

               

             

             
              
               Priority

              
               The options are as follows:

               
                Highest

                High

                Medium

                Low

                Lowest

               

               If this parameter is not specified, Lowest is used by default.

             

             
              
               Description

              
               Description of the rule.

             

             
              
               Rule Condition

              
               TQL expression. It can be left blank, indicating that all conditions are met.

             

             
              
               Rule Activity

              
               For details about the rule action parameters, see Table 3 and Table 4.

             

            
           
          

         

        

       Click Save.

      

      

     Configure a status change rule for the ProcessTask phase.
      

      
       Configure a status change rule for the ProcessTask phase in which Resolved is selected.
        

        

       Configure a status change rule for the ProcessTask phase in which Update is selected.
        

        

      

      

     Configure a status change rule for the ConfirmTask phase.
      

      
       Configure a status change rule for the ConfirmTask phase in which Reject is selected.
        

        

       Configure a status change rule for the ConfirmTask phase in which Accept is selected.

    From the planning and design perspective:

    
     When a ticket is submitted in the CreateTask phase, a message is directly sent to the handler specified in the form.

     Configure message sending rules for the ProcessTask phase based on the sequence flows and options in the form of the previous phase. (Two message sending rules are required because two transfer conditions of sequence flows exist.)

     The ConfirmTask phase has two sequence flows. A message sending rule needs to be configured for only one sequence flow. For the other sequence flow, that is, Operation Mode(Confirm Task)=Accept, the ticket will be closed and no handler can send messages. In some workflows, messages can be sent to all people who have handled the ticket.

    

    
      
     
      Status change rules vary depending on process phases and logical relationships.

           Variables can be set in the message title and content. Specify the variable value based on the form configuration.

           When Message Type is set only to Email, rich text editing is supported.
            

            

          

        

       Configure a message sending rule for the ProcessTask phase in which Update is selected.
        
         Configure parameters in the Rule Info and Rule Condition areas.
          

          

        

        
         Configure a rule activity. The message types SMS and Email are used as examples.
          

          

        

      

      

     Configure a message sending rule for the ConfirmTask phase.
      

      Configure a message sending rule for the ConfirmTask phase in which Reject is selected.

      
       Configure parameters in the Rule Info and Rule Condition areas.

name: Creating an Automated Process
title: Creating an Automated Process
text:
Creating an Automated Process
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to create a simple automated process, so that users can understand its basic configuration.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     A project and a module have been created.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access a created project and module.

     In the navigation pane, choose Business Process.
      

      

      

     Access the page for creating a process.
      

      
       Method 1
        On the displayed Business Process tab page, click  in the upper right corner.

      

      
       Method 2
        
         On the displayed Business Process tab page, click  in the upper right corner.

         On the displayed page, click Create

        

      

      

     Set the parameters related to the automated process.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         
          Table 1 Parameters for creating a process
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Parameter

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Process Type

           
            Select a value from the drop-down list. The options are as follows:

            
             Automated process: corresponds to the API process in version 1.0. In an automated process, the user task node cannot be used.

             Non-automated process: corresponds to the business process in version 1.0. In a non-automated process, the user task node can be used.

            

            By default, Non-auto process is selected.

          

          
           
            Display Name

           
            The process display name must be unique and entered manually.

          

          
           
            Process Abbreviation

           
            Used to distinguish processes for easy search.

            The value contains a maximum of 5 characters, including letters, and digits.

          

          
           
            Process Name

           
            The process name must be unique and entered manually.

            The value can contain lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_), and must start with a lowercase letter.

          

          
           
            Open Level

           
            The following levels are supported during process creation:

            
             Public

             Project

             Module

            

            The default value is Module.

            
              NOTE: 
             
              During process configuration, if other orchestration elements (such as services, processes, pages, and events) are needed, the restrictions on the orchestration elements and processes are as follows:

              
               If orchestration elements and the process belong to the same project and module, the open level of the orchestration elements is not limited.

               If orchestration elements and the process belong to different modules of the same project, the open level of the orchestration elements must be Public or Project.

               If orchestration elements and the process belong to different modules in different projects, the open level of the orchestration elements must be Public.

              

             

            

          

          
           
            Business Type

           
            The business type can be configured during process creation. By default, this parameter is left empty. You can select one of the following types from the drop-down list or enter a type.

            
             Hyperautomation

             Other

             SDM

             WFM

            

          

          
           
            Data Model

           
            The name of a data model can contain lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_), and must start with a lowercase letter.

            This parameter needs to be set only when Non-auto process is selected for Process Type.

          

          
           
            Sequence Format of Process Instance

           
            When creating a process, you can specify the sequence format of the process instance.

            This parameter needs to be set only when Non-auto process is selected for Process Type.

            
              NOTE: 
             
              
               The value of Sequence Format of Process Instance is in the format of Process abbreviation+connector+sequence number.

               You can log in as a tenant user to the GDE data zone portal and choose Products and Services > Administration > System Settings to restrict the connector. The configuration method is as follows: On the System Settings page, click Create. On the displayed page, set Name to order_seq_split_symbol, Category to adc-bpm, and Value to - or _. The default value is -. If the value is not specified, no connector is used. If an invalid value is entered, the default value is used.

              

             

            

          

          
           
            Customize Process Forms

           
            Whether to enable the process form customization capability during process creation.

            
             Enabled

             Disabled

            

            This function is disabled by default.

            This parameter needs to be set only when Non-auto process is selected for Process Type.

            
              NOTE: 
             
              
               After this function is enabled, properties can be customized for process models, log models, and process phase pages. When a page is created based on customizable properties, Custom Type can only be set to Override.

               After customizing a process form page, you need to customize the workflow_detail page. That is, if any modification is made on the customized process form page, the modification must be synchronized to the workflow_detail page. Otherwise, the customization content does not take effect on the transfer details page.

               After customizing a process form page, you need to customize services related to process creation and transfer. For details, see Customizing Services.

              

             

            

          

          
           
            Process Template

           
            The system provides process templates during process creation:

            
             If Non-automated process is selected: simple process template and default non-automated process template

             If Automated process is selected: default automated process template

            

          

         
        
       

      

      

     Click Submit.
      

      
       After the process is created, the process diagram designer page is displayed. By default, the page is in view mode.

       Click Enter Editing Mode to edit the process diagram.
        
          
         
          
           When the process canvas is locked or in view mode, you can drag the canvas and view the process and process property configuration.

           If you cannot enter the editing mode and the current user is an administrator or the same user who is editing the information, click Forced Entry.

          

         

        

      

      

      

      According to the process diagram, you can understand that:

      
       The default process created by the system consists of three phases.

       Automated process: Operation items are displayed on the right of each task phase.

      

      

     (Optional) If hot deployment is not enabled, perform one-click deployment.
      

      
       Click  in the upper right corner of the page.

       In the displayed dialog box, click One-Click Deployment.

       Click OK.

      

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After creating a process, you can perform the operations listed in the following table.

    
     
      
       Table 2 Operations after creating a process
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation

        
         Description

        
         Procedure

       

      
      
       
        
         Editing a process

        
         You can edit a process.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           When editing a process, you can change its open level, which will make some functions unavailable. Perform this operation when absolutely necessary.

          

         

        
         
          On the Business Process page, click Edit in the Operation column.

          On the displayed page, modify the values of Display Name and Open Level.

          Click Submit.

         

       

       
        
         Copying a process

        
         You can copy an existing process.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           
            You can copy processes and the internationalization information of forms across projects.

            Only incompatible non-automated processes of the source project can be copied to the target project.

            You can copy processes of a read-only project an external project only.

           

          

         

        
         
          On the Business Process page, choose More > Copy in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, configure the process.
           The values of Open Level, Process Type, and Business Type are inherited from existing processes and cannot be changed.

          Click Submit.

         

       

       
        
         Disabling a process

        
         You can disable an enabled process.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           When disabling a registered automated process, the registered APIs of the process will also be deleted.

          

         

        
         
          On the Business Process page, click Disable in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Enabling a process

        
         You can enable a disabled process.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           
            By default, the newly created process is enabled.

            Only one version of a process can be enabled.

           

          

         

        
         
          On the Business Process page, click Enable in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Deleting a process

        
         You can delete a process only when it is disabled and no longer used.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           
            When deleting a registered automated process, the registered APIs of the process will also be deleted.

            When a process is deleted, if multiple versions exist, the process itself and the copied elements are successfully deleted, but the shared elements are not deleted.

           

          

         

        
         Method 1:

         
          On the Business Process page, choose More > Delete in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

         Method 2:

name: Configuring an Automated Process Node
title: Configuring an Automated Process Node
text:
Configuring an Automated Process Node
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to set common parameters in API orchestration, and configure process components from the start node (Start Event), processing nodes (such as Service Task), to the output node (End Event) based on the API orchestration sequence.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     You have obtained the process configuration permission.

    

   

   
    Context

    On the automatic process node, only TEL can be used by the new processes (JUEL is not supported), and all conditions can be used by historical processes. Script condition expressions (JUEL and TEL) are used in the following scenarios:

    
     Configure the input parameters of Start Event.

     Configure the output parameters of End Event.

     Configure the conditions of Sequence Flow.

     Configure API Input, API Output, and Fault Handling Policy (Customize Exception) of Service Task.

    

    For details, see Guidance for the Conditional Expressions.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the new automated process.
      

      By default, the page is in view mode.

      

     Click Enter Editing Mode in the upper left corner of the page.

     Configure the Start Event node.
      

      Start Event is the start node of a process, and End Event is its end node. For an automated process, input parameters need to be set for the start node. After the execution ends, the final output result needs to be obtained. Initial input parameters can be configured on the Start Event node, and API output parameters can be configured on the End Event node.

      
       Click the Start Event node in the process diagram.
        

       Click the Parameter text box under Main attributes on the right of the page. The configuration page is displayed.
        

        

       Configure initial input parameters of Start Event.
        The format of an input parameter is as follows: The first layer is object, and the parameters are under the object layer.

        In the following figure, the input parameter is account_id, and its value is adminsdm. Configure the input parameters of the process on the Start Event node based on service requirements.

        

       Obtain the input parameters of the Start Event node.
        Once an input parameter is configured in Start Event, the parameter can be obtained in the subsequent Service Task phase. To obtain the parameter, enter ${API_Input.account_id}. For example, if the input parameter account_id in the Service Task phase needs to be set to the value of account_id configured in the Start Event node, perform the following steps:

        
         Click the Service Task node in the process diagram.

         Click the Service Task Parameter text box on the right of the page.

         Click the API Input tab.

         Click the configuration icon on the left of ${_context}.

         Click Append Params.
          

          

         On the displayed page, select account_id under StartNode.
          

        

        
         Click OK.
          The input parameter account_id of the Service Task node is automatically set to ${API_Input.account_id}.

          

         Click Submit.

        

      

      

     Configure the Service Task node.
      

      Service Task is used to call a service in an API catalog or app service.

      
       The Service Task node allows you to set input and output parameters of phases. When a phase starts, the API calls a required service using the input parameters, and generates output parameters using the returned result from the service.

       The Service Task node allows you to configure Record Calling Log, Asynchronize, Pause Before Execution, Automatic Execution Period, and Wait After Execute.

      

      
        
       
        The service task node supports dynamic API name configuration. The API name can contain dynamic variables. The format of the variables is the same as that of the default variables in the API expression, for example, {title} and {app_name}. The variable name must exist in the process context. For example, /adc-service/rest/v1/services/my_project/my_module/{service_name}, in which service_name indicates the variable name in the process context.

       

      

      The procedure is as follows:

      
       Select a service.
        
         Click the Select Service text box.

         In the displayed dialog box, select the required service.
          

         View the API name automatically generated on the API Service tab page.
          

          

        

       (Optional) Search for a service.
        
         Click  on the right of the Select Service text box.

         On the displayed page, click the Service tab.

         (Optional) Set the project, module, name, and open level, and click Search.

         On the service list page, select the required service.
          

         Click OK. View the API name automatically generated on the API Service tab page.

        

       (Optional) Select a registered service from the API tab page.
        
         Click  on the right of the Select Service text box.

         On the displayed page, click the API tab.

         In the left tree, select a category the service belong.
          
            
           
            The API catalog on the left can be filtered by permission.

           

          

         Select the required service from service cards.
          

         Click OK. View the API name automatically generated on the API Service tab page.
          

          

        

       Set parameters on the API Input tab page.
        
         Click the API Input tab.

         Click Load Params.

         In the displayed dialog box, click OK.
          After the parameters are loaded, the phase input parameters are automatically generated based on the service input parameters. The test personnel can adjust the input parameters as required.

          

        

       Set parameters on the API Output tab page.
        Set the output parameters displayed after a service is called. The first layer must be array, of which the length is 2. By default, object is ${_response}. The output parameter setting will be written in the process context _context.

        

        The following table details how to obtain variables from the Service Task node.

        
         
          
           Table 1 Methods of obtaining variables
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Variable Type

            
             How to Obtain

           

          
          
           
            
             Input parameter of Start Event

            
             ${API_Input}, for example, ${API_Input.account_id}.

           

           
            
             Original output of the service called by the current node, which is obtained from Service Task

            
             ${_response}

           

           
            
             Input or output parameters of a service task

            
             ${API10_input} or ${API10_output}. API10 indicates the phase ID.

           

           
            
             Process context

            
             ${_context}: contains parameters related to the current process instance. The parameters configured in the output parameters of Service Task are automatically written to the process context. You can modify the parameters in the process context in the script task.

           

          
         
        

       Configure the parameters of a Service Task node.
        Configure the parameters as required. Enable the switch to configure parameters.

        

        

        
         
          
           Table 2 Parameters on API Service
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Record Logs of Called Service

            
             This parameter specifies whether to record the logs of the called service of the phase in the automated process.

             
               NOTE: 
              
               
                Before setting Record Logs of Called Service, enable the tenant-level system configuration parameter recording_api_process_logs on the Products and Services > Administration > System Settings page of GDE data zone. The default value of this parameter is on, indicating that logs of the called service are recorded for all automated processes. If this parameter is set to off, logs of the called service are not recorded for all automated processes. The enabling operation takes effect only when the system configuration parameter is enabled.

                During automated process node configuration, Record Logs of Called Service is enabled and used only during automated process debugging. Before releasing an automated process, disable Record Logs of Called Service. Otherwise, the system performance deteriorates sharply.

               

              

             

           

           
            
             Log Scope

            
             This parameter specifies the scope of call logs, and the value can be All or Exception Log. The default value is Exception Log.

             This option is displayed only when Record Logs of Called Service is enabled.

             
               NOTE: 
              
               Log Scope is valid only for automated processes. For non-automated processes, all logs are recorded by default.

              

             

           

           
            
             Asynchronize

            
             This parameter specifies whether the called service can run asynchronously.

           

           
            
             Pause Before Execute

            
             Before the API service is called, the process instance is suspended. You need to configure the automatic execution period.

           

           
            
             Automatic Execution Period

            
             This option is displayed only when Pause Before Execution is enabled. If this function is selected, you can configure the execution period. The process instance is resumed during the period and is suspended in other periods.

             The automatic execution period must be longer than 5 minutes.

           

           
            
             Wait After Execution

            
             After the API service is called, the process instance enters the waiting state. After the timeout interval ends, the process instance is automatically resumed.

             After this parameter is enabled, you need to set the waiting duration. After the timing ends, the process instance proceeds to the next step.

             Value range: 30 seconds to 30 days

           

           
            
             Job Support Retry

            
             This parameter specifies whether a task can be retried after being interrupted.

             This parameter is displayed only when Pause Before Execute and Automatic Execution Period are enabled or Wait After Execution is enabled.

           

          
         
        

       Configure the exception handling policy for the service task.
        The exception handling policies are as follows:

        
         Terminate Exception

         Abort Exception

         Ignore Exception

         Customize Exception
          The system provides the customization page only when the value is Customize Exception, as shown in the following figure.

          

        

       Click Submit.

      

      

     (Optional) Configure the Redirection Task node.
      

      
       The Redirection Task node specifies redirections between components to prevent complex connections in the process diagram. Components can be redirected only to Service Task, Script Task, and User Task.

      

      
       Specify a target component for Redirection Task. This is like connecting Redirection Task to the component.
        

        

      

      

     (Optional) Configure the subprocess node to be called.
      

      
       Select the subprocess to be called, and choose Parameter from the shortcut menu or click the Parameter text box on the Primary Property tab page.
        

        

       After you select a subprocess, the associated subprocess is automatically matched. Configure required parameters on the Input and Output tab pages.
        

        

      

      

     Configure the Sequence flow node.
      

      You can use scripts to configure conditions for Sequence flow. For details about how to obtain process variables, see Guidance for the Conditional Expressions.

      

      

     Configure the End Event node.
      

      
       End Event is the final phase of a process. Similar to Start Event, End Event is mandatory. End Event is used to configure the final output of the API. If the parameters of End Event are not configured, output parameters of all automated phases are generated by default. You can also configure the output parameters of End Event.

      

      
       The format of the output parameter is as follows: The first layer must be array. The output object to be returned must be the only object element of array. You can change the element type, or add or delete elements in the left pane, and choose values from the right pane.

      

      The procedure is as follows:

      
       Click the Parameter text box under Main attributes on the right of the page. The configuration page is displayed.

       Click  and choose Type > Object.
        

       Click Append.
        

       Enter the name of the output parameter of End Event, for example, api_output.
        

       Click  and choose Add Params.
        

       In the displayed dialog box, specify the output of the phase as the output of End Event.
        

        

       Click OK.
        

       Click Submit.

      

      

     Click  to save the settings.

     (Optional) If hot deployment is not enabled, perform one-click deployment.
      

      
       Click  in the upper right corner of the page.

       In the displayed dialog box, click One-Click Deployment.

       Click OK.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Automated Process Development

name: Configuring a Global Exception Handling Policy
title: Configuring a Global Exception Handling Policy
text:
Configuring a Global Exception Handling Policy
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    
     A global exception handling policy can be configured for automated processes. The global exception handling policy supports only Terminate Exception.

    

    
     The global exception handling policy takes effect in the following scenarios:
      
       Service call fails on the Service Task node.

       After the policy is executed, the wakeup API carries exception information. (Currently, only the private API carries exception information during wakeup.)

       An exception occurs on the Script Task node.

       The operations cannot be continued because sequence flow conditions cannot be matched.

       The operations cannot be continued because conditions of an exclusive gateway cannot be matched.

      

    

    
      
     
      The exception handling policy at the process node level has a higher priority than that at the global level.

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the process to be configured.
      

      By default, the page is in view mode.

      

     Click Enter Editing Mode in the upper left corner of the page.

     Click the More Properties tab.

     Select the exception handling policy and exception callback API of the configured process based on the actual scenario.
      

      

      
       If such an API is configured, the API is called back asynchronously after the current process is terminated to notify the process caller that an exception occurs in the current process. The format of Fault Callback is cse://{Exception callback API}. The exception callback API supports the following parameters. Set the parameters based on site requirements.
       {
"order_id":"cm-00000001",
"phase_id":"AT10",
"error_code":{
     "code":"00040101",
     "message":"xxxxx",
     "solution":"xxxx"
     }
}
      

      

     Click  to save the settings.

     (Optional) If the full-link log function is enabled, you can locate the fault based on app O&M logs. On the Input Parameter tab page, click the Log icon to view app O&M logs.
      

      

      

      During step-by-step debugging, after you click the Log icon, the log information displayed on the app O&M log page is updated. Each time the step-by-step debugging is performed, a full-link ID is generated. Developers can view historical app O&M logs based on the link ID. App O&M logs are stored for only 30 minutes and cannot be viewed after 30 minutes. Each user can view only the app O&M logs generated during step-by-step debugging performed by the user.

      
        
       
        If the Log icon is not displayed or no information is displayed in the app O&M logs after you click the icon, the app O&M log function of the current system is unavailable. To use the function, apply to the administrator for enabling it.

name: Multi-Instance Type
title: Multi-Instance Type
text:
Multi-Instance Type
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    The multi-instance type is applicable to the scenario where multiple persons approve a task. In scenarios where multiple persons need to handle the task and make decisions at the same time, that is, a countersign task scenario, dynamic approvers are involved. In addition, different transfer paths need to be implemented based on the countersign approval result.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the User Task node to be configured in the process diagram.

     Click the Multi-Instance Type drop-down list in the property area on the right and select a value.
      

      
       The default value is None. The options in the Multi-instance Type drop-down list are as follows:
       
        None: If at least one person approves or rejects the ticket, the non-automated process continues.

        Parallel: The next phase can start only if multiple persons approve or reject the ticket and specific conditions are met. For example, the next phase can start only after everyone approves the ticket, more than three persons approve the ticket, or 50% of them approve the ticket.

        Sequential: The Accept phase can start only after all persons approve the ticket in sequence. If one person rejects the ticket, the Reject phase starts. The approval sequence is random.

       

      

      
        
       
        The approval conditions for the Multi-Instance type property are configured in the Handler property. When Multi-Instance Type is set to Sequential or Parallel, the Multi-Instance Completion Condition area appears in the Handler dialog box.

       

      

      

     Click Handler in the dialog box or click the text box next to Handler in the property area on the right.
      

      

      

      

     In the Multi-Instance Completion Condition area, click Create.

     Configure the approval conditions of the multi-instance type. Three countersign scenarios are provided: All (default value), Quantities, and Percent.
      

      
       If you do not configure the multi-instance rules or set Condition Type to All, all multi-instance tasks in this phase must be completed before the next phase starts. If no multi-instance rule meets the conditions, the multi-instance rule whose Condition Type is set to All is used.

       Based on the configured completion condition, the system obtains the submitted data of all approved subtasks for calculation. The calculation result is used as the multi-instance completion result of the task. If the multi-instance condition is met during the approval, the approval ends in advance. For example, if the number of handlers in the process phase for which Property is Operation Mode and Property Value is Accept exceeds 3, as shown in the following figure, the next phase starts.

name: Service Task Parameter
title: Service Task Parameter
text:
Service Task Parameter
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    
     Service tasks are used in the service phase in the automated ticket handling scenario and are not used in the non-automated process. Service Task Parameter is used to call a service in an API catalog or app.
     
      The Service Task node allows you to set input and output parameters, and exception handling policies of phases. When a phase starts, the API calls a required service using the input parameters, and generates output parameters using the returned result from the service.

      The Service Task node supports the following configuration switches: Record Calling Log, Asynchronize, Pause Before Execution, Automatic Execution Period, Wait After Execution, and Job Support Retry.

      The service task node supports dynamic API name configuration. The API name can contain dynamic variables. The format of the variables is the same as that of the default variables in the API expression, for example, {title} and {app_name}. The variable name must exist in the process context. For example, /adc-service/rest/v1/services/my_project/my_module/{service_name}, in which service_name indicates the variable name in the process context.

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the Service Task node to be configured in the process diagram.

     Click Service Task Parameter in the displayed dialog box or click the edit box of Service Task Parameter in the property area on the right.

     Select a service.
      

      
       Click the Select Service text box.

       In the displayed dialog box, select the required service.
        

       View the API name automatically generated on the API Service tab page.
        

        

      

      

     (Optional) Search for a service.
      

      
       Click  on the right of the Select Service text box.

       On the displayed page, click the Service tab.

       (Optional) Set the project, module, name, and open level, and click Search.

       On the service list page, select the required service.
        

       Click OK. View the API name automatically generated on the API Service tab page.

      

      

     (Optional) Select a registered service from the API tab page.
      

      
       Click  on the right of the Select Service text box.

       On the displayed page, click the API tab.

       In the left tree, select a category the service belong.
        
          
         
          The API catalog on the left can be filtered by permission.

         

        

       Select the required service from service cards.
        

       Click OK. View the API name automatically generated on the API Service tab page.
        

        

      

      

     Set parameters on the API Input tab page.
      

      
       Click the API Input tab.

       Click Load Params.

       In the displayed dialog box, click OK.
        After the parameters are loaded, the phase input parameters are automatically generated based on the service input parameters. The test personnel can adjust the input parameters as required.

        

      

      

     Set parameters on the API Output tab page.
      

      Set the output parameters displayed after a service is called. The first layer must be array, of which the length is 2. By default, object is ${_response}. The output parameter setting will be written in the process context _context.

      

      The following table details how to obtain variables from the Service Task node.

      
       
        
         Table 1 Methods of obtaining variables
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Variable Type

          
           How to Obtain

         

        
        
         
          
           Input parameter of Start Event

          
           ${API_Input}, for example, ${API_Input.account_id}.

         

         
          
           Original output of the service called by the current node, which is obtained from Service Task

          
           ${_response}

         

         
          
           Input or output parameters of a service task

          
           ${API10_input} or ${API10_output}. API10 indicates the phase ID.

         

         
          
           Process context

          
           ${_context}: contains parameters related to the current process instance. The parameters configured in the output parameters of Service Task are automatically written to the process context. You can modify the parameters in the process context in the script task.

         

        
       
      

      

     Configure the parameters of a Service Task node.
      

      Configure the parameters as required. Enable the switch to configure parameters.

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 2 Parameters on API Service
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Record Logs of Called Service

          
           This parameter specifies whether to record the logs of the called service of the phase in the automated process.

           
             NOTE: 
            
             
              Before setting Record Logs of Called Service, enable the tenant-level system configuration parameter recording_api_process_logs on the Products and Services > Administration > System Settings page of GDE data zone. The default value of this parameter is on, indicating that logs of the called service are recorded for all automated processes. If this parameter is set to off, logs of the called service are not recorded for all automated processes. The enabling operation takes effect only when the system configuration parameter is enabled.

              During automated process node configuration, Record Logs of Called Service is enabled and used only during automated process debugging. Before releasing an automated process, disable Record Logs of Called Service. Otherwise, the system performance deteriorates sharply.

             

            

           

         

         
          
           Log Scope

          
           This parameter specifies the scope of call logs, and the value can be All or Exception Log. The default value is Exception Log.

           This option is displayed only when Record Logs of Called Service is enabled.

           
             NOTE: 
            
             Log Scope is valid only for automated processes. For non-automated processes, all logs are recorded by default.

            

           

         

         
          
           Asynchronize

          
           This parameter specifies whether the called service can run asynchronously.

         

         
          
           Pause Before Execute

          
           Before the API service is called, the process instance is suspended. You need to configure the automatic execution period.

         

         
          
           Automatic Execution Period

          
           This option is displayed only when Pause Before Execution is enabled. If this function is selected, you can configure the execution period. The process instance is resumed during the period and is suspended in other periods.

           The automatic execution period must be longer than 5 minutes.

         

         
          
           Wait After Execution

          
           After the API service is called, the process instance enters the waiting state. After the timeout interval ends, the process instance is automatically resumed.

           After this parameter is enabled, you need to set the waiting duration. After the timing ends, the process instance proceeds to the next step.

           Value range: 30 seconds to 30 days

         

         
          
           Job Support Retry

          
           This parameter specifies whether a task can be retried after being interrupted.

           This parameter is displayed only when Pause Before Execute and Automatic Execution Period are enabled or Wait After Execution is enabled.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Submit.

name: Configuring the Policy for Handling Service Task Exceptions
title: Configuring the Policy for Handling Service Task Exceptions
text:
Configuring the Policy for Handling Service Task Exceptions
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    When an exception occurs in a service task, you can configure an exception handling policy including the following information:

    
     Terminate Exception: The process instance of the current service task is terminated unexpectedly, and the ticket status changes to Completed.

     Abort Exception: The process instance of the current service task is stopped unexpectedly, and the ticket status changes to Running.

     Ignore Exception: The process instance of the current service task ignores the exception and the ticket continues to be transferred.

     Customize Exception: custom exception. You can define a new exception handling policy based on the context of the current process instance.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the Service Task node to be configured in the process diagram.

     Click Service Task Parameter in the displayed dialog box or click the edit box of Service Task Parameter in the property area on the right.

     Click the Fault Handling Policy tab.

     Select the exception handling policy of the service task based on the actual scenario.
      

      
       The system provides the customization page only when the value is Customize Exception. You can customize multiple exception handling policies, in which FailedCondition indicates the exception condition. You can configure multiple exception conditions and customize multiple parameters. When all custom exception conditions are met, the policy with the highest array sequence is used. 
       
        
         
          
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Array

           
            Parameter

           
            Value

          

         
         
          
           
            0

           
            FailedCondition

           
            Condition 1

          

          
           
            Custom parameter 1

           
            Custom content 1

          

          
           
            Custom parameter 2

           
            Custom content 2

          

          
           
            1

           
            FailedCondition

           
            Condition 2

          

          
           
            Custom parameter 3

           
            Custom content 3

          

          
           
            Custom parameter 4

           
            Custom content 4

          

          
           
            Custom parameter 5

           
            Custom content 5

          

         
        
       

      

      

      

      

     Click Submit.

name: Sequence Flow Configuration Description
title: Sequence Flow Configuration Description
text:
Sequence Flow Configuration Description
 
 
  
  

  
   A sequence flow is used to identify the process execution direction. When a gateway is used together, you can configure conditions and default flows to implement multi-branch scenarios.

   
    Condition: This parameter needs to be configured only for the sequence flows behind the gateway component. A process supports the following condition types: TQL condition, script condition (JUEL), and script condition (TEL). TEL is a new condition added in 2.1. JUEL and TEL on the page are adapted and displayed based on the old and new processes.
     
      Only TQL and TEL can be used by new processes. JUEL cannot be used.

      TQL, JUEL, and TEL can be used by historical processes.

     

    Default Process: indicates whether the process is a default branch. Only one default process can be configured for a phase.
     
      Exclusive Gateway: If the sequence flow conditions of the exclusive gateway exit are not met, the default process is executed.

      Inclusive Gateway: If the sequence flow conditions of the inclusive gateway exit are not met, the default process is executed. If any of the sequence flow conditions of the inclusive gateway exit is met, the default process is not executed.

         Table 1 Parameters
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Configuration

         

        
        
         
          
           Component

          
           Name of the custom process component.

         

         
          
           Version

          
           Version of the custom process component.

         

         
          
           Developer Type

          
           Resource development permission control, that is, developers to whom the permissions to view, use, and delete themes are assigned.

           
            Personal: Grant the development permission only to the individual who creates the asset.

            Team: Grant the development permission to a specified team.

           Whether resources can be shared, that is, whether to allow other users except individuals or teams to view, use, copy, and export page templates (excluding change operations). Resource sharing is a restricted disclosure of resource permissions. That is, only the resource usage permission is shared, and the resource change permission is not.

name: Configuring the Process Archiving
title: Configuring the Process Archiving
text:
Configuring the Process Archiving
 
 
  
  

  
   Users can configure archiving for processes, and view the archiving configuration information.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     You have obtained the process configuration permission.

    

    
      
     
      In the runtime-state environment, the transfer logs of automated processes can be archived separately. When there are a large number of tickets, especially when there are a large number of phases in an automated process, the amount of log data to be archived is large. To ensure that the archiving speed is consistent with the new data generation speed and the disk usage is stable, the business side needs to plan disks in advance based on the number of tickets and archiving configuration.

     

    

   

   
    Context

    
     Process archiving configuration is a method for users to adjust the process storage time. Users can configure the archiving time and archiving policy for each process in the develop-state environment. The archiving policy can be deletion or dump. Processes configured with the deletion policy will be directly deleted when the target time is reached, and processes configured with the dump policy will be dumped to other databases when the target time is reached.

     For processes configured with dump archiving, secondary archiving can be configured. Secondary archiving is to archive the data that has been dumped to Elasticsearch and to delete the original data.

     During process archiving, you can customize the dump configuration and select the Elasticsearch model in the project module as the target model for dumping.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access the Process Archiving Configuration page.
      

      
       Method 1:
        On the Business Process page, choose More > Archive Config in the Operation column to configure the process archiving information.

       Method 2:
        
         On the Business Process page, click the process to be archived.

         Click Enter Editing Mode in the upper left corner of the page.

         In the Archive Config area in the lower right corner, click a blank area in the Archive Config box.

        

       Method 3:
        On the Business Process page, choose More > Process Archiving in the upper right corner to view, edit, and delete the configured process archiving information.

        If no information is configured, no data is displayed.

      

      

     On the displayed page, configure archiving information by referring to Table 1.
      

      

      
       
       
        
        
         
          Table 1 Parameters for archiving a process
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Parameter

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Archiving Type

           
            Archiving type of a process.

            
              NOTE: 
             
              
               For a non-automated process, Archiving Type can be set to Delete or Dump.

               For an automated process, Archiving Type can only be set to Delete.

              

             

            

          

          
           
            Retention Rows

           
            Number of rows for storing archived process data.

            
              NOTE: 
             
              Retention Rows is optional. After you enter this parameter, the priority of Retention Rows is higher than that of Time Left (Days).

             

            

          

          
           
            Retention Days

           
            Number of days for storing archived process data.

            
             For a non-automated process, the default value is 180. The value ranges from 1 to 1200.

             For an automated process, the default value is 7. The value ranges from 1 to 30.

            

            
              NOTE: 
             
              The end time of process archiving is calculated based on the following logic: For example, if today is June 20, 2023 and the value of Time Left (Days) is 1, after the process archiving task is executed today, data whose archiving end time is June 19 is retained, and data generated before 00:00 on June 19 is archived.

             

            

          

          
           
            Secondary Archiving Configuration

           
            This option is displayed only when Archiving Type is set to Dump.

            Whether to configure secondary archiving.

          

          
           
            Retention Days

           
            This parameter needs to be configured only when Secondary Archiving Configuration is enabled.

            Number of days for storing archived data during secondary archiving.

            
              NOTE: 
             
              It is recommended that the number of retention days for secondary archiving be greater than the number of retention days configured for archiving.

             

            

          

          
           
            Customize dump configuration

           
            The business side can customize the target model for dumping. When this parameter is enabled, the Elasticsearch elastic model can be used as the target model for dumping.

          

          
           
            Process Model

           
            This parameter is displayed only when Customize dump configuration is enabled.

            Select an Elasticsearch elastic model as the target model for custom dumping.

          

          
           
            Process Log Model

           
            This parameter is displayed only when Customize dump configuration is enabled.

            Select an Elasticsearch elastic model as the target log model for custom dumping.

          

         
        
       

      

      

     Click Submit.
      

      If Archiving Type is set to Dump on the archiving configuration page of a non-automated process, the backend system checks whether the elastic model used for archiving exists after you click Submit. If not, a message is displayed, asking you to create an elastic model.

      
       If you click Create, the system automatically creates the missing elastic model and saves the archiving configuration. After the process is deployed in the runtime-state environment, the archiving task can be properly executed.

       If you click Skip, the system only saves the archiving configuration. After the process is deployed in the runtime-state environment, the primary and secondary archiving tasks cannot be executed properly.

      

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    
     On the Business Process page, choose More > Process Archiving in the upper right of the page.

     On the Process Archiving page, click Refresh to update the process archiving configuration in real time.

     Click Edit in the Operation column to edit the process archiving.

     Click Delete in the Operation column to delete the process archiving.

name: Configuring a Data Dictionary
title: Configuring a Data Dictionary
text:
Configuring a Data Dictionary
 
 
  
  

  
   To ensure the normal running of non-automated processes, the administrator needs to configure the data dictionary for the parameters used by the process based on site requirements.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment.

     You have obtained the process configuration permission.

    

   

   
    Context

    The data dictionary function takes effect only for non-automated processes. Only the data dictionary of the current project can be imported.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the Business Process page, click Data Dictionary in the upper right corner.

     Create a data dictionary by importing a file.
      

      
        
       
        
         The data to be imported to the data dictionary cannot contain sensitive information.

         For the query service that is dynamically generated after the data dictionary is imported, you are advised to configure dynamic permissions for access permission control. For details, see Managing Dynamic Permissions.

        

       

      

      
       Choose Import > Data Import.

       Click studio_data_dictionary_template.xlsx to download the template to your local PC.

       Open the template and set parameters.
        
         Set parameters in the model sheet.
          
           Fields marked with an asterisk (*) are mandatory.

           In the Status column, 1 indicates that the resource option is in the Enabled state by default after being imported. 0 indicates that the resource option is in the Disabled state by default after being imported.

           In the Allow Customization column, yes indicates that the customization is supported. no: indicates that the customization is not supported.

          

        

        
         Set parameters in the option sheet.
          
           Fields marked with an asterisk (*) are mandatory.

           The values in the Project Name, Module Name, and Model Name columns in the option sheet must be the same as those in the model sheet.

           In the Status column, 1 indicates that the resource option is in the Enabled state by default after being imported. 0 indicates that the resource option is in the Disabled state by default after being imported.

          

        

        
         Save the edited template on the local PC.

        

      

      
       Set Import Type.
        Import Type can be Universal or Additional.

        
         If Universal is selected, the data in the Excel file is used as the data set of the model for overwriting.

         If Additional is selected, only the data in the Excel file can be changed.

        

       Click Add and select the edited template.

       Click Submit to import the data file.
        After the import is successful, the imported data dictionary is displayed in the list.

      

      

     Manually create a data dictionary.
      

      
       Create a data dictionary model.
        
         Click Create.

         Set Data Model and Allow Customization. Parent Model Name and Description are optional.

         Click Submit.
          
           After the submission is successful, the new data dictionary model is displayed in the list.

           The data dictionary model created by default is enabled.

          

        

       Create a data dictionary option.
        
         Click the name of the model for which you want to create a data dictionary.

         On the displayed page, click Create.

         Set Option Name and Option Label. Parent Option Name and Description are optional.

         Click Submit.
          
           After the submission is successful, the new data dictionary option is displayed in the list.

           The data dictionary option created by default is enabled.

          

        

      

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After creating a data dictionary, you can perform the following operations.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Operations after creating a data dictionary
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation

        
         Description

        
         Procedure

       

      
      
       
        
         Editing a data dictionary model

        
         You can edit a data dictionary model.

        
         On the Data Dictionary page, click Edit in the Operation column.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           Once a data model is created, it cannot be edited.

          

         

       

       
        
         Exporting data dictionaries

        
         You can batch export data dictionaries.

        
         
          On the Data Dictionary page, click Export.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.
           
             NOTE: 
            
             By default, all records on the page are exported. You can also export the required data dictionary based on the search criteria.

            

           

         

       

       
        
         Disabling a data dictionary model

        
         Only enabled data dictionary models can be disabled.

        
         Method 1:

         
          On the Data Dictionary page, click Disable in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

         Method 2:

         
          On the Data Dictionary page, select one or more enabled data dictionary models.

          Click Disable above the list.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Enabling a data dictionary model

        
         Only disabled data dictionary models can be enabled.

        
         Method 1:

         
          On the Data Dictionary page, click Enable in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

         Method 2:

         
          On the Data Dictionary page, select one or more disabled data dictionary models.

          Click Enable above the list.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Editing a data dictionary option

        
         You can edit a data dictionary option.

        
         
          Click the name of the model to be edited.

          On the Option Management page, click Edit in the Operation column.

         

       

       
        
         Disabling data dictionary options

        
         Only enabled data dictionary options can be disabled.

        
         Method 1:

         
          On the Option Management page, click Disable in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

         Method 2:

         
          On the Option Management page, select one or more enabled data dictionary options.

          Click Disable above the list.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Enabling data dictionary options

        
         Only disabled data dictionary options can be enabled.

        
         Method 1:

         
          On the Option Management page, click Enable in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

         Method 2:

         
          On the Option Management page, select one or more disabled data dictionary options.

text:
Basic RPA Concepts
 
 
  
  

  
   This topic describes the basic concepts of RPA and the functionalities of each module in RPA.

   
    What Is RPA?

    RPA is broadly considered a form of business process automation. RPA is a technology that mimics the way humans interact with software. RPA technology creates bots that can manipulate data, run applications, complete tasks, make decisions based on predefined rules, and communicate with other digital systems. RPA is used to automate human activities that are manual, rule-based, and repetitive, speeding up standard data input processes previously handled by humans.

    Compared with traditional workflow automation tools, RPA develops the action list by watching the user perform that task in the application's graphical user interface (GUI), and then perform the automation by repeating those tasks directly in the GUI. This can lower the barrier to use of automation and drastically speed up automation development.

    RPA tools have strong technical similarities to GUI testing tools. These tools also automate interactions with the GUI, and often do so by repeating a set of demonstration actions performed by a user. RPA tools differ from such systems in that they allow data to be handled in and between multiple applications, for instance, receiving email containing an invoice, extracting the data, and then typing that into a bookkeeping system.

    The use of RPA services also aligns with certain risks. For example, a more complex maintenance environment needs to be created for the existing software, or the GUI used by some applications may not be the most efficient and stable choice in some scenarios.

    In general, RPA is considered as one of the most efficient methods for digital transformation. It can be seen as labor force provided by a virtual robot that is operated and managed by the service line (supported by IT), just like a human labor.

   

   
    What Are RPA Modules?

    RPA consists of the following three modules: Studio, Management Center, and Robot. Figure 1 shows the relationship between these modules.

    
     Figure 1 Relationship between RPA modules
     
    

    
     Management Center: is a server system that can be accessed using a browser. It helps you monitor robots and manage (store) scripts, reusable components, assets, and processes used by robots in a unified manner. Management Center has the following functions:
      
       Control: Create and maintain connections to robots, and group robots.

       Manage: Assign automation process jobs or tasks to robots.

       Monitor: Record the execution status of robot jobs.

      

     Studio (automation design canvas): An agent system installed on the local PC and used to design automation workflows. In Studio, you can use the built-in recorder to record the drag-and-drop activities of the mouse to build an automation workflow intuitively. With a pre-set of robots, Studio can also be used to execute business processes on the GUI. The Studio agent supports two orchestration modes: Studio and StudioE, which can meet the requirements of both professional and citizen developers.

     Robot (executor): An agent system installed on a local PC and used to execute the designed automation process triggered locally or initiated by Management Center.

    

   

   
    RPA Applicable Scope

    When you design an RPA automation process, analyze whether RPA is applicable to the corresponding business processes based on the following factors:

    
     Clear rules exist in business processes.
      RPA can be used to implement process automation only when the business process has a clear logical sequence and each process branch has a clear judgment standard. If there are random judgment conditions in a business process or other context conditions that depend on experience or processes, it is difficult to use RPA to solve such problems.

     Business processes are repetitive.
      When a business process is executed, the execution can be repeated. In this case, RPA can be used to automate the process. RPA cannot be used to solve the problem if the execution processes are different.

     The input data or process data of business processes is identifiable.
      During the execution of a business process, the input data or process data must be identifiable and extractable, for example, numbers, strings, and so on. If images or other analog input information is used, RPA-related technologies such as optical character recognition (OCR) are required for collaborative processing. Therefore, RPA may not be applicable to complex data processing scenarios.

     The system that executes business processes has high stability.
      RPA integrates different systems in GUI interaction mode. If the system GUI or data input and output formats change frequently, the developed automation processes change accordingly, increasing the development and maintenance workload.

     Background-oriented business processes are complex.
      The advantage of using RPA is not obvious when designing responsible business processes for the background. In this case, you are advised to use programming languages to implement process automation.

    

   

   
    RPA Implementation Process

    Figure 2 shows the RPA implementation process.

    
     Figure 2 RPA implementation process
     
    

    The detailed process is as follows:

    
     RPA evaluation: Before RPA implementation, analyze and evaluate business processes to determine whether RPA is applicable to process automation.

     RPA design: Streamline the business logic of each business process phase, and analyze the input data, output data, and data rules required by each phase. The design results of a phase will be used as the input data for further RPA development.

     RPA development: Develop an RPA business process as designed and verify the development result.

     RPA test: Simulate the scenario of a requirement to test the correctness and availability of RPA. After the test is complete, put away the RPA asset.

     RPA optimization: Continuously optimize RPA based on service requirements, and optimize and evolve RPA from aspects such as requirement scenarios, usability, and performance.

Introduction to RPA
 
 
  
  

  
   RPA consists of Studio, Assistant, and Connector. The combination of these three tools meets different requirements of RPA.

   
    Studio

    Studio provides the right automation canvas for you to build workflows on your local PC. After Studio is installed, select a desired orchestration mode.

    

    

    
     Studio: designed for professional developers who are experienced in programming and can also use low-code tools to leverage all design capabilities of Studio.

     StudioE: designed for citizen developers to skip the error-prone manual programming. Its drag-and-drop mode reduces the coding workload but its development capability is weaker than that of Studio. Moreover, scripts developed in Studio cannot run in StudioE.

    

   

   
    Assistant

    Assistant is a tool created specifically to execute automated processes that are triggered locally or initiated by Management Center. When you install Assistant, select GDE IPA Assistant (executor).

   

   
    Connector

    Connector is a tool used to remotely connect to other executors. When you install Assistant, select GDE IPA Connector (connector).
