name: Security Statement
title: Security Statement
text:
Security Statement
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes possible security risks when RPA is used and provides operation suggestions.

   When RPA is used, the following security risks may exist. Read the following content and perform operations based on suggestions:

   
    If sensitive information or personal data is used during development, the information may be disclosed. You are advised to obtain user authorization, plan the saving and export locations of the project before development, and delete the local project information after the design is complete to prevent other users from obtaining the information.

    RPA provides security protection for robots by means of prompt messages, role permission separation, and whitelist control for high-risk commands. However, due to business scenario requirements, users can record any operation and develop executable scripts such as Python scripts. Therefore, users are liable for the security risks caused by these operations and executable scripts. Save a project in a specific user directory to prevent the project from being tampered with or attacked by other users. Exercise caution when opening a project whose source is unknown.

    You are advised to isolate physical executors from other systems and install antivirus software. If some antivirus software detects that the agent software and executor software are malicious, configure a whitelist for antivirus software.

    You are advised to install and use RPA as a user with low permissions in C:\Program Files. Users need to pay attention to and bear the security risks caused by operations such as executor installation and use by high-privilege users due to business scenario requirements.

    When email-related controls are used, RPA performs security hardening for information bombing. A single chatbot can send emails to a maximum of 100 recipients at the same time, and can send emails to the same recipient for a maximum of 20 times at an interval of 0.5 seconds.

    When Excel controls are used, macros or formulas can be used to process Excel and CSV data based on service requirements. However, data-driven engine (DDE) injection attacks may be caused. Exercise caution when performing this operation.

    When file processing controls are used, the capabilities of the OS are used to operate the file system. Consider the impact on the file system during development. Do not write large files, delete temporary files, or delete important files by mistake.

    RPA restricts the types and sizes of files in a compressed package to prevent the import of .zip compression bombs (compressed packages that are suspicious and generate a large amount of data after decompression).

   

   Besides, you understand and agree that your use of the Service must comply with applicable laws and regulations. We only provide a standard service upon your requests and are not responsible for the legal compliance of your use.

text:
Main GUIs
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes the GUIs and functions of the Studio agent in Studio and StudioE orchestration modes.

   
    Main GUI in Studio

    Figure 1 shows the main GUI in Studio orchestration mode.

    
     Figure 1 Main GUI in Studio orchestration mode
     

    

    The functions of each functional area on the main page in Studio orchestration mode are as follows:

    
     Area 1: The menu bar includes the following five level-1 menus: Home, Design, Settings, Help, and Extension Management. The main functions of the menu are as follows:
      
       Home: Studio home page used to open an existing project, import a recorded script, create a project, view recently edited projects, and create a project using a template

       Design: Studio process design page used to develop, debug, and verify RPA business processes

       Settings: Studio configuration page used to set parameters on the general, license, driver, certificate, connection, shortcut key, orchestration mode configuration, and other tab pages You can set the Studio information based on site requirements.

       Help: Help center of Studio used to provide help documents, access the forum, and obtain iLearning courses

       Extension Management: Extension package management page of Studio used to display installed extension packages and install required extension packages

      

     Area 2: The toolbar includes the UI Recorder, Run, Debug, Save, Publish, Advance, and other buttons. The functions of these buttons are as follows:
      
       UI Recorder: Start a recorder. When you record steps on a web page, local Windows, or local Java application, Studio automatically converts the steps into an execution script of the RPA executor.

       Run: Play back or execute a recorded script to check whether the process in Studio is correct.

       Debug: Debug a recorded script to check whether the script in Studio can be executed and analyze and rectify faults occurred during script execution.

       Save: Save a recorded script to prevent the information recorded in Studio from being lost.

       Publish: Publish a recorded and debugged script to a local disk, RPA Orchestrator, or GDE Store.

       Advance: Search for sub-modules or check items and scripts in the project to quickly locate the control corresponding to the source code or view the check items and scripts.

       Data Extract: Click this button to obtain the web page data by following the wizard, and automatically generate the corresponding control on the canvas.

      

     Area 3: This area displays projects and controls. You can drag the required controls to the canvas in Studio.

     Area 4: This area enables you to edit the canvas and source codes. In this area, you can develop RPA business processes.

     Area 5: This area provides canvas tools. You can use the Undo, Redo, Zoom In, Zoom Out, Overview, Locate to Start, Auto Layout, Enable Auto Layout, Collapse sidebar, and Clear buttons. When you develop an RPA process on the canvas, select tools as required.
      
       Undo: Go back to the previous operation.

       Redo: Go to the latest operation performed before you click Undo.

       Zoom In and Zoom Out: Zoom in or out on a process diagram on the canvas.

       Overview: View the overall thumbnail of the canvas.

       Locate to Start: Locate the start node in the middle of the canvas.

       Auto Layout: Display a process in the middle of the canvas and automatically arrange it.

       Enable Auto Layout: Automatically display a process in the middle of the canvas and arrange the process lines.

       Collapse sidebar: Collapse the sidebars on both sides of the canvas.

       Clear: Clear all controls on the current canvas.

      

     Area 6: This area displays the control properties. When clicking a control on the canvas, you can view and edit the control properties on the Attribute tab page or view the control functions, parameters, and usage examples on the Help tab page.

     Area 7: This area provides a debugging area. When executing or debugging a script, you can view the run logs and error list of the script, set global variables and parameters required for debugging the script, perform the health check on the script, view related script elements, or view script reference relationships.

    

   

   
    Home Page in StudioE Orchestration Mode

    Figure 2 shows the main window in StudioE orchestration mode.

    
     Figure 2 Home page in StudioE orchestration mode
     

    

    Compared with the main page in Studio orchestration mode, the main page in StudioE orchestration mode has the following differences:

    
     Area 1: The level-1 menu Extension Management is deleted from the menu bar. The installed or required plugin packages cannot be viewed.

     Area 2: The Debug, Publish, and Advance buttons are removed from the toolbar. You are not allowed to debug or publish recorded scripts, search for submodules in a project, and check projects and scripts.

     Area 3: The Reuse Script and Custom plug-in functions are removed from the project and control display area. The control categories such as AI and Dataprocess are deleted. Only basic control categories such as UI Automation and APP are retained.

     Area 4: The Source Code mode is removed from the canvas and source code editing area. RPA processes can be developed only on the canvas.

     Area 5: Canvas tool area, which has the same functions as those in Studio orchestration mode.

     Area 6: Property area, which is the same as that in Studio orchestration mode.

     Area 7: The All Variables and Global Parameters tab pages are removed from the debugging area. In this are, only run logs of the script can be viewed.

text:
First Instance Development
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to quickly develop robotic script instances using an example.

   
    Scenario

    During system maintenance, you need to open the local MaintainLog.txt file, enter the information about the daily maintenance work, and then save the file. To improve the maintenance efficiency, you can develop a robotic script instance to realize automation.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     Create a project.
      

      
       In the navigation pane, click .

       Click New Project.

       In the displayed dialog box, configure the project.
        

       Click Create.

      

      

     Record a robot script.
      

      
       On the Design page of the project, click UI Recorder.

       In the displayed window, click .

       Record the steps for double-clicking the MaintainLog.txt file.
        
         Move the cursor to the MaintainLog.txt file on the local PC, and move the cursor to the button displayed on .
          

         In the displayed drop-down list, select Double Click to open the MaintainLog.txt file.
          

        

       Record the steps for entering the daily maintenance information in the MaintainLog.txt file.
        
         In the MaintainLog.txt file, move the cursor to the text editing area, and then move the cursor to the button displayed on .
          

         In the displayed drop-down list, select Input.

         In the displayed dialog box, enter 2021/10/13: The system is running properly. Click OK.
          

        

       Record the steps for saving the MaintainLog.txt file.
        
         In the MaintainLog.txt file, move the cursor to the File menu, and then move the cursor to the button displayed on .

         In the displayed drop-down list, select Click.
          

         In the displayed File submenus, move the cursor to Save, and then move the cursor to the button displayed on .

         In the displayed drop-down list, select Click.
          

        

       Record the steps for closing the MaintainLog.txt file.
        
         In the MaintainLog.txt file, move the cursor to the X button, and then move the cursor to the button displayed on .

         In the displayed drop-down list, select Click.
          

        

       In the recorder window, click  to save the recorded script.

      

      

     Develop an RPA business process.
      

      
       Go back to the Design page and check whether the recorded script (block module) exists on the canvas.
        

       Create a connection between the Start node and the Block module.
        

      

      

     Replay the developed RPA business process.
      

      
       On the Design page, click Run.
        Studio automatically executes the RPA business process and demonstrates the recorded steps on the local PC.

       After the execution is complete, view the log information about the process. If the execution is successful, the developed process is successfully verified. If the execution fails, locate, analyze, and rectify the fault based on the log information, and then run the script again until the execution is successful.

text:
Studio Installation and Configuration
 
 
  
  

  
   Before using Studio to develop a robotic process, you need to install Studio and complete related configuration.

  

  
   
    Installing Studio
      Before using Studio to develop robotic processes, you need to install Studio.

    Configuring Studio
      After Studio is installed, you need to complete related configurations before using Studio functions.

    Managing RPA Certificates
      After Studio is installed, use the certificate management function to enhance the security of data exchanges between Studio and the server, preventing user personal information from being maliciously attacked or illegally obtained.

    Making Studio Interwork with RPA Orchestrator
      In Studio, you can import or set the connection information of RPA Orchestrator to connect Studio to RPA Orchestrator.

    Making Studio Interwork with GDE Store
      You can configure the parameters for making GDE Store interwork with Studio. After Studio is successfully interworked with GDE Store, you can view or download extensions from GDE Store on the Extension Management page of Studio.

    Making Studio Interwork with ADC Studio
      You can set the connection information about ADC Studio on Studio to make Studio interwork with ADC Studio. After ADC Studio is successfully interworked, you can release the developed RPA business process to GDE Store on the Design page of Studio.

    (Optional) Switching the Orchestration Mode
      You can switch the Studio orchestration mode based on site requirements.

    (Optional) Managing Extension Packages
      In the Studio orchestration mode, you can view the installed official and third-party extension packages and customize the local extension packages.

name: Installing Studio
title: Installing Studio
text:
Installing Studio
 
 
  
  

  
   Before using Studio to develop robotic processes, you need to install Studio.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     More than 5 GB of space has been reserved in the directory for installing the Studio agent software and ensuring its normal running.

     The agent software installed on the local PC does not support IPv6.

    

   

   
    Context

    Studio can be installed in overwriting mode. If Studio of an earlier version has been installed, automatically uninstall it and then install Studio of the new version.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Download the Studio agent software package.
      

      
       From the Support website
        
         Log in to the Support website, and access the software path of the corresponding version based on the version mapping table.

         Download the Studio agent software package ADC_x.x.x_Software_Windows-x64_Pkg-IPA-Studio-Setup.zip, manually verify the software package integrity by referring to OpenPGP Signature Verification Guide.

         After the check is complete, decompress the Studio agent software package to the local installation directory.

        

       From the RPA website
        
         Log in to the RPA website.

         In the Designer area, click the Windows tab.

         Click Download on the right of Business Edition or Education Edition based on the actual application scenario to save the Studio agent software package to the local PC.

         Decompress GDE_IPA_Studio_x.x.x_Windows.zip to the local installation directory.

        

      

      

     Install the Studio agent software.
      

      
       Access the installation directory and double-click GDE_IPA_Studio_x.x.x.exe.

       Select an installation language as required and click OK.

       In the displayed window, click Next.

       Enter the common name of the asset package certificate, for example, rpa-studio, and click Next.

       In the Privacy Data Use Agreement window, select I agree to the terms in the "Privacy Data Use Agreement" (Accept)., and click Next.
        
          
         
          If you want to withdraw the privacy statement, you can uninstall the RPA agent to prevent RPA from collecting personal data. You can also deregister the user on the server to delete personal information and disable the user from logging in to the agent, thereby preventing RPA from collecting user information.

         

        

       In the Choose Install Location window, click Browse, select an installation directory, and click Install.
        After the installation is complete, select Run GDE IPA Studio, and click Finish to close the installation page and start Studio.

        

        

      

      

     Double-click GDE IPA Studio on the desktop to start Studio.

name: Configuring Studio
title: Configuring Studio
text:
Configuring Studio
 
 
  
  

  
   After Studio is installed, you need to complete related configurations before using Studio functions.

   
    Prerequisites

    The server certificate file and CRL have been obtained and compressed into a .zip package. For details about how to obtain digital certificates on the web server, see How Do I Obtain the Service Certificate and CRL?

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, click .

     Configures the basic information of Studio.
      

      
       Choose Settings > General.

       Modify the configuration based on site requirements.
        

        

        
         
          
           Table 1 Parameter description
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Language

            
             Language used by Studio

             
              简体中文

              English

             

           

           
            
             Controller View Mode

            
             Display mode of controls on the Design page of Studio

             
              Command Mode: Commands corresponding to the control are displayed.

              Detailed Mode: The function description of the control is displayed.

             

             For example, the mouse click event control in detailed mode is the click control in command mode.

           

           
            
             Publish Timeout (s)

            
             Timeout interval for Studio to release a project If the release duration exceeds the value of this parameter, the project release fails.

             The value ranges from 1 to 600, in seconds.

           

           
            
             Automatically Trigger Health Check Before Release

            
             Whether to automatically start the health check before Studio is released.

             
              Yes

              No

             

           

           
            
             Default number of historical execution log files

            
             Number of execution log files stored in Studio. If the number of log files exceeds the value of this parameter, the system automatically overwrites the originally stored log files.

             Value range: [1,100]

           

           
            
             The quantity backup files

            
             Number of script backup files in Studio. After you modify and save the script, the system backs up the modified script file to the bak directory of the project. If the number of script backup files exceeds the value of this parameter, the system automatically overwrites the originally stored script files.

             Value range: [0,100]

           

           
            
             Minimize while running

            
             Whether to minimize Studio during script running

             
              Yes

              No

             

           

           
            
             Default Lines Quantity of Console Output

            
             Default number of output lines of the console during script running. If the number of output lines on the console during script running exceeds the value of this parameter, the system automatically overwrites the initial lines.

             Value range: [1,5000]

           

           
            
             Pause in the Event of Exceptions

            
             Whether to interrupt the debugging if an exception occurs during script debugging.

             
              Yes: Pause debugging at the script control where an exception occurs.

              Yes: Stop debugging at the script control where an exception occurs.

             

           

           
            
             Highlight Controls Being Executed

            
             Whether to highlight the controls that are being executed during script debugging.

             
              Yes

              No

             

           

           
            
             Project Save Path

            
             Default path for storing project files

             Click  to select a path.

           

           
            
             Run Screen Record and Acquire

            
             Whether to automatically take screenshots during script recording and element pickup

             
              Yes: Screenshots are automatically taken and the process execution effect can be previewed.

              No: No screenshot is taken and the process execution effect cannot be previewed.

             

           

           
            
             Enable Record Minimize

            
             Whether to minimize Studio during script recording

             
              Yes

              No

             

           

           
            
             Tips for Playback Progress

            
             Type of the progress information displayed when a script is played back

             
              Info

              Warning

              Error

              None

             

           

           
            
             Whether to display deprecated controls

            
             Whether to display controls that are not recommended in the control list

             
              Yes

              No

             

           

           
            
             Use display mode while using JSON editor

            
             Display mode of data content in Studio when the JSON editor is used

             
              Tree Mode

              Code Mode

             

           

           
            
             Parameter Name Is Visible

            
             Whether to display the actual name of a parameter in the Parameter area of the control property

             
              Yes

              No

             

           

           
            
             To display subscript parameters in a table

            
             Whether to use a table to edit and display parameters of the control property in a subscript

             
              Yes: Use a table to edit and display parameters.

              No: Directly edit and display parameters.

             

           

           
            
             Show Action Name in Graphic Title

            
             Whether to display the control name in the diagram element title

             
              Yes

              No

             

           

          
         
        

      

      

     Configure the Studio license.
      

      
       Choose Settings > License.

       Click  under ESN to copy the ESN of the local PC and record it to the local PC for future use.
        
          
         
          ESN is the device identifier of the RPA agent and is not associated with a personal account.

         

        

       Click  under Official website link to go to the RPA official website.

       On the Trial Activation tab page, enter the ESN obtained in 4.b and select Designer for Product.

       Click Get License to download the license file.

       Go back to the Apply License page of Studio, and click Re-import to import the downloaded license file.

       (Optional) To delete the imported license, click Remove. In the displayed dialog box, click Confirm.

      

      

     (Optional) If a browser other than Chrome is used, configure the web driver of Studio in the target browser.
      

      
       Choose Settings > Driver.

       Based on the browser type, click  on the right of Current Browser Version.

       Based on the browser version in use, access the directory of the corresponding version and download the web driver file whose name contains Driver.

       After the download is complete, click  on the right of Current Driver Version to import the downloaded web driver file.
        

      

      

     (Optional) If a browser other than Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge is used, install the WeAutomate Web plugin for the browser to ensure that the function of picking up web elements is normal.
      

      
       Choose Settings > Tools.

       Click the corresponding card to install the plugin of the browser by browser type.
        

       In the displayed dialog box, perform subsequent operations as prompted and click OK.

      

      

     After the plugin of the browser is installed, enable the WeAutomate Web plugin in the browser to ensure that the web elements can be picked up during Studio recording.
      

      
       The following uses the Chrome browser as an example to describe how to enable the plugin. For details about how to enable other browsers, see the related browser documents.
       
        Open Google Chrome, click  in the upper right corner, and select Settings.

        In the navigation pane, choose Extension Management.

        On the displayed page, enable WeAutomate Web.
         

        Restart the browser for the new plugin to take effect.

       

      

      

     (Optional) If you want to record the Java desktop app, install corresponding plugins to ensure that the function of picking up Java elements can be used properly.
      

      
       Choose Settings > Tools.

       Select the plugin installation mode in the Java card based on the installation directory of the Java app.
        

        
         In default mode, install plugins for Java apps that are installed in the Program Files or Program Files(x86) directory and for which the %JRE_HOME% environment variable is set. In this case, click Default Installation and wait until the installation is complete.

         In manual mode, install plugins for Java apps that are not installed in the Program Files and Program Files(x86) directories. In this case, click Manual Installation. In the displayed Install Java Plugin in Custom Directory dialog box, enter or select the Java app plugin installation directory and click Install.

name: Managing RPA Certificates
title: Managing RPA Certificates
text:
Managing RPA Certificates
 
 
  
  

  
   After Studio is installed, use the certificate management function to enhance the security of data exchanges between Studio and the server, preventing user personal information from being maliciously attacked or illegally obtained.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     The server certificate file and CRL have been obtained and compressed into a .zip package. For details about how to obtain digital certificates on the web server, see How Do I Obtain the Service Certificate and CRL?

     (Optional) The latest asset package certificate file has been obtained and compressed into a .zip package.

    

   

   
    Background

    The certificate management function of Studio is mainly used to manage the following certificates:

    
     Service certificate and CRL: used to establish a secure connection between Studio and the server. The trusted certificate issued by the CA does not need to be imported to Studio, for example, the trust certificates provided on www.baidu.com.

     Asset package certificate: used to establish a secure connection between Studio and executor.

    

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, choose .

     Choose Settings > Certificate Management.

     Import the service certificate to Studio.
      

      
       Click Import under Service Certificate.

       In the displayed dialog box, click  and select the obtained service certificate file in ZIP format.

       Click OK.

      

      

     Import the CRL to Studio.
      

      
       Click Import under Revoked Certificate List.

       In the displayed dialog box, click  and select the obtained CRL file in ZIP format.

       Click OK.

      

      

     (Optional) Update the asset package certificate in Studio.
      

      
       Under Asset Certificate, click Update.

       In the displayed dialog box, click  on the right of New Certificate and select the obtained new certificate file of the asset package.

       Click  on the right of New KeyStore and select the new keystore file of the obtained asset package.

       In the New KeyStore Password text box, enter the password of the new keystore file of the asset package.
        

       Click Update.

       In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

name: Making Studio Interwork with RPA Orchestrator
title: Making Studio Interwork with RPA Orchestrator
text:
Making Studio Interwork with RPA Orchestrator
 
 
  
  

  
   In Studio, you can import or set the connection information of RPA Orchestrator to connect Studio to RPA Orchestrator.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     Application Development Center (ADC), server of RPA Orchestrator, has been installed and deployed. For details, see topic "Installation" in GDE x.x.x Product Documentation.

     You have created a user or machine-machine user on ADC for logging in to RPA Orchestrator. For details, see Data Zone Configuration > Data Zone Configuration (default Tenant) > Identity Authentication Management > User and Role Permission Management > Configuring Machine-Machine User Authentication in GDE x.x.x Product Documentation.

    

   

   
    Context

    Studio allows you to set the connection information in either of the following ways:

   

   
    (Preferred) Import configuration: Import the Studio configuration package exported from the Studio page in RPA Orchestrator.

   

   
    Manual configuration: Manually enter the parameters of RPA Orchestrator, including the configuration name and management center address.

   

   
    Procedure (Import Configuration)

    
     Obtain the Studio configuration package from RPA Orchestrator.
      

      
       Log in to the RPA Orchestrator page.

       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click RPA Orchestrator. 

       In the navigation pane, choose Products and Services > RPA Orchestrator > Workstations > Studio.

       On the studio list page, choose More > Export Configuration in the Operation column of the studio.

       Save the imported studio configuration package to a specified directory for future use.

      

      

     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, click .

     Choose Settings > Connection Configuration > RPA Orchestrator.

     On the displayed page, click Create.

     In the Basic Configuration area, set parameters related to RPA Orchestrator.
      

      
       In the Basic Configuration area, set Configuration Name, click Import, and select the configuration package exported in 1.
        

        

       (Optional) If the verification certificate of the configuration package does not exist in the trust certificate store, check the security of the certificate. In the Certificate dialog box, click Trust the certificate.
        

      

      

     In the Access Configuration area, configure the access information.

           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Login Type

          
           Method for logging in to RPA Orchestrator

           
            User Login: Use a user account to log in to the system.

            Machine-Machine Login: Use a machine-machine account whose authentication type is Basic for login.

           

         

         
          
           User Account

          
           User account for connecting to RPA Orchestrator

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Type is set to User Login.

         

         
          
           User Password

          
           Password of the user account for connecting to RPA Orchestrator

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Type is set to User Login.

         

         
          
           Default Tenant Account

          
           Default tenant name corresponding to the user account

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Type is set to User Login.

         

         
          
           AccessId(AccessId)

          
           Machine-machine account used to connect to RPA Orchestrator

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Type is set to Machine-Machine Login.

         

         
          
           Secretkey(Secretkey)

          
           Password of the machine-machine account, which is used to connect to RPA Orchestrator

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Type is set to Machine-Machine Login.

         

        
       
      

      

     (Optional) If you need to connect to RPA Orchestrator through a proxy server, configure the proxy information.
      

      
       In the Proxy Configuration area, set Enable Proxy to Yes.

       Set proxy parameters. 
        
         
          
           Table 2 Parameter description
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Proxy Account

            
             Account for logging in to the proxy server

           

           
            
             Proxy Password

            
             Password for logging in to the proxy server

           

           
            
             Agent Host

            
             Host IP address or domain name of the proxy server

           

           
            
             Proxy Port

            
             Port number of the host where the proxy server is located

           

          
         
        

      

      

     Check whether Studio is properly connected to RPA Orchestrator.
      

      
       Click Check Connections to check whether RPA Orchestrator can be connected.

       After the connection is verified, click Save.

      

      

     Establish a connection between Studio and RPA Orchestrator.
      

      
       You can use either of the following methods to make Studio interwork with RPA Orchestrator:
       
        Method A: Establish a connection on the RPA Orchestrator configuration page of Studio.
         
          On the RPA Orchestrator configuration page of Studio, click  in the Operation column of the configured RPA Orchestrator.
           After the connection is successful, the dot on the left of the RPA Orchestrator configuration name changes from gray to green.

          (Optional) If there are multiple RPA Orchestrators, click  in the Operation column of the RPA Orchestrator to be connected.
           
             
            
             Only one RPA Orchestrator can be connected at a time.

            

           

         

        Method B: Click the button in the lower right corner of Studio to set up a connection.
         
          In the lower right corner of Studio, click Select RPA Orchestrator Configuration.

          In the RPA Orchestrator configuration list, select the RPA Orchestrator to be connected and click  to switch the connection status to Online.
           After the connection is successful, Offline in the lower right corner changes to Online and Select RPA Orchestrator Configuration changes to the corresponding RPA Orchestrator configuration name.

           

          (Optional) If there are multiple RPA Orchestrators, switch to different RPA Orchestrators for connection based on site requirements.
           
             
            
             Only one RPA Orchestrator can be connected at a time.

            

           

         

       

      

      

    

   

   
    Procedure (Manual Configuration)

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, click .

     Choose Settings > Connection Configuration > RPA Orchestrator.

     On the displayed page, click Create.

     In the Basic Configuration area, set parameters related to RPA Orchestrator.
      

      
       
        
         Table 3 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Configuration Name

          
           Name of the management center configuration. The value can contain digits, letters, Chinese characters, underscores (_), and hyphens (-), and must start with a digit, letter, or Chinese character.

         

         
          
           Configure Tenant ID

          
           Tenant ID used for connecting to RPA Orchestrator

           No configuration is required.

         

         
          
           Configure Tenant ID

          
           Tenant name used for connecting to RPA Orchestrator

           No configuration is required.

         

         
          
           ESN of Studio

          
           Studio ESN

           The value is automatically generated after Studio is installed.

         

         
          
           RPA Orchestrator Address

          
           Address of the RPA Orchestrator to be connected. The value format is as follows: {IP address or domain name}:{Port number}.

         

         
          
           Studio ID

          
           Custom studio ID. It must contain 32 characters.

         

         
          
           Studio Name

          
           Name of Studio

           No configuration is required.

         

         
          
           Team Name

          
           Name of the team that Studio belongs to

           No configuration is required.

         

         
          
           Team UID

          
           UID of the team that Studio belongs to

           No configuration is required.

         

        
       
      

      

     In the Access Configuration area, configure the access information.
      

      
       
        
         Table 4 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Login Type

          
           Method for logging in to RPA Orchestrator

           
            User Login: Use a user account to log in to the system.

            Machine-Machine Login: Use a machine-machine account whose authentication type is Basic for login.

           User account for connecting to RPA Orchestrator

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Type is set to User Login.

         

         
          
           User Password

          
           Password of the user account for connecting to RPA Orchestrator

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Type is set to User Login.

         

         
          
           Default Tenant Account

          
           Default tenant name corresponding to the user account

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Type is set to User Login.

         

         
          
           AccessId(AccessId)

          
           Machine-machine account used to connect to RPA Orchestrator

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Type is set to Machine-Machine Login.

         

         
          
           Secretkey(Secretkey)

          
           Password of the machine-machine account, which is used to connect to RPA Orchestrator

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Type is set to Machine-Machine Login.

         

        
       
      

      

     (Optional) If you need to connect to RPA Orchestrator through a proxy server, configure the proxy information.
      

      
       In the Proxy Configuration area, set Enable Proxy to Yes.

       Set proxy parameters. 
        
         
          
           Table 5 Parameter description
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Proxy Account

            
             Account for logging in to the proxy server

           

           
            
             Proxy Password

            
             Password for logging in to the proxy server

           

           
            
             Agent Host

            
             Host IP address or domain name of the proxy server

             Port number of the host where the proxy server is located

           

          
         
        

      

      

     Check whether Studio is properly connected to RPA Orchestrator.
      

      
       Click Check Connections to check whether RPA Orchestrator can be connected.

       After the connection is verified, click Save.

      

      

     Establish a connection between Studio and RPA Orchestrator.
      

      
       You can use either of the following methods to make Studio interwork with RPA Orchestrator:
       
        Method A: Establish a connection on the RPA Orchestrator configuration page of Studio.
         
          On the RPA Orchestrator configuration page of Studio, click  in the Operation column of the configured RPA Orchestrator.
           After the connection is successful, the dot on the left of the RPA Orchestrator configuration name changes from gray to green.

          (Optional) If there are multiple RPA Orchestrators, click  in the Operation column of the RPA Orchestrator to be connected.
           
             
            
             Only one RPA Orchestrator can be connected at a time.

            

           

         

        Method B: Click the button in the lower right corner of Studio to set up a connection.
         
          In the lower right corner of Studio, click Select RPA Orchestrator Configuration.

          In the RPA Orchestrator configuration list, select the RPA Orchestrator to be connected and click  to switch the connection status to Online.
           After the connection is successful, Offline in the lower right corner changes to Online and Select RPA Orchestrator Configuration changes to the corresponding RPA Orchestrator configuration name.

           

          (Optional) If there are multiple RPA Orchestrators, switch to different RPA Orchestrators for connection based on site requirements.

Making Studio Interwork with GDE Store
 
 
  
  

  
   You can configure the parameters for making GDE Store interwork with Studio. After Studio is successfully interworked with GDE Store, you can view or download extensions from GDE Store on the Extension Management page of Studio.

     GDE Store has been installed and deployed. For details, see topic "Installation (OP)" in GDE x.x.x Product Documentation.

            Name

           
            Description

name: Making Studio Interwork with ADC Studio
title: Making Studio Interwork with ADC Studio
text:
Making Studio Interwork with ADC Studio
 
 
  
  

  
   You can set the connection information about ADC Studio on Studio to make Studio interwork with ADC Studio. After ADC Studio is successfully interworked, you can release the developed RPA business process to GDE Store on the Design page of Studio.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     ADC Studio has been installed and deployed. For details, see topic "Installation" in GDE x.x.x Product Documentation.

     GDE Store has been configured on the runtime-state page corresponding to ADC Studio. For details, see GDE Store Configuration.

     You have created a machine-machine account for connecting to ADC Studio. Authentication Type of the machine-machine account must be AK/SK and the account must be associated with the machine-machine role adc_integration. For details, see Configuring Machine-Machine User Authentication and Authorization.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, click .

     Choose Settings > Connection Configuration > ADC Studio.

     On the displayed page, click Create.

     In the Basic Information and Basic Configuration areas, set parameters related to ADC Studio.
      

      

      
       
       
        
         
          Table 1 Parameter description
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Name

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Configuration Name

           
            Name of the configuration item of ADC Studio. The value can contain digits, letters, underscores (_), and hyphens (-), and must start with a digit or letter.

          

          
           
            Design State Address

           
            Login address of ADC Studio. The value can only be in the format of "https://IP address:Port number" or "https://Domain name".

          

          
           
            AccessId(AccessId)

           
            Machine-machine user name for connecting to ADC Studio

          

          
           
            Secretkey(Secretkey)

           
            Machine-machine user password for connecting to ADC Studio

          

         
        
       

      

      

     Check whether the Studio is properly connected to ADC Studio.
      

      
       Click check connection to check whether ADC Studio can be connected.

       After the connection is verified, click Save. If the connection fails, check whether the corresponding configuration is correct and check the connection again.

      

      

     Establish a connection between Studio and ADC Studio.
      

      
       On the configuration list page of ADC Studio, click  on the right of a saved ADC Studio configuration item.
        
         After the connection is successful, the dot on the left of the ADC Studio configuration name changes from gray to green.
          

         After the connection is successful, click  in the navigation pane on the left. On the displayed Design page, click Publish to release the RPA business process to GDE Store.

        

       (Optional) If there are multiple configurations of ADC Studio, click  on the right of a configuration for switching based on site requirements.
        
          
         
          A user can connect to only one ADC Studio at a time.

name: (Optional) Switching the Orchestration Mode
title: (Optional) Switching the Orchestration Mode
text:
(Optional) Switching the Orchestration Mode
 
 
  
  

  
   You can switch the Studio orchestration mode based on site requirements.

   
    Context

    Studio supports the following two orchestration modes:

    
     Studio: designed for professional developers who are experienced in programming and can also use low-code tools to leverage all design capabilities of Studio. After Studio is installed, the Studio mode is used by default.

     StudioE: designed for citizen developers to skip the error-prone manual programming. Its drag-and-drop mode reduces the coding workload but its development capability is weaker than that of Studio. Moreover, scripts developed in Studio cannot run in StudioE.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, click .

     Choose Settings > Orchestration Mode.

     Click View or change the orchestration mode of Studio.

     In the displayed dialog box, select the required orchestration mode.
      

      

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Studio Installation and Configuration

name: (Optional) Managing Extension Packages
title: (Optional) Managing Extension Packages
text:
(Optional) Managing Extension Packages
 
 
  
  

  
   In the Studio orchestration mode, you can view the installed official and third-party extension packages and customize the local extension packages.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     The orchestration mode has been set to Studio.

     (Optional) To install the extension package of RPA Orchestrator, the following conditions must be met:
      
       Studio has been connected to RPA Orchestrator and switched to Online. For details, see Making Studio Interwork with RPA Orchestrator.

       The extension package has been uploaded on the Products and Services > RPA Orchestrator > Robots Asset > Plugin Management page of RPA Orchestrator.

      

     (Optional) To install the GDE Store extension package, either of the following conditions must be met:
      
       Studio has been connected to GDE Store and switched to Online. For details, see Making Studio Interwork with GDE Store.

       Studio is not connected to GDE Store, but is successfully connected to RPA Orchestrator and is in the Online state. In addition, the GDE Store configuration already exists on the Products and Services > Administration > GDE Store Configuration page of RPA Orchestrator.

      

    

   

   
    Background

    The extension center of Studio provides the following functions:

    
     View and uninstall preset extensions, locally installed official extensions, and third-party extensions of RPA Orchestrator and GDE Store.

     View and install local official extensions in the Extension Market and third-party extensions of RPA Orchestrator and GDE Store.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, choose .

     View the installed extension package.
      

      
       Click the Installed tab.

       In the extension list, click an extension name to view its version and release date on the right.

       (Optional) If the extension is no longer required, click Uninstall to delete it.

      

      

     Import a local extension package.
      

      
       Choose Extension Market > Local, and click + on the right of Local.

       In the displayed dialog box, set the extension type to Customized or Official, click  on the right of the Plug-in File Path box, and select the extension package to be uploaded.
        
          
         
          
           If the extension type is set to Customized, the extension file to be imported must be in .zip or .gdk format.

           If the extension type is set to Official, the extension file to be imported must be in .whl format.

          

         

        

       (Optional) If the verification certificate of the plugin file does not exist in the trust certificate store, check the security of the certificate. In the displayed dialog box, click Trust the certificate.
        

       After the file is parsed, set Description as required.
        

       Click Import.

       (Optional) If you need to uninstall a local extension, return to the Installed tab page and select the extension to uninstall it.

      

      

     Install an extension package in RPA Orchestrator.
      

      
       Choose Extension Market > Management Center.

       In the extension list of the management center, click the name of the extension to be installed and view the version and release date of the extension on the right.
        

       In the extension list of the management center, click  on the right of the extension to be installed.
        After the installation is successful, the status of the extension in the extension list is Installed.

        

       (Optional) If you need to uninstall an extension of the management center, return to the Installed tab page and select the extension to uninstall it.

      

      

     Install an extension package that exists on GDE Store.
      

      
       Choose Extension Market > GDE Store.

       In the extension list of GDE Store, click the name of the extension to be installed and view the version and release date of the extension on the right.
        

       In the extension list of GDE Store, click  on the right of the extension to be installed.

       (Optional) If the verification certificate of the plugin file does not exist in the trust certificate store, check the security of the certificate. In the displayed dialog box, click Trust the certificate.
        

       Check whether the GDE Store extension is successfully installed.
        After the installation is successful, the status of the extension in the extension list is Installed.

        

       (Optional) If you need to uninstall the GDE Store extension, return to the Installed tab page and select the extension to uninstall it.

name: Installing the RPA Agent
title: Installing the RPA Agent
text:
Installing the RPA Agent
 
 
  
  

  
   The agent software includes GDE IPA Assistant (executor) and GDE IPA Connector (connector). The installation methods for them are the same. This section uses GDE IPA Assistant as an example to describe how to install an agent software.

   
    Prerequisites

    To ensure the normal installation and use of the agent software, the installation directory size must be greater than 3 GB.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Download and decompress the agent software package of the executor.
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Downloading the agent software package of the executor
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Download Path

          
           Download Method

         

        
        
         
          
           Support website

          
           
            Visit the Support website and go to the software directory of the corresponding version based on the version mapping table.

            Download the agent software package ADC_x.x.x_Software_Windows-X64_Pkg-IPA-Agent.zip and manually verify the software package integrity by referring to OpenPGP Signature Verification Guide. x.x.x indicates the version of the agent software package.

            After the check is completed, decompress the agent software package to the local installation directory.

           

         

         
          
           RPA Orchestrator

          
           
            Contact the RPA administrator to upload the agent software package on the Products and Services > RPA Orchestrator > Tools > Agent Package page.

            After the upload is complete, go to the runtime-state page and choose Products and Services > RPA Orchestrator > Workstations > Executor or Products and Services > RPA Orchestrator > Workstations > Connector.

            Click Download Agent Package, download the agent software package to the local PC, and decompress it to the local installation directory.

           

         

         
          
           RPA website

          
           
            Log in to the RPA website.

            In the Robot Assistant area, click the Windows tab.

            Click Download on the right of Business Edition or Education Edition based on the actual application scenario to save the agent software package to the local PC.

            Decompress the downloaded agent software package GDE_IPA_Assistant_x.x.x_xxx.zip to the local installation directory. Replace x.x.x with the version and xxx with the OS architecture (that is, arm64 or amd64), respectively.

           

         

        
       
      

      

     Access the installation directory and double-click GDE_IPA_Assistant_x.x.x.exe.

     Select the installation language and click OK.

     On the WebUI, select the type of the agent to be installed and set Installation Path.
      

      
       If the executor agent needs to be installed, select GDE IPA Assistant.

       If the connector agent needs to be installed, select GDE IPA Connector.

      

      
       Figure 1 Selecting the agent type
       

      

      
        
       
        
         To install GDE IPA Assistant or GDE IPA Connector for all users, select Install for all users.

         If you want to withdraw the privacy statement, you can uninstall the RPA agent to prevent RPA from collecting personal data. You can also deregister the user on the server to delete personal information and disable the user from logging in to the agent, thereby preventing RPA from collecting user information.

        

       

      

      

     Click Install Now.

     After the installation is complete, select Create Desktop Shortcut, Add to Start Menu, Start Upon Power-on, or Start Now as required.
      

      
       Figure 2 Installation success
       

      

      

     Click OK to complete the installation of GDE IPA Assistant, and exit the installation program.

Configuring the RPA Agent
 
 
  
  

  
   This section uses GDE IPA Assistant as an example to describe how to configure the RPA agent software.

  

  
   
    Common Settings
      Before you use the agent, configure the basic information about the agent, including the language, script scanning path, and license.

    Connection Settings
      Before using the agent, set the parameters for connecting the agent and management center, for example, the management center address, executor or connector ID, and machine-machine account and password.

      Before using an agent, you need to apply for the license of the agent, and then import the license file to the agent software.

    Certificate Management
      Before using the agent, import the SSL certificate for establishing a secure connection between the agent and the management center.

    Configuring a Credential
      A Picture in Picture (PiP) credential password frees users from repeatedly entering the credential password when running a script job in PiP mode.

    Tool Management
      Before using the agent, you need to install the corresponding extension program and web driver for the used browser.

name: Common Settings
title: Common Settings
text:
Common Settings
 
 
  
  

  
   Before you use the agent, configure the basic information about the agent, including the language, script scanning path, and license.

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the home page of the agent, click  in the upper right corner, and choose Settings.

     In the navigation pane, choose Common Settings.

     Modify the basic settings of the RPA agent based on site requirements.
      

      
       Figure 1 Common Settings
       

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters on the Common Settings page
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Agent Version

          
           Agent software version

         

         
          
           PC ESN

          
           ESN of the PC where the agent software is installed, which is used to apply for a license

         

         
          
           VC Running Library

          
           Whether the VC running library is installed

           
            Installed

            Not installed

           

         

         
          
           Select Language

          
           Language used by the agent software

           
            Simplified Chinese

            English

           

         

         
          
           Open Log When running

          
           Whether to record logs when the agent software is running

           
            Yes

            No

           

         

         
          
           Clean Environment After Execution

          
           Whether to clear the data generated during the running of the agent software after the agent software is started

           
            Yes

            No

           

         

         
          
           Start When System Boot

          
           Whether to start the agent software when the PC is started

           
            Yes

            No

           

         

         
          
           When closing the main window

          
           Status of the agent software after the main window is closed

           
            Close

            Minimize

           

           You can also set prompt box appears to determine whether to receive a prompt message after the main window is closed.

         

         
          
           Script Scan Path

          
           Path of the agent software scanning script

           Click Browse, and then select the path of the script to be scanned by the agent software.

         

         
          
           Recorded File Save Path

          
           Path where the agent software stores screen recording files

           Click Browse, and then select the path for storing the screen recording files of the agent software.

           You can click Open or Clean to view log files or delete unnecessary log files based on site requirements.

           You can click Open or Clean to view third-party cache files or delete unnecessary third-party cache files based on site requirements.

           Size of the screen recording file generated when the agent software is executed

           You can click Open or Clean to view screen recording files or delete unnecessary screen recording files based on site requirements.

         

         
          
           Script Backup

          
           Size of the script backup file that is automatically downloaded or manually delivered when the agent software is in Online state

           You can click Open or Clear to view script backup files or delete unnecessary script backup files based on site requirements. The deletion does not affect the execution of subsequent tasks.

name: Connection Settings
title: Connection Settings
text:
Connection Settings
 
 
  
  

  
   Before using the agent, set the parameters for connecting the agent and management center, for example, the management center address, executor or connector ID, and machine-machine account and password.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have obtained the machine-machine account or login user account of GDE data zone.
      
       Machine-machine account: Access the GDE data zone page, choose Administration > Identity Authentication > Machine-Machine User Management to create a machine-machine account and record its password. The authentication type of the machine-machine account must be basic, and the bound human-machine user must be an existing RPA user. Otherwise, the created machine-machine account cannot be used to connect the agent to the management center.

       User account: user account (except the W3 account) and password for logging in to the GDE data zone.

      

     You have checked that the agent is in the Offline state. Otherwise, the connection cannot be set.

    

   

   
    Context

    The agent software allows you to set the connection information in either of the following ways:

   

   
    (Recommended) Import configuration: Import the executor configuration package exported from the Executor page in RPA Orchestrator.

   

   
    Manual configuration: Manually enter the parameters of RPA Orchestrator, including the configuration name and management center address.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the home page of the agent, click  in the upper right corner, and choose Settings.

     In the navigation pane, choose Connection Settings and click Create.

     In the Common Settings area, set the parameters of RPA Orchestrator using either of the following methods:
      

      
       Manual configuration: Set the parameters of RPA Orchestrator by referring to Table 1. 
        
         
         
          
           Table 1 Parameters of RPA Orchestrator
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Config Name

            
             Name of an RPA Orchestrator configuration item

           

           
            
             Tenant ID

            
             Tenant ID used for connecting to RPA Orchestrator

           

           
            
             Tenant Account

            
             Tenant name used for connecting to RPA Orchestrator

           

           
            
             Management Center Address

            
             Address of the RPA Orchestrator to be connected. The value format is as follows: {IP address or domain name}:{Port number}.

           

           
            
             Executor ID

            
             Customized studio ID. It must contain 32 characters.

           

           
            
             Executor Name

            
             Executor name

           

           
            
             Team Name

            
             Name of the team that the executor belongs to

           

           
            
             Team UID

            
             UID of the team that the executor belongs to

           

          
         
        

       Import configuration: Export the configuration package of the agent from the runtime-state environment and import the configuration package to the agent.
        
         Access the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > RPA Orchestrator > Workstations > Executor or Products and Services > RPA Orchestrator > Workstations > Connector.

         On an executor or connector card, choose More > Export Configuration to download the compressed configuration file package to the local PC.

         Return to the connection configuration page of the agent, enter the configuration name, click Import, and select the configuration package exported in the previous step.
          
           Figure 1 Importing the connection configuration
           

          

         (Optional) If the verification certificate of the configuration package does not exist in the trust certificate store, check the security of the certificate. In the displayed dialog box, click OK to complete the basic information configuration.
          
           Figure 2 Confirming certificate security
           

          

        

      

      

     In the Access Config area, configure the access information.
      

      
       
        
         Table 2 Parameters for access configuration
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Login Method

          
           Method for logging in to RPA Orchestrator

           
            User Login: Use a user account to log in to the system.

            Machine-machine Login: Use a machine-machine account to log in to the system.

           

         

         
          
           User Account

          
           User account for connecting to RPA Orchestrator

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Method is set to User Login.

         

         
          
           Password

          
           Password of the user account for connecting to RPA Orchestrator

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Method is set to User Login.

         

         
          
           Default Tenant Account

          
           Default tenant name corresponding to the user account

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Method is set to User Login.

         

         
          
           AccessId(AccessId)

          
           Machine-machine account used to connect to RPA Orchestrator

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Method is set to Machine-machine Login.

         

         
          
           Secretkey(Secretkey)

          
           Password of the machine-machine account, which is used to connect to RPA Orchestrator

           This parameter is displayed only when Login Method is set to Machine-machine Login.

         

        
       
      

      

     (Optional) If you need to connect to RPA Orchestrator through a proxy server, set Whether to enable to Yes in the Proxy Settings area and set proxy parameters.
      

      
       
        
         Table 3 Parameters for proxy configuration
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Proxy Account

          
           User name for logging in to a proxy server

         

         
          
           Proxy Password

          
           User password for logging in to a proxy server

         

         
          
           Proxy Host

          
           Host IP address or domain name of the proxy server

         

         
          
           Proxy Port

          
           Port number of the host where the proxy server is located

         

        
       
      

      
        
       
        
         The proxy settings cannot be modified when the agent is in the Online state. Switch the agent to the Offline state before modifying the proxy settings.

         To disable the proxy, set Whether to enable to No, click Save, and establish the reconnection.

        

       

      

      

     Click Check Connection to check whether agent software is properly connected to RPA Orchestrator.
      

      
       If the connection is successful, click Save.

       If the connection fails, correct the connection configuration and check the connection again until the connection is successful.

      

      

     Establish a connection between the agent and RPA Orchestrator as required.
      

      
       Establishing a connection on the Connection Configuration page of the agent software
        
         On the Connection Configuration page of the agent software, click  in the Operation column of the configured RPA Orchestrator.
          After the connection is successful, the dot on the left of the RPA Orchestrator configuration name changes from gray to green.

         (Optional) If there are multiple RPA Orchestrator configuration items, click  in the Operation column of the RPA Orchestrator configuration item to be connected.
          
            
           
            Only one RPA Orchestrator can be connected at a time.

           

          

        

       Clicking the button in the upper right corner of the agent software to establish a connection
        
         In the upper right corner of the agent software, click no config.

         In the RPA Orchestrator configuration list, select the management center to be connected and click  to switch the connection status to Online.
          After the connection is successful, the color of the dot in the upper right corner changes from gray to green. That is, the status changes from Offline to Online, and Not configured changes to the name of the corresponding management center.

          
           Figure 3 Establishing a connection with RPA Orchestrator
           
          

         (Optional) If there are multiple RPA Orchestrator configuration items, switch to different configuration items for connection based on site requirements.
          
            
           
            Only one RPA Orchestrator can be connected at a time.

Tool Management

     After the plugin of the browser is installed, enable the WeAutomate Web plugin in the browser to ensure that the related web scripts can be executed by WeAutomate Assistant.
      

      
       The following uses the Google Chrome browser as an example to describe how to enable the plugin. For details about how to enable other browsers, see the related browser documents.
       
        Open Google Chrome, click  in the upper right corner, and select Settings.

        In the navigation pane, choose Extension Management.

        On the Extension Management page, toggle on WeAutomate Web and restart the browser for the new plugin to take effect.

     (Optional) To use Assistant to execute Java desktop app scripts, install the corresponding Java app plugin.

        In the manual mode, install plugins for Java apps that are not installed in the Program Files and Program Files(x86) directories. In this case, click Manual Installation. In the displayed Install Java Plugin in Custom Directory dialog box, enter or select the Java app installation directory and click Install.

       

      

      

      

      

     (Optional) Install the web driver tool of the Assistant.
      

      
       Download the web driver tool.
        In the Web Driver area on the Tools page of the agent, click  on the right of Current Browser Version on the card based on the browser type, and then go to the directory based on the browser version to download the web driver file containing Driver.

name: RPA Business Process Development
title: RPA Business Process Development
text:
RPA Business Process Development
 
 
  
  

  
   After learning how to develop RPA business processes, you can master common Studio operations.

  

  
   
    RPA Business Development Process
      This section describes how to develop an RPA business process.

    Creating a Project
      Studio allows you to create a project manually or using a template.

    Recording Robotic Functional Blocks or Scripts
      This section describes how to record robotic functional blocks or scripts.

    Orchestrating an RPA Business Process
      After the robotic script is recorded, orchestrate an RPA business process to realize business automation.

    Saving an RPA Business Process
      After you orchestrate an RPA business process, save the process to prevent data loss.

    Checking an RPA Business Process
      After the orchestrated RPA business process is saved, perform health check on the business process.

    Debugging an RPA Business Process
      After the RPA business process is checked, debug it to verify that each step in the process is available.

    Running an RPA Business Process
      After the RPA business process is debugged, run the entire process to check whether it is correct.

    Releasing an RPA Business Process
      After the RPA business process is debugged and running properly, release it to RPA Orchestrator, GDE Store, or a local disk.

   

   
    
     Parent topic: RPA Development Guide

name: RPA Business Development Process
title: RPA Business Development Process
text:
RPA Business Development Process
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to develop an RPA business process.

   Figure 1 shows how to develop an RPA business process.

   
    Figure 1 Development process
    
   

   
    
     
      Table 1 Process description
     
     
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Step

       
        Sub-step

       
        Description

      

     
     
      
       
        Project Creation

       
        Creating a Project

       
        Create a project before developing an RPA business process.

      

      
       
        RPA Business Process Development

       
        Recording Robotic Functional Blocks or Scripts

       
        Record robot functional blocks or scripts for orchestrating the RPA business process based on site requirements.

      

      
       
        Orchestrating an RPA Business Process

       
        Orchestrate RPA business process elements such as function blocks, scripts, and controls based on site requirements.

      

      
       
        Saving an RPA Business Process

       
        Save the orchestrated RPA business process to prevent data loss.

      

      
       
        RPA Business Process Verification

       
        Checking an RPA Business Process

       
        After the RPA business process is successfully saved, perform health check on the RPA business process.

      

      
       
        Debugging an RPA Business Process

       
        Debug the saved RPA business process to check whether it works properly. If no, locate the fault, analyze the fault cause, and rectify the fault.

      

      
       
        Running an RPA Business Process

text:
Manually Creating a Project
 
 
  
  

  
   Manually create a project before you develop robot scripts.

   
    Background

    After a project is created, Studio saves the project files to a specified project path. The following figure shows the directory structure of the project.

    

    Each folder and file can be used as follows:

    
     bak: stores robot script backup files of a project.

     Input: stores the input files of a project.

     Lib: stores the third-party libraries or codes on which the robot script of a project depends.

     Project: stores the robot script files of a project.

     ScreenShot: stores screenshot files generated during robot script recording.

     temp: stores temporary files of a project.

     readme_en_US.txt: stores the directory notes in English.

     readme_zh_CN.txt: stores the directory notes in Chinese.

     Robot.xml: stores the project basic information.

     *.rpa: stores the RPA file of a project that can be opened in one-click mode.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, choose .

     Click New Project.

     In the displayed dialog box, configure the project.

           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Project Name

          
           Project name, which can contain only Chinese characters, letters, digits, and underscores (_). The value must start with a letter or Chinese character.

         

         
          
           Saved Path

          
           Path for saving project files. Click  to select a path.

            Windows
