title: Using Git for Collaborative Project Development
text:
Using Git for Collaborative Project Development
 
 
  
  

  
   By cloning an existing Git repository, you can develop a project collaboratively.

   
    Restrictions

    Currently, a local Git repository cannot be created. You can clone an existing Git repository.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, click .

     Choose Repository Project > Clone Git Repository.

     In the displayed dialog box, configure the Git repository information.
      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Authentication Mode

          
           Authentication mode of the Git repository

           
            SSH

            HTTPS

           

         

         
          
           URL

          
           URL of the Git repository

           
            When Authentication Mode is set to SSH, the URL must start with ssh://.

            When Authentication Mode is set to HTTPS, the URL must start with https://.

           

         

         
          
           Sign-out Path

          
           Local path to which the Git repository is cloned

           Click  and select a local directory based on site requirements.

         

         
          
           Use Certificate

          
           Whether to use credentials to log in to the Git repository

           This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Mode is set to HTTPS.

         

         
          
           User Name

          
           User name for logging in to the Git repository

           This parameter is displayed only when Use Certificate is selected.

         

         
          
           Password

          
           Password for logging in to the Git repository

           This parameter is displayed only when Use Certificate is selected.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Clone.
      

      
       After the cloning is successful, Studio automatically opens a Studio project in the Git repository.
       
         
        
         If the Git repository to be cloned contains multiple Studio projects, click OK in the dialog box displayed after the cloning is successful to manually select the corresponding project.

        

       

      

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After the Git repository is cloned, project members can perform the following operations for collaborative development:

    
     
      
       Table 2 Operations after cloning the Git repository
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation

        
         Description

        
         Procedure

       

      
      
       
        
         Managing branches

        
         You can add, rename, or delete project branches in the local Git repository.

        
         
          In the navigation pane, click .

          In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project in the local Git repository.

          Click the current branch in the lower right corner and select Manage Branches from the drop-down list.

          Add a branch.
           
            In the displayed Branch Management dialog box, select the branch and click .

            Enter the name of the branch and click New from {Branch name}.

           

          Rename a branch.
           
            In the displayed Branch Management dialog box, select the branch.

            Enter a new name for the branch and click Update Branch.

           

          Delete a branch
           
            In the displayed Branch Management dialog box, select the branch and click .

            In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

           

         

       

       
        
         Switching branches

        
         You can switch the branch of a project in the local Git repository based on site requirements.

         
           NOTICE: 
          
           Before switching the branch of a project in the local Git repository, ensure that the content of the local project has been saved and submitted.

          

         

        
         
          In the navigation pane, click .

          In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project in the local Git repository.

          Click the current branch in the lower right corner and select another branch from the drop-down list.
           

           

         

       

       
        
         Refreshing a remote branch

        
         You can refresh the remote branch of a project in the local Git repository and synchronize the branch from the remote repository to the local repository.

        
         
          In the navigation pane, click .

          In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project in the local Git repository.

          Click the current branch in the lower right corner and select Refresh Remote Branches from the drop-down list.

         

       

       
        
         Managing the remote repository address

        
         You can set the default remote repository address, and add, delete, or rename the remote repository address.

        
         
          In the navigation pane, click .

          In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project in the local Git repository.

          Click the current branch in the lower right corner and select Manage Remote Addresses from the drop-down list.

          Set the default remote repository address.
           
            In the displayed Remote Address Management dialog box, right-click the remote repository.

            Click Set as Default Address.

           

          Add the remote repository address.
           
            In the displayed Remote Address Management dialog box, click .

            Enter the name and address of the remote repository.

            Click Add.

           

          Rename the remote repository address.
           
            In the displayed Remote Address Management dialog box, click the remote repository.

            Change the name and address of the remote repository.

            Click Update.

           

          Delete the remote repository address.
           
            In the displayed Remote Address Management dialog box, select the branch and click .

            In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

           

         

       

       
        
         Viewing script changes

        
         You can view the script changes of the local project compared with the last submission record in the local Git repository.

        
         
          In the navigation pane, click .

          In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project name in the local Git repository.

          Click the Project tab, right-click any script name in the project, and choose Git > Show Changes.

          View the changes in the script.

         

       

       
        
         Submitting the change content

        
         You can submit the changes of a local project to the local Git repository.

        
         
          In the navigation pane, click .

          In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project name in the local Git repository.

          Click the Project tab, right-click the modified script name in the project, and choose Git > Submit.

          In the displayed dialog box, select the modified file and enter Submit Message.
           
             NOTE: 
            
             In the modified files list, right-click a modified file to view the modified content.

            

           

          Click Submit. To push the package to the remote Git repository, click Submit and Push.

         

       

       
        
         Undo

        
         You can cancel the changes in a local project to restore the project to the status before the last submission.

        
         
          In the navigation pane, click .

          In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project name in the local Git repository.

          Click the Project tab, right-click the modified script name in the project, and choose Git > Undo.

          In the displayed dialog box, select the modified file.
           
             NOTE: 
            
             In the modified files list, right-click a modified file to view the modified content.

            

           

          Click Undo.

         

       

       
        
         Viewing the script submission records

        
         You can view the submission records of a script in the project.

        
         
          In the navigation pane, click .

          In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project name in the local Git repository.

          Click the Project tab, right-click any script name in the project, and choose Git > Show History.

          In the displayed dialog box, view the submission history of the script.
           
            Double-click a submission record to view the changes made before the last submission.

            Right-click any two submission records and compare the changes between the two versions.

            Select a submission record and click the Details and Modification History tabs to view the detailed submission information and modification content.

           

         

       

       
        
         Pull

        
         You can obtain the latest project content from the remote Git repository based on site requirements.

         
           NOTICE: 
          
           Before you obtain the latest project content from the remote Git repository, ensure that the content of the local project has been saved and submitted.

          

         

        
         
          In the navigation pane, click .

          In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project name in the local Git repository.

          Click the Project tab, right-click any script name in the project, and choose Git > Pull.
           After the pulling is successful, the user can obtain the content pushed by other users to the remote Git repository.

         

       

       
        
         Push

        
         You can push the submission records of the local Git repository to the remote Git repository.

        
         
          In the navigation pane, click .

          In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project name in the local Git repository.

          Click the Project tab, right-click any script name in the project, and choose Git > Push.
           After the push is successful, other users can obtain the content pushed to the remote Git repository in pull mode.

name: Introducing Recording Functions
title: Introducing Recording Functions
text:
Introducing Recording Functions
 
 
  
  

  
   This topic describes the basic concepts and functions related to recording.

   
    Basic Concepts

    
     Control: corresponds to a step in the RPA business process. For example, you can use the Open Web Page control to open a specified web page.

     Functional Block: corresponds to a sub-process in the RPA business process. Multiple steps are encapsulated into a functional block during recording for the RPA business process to use.

     Subscript: corresponds to a sub-process in the RPA business process. Multiple steps are stored in a subscript during recording for the RPA business process to call.

    

   

   
    Function Description

    Studio supports the following three recording functions:

    
     Record and generating function blocks (Ctrl+R): Steps during recording are converted into an executable functional block. If the functional block needs to be used in an RPA business process, connect it to other controls of the process.

     Clear and record: You need to clear the canvas before recording. Steps during recording are converted into an executable script. If the script needs to be used in an RPA business process, connect it to other controls of the process.

     Creating and Recording Subscripts: Steps during recording are converted into an executable subscript. If the subscript needs to be used in an RPA business process, call the Invoke subscript control.

              Local Variables: indicates that this parameter can only be used by the current script.

             

           

           
            
             Variable Type

            
             Type of a variable

             
              String

              Number

              Sensitive (displayed only when Scope is set to Global Parameters)

             

           

           
            
             Variable Value

            
             Value of a variable

           

          
         
        

       Click OK.

       Reference the created variable in @{} format in the control. For example, reference the test_param2 variable in the input value of the type control.
        

      

      

     After the recording is complete, click .

     In the recorder window, check whether the operations in the recording list are redundant and meet scenario requirements.
      

      
       If there are redundant operations, for example, dragging the mouse back and forth or clicking an incorrect operation, click  corresponding to the operation to delete it.

       If the recording does not meet scenario requirements, click  to continue recording or  to record again.

      

      

     After the check is complete, click  to save the recorded subscript and exit the recorder window.

     Go back to the Design page of the project and check whether the recorded steps exist on the canvas of the subscript.
      

      
       If yes, the recording is successful.

       If no, contact Huawei technical support.

text:
Recording a Local Application Subscript
 
 
  
  

  
   After you record a local application script, operations can be automatically performed on the specified local application pages.

   
    Prerequisites

    A project has been created.

   

   
    Context

    Studio supports the recording of the following local application subscripts:

    
     Windows applications: Software provided by Windows OS and installed on Windows OS
      
       Windows 10 built-in software: Notepad, Control Panel, Resource Manager, and Settings

       Software installed on Windows OS: PuTTY, Notepad++, WinRAR, Visual Studio 2017, Kingdee Cloud, PowerBuilder, and others

      

     Java applications: Application software developed using Java

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, click .

     In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project name to go to the project design page.

     Choose UI Recorder > Creating and Recording Subscript.

     In the displayed dialog box, configure the script.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

           Script name. The value can only Chinese characters, letters, digits, and underscores (_). The value must start with a letter or Chinese character.

         

         
          
           Developers

           Description of a script

           Script template

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Create.

         Move the cursor to the target file, select the file, and move the cursor to the button displayed on .

         In the displayed drop-down list, select Double-click.

        

       

      

      

     (Optional) Create variables required by the subscript and reference the variables in the control.

       In the displayed dialog box, configure the variable information.
        

        
         
          
           Table 2 Parameter description

       Click OK.

     After the recording is complete, click .

       If there are redundant operations, for example, dragging the mouse back and forth or clicking an incorrect operation, click  corresponding to the operation to delete it.

       If the recording does not meet scenario requirements, click  to continue recording or  to record again.

      

      

     After the check is complete, click  to save the recorded subscript and exit the recorder window.

     Go back to the Design page of the project and check whether the recorded steps exist on the canvas of the subscript.

text:
Clearing the Canvas and Recording a Robotic Script
 
 
  
  

  
   You can clear the current canvas and record robotic scripts to automatically perform operations on specified web application pages or local applications.

   
    Prerequisites

    A project has been created.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, click .

     In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project name to go to the project design page.

     Choose UI Recorder > Clear and record.

     Record a web application script.
      

      
       In the displayed window, click .

       Select the corresponding browser, enter the URL of the web application, and press Enter.
        Studio automatically opens the entered web application URL and accesses the web application page to be recorded.

        

       In the recorder window, click .

       Perform operations on the web application page based on site requirements. In this case, Studio automatically records the operations on the web application page and converts them into an executable script.

       Click Main or  on the right of other subscripts to create required variables and reference them in the control.

      

      

     Record a local application script.
      

      
       In the displayed window, click .

       Start a local application and perform operations based on site requirements. In this case, Studio automatically records the operations on the local application page and converts them into an executable script.

       Click Main or  on the right of other subscripts to create required variables and reference them in the control.

      

      

     After the recording is complete, click .

     In the recorder window, check whether the operations in the recording list are redundant and meet scenario requirements.
      

      
       If there are redundant operations, for example, dragging the mouse back and forth or clicking an incorrect operation, click  corresponding to the operation to delete it.

       If the recording does not meet scenario requirements, click  to continue recording or  to record again.

      

      

     After the check is complete, click  to save the recorded script and exit the recorder window.

     Go back to the Design page of the project and check whether the recorded steps exist on the canvas of the current tab page.
      

      
       If yes, the recording is successful.

       If no, contact Huawei technical support.

name: Orchestrating an RPA Business Process
title: Orchestrating an RPA Business Process
text:
Orchestrating an RPA Business Process
 
 
  
  

  
   After the robotic script is recorded, orchestrate an RPA business process to realize business automation.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     A project has been created.

     The robotic functional block or script has been recorded.

    

   

   
    Context

    RPA business processes are classified into the following two types:

    
     Sequential execution (simple): Recorded robotic scripts are executed one by one in sequence. For example, you can execute the robotic script A, B, and C one after another.

     Logic execution (complex): Logic judgment statements or loop operations are added during robotic script execution. For example, you can execute the robotic script A for X times under condition A, and the robotic script B once under condition B.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, click .

     In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project name to go to the project design page.

     (Optional) Add controls irrelevant to the RPA business process based on site requirements.
      

      
       On the Controller tab page, select one of the following methods to find the required control:
        
         Method 1: Click  and enter the control name in the text box to search for the control. In this case, search-related controls are highlighted in the control list.

         Method 2: In the control list, click the plus sign (+) in front of a control category to locate the required control.

        

       Drag the located control to the canvas and set parameters of the control. After that, you can click  to edit the control or click  to pick up web or local app elements.

       Repeat 4.a and 4.b to add other controls irrelevant to the process.

      

      

     (Optional) Add controls relevant to the RPA business process based on site requirements.
      

      
       Click the Controller tab, and click the plus sign (+) before Workflow in the control list.
        

       Drag controls of the corresponding type to the canvas based on site requirements. For example, you can drag the If control under Workflow to the canvas.
        

        

       Set control parameters by referring to Parameter and Variable Description or click  to edit the control. For example, you can enter a conditional expression in the text box of the If control.
        

        

       (Optional) Repeat 5.b and 5.c to add other process-related controls.

      

      

     On the canvas, create a connection for each robotic script and control.
      

      
       Create a connection between the Start node and the Block module or control. That is, pull a line from the Start node and connect it to the Block module or control.

       Pull the connection line to connect other Block modules or controls in sequence.
        

        
         
         
           
          
           When you connect the Flow Control control to the Block module or other controls, Studio displays process-related options for you to set and select. For example, when you create a line between the If and openurl controls, set Select a value for the branch connection to The condition is met, The condition is not met, or Exit If condition.

          

         

        

       (Optional) Perform the following operations to add controls if necessary:
        
         Move the cursor to any robotic script or control, and click the target blue arrow (for example, ).

         In the displayed search box, enter a control name.

         In the search result, click the required control to add it to the canvas.

         Set control parameters or click  to edit the control.

        

      

      

     (Optional) Add the Python third-party components relevant to RPA business processes based on site requirements.
      

      
        
       
        If the Python third-party components on which the project depends are not included in the installed modules, perform the following steps to install the required Python third-party components:

       

      

      
       Choose Advance > Project Configuration > Python Module Management.

       Click the New Modules tab and configure information about the dependent Python third-party components.
        

        

        
         
          
           Table 1 Parameter description
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Name

            
             Name of the dependent Python third-party component

           

           
            
             Version

            
             Version of the dependent Python third-party component

           

           
            
             Image Address

            
             Image address of the dependent Python third-party component

           

           
            
             Outputs

            
             Output information generated when the dependent Python third-party component is installed

           

          
         
        

       Click Install.
        After the installation is complete, click the Installed Modules tab to check whether the required Python third-party component exists. If yes, the installation is successful. Otherwise, locate, analyze, and rectify the fault based on the output information.

        

        

       (Optional) Repeat 7.b and 7.c to install all the other dependent Python third-party components and click Close to return to the Design page.

      

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After the RPA business process is orchestrated, perform the following operations:

    
     
      
       Table 2 Operations after the RPA business process is orchestrated
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation

        
         Description

        
         Procedure

       

      
      
       
        
         Creating an element group in the element library

        
         You can create an element group in the element library to manage elements by category.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, select Element Library under the canvas.

          Click  on the right.

          In the displayed dialog box, enter an element group name.

          Click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Creating an element in the element library

        
         You can create elements in the element library for the pick-up controls of all projects to reference.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, select Element Library under the canvas.

          Click  on the right to pick up the corresponding element.

          After the element is picked up, change the element name in the Create Element dialog box based on site requirements.

          (Optional) Click the Element Value tab and modify element values based on site requirements.

          (Optional) Click Check Element to check whether the picked-up element is correct.
           After the element is verified, the system automatically highlights the element and blinks it three times for users to identify it.

          (Optional) If the new element is a web-related UI element, click Repair Element and pick up similar elements on different pages to perform fuzzy match on similar information in url and title of the two elements. Then, elements in the element library can be matched and obtained by various similar elements.
           
             NOTICE: 
            
             If two elements are similar, the following conditions must be met:

             
              The two elements cannot be the same.

              The two elements have the same locating mode. That is, the URLs of the two elements or the titles of the browser tabs contain similar content.

             

            

           

          Click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Creating an element in a specified element group in the element library

        
         You can create an element in a specified element group in the element library for pickup controls of all projects.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, select Element Library under the canvas.

          Right-click the element group and select Pickup Element.

          After the element is picked up, change the element name in the Create Element dialog box based on site requirements.

          (Optional) Click the Element Value tab and modify element values based on site requirements.

          (Optional) Click Check Element to check whether the selected element is correct.
           After the element is verified, the system automatically highlights the element and blinks it three times for users to identify it.

          (Optional) If the new element is a web-related UI element, click Repair Element and pick up similar elements on different pages to perform fuzzy match on similar information in url and title of the two elements. Then, elements in the element library can be matched and obtained by various similar elements.
           
             NOTICE: 
            
             If two elements are similar, the following conditions must be met:

             
              The two elements cannot be the same.

              The two elements have the same locating mode. That is, the URLs of the two elements or the titles of the browser tabs contain similar content.

             

            

           

          Click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Modifying an element in the element library

        
         You can modify element information in the element library based on site requirements.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, select Element Library under the canvas.

          Enter an element name in the search box.

          In the search result, right-click the element and choose Edit Element from the shortcut menu.

          In the Edit Element dialog box, change the element name or click Re-pick Element to retrieve the element again.

          Click the Element Preview tab to view the elements that have been picked up.

          (Optional) Click the Tree Table tab and add or delete properties, or change property values based on site requirements.
           
            To add a property, click a property of the same level as the property to be added in the property list, click Add, enter the property name, description, and value, and click OK.

            To delete a property, deselect the property to be deleted in the property list and click OK. To delete all properties, deselect all properties and click OK.

            To modify a property value, modify the value in the Attribute Value column of the property and click OK.

           

          (Optional) Click the Element Value tab and modify element values based on site requirements.

          Click Check Element to check whether the element that is picked up or modified is correct.
           After the element is verified, the system automatically highlights the element and blinks it three times for users to identify it.

          (Optional) If the edited element is a web-related UI element, click Repair Element and pick up similar elements on different pages to perform fuzzy match on similar information in url and title of the two elements. Then, elements in the element library can be matched and obtained by various similar elements.
           
             NOTICE: 
            
             If two elements are similar, the following conditions must be met:

             
              The two elements cannot be the same.

              The two elements have the same locating mode. That is, the URLs of the two elements or the titles of the browser tabs contain similar content.

             

            

           

          Click OK.

          In the displayed dialog box, determine whether to synchronize the elements that have been referenced in the project based on site requirements.
           
            Yes: Synchronize the elements that have been referenced in the project.

            No: Referenced elements in the project are not synchronized. Referenced elements in the project are unbound from elements in the element library. After an element is modified in the element library, the modification cannot be synchronized to the referenced elements in the project even if you click Yes.

           

         

       

       
        
         Moving an Element in the Element Library

        
         You can move elements to a specified element group in the element library based on site requirements.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, select Element Library under the canvas.

          Enter an element name in the search box.

          In the search result, right-click the element and choose Move Element Group from the shortcut menu.

          In the displayed dialog box, select the specified element group name.

          Click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Copying an element value in the element library

        
         You can copy the required element value in the element library based on site requirements.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, select Element Library under the canvas.

          Enter an element name in the search box.

          In the search result, right-click the element and select Copy Element Value from the shortcut menu.
           After the control is copied successfully, you can paste it to the Text area of the control or paste it to the text editor.

         

       

       
        
         Searching for element references in the element library

        
         You can search for the reference relationship of a specified element in the current project based on site requirements.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, select Element Library under the canvas.

          Enter an element name in the search box.

          In the search result, right-click the element and select Search Referenced Element from the shortcut menu.
           
            If the search result does not exist, the element is not referenced.

            If the search result exists, the element is referenced by the corresponding control. In this case, you can double-click the control in the search result to locate to the control.

           

          (Optional) If the reference relationship of the element changes, click Refresh on the right to obtain the latest reference relationship of the element.

         

       

       
        
         Deleting an element from the element library

        
         You can delete unnecessary elements from the element library based on site requirements.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, select Element Library under the canvas.

          Enter an element name in the search box.

          In the search result, right-click the element and click Delete.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Saving picked elements to the element library

        
         Users can save the elements picked up by controls in the RPA business process to the element library, for example, mouse clicking control.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, click  next to  in the control and select Save to Element Library.

          In the displayed dialog box, enter an element name.

          (Optional) Click Check Element to check whether the saved element is correct.
           After the element is verified, the system automatically highlights the element and blinks it three times for users to identify it.

          (Optional) If the saved element is a web-related UI element, click Repair Element and pick up similar elements on different pages to perform fuzzy match on similar information in url and title of the two elements. Then, elements in the element library can be matched and obtained by various similar elements.
           
             NOTICE: 
            
             If two elements are similar, the following conditions must be met:

             
              The two elements cannot be the same.

              The two elements have the same locating mode. That is, the URLs of the two elements or the titles of the browser tabs contain similar content.

             

            

           

          Click OK.
           
            After the element is saved, the value of the element changes to blue or red underline, indicating that the element is bound to the element saved in the element library.
            
              NOTICE: 
             
              If you click  next to  in the control and select Edit Element or directly edit the element text box after saving the element to the element library, the element reference becomes invalid. After that, the element value is displayed in black.

             

            

           

         

       

       
        
         Referencing an element in the element library

        
         You can reference existing elements in the element library when you use pickup controls.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, click  next to  in the control and select Reference Element.

          In the Reference Element dialog box, select the element to be referenced.

          Click OK.
           After the reference is successful, the value of the element changes to blue or red underline.

           
             NOTICE: 
            
             After an element is referenced, if you click  next to  in the control and select Edit Element or directly edit the element text box, the element reference becomes invalid. After that, the element value is displayed in black.

            

           

         

       

       
        
         Viewing elements in the element library of a control

        
         You can view the referenced element in the element library when using the pickup control.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, click  next to  in the control and select View Element.

          In the lower part of the canvas, double-click the highlighted result to view the element information referenced by the control.

         

       

       
        
         Unbinding an element in the element library from a control

        
         You can unbind the referenced element in the element library when using the pickup control.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, click  next to  in the control and select Unbind Element.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.
           After the unbinding is successful, the element value is displayed in black.

         

       

       
        
         Editing elements in a control

        
         You can edit elements when using a pick class control.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, click  next to  in the control and select Edit Element.

          (Optional) Click Validate Element to check whether the elements in the control are correct.
           After the element is verified, the system automatically highlights the element and blinks it three times for users to identify it.

          (Optional) Click the Tree Table tab and add or delete properties, or change property values based on site requirements.
           
            To add a property, click a property of the same level as the property to be added in the property list, click Add, enter the property name, description, and value, and click OK.

            To delete a property, deselect the property to be deleted in the property list and click OK. To delete all properties, deselect all properties and click OK.

            To modify a property value, modify the value in the Attribute Value column of the property and click OK.

           

          (Optional) Click the Source Code tab and modify the code related to the element based on site requirements.

          (Optional) If the edited element is a web-related UI element, click Repair Element and pick up similar elements on different pages to perform fuzzy match on similar information in url and title of the two elements, finally, elements in the element library can be matched and obtained by various similar elements.
           
             NOTICE: 
            
             If two elements are similar, the following conditions must be met:

             
              The two elements cannot be the same.

              The two elements have the same locating mode. That is, the URLs of the two elements or the titles of the browser tabs contain similar content.

             

            

           

          (Optional) If the edited element is a web-related UI element, click Parameterize and pick up similar elements on the same page. In the displayed dialog box, view or edit the variable names of the elements that can be extracted, and click OK.
           
             NOTE: 
            
             In the Element Parameterize dialog box, if Create As New Variable is set to Yes, Studio automatically creates the corresponding variable. In this case, if the control is in the main script, the created variable is a global variable. Otherwise, the variable is automatically created. If Create As New Variable is set to No, ensure that Variable Name is an existing variable. Otherwise, an error will be reported.

            

           

          Click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Picking up web page data

        
         You can pick up a single column of data or a table on the web page based on site requirements.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, choose Data Extract > Web Data Extraction.

          In the Web Data Extract Guide dialog box, locate the Pick First Element step, click  on the right of First Element to pick up the corresponding web page element, and click Next Step.

          Locate the Pick Similar Element step, click  on the right of Similar Data to pick up other similar web page elements, and click Next Step.

          Locate the Rule Setting step, and configure the information about the data extraction rule, such as Data Range, Content, and Numbers of Page. Then, click Next Step.

          Locate the Results Preview step, check whether the extracted web page element meets the requirements. If no, repeat the preceding steps to extract the data again. If yes, click Finish.
           After the web page element is successfully extracted, a web page element pickup control is automatically generated on the canvas.

         

       

       
        
         Picking up web page data (advanced)

        
         You can pick up multiple columns of data or a table on the web page based on site requirements.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, choose Data Extract > Web Data Extraction(advanced).

          In the Data Select step of the Web Data Extract Guide window, click  on the right of First Data and Similar Data corresponding to Data Name to pick up the corresponding web page data element and other similar web page data elements.

          (Optional) To pick up data in multiple columns, click Add data, and click  on the right of First Data and Similar Data to pick up the corresponding web page data elements and other similar web page data elements.

          Click Next.

          In the rule setting step, configure the rule information about data extraction, such as Data Range, Numbers of Page, and Save data to local xlsx file. Then, click Next Step.

          Locate the Results Preview step, check whether the extracted web page element meets the requirements. If no, repeat the preceding steps to extract the data again. If yes, click Finish.
           After the web page data is successfully extracted, the advancedExtractWebData control is automatically generated on the canvas.

         

       

       
        
         Managing Python dependency packages

        
         You can manage the installed Python third-party components as required, including upgrading, uploading, and deleting the components.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, click Advance > python dependency package management.

          Click the Manage installed modules tab and select the desired Python dependency package.

          Click Delete to delete an unnecessary Python dependency package.

          Click Upgrade to upgrade the Python dependency package to the latest version.

          (Optional) After Studio is successfully connected to the RPA Orchestrator of 23.2 or later, click Publish to release the Python dependency package to the RPA Orchestrator and display it on the Python Third-Party Management page.

         

       

       
        
         Viewing the overall reference relationship of a script

        
         You can view the overall script reference relationship during RPA business process orchestration to quickly understand the calling logic between scripts, improving the O&M efficiency of the RPA business process.

        
         
          In the Project area of the Design tab page, right-click Main under the project name and choose View Overall References from the shortcut menu.

          In the displayed window, view the detailed reference relationships between the main script and subscripts.

         

       

       
        
         Searching for the reference relationship of a subscript

        
         You can search for the reference relationship of a subscript during RPA business process orchestration to obtain the script that calls the subscript and the corresponding calling information.

        
         
          In the Project area of the Design tab page, right-click the subscript name under the project name and choose Find References from the shortcut menu.

          On the Script Reference Relationships tab page in the lower part of the canvas, view the name of the script that calls the subscript and the information about the called control.

         

       

       
        
         Managing elements in the UI analyzer

        
         You can view the control tree, properties, and tree table of picked elements in the UI analyzer. If the picked elements do not meet the requirements, you can pick up and verify the elements again.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, click  next to  in the control and select Open in UI Analyzer from the drop-down list.

          On the UI analyzer page, view information such as the control tree and properties of picked elements in the control.
           When you click another control node in the control tree, the information in the Properties area and Tree Table and Source Code tab pages in the UI analyzer is refreshed accordingly.

          (Optional) To modify the properties of a picked element, click the Tree Table or Source Code tab and add, delete, or modify properties based on site requirements.

          (Optional) To highlight the area where picked elements are displayed, toggle on the Highlight switch.

          (Optional) To check whether a picked element is correct, click Check Element in the upper left corner to view the position of the element.
           After the element is verified, the system automatically highlights the element and blinks it three times for users to identify it.

          (Optional) To pick up an element again, click Pickup Element in the upper left corner.

          Click OK. The element information in the UI analyzer is synchronized to the control parameters of the script.

         

       

       
        
         Picking up an anchor

        
         When using a pickup control, you can obtain the position of the target element in anchor pickup mode to avoid control unavailability caused by element property changes.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, click  next to  in the control and select Pick Up Anchors.

          In the Select Anchor Element step of the Anchor Pickup Wizard dialog box, click  on the right of Anchor Element to pick up the anchor element of the target element and click Next.

          In the Select Target Element step, click  on the right of Target Element to pick up the required target element and click Finish.

name: Saving an RPA Business Process
title: Saving an RPA Business Process
text:
Saving an RPA Business Process
 
 
  
  

  
   After you orchestrate an RPA business process, save the process to prevent data loss.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     A project has been created.

     The RPA business process has been orchestrated.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, click .

name: Checking an RPA Business Process
title: Checking an RPA Business Process
text:
Checking an RPA Business Process
 
 
  
  

  
   After the orchestrated RPA business process is saved, perform health check on the business process.

   
    Prerequisites

    The RPA business process has been saved.

   

   
    Context

    Studio supports the following two check modes:

    
     Check Item: Health check is performed on all scripts in the project. The check items include the design of the main script architecture, scripts that are not referenced in the project, global variable naming specifications, local parameter naming specifications, and local variable naming specifications.

     Check Script: Health check is performed on the current script. The check items include the number of functional controls, maximum nesting depth, local parameter naming specifications, local variable naming specifications, number of local parameters, and number of diagram elements in a branch.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, click .

     In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project name to go to the project design page.

     Perform a health check on the project.
      

      
       Use either of the following methods to check the health status of the project:
        
         On the Project tab page, right-click Main under the project name, and choose Health Check > Check Item from the shortcut menu.

         Choose Advance > Health Check > Check Item.

        

       On the Health Check tab page, view the check result.
        

        

       (Optional) Click Check Criteria to view the check items and check rules of the health check. To export the check criteria, click Export to save the file to the local PC.
        

        

       (Optional) Click Export to export the check result to the local PC.

       Modify the scripts, parameters, and variables in the project based on handling suggestions in the check result.

       After the modification is complete, click Recheck to verify that the modification is correct.

      

      

     Perform a health check on the script.
      

      
       Use either of the following methods to check the health status of a specified script:
        
         On the Project tab page, right-click Main or another subscript under the project name, and choose Health Check > Check Script from the shortcut menu.

         Open the script to be checked, and choose Advance > Health Check > Check Script.

        

       On the Health Check tab page, view the check result.

       (Optional) Click Check Criteria to view the check items and check rules of the health check. To export the check criteria, click Export to save the file to the local PC.

       (Optional) Click Export to export the check result to the local PC.

       Modify the scripts, parameters, and variables in the project based on handling suggestions in the check result.

       After the modification is complete, click Recheck to verify that the modification is correct.

name: Debugging an RPA Business Process
title: Debugging an RPA Business Process
text:
Debugging an RPA Business Process
 
 
  
  

  
   After the RPA business process is checked, debug it to verify that each step in the process is available.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     A project has been created.

     The RPA business process has been orchestrated.

    

   

   
    Context

    When you debug the RPA business process, set process breakpoints as required. Studio executes each node in the process one by one until the breakpoint is reached and returns the execution result of each node. After that, you can locate and analyze faults based on the execution result of each node before the breakpoint. Studio supports the following two debugging methods:

    
     Debug the current script: You can debug the script corresponding to the currently opened tab page.

     Debug the main script: You can debug the script on the Main tab page.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, click .

     In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project name to go to the project design page.

     Choose Debug > Debug the current script (Ctrl+F9) or Debug > Debug the main script (Ctrl+Shift+F9).
      

      Studio automatically executes the entire RPA business process. You can view the execution logs on the Log tab page in the lower part of the canvas.

      

     If an error occurs during execution, perform the following operations to locate the fault and analyze it:
      

      
       On the canvas, right-click any node of the RPA business process and choose Set a Breakpoint from the shortcut menu.

       (Optional) Repeat the previous step to set multiple breakpoints as required.

       Click Restart.

       Locate the fault and rectify it based on the following information:
        
         On the left, view the execution result of the control before the breakpoint and the breakpoint position.

         On the Log tab page, view the execution logs before the breakpoint, and locate the fault and rectify it.

        

       After the fault is located and rectified, click Next or Next Breakpoint to continue the fault locating and analysis.

       After all faults are rectified, right-click any breakpoint and choose Remove All Breakpoints from the shortcut menu. Then, click Restart to verify that all modifications are correct.

       Repeat the preceding steps until the RPA business process is successfully debugged.

      

      

     After the debugging is successful, click Exit.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After the RPA business process is debugged, you can perform the operations listed in the following table.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Operations after the RPA business process is debugged
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation

        
         Description

        
         Procedure

       

      
      
       
        
         Viewing breakpoints

        
         You can view breakpoint information in the breakpoint list based on site requirements.

        
         
          On the Design tab page, click the Breakpoint Management tab in the lower part of the canvas.

          In the breakpoint list, view the script path and control name of the breakpoint.

          In the breakpoint list, double-click the control name of the breakpoint to go to the breakpoint location in the canvas.

         

       

       
        
         Deleting breakpoints

        
         You can delete unnecessary breakpoints from the breakpoint list based on site requirements.

         
           NOTICE: 
          
           A maximum of 1000 breakpoints can be set. If the number of breakpoints exceeds 1000, delete unnecessary breakpoints based on site requirements and set new ones.

          

         

        
         
          On the Design tab page, click the Breakpoint Management tab in the lower part of the canvas.

          In the breakpoint list, select one or more breakpoints to be deleted and click  in the upper right corner to delete unnecessary breakpoints.

name: Running an RPA Business Process
title: Running an RPA Business Process
text:
Running an RPA Business Process
 
 
  
  

  
   After the RPA business process is debugged, run the entire process to check whether it is correct.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     A project has been created.

     The RPA business process has been orchestrated.

    

   

   
    Context

    When you run the RPA business process, Studio automatically executes the RPA business process and demonstrates the orchestration steps on the local PC. Studio supports the following running modes:

    
     Run the current script: You can run the script corresponding to the currently opened tab page.

     Run the main script: You can run the script on the Main tab page.

     Run the script in PIP: Studio opens an independent Picture in Picture (PiP) window for the RPA business process, ensuring that user operations on the desktop are not affected. The PiP window uses the sub-session environment provided by Windows, and the sub-session environment shares the resources of the main session (current desktop). Therefore, no additional OS resources are occupied. However, running in the PiP window also has the following restrictions:
      
       This running mode applies only to Windows Studio. The supported Windows versions include Windows 8 or later (non-home version) and Windows Server 2016 or later (non-home version).

       You are advised to run the current script or main script to verify that the RPA business process is correct, and then run the RPA business process.

       Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Office apps cannot be started in the PiP window and on the desktop at the same time. If the RPA business processes related to these apps run in the PiP window, you need to close these apps on the desktop. Otherwise, the RPA business process fails to be executed in the PiP window.

      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, click .

     In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project name to go to the project design page.

     Choose Run > Run the current script (Ctrl+F10) or Run the main script (Ctrl+Shift+F10).

     After the execution is complete, view the log information about the process. If the execution is successful, the developed process is successfully verified. If the execution fails, locate, analyze, and rectify the fault based on the log information, and then run the script again until the execution is successful.
      

      

      

      In the upper right corner of the Log tab page, the following icons are used as follows:

      
       : Open the directory where the execution log file is located.

       : Clear execution logs.

        or : Display execution logs in a single line or in different lines.

       : View historical execution logs.

       : Close the pane where the log is located.

      

      

     (Optional) Run the RPA business process in the PiP window.
      

      
       (Optional) If the RPA business processes of Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Office are running, close these apps on the current desktop to prevent RPA business process execution failure in the PiP window.

       Choose Run > Run the script in PIP.

       The WeAutomate Virtual Desktop and Windows Security Center windows are displayed. In the Windows Security Center window, enter the password of the current login user and click OK.
        

       (Optional) After the login is successful, the sub-session desktop is displayed in the PiP window, and the RPA business process is automatically executed. If you want to perform operations on the sub-session desktop during the execution of RPA business processes, deselect Disable control in the upper right corner of the PiP window, and then perform operations on the sub-session desktop.
        

       (Optional) After the RPA business process is executed, the system automatically exits the PiP window and deregisters the sub-session. To interrupt the RPA business process in the PiP window, click X in the upper right corner of the PiP window or click Stop in Studio.
        
          
         
          During the execution of RPA business processes in the PiP window, if you use Task Manager to forcibly close the PiP window, the sub-session is not deregistered. As a result, the PC cannot be restarted or shut down. In this case, you need to execute the process in the PiP window again and click Stop in Studio.

         

        

       After the RPA business process is executed or the PiP window exits, you can view the execution result of the process on the Log tab page of Studio.

      

      

     Analyze the performance of successfully-executed RPA business processes to optimize these processes and improve their running efficiency.
      

      
       View performance information about RPA business processes during running.
        

        
         
         
          Overview: collects statistics on the total number of control execution times, total execution duration, and average control execution duration of the RPA business processes.

          Top 10 Controls with the Longest Average Usage Duration: collects statistics on the top 10 controls with the longest average usage duration during RPA business process running and the duration of each control.

          Control Details: collects statistics on the number of execution times, maximum execution duration, and minimum execution duration of each control in the RPA business process.

         

        

       Click Export to save the performance analysis result of the RPA business process to the local PC.

       Optimize the controls that have a long execution duration and large number of execution times in the RPA business process, and analyze the performance again to gradually improve the process running efficiency.

name: Releasing an RPA Business Process
title: Releasing an RPA Business Process
text:
Releasing an RPA Business Process
 
 
  
  

  
   After the RPA business process is debugged and running properly, release it to RPA Orchestrator, GDE Store, or a local disk.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     To release a project to RPA Orchestrator, Studio has been successfully switched to online and connected to RPA Orchestrator.

     To release a project to GDE Store, Studio must be successfully switched to Online and connected to ADC in develop state.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Start Studio.

     In the navigation pane, click .

     In the Recently Edited Items area, click the project name to go to the project design page.

     Click Publish.
      

      
       Before the release, Studio controls whether to start the health check based on the setting of Automatically Trigger Health Check Before Release on the Settings > General page.
       
        If Automatically Trigger Health Check Before Release is set to Yes, Studio automatically starts the health check. In this case, you need to perform the following operations based on the health check result:
         
          If the health check is passed, go to 5.

          If the health check fails, click View Results to rectify the check items that do not meet the requirements and then release the check items again. Alternatively, click Continue Publishing to ignore the check items that do not meet the requirements and go to 5.

         

        If Automatically Trigger Health Check Before Release is set to No, Studio does not start the health check. In this case, go to 5.

       

      

      

     In the displayed Publish dialog box, click the General tab and set the release-related information.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Project name

          
           Name of the project to be released, which cannot be changed

         

         
          
           Version

          
           Version of the project to be released

           The format is YY.XX.XX. The value of YY ranges from 1 to 99 while the value of XX range from 0 to 99, for example, 1.1.22.

         

         
          
           Publish To

          
           Destination of the released process

           
            Local Disk: The developed RPA business process is released to the local disk for future use.

            Management Center: The developed RPA business process is released to RPA Orchestrator. You can deliver scripts to robots.

            GDE Store: The developed RPA business process is released to GDE Store from ADC in develop state.

           

         

         
          
           Local Path

          
           Local disk to which the process is released

           Click  to select a path.

           This parameter is displayed only when Publish To is set to Local Disk.

         

         
          
           Script Type

          
           Type of the script to be released, that is, the running mode of a robot

           
            Interactive

            Backstage

           

         

         
          
           Obfuscate Project

          
           Whether to obfuscate the project

           
            Yes: Project is obfuscated. After that, the project cannot be orchestrated again in Studio.

            No: Project is not obfuscated.

           

         

         
          
           Generate Dependency Package List

          
           Whether to generate a dependency package list

           
            Yes: When a project is released, the dependent Python third-party component is not carried, and only the list of dependent Python third-party components is generated for the executor to automatically download and use.

            No: When a project is release, the dependent Python third-party component is carried.

           

           This parameter is displayed only when the project depends on the Python third-party component.

         

         
          
           Project Dependency Package

          
           List of the Python third-party components on which the project depends. Select a component based on site requirements.

           This parameter is displayed only when the project depends on the Python third-party component.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Description of the process to be released

         

        
       
      

      

     (Optional) If the project has used customized plugins (that is, a blue dot is displayed in the upper right corner of the Custom Plugin tab page), click the Custom Plugin tab on the Publish page and set Runtime Version for the customized plugins in the project.
      

      

      

      The options of Runtime Version are as follows:

      
       Latest version: After the project is released, the executor automatically obtains the customized plugin of the latest version from the Plugin Management page in RPA Orchestrator when running the release script.

       Specified version: After the project is released, the executor automatically obtains the customized plugin of the specified version from the Plugin Management page in RPA Orchestrator when running the release script.

      

      

     Click Publish.
      

      
       After the business process is successfully released to RPA Orchestrator, a message is displayed in the upper right corner of Studio, indicating that the XX(xx.xx.xx) is successfully released to RPA Orchestrator.

       After the business process is successfully released to the local disk, a message is displayed in the upper right corner of Studio, indicating that XX(xx.xx.xx) is successfully released to the local disk.

      

      

     (Optional) To release the RPA business process to GDE Store, perform the following operations after clicking Publish.
      

      
       On the displayed page, log in to ADC in develop state and go to the Publish to GDE Store page.

       Enter asset putaway information. For details, see GDE Orchestration > CI/CD Tool Chain > Asset Putaway > Putaway Page in GDE x.x.x Product Documentation.

       Click Confirm to complete the asset putaway application.
        In this case, the message "The release application is successful and can be viewed on the Asset Library page in the develop-state environment." is displayed in the upper right corner of Studio. After the GDE Store administrator approves the application, you can view or download the asset in GDE Store.

      

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After you create a project, perform the following operations:

    
     
      
       Table 2 Operations after a project is created
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation

        
         Description

        
         Procedure

       

      
      
       
        
         Viewing the release record

        
         You can view the release records of a project.

        
         
          On the process design page, click  next to Publish.

          Select Publish Record from the drop-down list.

          In the displayed dialog box, enter a project name in the search box.

          In the search result, view the release type, status, and release time of the project.

          (Optional) To delete a release record, click  in the Operation column.

text:
Manually Developing a Customized Plugin

    Preparing for the Development
      Before you develop a customized plugin, download the required plugin template file and set the corresponding Python development environment.

name: Preparing for the Development

Preparing for the Development

name: Developing and Packaging Customized Plugins
title: Developing and Packaging Customized Plugins
text:
Developing and Packaging Customized Plugins
 
 
  
  

  
   When you develop customized plugin, develop files such as help.json, register.json, and action_ext.py based on site requirements. After the development is complete, package the customized plugin project file.

   
    Context

    During customized plugin development, pay attention to the following associated modifications:

    
     When you modify or add a command, modify the following information:
      
       Method name in the action_ext.py file

       Commands in the ExtDemon list of the register.json file

       Commands in the commands list in the help.json file

      

     When you change the name or version number of a customized plugin package, modify the following content:
      
       Name of the folder in the level-1 directory where the customized plugin project file is located
        The folder name is in the ext_ Plugin package name _ Version format. The value of Version must be in the format of XX_XX_XX.

       name and version in the actionx.rapx file

      

     When you modify the class name, modify the following information:
      
       Name of the class on which the command in the action_ext.py file depends

       Class name in the register.json file

      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Develop the customized plugin file action_ext.py to implement the corresponding function.
      

      
       In PyCharm, open the action_ext.py file for implementing the customized plugin function.

       Develop customized plugin functions based on site requirements and save the settings.
        During development, keep the following rules:

        
         The entry method must start with action_.

         During RPA built-in module import, only the com.huawei.antrobot.actions.base module can be imported.

         The instance properties provided by BaseAction can be inherited.

         The command entry receives defined parameter names. (By default, a parameter value of the character string type is obtained.) (For example, if the add command has the mandatory parameter target and default parameter value, the entry method uses the formal parameter to obtain the action_add(self, target, value="1" parameter.)

         If the Python interpreter provided by Studio has been configured, use the UT to debug and verify specific functions. The Context and ActionOutParam classes are required for input and output parameters. After instantiation, values are assigned to action.context and action.out_param.

         The following table lists the supported properties. 
          
           
            
             Table 1 Property list
            
            
             
             
             
            
            
             
              
               Property

              
               Type

              
               Description

             

            
            
             
              
               self.logger

              
               obj

              
               logger object used to record logs. The log levels include info, error, warning, and debug.

             

             
              
               self.console_logger

              
               obj

              
               console_logger object used to print logs to the console in real time. The log levels include info, error, warning, and debug.

             

             
              
               self.ret_value

              
               obj

              
               Returned value of a specified action property

             

             
              
               self.reference

              
               obj

              
               Name of the return object that references the previous action, which is used together with self.context.get_reference

             

             
              
               self.command

              
               str

              
               Command name, which must be defined based on the Python method name

             

             
              
               self.params

              
               dict

              
               Used to obtain the corresponding parameter value in the XML file

               For example, self.params.get("target", "").

               By default, the obtained parameters are of the string type. This parameter is not required when the formal parameter receiving function is used at the entry.

             

             
              
               self.out_param

              
               obj

              
               The out_param object has the following properties:

               
                out_param_name: corresponds to the return value of the action property.

                out_param_type: corresponds to the value of return_type.

                out_param_value: The ret_value value is assigned to this property through the save method based on return_type.)

               

             

             
              
               self.context

              
               obj

              
               
                Value of the project directory @{WORK_DIR} obtained using the get_project_path() method

                Object returned by the action obtained using the get_reference(self.reference) method

               

             

            
           
          

        

      

      

     (Optional) If the Python third-party component is required for customized plugin but is not in the built-in Python of Studio, develop the requirements.txt file for the customized plugin.
      

      
       Open the help file requirements.txt in PyCharm.

       Enter the name and version of the dependent third-party component in the file based on site requirements and save the file.
        Format: Third-party component name==Third-party component version

        If there are multiple third-party components, enter them in different lines.

       Go to the %Studio installation directory%\python directory.

       Enter cmd in the address box to access CLI.

       Run the following command to download and install the dependent third-party component:
        python\robot.exe -m pip download -d %project_path%\ext_xxx_1_0_1\lib -r %localappdata%\HuaweiRPA\ext\ext_xxx_1_0_1\requirements.txt

        %project_path% indicates the path of the customized plugin file. ext_xxx_1_0_1 indicates the name of the customized plugin package.

        
          
         
          If the third-party component fails to be downloaded, use the -i parameter in the preceding command to specify the download source.
