text:
What Do I Do When Logs Are Not Properly Displayed When the Executor of Windows Server 2012 Is Used to Execute Tasks?
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Symptom

    When the executor of Windows Server 2012 is used to execute tasks, the logs are improperly displayed.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    In the executor of Windows Server 2012 OS, the system does no have the Chinese character library. When commands and description in XML files related to the project are in Chines, the terminal logs of the executor or Studio cannot generate Chinese characters. As a result, logs are improperly displayed.

   

   
    Solution

    Use English in all XML files related to the project in the executor of Windows Server 2012.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: OS Issues

name: What Do I Do If the Message "Could not find the module" Is Displayed When a Script Is Executed in Windows Server 2008 or Windows Server 2012?
title: What Do I Do If the Message "Could not find the module" Is Displayed When a Script Is Executed in Windows Server 2008 or Windows Server 2012?
text:
What Do I Do If the Message "Could not find the module" Is Displayed When a Script Is Executed in Windows Server 2008 or Windows Server 2012?
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Symptom

    When a script is executed in Windows 2008 or Windows 2012, Citrix displays the message "LL load failed: Could not find the module".

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The OS configuration is incorrect. As a result, the script fails to be executed.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Windows Server 2008:
      
       Choose Control Panel > Programs, and click Turn Windows features on or off.

       Skip the role page and go to the function page.

       In the User Interfaces and Infrastructure area, select Desktop Experience.

       Restart your PC for the settings to take effect.

      

     Windows 2012:
      
       Run Windows PowerShell as an administrator to open the Windows PowerShell CLI.

       Run the following commands:
        Import-Module ServerManager

        Install-WindowsFeature Server-Media-Foundation

       Restart your PC for the settings to take effect.

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: OS Issues

name: What Do I Do If Garbled Characters Are Displayed When a Script Is Executed in Windows Server 2012?
title: What Do I Do If Garbled Characters Are Displayed When a Script Is Executed in Windows Server 2012?
text:
What Do I Do If Garbled Characters Are Displayed When a Script Is Executed in Windows Server 2012?
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Symptom

    When a script is executed in Windows Server 2012, garbled characters are displayed.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    English is used by default in Windows Server 2012. When the project description or path contains Chinese characters, garbled characters are displayed.

   

   
    Solution

title: What Do I Do If the Message "Communication with Studio or Agent failed." Is Displayed When a Script Is Executed in Windows Server 2012?
text:
What Do I Do If the Message "Communication with Studio or Agent failed." Is Displayed When a Script Is Executed in Windows Server 2012?
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Symptom

    When a script is executed in Windows Server 2012, in the Log area in the lower part of the canvas, the message "Communication with Studio or Agent failed." is displayed.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    A proxy server is configured for the browser. As a result, the connection between the browser and Studio or Connector is interrupted.

   

   
    Solution

    The following uses Google Chrome as an example to describes how to modify the browser proxy settings.

    
     Open Google Chrome, click  in the upper right corner, and select Settings.

     In the navigation pane on the left, choose Advanced > System.

     Click  on the right of Open your computer's proxy settings.

     Enter 127.0.0.1 in the text box under Do not use proxy server for addresses beginning with:.

     Click Save.

     Restart Google Chrome for the settings to take effect.

     Run the script again. If the fault persists, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

title: What Do I Do If the Message "Failed to get temporary dir path" Is Displayed When a Script Is Executed In Windows Server 2016 or 2019?
text:
What Do I Do If the Message "Failed to get temporary dir path" Is Displayed When a Script Is Executed In Windows Server 2016 or 2019?
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Symptom

    When operations are performed by Studio of Windows Server 2016 or 2019 on a temporary directory, an exception occurs. In the Log area in the lower part of the canvas, the message "Failed to get temporary dir path" is displayed.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    Do not use temporary folders per session is not enabled.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Open the Run window, and enter gpedit.msc to open Local Group Policy Editor.

     In the navigation pane on the left, choose Local Computer Policy > Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Remote Desktop Services > Remote Desktop Session Host > Temporary folders.

     In the Setting area, right-click Do not use temporary folders per session, and choose Edit.

     In the displayed dialog box, click Enabled.

     Click Apply and then OK.

     Restart your PC for the settings to take effect.

     Run the script again. If the fault persists, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

name: About RPA Studio
title: About RPA Studio
text:
About RPA Studio
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes the background and functions of RPA Studio.

   
    Background

    Robotic Process Automation (RPA) is the software that automates the working process by simulating the interaction between humans and computers. It reduces the repetitive work of engineers and makes engineers focus more on creative work. Complex single-robot tasks bring challenges and higher error probability during recording and playback.

    RPA Studio is a develop-state module of RPA Orchestrator and manages the RPA script and plugin packages. You can release the script and plugin packages to RPA Orchestrator in the runtime-state environment in one-click mode using a project. In this way, you can deliver script packages to the specified executor for unified management.

   

   
    Function Description

    Figure 1 shows the main functional modules of RPA Studio. RPA Studio allows you to manage RPA script and plugin packages and release project-based RPA assets to the runtime-state environment for RPA Orchestrator.

    
     Figure 1 RPA Studio functional modules

name: RPA Script Package Management
title: RPA Script Package Management
text:
RPA Script Package Management
 
 
  
  

  
   An RPA script package is a single robot created by a user to complete a specified job. On the page for managing RPA script packages, you can upload, download, view, and delete a single robot.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment and created RPA-related projects and modules based on site requirements. For details, see Setting Up a Project.

     A script package has been recorded using RPA Studio and released to obtain the ZIP package. For details, see RPA Development Guide.

     If the Application service call 2.0 control is used in the script and Open Level of the service called by the control is set to Module or Project, ensure that the script and the called service belong to the same module or project and the project is deployed to the runtime-state environment. Otherwise, the script fails to call the service.

     (Optional) The script package (if exists) has been imported to the system based on Managing RPA Plugin Packages.

     (Optional) You have downloaded the required script file from GDE Store.

    

   

   
    Context

    
     The system can verify the signature of the GDE Store script package.
     
      When GDE Store Auth Switch on the Products and Services > Administration > GDE Store Configuration page is enabled, the system verifies the signature of the uploaded GDE Store script package. In this case, the script package to be uploaded must contain the script package and the corresponding signature file. Otherwise, the system fails to verify the file integrity. The system fails to verify the package integrity in the following scenarios:
       
        If the script package does not contain the signature file, the script package is successfully uploaded, but the error message "Signature verification not passed: Cannot find the signature file in the GDE Store asset package." is displayed.

        If the signature file in the script package is tampered with, the script package fails to be uploaded and the error message "Signature verification failed: The GDE Store signature file has been tampered with. Upload the original file." is displayed. In this case, store the original signature file into the script package and upload the script package again.

       

      When GDE Store Auth Switch on the Products and Services > Administration > GDE Store Configuration page is disabled, the system does not verify the signature of the uploaded GDE Store script package. In this case, the script package is successfully uploaded regardless of whether the uploaded script package contains the corresponding signature file. However, the message "Signature verification not passed: GDE Store Auth Switch is disabled." is displayed.

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the created RPA project to access the project.

     In the navigation pane, choose RPA Script.

     On the displayed page, click Create.

     In the displayed dialog box, click Choose to upload under Script Package, and select the script package to be uploaded.
      

      
        
       
        Before uploading the script package, you need to know the resource attack risks that may be caused by the package, and then perform related operations.

       

      

      

      

      

     After the package is parsed, enter the description of the package.

     In the Cert Information area, select Accept and trust this Certificate.

     Click Import.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After configuring the script package, you can perform the operations in the following table.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Operations after the script package is configured
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation

        
         Description

        
         Procedure

       

      
      
       
        
         Deleting a script package

        
         You can delete unnecessary script packages.

        
         
          On the script package list page, click Delete in the Operation column of the target script package.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Viewing a script package

        
         You can view the script package details.

        
         
          On the script package list page, click Details in the Operation column of the target script package.

          On the displayed page, view the basic information about the script package, including the package name, upload time, and version number.

         

       

       
        
         Downloading a script package

        
         You can download the uploaded script package to the local PC.

        
         On the script package list page, click Download in the Operation column of the target script package.

       

       
        
         Saving a script package as an asset

        
         You can save a script package as an asset for other projects based on site requirements.

        
         
          On the script package list page, click Save As Asset in the Operation column of the target script package.

          On the displayed page, set Version Type and Business Type based on site requirements.

          Click OK.

name: Managing RPA Plugin Packages
title: Managing RPA Plugin Packages
text:
Managing RPA Plugin Packages
 
 
  
  

  
   The RPA plugin package is a third-party software package required for script execution. This section describes how to upload, download, view, and delete a plugin package.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment and created RPA-related projects and modules based on site requirements. For details, see Setting Up a Project.

     A plugin package has been recorded using RPA Studio and compressed into a ZIP package whose size is less than 200 MB. For details, see RPA Development Guide.

    

   

   
    Context

    After you upload an RPA plugin package, the package is globally valid and can be used by all projects and modules.

    
     The system can verify the signature of the GDE Store plugin package.
     
      When GDE Store Auth Switch on the Products and Services > Administration > GDE Store Configuration page is enabled, the system verifies the signature of the GDE Store plugin package to be uploaded. In this case, the ZIP plugin package to be uploaded must contain a plugin package and the corresponding signature file. Otherwise, the system fails to verify the package integrity. The system fails to verify the package integrity in the following scenarios:
       
        If the ZIP plugin package does not contain the signature file, the ZIP plugin package is successfully uploaded, but the error message "Signature verification not passed: Cannot find the signature file in the GDE Store asset package." is displayed.

        If the signature file in the ZIP plugin package is tampered with, the ZIP plugin package fails to be uploaded and the error message "Signature verification failed: The GDE Store signature file has been tampered with. Upload the original file." is displayed. In this case, place the original signature file into the ZIP plugin package and upload the package again.

       

      When GDE Store Auth Switch on the Products and Services > Administration > GDE Store Configuration page is disabled, the system does not verify the signature of the uploaded ZIP GDE Store plugin package. In this case, the plugin package is successfully uploaded regardless of whether the uploaded ZIP plugin package contains the corresponding signature file. However, the message "Signature verification not passed: GDE Store Auth Switch is disabled." is displayed.

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the created RPA project to access the project.

     In the navigation pane, choose RPA Plugin.

     On the displayed page, click Create.

     In the displayed dialog box, click Choose to upload under Plugin Package, and select the plugin package to be uploaded.
      

      

      

      

     After the package is parsed, select a service type as required.

     In the Cert Information area, select Accept and trust this Certificate and Confirm that the extension package is trustworthy.

     Click Import.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After configuring the plugin package, you can perform the operations in the following table.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Operations after the plugin package is configured
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation

        
         Description

        
         Procedure

       

      
      
       
        
         Viewing a plugin package

        
         You can view the plugin package details.

        
         
          On the plugin package list page, click Details in the Operation column of the target plugin package.

          On the displayed page, view the information about the plugin package name, version, and business type.

         

       

       
        
         Download a plugin package

        
         You can download the uploaded plugin package to the local PC.

        
         On the plugin package list page, click Download in the Operation column of the target plugin package.

       

       
        
         Deleting a plugin package

        
         You can delete unnecessary plugin packages.

        
         
          On the plugin package list page, click Delete in the Operation column of the target plugin package.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

Service Scenario Description
 
 
  
  

  
   Analyze the requirements of a typical service scenario of the hyper-automation process to prepare for the subsequent development.

   
    Scenario Description

    Assume that a manual process for collecting city weather information is required. When a user enters the city name and number of days for which weather information is to be collected on the front-end page, the remote robot automatically captures data from the weather website and writes down the data in an Excel file.

         Process activity

        
         
          Manual task: The user needs to manually enter the city name and number of days for which data is to be collected on the frontend page.

          Robot task: The remote robot needs to automatically capture data from the weather website and writes down the data.

         

       

       
        
         Information to be recorded in process activities

name: Orchestrating the Hyper-Automation Process
title: Orchestrating the Hyper-Automation Process
text:
Orchestrating the Hyper-Automation Process
 
 
  
  

  
   Create a hyper-automation process, and orchestrate and develop process nodes based on the service scenario description.

   
    Procedure

    
     On the project list page, click the created HyperAutoProcess project.

     Create a hyper-automation process.
      

      
       In the navigation pane, choose Business Process.

       On the displayed Business Process tab page, click  in the upper right corner.

       Set the parameters related to the hyper-automation process.
        

        

        The parameters are described as follows:

        
         Process Type: Set this parameter to Non-auto process.

         Business type: Set this parameter to Hyperautomation.

         Process Template: Select Basic Process Template for Quick Start.

         Set other parameters based on site requirements.

        

       Click Submit.

      

      

     Adjust the nodes of the hyper-automation process based on the service scenario requirements.
      

      
       Go to the process canvas page and click Enter Editing Mode.

       Click the Calculating prime node and click  on the toolbar of the canvas to delete unnecessary process nodes.

       Click the Displaying results node and click  on the toolbar of the canvas to delete unnecessary process nodes.

       In the component list under Components > Activity on the left, drag RPA Task to the canvas and connect it to the Enter query scope and End Event nodes.
        

      

      

     Configure the form page for the manual task node.
      

      
       Click the Enter query scope node. On the Primary Property tab page on the right, configure the node properties.
        

        

       Click the Input City and Days node again and choose User Task > Form to access the process form page designer.
        

        

       In the page designer, right-click the Please enter the starting number component and select Delete from the shortcut menu to delete unnecessary page component.

       In the component list under Components > Data Field on the left, drag Text Input to the canvas and place it above the Please enter an end value component.
        

        

       Click the Text Input component. On the Properties tab page on the right, configure information about the component based on the actual service scenario.
        

        

       Click the Please enter an end value component. On the Properties tab page on the right, configure information about the component based on the actual service scenario.
        

        

       Click  in the upper part of the canvas to save the configuration of the hyper-automation process form page.

      

      

     Configure the RPA task node.
      

      
       Return to the process canvas page and click the RPA Task node.

       On the Primary Property tab page on the right, click RPA Task Parameters.

       In the RPA Task Parameters dialog box, configure the basic information and parameters of the task.
        

        

        
         
          
           Table 1 Parameter description
          
          
           
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

            
             Configuration Example

           

          
          
           
            
             Basic Info

           

           
            
             Script

            
             Robot script used during robot task execution

            
             Weather information collection robot

           

           
            
             Procedure Version Match Type

            
             Mode of matching robot scripts during robot task execution

             
              Specified Version: Only the robot scripts of the specified version are executed in the robot task.

              Always Latest: Only the robot scripts of the latest version are executed in the robot task.

             

            
             Specified Version

           

           
            
             Script Version

            
             Version of the robot scripts used during robot task execution

             This parameter is displayed only when Procedure Version Match Type is set to Specified Version.

            
             1.0.6

           

           
            
             Running Mode

            
             Available client types that are found by the system during robot task execution

             
              Executor: An available executor is used in a robot task to execute the robot scripts. Rules for determining the executor availability are as follows: whether the executor is public, whether the OS of the executor matches that of the system that the script applies to, and whether the executor is online.

              Cluster: An available cluster is used in a robot task to execute the robot scripts. Rules for determining the cluster availability are as follows: whether the cluster is public, whether the OS of the cluster matches that of the system that the script applies to, and whether an available executor exists in the cluster.

             

            
             Executor

           

           
            
             Preferential Search

            
             Name of the agent that is preferentially searched for during robot task execution

             
              Running Mode is set to Executor: When searching for available executors, the system preferentially selects the executor whose name matches the value of this parameter.

              Running Mode is set to Cluster: When searching for available clusters, the system preferentially selects the cluster whose name matches the value of this parameter.

             

             To reference a parameter in the process form, click  and select the parameter. If the required parameter cannot be selected, enter the JSON path of the parameter to be referenced and enclose the path with $().

            
             test

           

           
            
             Timeout (min)

            
             Timeout interval for executing a robot job. The default value is 120. If the timeout interval is not limited, set this parameter to -1.

             To reference a parameter in the process form, click  and select the parameter. If the required parameter cannot be selected, enter the JSON path of the parameter to be referenced and enclose the path with $().

            
             120

name: About Integration Services
title: About Integration Services
text:
About Integration Services
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes the architecture, functions, concepts, and scenarios of the integration services.

   
    Architecture and Functions

    

    ADC can interact with third-party systems through integration services. The core functions are as follows:

    
     The client of the third-party system calls the inbound SOAP/REST API of ADC to implement service functions.

     ADC calls the outbound SOAP or REST API provided by the third-party system server to implement service functions.

    

    The ADC integration service architecture consists of the following modules:

    
     SOAP API management: provides unified management of inbound and outbound SOAP APIs, including creating, modifying, querying, and debugging SOAP APIs.

     Log management: provides the function of querying logs of inbound and outbound SOAP or REST APIs, including querying received and sent logs and retrying upon an API sending failure.

     Authentication management: provides authentication for inbound and outbound SOAP or REST APIs and supports multiple authentication modes, such as basic authentication, OAuth 2.0, WSSE, and Keystore.

     REST API management: provides unified management of inbound and outbound REST APIs, including creating, modifying, querying, and debugging REST APIs.

    

   

   
    Concepts and Scenarios

    
     Inbound APIs, including inbound REST and SOAP APIs, are provided for third parties.
      
       For example, you can develop a member management system in ADC, which provides table data of the memberInfo data model and the memberInfo_getList service for member query. The service can be encapsulated into an inbound REST API for third parties to query a member in the developed system.
       
        Figure 1 Inbound APIs
        
       

      

     The outbound APIs are used to call third-party APIs, including outbound REST and SOAP APIs.
      
       For example, when querying data on a page developed in ADC, an API provided by third-party apps is required to obtain the query result on the page developed in ADC. In this case, you can use the outbound API to call the external API.
       
        Figure 2 Outbound APIs
        
       

      

    

   

   
    Authentication Strategy

    Configure an authentication strategy on the corresponding service configuration page.

    
     Unidirectional authentication means that the client verifies the authenticity of the server. After a server certificate is exported, you need to import it to the truststore of the client so that the client builds a trust relationship with the server. When connecting to the server, the client uses the public key of the server to verify whether the server is trustworthy. If the verification is passed, the client establishes a connection with the server.

     Two-way authentication means that the client and the server verify the authenticity of each other. In this case, the server certificate needs to be imported to the client and the keystore of the client needs to be configured on the server.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Integration Service API Configuration

name: Development Process of an Integration Service
title: Development Process of an Integration Service
text:
Development Process of an Integration Service
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to develop an integration service.

   
    Scenario Description

    Integration services provide the capability of interacting with third-party systems through REST or SOAP APIs. From the perspective of service interaction direction, integration services are classified into outbound and inbound APIs. For example, a third-party system calls an inbound API developed in ADC to query specified service data, or ADC calls a developed outbound API to obtain service information from the third-party system.

   

   
    Development Process

    Figure 1 shows the development process of an integration service.

    
     Figure 1 Development process of an integration service
     
    

    
     
      
       Table 1 Development process description
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Process

        
         Subprocess

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Preparing for integration service development

        
         Creating a Project for the Integration Service

        
         Create a project for the integration service to facilitate subsequent integration service development.

       

       
        
         Configuring Common Parameters for the Integration Service

        
         Identify the common information of the integration service and configure it as a common variable in the project to reduce the integration service development complexity.

       

       
        
         Creating a Machine-Machine User for Authentication

        
         Create a machine-machine user for the integration service to perform authentication, and associate the user with roles and IP address access control policies.

       

       
        
         Analyzing the integration service development requirement

        
         -

        
         Analyze the API type, service function processing logic, and input and output parameters of the integration service to be developed based on scenario requirements.

       

       
        
         Developing the integration service

        
         Developing an Inbound REST API

        
         Develop an inbound REST API to encapsulate developed services into the REST API for a third-party system to use.

       

       
        
         Developing an Inbound SOAP API

        
         Develop an inbound SOAP API to encapsulate developed services into the SOAP API for a third-party system to use.

       

       
        
         Developing an Outbound REST API

        
         Develop an outbound REST API so that the REST API provided by a third-party system can be called on a page or in a service to use the corresponding service functions.

       

       
        
         Developing an Outbound SOAP API

        
         Develop an outbound SOAP API so that the SOAP API provided by a third-party system can be called on a page or in a service to use the corresponding service functions.

name: Configuring Common Parameters for the Integration Service
title: Configuring Common Parameters for the Integration Service
text:
Configuring Common Parameters for the Integration Service
 
 
  
  

  
   Before developing an integration service, you need to configure required common parameters.

   
    Context

    During API development, you need to identify the common information of APIs and configure the information as common variables in the project. Common parameters include the interworking address, authentication mode, machine-machine user account, and authentication key.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     On the Project Management page, click  in the Operation column of the created project.

     On the displayed page, click Create.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Parameter Name

          
           Parameter name, which can contain letters, digits, underscores (_), and hyphens (-). The value contains 1 to 50 characters.

         

         
          
           Parameter Type

          
           The value can be Number or String.

         

         
          
           Configurable

          
           Whether parameters can be modified after an app is installed and enters the runtime-state environment.

         

         
          
           Encrypt

          
           Whether to encrypt the value.

         

         
          
           Parameter Value

          
           Default value of the parameter.

         

         
          
           DisplayOrder

          
           Sequence of a parameter in the app parameter list in the runtime-state environment. A smaller value indicates a higher sequence. If this parameter is not set, the parameter is displayed at last.

         

         
          
           Parameter Label

          
           Name displayed in Chinese and English.

         

        
       
      

      

     After the configuration is complete, click Save.

     Use the configured common parameters in the API configuration.
      

      
       In the Service Address field of the outbound REST and SOAP APIs, if connect_address indicates the service address, the address is in the format of "https://${connect_address}/", that is, the calling mode is ${parameter}.

       In the outbound and inbound REST or SOAP APIs, if the default value needs to be transferred by defining a parameter (for example, user_name indicates the authentication user name), the default value is set in the format of "$.user_name", that is, the calling mode is $.parameter.

      

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After the project for the integration service is deployed in the runtime-state environment, if you need to modify a common parameter of that project, perform the following operations:

    
     Modify a common app parameter of the project on the App Management page.
      
       Access the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Administration > Assets > App Management.

       On the app list page, click Configure on the right of the project for the integration service.

       In the Configuration dialog box, click  in the Operation column of the common parameter to be modified.
        

        

       In the Update Common Parameter Configuration dialog box, change Parameter Value of the common parameter as needed.
        

        

       Click Save.

      

     Modify a common app parameter of the project on the GDE App Manager page.
      
       Access the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager.

       On the app list page, click Set Parameters on the right of the project for the integration service.

       In the Set Parameters dialog box, click the App Parameters tab and change the value of the common parameter as needed.
        

        

       Click Submit.

name: Creating a Machine-Machine User for Authentication
title: Creating a Machine-Machine User for Authentication
text:
Creating a Machine-Machine User for Authentication
 
 
  
  

  
   Before developing an integration service, you need to create a machine-machine user required for the integration service to perform authentication.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the runtime-state environment.

     The role required by the machine-machine user has been created. For details, see User and Role Permission Management.

     (Optional) The IP address access control policy required by the machine-machine user has been created. For details, see Creating an IP Access Control Policy.

    

   

   
    Context

    If the following authentication types are selected during the authentication strategy configuration for the integration service, you need to create a machine-machine user in advance for normal usage of subsequent API functions:

    
     Inbound REST APIs: Authentication Type can be Basic or OAuth2.

     Inbound SOAP APIs: Authentication Type can be WSSE (with User name token enabled), Machine Account, or Custom Account.

     Outbound REST and SOAP APIs: Authentication Type can be Basic Auth.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

     Choose Products and Services > Administration > Identity Authentication > Machine-Machine User Management.

     Create a machine-machine user required for integration service to perform the authentication.
      

      
       Click Create Machine-Machine User.

       Configure information about the machine-machine user required by the integration service.
        

        

        
         
          
           Table 1 Parameter description
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Machine-Machine User Account

            
             Account of the machine-machine user, which is used for subsequent login.

           

           
            
             Expiration Time

            
             Validity period of the machine-machine user.

           

           
            
             Authentication Type

            
             Authentication type used by the machine-machine user. The value can be Basic or AK/SK.

             In the integration service authentication scenario, set this parameter to Basic.

           

           
            
             Select Human-Machine User

            
             Human-machine user associated with the machine-machine user. Only one human-machine user account can be associated.

           

           
            
             Description

            
             Description of the machine-machine user.

           

          
         
        

       Click Submit.

       In the displayed dialog box, click Click One-Click Copy to save and record the key information (values of AccessId and Secretkey) of the machine-machine user, and select I have confirmed to save the Basic key.

       Click OK.

      

      

     Associate the created machine-machine user with the machine-machine roles.
      

      
       Return to the Machine-Machine User List page and click the created machine-machine user name.

       Click the Machine-Machine User Authorization tab and click Machine-Machine Role.

       In the SelectableMachine-Machine Role list, select the required roles.
        

        

       Click Associate.

      

      

     (Optional) Associate the created machine-machine user with the IP address access policies.
      

      
       Return to the Machine-Machine User List page and click the created machine-machine user name.

       Click the IP Access Control Policy tab and click IP Access Control Policy.

       In the SelectableIP Access Control Policy list, select the required IP policies.
        

        

       Click Associate.

name: Configuring an Inbound REST API
title: Configuring an Inbound REST API
text:
Configuring an Inbound REST API
 
 
  
  

  
   Configure an inbound REST service to encapsulate developed services into an REST API. The third-party systems can call the inbound REST API to use the corresponding service functions.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     A project and a module have been created.

     The machine-machine user required by the inbound REST API has been created and associated with specified roles.

    

   

   
    Context

    A member management system, including table data of the memberInfo data model and the memberInfo_getList service for querying member information, has been developed in the system. Developers need to encapsulate the service into an inbound REST API for third-party systems to call to query member information in the member management system.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the project list page, click the created project for the integration service.

     In the navigation pane, choose Inbound REST.

     On the Inbound REST page, click Create.

     Configure basic information about the API.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters for configuring basic information
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Service Name

          
           Name of the service corresponding to the inbound REST API

         

         
          
           Basic Path

          
           Basic path of the inbound REST API. The value of this parameter is automatically generated.

         

         
          
           Authentication Strategy

          
           Authentication strategy configured for an inbound REST API. For details, see 5.

         

         
          
           Log Saving Mode

          
           Whether the inbound REST API records logs and the log type. The options are as follows:

           
            Not record logs

            Record failure logs

            Record successful logs without those of the packet type

            Record all logs

           

         

         
          
           Manifest Version

          
           Metadata version of the inbound REST API

           
            1.0: baseline version. The return structure is {success: '', error: {}, logId: '', result: {}}.

            1.1: Compared with version 1.0, this version shrinks the returned object and returns only the result information.

            1.2: Compared with version 1.1, this version provides the asynchronous function.

            1.3: Compared with version 1.2, this version modifies the URL encoding mode.

           

         

         
          
           legacy

          
           Whether the inbound REST API is a legacy asset

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Description of the inbound REST API

         

        
       
      

      

     Configure an authentication strategy for the API.
      

      You can create an authentication strategy or select an existing one. The following describes how to create an authentication strategy.

      
       Click Create on the right of Authentication Strategy.

       Configure basic information about the authentication strategy.
        

        

        
         
          
           Table 2 Authentication strategy parameters
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Name

            
             Authentication strategy name

           

           
            
             Service Type

            
             Type of the integration service protocol for the authentication strategy. The options are as follows:

             
              REST

              SOAP

             

           

           
            
             Authentication Type

            
             Authentication type for the authentication strategy. When Service Type is set to REST, the following authentication types are supported:

             
              Basic: The roles associated with the created machine-machine user are used for authentication.

              OAuth2: Open Authorization (OAuth) is an open authorization protocol, and OAuth 2.0 refers to the second-generation version of OAuth authentication. In this authentication type, the roles associated with the created machine-machine user are also used for authentication.

              Custom: A customized authentication service is used for authentication. The security of this authentication type is ensured by a customized service. When the inbound REST API of the customized authentication is called, the client needs to set the tenant ID in the header. The field name is x-gde-tenant-id.
               
                 NOTICE: 
                
                 The customized authentication mode is used only for compatibility with legacy assets of ADC 1.x. In other scenarios, use the other two authentication modes.

                

               

             

           

           
            
             Access Role

            
             Machine-machine user role used when Authentication Type is set to Basic

             This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to Basic.

           

           
            
             Authentication Role

            
             Machine-machine user role used when Authentication Type is set to OAuth2

             This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to OAuth2.

           

           
            
             Authentication Service

            
             Authentication service used for customized authentication

             
               NOTICE: 
              
               In ADC 1.x, the authentication service can be associated in the API package, but the system in the current version does not support the creation of the authentication service. Therefore, only the authentication service imported along with legacy assets can be selected.

              

             

             This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to Customize.

           

           
            
             Description

            
             Description of the authentication policy

           

          
         
        

       Click Submit.

       Return to the Create Inbound REST page and select the created authentication strategy from the Authentication Strategy drop-down list.

      

      

     (Optional) Configure a routing policy for the API to forward messages.
      

      
       In the basic information area of the inbound REST API, enable Forwarding.

       Configure a routing policy.
        You can create a routing policy or select an existing one. The following describes how to create a routing policy.

        
         Click Create on the right of Routing policy.

         Configure basic information about the routing policy.
          

          

          
           
            
             Table 3 Parameters for configuring a routing policy
            
            
             
             
            
            
             
              
               Name

              
               Description

             

            
            
             
              
               Name

              
               Routing policy name

             

             
              
               Policy Type

              
               Type of the routing policy. Currently, this parameter can only be set to Customize.

             

             
              
               Custom Policy Service

              
               Service corresponding to the routing policy

               The selected service must comply with the standard return structure: {"forwardUrl": "url"}. If url is localhost, the API request is not forwarded; if url is other values, the API request is forwarded to the returned URL.

             

             
              
               Description

              
               Description of the routing policy

             

            
           
          

         Click OK.

        

      

      

     Configure the API information.
      

      
       Enter an API name.

       Click  in the Select Service text box to search for the developed service memberInfo_getList.

       Click Load Params to load input and output parameters of the searched service. The loaded parameters can be used as API parameters.
        

        
         
         
          
           
            Table 4 API parameter description
           
           
            
            
           
           
            
             
              Name

             
              Description

            

           
           
            
             
              API Name

             
              API name

            

            
             
              Service Address

             
              Address composed of the API name, inbound REST service name, and environment information

            

            
             
              Select Service

             
              Service encapsulated by APIs for external use

              Click Load Params to load service-related parameters to the input or output parameters of the API.

            

            
             
              Asynchronous

             
              Whether to enable the asynchronous execution function

              
               Enabled: After a request is sent through a client API, the process continues without waiting. After receiving the response, the client processes the response and updates the status.

               Disabled: After a request is sent through a client API, the process waits for a response and continues the subsequent services.

              

            

            
             
              Description

             
              Description of the API

            

           
          
         

        

      

      

     Set the input parameters of the API.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 5 Input parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Customized URL

          
           Customized URL of a service

         

         
          
           HTTP Method

          
           HTTP method for requesting a service URL

           The GET, PUT, POST, DELETE, and PATCH methods are supported.

         

         
          
           Content Type

          
           Request content type of a service URL. The options are as follows:

           
            x-www-form-urlencoded

            form-data

name: Debugging the Inbound REST API
title: Debugging the Inbound REST API
text:
Debugging the Inbound REST API
 
 
  
  

  
   After an inbound REST API is configured, you can debug the API to verify the configuration correctness.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     An inbound REST API has been configured.

     The API project has been deployed to the runtime-state environment.

    

   

   
    Context

    During API debugging, the debugging parameter format varies with the content type. Set parameters based on the actual definition in the API and the template loaded by the API.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     In the navigation pane, choose Inbound REST.

     In the API list, click Debug in the Operation column of the API to be debugged.

     On the displayed page, specify Operation to obtain the corresponding parameter template and set parameters based on the template.
      

      

      

      

     Click Execute.

     In the Response area, check whether the information on the Output tab page meets the expectation.
      

      
       If yes, the API functions properly.

       If not, click the Log tab to view debug logs, locate and analyze the API, rectify the fault, and debug the API again.

name: Verifying the Inbound REST API (by Calling the API by a Simulated Third-Party System)
title: Verifying the Inbound REST API (by Calling the API by a Simulated Third-Party System)
text:
Verifying the Inbound REST API (by Calling the API by a Simulated Third-Party System)
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to use a tool to simulate a third-party system and call the inbound REST API to verify it.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     An inbound REST API has been configured.

     The project designed for the inbound REST API has been deployed to the runtime-state environment.

    

   

   
    Context

    The debugging is performed only on APIs and cross-platform authentication is not involved. In actual scenarios, factors such as network interworking and authentication interworking must be considered when APIs are used by third parties. In this case, the following conditions must be met before the APIs are provided for third-party systems:

    
     The third-party systems can communicate with the current system network.

     When Authentication Type is set to Basic, you have configured a machine-machine account and provided the authentication information for third parties.

     When Authentication Type is set to Custom, you have configured a custom service and provided custom constraints for third parties.

     You have provided the service URL for third parties.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    The following describes how to configure a machine-machine account and how to simulate a third-party system to call an inbound REST API for verification when Authentication Type is set to Basic.

    
     Configure a machine-machine account.
      

      
       Access the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Administration > Identity Authentication > Machine-Machine User Management.

       Click Create Machine-Machine User.

       Configure information about the machine-machine account based on site requirements.
        

        
         
         
          Machine-Machine User Account: account of a machine-machine user

          Expiration Time: expiration time of the machine-machine user

          Authentication Type: authentication type of the machine-machine user. Set this parameter to Basic.

          Select Human-Machine User: human-machine user corresponding to the machine-machine user

          Description: description of the machine-machine user

         

        

       Click Submit.
        After the submission, AccessId and Secretkey are displayed for only once. The values of these two parameters correspond to Username and Password for basic authentication. Store the values properly.

       After the creation is complete, return to the machine-machine user list and click the machine-machine user account.

       Click the Machine-Machine User Authorization tab and select a user role.
        The selected user roles must be the same as those configured for authentication.

      

      

     Use a tool to simulate a third-party system and call the inbound REST API.
      

      
       In the tool, configure the service type and URL based on the actual information about the inbound REST API.
        
         Figure 1 Configuring the service type and URL
         
        

       In the tool, configure the authentication information about the inbound REST API.
        
         Figure 2 Authentication information
         
        

       In the tool, configure the corresponding input parameters based on the parameters set using the inbound REST API. For example, if parameters exist in the body of the inbound REST API, set the parameters in the body of the tool. In addition, the message content format must be the same as that of the inbound REST API.
        
         Figure 3 Configuration message
         
        

       After the parameters are set, send an inbound REST request message and check the sending result.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Developing an Inbound REST API

Developing an Inbound SOAP API
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to develop an inbound SOAP API.

  

  
   
    Configuring an Inbound SOAP API

    (Optional) Uploading the Inbound Authentication Strategy Certificate
      If an inbound SOAP API uses the WSSE authentication mode and Signature Type or User Name Token is enabled, or an inbound SOAP API uses the Custom Account authentication mode, you need to upload the WSSE signature certificate file to the system or change the user password to ensure smooth API debugging.

    Debugging the Inbound SOAP API
      After an inbound SOAP API is configured, you can debug the API to verify the configuration correctness.

    Verifying the Inbound SOAP API (by Calling the API by a Simulated Third-Party System)
