name: Configuring an Inbound SOAP API
title: Configuring an Inbound SOAP API
text:
Configuring an Inbound SOAP API
 
 
  
  

  
   Configure an inbound SOAP service to encapsulate developed services into an SOAP API. The third-party systems can call the inbound SOAP API to use the corresponding service functions.

   
    Prerequisites

    A project and a module have been created.

   

   
    Context

    A member management system, including table data of the memberInfo data model and the memberInfo_getList service for querying member information, has been developed in the system. Developers need to encapsulate the service into an inbound SOAP API for third-party systems to call to query member information in the member management system.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the project list page, click the created project for the integration service.

     In the navigation pane, choose Inbound SOAP.

     On the Inbound SOAP page, click Create.

     Configure basic information about the API.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters for configuring basic information
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Service Name

          
           Name of the service corresponding to the inbound SOAP API

         

         
          
           Service Type

          
           Type of the service corresponding to the outbound SOAP API. The options are as follows:

           
            Custom: Select a developed service to load service parameters.

            WSDL: Upload a defined SOAP WSDL file to obtain service parameters.

           

         

         
          
           Initialize WSDL

          
           WSDL file used by the inbound SOAP API

           Click Add and select the defined WSDL file.

         

         
          
           Authentication Strategy

          
           Authentication strategy configured for an inbound SOAP API. For details, see 5.

         

         
          
           Log Saving Mode

          
           Whether the inbound SOAP API records logs and the log type. The options are as follows:

           
            Not record logs

            Record failure logs

            Record successful logs without those of the packet type

            Record all logs

           

         

         
          
           Token

          
           Whether the inbound SOAP API verifies user token information

         

         
          
           legacy

          
           Whether the inbound SOAP API is a legacy asset

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Description of the inbound SOAP API

         

        
       
      

      

     Configure an authentication strategy for the API.
      

      
       You can create an authentication strategy or select an existing one. The following describes how to create an authentication strategy.
       
        Click Create on the right of Authentication Strategy.

        Configure basic information about the authentication strategy.
         

         

         
          
           
            Table 2 Authentication strategy parameters
           
           
            
            
           
           
            
             
              Name

             
              Description

            

           
           
            
             
              Name

             
              Authentication strategy name

            

            
             
              Service Type

             
              Type of the integration service protocol for the authentication strategy. The options are as follows:

              
               REST

               SOAP

              

            

            
             
              Authentication Type

             
              Authentication type for the authentication strategy. When Service Type is set to SOAP, the following authentication types are supported:

              
               WSSE: The WSSE signature, user name token, or timestamp is used for authentication.

               Machine Account: The roles associated with the created machine-machine user are used for authentication.

               Custom Account: The user name and password are used for authentication. This authentication type has low security and applies only to legacy assets.

              

            

            
             
              Signature Type

             
              Whether the authentication strategy uses signatures for authentication

              This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to WSSE.

            

            
             
              WSSE Signature

             
              WSSE signature used by the authentication strategy. For details, see 5.c.

              This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to WSSE and Signature Type is enabled.

            

            
             
              User Name Token

             
              Whether the authentication strategy uses the user name token for authentication

              This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to WSSE.

            

            
             
              User Name

             
              Authentication user name used in the authentication strategy. Customize this parameter for authentication when a third-party system calls the SOAP API of the system.

              This parameter is displayed only in the following scenarios:

              
               Authentication Type is set to WSSE and User Name Token is enabled.

               Authentication Type is set to Custom Account.

              

            

            
             
              Timestamp

             
              Whether the authentication strategy uses timestamps for authentication

              This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to WSSE.

            

            
             
              Reset Password Upon First Machine-Machine Connection Setup

             
              Whether to reset the user password when the machine-machine connection is established for the first time

              This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to WSSE or Custom Account.

            

            
             
              Access Role

             
              Access role used for authentication in the authentication strategy

              This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to Machine Account.

            

            
             
              Authentication Node Name

             
              Name of the access node used for authentication in the authentication strategy

              This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to Machine Account or Custom Account.

            

            
             
              Description

             
              Description of the authentication policy

            

           
          
         

        (Optional) When Authentication Type is set to WSSE, configure the WSSE signature.
         
          You can create a WSSE signature or select an existing one. The following describes how to create a WSSE signature.
          
           Click Create on the right of WSSE Signature.

           Configure basic information about the WSSE signature.
            

            

            
             
              
               Table 3 WSSE signature parameters
              
              
               
               
              
              
               
                
                 Name

                
                 Description

               

              
              
               
                
                 Name

                
                 WSSE signature name

               

               
                
                 Signature Type

                
                 WSSE signature type. The options are as follows:

                 
                  Inbound Signature

                  Outbound Signature

                  All

                 

               

               
                
                 Keystore

                
                 Keystore file used for WSSE signature, which is obtained from the interworked third-party system. For details, see 5.d.

               

               
                
                 Identifier

                
                 Identifier information in the WSSE signature, which is obtained from the interworked third-party system. The options are as follows:

                 
                  
                   X509KeyIdentifier

                  
                   BSTIdentifier

                  
                   IssueSerialIdentifier

                  
                   SKIdentifier

                 

               

               
                
                 Algorithm

                
                 Encryption algorithm for the WSSE signature, which must be consistent with the algorithm used in a third-party system.

               

               
                
                 Canonicalization

                
                 Canonicalization information in the WSSE signature, which must be the same as the canonicalization configuration of the third-party system.

               

              
             
            

           Click Save.

          

         

        (Optional) When Authentication Type is set to WSSE, configure the keystore certificate based on site requirements.
         
          You can create a keystore certificate or select an existing one. The following describes how to create a keystore certificate.
          
           Click Create on the right of Keystore.

           Configure basic information about the keystore certificate.
            

            

            
             
              
               Table 4 Keystore certificate parameters
              
              
               
               
              
              
               
                
                 Name

                
                 Description

               

              
              
               
                
                 Name

                
                 Name of a keystore certificate

               

               
                
                 Type

                
                 Type of the keystore certificate

                 Essentially, both keystore and truststore are keystore certificates. The only difference is that the owners of the keys stored in Keystore and Truststore are different.

                 
                  Keystore: client certificate, which stores its own private and public keys. This certificate is used by the server to verify whether the client is secure and valid.

                  Truststore: server certificate, which is used to store the public keys of trusted objects. This certificate is used by the client to verify whether the server is secure and valid.

                 

                 The WSSE signature requires only the keystore certificate. Therefore, Type must be set to Keystore.

               

               
                
                 Description

                
                 Description of the keystore certificate

               

              
             
            

           Click Save.

           Return to the Create WSSE Signature page, select the created keystore certificate from the Keystore drop-down list, and click Save.

           Return to the Create Inbound Strategy page, select the created WSSE signature from the WSSE Signature drop-down list, and click Submit.

          

         

        Return to the Create Inbound SOAP page and select the created authentication strategy from the Authentication Strategy drop-down list.

        Click Submit.

       

      

      

     Configure the API information.
      

      
       In the operation area, enter an operation name.

       Click  in the Called Service URL text box to search for the developed service memberInfo_getList.

       Click Load Params to load input and output parameters of the searched service. The loaded parameters can be used as API parameters.
        

        

        
         
          
           Table 5 API parameter description
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Operation Name

            
             Operation name of the API

           

           
            
             Called Service URL

            
             Service encapsulated by APIs for external use

             Click Load Params to load service-related parameters to the input or output parameters of the API.

           

           
            
             Description

            
             Description of the API.

           

          
         
        

      

      

     Set the input parameters of the API.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 6 Input parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Parameter Name

          
           Name of an input parameter

         

         
          
           Mandatory

          
           Whether the input parameter is mandatory

           If this field is selected, the parameter is mandatory. If this field is not selected, the parameter is optional.

         

         
          
           Type

          
           Data type of the input parameter. The options are as follows:

           
            boolean

            integer

            number

            string

            object

            decimal

            file (This type can be manually selected only when form-data or octest-stream is selected for Content Type.)

           

         

         
          
           Sensitive Data

          
           Whether the input parameter is sensitive data

           If this field is selected, the parameter is sensitive data. If this field is not selected, the parameter is non-sensitive data.

         

         
          
           Mapping Path

          
           Mapping path of the input parameter

           This parameter is optional for parameters added by clicking Load Params.

         

         
          
           Default Value

          
           Default value of the input parameter

           If a common parameter is defined, you can use $.parameter to reference the parameter value. For details, see Configuring Common Parameters for the Integration Service.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Description of the input parameter

         

         
          
           Validator

          
           Validator used by the input parameter

         

        
       
      

      

     Set the output parameters of the API.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 7 Output parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Parameter Name

          
           Name of an output parameter

         

         
          
           Type

          
           Data type of the output parameter. The options are as follows:

           
            boolean

            integer

            number

            string

            object (Only this type supports child nodes.)

           

         

         
          
           Sensitive Data

          
           Whether the output parameter is sensitive data

           If this field is selected, the parameter is sensitive data. If this field is not selected, the parameter is non-sensitive data.

         

         
          
           Mapping Path

          
           Mapping path of the output parameter

           Obtain the value from the context. $.headers.xxx.xxx is supported to obtain the response header.

         

         
          
           Default Value

          
           Default value of the output parameter, which is used when the third-party system does not return a value.

           If a common parameter is defined, you can use $.parameter to reference the parameter value. For details, see Configuring Common Parameters for the Integration Service.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Description of the output parameter

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Submit.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    
     Deploy the API project to the runtime-state environment.
      
       If Enable Hot Deployment is selected for the project, no operation is required.

       If Enable Hot Deployment is disabled for the project, click  in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment to package and deploy the API project to the runtime-state environment.

      

     After the API project is deployed to the runtime-state environment, the system generates an API calling URL. You can also perform debugging based on the URL.

     Go to the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Log Management > Integration Log > SOAP Receive Log to view the log information about the API.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Developing an Inbound SOAP API

name: (Optional) Uploading the Inbound Authentication Strategy Certificate
title: (Optional) Uploading the Inbound Authentication Strategy Certificate
text:
(Optional) Uploading the Inbound Authentication Strategy Certificate
 
 
  
  

  
   If an inbound SOAP API uses the WSSE authentication mode and Signature Type or User Name Token is enabled, or an inbound SOAP API uses the Custom Account authentication mode, you need to upload the WSSE signature certificate file to the system or change the user password to ensure smooth API debugging.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     The project designed for the inbound SOAP API has been deployed to the runtime-state environment.

     (Optional) You have obtained the keystore certificate files required for WSSE signature.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     If an API uses the WSSE authentication mode and Signature Type is enabled, upload the keystore certificates required for WSSE signature.
      

      
       Go to the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Administration > Integration Service > Certificate Management.

       In the certificate list, click the name of the certificate required for the WSSE signature configured in the API authentication strategy. The Edit Certificate page is displayed.

       Set Alias for the certificate and set Type to Keystore.

       Click Add under Keystore File, upload the obtained certificate file, and set Password for the certificate.
        

        

       Click Confirm.

       Repeat 1.b to 1.e to upload and configure all keystore certificate files required for WSSE signature.

      

      

     If an API uses the WSSE authentication mode and User Name Token is enabled, set password for the user.
      

      
       Go to the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Administration > Integration Service > Inbound Strategy Management.

       In the inbound authentication strategy list, click the name of the authentication strategy associated with the API. The Edit Inbound Strategy page is displayed.

       Click Modify Password on the right of Password. In the displayed dialog box, click Confirm.

       In the InitPassword dialog box, click Validate because the user password is not set in the authentication strategy of the develop-state environment.

       Return to the Edit Inbound Strategy page and enter the password of the user in the authentication strategy in the Password text box. Alternatively, click Auto Generate Password, copy the password generated by the system, and enter the password in the Password text box.
        

        

       Click Confirm.
        
          
         
          After the user password is set, if you need to change it, enter the previous password for verification.

         

        

      

      

     If an API uses the Custom Account authentication mode, set password for the user.
      

      
       Go to the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Administration > Integration Service > Inbound Strategy Management.

       In the inbound authentication strategy list, click the name of the authentication strategy associated with the API. The Edit Inbound Strategy page is displayed.

       In the Password text box, enter the password of the user specified in the authentication strategy. Alternatively, click Auto Generate Password, copy the password generated by the system, and enter the password in the Password text box.

       Click Confirm.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Developing an Inbound SOAP API

name: Debugging the Inbound SOAP API
title: Debugging the Inbound SOAP API
text:
Debugging the Inbound SOAP API
 
 
  
  

  
   After an inbound SOAP API is configured, you can debug the API to verify the configuration correctness.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     An inbound SOAP API has been configured.

     The API project has been deployed to the runtime-state environment.

    

   

   
    Context

    
     During API debugging, the debugging parameter format varies with the content type. Set parameters based on the actual definition in the API and the template loaded by the API.

     Only inbound SOAP APIs for which Authentication Type is Custom can be debugged. If Authentication Type of an inbound SOAP API is WSSE, the API cannot be debugged directly.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    The following uses the inbound SOAP APIs for which Authentication Type is set to Custom as an example to describe how to debug an API.

    
     Configure a machine-machine account.
      

      
       Access the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Administration > Identity Authentication > Machine-Machine User Management.

       Click Create Machine-Machine User.

       Configure information about the machine-machine account based on site requirements.
        

        
         
         
          Machine-Machine User Account: account of a machine-machine user

          Expiration Time: expiration time of the machine-machine user

          Authentication Type: authentication type of the machine-machine user. Set this parameter to Basic.

          Select Human-Machine User: human-machine user corresponding to the machine-machine user

          Description: description of the machine-machine user

         

        

       Click Submit.
        After the submission, AccessId and Secretkey are displayed for only once. The values of these two parameters correspond to Username and Password for basic authentication. Store the values properly.

       After the creation is complete, return to the machine-machine user list and click the machine-machine user account.

       Click the Machine-Machine User Authorization tab and select a user role.
        The selected user roles must be the same as those configured for authentication.

      

      

     Debug an API.
      

      
       In the navigation pane, choose Inbound SOAP.

       In the API list, click Debug in the Operation column of the API to be debugged.

       On the displayed page, specify Operation to obtain the corresponding parameter template and set parameters based on the template.
        Set userName and Password to the values of AccessId and Secretkey of the machine-machine account created in 1.

        

        

       Click Execute.

       In the Response area, check whether the information on the Output tab page meets the expectation.
        
         If yes, the API functions properly.

         If not, click the Log tab to view debug logs, locate and analyze the API, rectify the fault, and debug the API again.

        

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Developing an Inbound SOAP API

name: Verifying the Inbound SOAP API (by Calling the API by a Simulated Third-Party System)
title: Verifying the Inbound SOAP API (by Calling the API by a Simulated Third-Party System)
text:
Verifying the Inbound SOAP API (by Calling the API by a Simulated Third-Party System)
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to use a tool to simulate a third-party system and call the inbound SOAP API to verify it.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     An inbound SOAP API has been configured.

     The project designed for the inbound SOAP API has been deployed to the runtime-state environment.

    

   

   
    Context

    The debugging is performed only on APIs and cross-platform authentication is not involved. In actual scenarios, when an API is used by a third-party system, ensure that the third-party system can communicate with the current system and provide authentication information for the third-party system based on the API authentication type:

   

   
    If Authentication Type is set to WSSE, configure the required authentication information based on site requirements and provide the information for the third-party system.
     
      For the WSSE Signature parameter, set Keystore, Identifier, and Algorithm.

      For the User Name Token parameter, enable this function and configure the corresponding user name.

      For the Timestamp parameter, enable this function.

     

    If Authentication Type is set to Custom, create a machine-machine user on the Products and Services > Administration > Identity Authentication > Machine-Machine User Management page in runtime-state environment and provide the values of AccessId and Secretkey for the third-party system.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Provide authentication information for the third party based on the authentication type of the inbound SOAP API.

     In the navigation pane, choose Inbound SOAP.

     In the API list, click Edit in the Operation column of the API to be verified.

     View the WSDL address of the inbound SOAP API.
      

      

      

      

     Use a tool to simulate a third-party system to call the inbound SOAP API.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Developing an Inbound SOAP API

name: Developing an Outbound REST API
title: Developing an Outbound REST API
text:
Developing an Outbound REST API
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to develop an outbound REST API.

  

  
   
    Configuring an Outbound REST API
      This section describes how to configure an outbound REST service so that the REST API provided by a third-party system can be called on a page or in a service to use the corresponding service functions.

    (Optional) Uploading the Outbound Authentication Strategy Certificate
      If an outbound REST API uses the basic authentication mode or the protocol specified in the authentication strategy is HTTPS, you need to change the user password or upload the truststore certificate file required by the HTTPS protocol to ensure smooth API debugging.

    Debugging the Outbound REST API
      After an outbound REST API is configured, you can debug the API to verify the configuration correctness.

name: Configuring an Outbound REST API
title: Configuring an Outbound REST API
text:
Configuring an Outbound REST API
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to configure an outbound REST service so that the REST API provided by a third-party system can be called on a page or in a service to use the corresponding service functions.

   
    Prerequisites

    A project and a module have been created.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the project list page, click the created project for the integration service.

     In the navigation pane, choose Outbound REST.

     On the Outbound REST page, click Create.

     Configure basic information about the API.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters for configuring basic information
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Service Name

          
           Name of the service corresponding to the outbound REST API

         

         
          
           Service Type

          
           Service type corresponding to the outbound REST API

           
            OAuth2 Token Service: authenticates the outbound REST API.

            Standalone Service: indicates the common outbound REST API.

           

         

         
          
           Authentication Strategy

          
           Authentication strategy configured for an outbound REST API. For details, see 5.

         

         
          
           Log Saving Mode

          
           Whether the outbound REST API records logs and the log type. The options are as follows:

           
            Not record logs

            Record failure logs

            Record successful logs without those of the packet type

            Record all logs

           

         

         
          
           Swagger Specifications

          
           Swagger definition file (*.yaml) provided by a third-party system. It can help developers configure services more quickly.

           After the file is uploaded, you can select an operation to view the related service URL.

         

         
          
           Service Address

          
           Web service URL provided by a third-party system. You can use either of the following methods to obtain the service URL:

           
            After you upload a YAML file and select an operation, the system automatically parses the file to obtain the service URL.

            Manually enter a service URL provided by a third-party system. You can use defined common parameters in the format of "${parameter}". For details, see Configuring Common Parameters for the Integration Service.

           

         

         
          
           Operation

          
           REST service operations provided by a third-party system. After the YAML file is uploaded, you can select required options from the Operation drop-down list.

         

         
          
           Asynchronous

          
           Whether to enable the asynchronous execution function

           
            Enabled: After a request is sent through a client API, the process continues without waiting. After receiving the response, the client processes the response and updates the status.

            Disabled: After a request is sent through a client API, the process waits for a response and continues the subsequent services.

           

         

         
          
           Connect Timeout (ms)

          
           Timeout interval for the outbound REST API to connect to the server, in milliseconds

         

         
          
           Read Timeout (ms)

          
           Timeout interval for the outbound REST API to read the server data, in milliseconds

         

         
          
           Open Level

          
           Open level of the outbound REST API

           
            
             Public: indicates that the service is public and can be used within the system.

            
             Project: indicates that the service can be used within a project. When there are multiple modules in the project, the service can also be used within the project modules.

            
             Module: indicates that the service can be used within a module.

           

         

         
          
           Registration in API

          
           Whether the outbound REST API is registered into the API center. After the API is registered, you can view it on the API Catalog page.

           This parameter is displayed only when Open Level is set to Public.

         

         
          
           API Catalog

          
           When this is enabled, set the location for registering with the API catalog.

           The directory must have at least three levels.

           You can view and manage API catalogs on Asset Management > Asset Library.

           
            Figure 1 Catalog management
            
           

         

         
          
           Scope

          
           
            If the project to which the API belongs is at the personal level, set this parameter to Personal or Public.

            If the project to which the API belongs is at the team level, set this parameter to Team or Public.

            When the project to which the API belongs is changed, the registered API sharing scope needs to be changed manually.

           

         

         
          
           legacy

          
           Whether the outbound REST API is a legacy asset

         

         
          
           Manifest Version

          
           Metadata version of the outbound REST API

           
            1.0: baseline version. The return structure is {success: '', error: {}, logId: '', result: {}}.

            1.1: Compared with version 1.0, this version supports spaces in a path parameter. For example, if the path parameter needs to support 2024-04-28 00:00:00, version 1.1 is used.

           

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Description of the outbound REST API

         

        
       
      

      

     Configure an authentication strategy for the API.
      

      
       You can create an authentication strategy or select an existing one. The following describes how to create an authentication strategy.
       
        Click Create on the right of Authentication Strategy.

        Configure basic information about the authentication strategy.
         

         

         
          
           
            Table 2 Authentication strategy parameters
           
           
            
            
           
           
            
             
              Name

             
              Description

            

           
           
            
             
              Name

             
              Authentication strategy name

            

            
             
              Authentication Type

             
              Authentication type for the authentication strategy. The options are as follows:

              
               Basic Auth: The user name and password are used for authentication.

               OAuth2 Token Service: The outbound REST API whose Service Type is OAuth2 Token Service is used for authentication.

               Custom: Authentication is not performed. This authentication type is insecure. Exercise caution when selecting this authentication type.

              

            

            
             
              Auth Header

             
              Auth header configuration in the authentication strategy. The options are as follows:

              
               Without Type Field

               With Type Field

              

            

            
             
              User Name

             
              User name used for authentication in the authentication strategy

              This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to Basic Auth.

            

            
             
              Protocol

             
              Type of the protocol used for authentication in the authentication strategy. The options are as follows:

              
               HTTPS

               HTTP

              

            

            
             
              Truststore

             
              Truststore certificate used in the authentication strategy. For details, see 5.c.

              This parameter is displayed only when Protocol is set to HTTPS.

            

            
             
              OAuth Name

             
              OAuth configuration used in the authentication strategy

              This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to OAuth2 Token Service.

            

            
             
              Two-way Authentication

             
              Whether to enable the two-way authentication function. The options are as follows:

              
               Enabled: mutual authentication of an API caller and provider. After the client authenticates the server, the server also authenticates the agent. Two-way authentication requires that both client and server have certificates. In this case, you need to configure the client authentication and provide the client keystore file or directly use the system key of the client.

               Disabled: authentication only of an API caller. That is, only the client needs to authenticate the server. Therefore, only the certificate of the server is required.

              

              This parameter is displayed only when Protocol is set to HTTPS.

            

            
             
              Host Name Check

             
              Whether to enable the function of checking the host name. The options are as follows:

            

            
             
              Use System Secret Key

             
              Whether to use the system key for authentication after the two-way authentication function is enabled. The options are as follows:

              
               Enabled: The system key is used. You do not need to upload the keystore file of the client for authentication.

               Disabled: The system key is not used. You need to upload the keystore file of the client for authentication.

              

              This parameter is displayed only when Two-way Authentication is enabled.

            

            
             
              Keystore

             
              Client keystore used in the authentication strategy after the two-way authentication function is enabled. The method of configuring the keystore is similar to that of configuring the truststore. For details, see 5.c.

              This parameter is displayed only when Two-way Authentication is enabled and Use System Secret Key is disabled.

            

            
             
              Description

             
              Description of the authentication policy

            

           
          
         

        Configure the truststore certificate required in the authentication strategy.
         
          You can create a truststore certificate or select an existing one. The following describes how to create a truststore certificate.
          
           Click Create on the right of Truststore.

           Configure basic information about the truststore certificate.
            

            

            
             
              
               Table 3 Truststore certificate parameters
              
              
               
               
              
              
               
                
                 Name

                
                 Description

               

              
              
               
                
                 Name

                
                 Name of the truststore certificate

               

               
                
                 Type

                
                 Type of the keystore certificate

                 Essentially, both keystore and truststore are keystore certificates. The only difference is that the owners of the keys stored in Keystore and Truststore are different.

                 
                  Keystore: client certificate, which stores its own private and public keys. This certificate is used by the server to verify whether the client is secure and valid.

                  Truststore: server certificate, which is used to store the public keys of trusted objects. This certificate is used by the client to verify whether the server is secure and valid.

                 

                 The outbound authentication strategy requires only the truststore certificate. Therefore, Type must be set to Truststore.

               

               
                
                 Description

                
                 Description of the truststore certificate

               

              
             
            

           Click Save.

           Return to the Create Outbound Strategy page, select the created truststore certificate from the Truststore drop-down list, and click Submit.

          

         

        Return to the Create Outbound REST page and select the created authentication strategy from the Authentication Strategy drop-down list.

        Click Submit.

       

      

      

     Set input parameters of the API.
      

      Set input parameters of the API based on the requirements of the third-party system. That is, the input parameters of the API must match the requests sent to the third-party system. Otherwise, the third-party system will fail to handle the requests.

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 4 Input parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           HTTP Method

          
           HTTP method for requesting a service URL. The GET, PUT, POST, DELETE, and PATCH methods are supported.

         

         
          
           Content Type

          
           Request content type of a service URL. The options are as follows:

           
            x-www-form-urlencoded

            form-data

            application/json

            application/yang-data+json

            text/plain

            octet-stream

           

         

         
          
           Header/Path/Query

          
           HTTP request header, path, and parameters used in the query

         

         
          
           Body

          
           Input parameter used in the request body

           This tab page is displayed only when HTTP Method is set to PUT, POST, or PATCH.

           
             NOTICE: 
            
             When only one object parameter is configured on the Body tab page of the input parameter, the parameter can be obtained from the packet and transparently transferred to an external API.

            

           

         

         
          
           Parameter Name

          
           Name of an input parameter

         

         
          
           Type

          
           Data type of the input parameter. The options are as follows:

           
            boolean

            integer

            number

            string

            object (Only this type supports child nodes.)

           

         

         
          
           Sensitive Data

          
           Whether the input parameter is sensitive data

           If this field is selected, the parameter is sensitive data. If this field is not selected, the parameter is non-sensitive data.

         

         
          
           Mandatory

          
           Whether the input parameter is mandatory

           If this field is selected, the parameter is mandatory. If this field is not selected, the parameter is optional.

         

         
          
           Retain Null

          
           Whether to retain the null value for the input parameter

           If this field is selected, the null value is reserved for this parameter. If this field is not selected, the null value is not reserved for this parameter.

         

         
          
           Mapping Path

          
           Mapping path of the input parameter

         

         
          
           Default Value

          
           Default value of the input parameter

           If a common parameter is defined, you can use $.parameter to reference the parameter value. For details, see Configuring Common Parameters for the Integration Service.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Description of the input parameter

         

         
          
           Validator

          
           Validator used by the input parameter

         

        
       
      

      

     Set the output parameters of the API.
      

      Set the output parameters of the API based on the result returned by the third-party system. If the output parameters are not set, the original HTTP response result will be returned.

      

      
       
       
        
         
          Table 5 Output parameter description
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Name

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Return Type

           
            Return type of the REST service. The options are as follows:

            
             JSON: JSON objects will be returned.

             TEXT: Texts will be returned.

             BINARY: batchid will be returned.

            

          

          
           
            Incorrect Path

           
            Path for checking the sending result. The XML file returned by a third-party system is parsed based on the xPath syntax.

          

          
           
            Parameter Name

           
            Name of an output parameter

          

          
           
            Type

           
            Data type of the output parameter. The options are as follows:

            
             boolean

             integer

             number

             string

             object (Only this type supports child nodes.)

            

          

          
           
            Sensitive Data

           
            Whether the output parameter is sensitive data

            If this field is selected, the parameter is sensitive data. If this field is not selected, the parameter is non-sensitive data.

          

          
           
            Mapping Path

           
            Mapping path of the output parameter

            Obtain the value from the context. This parameter can be set to $$.headers.xxx.xxx to obtain the response header.

          

          
           
            Default Value

           
            Default value of the output parameter, which is used when the third-party system does not return a value.

            If a common parameter is defined, you can use $.parameter to reference the parameter value. For details, see Configuring Common Parameters for the Integration Service.

          

          
           
            Description

           
            Description of the output parameter

          

         
        
       

      

      

     (Optional) Configure extended information about the API.
      

      

      
       
       
        Successful Callback Service: services that are executed after an API is successfully called.

        Error Callback Service: services that are executed after an API fails to be called.

       

      

      

     Click Submit.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    
     Deploy the API project to the runtime-state environment.
      
       If Enable Hot Deployment is selected for the project, no operation is required.

       If Enable Hot Deployment is disabled for the project, click  in the upper right corner and select One-Click Deployment to package and deploy the API project to the runtime-state environment.

      

    

    
     Go to the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Log Management > Integration Log > REST Send Log to view the log information about the API.

name: (Optional) Uploading the Outbound Authentication Strategy Certificate
title: (Optional) Uploading the Outbound Authentication Strategy Certificate
text:
(Optional) Uploading the Outbound Authentication Strategy Certificate
 
 
  
  

  
   If an outbound REST API uses the basic authentication mode or the protocol specified in the authentication strategy is HTTPS, you need to change the user password or upload the truststore certificate file required by the HTTPS protocol to ensure smooth API debugging.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     The project designed for the outbound REST API has been deployed to the runtime-state environment.

     You have obtained the authentication keystore file of the third-party system or created the integration service certificate file by referring to How Do I Create a Truststore Certificate for HTTPS-based Outbound APIs?

     (Optional) You have obtained the keystore certificate files required for authentication.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     If an API uses the basic authentication mode, set password for the user.
      

      
       Go to the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Administration > Integration Service > Outbound Strategy Management.

       In the outbound authentication strategy list, click the name of the authentication strategy associated with the API. The Edit Outbound Strategy page is displayed.

       Enter the password of the user specified in the authentication strategy in the Password text box, or enter the common project parameter corresponding to the password and enable Variable Value.
        

        

       Click Submit.

      

      

     If an API uses the basic authentication mode, upload the truststore certificate required by the HTTPS protocol.
      

      
       Go to the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Administration > Integration Service > Certificate Management.

       In the certificate list, click the certificate name corresponding to the truststore specified in the API authentication strategy. The Edit Certificate page is displayed.

       Set Alias for the certificate and set Type to Truststore.

       Click Add under Keystore File, upload the obtained certificate file, and set Password for the certificate.
        

        

       Click Confirm.

      

      

     (Optional) If an API uses the basic authentication mode, Two-way Authentication is enabled, and Use System Secret Key is disabled, upload the keystore certificate required for authentication.
      

      
       Go to the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Administration > Integration Service > Certificate Management.

       In the certificate list, click the certificate name corresponding to the keystore specified in the API authentication strategy. The Edit Certificate page is displayed.

       Set Alias for the certificate and set Type to Keystore.

       Click Add under Keystore File, upload the obtained certificate file, and set Password for the certificate.

       Click Confirm.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Developing an Outbound REST API

name: Debugging the Outbound REST API
title: Debugging the Outbound REST API
text:
Debugging the Outbound REST API
 
 
  
  

  
   After an outbound REST API is configured, you can debug the API to verify the configuration correctness.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     An outbound REST API has been configured.

     API configurations have been deployed in the runtime-state environment.

     The REST API called from external systems is available.

    

   

   
    Context

    During API debugging, the debugging parameter format varies with the content type. Set parameters based on the actual definition in the API and the template loaded by the API.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     In the navigation pane, choose Outbound REST.

     In the API list, click Debug in the Operation column of the API to be debugged.

     On the debugging page, enter the user name and password, and set parameters based on the automatically loaded parameter template.
      

      

      

      

     Click Execute.

     In the Response area, check whether the information on the Output tab page meets the expectation.
      

      
       If yes, the API functions properly.

       If not, click the Log tab to view debug logs, locate and analyze the API, rectify the fault, and debug the API again.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Developing an Outbound REST API

text:
Configuring an Outbound SOAP API
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to configure an outbound SOAP service so that the SOAP API provided by a third-party system can be called on a page or in a service to use the corresponding service functions.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     A project and a module have been created.

     The Outbound SOAP page has been accessed.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the project list page, click the created project for the integration service.

     In the navigation pane, choose Outbound SOAP.

     On the Outbound SOAP page, click Create.

     Configure basic information about the API.

           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Service Name

          
           Name of the service corresponding to the outbound SOAP API

         

         
          
           Service Type

          
           Type of the service corresponding to the outbound SOAP API. Currently, only Standalone Service can be selected. The called input parameter of this type comes from the service.

         

         
          
           WSDL

          
           Web service URL provided by a third-party system. The address can be set in either of the following two modes:

           
            Completed online: If this mode is selected, enter the URL in the text box below.

           Whether the outbound SOAP API uses the SOAP12 protocol

           Authentication strategy used by an outbound SOAP API. For details, see 5.

         

         
          
           Log Saving Mode

          
           Whether to record logs for the outbound SOAP API. The options are as follows:

           
            Not record logs

            Record failure logs

            Record successful logs without those of the packet type

            Record all logs

           

         

         
          
           Service Address

          
           Web service URL provided by a third-party system. You can use defined common parameters in the format of "${parameter}". For details, see Configuring Common Parameters for the Integration Service.

            Figure 1 Catalog management

           legacy

           Timeout interval for the outbound SOAP API to connect to the server, in milliseconds

         

         
          
           Read Timeout (ms)

          
           Timeout interval for the outbound SOAP API to read the server data, in milliseconds

         

         
          
           Delete actionName from URL

          
           Whether to delete the actionName parameter from the URL of the outbound SOAP API

           
            Enabled: Delete the actionName parameter.

            Disabled: Retain the actionName parameter.

           

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Description of the outbound SOAP API

         

        
       
      

      

     Configure an authentication strategy for the API.
      

      
       You can create an authentication strategy or select an existing one. The following describes how to create an authentication strategy.
       
        Click Create on the right of Authentication Strategy.

        Configure basic information about the authentication strategy.
         

         

         
          
           
            Table 2 Authentication strategy parameters
           
           
            
            
           
           
            
             
              Name

             
              Description

            

           
           
            
             
              Name

             
              Authentication strategy name

            

            
             
              Authentication Type

             
              Authentication type for the authentication strategy. The options are as follows:

              
               Basic Auth: The user name and password are used for authentication.

               OAuth2 Token Service: The outbound REST API whose Service Type is OAuth2 Token Service is used for authentication.

               Custom: Authentication is not performed. This authentication type is insecure. Exercise caution when selecting this authentication type.

              

            

            
             
              Auth Header

             
              Auth header configuration in the authentication strategy. The options are as follows:

              
               Without Type Field

               With Type Field

              

            

            
             
              User Name

             
              User name used for authentication in the authentication strategy

              This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to Basic Auth.

            

            
             
              Protocol

             
              Type of the protocol used for authentication in the authentication strategy. The options are as follows:

              
               HTTPS

               HTTP

              

            

            
             
              Truststore

             
              Truststore certificate used in the authentication strategy. For details, see 5.c.

              This parameter is displayed only when Protocol is set to HTTPS.

            

            
             
              OAuth Name

             
              OAuth configuration used in the authentication strategy

              This parameter is displayed only when Authentication Type is set to OAuth2 Token Service.

            

            
             
              Two-way Authentication

             
              Whether to enable the two-way authentication function. The options are as follows:

              
               Enabled: mutual authentication of an API caller and provider. After the client authenticates the server, the server also authenticates the agent. Two-way authentication requires that both client and server have certificates. In this case, you need to configure the client authentication and provide the client keystore file or directly use the system key of the client.

               Disabled: authentication only of an API caller. That is, only the client needs to authenticate the server. Therefore, only the certificate of the server is required.

              

              This parameter is displayed only when Protocol is set to HTTPS.

            

            
             
              Host Name Check

             
              Whether to enable the function of checking the host name. The options are as follows:

              Whether to use the system key for authentication after the two-way authentication function is enabled. The options are as follows:

              
               Enabled: The system key is used. You do not need to upload the keystore file of the client for authentication.

               Disabled: The system key is not used. You need to upload the keystore file of the client for authentication.

              Description

             
              Description of the authentication policy

            

           
          
         

        Configure the truststore certificate required in the authentication strategy.
         
          You can create a truststore certificate or select an existing one. The following describes how to create a truststore certificate.
          
           Click Create on the right of Truststore.

           Configure basic information about the truststore certificate.
            

            

            
             
              
               Table 3 Truststore certificate parameters
              
              
               
               
              
              
               
                
                 Name

                
                 Description

               

              
              
               
                
                 Name

                
                 Name of the truststore certificate

               

               
                
                 Type

                
                 Type of the keystore certificate

                 Essentially, both keystore and truststore are keystore certificates. The only difference is that the owners of the keys stored in Keystore and Truststore are different.

                 
                  Keystore: client certificate, which stores its own private and public keys. This certificate is used by the server to verify whether the client is secure and valid.

                  Truststore: server certificate, which is used to store the public keys of trusted objects. This certificate is used by the client to verify whether the server is secure and valid.

                 

                 The outbound authentication strategy requires only the truststore certificate. Therefore, Type must be set to Truststore.

               

               
                
                 Description

                
                 Description of the truststore certificate

               

              
             
            

           Click Save.

           Return to the Create Outbound Strategy page, select the created truststore certificate from the Truststore drop-down list, and click Submit.

          

         

        Return to the Create Outbound SOAP page and select the created authentication strategy from the Authentication Strategy drop-down list.

        Click Submit.

       

      

      

     Set the input parameters of the API.
      

      Click Load WSDL File to automatically load the input parameters of the API and modify and adjust the parameters based on the actual service scenario.

      

      
       
       
        
         
          Table 4 Input parameter description
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Name

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Parameter Name

           
            Name of an input parameter

          

          
           
            Node Type

           
            Node type of the input parameter. The options are as follows:

            
             element

             namespace

             attribute

name: Uploading the Outbound Authentication Strategy Certificate
title: Uploading the Outbound Authentication Strategy Certificate
text:
Uploading the Outbound Authentication Strategy Certificate
 
 
  
  

  
   If an outbound SOAP API uses the basic authentication mode or the protocol specified in the authentication strategy is HTTPS, you need to change the user password or upload the truststore certificate file required by the HTTPS protocol to ensure smooth API debugging.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     The project designed for the outbound SOAP API has been deployed to the runtime-state environment.

     You have obtained the authentication keystore file of the third-party system or created the integration service certificate file by referring to How Do I Create a Truststore Certificate for HTTPS-based Outbound APIs?

     (Optional) You have obtained the keystore certificate files required for authentication.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     If an API uses the basic authentication mode, set password for the user.
      

      
       Go to the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Administration > Integration Service > Outbound Strategy Management.

       In the outbound authentication strategy list, click the name of the authentication strategy associated with the API. The Edit Outbound Strategy page is displayed.

       Enter the password of the user specified in the authentication strategy in the Password text box, or enter the common project parameter corresponding to the password and enable Variable Value.
        

        

       Click Submit.

      

      

     If an API uses the basic authentication mode, upload the truststore certificate required by the HTTPS protocol.
      

      
       Go to the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Administration > Integration Service > Certificate Management.

       In the certificate list, click the certificate name corresponding to the truststore specified in the API authentication strategy. The Edit Certificate page is displayed.

       Set Alias for the certificate and set Type to Truststore.

       Click Add under Keystore File, upload the obtained certificate file, and set Password for the certificate.
        

        

       Click Confirm.

      

      

     (Optional) If an API uses the basic authentication mode, Two-way Authentication is enabled, and Use System Secret Key is disabled, upload the keystore certificate required for authentication.
      

      
       Go to the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Administration > Integration Service > Certificate Management.

       In the certificate list, click the certificate name corresponding to the keystore specified in the API authentication strategy. The Edit Certificate page is displayed.

       Set Alias for the certificate and set Type to Keystore.

       Click Add under Keystore File, upload the obtained certificate file, and set Password for the certificate.

       Click Confirm.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Developing an Outbound SOAP API

name: Debugging the Outbound SOAP API
title: Debugging the Outbound SOAP API
text:
Debugging the Outbound SOAP API
 
 
  
  

  
   After an outbound SOAP API is configured, you can debug the API to verify the configuration correctness.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     An outbound SOAP API has been configured.

     API configurations have been deployed in the runtime-state environment.

     The called external SOAP API is available.

    

   

   
    Context

    During API debugging, the debugging parameter format varies with the content type. Set parameters based on the actual definition in the API and the template loaded by the API.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     In the navigation pane, choose Outbound SOAP.

     In the API list, click Debug in the Operation column of the API to be debugged.

     On the debugging page, set parameters based on the automatically loaded parameter template.
      

      

      

      

     Click Execute.

     In the Response area, check whether the information on the Output tab page meets the expectation.
      

      
       If yes, the API functions properly.

       If not, click the Log tab to view debug logs, locate and analyze the API, rectify the fault, and debug the API again.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Developing an Outbound SOAP API

name: How Does the System Dynamically Transfers Parameters in an Outbound API URL?
title: How Does the System Dynamically Transfers Parameters in an Outbound API URL?
text:
How Does the System Dynamically Transfers Parameters in an Outbound API URL?
 
 
  
  

  
   You can reference the common project parameters or API input parameters in the service URL of an outbound API to enable the system to dynamically transfer parameters in the API URL.

   
    Context

    The system supports the function of referencing variables in the service URL of an outbound API to dynamically transfer parameters. The variables that can be referenced are classified into the following types:

    
     Common parameters: common project parameters obtained from the service URL. The format is ${Parameter name}.

     Path parameters: API input parameters whose Parameter Location is Path in the service URL. The format is {Parameter name}.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Reference common parameters in the service URL.
      

      
       Set the common parameters required in the service address by following instructions provided in Configuring Common Parameters for the Integration Service.

       In Service Address configured for an outbound API, use ${Parameter name} to reference common parameters.
        

        

      

      

     Reference path parameters in the service URL.
      

      
       In the Input Parameter area, set path parameters.

       In Service Address configured for an outbound API, use {Parameter name} to reference common parameters.
        

        

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: FAQs

name: How Do I Create a Truststore Certificate for HTTPS-based Outbound APIs?
title: How Do I Create a Truststore Certificate for HTTPS-based Outbound APIs?
text:
How Do I Create a Truststore Certificate for HTTPS-based Outbound APIs?
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to create a truststore certificate for HTTPS-based outbound APIs to prepare for the configuration of authentication strategies for outbound APIs.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have obtained the API URL provided by the third-party system.

     The JDK has been installed on the PC where a certificate is to be created.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Export the CA certificate of the third-party system.
      

      
       Use Google Chrome to open the API URL provided by the third-party system.

       Click  on the left of the address box and select Connection is secure.
        

        

       In the Security area, select Certificate is valid.
        

        

       In the Certificate Viewer dialog box, click the Details tab, click the CA certificate name, and click Export in the lower right corner.
        

        

       In the displayed Save As dialog box, select a directory for saving the certificate file and change the file name to xxxx.cer. Then, the certificate file of the third-party system is downloaded to the specified local directory. xxxx indicates the name of the certificate file.

      

      

     Convert the downloaded certificate to the needed truststore certificate.
      

      
       Go to the directory where the certificate file of the third-party system is downloaded and enter cmd in the address box to go to the CLI.

       Run the following command to convert the downloaded certificate to the needed truststore certificate:
        keytool -import -alias {Certificate alias} -file {Certificate file name obtained in 1.e}.cer -keystore {Name of the truststore certificate file to be generated}.keystore

        Enter the keystore password of the truststore certificate as prompted and enter Y when the message "Do you want to trust this certificate?" is displayed.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: FAQs

name: What Can I Do If the Message "config with https protocol but has no truststore" Is Displayed When an Outbound REST API Fails to Be Debugged?
title: What Can I Do If the Message "config with https protocol but has no truststore" Is Displayed When an Outbound REST API Fails to Be Debugged?
text:
What Can I Do If the Message "config with https protocol but has no truststore" Is Displayed When an Outbound REST API Fails to Be Debugged?
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Symptom

    During the debugging of an outbound REST API, the message "config with https protocol but has no truststore" is displayed.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The truststore certificate for the HTTPS protocol is not configured in the authentication strategy of the outbound REST API in the runtime-state environment.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Create a truststore certificate for the HTTPS protocol by referring to How Do I Create a Truststore Certificate for HTTPS-based Outbound APIs?

     Check the authentication strategy of the outbound REST API.
      

      
       Go to the develop-state environment and click the name of the project for the outbound REST API.

       In the navigation pane, choose Outbound REST.

       In the outbound REST API list, click the name of an outbound REST API. The Edit Outbound REST API page is displayed.

       Check the authentication strategy of the outbound REST API.
        For example, outrest_basic in Authentication Strategy shown in the following figure is the authentication strategy.

        

        

      

      

     Modify the authentication strategy configuration of the outbound REST API.
      

      
       Go to the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Administration > Integration Service > Outbound Strategy Management.

       In the outbound authentication strategy list, click the name of the authentication strategy. The Edit Outbound Strategy page is displayed.

       Click Edit on the right of Truststore.

       On the Edit Certificate page, set Alias to the alias of the truststore certificate file and Password to the keystore password after uploading the keystore file.
        

        

       Click Confirm.

      

      

     Debug the outbound REST API again.

name: What Can I Do If the Message "unable to find valid certification path to requested target" Is Displayed When an Outbound REST API Fails to Be Debugged?
title: What Can I Do If the Message "unable to find valid certification path to requested target" Is Displayed When an Outbound REST API Fails to Be Debugged?
text:
What Can I Do If the Message "unable to find valid certification path to requested target" Is Displayed When an Outbound REST API Fails to Be Debugged?
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Symptom

    During the debugging of an outbound REST API, the message "PKIX path building failed, unable to find valid certification path to requested target" is displayed.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The issuer of the external CER certificate file generated by the intranet browser is Huawei Web Secure Internet Gateway CA. As a result, the API certificate verification fails.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Go to the directory where a local file is stored and enter cmd in the address box to access the CLI.

     Run the following command to obtain the IP address corresponding to the API domain name provided by the third-party system:
      

      ping {API domain name provided by the third-party system}

      In the command output, obtain the corresponding IP address.

      

     Use a browser to open the search page and check whether the IP address obtained in 2 is an external IP address.
      

      
       Yes: Use the jump server on the public network or export the CER certificate from the external network, convert the CER certificate to a truststore certificate, and upload the truststore certificate to the outbound authentication strategy.

       No: Contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: FAQs
