name: Usage Overview
title: Usage Overview
text:
Usage Overview
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes the function restrictions and the content that you need to pay attention to when using the functions.

   
     
    
     With this development mode enabled by the API Fabric, developers can create asset programs that can run on the API Fabric app execution engine by simply dragging and dropping with simple JavaScript code. Due to orchestration flexibility, developers can run any custom code, which may cause malicious code execution risks. To better utilize this capability, the following requirements must be met:

     
      All developers must perform orchestration and development by strictly following the operations in section "Development Specifications" in API Fabric VXXXRXXXCXX Product Documentation (Customized Development). Malicious code in any form is prohibited, including but not limited to viruses, rogue software, Trojan horses, backdoors, listening programs, and mining programs.

      The system administrator must strictly review the development qualification of developers and assign permissions to developers who have obtained the asset development certification. Assigned permissions cannot be abused.

     

    

   

  

  
   
    General Restrictions
      This section describes the function restrictions and precautions that are not closely related to protocols.

    SOAP
      This section describes the special usage and restrictions of the SOAP protocol in the API Fabric.

   

   
    
     Parent topic: Develop-State API Fabric Usage Guide

name: General Restrictions
title: General Restrictions
text:
General Restrictions
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes the function restrictions and precautions that are not closely related to protocols.

   
    Common Process

    Pay attention to the following restrictions when common processes are used in API orchestration:

    
     If input or output parameters of the common process to be called by an API are changed, the API Fabric does not automatically update process variables of the API. You need to manually update the process variables.

     A common process can be called by an API only once.
      To call common processes for multiple times, you are advised to define different common processes. If a common process must be called multiple times, service personnel need to modify sub-process data cached when an API calls the common process upon recall of the common process.

    

   

   
    API Version

    The developed API does not distinguish the version number. The version number displayed after the API is deployed in the runtime state is meaningless.

   

   
    API Update

    
     For the added REST-based northbound APIs:
      
       After the method name or resource (path) of the API is modified, the policy configuration and orchestration information of the API remains unchanged.
        As shown in the following figure, modifying the method name POST, the method resource, or both does not affect the original policy configuration and orchestration information.

        

        

       With different operations using the same resource, modifying the resource of one operation does not affect the others.

      

     For APIs using protocols other than REST, modifying the URL of a method is treated as creating an API. In this case, you need to orchestrate the process and configure policies for the API again.
      For example, in SOAP, changing the method name in API Design is considered as a URL change.

    

    
     For APIs using all protocols, modifying the following parameters in the endpoint description file associated with an API and updating parameter settings on the Develop API are treated as creating an API. In this case, you need to orchestrate the process and configure policies for the API again.
      
       REST: Change the value of paths.

       SOAP: Change the value of name of operation.

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Usage Overview

name: SOAP
title: SOAP
text:
SOAP
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes the special usage and restrictions of the SOAP protocol in the API Fabric.

  

  
   
    mustUnderstand Subelement Is Not Verified
      The API Fabric does not verify the mustUnderstand subelement contained in the SOAP header and processes the subelement as a normal packet.

    Packets with the multiRef Tag Cannot Be Parsed
      The API Fabric uses Axis2, and multiRef is the tag of Axis1. Therefore, the tag cannot be parsed.

    Packets in XOP Format Are Not Supported
      The southbound and northbound services do not support packets in XML-binary Optimized Packaging (XOP) format. Do not use packets in XOP format to call APIs.

    Attachments Cannot Be Transferred
      Attachments cannot be transferred in the southbound and northbound services during API calling.

    Prefix of the Packet Namespace Cannot Be Modified
      For northbound response and southbound request packets, the namespace prefix in the packets cannot be modified.

    any Element Cannot Be Defined in the XSD File
      If the any element is defined in the XSD file, the element will be lost after being parsed by the API Fabric.

    duration Data Type Cannot Be Defined in the XSD File of the Southbound Service
      If the XSD file of the southbound service contains the definition of the duration data type, data will be lost when data is sent back to the northbound service through the API Fabric.

    Namespace Defined in the WSDL File Cannot End with type
      For the SOAP protocol, the namespace defined in the WSDL file cannot end with type. Otherwise, the compilation fails.

    Header Format in a Northbound Request Must Be the Same As That Defined in the WSDL File
      When a northbound request of the SOAP protocol is sent to the API Fabric, the node names and node quantity of the SOAP header in the request must be the same as those defined in the WSDL file.

    Fault Element Can Be Returned to the Northbound Client
      The API Fabric cannot properly parse the value of Fault returned by the southbound service. You can customize a JavaScript script in the exception diagram element to return the value of Fault in the SOAP packet to the northbound client.

    HTML Entities in the CDATA Section Can Be Restored
      HTML entities in southbound requests can be restored by adding JavaScript to the diagram element script executed at any time during flow orchestration.

    Values Can Be Assigned to Element Attributes in Packets During Flow Orchestration
      If you want to assign values to element attributes in northbound responses or southbound requests during flow orchestration, you can use mapping during flow orchestration.

   

   
    
     Parent topic: Usage Overview

name: mustUnderstand Subelement Is Not Verified
title: mustUnderstand Subelement Is Not Verified
text:
mustUnderstand Subelement Is Not Verified
 
 
  
  

  
   The API Fabric does not verify the mustUnderstand subelement contained in the SOAP header and processes the subelement as a normal packet.

   
    Overview

    The optional subelement mustUnderstand in the SOAP header indicates whether the server verifies the SOAP header. The API Fabric functions as the gateway only to process and forward requests or impacts. Therefore, the API Fabric does not identify mustUnderstand. That is, the API Fabric processes the request normally no matter whether the SOAP header contains mustUnderstand.

   

   
    Examples

    
     The following is an example of a packet with mustUnderstand:
     <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-16"?>
<s:Envelope xmlns:s="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
    <s:Header>
        <Action s:mustUnderstand="1" xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2005/05/addressing/none">GetSubscriberOverviewForESP</Action>
    </s:Header>
    <s:Body xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema">
    </s:Body>
</s:Envelope>
    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: SOAP

name: Packets with the multiRef Tag Cannot Be Parsed
title: Packets with the multiRef Tag Cannot Be Parsed
text:
Packets with the multiRef Tag Cannot Be Parsed
 
 
  
  

  
   The API Fabric uses Axis2, and multiRef is the tag of Axis1. Therefore, the tag cannot be parsed.

   If a packet contains the multiRef tag, the packet format is abnormal. Do not pass packets with the multiRef tag during API calling of the API Fabric.

   
    Examples

    
     The following is an example of a packet segment with the multiRef tag:
     <?xml version='1.0' encoding='utf-8'?>
<soapenv:Envelope
    xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
    <soapenv:Header/>
    <soapenv:Body>
        <ns1:vRBTAddCallerGroupMemResponse
            xmlns:ns1="http://impl.prbt.cmcc.com" soapenv:encodingStyle="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/">
            <vRBTAddCallerGroupMemReturn
                xmlns:soapenc="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/"
                xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" soapenc:root="0" soapenv:encodingStyle="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/" xsi:type="ns2:VRBTAddCallerGroupMemResp">
                <memberResult soapenc:arrayType="ns2:MemberResult[1]" xsi:type="soapenc:Array">
                    <MemberResult soapenc:root="0" soapenv:encodingStyle="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/" xsi:type="ns3:MemberResult">
                        <MSISDN xsi:type="soapenc:string">135XXXXXXXX</MSISDN>
                        <description xsi:type="soapenc:string">1111111</description>
                        <result xsi:type="soapenc:string">000000</result>
                    </MemberResult>
                </memberResult>
                <description xsi:type="soapenc:string">111111</description>
                <returnCode xsi:type="soapenc:string">000000</returnCode>
            </vRBTAddCallerGroupMemReturn>
        </ns1:vRBTAddCallerGroupMemResponse>
        <multiRef
            xmlns:soapenc="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/"
            xmlns:ns2="http://schemas.prbt.cmcc.com"
            xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" id="id0" soapenc:root="0" soapenv:encodingStyle="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/" xsi:type="ns2:VRBTAddCallerGroupMemResp">
            <memberResult soapenc:arrayType="ns2:MemberResult[1]" xsi:type="soapenc:Array">
                <memberResult href="#id1"/></memberResult>
            <description xsi:type="soapenc:string">111111</description>
            <returnCode xsi:type="soapenc:string">000000</returnCode>
        </multiRef>
    </soapenv:Body>
</soapenv:Envelope>
    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: SOAP

name: Packets in XOP Format Are Not Supported
title: Packets in XOP Format Are Not Supported
text:
Packets in XOP Format Are Not Supported
 
 
  
  

  
   The southbound and northbound services do not support packets in XML-binary Optimized Packaging (XOP) format. Do not use packets in XOP format to call APIs.

   
    Examples

    
     The following is an example of a packet in XOP format:
     POST /test HTTP/1.0
Content-Type: Multipart/Related; boundary=MIME_boundary; type=text/xml
Content-Length: XXXX
SOAPAction: http://www.soapattach.com/test
 
--MIME_boundary
 
Content-Type: text/xml; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit
 
<?xml version='1.0'?>
<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
 <soap:Body>
 <Car name="myCar">
<Picture>
< xbinc:Include href = "cid:*******"/>
</Picture>
 </Car>
 </soap:Body>
</soap:Envelope>
 
--MIME_boundary
Content-Type: image/jpeg
Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary
Content-ID: <*******>
...1010100010101011011101010100101110101001001010101010101011...
--MIME_boundary—

text:
Prefix of the Packet Namespace Cannot Be Modified
 
 
  
  

  
   For northbound response and southbound request packets, the namespace prefix in the packets cannot be modified.

   
    Overview

    The prefix of the namespace in the packet is calculated using an algorithm based on the URL of the namespace defined in the WSDL file. The API Fabric cannot intervene and can pass the packet only based on the prefix calculated using the algorithm.

    
     For example, in the following packet segment, http://www.aa.com/servers/samples/javaclass is the complete namespace address, and jav is the namespace prefix computed by the algorithm and cannot be modified.
     <jav:aa xmlns:jav="http://www.aa.com/servers/samples/javaclass">
    

   

   
    Examples

    
     The following is an example of a namespace in a packet segment:
     <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
    <soapenv:Header/>
    <soapenv:Body>
        <jav:aa xmlns:jav="http://www.aa.com/servers/samples/javaclass">
            <string>111</string>
        </jav:aa>
    </soapenv:Body>
</soapenv:Envelope>
    

   

   
    Namespace Prefix Generation Algorithm

    
     The API Fabric complies with the following algorithm for generating namespace prefixes:
     
      You need to check whether the input namespace URI already exists in the namespace mapping table. If it exists, use the existing prefix name.
       The namespace mapping table is as follows.

       
        
         
          Table 1 Namespace mappings
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Namespace URI

           
            Prefix

          

         
         
          
           
            http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace

           
            xml

          

          
           
            http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema

           
            xs

          

          
           
            http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance

           
            xsi

          

          
           
            http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/wsdl/

           
            wsdl

          

          
           
            http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/

           
            soapenc

          

          
           
            http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

           
            soapenv

          

         
        
       

      If the prefix does not exist, a new prefix is automatically generated.
       
        The rules for generating a new prefix are as follows:
        
         If an URI ends with /, delete the last /.

         Obtain the character string following the last / in the remaining URI. If the character string starts with www., delete www.

         Calculate the length of the remaining character string. Only letters and digits are counted.
          
           Check whether the characters in the character string are in the Unicode set one by one according to the following rules. If a character is in the set, the character string length is incremented by 1. Otherwise, the character is not counted in the length.
           
            If the character is a colon (:), it is not counted in the length because the colon can only be used to separate the namespace prefix from the local name.

            If the character is an underscore (_) or a letter, the character is counted in the length.

            If the character is a Unicode character and its category is letter L, mark M, or connector Pc, the character is counted in the length. If its category is none of the preceding ones, the character is not counted in the length.

           

          

         Generate a prefix based on the length of a character string.
          
           The prefix generation rules are as follows:
           
            If the character string starts with xml and the length of the character string is greater than 4, use x{Fourth character} as the prefix. Otherwise, use the default value ns as the prefix.

            If the length of the character string is greater than 4, the third character is a vowel, and the fourth character is not a vowel, the first four characters are used as the prefix. Otherwise, the first three characters are used as the prefix.

            If the length of the character string is less than or equal to 4, the remaining characters are used as the prefix. If the length is 0, ns is used as the prefix by default.

           

          

        

       

     

    

   

   The following table lists examples of common namespace prefix generation.

   
    
     
      Table 2 Examples of namespace prefix generation
     
     
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Namespace URI

       
        Prefix Automatically Generated by the Algorithm

      

     
     
      
       
        www.schemas.xmlsoap.org/www.ab/

       
        ab

        
         The determination process is as follows:
         
          Ensure that the URI is not in the mapping table.

          Delete the last /.

          Obtain the www.ab character string following the last / in the remaining part.

          Delete www. and calculate the length of the ab character string.
           In this example, the characters are both letters. Therefore, the length is 2.

          Generate the prefix ab based on rules.
           Because the length is less than or equal to 4 and the character string does not start with xml, ab is directly used as the prefix.

         

        

      

      
       
        www.schemas.xmlsoap.org/xml.abc/

       
        x.

        
         The determination process is as follows:
         
          Ensure that the URI is not in the mapping table.

          Delete the last /.

          Obtain the xml.abc character string following the last / in the remaining part.

          Calculate the length of the xml.abc character string.
           In this example, . is not a letter or digit and is not counted in the length. Therefore, the length is 6.

          Generate the prefix x. based on rules.
           Because the character string starts with xml and the length is greater than 4, x and the fourth character . are used together as the prefix.

         

        

      

      
       
        www.schemas.xmlsoap.org/xml

       
        ns

        
         The determination process is as follows:
         
          Ensure that the URI is not in the mapping table.

          Obtain the xml character string following the last / in the remaining part.

          Calculate the length of the xml character string.
           In this example, the characters are all letters. Therefore, the length is 3.

          Generate the prefix ns based on rules.
           Because the character string starts with xml and the length is less than 4, ns is used as the prefix by default.

         

        

      

      
       
        www.schemas.xmlsoap.org/abcde

       
        abc

        
         The determination process is as follows:
         
          Ensure that the URI is not in the mapping table.

          Obtain the abcde character string following the last / in the remaining part.

          Calculate the length of the abcde character string.
           In this example, the characters are all letters. Therefore, the length is 5.

          Generate the prefix abc based on rules.
           Because the length is greater than 4 and the third character c is not a vowel, the first three characters abc are used as the prefix.

         

        

      

      
       
        www.schemas.xmlsoap.org/abade

       
        abad

        
         The determination process is as follows:
         
          Ensure that the URI is not in the mapping table.

          Obtain the abade character string following the last / in the remaining part.

          Calculate the length of the abade character string.
           In this example, the characters are all letters. Therefore, the length is 5.

          Generate the prefix abad based on rules.
           Because the length is greater than 4, the third character a is a vowel, and the fourth character d is not a vowel, the first four characters abad are used as the prefix.

         

        

      

      
       
        www.schemas.xmlsoap.org/abaae

       
        aba

        
         The determination process is as follows:
         
          Ensure that the URI is not in the mapping table.

          Obtain the abaae character string following the last / in the remaining part.

          Calculate the length of the abaae character string.
           In this example, the characters are all letters. Therefore, the length is 5.

          Generate the prefix aba based on rules.
           Because the length is greater than 4, and both of the third character a and the fourth character a are vowels, the first three characters aba are used as the prefix.

         

        

      

     
    
   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: SOAP

name: any Element Cannot Be Defined in the XSD File
title: any Element Cannot Be Defined in the XSD File
text:
any Element Cannot Be Defined in the XSD File
 
 
  
  

  
   If the any element is defined in the XSD file, the element will be lost after being parsed by the API Fabric.

   
    Overview

    The following figure shows an example of the packet segment in the XSD file, in which the any element is defined and two simple elements balance and type are defined in the extension complex structure.

    

    The Axis2 does not support the use of the any element in the class file compiled by the WSDL. As a result, the API Fabric cannot obtain the content of the any element during object conversion based on the aar, and the balance and type elements are lost after the XSD is parsed into the MessageObject.

   

   
    Workaround

    You can use either of the following methods:

    
     Use the bypass capability.
      The API Fabric supports complete bypass and retains the authentication capability. In this case, the API Fabric does not parse packets. This problem can be avoided.

     Replace the any element in the XSD.
      Replace the any element with a specific element. In this case, all possible element types in the packet need to be enumerated.

    

   

   
    Examples

    
     The following packet segment indicates the declaration of a person element. Through the any element, the content of person can be extended after <last> through any element.
     <xs:element name="person">
  <xs:complexType>
    <xs:sequence>
      <xs:element name="first" type="xs:string"/>
      <xs:element name="last" type="xs:string"/>
      <xs:any minOccurs="0"/>
    </xs:sequence>
  </xs:complexType>
</xs:element>
    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: SOAP

name: duration Data Type Cannot Be Defined in the XSD File of the Southbound Service
title: duration Data Type Cannot Be Defined in the XSD File of the Southbound Service
text:
duration Data Type Cannot Be Defined in the XSD File of the Southbound Service
 
 
  
  

  
   If the XSD file of the southbound service contains the definition of the duration data type, data will be lost when data is sent back to the northbound service through the API Fabric.

   
    Overview

    In the API Fabric, the duration data type is processed by the org.apache.xmlbeans.GDuration open-source class. In the class, the field attribute is inconsistent with the names of the corresponding get and set methods. As a result, data is lost when the API Fabric receives southbound packets and converts them into MO messages, and the constructor of org.apache.xmlbeans.GDuration is called to generate a value of PT0S when the value is sent back to the northbound service.

   

   
    Examples

    
     The following is an example of the duration data type declaration in the XSD file:
     <xs:element name="period" type="xs:duration"/>
    

    
     The following is an example of elements indicating a one-year period in the document:
     <period>P1Y</period>

Namespace Defined in the WSDL File Cannot End with type
 
 
  
  

  
   For the SOAP protocol, the namespace defined in the WSDL file cannot end with type. Otherwise, the compilation fails.

   
    Overview

    If the namespace defined in the WSDL file cannot end with type during API development, type is regarded as a variable of the Java class when the WSDL file is compiled into a JAR package. As a result, the compilation fails.

name: Header Format in a Northbound Request Must Be the Same As That Defined in the WSDL File
title: Header Format in a Northbound Request Must Be the Same As That Defined in the WSDL File
text:
Header Format in a Northbound Request Must Be the Same As That Defined in the WSDL File
 
 
  
  

  
   When a northbound request of the SOAP protocol is sent to the API Fabric, the node names and node quantity of the SOAP header in the request must be the same as those defined in the WSDL file.

   
    Overview

    In some scenarios, the SOAP header defined in the WSDL file contains multiple nodes. In this case, when the client sends a request to the API Fabric, if the node names and node quantity of the SOAP header in the request packet are different from those defined in the WSDL file, the Apache Axis2/Java open-source framework determines that the verification fails.

   

   
    Examples

    
     For example, if the following WSDL definition example contains the TransactionList and ErrorList nodes, the header of the request must contain the two nodes.
     <soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:env="http://xmlns.kpn.com/mobile/m2c/cdm/sml/envelope.1" xmlns:req="http://xmlns.kpn.com/mobile/m2c/cdm/requestporting.1request.xsd">
   <soapenv:Header>
      <env:TransactionList>
         <env:Transaction>
            <env:Interaction>Ah</env:Interaction>
            <env:TransactionId>Ai</env:TransactionId>
            <env:SystemId>S32</env:SystemId>
            <env:MessageId>Aj</env:MessageId>
            <env:Timestamp>2015-01-01T00:00:00.000Z</env:Timestamp>
         </env:Transaction>
      </env:TransactionList>
      <env:ErrorList>
         <env:Error>
            <env:Code>S29</env:Code>
            <env:Reason>Aa</env:Reason>
            <env:Service>
               <env:Paradigm>Ab</env:Paradigm>
               <env:Name>Ac</env:Name>
            </env:Service>
         </env:Error>
      </env:ErrorList>
   </soapenv:Header>
   <soapenv:Body>
      <req:Request>
         <req:EXTERNAL_ORDER_REF>S00</req:EXTERNAL_ORDER_REF>
         <req:PORTING_ORDER>
            <req:ID_OLO>AB</req:ID_OLO>
      </req:Request>
   </soapenv:Body>
</soapenv:Envelope>

name: HTML Entities in the CDATA Section Can Be Restored
title: HTML Entities in the CDATA Section Can Be Restored
text:
HTML Entities in the CDATA Section Can Be Restored
 
 
  
  

  
   HTML entities in southbound requests can be restored by adding JavaScript to the diagram element script executed at any time during flow orchestration.

   
    Overview

    The HTML entities in the SOAP southbound request packet may be escaped. If you do not want to escape the HTML entity, you can restore the HTML entities in the packet.

    Entities that support escape include <, >, and &.

   

   
    Examples

    
     The packet containing the HTML entities that support escape is as follows:
     <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
    <soapenv:Header/>
    <soapenv:Body>
        <jav:aa xmlns:jav="http://www.aa.com/servers/samples/javaclass">
            <string><![CDATA[
                <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><bb><PASSWORD>1234</PASSWORD><cc>TEM</cc><dd>10</dd><ee>123</ee><ff>200303</ff><gg>00</gg></bb>
            ]]></string>
        </jav:aa>
    </soapenv:Body>
</soapenv:Envelope>
    

   

   
    JavaScript Example

    
     During API development, add the following JavaScript to the diagram element script that is executed at any time during flow orchestration:
     (function(){
 var context = getBinding()[""_bpmnContext""];
 context.unescapeMessage= true;
 return true;
 })();
    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: SOAP

name: Design API
title: Design API
text:
Design API
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Function Description

    As an auxiliary tool for SA survey, the API Investigator generates an API definition file or exports an API document based on the original definition file or API document provided at the site.

   

   
    Usage Scenarios

    When conducting API survey by SAs onsite, API definition documents are missing, or content of API definition documents is in disrepair and inaccurate, which incurs issues such as heavy workload, low survey accuracy, and no API instantiation data.

    The API Investigator can automatically calibrate API documents and generate correct API documents based on the API packets and definition files on the real network.

    

   

  

  
   
    Adding APIs
      This section describes how to add APIs in the system, including defining the API names, versions, and protocols, before API investigation.

    Defining APIs
      This section describes how to define APIs based on different protocol types.

    Comparing APIs
      You can use the API comparison function to compare API definition files. The system automatically marks the differences between two API definition files.

    Adding a Common Definition of Northbound APIs
      On the Common Definition tab page, you can define common configuration for all APIs or northbound services, including common structures and common error codes.

   

   
    
     Parent topic: Develop-State API Fabric Usage Guide

name: Adding APIs
title: Adding APIs
text:
Adding APIs
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to add APIs in the system, including defining the API names, versions, and protocols, before API investigation.

   
    Context

    The tool supports the following methods of adding APIs:

    
     Manually creating a single API

     Copying an existing API in the system

     Importing APIs

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required.

     Click Create on the Design API page.
      

      On the Basic Information page, set API parameters as prompted. Parameters vary depending on the protocol. You need to set parameters based on site requirements.

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           API Name

          
           API name, which can be customized.

         

         
          
           API Type

           

          
           API protocol type. You can select a protocol as required.

           
            Rest
             
              Protocol specification. Swagger 2.0 and OpenAPI 3.0 are supported.

              Basic path, which must start with /.

             

            SOAP
             Custom basic path, which must start with /.

            TCP+XML

            RabbitMQ
             
              Vhost: Multiple vhosts can be created in a broker to separate the permissions of different users. An example format is /vhost.

              Exchange: A message exchange under a vhost. The exchange specifies the rules according to which messages are routed to different queues.

             

            JetMQ

            ActiveMQ

            EXTJMSMQ

           

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Next. The Parameter Definition page is displayed.
      

      The operations vary according to the protocols. For details, see REST, SOAP, TCP+XML, and RabbitMQ.

      
        
       
        The API name must be unique in the system (in all projects and catalogs). If an API fails to be added, change the API name or version number.

       

      

      

    

    
     Click Next to go to the Done page.
      

      Select the type of the API to be generated as required. The options are as follows:

      
       Generate a Northbound API: APIs that are exposed to other services through the API Fabric.

       Generate a public endpoint: APIs and service addresses provided by the actual service providers for external systems.
        
          
         
          If the endpoint description file cannot be obtained and the endpoint cannot be directly imported to the API Fabric, you can use this method to generate an endpoint.

         

        

       One-click transparent transmission API: APIs that forward service requests only through the API Fabric.
        For a transparent transmission API, the API Fabric directly generates an endpoint that is the same as the definition of the transparent transmission API, and completes 1V1 mapping between the API and the method in the endpoint. Except the parameters in the path position, other request parameters are not mapped or verified, and client parameters are transparently transmitted to the server.

      

      

     Click Done.

title: SOAP
text:
SOAP
 
 
  
  

  
   After an API is added, you can import the existing API definition files or manually define APIs for API design.

   
    Restrictions and Description

    
     You can choose More > API Definition File Management next to the API to import or add a definition file. If a definition file already exists, you cannot add a definition file.

     You can import WSDL and ZIP files. The size of a WSDL file (including an XSD file) cannot exceed 5 MB.

     For details about special usages and restrictions of the SOAP protocol in the API Fabric, see SOAP.

     Currently, the API Fabric can parse the following SOAP media types:
      
       text/xml

       application/soap+xml

      

    

   

   
    Prerequisites

    
     The operations in Adding APIs have been performed.

     The API design details page is displayed, as shown in the following figure.
      The details page is displayed after an API is created, or you can click a target API in the API list to go to the details page.

      

      

    

   

   
    Context

    
     On the API design details page, you can add, delete, or modify a global or single schema namespace. For details, see Table 1. 
      
       
       
        
         Table 1 Namespace configuration description
        
        
         
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Configuration Name

          
           Scope

          
           Procedure

         

        
        
         
          
           Global namespace

          
           
            Global namespace.
             Namespace of the current WSDL file.

            Namespace of the application in the WSDL file of the API.

            Open-source namespace.

           

          
           
            Click the Namespace tab on the Parameter Definition page, click Add.

            On the Namespace tab page, perform operations (including addition, deletion, and modification) by scenario.

            Click Save.

           

         

         
          
           Namespace of a single schema

          
           
            Namespace of another schema referenced by the current schema.

            Namespace referenced by elements in the current schema.

           

          
           
            Import the API definition file or create the API definition.
             Go to the API design details page.

            Click the corresponding schema under the structure.

            On the Namespace tab page, click Add and set parameters (add, delete, or modify) based on site requirements.
             For details, see the following figure.

             

             

            Click Save.

           

         

        
       
      

     In most cases, the drop-down list on the API design details page is designed with the filtering function. To select a parameter of a non-default type, delete the default type from the drop-down list, and enter the value of Type, as shown in Figure 1.
      
       Figure 1 Drop-down list with the filtering function
       
      

      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the add button next to Method.
      

      The default operation name is NewOperation. You can change the operation name next to Method in the Basic Information area.

      Configure data by scenario on the method details page, and click Save.

      

     Edit the parameters in the method.
      

      
        
       
        After the editing, ensure that the parameters are complete and valid. Otherwise, the parsing fails because the WSDL file is invalid, and the parameters on the method details page are displayed incompletely.

       

      

      On the API details page, click an operation name under Method. On the method details page, you can configure information such as request parameters, response parameters, error response parameters, and error codes. For details, see Table 2.

      
       
       
        
         Table 2 Configuration items
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Request Parameter

          
           Input parameter in a request.

         

         
          
           Response Parameter

          
           Output parameter in a response.

         

         
          
           Error Response Parameter

          
           Output parameter in an error response.

           
             NOTICE: 
            
             This function is not supported currently.

            

           

         

        
       
      

      

     (Optional) Configure the structure.
      

      
       The parameter type of a method can reference the elements and complex types defined in the structure.
       
        Click the add button next to Structure.

        On the API details page, click the operation name under Structure and configure the namespace, element, and complex type parameters based on the API design.
         The naming rule of Structure is @+{Currently targetNamespace declared in Structure}.

         
           
          
           When a structure with the same name is added and saved, the original structure is overwritten by the new one.

          

         

        (Optional) Edit parameters in the XSD file.
         Click a schema under Structure on the API details page to modify the XSD file namespace and XSD elements. The parameters on the schema details page comply with the XSD specifications.

name: REST
title: REST
text:
REST
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Restrictions

    
     Currently, the API Fabric supports the following media types configured for the REST protocol. The application/octet-stream type does not support commissioning or mocker.
      
        
       
        
         When the media type application/octet-stream is used to download files, you can change the file size by configuring access_max_req_size and access_max_resq_size during installation.

         After the installation, text/event-stream can be used only after sse_switch is set to YES by upgrading the stack. If sse_switch is not set, text/event-stream is disabled by default. The streaming API function can be used only when the APIF LB service is interconnected.

        

       

      

      
       application/json

       application/xml

       application/x-www-form-urlencoded

       multipart/form-data

       application/octet-stream

      

      
       text/event-stream (selected only when the REST Swagger 2.0 response type is configured)

      

    

   

   
    When the REST request or response parameters contain ., the API mapping cannot be saved during orchestration.

    In the CSE scenario, the API Fabric supports file upload and download through REST Swagger 2.0 APIs. The restrictions on requests are as follows:
     
      When configuring an API, ensure that the request parameters are different from the parameters in the method.
       For example, if the POST /request method has been configured, the request parameter cannot be configured for any field (such as body, header, query, and path) in the request parameters.

      When configuring an API, ensure that body, header, query, and path fields in the request parameters do not contain duplicate keys.
       For example, if the name parameter has been configured for body, the same parameter cannot be configured for header, query, and path.

     

    When RESTful APIs are used to interconnect with the file server for large file transfer, the following restrictions apply:
     
      Only transparent transmission APIs are supported.

      Interconnecting with the File Server can be configured only when Media Type/Referenced Parameter is set to multipart/form-data or application/octet-stream.

      The large file upload and download capabilities are available only when Connect to Media Type/Referenced Parameter of Media Type/Referenced Parameter is enabled. OpenAPI 3.0 needs to be enabled during method configuration.
       

       

      The maximum validity period of a fileToken is 24 hours. When the fileToken is used to download files from the file server, if multiple files exist on the server, the first file is downloaded by default.

      When the media type is application/octet-stream, if multiple keys corresponding to fileTokens are configured in the request body or response body, the first key value in the definition file is obtained by default.

      When the media type is application/octet-stream, the request header or response header must contain content-disposition:attachment; filename=File name. Otherwise, data fails to be obtained.

      When transferring a large file, you need to configure parameters in the request body or response body to receive the file or fileToken. The following table describes the restrictions. 
       
        
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Scenario

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Scenario 1: Uploading a file using an inbound API.

           
            
             When the request media type is multipart/form-data, the request body must be set to form-data.
              The request body parameter type must be set to file. You do not need to set the request body parameters. The system automatically identifies them.

              

              

             When the media type is application/octet-stream, the parameters in the body must be set to string.
              The parameters in the body are optional. If they are configured, the parameter type must be set to string. If the parameters are not configured, the system uses the request body parameter named fileTokenKey to transfer the fileToken by default.

              

              

            

          

          
           
            Scenario 2: Downloading a file using an inbound API

           
            When the response media type is application/octet-stream, the response body must be set to octet-stream.

            The parameters in the body are optional. If they are configured, the parameter type must be set to string.

            

            

          

          
           
            Scenario 3: Uploading a file using an outbound API

           
            
             When the request media type is multipart/form-data, the request body must be set to form-data.
              The request body parameter type must be set to file.

              

              

             When the media type is application/octet-stream, the parameters in the body must be set to string.
              

              

            

          

          
           
            Scenario 4: Downloading a file using an outbound API

           
            When the response media type is application/octet-stream, the response body must be set to octet-stream.

            The parameters in the body are optional. If they are configured, the parameter type must be set to string. If the parameters are not configured, the system uses the request body parameter named fileTokenKey to transfer the fileToken by default.

   The configuration item is used to centrally manage the parameter structures that are referenced across APIs in the northbound API definition. The common structures defined in the Investigator tool and Builder tool can be shared. A common structure is included when the API that references the common structure is exported.

   
    Procedure

        The REST API described in the tool is based on the Swagger 2.0 framework and OpenAPI specifications (for details, see https://swagger.io/specification/). The parameters and data structures defined on the page must meet the specifications.

       Click Save.

      

      

    

   

   
    Usage Instruction

    The defined common structure is directly selected during API definition. You can select NormalStruct or HeaderStruct.

    For example, the common structure shown in Figure 2 is defined on the Common Structure page. In the API Definition structure of the API management, the parameter type can be set to NormalStruct, as shown in Figure 3.

name: Develop API
title: Develop API
text:
Develop API
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Function Description

    API Builder is a tool that can develop APIs online using scripts and graphs. It allows API providers to develop APIs through GUI configuration and scripts, reducing technical barriers and improving development efficiency.

   

   
    Usage Scenarios

    In most scenarios, northbound APIs and southbound APIs use different protocols and cannot connect to each other. The API Builder can convert southbound and northbound protocols to achieve fast interconnection and adaptation to the third-party systems.

    The API Builder opens the suite baseline customization capability, supports graph-based or script-based API customization and orchestration, and provides sandbox and baseline APIs to assist DSVs in independent customization and delivery.

   

   
    Development Experience Requirements

    Ensure that developers meet the following requirements:

    
     Master basic JavaScript programming methods.

     Know Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN).

     Be familiar with API protocols (SOAP/REST).

    

   

   
    Procedure

    The procedure on the API Builder is as follows:

    
     Add a northbound API.
      Add northbound APIs called by third-party systems. After the APIs are added, API definitions can be displayed or modified, processes can be orchestrated, policies can be configured, and configuration can be extended. For details, see Configuring APIs.

     Add the southbound service.
      Configure a southbound service using the endpoint management function. The service name is used as a unique ID. For details, see Configuring Endpoints.

     (Optional) Add common configurations.
      Define common configurations for all APIs or southbound services on the Common Definition tab page. The following information is included: variable definition, dictionary value mapping, key management, user group management, common function, and common structure. For details, see Adding a Common Definition of an API or Endpoint.

    

   

  

  
   
    Configuring APIs
      This function is used to manage northbound APIs. Northbound APIs or APIs refer to APIs provided by the API Fabric for third-party systems to call.

    Configuring Endpoints
      Endpoint management is used to manage southbound services in a unified manner. The service name is used as a unique identifier.

    Configuring a Timer for the API Fabric

    Adding a Common Definition of an API or Endpoint

    Deploying and Commissioning APIs

    Importing or Exporting an API

   These APIs can be managed and customized, such as configuring policies, referencing southbound services, and orchestrating processes. In addition, this function is used to convert protocols used for southbound and northbound APIs to solve the problem that the northbound and southbound APIs in the real service system cannot be interconnected because they use different protocols. Quick customization can be implemented for baseline APIs.

  

  
   
    Adding an API

    Generating a Northbound ISO8583 Definition File
      The develop-state API Fabric supports the function of generating APIs by importing ISO8583 definition files and configuring policies on the page.

    Orchestrating APIs
      The API Fabric supports graphical orchestration. You can adjust the diagram element structure and configure diagram element data for orchestration.

    Configuring API Policies
      This section describes how to configure API-level policies and sensitive logs.

    API Registration

text:
Adding an API
 
 
  
  

  
   Add APIs called by third-party systems. After the APIs are added, API definitions can be displayed or modified, processes can be orchestrated, and policies can be configured.

   You can add the API manually or by importing an API definition file in ZIP format. The ZIP file for adding the API must be exported from the API Builder.

   
    Context

    The protocols supported for manual adding and adding by ZIP file import are different.

    
     Manual adding
      
       APIs of custom protocols can be added using the API Designer.
       
        REST

        RabbitMQ
         RabbitMQ is a northbound protocol and does not support endpoint management configuration.

       

      

     Adding an API by importing existing files
      
       SOAP

       REST
        One or more XSD files (except a single YAML file) can be directly imported. (Multiple XSD files need to be compressed into a ZIP package.)

      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop API.

     Add an API.

Variable fields, such as global variables, request fields, and response fields, are set by configuring process variables and transferred to endpoints by orchestrating diagram elements.

After the configuration is complete, click the API name on the Develop API page. On the Basic Information page, click More and modify this parameter in Service System.

title: Orchestrating APIs
text:
Orchestrating APIs
 
 
  
  

  
   The API Fabric supports graphical orchestration. You can adjust the diagram element structure and configure diagram element data for orchestration.

   Methods in API definition can be orchestrated or bypassed, and the orchestration mode is used by default.

   
     
    
     After the structure information is defined on the Design API page, when you click an API name on the Develop API page to access the Process Orchestration page, the API for querying the structure data is called. The API data is cached on the frontend and is automatically cleared when you exit the orchestration page. When you switch the method on the orchestration page, the cache always takes effect.

     If both the Design API and Process Orchestration pages are opened, the original data is still displayed on the Process Orchestration page when the structure data is modified on the Design API page. You need to save the orchestrated content and access the orchestration page again to view the new data.

     After the structure data is updated, you need to manually modify the value assignment information reserved for previous orchestration. Otherwise, subsequent orchestration and connection will be affected.

    

   

   
    Prerequisites

    
     An API has been added.

     You have accessed the Process Orchestration tab page.
      After adding an API or clicking an added API on the Develop API page, the Process Orchestration tab page is displayed by default.

    

   

  

  
   
    Orchestration
      API graphical or script-based orchestration can be performed.

    Bypass
      The API Fabric supports the bypass mode.

    Proxy Mode
      If an API to be developed uses only one endpoint, the proxy mode can be used. This mode supports only REST and SOAP. The proxy mode does not support orchestration. You can use Groovy to perform a simple parameter mapping.

    CSE Mode
      The CSE mode is a special proxy mode. Only outbound APIs are supported in this mode. In the outbound scenario, you can select the proxy mode or the CSE mode.

    Process Orchestration Examples
      This section provides an example of process orchestration.

name: Orchestration
title: Orchestration
text:
Orchestration
 
 
  
  

  
   API graphical or script-based orchestration can be performed.

   The service type of the route is BPM or script. The BPMN definition is generated by graphical or script-based orchestration.

   The orchestration mode can also map data. In addition to the source, destination, and variable definition of requests and responses, the mapping line supports script logic and provides auxiliary functions.

   
    Procedure

    An API method can call one or more southbound services.

    The process orchestration complies with BPMN 2.0 specifications. For details about the diagram elements, see Diagram Elements.

    
     Select the method to be orchestrated in the Method column on the left.

     Add a diagram element.
      

      Drag diagram elements from the diagram element panel to the editing area based on the process design requirements.

      For example, if the method to be orchestrated needs to call a SOAP southbound service and then a REST southbound service, drag the SOAP diagram element and then drag the REST diagram element.

      
        
       
        To delete an added diagram element, select the diagram element and press Delete.

       

      

      

     Connect a diagram element.
      

      Select a connection line based on the process design requirements.

      
        
       
        To delete an added connection, select the line and press Delete.

       

      

      
       Click the connection line in the diagram element panel.

       Move the pointer to the start diagram element to be connected in the diagram element orchestration area.
        When the cursor changes to +, many connection points are displayed on the diagram element.

       Click any connection point.

       Drag to any connection point of the target diagram element, and click the connection point.

      

      

     Create a mapping between services and data.
      

      
       Double-click the diagram element to be orchestrated and select the service and method to be called.
        
          
         
          In the integrated orchestration scenario, when selecting the service to be called for the REST protocol, you can click Select service. In the Search Service window, search for and select a service in Service or API Catalog as prompted.

          The logic flow corresponds to Service on the menu, and the API catalog is the API on the page displayed after you choose Asset Management > Service Category.

         

        

       Click the Request tab in the Advanced Parameters area, map the data based on the actual relationship, and click Save.

       Click the Response tab in the Advanced Parameters area, map the data based on the actual relationship, and click Save.
        Response parameters of the endpoint are displayed on the left. Response parameters of the API are displayed on the right.

      

      
        
       
        
         You can name diagram elements to understand the entire service process on the process orchestration page.

         Click the automatic matching button. When the parameters in the source and target objects are consistent, the parameters are automatically associated.

         If you move the cursor to , a message is displayed. You can view the displayed data mapping.
          The API Fabric displays the message based on the parameter type in the definition file, but does not perform any logic processing. JavaScript is a loosely-typed language. You can use the auxiliary function Numbertils for type conversion based on site requirements.

          For example, if the called API performs strong verification for the parameter type, special processing is mandatory. If the input parameters do not affect the status, no special processing is required.

         You can click  of the target parameter to set the function.

         After the configuration is complete, you can click the non-configuration area of the diagram element to return to the Process Orchestration page.

         The response parameters of the previous diagram element are displayed on the request parameter page of the next diagram element. If multi-level connected diagram elements exist, the response parameters of all upper-level diagram elements are displayed on the request parameter page of the current diagram element.

Proxy Mode

   All functions of the proxy mode can be implemented based on process orchestration. In the same conditions, the proxy mode provides higher performance by using Groovy scripts than that by using JavaScript scripts. This makes the API execution faster than orchestration APIs but slower than transparent transmission APIs.

text:
Authentication
 
 
  
  

  
   Configure the API security authentication mode so that only users meeting the requirements can access the API. Malicious users are not allowed to construct URLs that are not authenticated by copying URLs and access the APIs without permission. Both the API-level and method-level authentication can be configured.

   Except for a custom API-level authentication policy, you can reference a defined common policy as the API authentication policy. For details about how to reference common policies, see Referencing a Common Policy.

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Access Control > Authentication Mode and select an authentication mode.
      

      Choose API-Level Policy or API Method-Level Policy based on the configuration granularity. The following authentication modes are supported:

      
        
       
        
         If no authentication mode is selected, authentication is not required.

         If multiple authentication modes are selected, you can use one of them.

        

       

      

      
       OAuth 2.0

       HIS API

       GTS API

       GAM Authentication

       Username and password
        
         If Pattern is set to APP, subscribe to the API through an app in the runtime-state API Fabric and use the AK/SK for username and password authentication.

         If Pattern is set to Basic Authentication, select a user group based on site requirements.

         If Pattern is set to Customize, configure user information in the Attribute Variables of Extension Policies dialog box. For details, see Configuring Attribute Variables of Extension Policies.

        

       OpenID

       AK/SK signature
        If this authentication mode is selected, you need to configure Expiration Time and Whether the signature contains the message body.

      

      

     Click Save.

    

   

   
    
    Configuring Attribute Variables of Extension Policies

    Perform access authentication on the fields in the packet. Select User Name And Password and set Pattern to Customize. The Attribute Variable of Extension Policies dialog box is displayed, as shown in Figure 1.

    
     Figure 1 Attribute Variables of Extension Policies dialog box
     
    

    
     Specify an extended field.
      

      The username and password are used in terms of concepts. You can use JSONPath to specify the field to be extended. JSONPath for JSON is equivalent to XPATH for XML. For details about the syntax, visit https://goessner.net/articles/JsonPath/.

      
       For the fields in the header, the example is $.header.userName or $.header.password.

       For the fields in the body, the example is $.body.batchCreateSubscriber.userName or $.body.batchCreateSubscriber.password.

      

      

     (Optional) Set the field to the default value.
      

      The default value is optional. If the default value is selected, the default value can be used when the corresponding field cannot be found.

      

     (Optional) Modify the encryption algorithm.
      

      In the JavaScript, fields can be encrypted. The default algorithm is aes256Encode. To update the encryption algorithm, edit the JavaScript on the Algorithm tab page.

      

     (Optional) Add a user group.
      

      If the added user has the home user group, click Add User Group, and select the user group defined in User Group Management.

name: Blacklist and Whitelist
title: Blacklist and Whitelist
text:
Blacklist and Whitelist
 
 
  
  

  
   The API Fabric supports the configuration of the IP address blacklist and whitelist for each API.

   
    Restrictions

    The blacklist and whitelist are used to forbid and allow access to APIs or the IP addresses of methods. You can configure the policy at the API level and method level. The priority of the method level is higher than that of the API level. A maximum of 50 records can be configured at the API level and method level respectively.

    The API-level blacklist and whitelist policy not only can be customized, but also can reference a defined common policy.

    The rules for verifying blacklists and whitelists are as follows:

    
     If multiple policies are configured with IP addresses, the system preferentially determines the IP address that is in the same network segment as the access IP address. If an IP address configured in the policy is in the same network segment as the access IP address, the system directly returns a determination result indicating whether to accept the access IP address. Otherwise, the system determines whether the access IP address is on a different network segment from the IP address configured in the policy.

     If the access IP address is on the same network segment as the IP address configured in the policy, the blacklist rule is preferentially used for verification. If the blacklist contains an IP address configured for the policy, the system directly returns the determination result, indicating that the access from the IP address is denied. If no IP address is in the blacklist, the rule that exists only in the whitelist is used for verification.

     If the access IP address is on a different network segment from the IP address configured in the policy, the whitelist rule is preferentially used for verification. If the whitelist contains an IP address configured for the policy, the system directly returns the determination result, indicating that the access from the IP address is denied. If no IP address is in the whitelist, the rule that exists only in the blacklist is used for verification.

     The rules for determining whether to accept an access request are as follows:
      
       In the case that the access IP addresses are on the same network segment as the IP address configured in the policy, if the network segment is added to the blacklist, all IP addresses in the network segment are denied. If the network segment is added to the whitelist, all IP addresses in the network segment can be accessed.

       In the case that the access IP addresses are on a different network segment from the IP address configured in the policy, if the IP address configured in the policy is added to the whitelist, the access to the IP address that is on a different network segment from the IP address configured in the policy is denied. If the IP address configured in the policy is added to the blacklist, the IP addresses that are on a different network segment from the IP addresses configured in the policy can be accessed.

      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Access Control > Blacklist/Whitelist. On the Blacklist or Whitelist tab page, enter the IP address and subnet mask.
      

      Based on the configuration granularity, set information on the Blacklist/Whitelist tab page under API-Level Policy or API Method-Level Policy.

      
       In IPv4 scenarios:
        
         To set a single IP address, set the subnet mask to 255.255.255.255.

         To set an IP address network segment, use the subnet mask.
          For example, if the IP address is 127.0.0.1 and the subnet mask is 255.255.255.0, the network segment is 127.0.0.0–127.0.0.254.

        

       In IPv6 scenarios:
        The blacklist and whitelist must comply with the IPv6 address format. The configuration method is as follows:

        Set IP Address (for example, 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:0) and Subnet prefix length (for example, 128).

      

      

     Click Confirm.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Access Control

name: JWT Validation
title: JWT Validation
text:
JWT Validation
 
 
  
  

  
   JSON Web Token (JWT) is a JSON-based open standard. The API Fabric can verify whether a request sent by a client is valid based on the JWT.

   
    Context

    If a JWT validation policy is configured, the API Fabric verifies the JWT token after receiving the request. During JWT token verification, the digital signature is verified first. If the verification fails, a 401 response is returned and a security log is recorded. After the digital signature is successfully verified, the declaration is verified. If the verification fails, a 403 response is returned and a security log is recorded.

   

   
     
    
     Currently, only the REST protocol is supported. The API-level and method-level configuration granularities are supported. The method-level configuration has a higher priority than the API-level configuration.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Access Control > Authentication Method and click JWT Validation.

     Click  next to Policy Switch to enable JWT Validation Policy.
      

       indicates that the function is enabled.

      

     Set the parameters related to the JWT policy.
      

      
        
       
        To define a key, you need to manually toggle on Whether the user defines the key.

       

      

      The following table describes related parameters.

      
       
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Header Field

          
           Name of a user-defined JWT validation policy.

           The API Fabric obtains the corresponding JWT based on the configured header field and parses the JWT content.

         

         
          
           Algorithm

          
           Encryption algorithm used for generating the JWT value. This parameter is available after Customize the key is enabled. Currently, the following algorithms are supported:

           
            HMAC SHA-256

            HMAC SHA-384

            HMAC SHA-512

            SHA-256withRSA

            SHA-384withRSA

            SHA-512withRSA

           

         

         
          
           Key Name

          
           Key name customized on the Develop API page. The key value is configured on the page displayed after you choose Common Definition > Key Management of the API Governance. This parameter is available after Customize the key is enabled.

         

         
          
           Offset Time (s)

          
           Whether the offset time takes effect. This parameter is available after Customize the key is enabled.

         

         
          
           Offset Time (s)

          
           Expiration time of the JWT value. This parameter is available after Customize the key is enabled.

           If Offset Time (s) is set, the JWT expiration time is the JWT expiration time specified by the user plus the offset time.

           
             NOTE: 
            
             To set Offset Time (s), you need to manually enable Offset Time Switch.

            

           

         

         
          
           Claim Verification

          
           If Key and Value under this parameter are configured during API calling, the API can be successfully called only when the request contains the corresponding values of Key and Value. This parameter is available after Customize the key is enabled.

           Click Add next to Claim Verification. In the dialog box that is displayed, set Key and Value.

text:
Flow Control

name: Configuring the Flow Control Policy
title: Configuring the Flow Control Policy
text:
Configuring the Flow Control Policy
 
 
  
  

  
   Flow control is used to limit the total number of API requests. If the number of API requests exceeds the threshold, the system rejects new requests and returns error information.

   The API-level and method-level configuration granularities are supported. The API-level configuration is used to perform flow control on APIs, and the method-level configuration is used to perform flow control on specified API methods. If both API-level and method-level flow controls are configured, the one that first meets the flow control conditions takes effect.

   Except for a custom API-level flow control policy, you can reference a defined common policy as the API-level flow control policy. For details about how to reference common policies, see Referencing a Common Policy.

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Flow Control > Flow control Policy, set Traffic Control Speed and Duration.
      

      Based on the configuration granularity, set information on the Flow control Policy tab page under API-Level Policy or API Method-Level Policy.

      
       
        
         Table 1 Flow control parameters
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Threshold

          
           Number of calls on APIs in a period. This configuration applies to all Access nodes or Access pods in the system. For example, if this parameter is set to 100, the total number of times that APIs can be called by all API Access nodes or API Access pods in the system is 100.

           
             NOTE: 
            
             If this parameter is set to 0, the flow control is not performed.

            

           

         

         
          
           Duration

          
           Period during which APIs can be called.

           The Redis is used to implement flow control. You are advised to select a larger time granularity, for example, Minute, to improve the performance and collect statistics on the number of access requests.

           If the time granularity is too small, the number of accesses may be inaccurate, affecting the flow control effect. For example, if Cycle is set to 1 Second, data is continuously updated to the Redis every second, affecting the overall performance.

         

         
          
           Degradation Policy

          
           If the Redis service is interconnected and is unavailable, Degradation Policy can be configured.

           
            No Flow Control: The flow control policy is invalid.

            Single Machine Flow Control: If two nodes exist in the Access cluster and Threshold is set to 100, after Single Machine Flow Control is selected, the number of calls in a period changes to 200.

            Single Machine Share: If two nodes exist in the Access cluster and Threshold is set to 100, after Single Machine Share is selected, the number of calls of a single node in a period is 50.

           

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Save.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Flow Control

API Logs

name: Interface Logs
title: Interface Logs
text:
Interface Logs
 
 
  
  

  
   The API Fabric can print logs based on the log scope and log level.

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose API-Level Policy > API Log > Log Policy.

     Set Log Type to Interface Log.

     Configure interface logs.
      

      Select the range of interface logs to be recorded based on site requirements. The values of Printing Scope and Log Level of the interface logs to be printed are described as follows.

      
       
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Printing Scope

          
           
            Receiver and sender
             All logs generated when the API Fabric functions as the client and server are printed.

            Receiver
             All logs generated when the API Fabric functions as the server are printed.

            Sender
             All logs generated when the API Fabric functions as the client are printed.

            None
             No log is printed.

           

         

         
          
           Log Level

          
           
             NOTE: 
            
             If this parameter is set to INFO or ERROR, you need to configure sensitive log policies in develop state. For details, see API Log Desensitization.

            

           

           
            INFO
             All request and response packets are printed.

             The following is a log example:

             2023-03-21 17:03:53,989|INFO|apiaccess|DefaultSpace|1638104128372604928||1||REST|Endpoint_WeatherService||127.0.0.1|https://127.0.0.1:8081/weather/getWeatherByCityId/undefined|get|/getWeatherByCityId/{cityId}|200|159|||{"request":{"headers":{"x-sandbox-jaggerid":"1638104128372604928","x-sandbox-dialtest":"true","accept-encoding":"gzip, x-gzip, deflate","host":"127.0.0.1:8081","connection":"keep-alive","user-agent":"APIFabric","content-length":"0","content-type":"application/json;charset=UTF-8","date":"Tuesday, March 21, 2023 09:03:53 GMT","x-forwarded-for":"127.0.0.1,127.0.0.1"},"body":}, "response":{"headers":{"Content-Type":"text/plain;charset=UTF-8","Keep-Alive":"timeout=60"},"body":"Sunny"}}

            ERROR
             Only the request and response packets sent when the calling fails are printed.

             The following is a log example:

             2023-03-20 16:02:09,843|ERROR|apiaccess|DefaultSpace|1637726043114569728||1||REST|Endpoint_WeatherService||127.0.0.1|https://127.0.0.1:8081/weather/getWeatherByCityId/undefined|get|/getWeatherByCityId/{cityId}|500|15359|||{"request":{"headers":{"x-sandbox-jaggerid":"1637726043114569728","x-sandbox-dialtest":"true","accept-encoding":"gzip, x-gzip, deflate","host":"127.0.0.1:8081","connection":"keep-alive","user-agent":"APIFabric","content-length":"0","content-type":"application/json;charset=UTF-8","date":"Monday, March 20, 2023 08:01:43 GMT","authorization":"****** ","x-forwarded-for":"127.0.0.1,127.0.0.1","X-APP-Key":"******"},"body":}, "response":{"headers":{},"body":"49401024991:can not make connection to service"}}

            No packet
             No packet is printed.

           

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Save.
