name: API Log Desensitization
title: API Log Desensitization
text:
API Log Desensitization
 
 
  
  

  
   The API Fabric accurately anonymizes various calling logs, including debug logs and API logs, based on the API sensitive field configuration.

   
    Restrictions and Description

    
     After the configuration is successful, the content of these fields is displayed as ****** in the runtime-state logs. Only method-level configuration is supported.

     If both endpoint method–level and API method–level desensitization policies are configured for a transparent transmission API, the two policies must be the same. Otherwise, the endpoint method–level policy may overwrite the API method–level policy.

     The user-defined desensitization rule takes effect only for interface logs. Other types of logs do not comply with this rule. By default, all sensitive fields are desensitized.

     If an XPath directory has been configured for Prefix (that is, Prefix is set to //), you are advised not to configure an XPath desensitization rule.

     If Parameter Name is configured using the fastjson syntax and contains a hyphen (-), set the parameter name based on the example ['test-01'].

     When using JPath desensitization rules, configure them based on the fastjson specifications.

     If five or more desensitization rules are configured, exact desensitization is used. To retain fuzzy desensitization, change the value of sys_sensitive_fuzzy_enable to true by referring to "Commissioning > Feature Commissioning > API Fabric Feature Commissioning > Modifying System Configurations" in GDE x.x.x Product Documentation.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Method-Level Policy > API Log > Log Desensitization.

     Click the method name, and click Add on the Request or Response tab page.

     Select the location of a field, for example, body, header, or path.

     Anonymize field values by setting the lengths of prefixes, suffixes, and intermediate fields.
      

      
       Desensitization rules can reference common rules. The values of Prefix and Parameter Name can be automatically matched.
       
        Prefix desensitization: n digits are desensitized from the first digit of the information to be desensitized (in order). For example, if Desensitization Length is set to 5, five digits are desensitized from the first digit of the information to be desensitized (in order).

        Infix desensitization: n digits are desensitized from the specified mth digit of the information to be desensitized (in order). For example, if Start Position is set to 3 and Desensitization Length is set to 5, five digits are desensitized from the third digit of the information to be desensitized (in order).

        Suffix desensitization: n digits are desensitized from the last digit of the information to be desensitized (in reverse order). For example, if Desensitization Length is set to 5, five digits are desensitized from the last digit of the information to be desensitized (in reverse order).

        Regular desensitization: Desensitize data based on regular expressions.

        XPath desensitization: Desensitize data based on XPath expressions.

        JPath desensitization: Desensitize data based on JPath expressions.

       

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: API Logs

name: Packet Validation
title: Packet Validation
text:
Packet Validation
 
 
  
  

  
   

  

  
   
    Parameter Verification
      Northbound request packets of the SOAP protocol support XSD verification and filtering, and northbound request packets of the HTTP protocol support Content-Type verification. The API Fabric intercepts request packets that fail the verification.

    JSON Protection
      If the request body is in JSON format, you can configure a JSON protection policy to standardize the JSON content of the request body and verify the JSON content.

    API Deduplication
      The API Fabric supports API deduplication to prevent an interface from being repeatedly called by the same request in a specified period. Currently, the API Fabric supports operation-level definition.

name: Parameter Verification
title: Parameter Verification
text:
Parameter Verification
 
 
  
  

  
   Northbound request packets of the SOAP protocol support XSD verification and filtering, and northbound request packets of the HTTP protocol support Content-Type verification. The API Fabric intercepts request packets that fail the verification.

   
    Context

    XSD filtering is also supported for SOAP requests and responses. After this policy is configured, if a packet contains fields that are not defined in the XSD, the API Fabric removes these fields during packet transmission.

   

   The following parameters can be verified:

   
    Content-Type

    Request parameters: path, query, header, and body
     
      Body types: JSON, XML, and FormData

      Parameter types: mandatory parameter, character string, number, array, object, and reference
       
        The following elements of parameter types are verified:
        
         Character string: length, enumeration, and regular expression

         Number: type and value range

         Array: length and elements

         Object: elements and number of elements

        

       

     

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Message Verification > Parameter Verification.

     Click  next to Policy Switch to enable the parameter verification policy.
      

       indicates that the function is enabled.

      You can configure this policy during API development. You can also add this policy or modify policy configurations on the API Manager. The parameters are described as follows.

      Determine whether to enable Parameter verification as required. If you select Yes, parameter verification is enabled. If you select No, parameter verification is disabled.

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Packet Validation

name: JSON Protection
title: JSON Protection
text:
JSON Protection
 
 
  
  

  
   If the request body is in JSON format, you can configure a JSON protection policy to standardize the JSON content of the request body and verify the JSON content.

   
    Context

    If the JSON content of the request body does not comply with the rule configured on the GUI, the API Fabric returns the error code 49401026092.

   

   
     
    
     The API-level and method-level configuration granularities are supported. The method-level configuration has a higher priority than the API-level configuration.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Message Verification > Json Protection.

     Click  next to Policy Switch to enable Json Protection Policy.
      

       indicates that the function is enabled.

      You can configure this policy during API development. You can also add this policy or modify policy configurations on the API Manager. The parameters are described as follows.

      
       
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Maximum Number of Nesting Layers

          
           Maximum number of layers nested in a JSON object.

         

         
          
           Maximum Number of Subobjects

          
           Maximum number of sub-objects in a JSON object (map).

         

         
          
           Maximum Array Length

          
           Maximum length of a JSON array.

         

         
          
           Maximum Key Length

          
           Maximum length of a key in a JSON object.

         

         
          
           Maximum Value Length

          
           Maximum length of a value in a JSON object.

         

        
       
      

      

     Set parameters on the Json Protection Policy tab page.
      

      Set parameters to -1 for rules that are not enabled.

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Packet Validation

name: API Deduplication
title: API Deduplication
text:
API Deduplication
 
 
  
  

  
   The API Fabric supports API deduplication to prevent an interface from being repeatedly called by the same request in a specified period. Currently, the API Fabric supports operation-level definition.

   
    Context

    The API Fabric supports API deduplication. After defining the deduplication field in an API request, the system determines whether the API is called by the same request based on the field in the method to prevent the API from being called by the same request repeatedly in a specified period.

    For example, if your click Submit twice on the frontend page, an API in the API Fabric is repeatedly called.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose API Method-Level Policy > Message Verification > Deduplicate Field.

     Set deduplication field and deduplication period.
      

      The API Fabric supports field association. In the configured time period, the API obtains two values through the deduplication expression. If the two values are the same, the request cannot be sent repeatedly.

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters for deduplication
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Parameter type

          
           Request parameter types contained in the current method, for example, header and query.

         

         
          
           Parameter Name

          
           Field contained in request parameters.

         

         
          
           Time Period

          
           Deduplication period.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Save.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After the API is exported, source\config\connection\deduplicationPolicy.yaml is added to the asset package to store deduplication information. The location of the deduplication policy file and the policy ID are stored in the API definition file definition.yaml.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Packet Validation

text:
User Extension

name: Configuring an Error Processing Policy
title: Configuring an Error Processing Policy
text:
Configuring an Error Processing Policy
 
 
  
  

  
   You can configure the endpoint error structure, API error code structure, error code definition, and error code mapping.

   For details about how to configure method-level error response operations, see API Error Response.

   After configuring the mapping between error codes, you need to check whether the error response is configured. If the error response is not configured, the error code mapping does not take effect.

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose User Extensions > Error Handling.

     Configure error codes.
      

      
       Gateway error code mapping
        
         The API Fabric error code is used to preset the error code in the runtime state for error code mapping when an internal error occurs in the API Builder.
         
          In the Error Code Mapping Rule column, select the defined error code mapping name from the drop-down list.

          In the Error Code Returned When No Mapping Is Found column, select the list return code from the drop-down list. The information in the drop-down list is automatically displayed in the text box.

         

        

       Endpoint error code mapping
        If only the service name is entered, the error code is mapped for the entire service. If both the service name and method are entered, the error code is mapped to the method.

        
         On the Error Handling Strategy tab page, enter the endpoint error code mapping.
          Click Add and configure the endpoint error code mapping. Table 1 describes the parameters.

         Select the service name and method of the endpoint and define the path of the error code.

         In the Error Code Group column, click the text box and select an existing common error code group.

         In the Error Code Mapping Rule column, click the text box and select an existing common error code mapping rule.

         In the Error Code Returned When No Mapping Is Found column, select the defined return code for the endpoint error code mapping. 
          
           
            
             Table 1 Endpoint error code parameters
            
            
             
             
            
            
             
              
               Parameter

              
               Description

             

            
            
             
              
               Service Name

              
               (Mandatory) Endpoint name.

             

             
              
               Method

              
               Name of the method called by the endpoint.

             

             
              
               Error Code Path

              
               (Mandatory) Error code path. The parameter is specified by the JSONPath and needs to be extended.

             

             
              
               Error Code Description Path

              
               Path for storing error code information. The parameter is specified by the JSONPath and needs to be extended.

             

             
              
               Code Details Path

              
               Path for storing error code details. The parameter is specified by the JSONPath and needs to be extended.

             

             
              
               Error Code Group

              
               Error code group.

             

             
              
               Error Code Mapping Rule

              
               Error code mapping rule.

             

             
              
               Error Code Returned When No Mapping Is Found

              
               Information defined and returned if no error code is returned.

             

            
           
          

        

       API error response
        The API error code structure can be configured for the API error response.

        
         In the Error Code Path column, enter the error code path.

         In the Error Code Description Path column, enter the error code description path.

         In the Code Details Path column, enter the error code details path.

        

      

      

     Click Save.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: User Extension

name: API Registration
title: API Registration
text:
API Registration
 
 
  
  

  
   In the integrated orchestration scenario, after an API is added, the API information can be registered with the corresponding document in the API directory of Asset Management > Service Category.

   This capability supports only the REST protocol.

   
    Prerequisites

    The API to be registered has been developed.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop API.

     Register an API
      

      
       Click Register next to the API.

       In the API Catalog window, select the path of the document to be registered, as shown in Figure 1.

       In the API Catalog window, configure the API sharing scope.
        
          
         
          If the project of the API belongs to an individual, the sharing scope can only be set to individual or public. If the project of the API belongs to a team, the sharing scope can be team or public.

         

        

      

      
       Figure 1 API Catalog
       
      

      

     After the registration is complete, reference the API.
      

      
       Click the name of the API to be registered. The Process Orchestration page is displayed.

       Double-click the REST diagram element. In the dialog box that is displayed, select Select service from the Service Name drop-down list.
        

        

       In the Search Service dialog box, click the API Catalog tab.

       Select the API in the corresponding path under API Catalog.

      

      

     Click Save.

name: Configuring Endpoints
title: Configuring Endpoints
text:
Configuring Endpoints
 
 
  
  

  
   Endpoint management is used to manage southbound services in a unified manner. The service name is used as a unique identifier.

   The southbound integrated service (endpoint) refers to the service to be called by the API Fabric. The service is provided by a third-party system and encapsulated by a downstream solution.

   After importing endpoint configuration files and configuring service address sources in endpoint management, API developers can directly reference these services for developing APIs. After API development, when API developers export APIs in batches, the tool packs the service configuration information referenced by APIs. You can import APIs for deployment, and can import southbound service information with these APIs. The following figure shows the usage scenario.

   

   
    Supported Protocols

    Currently, the endpoint management function supports endpoints of the REST and SOAP protocols.

   

  

  
   
    Adding an Endpoint
      You can use endpoint management to add and configure common endpoints. The service name is used as a unique identifier.

    Generating a Southbound ISO8583 Definition File
      On the develop-state API Fabric, an ISO8583 definition file can be imported to generate the corresponding endpoint, and policies can be configured for the endpoint on the page.

    Configuring an Endpoint-Level Policy
      This section describes the endpoint-level policy and configuration method. You can select and configure the policy as required.

    Configuring an Endpoint Method-Level Policy

    Southbound Service Exporting, Importing, and Updating

   

   
    
     Parent topic: Develop API

name: Adding an Endpoint
title: Adding an Endpoint
text:
Adding an Endpoint
 
 
  
  

  
   You can use endpoint management to add and configure common endpoints. The service name is used as a unique identifier.

   
    Context

    
      
     
      
       Endpoints associated with the APIs cannot be deleted.

       Choose More > Associated APIs next to an endpoint to view the APIs associated with the endpoint. In the dialog box that is displayed, click an API name to go to the Basic Information page of the API.

      

     

    

    Endpoints can be imported and exported separately or be imported in batches. Endpoints are exported based on the catalog level and placed in the corresponding catalogs. Figure 1 shows the ZIP package structure.

    
     endpoint: common service definition. Default indicates the name of the catalog where the endpoint is located.

     config: common configuration.

     .mf: asset signature list file, including the file directory and hash value corresponding to the file.

     .cms: signature file generated after the .mf file is digitally signed.

     .package: description file used to identify the package types when importing packages to the API Governance portal.

    

    
     Figure 1 Endpoint package structure
     
    

   

   
    Supported Protocols

    Currently, endpoints of the following protocols can be added:

    
     REST
      One or more XSD files (except YAML files) can be directly imported. (Multiple XSD files need to be compressed into a ZIP package.)

     SOAP

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop API.

     Go to the EndPoint Management tab page.
      

      Click EndPoint Management on the API Builder page, as shown in the following figure.

      
       Figure 2 Endpoint Management
       
      

      

      

     Add an endpoint.
      

      
       Click Create.

       In the Create Endpoint dialog box, upload the endpoint file as prompted.
        YAML+XSD or WSDL+XSD files can be compressed to a ZIP file.

       After the upload is complete, set parameters as prompted. The following table describes the parameters. 
        
         
          
           Table 1 Endpoint parameters
          
          
           
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

            
             Setting

           

          
          
           
            
             Protocol

            
             Protocol used by a southbound endpoint.

            
             The value is automatically obtained by the system and cannot be changed.

           

           
            
             Service URL

            
             URL of the server, which is called when the service functions as a southbound service.

            
             Example:

             Service request path:

             https://{IP address}:{Port number}/xxxx

             If a global variable defines a URL, you can directly use the global variable setting. If you enter ${, all common variables are automatically associated.

           

           
            
             Service Name

            
             Name of a southbound endpoint.

            
             Get data from file

             The value is automatically obtained by the system and can be changed.

           

           
            
             Read Timeout(ms)

            
             Read timeout interval.

            
             The value ranges from 1 to 300000, in milliseconds. The default value is 10000.

           

           
            
             Connection timeout(ms)

            
             Connection timeout interval.

            
             The value ranges from 1 to 60000, in milliseconds. The default value is 3000.

           

          
         
        

       After the configuration is complete, click Confirm.

Mock

name: Endpoint Authentication Mode
title: Endpoint Authentication Mode
text:
Endpoint Authentication Mode
 
 
  
  

  
   This mode is set to configure authentication policies and extended policies for the southbound endpoint.

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the name of the endpoint to be configured, and choose Endpoint-Level Policy > Authentication Method.

     Set the authentication mode.
      

      
       When a request is forwarded to a southbound service, the southbound service needs to authenticate the request before forwarding it to a third party. The authentication policy is used for configuring southbound service call. The supported authentication modes are as follows:
       
        No Authentication
         No authentication is performed on southbound services.

        Basic Authentication
         You need to enter the password obtained from the endpoint on the API Manager. The username is user-defined.

        GDE Store
         The app key needs to be selected based on the request header. Choose Endpoint Management > HTTP Service Management/SOAP Service Management in the API Governance, and set the secret key.

        GAM Authentication

        Username and Password
         For details about how to configure extended authentication of the username and password, see Configuring Attribute Variables of Extension Policies.

        OAuth 2.0 
         
          
           
            Table 1 Parameters
           
           
            
            
           
           
            
             
              Parameter

             
              Description

            

           
           
            
             
              Authentication Service Address

             
              Service address provided by Huawei IT Service (HIS) for the client to apply for tokens.

            

            
             
              Client ID

             
              Client ID, for example, AK of the client.

            

            
             
              OAuth type

             
              
                NOTICE: 
               
                During the extension, do not change the names of the predefined functions. When the endpoint is called, the API Access module of the API Fabric sends a request message containing the token field to the endpoint based on the extended JavaScript script.

               

              

              
               Custom scripts
                If Custom scripts is selected, set Authentication Service Address to the address of the server that performs token authentication, and Client ID to the app ID in the JavaScript script. On the API Governance page, the two parameters are read synchronously and you need to enter the client key obtained from the endpoint.

               HIS

               FABRIC

              

            

           
          
         

        WSSE
         This feature applies only to Huawei Cloud scenarios.

         You can configure APPKey and SecretKey on the API Portal to implement WSSE authentication. When an external system calls an API, the API Fabric forwards the request to the southbound system for processing and adds Authorization and X-WSSE to the request header. The following table describes the configuration.

         
          
           
            
            
            
            
            
           
           
            
             
              Parameter

             
              Mandatory

             
              Parameter Type

             
              Default Value

             
              Description

            

           
           
            
             
              Authorization

             
              Yes

             
              String

             
              -

             
              Set this parameter to WSSE realm="{SDP}",profile="{UsernameToken}",type="{Value of APPKey}".

            

            
             
              X-WSSE

             
              Yes

             
              String

             
              -

             
              
               Set this parameter to UsernameToken Username="{Value of APPKey}", PasswordDigest="{Value of PasswordDigest}", Nonce="{Random number}, Created="{Time when the random number is generated}".
               
                PasswordDigest: The value is generated based on PasswordDigest = Base64 (SHA256 (Nonce + Created + Password)). The value is a character string generated by combining Nonce, Created, and Password, and is encrypted using SHA256. The character string does not contain the plus sign (+) or spaces. Password is the value of SecretKey.

                Nonce: A random number generated when a customer sends a request. The value is a string of 1 to 128 characters, including digits, and letters. For example, 66C92B11FF8A425FB8D4CCFE0ED9ED1F.

                Created: Time when a random number is generated. The value is in the standard UTC format, for example, 2018-02-12T15:30:20Z.

               

              

            

           
          
         

       

      

      

     Click Save.

name: Dynamic Routing
title: Dynamic Routing
text:
Dynamic Routing
 
 
  
  

  
   Configure a route policy on the southbound endpoint to obtain the service URL based on the information in the message for routing.

   Only REST and SOAP are supported.

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the name of the endpoint to be configured, and choose Endpoint-Level Policy > Routing Policy.

     Configure a dynamic route.
      

      
       Set Choose Type to Dynamic Routing.

       Configure the route type and path expression by referring to Table 1. 
        
         
         
          
           Table 1 Parameters
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Route Type

            
             (Mandatory) When the type is jsonpath, select the corresponding packet field. Currently, $.header, $.body, and $.query are supported.

           

           
            
             Routing Expression

            
             Set this parameter based on the selected route type. For example, the format of jsonpath is $.header.addr.

           

           
            
             URL Address

            
             URL set based on Path Expression. For example, if URL Address is set to https://${servicename}:port, ${servicename} is automatically replaced by the URL in the request.

             
               NOTE: 
              
               When the dynamic route is used, the system replaces the path expression with the corresponding URL in the request message. The following two situations exist:

               
                If URL Address is set to https://${addr}/service, ${addr} is replaced by the corresponding part of the URL in the request.

                If URL Address is set to ${addr}, the complete URL in the request is used.

               

              

             

           

          
         
        

      

      

     Click Save.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Routing Policy

name: Conditional Routing
title: Conditional Routing
text:
Conditional Routing
 
 
  
  

  
   Configure a routing policy on the southbound endpoint policy and select a route address based on the request message information.

   You can use either of the conditional routing or dynamic routing.

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the name of the endpoint to be configured, and choose Endpoint-Level Policy > Routing Policy.

     Configure a conditional route.
      

      
       Choose Choose Type > Conditional Routing.

       Set Default URL and Route URL.

       Click Add Parameters next to Route URL, and set parameters as required. For details about the parameters, see Table 1. 
        
         
         
          
           Table 1 Parameters for configuring conditional routing
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Condition

            
             Condition name. The default value is Condition1. If multiple conditions exist, the conditions are indexed in ascending order, for example, Condition1 and Condition2.

           

           
            
             Route URL

            
             User-defined routing URL.

           

           
            
             Parameter Name

            
             Parameter name in a request message.

           

           
            
             Parameter Position

            
             Location of a parameter in a request packet. The value must be in the JSONPath format.

           

           
            
             Match Type

            
             The options are as follows:

             
              Exact Match: If one or more parameters exist, the matching is successful only when all parameters are met.

              Fuzzy Match: If multiple parameters exist, the matching is successful when one of the parameters is met.

             

           

           
            
             Parameter Value List

            
             Preset parameter information. When the information in a request message matches a parameter in the parameter value list, the corresponding route URL is called.

           

          
         
        

        
          
         
          You can add multiple conditions. When two or more conditions are met, the first condition that is met is used for routing by default.

         

        

      

      

     Click Save.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Routing Policy

text:
Health Check

You can view the number of healthy endpoints and the number of abnormal endpoints on the Endpoint Management page.

           Health API of an endpoint. You can add a maximum of 500 health check URLs.

           The URL format can be https://xxxx or ${xxxx}.

name: URL Encoding Policy
title: URL Encoding Policy
text:
URL Encoding Policy
 
 
  
  

  
   The API Fabric can encode endpoint URLs based on the specified encoding mode.

   
    Constraints

    
     The API Fabric supports two encoding modes: RFC and W3C.
      RFC and W3C escape special characters in URLs to the %HH format. The following table describes the escape rules in the API Fabric.

      
       
        
         Table 1 Special character escape rules
        
        
         
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Encoding Mode

          
           Special Character in the URL

          
           After Being Escaped

         

        
        
         
          
           RFC

          
           Space

          
           %20

         

         
          
           W3C

          
           Space

          
           +

         

        
       
      

     This policy supports only the RESTful protocol and can be configured only in the develop-state API Fabric.

     The default encoding mode of existing endpoints created in versions earlier than API Fabric V600R025C00 is W3C. If no encoding mode is configured for a new endpoint in API Fabric V600R025C00 or later, the RFC encoding mode is used by default. The scenarios for adding an endpoint are as follows:
      
       When an API is added on the Design API tab page, you need to click Generate a public endpoint or One-click transparent transmission API to generate an endpoint.

       When an API is added on the Develop API tab page, you need to set Orchestration Mode to Transparent Transmission Mode to add an endpoint.

       In Endpoint Management, add an endpoint.

      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the name of the endpoint to be configured, and choose Endpoint-Level Policy > URL Encode Policy.

     Select an encoding mode based on site requirements.

     Click Save.

name: Configuring a Timer for the API Fabric
title: Configuring a Timer for the API Fabric
text:
Configuring a Timer for the API Fabric
 
 
  
  

  
   The API Fabric can simplify operations of calling third-party orchestration processes. A timer is released to call third-party orchestration processes based on the configured number of repetitions in a specified execution period.

   The timer needs to be created in the develop state of the API Fabric.

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop API.

     On the Develop API page, choose More > Timer Management.
      

      

      

      

     On the Timer Management page, click Create. Set parameters based on site requirements. The following table describes the parameters.
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters for configuring a timer
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           User-defined timer name.

         

         
          
           Type

          
           Timer type. Currently, only repeat is supported.

         

         
          
           Execution period

          
           Execution period of the timer. For example, if Execution period is set to 1000 and Duration Unit is set to Milliseconds, the timer is executed for the second time 1000 ms after the first execution ends, and so on until the number of repetition times is met.

         

         
          
           Repetition Times

          
           Number of repetition times of the timer. For example, if this parameter is set to 4, after the first execution is complete, the timer is executed for the second time 1000 ms later, and so on. When the timer is executed for four times, the timer stops triggering the third-party orchestration process.

           
             NOTE: 
            
             If this parameter is set to 0, the timer triggers the third-party orchestration process for unlimited times until you manually cancel the release of the timer.

            

           

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Description of a user-defined timer.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Confirm.

     On the Timer page, click the timer name. The timer process orchestration page is displayed.
      

      For details about process orchestration, see Orchestration. The timer process orchestration is different from the API process orchestration. For example, when a user clicks a diagram element, only the service to be called can be configured, and no request parameter is required.

      The timer process is orchestrated by a third party and is configured by users. The message returned during calling is also processed by users.

      

     After the orchestration is complete, click Save.
      

      You can modify or delete a configured timer on the Timer page.

      

     After the timer is configured, select the timer to be exported and click Export.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Develop API

name: Adding a Common Definition of an API or Endpoint
title: Adding a Common Definition of an API or Endpoint
text:
Adding a Common Definition of an API or Endpoint
 
 
  
  

  
   This function is used to define common configurations for all APIs or southbound services in the tool. The variables defined in the develop state are set to specific values in the API Fabric runtime state. The following information is included: variable definition, dictionary value mapping, key management, user group management, common function, and common structure.

   You can define common configurations for all APIs or southbound services on the Public Definition tab page. The following information is included: variable definition, dictionary value mapping, key management, user group management, common function, and common structure.

   
    Overview

    The configuration items defined on the Public Definition page are global variables. Table 1 describes the configuration items.

    
     
     
      
       Table 1 Configuration items on Public Definition
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Configuration Item

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Variable Definition

        
         Used for centralized configuration and management of project-level common variables (shared with all APIs in a project), obtaining environment information and cross-API shared configuration during the API development. After common variables are set, you can enter ${ to associate them when defining APIs or adding southbound endpoints.

       

       
        
         KV Mapping

        
         Used to manage mappings at different sites to meet the requirements. After being set, the configuration item can be used during API development.

       

       
        
         Key Management

        
         Used to obtain a decrypted field of a service during API orchestration. After being set, the configuration item can be used during API definition.

       

       
        
         User Management

        
         Used to manage users and passwords by a user group in a unified manner. After the configuration item is set, user groups can be associated during API development. If authentication is configured in the API test or application, the system searches for the corresponding username and password from the associated user group. If the matching is successful, the authentication is successful. Otherwise, the authentication fails and invalid users are intercepted.

       

       
        
         Public Function

        
         JavaScript function used in the policy such as the process orchestration or responsibility chain (such as flow control, authentication, and data mapping). Common functions can be defined to prevent repeated definition of functions.

         The common functions defined here are global functions and are used by all APIs of a project.

       

       
        
         Public Structure

        
         The configuration item is used to centrally manage the parameter structures that are referenced across APIs in the northbound API definition. The common structures defined in the Investigator tool and Builder tool can be shared. A common structure is included when the API that references the common structure is exported.

         Currently, the Builder tool supports only the common structure of the REST protocol. After the definition, for REST APIs, common structures can be directly referenced in the API definition to meet users' requirements for reusing common structures across APIs.

       

       
        
         Public Process

        
         You can define the southbound service orchestration process of an endpoint as a common process to implement process reuse. The process nesting is not supported currently.

       

       
        
         Public Error Handling Strategy

        
         The configuration item is used to define a common error response so that the service side can notify the tool platform of the error response structure for the platform to obtain and construct error objects. When handling an exception message, the API running engine constructs an exception message based on the exception message format defined in the API policy and returns the message.

       

       
        
         Error Code

        
         The configuration item is used to set the common error code for multiple APIs.

       

       
        
         Public Policy

        
         The configuration item is used to configure a common policy for multiple APIs. Currently, only the API-level common policy can be referenced.

       

      
     
    

    The configuration on the Common Definition tab page can be used for common asset import or export. The structure of the import or export package is shown in Figure 1.

    
     source\config: stores the common definition file.

     js: stores the common script.

     .mf: asset signature list file, including the file directory and hash value corresponding to the file.

     .cms: signature file generated after the .mf file is digitally signed.

     .package: description file, which is used to identify the package type when a package is imported to the Governance portal.

    

    
     Figure 1 Common asset package structure
     
    

    
      
     
      
       For information security, Key Management and User Management in the exported asset package are unavailable. You need to set them again after the API is deployed.

       The exported asset package does not contain common structure information. The common structure information needs to be exported separately.

      

     

    

   

  

  
   
    Variable Definition

    Dictionary Value Mapping

    Key Management

    User Group Management

    Common Function

    Common Structures

    Common Process

    Common Error Handling Policy

    Error Codes

    Common Policy

    Importing or Exporting Common Assets

title: Variable Definition
text:
Variable Definition
 
 
  
  

  
   The configuration item is used for centralized configuration and management of project-level common variables (shared with all APIs in a project), obtaining environment information and cross-API shared configuration during the API development. After common variables are configured, they can be used during process orchestration and southbound endpoint addition.

   
    Usage Scenarios

    
     When adding a southbound service, you can use ${Variable name} to reference a variable, as shown in Figure 1.
      The defined variable is cbs.server.

      
       Figure 1 Referencing a variable when adding an endpoint
       
      

     Use apigw.getProperty('{Variable name}') in the JavaScript of Process orchestration to obtain the variable value.
      Figure 2 shows an example. The tool supports association. Enter the first letter of the variable in the JavaScript, as shown in Figure 3.

      
       Figure 2 Referencing the variable in the JavaScript
       
      

      
       Figure 3 Associating the variable name in the JavaScript
       
      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop APIs.

     Go to the Public Definition tab page.
      

      
       Click Public Definition on the API Builder page. The Variable Definition page is displayed by default.
       
        Figure 4 Accessing the Common Definition page
        
       

      

      

      

     Add a variable.
      

      On the Variable Definition page, click Add and set parameters as prompted, as shown in Table 1.

      
       
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters for setting variables
        
        
         
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

          
           Example

         

        
        
         
          
           Variable Name

          
           Custom variable name. Set this parameter based on site requirements.

           
             NOTE: 
            
             To import a variable package to the runtime state, ensure that Variable Name contains 4 to 36 characters. Otherwise, the import fails.

            

           

          
           _port

         

         
          
           Variable Value

          
           Value of a variable.

           
             NOTE: 
            
             To import a variable package to the runtime state, ensure that Variable Value contains 1 to 300 characters. Otherwise, the import fails.

            

           

          
           2026

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Description of a variable.

          
           port

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Confirm.

     (Optional) Configure whether to overwrite the original configuration when importing Variable Definition to the API Manager.
      

      If the value in the Override Allowed column next to the corresponding record is true, the new configuration will overwrite the original configuration on the API Manager after being imported to the API Manager. After the overwriting, the new configuration cannot be modified on the API Manager.

      
        
       
        If the Override Allowed capability is configured, the source/config/override/override.yaml file is automatically generated after the common configuration is exported. The file records the variables and dictionary values that can overwrite the capability.

Dictionary Value Mapping
 
 
  
  

  
   The configuration item is used to manage mappings at different sites to meet the requirements. After being set, the configuration item can be used during API development.

   
    Usage Scenarios

    
     When receiving one or more southbound responses, the service needs to map the response code, error code, and cause value in the southbound response to the corresponding fields in the northbound response during API orchestration.
      The following figure shows an example.

      

     The service needs to map values between northbound and southbound APIs (from north to south or from south to north).
      The following figure shows an example.

      

    

   

   
    Procedure

        Figure 1 Accessing the Common Definition page

      In the navigation pane, choose KV Mapping.

     Add a mapping source and a mapping target.
      

      Click Add, configure the mapping source and target as prompted, and click Confirm, as shown in Figure 3.

      
       Figure 3 Adding a mapping source and target
       
      

      

      
        
       
        The mapping source is specified by a variable transmitted from the upstream component.

       

      

      

     (Optional) Configure whether to overwrite the original configuration when importing KV Mapping to the API Manager.
      

      If the value in the Override Allowed column next to the corresponding record is true, the new configuration will overwrite the original configuration on the API Manager after being imported to the API Manager. After the overwriting, the new configuration cannot be modified on the API Manager.

      
        
       
        If the Override Allowed capability is configured, the source/config/override/override.yaml file is automatically generated after the common configuration is exported. The file records the variables and dictionary values that can overwrite the capability.

       

      

      Select the check box of a mapping that can be overwritten and click Override Allowed.

      To disable the overwriting function, click Edit next to the record, deselect the check box, and click Confirm.

      

    

   

   
    Usage Instruction

    The KV value can be called using the dataMapping function in the JavaScript of Process orchestration during the API definition. The calling format is as follows:

    
     dataMapping(groupName, itemName, sourceValue)
      The tool returns the mapping target value based on the three parameters. If the target value fails to be obtained, the target value cannot be returned.

      Figure 4 describes the mapping between calling parameters and parameters on the KV Mapping tab page.

      
       Figure 4 Parameter mapping
       
      

     dataMapping(groupName, itemName, sourceValue, defaultValue)
      The defaultValue parameter is set by the user. If the target value cannot be obtained based on the first three parameters, defaultValue is returned.

    

    In the JavaScript, you can use kvMapping to associate fields to be mapped, as shown in Figure 5. The dataMapping function is used to find the values of groupName, itemName, and sourceValue, as shown in Figure 6.

name: Key Management
title: Key Management
text:
Key Management
 
 
  
  

  
   The configuration item is used to obtain a decrypted field of a service during API orchestration. After being set, the configuration item can be used during API definition.

   
    Context

    After the key is configured and exported as a common asset, the storage structure in the definition.yaml file is shown in Figure 1.

    
     dftGrp: default group.

     name: key name.

     key: ciphertext key.

    

    
     Figure 1 Key management storage structure
     
    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop APIs.

     Go to the Public Definition tab page.
      

      
       Click Public Definition on the API Builder page. The Variable Definition page is displayed by default.
       
        Figure 2 Accessing the Common Definition page
        
       

      

      

      

     Go to the Key Management page.
      

      In the navigation pane, choose Key Management.

      

     Add a key.
      

      Click Add and set the mapping key name as prompted.

      The key cannot be configured in develop state, and is displayed as * on the GUI. The key can be configured only after it is imported to the API Manager page.

      

     Click Confirm.

    

   

   
    Usage Instruction

    The set key can be obtained using the getConfig function in the JavaScript script for the authentication mode of CUSTOMEAUTH on the Policy Configuration tab page during API definition. The format is as follows:

    getConfig('secretKeys','dftGrp','xxxname')

    In the preceding information:

    
     secretKeys and dftGrp: fixed parameters.

     xxxname: key name on the Key Management page.

    

    Figure 3 shows the configuration example in the JavaScript. Except xxx, other configurations are fixed. You need to replace xxx with the set key.

    
     Figure 3 Obtaining the key setting from the JavaScript
     
    

    In the JavaScript, you can use secretKeys to associate the key name, as shown in Figure 4.

    
     Figure 4 Association of secretKeys

name: User Group Management
title: User Group Management
text:
User Group Management
 
 
  
  

  
   The configuration item is used by a user group to manage users and passwords in a unified manner. After the configuration item is set, user groups can be associated during API development. If authentication is configured in the API test or application, the system searches for the corresponding username and password from the associated user group. If the matching is successful, the authentication is successful. Otherwise, the authentication fails and invalid users are intercepted.

   
    Context

    After a user group is configured and exported as a common asset, the storage structure of the user group in the definition.yaml file is shown in Figure 1, in which groupx indicates a user group name.

    
     Figure 1 Storage structure of the user group
     
    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop APIs.

     Go to the Public Definition tab page.
      

      
       Click Public Definition on the API Builder page. The Variable Definition page is displayed by default.
       
        Figure 2 Accessing the Common Definition page
        
       

      

      

      

     Go to the User Management page.
      

      In the navigation pane, choose User Management.

      

     Add a user group.
      

      
       Click Add and set the user group name and description as prompted.

       Click Confirm.

      

      

     Add user information.
      

      
       Click the added user group. The User Configuration dialog box is displayed.

       Click Add and configure the username as prompted.
        The user password must be imported to the API Governance before being configured.

       Click Confirm.

      

      

    

   

   
    Usage Instruction

    The user group information can be obtained using the getConfig function in the JavaScript script for the authentication mode of CUSTOMEAUTH on the Policy Configuration tab page during API definition. The format is as follows:

    getConfig('userAuth','groupname','users')

    In the preceding information:

    
     userAuth and users: fixed parameters.

     groupname: user group name set on the User Management page.

    

    Figure 3 shows a setting example in the JavaScript.

    
     Figure 3 Obtaining the user group configuration in the JavaScript
     
    

    In the JavaScript, you can use userAuth to associate the key name, as shown in Figure 4.

    
     Figure 4 Association of userAuth

name: Common Function
title: Common Function
text:
Common Function
 
 
  
  

  
   A common function indicates the JavaScript function used in the policy such as the process orchestration or responsibility chain (such as flow control, authentication, and data mapping). Common functions can be defined to prevent repeated definition of functions.

   The common function defined here is a global function and is used by all APIs of only a project.

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop APIs.

     Go to the Public Definition tab page.
      

      
       Click Public Definition on the API Builder page. The Variable Definition page is displayed by default.
       
        Figure 1 Accessing the Common Definition page
        
       

      

      

      

     Go to the Public Function page.
      

      In the navigation pane, choose Public Function.

      

     Add a function category.
      

      
       In the navigation pane, click  and enter a category name.

       Click Confirm.
        Select a category and click  to add a subcategory.

      

      

     Add a common function.
      

      
       Select the category to which the function belongs, and click Add Function.
        In the displayed dialog box, enter the name, description, and function definition.

       Click Confirm.

      

      

    

   

   
    Usage Instruction

    You can drag the defined common function during API definition.

    For example, the TestCase function shown in Figure 2 is defined in Public Function. The Test1 method defined in the TestCase function is displayed in the JavaScript of Process orchestration of the API management, as shown in Figure 3. Drag the Test1 method to the editing area on the right.

    
     Figure 2 Defined common function
     
    

    
     Figure 3 Common functions in the JavaScript

name: Common Structures
title: Common Structures
text:
Common Structures
 
 
  
  

  
   The configuration item is used to centrally manage the parameter structures that are referenced across APIs in the northbound API definition. The common structures defined in the Investigator tool and Builder tool can be shared. A common structure is included when the API that references the common structure is exported.

   Currently, the Builder tool supports only the common structure of the REST protocol. After the definition, for REST APIs, common structures can be directly referenced in the API definition to meet users' requirements for reusing common structures across APIs.

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop APIs.

     Go to the Public Definition tab page.
      

      
       Click Public Definition on the API Builder page. The Variable Definition page is displayed by default.
       
        Figure 1 Accessing the Common Definition page
        
       

      

      

      

     Go to the Public Structure page.
      

      In the navigation pane, choose Public Structure.

      

     Add a structure catalog.
      

      In the navigation pane, click  and enter a structure catalog name.

      

     Add a common structure.
      

      
       Select the category to which a structure belongs and click Add.
        Enter the structure name and define parameters based on site requirements.

        The REST API described in the tool is based on the Swagger 2.0 framework and OpenAPI specifications (for details, see https://swagger.io/specification/). The parameters and data structures defined on the page must meet the specifications.

       Click Save.

      

      

    

   

   
    Usage Instruction

    The defined common structure is directly selected during API definition. You can select NormalStruct or HeaderStruct.

    For example, the common structure shown in Figure 2 is defined on the Common Structure page. In the API Definition structure of the API management, the parameter type can be set to NormalStruct, as shown in Figure 3.

    
     Figure 2 Defined common structure
     
    

    
     Figure 3 Common structure displayed in the parameter type
     
    

   

   
    Viewing Reference Points

    On the page for modifying a common structure, click View references to view the API or other structures that reference the structure, as shown in Figure 4.

    
     Figure 4 Viewing reference points
     
    

    

    
     Click Edit next to the structure where the reference point is to be viewed.
      Go to the Modify Public Structure tab page.

     Click View references. The APIs and structures that reference the structure page is displayed.

    

   

   
    Importing or Exporting Structures

    The import and export of common structures support the reuse of the structures in different projects or environments.

    
     Export
      On the Public Structure tab page, select one or more structures to be exported, and click Export.

     Import
      On the Public Structure tab page of a target project or environment, click Import and select the ZIP package to be imported. The ZIP package to be imported must be the structure package exported from the tool.

name: Common Process
title: Common Process
text:
Common Process
 
 
  
  

  
   You can define the southbound service orchestration process of an endpoint as a common process to implement process reuse. The process nesting is not supported currently.

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop APIs.

     Go to the Public Definition tab page.
      

      
       Click Public Definition on the API Builder page. The Variable Definition page is displayed by default.
       
        Figure 1 Accessing the Common Definition page
        
       

      

      

      

     Select Public Process and click Add to create a common process.
      

      In the displayed dialog box, enter the process name and description, and click Confirm.

      

     Define common process variables.
      

      
       Select the common process to be defined. The process orchestration page is displayed.

       Click Process Variable. On the displayed Process Variable page, click Add.
        Enter the variable name, type, and parameter attribute (input or output) as required. The type can reference the common structure.

      

      

     Orchestrate a common process.
      

      For details, see Procedure.

      

     Click Confirm.

name: Common Error Handling Policy
title: Common Error Handling Policy
text:
Common Error Handling Policy
 
 
  
  

  
   The configuration item is used to define a common error response so that the service side can notify the tool platform of the error response structure for the platform to obtain and construct error objects. When handling an exception message, the API running engine constructs an exception message based on the exception message format defined in the API policy and returns the message.

   
    Context

    The error handling policy configured in Public Definition is specified by a global variable, which is used by all APIs in the project. The error structure configured in API Management is used only by the API.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop APIs.

     Go to the Public Definition tab page.
      

      
       Click Public Definition on the API Builder page. The Variable Definition page is displayed by default.
       
        Figure 1 Accessing the Common Definition page
        
       

      

      

      

     Go to the Error Handling page.
      

      In the navigation pane, choose Error Handling.

      

     Set Code Path, Code Description Path, and Code Details Path.
      

      

      
       
       
         
        
         Common error response information is configured using fields specified by the JSONPath. For details about the JSONPath syntax, see https://goessner.net/articles/JsonPath/.

        

       

      

      

     (Optional) Click Advanced configuration and customize an API error response extension script. Figure 2 shows a configuration example.
      

      
       Figure 2 Configuring an extension script
       
      

      
        
       
        The code priority in the Advanced configuration area is higher than that in the preceding text box. You can set either of the code priorities when configuring the common error handling policy.

       

      

      

     Click Save.

name: Error Codes
title: Error Codes
text:
Error Codes
 
 
  
  

  
   The configuration item is used to set the common error code for multiple APIs.

   
    Procedure (Error Code Definition)

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop APIs.

     Go to the Public Definition tab page.
      

      
       Click Public Definition on the API Builder page. The Variable Definition page is displayed by default.
       
        Figure 1 Accessing the Common Definition page
        
       

      

      

      

    

    
     Go to the Error Code Definition page.
      

      In the navigation pane, choose Error Code > Error Code Definition.

      

     Add a source error code category.
      

      
        
       
        The source error code is used for error code information returned by the API Fabric or third-party system.

        The error code group GatewayInner of the API Fabric in O&M state is embedded in the tool.

       

      

      Choose Source and click  next to the catalog. In the dialog box that is displayed, enter the source name and click Confirm.

      

     Add a source error code.
      

      
       Select the category to which the source error code belongs and click Add.
        Enter the error code name, description, and error details as prompted.

       Click Confirm.

      

      

     Add a target error code category.
      

      
        
       
        The target error code is defined by the service side and is an error code that can be identified by the service side.

       

      

      Choose Target and click  next to the catalog. In the dialog box that is displayed, enter the target name and click Confirm.

      

     Add a target error code.
      

      
       Select the category to which the target error code belongs and click Add.
        Enter the error code name, description, and error details as prompted.

       Click Confirm.

      

      

    

   

   
    Procedure (Error Code Mapping)

    Map a source error code to a target error code that can be recognized by the service and set the status code returned when an API is called.

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop APIs.

     Access Error Code Mapping and configure a global error code mapping.
      

      In the navigation pane, choose Error Code > Error Code Mapping.

      

     Add a structure group.
      

      
       Click  next to the catalog. In the dialog box that is displayed, enter the group name.

       Click Confirm.

      

      

     Add an error code mapping.
      

      
       Click Add and select the corresponding source error code group and error code from the Mapping Source drop-down list.

       Select the mapped target error code group and error code from the Mapping Destination drop-down list.

       Set Status Code to the message code to be returned and click Confirm.

      

      

    

   

   
    Usage Instruction

    The set error code can be used under API Management > API Definition > Policy Configuration > API-Level Policy. For details, see Configuring an Error Processing Policy.

    If the common error code changes, the referenced error code needs to be changed accordingly.

    After configuring the mapping between error codes, you need to check whether the error processing policy is configured. If the error processing policy is not configured, the error code mapping does not take effect.

name: Common Policy
title: Common Policy
text:
Common Policy
 
 
  
  

  
   The configuration item is used to configure a common policy for multiple APIs. Currently, only the API-level common policy can be referenced.

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop APIs.

     Go to the Public Definition tab page.
      

      
       Click Public Definition on the API Builder page. The Variable Definition page is displayed by default.
       
        Figure 1 Accessing the Common Definition page
        
       

      

      

      

    

    
     Configure a policy as required.
      

      
       Authentication
        
         In the navigation pane, choose Common Policy > Authentication Mode.

         Click Add, enter the policy name and description, and select an authentication mode.
          OAuth 2.0, and username and password can be configured. For details about the authentication mode, see Procedure.

          
           Enable Endpoint Authentication. You can configure only the OAuth 2.0 authentication of the endpoint.
           
             
            
             On the Endpoint Management page, you can reference the configured southbound OAuth 2.0 authentication policy when editing an endpoint.

            

           

          

         Click Confirm.

        

      

      
       Flow control
        
         In the navigation pane, choose Common Policy > Traffic Policy.

         Click Add, and enter the policy name, description, and flow control information.
          For details about flow control information, see Configuring the Flow Control Policy.

         Click Confirm.

        

       Blacklist and whitelist
        
         In the navigation pane, choose Common Policy > Black/White List.

         Click Add and enter the policy name and description to add one or more blacklists or whitelists.
          For details about IP addresses, see Blacklist and Whitelist.

         Click Confirm.

        

       Dynamic parameters
        Dynamic parameters are used to adjust request parameters sent to the southbound system, for example, adding parameters to the header of a request.

        
         In the navigation pane, choose Common Policy > Dynamic Parameters.

         Click Add. In the Add Dynamic Parameters dialog box, set parameters such as Policy Name and Description.

         Click Add and set Parameter Name, Position, Type, and Field Value. The following table describes related parameters.
          
            
           
            If type is set to Variable or PRESETPARAM, the parameter is not transferred if no parameter value is obtained during calling, and the dynamic parameter content is not recorded in logs.

            Modifying or deleting standard HTTP headers has the following risks:

            
             The request may fail.

             Field values may fail to be modified or deleted due to the restrictions of HTTP specifications.

            

           

          

          
           
            
             Table 1 Parameters
            
            
             
             
            
            
             
              
               Parameter

              
               Description

             

            
            
             
              
               Policy Name

              
               Unique name of a custom dynamic parameter policy.

             

             
              
               Add

             

             
              
               Param Name

              
               Name of a southbound parameter.

             

             
              
               Param Location

              
               Location for storing southbound parameters after obtaining northbound parameters. The options are as follows:

               
                header

                query

                cse_context

               

             

             
              
               type

              
               Type of a northbound parameter. The options are as follows:

               
                CONSTANT

                Variable

                PRESETPARAM

               

             

             
              
               value

              
               Value of a northbound parameter, which can be customized.

               
                If type is set to Variable, value can be set to $.header.abc or $.query.abc, indicating that the value named abc of the northbound parameter header or query is used as the value of the parameter sent to the southbound.

                If type is set to PRESETPARAM, value can be set to any of the following values:
                 
                  app_key

                  app_name

                  tenant_id

                  tenant_name

                  client_ip

                  gam_username

                 

               

             

             
              
               Delete

             

             
              
               Param Name

              
               Name of the parameter to be deleted from the request packet sent to the southbound.

             

             
              
               Param Location

              
               Location of the parameter to be deleted from the request packet sent to the southbound.

             

            
           
          

        

      

      

     (Optional) Modify the policy.
      

      After a policy is configured, click Edit to modify the policy name or parameters.

      

     (Optional) Bind an API.
      

      After the policy is configured, click Setting and bind the policy to an API, as shown in Figure 2. After the binding is successful, you can reference the policy in the API-level policy of the API, as shown in Figure 3.

      
       Figure 2 Binding a policy to an API
       
      

      
       Figure 3 Policy reference example

name: Importing or Exporting Common Assets
title: Importing or Exporting Common Assets
text:
Importing or Exporting Common Assets
 
 
  
  

  
   For information security, Key Management and User Management in the exported asset package are unavailable. You need to set them again after the API is deployed.

   
    Procedure (Export)

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop APIs.

     Go to the Public Definition tab page.
      

      
       Click Public Definition on the API Builder page. The Variable Definition page is displayed by default.
       
        Figure 1 Accessing the Common Definition page
        
       

      

      

      

     Click Export and select a signature certificate.
      

      In the dialog box that is displayed, select the configuration items to be exported and click Confirm.

      

    

   

   
    Constraints

    
     In GDE 26.1.0 and later versions, a signature certificate can be selected during API export.
     
      You can use the API Fabric default signature certificate GDE_API-FABRIC_SIGN and the XMS default signature certificate acm.sign.jks. If you need to use a new self-issued certificate of the XMS, name it in the format of GDE_API-FABRIC_****, for example, GDE_API-FABRIC_custom.

      When importing API asset packages from the develop state environment of GDE 26.1.0 or later to the runtime state environment of a version earlier than GDE 26.1.0, select the GDE_API-FABRIC_SIGN signature certificate during the export of the API asset packages.

      The API Fabric polls the signature certificate, signature verification certificate, and certificate revocation list every 5 minutes. In this case, the certificates displayed in the develop state environment cannot be synchronized in real time.

     

    

   

   
    Procedure (Import)

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop APIs.

     Go to the Public Definition tab page.
      

      
       Click Public Definition on the API Builder page. The Variable Definition page is displayed by default.
       
        Figure 2 Accessing the Common Definition page
        
       

      

      

      

     Click Import.
      

      Select the ZIP package to be imported. The ZIP package must be the common asset package exported from the tool.
