name: Deploying and Commissioning APIs
title: Deploying and Commissioning APIs
text:
Deploying and Commissioning APIs
 
 
  
  

  
   If the develop-state API Fabric and API Governance are deployed on the same plane, after API development is complete, you can deploy APIs to the API Governance on the Deploy and Test page for API commissioning and view the API calling track, diagram element context information, and logs.

   For an API in proxy mode, only logs can be viewed during commissioning, and the diagram element trace is not displayed.

   
    Restrictions and Description

    
     The commissioning function applies only to APIs whose processes have been orchestrated.

     Only the SOAP and REST protocols are supported.

     The commissioning function supports the following authentication modes: OAuth 2.0, GAM authentication, and username and password.

     The API Fabric limits the size of a request body to 10 KB. If the size of the request body of an API exceeds 10 KB, the page performance may be abnormal and frame freezing may occur. Therefore, you are advised not to use the commissioning function to call the API.

     You can enable or disable the deployment commissioning function as required. The procedure is as follows:
      
       Log in to the GDE data zone as the admin user.

       Choose Products and Services > Administration > Common Setting > Config Management.

       On the Config Center page, enable Display All Configurations in the upper right corner.

       Search for the keyword gde.apifabric.builder.test.active in the search box and click the search icon.

       Click  next to gde.apifabric.builder.test.active and modify the gde.apifabric.builder.test.active configuration based on site requirements.
        
         The options are as follows:
         
          If this parameter is set to true, the deployment and commissioning function is enabled.

          If the parameter is set to false, the deployment and commissioning function is disabled.

         

        

      

    

   

   
    Prerequisites

    An API has been added.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required.

     Choose Develop API and click the API to be deployed. The Deploy and Test tab page is displayed.
      

      For an API that has been developed, click the Deploy and Test tab. For an API that has not been developed, click Next to go to the Deploy and Test tab page.

      

     Commission an API.
      

      
       Click Deploy to deploy the API to API Governance.

       Set the parameters to be carried, click Execute, and wait until a response is returned.
        After the response is returned, view the returned result in the text box below.

       Click the Log tab to view all the log information returned by the current calling.
        

        

      

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After the API is deployed to the runtime-state environment, you can perform the following operations on the Debugging page:

    
     Locate and analyze.
      If the cause of the calling failure cannot be located by viewing logs, click Locate and analyze.

      On the Locate and analyze page, locate the exception in the calling process.

      

      

     View log information of the corresponding diagram element.
      Click a diagram element to view detailed log information, as shown in the following figure.

      

      

     Click Execute. The current request parameters are cached. If you have modified the request parameters on the Design API tab page, click Reset Parameters to refresh the request parameters.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Develop API

name: Importing or Exporting an API
title: Importing or Exporting an API
text:
Importing or Exporting an API
 
 
  
  

  
   When an API is exported, the endpoint referenced by the API, full public definition, and catalog information about the API are automatically exported. The exported asset package can be used for API reuse or deployment to the API Governance.

   The exported ZIP package contains two directories:

   
    catalog: stores APIs by API catalog.

    common: stores southbound ports and common resources referenced by APIs.

   

   Figure 1 shows the API structure in catalog\{Catalog name}.

   
    api: stores API definition files.

    source\config: stores endpoint description files.

    source\bpm: stores data mapping files.

    source\js: stores scripts.

    .mf: asset signature list file, including the file directory and hash value corresponding to the file.

    .cms: signature file generated after the .mf file is digitally signed.

    .package: description file used to identify the type of packages that are being imported to the API Governance portal. In the ADC scenario, the .package file records information such as inbound APIs, outbound APIs, and project modules.

   

   
    Figure 1 API storage structure
    
   

   
    Constraints

    
     In GDE 26.1.0 and later versions, a signature certificate can be selected during API export.
     
      You can use the API Fabric default signature certificate GDE_API-FABRIC_SIGN and the XMS default signature certificate acm.sign.jks. If you need to use a new self-issued certificate of the XMS, name it in the format of GDE_API-FABRIC_****, for example, GDE_API-FABRIC_custom.

      When importing API asset packages from the develop state environment of GDE 26.1.0 or later to the runtime state environment of a version earlier than GDE 26.1.0, select the GDE_API-FABRIC_SIGN signature certificate during the export of the API asset packages.

      The API Fabric polls the signature certificate, signature verification certificate, and certificate revocation list every 5 minutes. In this case, the certificates displayed in the develop state environment cannot be synchronized in real time.

     

    

   

   
    Prerequisites

    An API has been added by referring to Adding an API.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Select Inbound API or Outbound API as required and click Develop API.

     Select the API to be exported.
      

      Select one or more APIs to be exported. Batch export by directory is supported.

      

     Click Export and select a signature certificate.
      

      
        
       
        
         APIs with only initial definitions, such as API names, protocols, and methods, cannot be imported to the API Fabric runtime state. Before importing APIs to the API Fabric runtime state, complete API development activities such as Process Orchestration and Policy Configuration on the Develop API page.

         In an exported API package, the value of stage in the definition.yaml file indicates the API package status.
          The API Fabric runtime state does not import API packages whose stage value is defined (indicating that the APIs are not orchestrated). Attempts to doing so will be ignored. Only when the APIs are orchestrated, which turns the stage value to developing, such an API package can be imported to the API Fabric runtime state.

title: (Optional) Creating a Test Stub
text:
(Optional) Creating a Test Stub
 
 
  
  

  
   If no real test case exists in the API Tester, add a simulation stub and use the test stub to perform the test.

   Only the SOAP and REST protocols are supported.

   
    Procedure

    
     Click the API name, click the Test Stub tab, and click New Test Stub. The page for creating a test stub is displayed.

     Enter the test stub information based on site requirements. The parameters are described in Table 1.
      

      
       
       
        
         Table 1 Test stub parameters
        
        
         
         
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Category

          
           Parameter

          
           Description

          
           Example

         

        
        
         
          
           Basic Information

          
           Policy Type

          
           If multiple response packets exist, this policy is used to determine the response to be returned.

           You need to select a value from the drop-down list as required.

          
           Sequential return

         

         
          
           Match Rule

          
           -

          
           Add the information as required.

           For details about the parameters, see Table 2.

          
           For details, see Table 2.

         

         
          
           Response Message

          
           -

          
           Custom message returned by the test stub.

           After entering the response message name, click + in the response message area to add the content of the response body and response header.

           
             NOTE: 
            
             Configure the SOAP response message structure based on site requirements.

            

           

          
           {
    "orderBaseInfo": {
        "accessChanelType": "",
        "beId": 0,
        "createDeptId": 0,
        "createOperId": 0,
        "interactionEventId": 0,
        "orderId":10,
    }
}

         

        
       
      

      
       
       
        
         Table 2 Matching rule parameters
        
        
         
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

          
           Example

         

        
        
         
          
           Match Parameter

          
           Body: Request parameter.

           Header: Request header.

           
             NOTICE: 
            
             A header indicates the request header configured by a user on the test case page. These values will be contained in the protocol header of a message. The header here is different from the header configured in the BES business code.

            

           

          
           Body

         

         
          
           Match Way

          
           Select JsonPath.

           If this parameter is set to JsonPath, set Match Rule to JsonPath/XPath.

          
           JsonPath

         

         
          
           Match Rule

          
           If the matching rule is JSONPath, set this parameter by referring to the rule for setting JSONPath.

           For example, if Match Parameter is set to Body, set Match Rule to a field name or path name in the method request body.

          
           test

         

         
          
           Expected Value

          
           Expected value.

           For example, if the value of test in Match Rule is 101, the test case is passed. If the value of test is not 101, the test case fails.

          
           101

         

        
       
      

      

     After configuring the test stub, click Save. The Test Stub page is displayed.

     Click the start-stop button to start the test stub server.
      

      After the test stub server is started, you cannot edit the information about the test stub server. You need to stop the test stub server before updating it.

name: Creating a Test Case
title: Creating a Test Case
text:
Creating a Test Case
 
 
  
  

  
   In the API Tester, you need to add a test case in the system. This section describes how to add a test case. By managing test cases, API test results and success rates are generated automatically, online, and visually.

   
    Procedure

    
     Select the API to which the test case is to be added.

     Go to the API test case page and perform the API test. The following two types of test scenarios are available. You can select a test scenario based on site requirements.
      

      
        
       
        Test cases can be called in the following three modes: Invoke Test Stub, Invoke Service Address, and Use the API invocation rule. Invoke Test Stub and Invoke Service Address are the calling modes configured during case creation. Use the API invocation rule is the global calling mode of the API test case configured above the test case list.

        Use the API invocation rule (the calling mode selected above the test case list) is the global calling mode of all test cases in the API. The calling mode (Invoke Test Stub or Invoke Service Address) configured in the test case applies only to the test case. The calling mode is used in the following scenarios:

        
         When you need to call the test stub of the test service, select Invoke the test stub.

         When you need to call a test case through a specific path, select Invoke the base path.

        

       

      

      
       If there are real test cases, click Import Test Case. In the dialog box that is displayed, select local test cases and import them.
        You can also click New Test Case to manually add a case.

        After the configuration is completed, click the Execute button or return to the API page. On the API page, click  of the case.

        After the execution is complete, view the execution result in the response body on the case page. If the execution is successful, a success response is returned. If the execution fails, an error cause message is displayed.

       If there are no real test cases, add a test stub based on 6.2.4 (Optional) Creating a Test Stub, and use the test stub for test.
        
         After the test stub is configured, click the Test Case tab and click New Test Case. The page for adding a test case is displayed.

         Configure test case information based on site requirements.

         Click Save and Execute to execute the test case.

         After the execution, if the response body is the same as that in the test stub, the test is successful.

        

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Test API

name: Configuring a Connector
title: Configuring a Connector
text:
Configuring a Connector
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to configure a connector. Connectors can integrate applications with third-party APIs, databases, and standard integration protocols. You can directly reuse a configured connector during flow orchestration to simplify the flow for connecting to a third-party system.

   
    Application Scenario

    
     After the configured connector is exported and imported to the runtime state, it is directly called by a third-party service.

     During API orchestration, reference the configured connector, as shown in the following figure.
      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access the connector page.
      

      
       Log in to the GDE data zone and choose Products and Services > Development State Studio.

       After a project is created, the page for creating a module is displayed. After the module is created, click More.

       Select Connector under Openness Integration and click Save.

       Click Connector in the navigation pane.

      

      

     Create a connector.
      

      
       Click Create.

       On the Basic Information tab page, set related parameters. The following table describes the parameters. 
        
         
          
           Table 1 Connector parameters
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Connector Name

            
             User-defined connector name, which must be unique under the same tenant.

           

           
            
             Icon

            
             Icon of a connector. You can customize or select a built-in icon.

           

           
            
             Sharing Level

            
             Sharing level of the connector asset.

             
              Public: All services of the current tenant can use this connector.

              Protected: Only services in the same project can use this connector.

              Private: Only services in the same module of the same project can use this connector.

             

           

           
            
             Description

            
             User-defined description.

           

           
            
             Authentication Type

            
             Authentication type of the connector. The supported authentication types are subject to the WebUI.

           

           
            
             More Settings/Tags

            
             Field used to mark the connector. Labels provider (connector provider) and type (connector type) are preset.

           

          
         
        

       Click Next.

      

      

     Configure the connection.
      

      
       Click Create.

       In the Create Connection dialog box, configure the connection information. The following table describes the parameters. 
        
         
          
           Table 2 Connection parameters
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Connection Name

            
             User-defined connection name.

           

           
            
             Service URL

            
             IP address of the third-party server to be interconnected.

           

           
            
             Basic Path

            
             Location of the resource to be accessed. For example, if the base directory is set to /apitest and the server address is set to https://xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx:XXXX, the address used to access the server is https://xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx:XXXX/apitest/{Action execution interface directory}.

           

           
            
             Description

            
             Description of the user-defined connection.

           

          
         
        

       Click Confirm and then Next.

      

      

     Configure an execution action.
      

      
       Click Create.

       On the execution action tab page, set related parameters. The following table describes the parameters. 
        
         
          
           Table 3 Execution action parameters
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Name

            
             User-defined action name, for example, Creating xxx.

           

           
            
             Type

            
             User-defined label.

           

           
            
             Interface Path

            
             Method of configuring the execution action, for example, GET /XXX. The restrictions are subject to the WebUI.

           

           
            
             Description

            
             User-defined description.

           

           
            
             Request Parameter

            
             Input parameters required by the connector to access the backend system (target system accessed by the connector), including BODY, HEADERS, PATH, and QUERY.

           

           
            
             Response Parameter

            
             Output parameters returned by the connector to the API caller after the connector receives a response from the backend system, including BODY and HEADERS.

           

           
            
             Media Type/Referenced Parameter

            
             Body of the request or response. The body content can be set based on the specified media type or directly reference parameters.

             
              Media type: The connector performs serialization and parsing operations based on the media type, generates correct request packets, and parses backend response messages.
               API Fabric supports multiple media types. The media types are subject to the WebUI. For example, if application/yang-data+json is selected, the body content must meet the JSON format of the Yet Another Next Generation (YANG) model.

              Referenced parameter: The media type of the referenced content is inherited.

             

           

          
         
        

       Click Save.

      

      

     Return to the connector page to view the created connector.
      

      You can perform other operations on the created connector as prompted, such as editing, exporting, and deleting the connector.

      

     (Optional) Commission the connector.
      

      
        
       
        
         You can enable or disable the deployment commissioning function as required. The procedure is as follows:
         
          Log in to the GDE data zone as the admin user.

          Choose Products and Services > Administration > Common Setting > Config Management.

          On the Config Center page, enable Display All Configurations in the upper right corner.

          Search for the keyword gde.apifabric.builder.test.active in the search box and click the search icon.

          Click  next to gde.apifabric.builder.test.active and modify the gde.apifabric.builder.test.active configuration based on site requirements.
           
            The options are as follows:
            
             If this parameter is set to true, the deployment and commissioning function is enabled.

             If the parameter is set to false, the deployment and commissioning function is disabled.

            

           

         

        

       

      

      
       Click Commission for the corresponding connector.

       On the commissioning page, click Deploy to deploy the corresponding connector to the runtime state.

       On the Connector Management tab page in the corresponding runtime state, configure connection authentication information.
        The password must be configured after the connector is imported to the runtime state.

       After the configuration is complete, release the connector.

       Go back to the connector commissioning page in the develop state and click Reset Parameters to synchronize the configuration in the runtime state.

       Click Execute.
        If you want to use a connector in the function service center, click CSE Invocation URL to copy the corresponding CSE address.

name: Diagram Elements
title: Diagram Elements
text:
Diagram Elements
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Branch Diagram Elements

    Branches connect diagram elements in a process.

    Events influence the execution of a process. Usually, each event has a cause and impact.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Branch diagram elements
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Name

        
         Icon

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Sequence branch

        
         

        
         Sequence flow. After a node using a sequence flow is accessed, the process is executed based on the sequence flow direction. A node can have one or more sequence flows.

       

       
        
         Condition branch

        
         

        
         Conditional flow. A process using conditional flows can be executed only when required conditions are met. A node can have one or more conditional flows. Double-click a connection line to add a determination function.

       

       
        
         Default branch

        
         

        
         Default flow. When no condition is met for the conditional flows on a node, the default flow is used to execute the process. A node can have only one default flow.

       

       
        
         Mutually exclusive branch

        
         

        
         Exclusive gateway, which is used to determine the output flow in the process (the calculation result of the output flow without any condition is true). When multiple output flows exist, only the first flow that meets the conditions is executed.

         
          A conditional flow can be defined for the exclusive gateway diagram element. If the calculation result of the conditional flow is true, the process is executed properly.

          Multiple conditional flows can be defined for the exclusive gateway diagram element. If the calculation results of all conditional flows are false and the default flow is not defined, an error is reported, and the process ends.

         

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Event Diagram Elements

    Events influence the execution of a process. Usually, each event has a cause and impact.

    
     
      
       Table 2 Event diagram elements
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Name

        
         Icon

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Start

        
         

        
         Start event, indicating the start of a service process.

         
          A service process can contain only one start event diagram element.

          This diagram element does not have any entry connection line but can have multiple exit connection lines.

         

       

       
        
         End

        
         

        
         End event, indicating the end of a service flow.

         
          A service process can contain one or more end event diagram elements.

          The end event diagram element can have multiple entry connection lines.

          Each branch in a service process can connect to an end event diagram element separately.

         

       

       
        
         Exception

        
         

        
         Exception capture diagram element.

         The process variable _exception is preset. The variable contains the following parameters: _exception.name (name of an exception) and _exception.cause (details of an exception).

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Call Service Diagram Elements

    These diagram elements are protocol conversion diagram elements, which are used to associate southbound services to be called by northbound APIs.

    
     
      
       Table 3 Call service diagram elements
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Name

        
         Icon

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         REST

        
         

        
         Endpoint of the REST protocol.

       

       
        
         SOAP

        
         

        
         Endpoint of the SOAP protocol.

       

       
        
         MQ

        
         

        
         Endpoint of the MQ protocol.

       

       
        
         TCP+XML

        
         

        
         Endpoint of the TCP+XML protocol.

       

       
        
         Connector

        
         

        
         Connector.

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Task Diagram Elements

    A task diagram element indicates an activity on a node in a service process. A task cannot be divided into smaller subtasks.

    Events influence the execution of a process. Usually, each event has a cause and impact.

    
     
      
       Table 4 Task diagram elements
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Name

        
         Icon

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Parameter script

        
         

        
         Script task, which contains pre-compiled scripts. When the script task is executed, the scripts in the task will also be executed.

       

       
        
         Parameter mapping

        
         

        
         Mapping diagram element, which configures data mapping between source and target process variables.

       

       
        
         Subprocess

        
         

        
         Subprocess calling diagram element, which is used to call a defined common subprocess.

       

      
     
    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Appendix

text:
Preset Function Reference
 
 
  
  

  
   The JavaScript function is preconfigured by the tool and used in the process orchestration or responsibility chain (such as flow control, authentication, and data mapping) policies.

   The auxiliary functions defined here are common functions and are used by all APIs of a project.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     An API has been added.

     You have accessed the auxiliary functions tab page.

    

   

   
    Redis Service

    Currently, the tool does not support the import of the deployed Redis service. You can directly add the deployed Redis service on the API Manager. You can use the preconfigured JavaScript function to access the deployed Redis service.

    The preconfigured JavaScript functions are as follows for accessing the Redis instance:

    
     Global Redis
      
       _redis

       redis.GLOBAL
        
         JavaScript function example:
         redis.GLOBAL.set("request ", "123123123")
        

      

     Tenant Redis: redis.forName("redisName")
      
       JavaScript function example:
       redis.forName("redis1").set("response", response);
redis.GLOBAL.set("request ", "123123123")
      

    

    The API Fabric uses the Spring and Jedis components as the Redis client. The common methods supported by each instance are as follows:

    /**

 */

/**

double hincr(String keyName, String item, double by);

text:
JSONPath Usage
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Function Overview

    JSONPath is used in JSON to replace XPath. The greatest advantage of XML is that a large number of tools can be used to analyze, convert, and selectively extract data from a document. XPath is one of these most powerful tools.

    If XPath can be used to parse JSON, the following problems can be solved:

    
     The data does not use special scripts. You can find and obtain the scripts on the client.

     The JSON data requested by the client can reduce so that the data amount is the same as that of the data on the server, which minimizes the bandwidth usage for the response of server.

    

   

   
    Expression

    The JSONPath expression is usually used to search for a path or configure JSON. JSONPath is for reference. The XPath expression is used to parse XML documents. JSON data structures are usually anonymous and do not need to have root elements. JSONPath uses $ to represent the outermost object.

    The JSONPath expression format is as follows:

    
     $.store.book[0].title

     $['store']['book'][0]['title']

    

   

   
    Element Description

    Compare JSONPath syntax elements and the corresponding XPath elements. Table 1 describes the result.

    
     
     
      
       Table 1 Element comparison
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         XPath

        
         JSONPath

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         /

        
         $

        
         Root element, that is, root node object to be queried, which is used to indicate JSON data. The element can be an array or an object.

       

       
        
         .

        
         @

        
         Current element, that is, node object processed by the filter predicate. The element is similar to the this field in Java.

       

       
        
         /

        
         . or []

        
         Sub-element.

       

       
        
         ..

        
         n/a

        
         Element.

       

       
        
         //

        
         ..

        
         Recursive decrease. The element of the JSONPath is referenced from E4X.

       

       
        
         *

        
         *

        
         Wildcard, indicating all elements.

       

       
        
         @

        
         n/a

        
         Attribute access character.

       

       
        
         []

        
         []

        
         Sub-element operator.

       

       
        
         |

        
         [,]

        
         Connection operator for calculating two node sets in XPath. Example:

         //book | //cd: All nodes with the book and cd elements are returned.

         JSONP: The element can be a name or an array index.

       

       
        
         n/a

        
         [start:end:step]

        
         Array partitioning operation, which is referenced from ES4.

       

       
        
         []

        
         ?()

        
         Application filtering expression.

       

       
        
         n/a

        
         ()

        
         Script expression, which is used under the script engine.

       

       
        
         ()

        
         n/a

        
         XPath group.

       

      
     
    

    
      
     
      
       []: In the XPath expression, the element always uses the previous path to operate the array. The index starts from 1.

       Use the [] operator of JOSNPath to operate an object or array. The index starts from 0.

      

     

    

   

   
    Example

    Use examples to practice the JSONPath expression. The following is a simple JSON structure constructed based on the XML example (original XML file) of a bookstore:

    { "store": {
    "book": [ 
      { "category": "reference1",
        "author": "Nigel Rees",
        "title": "Sayings of the Century",
        "price": 8.95
      },
      { "category": "fiction1",
        "author": "Evelyn Waugh",
        "title": "Sword of Honour",
        "price": 12.99
      },
      { "category": "fiction1",
        "author": "Herman Melville",
        "title": "Moby Dick",
        "isbn": "0-553-21311-3",
        "price": 8.99
      },
      { "category": "fiction1",
        "author": "J. R. R. Tolkien",
        "title": "The Lord of the Rings",
        "isbn": "0-395-19395-8",
        "price": 22.99
      }
    ],
    "bicycle": {
      "color": "red",
      "price": 19.95
    }
  }
}
    
     
      
       Table 2 Comparison between XPath and JSONPath expressions
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         XPath

        
         JSONPath

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         /store/book/author

        
         $.store.book[*].author

        
         Authors of books in the store.

       

       
        
         //author

        
         $..author

        
         All authors.

       

       
        
         /store/*

        
         $.store.*

        
         All elements of the store, including all booksts and bicycles.

       

       
        
         /store//price

        
         $.store..price

        
         Price of all things in the store.

       

       
        
         //book[3]

        
         $..book[2]

        
         Third book.

       

       
        
         //book[last()]

        
         $..book[(@.length-1)]

        
         Last book.

       

       
        
         //book[position()<3]

        
         $..book[0,1]

        
         First two books.

       

       
        
         $..book[:2]

       

       
        
         //book[isbn]

        
         $..book[?(@.isbn)]

        
         Selects all the books that contain isbn.

       

       
        
         //book[price<10]

        
         $..book[?(@.price<10)]

        
         Selects books whose price is lower than 10.

       

       
        
         //*

        
         $..*

        
         All elements.

       

      
     
    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Appendix

name: Array Mapping Rule
title: Array Mapping Rule
text:
Array Mapping Rule
 
 
  
  

  
   When data mapping is performed during process orchestration, for arrays that in the same dimensions or different dimensions, the tool generates JS code rules based on the mapping scenario.

  

  
   
    Array in the Same Dimension

    Arrays in Different Dimensions

   

   
    
     Parent topic: Appendix

name: Array in the Same Dimension
title: Array in the Same Dimension
text:
Array in the Same Dimension
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Processing Rules

    The rules for JS script processing are as follows for the arrays in the same dimension but in different mapping scenarios:

    
     Assign a value on only the root element. The tool assigns a value on the array object.

     Assign a value on only the sub-element. The tool generates the following FOR loop statement:
      for(int i = 0; i<X.length; i++){
Z.[i].e = X[i].a;
Z.[i].f = X[i].b;
}

     Assign values on the root element and sub-element, as shown in Figure 1. The tool assigns values on the array objects.
      
       Figure 1 Assigning values on the root element and sub-element
       
      

    

    The value in the Js Editor window has a higher priority than that in Array Mapping code generated by system. That is, if a user assigns a value on an array, as shown in Figure 2, the tool uses the value as the actual mapping value. The JS in Array Mapping code generated by system does not take effect.

    
      
     
      The code in Array Mapping code generated by system is automatically generated by the tool for reference but cannot be modified.

     

    

    
     Figure 2 Example of value priority
     
    

   

   
    Mapping Description

    For the mapping of arrays in the same dimension, directly connect the sub-element to be mapped in the array, as shown in Figure 3.

    
     Figure 3 Sub-element mapping
     
    

    After the mapping is complete, perform the following steps to view the mapping script generated by the tool:

    
     Click  next to the root element of the mapped array in the mapping target, as shown in the red box in the preceding figure.
      

      The Js Editor window is displayed.

      

     Click the button to generate intermediate code in the data mapping.

    

    If the connection for the mapping of a sub-element cannot meet the requirement, you need to use a script for editing. In the Js Editor window, configure the mapping self-array option, as shown in Figure 4 and Figure 5.

    
     Figure 4 User-defined mapping value
     
    

    
     Figure 5 Specified mapping source array
     
    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Array Mapping Rule

name: Arrays in Different Dimensions
title: Arrays in Different Dimensions
text:
Arrays in Different Dimensions
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Processing Rules

    The rules for JS script processing are as follows for the arrays in different dimensions and in different mapping scenarios:

    
     Root element Y is mapped to Z, as shown in Figure 1. The tool generates the following code:
      Z = X[0].Y
      
       Figure 1 Mapping root element Y to Z
       
      

     Sub-element Y is mapped to sub-element Z, as shown in Figure 2. The tool generates the following code:
      Z[0].e = X[0].Y[0].a 
Z[0].f =  X[0].Y[0].b
      
       Figure 2 Mapping sub-element Y to sub-element Z
       
      

     Assign values on the root element and sub-element, as shown in Figure 3. The tool assigns values on the array objects.
      For(int i=0;i<Y.length;i++){
     Z[i].e = X[0].Y[i].a;
     Z[i].f = X[0].Y[i].b;
}
      
       Figure 3 Assigning values on both the root element and sub-element in different dimensions
       
      

      The priorities of the value in the Js Editor window and of the intermediate code generated in data mapping are the same as those in Array in the Same Dimension.

    

   

   
    Mapping Procedure

    To map arrays in different dimensions, perform the following steps without sequence.

    
     Connect the root elements of two arrays.
      Two arrays of different dimensions need to be mapped, as shown in Figure 4.

      
       Figure 4 Connecting the root element
       
      

    

    
     Connect sub-elements in the array,
      as shown in Figure 5.

      
       Figure 5 Connecting the sub-elements
       
      

    

    Based on Mapping Description, you can view the mapping script generated by the tool or handle the problem indicating that the sub-element connection cannot meet the requirements.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Array Mapping Rule

GDELink Mobile App Orchestration
 
 
  
  

  
   To support mobile app development of GDE developers, GDELink provides visualized Web-based orchestration pages, rich orchestration resources, low-barrier drag-and-drop development mode, and flexible and convenient UI customization capabilities. In addition, it has the following advantages: native code expansion of the mobile app, integration of custom plugins, HTML5 apps, and applets, and flexible release and upgrade management modes for mobile apps to achieve custom packaging and release or upgrade management for services. GDELink provides multi-layer orchestration and development capabilities in multiple dimensions and at multiple intervals to enable ecosystem users and partners to quickly build mobile app capabilities and support efficient implementation of various mobile office solutions. This section describes how to orchestrate the GDELink mobile app.

text:
Overview of the Mobile Page Development
 
 
  
  

  
   When frontline engineers need to execute field tasks, for example, checking base stations, they need to view task assignment, take and upload photos, and confirm the process on their mobile phones. Therefore, mobile apps are required. GDELink is an execution platform on the mobile phone. Developers can develop apps on ADC, orchestrate mobile pages, and release mobile apps to GDELink. You can obtain GDELink from the app store on the mobile phone, and obtain various service apps provided by developers from GDELink.

   
    Figure 1 Mobile app
    
   

   Mobile pages can be rendered in the GDELink style or compatible Mateline style.

   By default, the Mateline style is used. To use the GDELink style, set the tenant-level system parameter mobile_engine_type. For details, see Data Zone Configuration > Data Zone Configuration (default Tenant) > Mobile Service Configuration > Mobile Service Parameter Configuration > Tenant-Level System Parameters in GDE x.x.x Product Documentation.

Example - Configuring the Photo Upload Page
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    
     A project and a module have been created.

    Scenario

    When executing tasks, field engineers need to take photos and upload the photos to the system. Therefore, you need to configure a page that allows field engineers to take photos, write remarks, and submit settings.

    
     Figure 1 Scenario description
     
    

    The service configuration is not described in detail here. You only need to focus on the development of the mobile page.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access the project and module that need to orchestrate the mobile page.

     Choose Mobile Page.

     Click , set the page name, and click OK.
      

      

      

      

     On the BasicControls tab page, drag the required component to the canvas or component tree.
      

      
       Drag Form Panel to the canvas, and drag Photograph and Text Input to the Form Panel > Data Fields directory and Service Button to the Form Panel > Button directory.
       
        Figure 2 Component tree
        
       

      

      

     Set properties of the Form Panel component.
      

      
       Figure 3 Properties of the Form Panel component
       
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Property description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Id

          
           Component ID, which is used to identify the parameter transferred during service calling

           To obtain the parameter value of the bbb component (the value of Id of Form Panel is aaa) in the form panel aaa (the value of Id of Form Panel is aaa), write as follows:

           #Form[aaa.bbb]
           For details about the application scenario, see the parameter configuration of Service Button in 8.

         

        
       
      

      

     Configure the properties of the Photograph component.
      

      
       
        
         Table 2 Property description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Total

          
           Maximum number of photos that can be uploaded

         

         
          
           Id

          
           Component ID, which is used to identify the field transferred during service calling

         

         
          
           Name

          
           Component name, which must be unique on the current page

         

         
          
           Photo Title

          
           Component name visible to users, which is similar to the display name For example, if this parameter is set to Photo Here, the Photo Here component is visible to users.

         

        
       
      

      

     Configure the properties of the Text Input component.
      

      
       
        
         Table 3 Property description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Id

          
           Component ID, which is used to index the field name in the service

         

         
          
           Name

          
           Component name, which must be unique on the current page

         

         
          
           Label

          
           Component label, which is the component name visible to users and is similar to the display name For example, if Label is set to Remarks, the Text Input component is used to enter remarks.

         

        
       
      

      

     Configure the properties of the Service Button component.
      

      
       
        
         Table 4 Property description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Interface

          
           Service triggered by the service button, which can be a service or an API Set this parameter to the service triggered when clock-in/out data is submitted.

         

         
          
           Id

          
           Component ID

         

         
          
           Text

          
           Component label, which is the component name visible to users and is similar to the display name

         

         
          
           Parameters

          
           Set this parameter to the input parameter of the corresponding service. For example, if task_record_create is selected for Service ID and two input parameters photo and remark are required, you need to define how to obtain the values of these two parameters.

           

           
            The value of photo is obtained from the Photograph component (Id is set to photo) in the Form Panel area, that is, #Form[aaa.photo].

            The value of remark of the Text Input component (Id is set to remark) is obtained from the Form Panel area, that is, #Form[aaa.remark].

           

         

         
          
           Styles

          
           Multiple button styles are preconfigured in the system. You can select different button styles and colors from Style and CSS Class.

         

        
       
      

      

     Save the configuration, and click Preview to view the effect.
      

      
       Figure 4 Page effect

    After an app is developed, choose Products and Services > Administration > GDELink Mobile Management > Light App Management > App Management in the runtime-state environment to release the app. For details, see Data Zone Configuration > Data Zone Configuration (default Tenant) > Mobile Service Configuration > Light App Management.

title: Installing the CLI Offline Tool
text:
Installing the CLI Offline Tool
 
 
  
  

  
   Use the CLI offline tool to develop highly complex pages using codes.

   
    Prerequisites

    A Node.js whose version is between v14.17.1 and v18.20.1 has been installed.

    
     To check the Node.js version, open the CMD window on the local PC and run node -v on the CLI to check the node version.

     You can download Node.js from https://nodejs.org/en/download/. If the version of the installed Node.js is too early, download and install it.

     There is a version mapping between Node.js and npm. Ensure that the NPM version matches the Node.js version based on the mapping provided in Nodejs Version Mapping to avoid version mismatch caused by manual npm upgrade.
      Method of checking the NPM version: Open the CMD command window on the local host and run the npm -v command to check the NPM version.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access a created project and module.

     Download the CLI offline tool.
      

      Portal 1:

      
       In the navigation pane, choose Page > Orchestration Resource > Customized Page.

       Click Download in the upper right corner of the page to download the tool package to the local PC.

      

      Portal 2:

      
       In the navigation pane, choose Page > Orchestration Resource > Customized Page Components.

       Click Download CLI in the upper part of the page to download the tool package to the local PC.

      

      

     In a local file directory, hold Shift, right-click in the blank area, and choose Open PowerShell Here or Open PowerShell window here (S) from the shortcut menu.

     Run npm config edit to check the NPM repository configuration. In the displayed .npmrc file, check whether the file contains the following configuration information:
      

      no-proxy=.huawei.com
registry=https://cmc.centralrepo.rnd.huawei.com/npm
@adc:registry=https://cmc.centralrepo.rnd.huawei.com/artifactory/api/npm/product_npm/@adc/
@gde:registry=https://cmc.centralrepo.rnd.huawei.com/artifactory/api/npm/product_npm/@gde/
strict-ssl=false
      If the file does not contain the information, add the information to the file, save the file, and close the file.

Usage: adc [options] [command]

           Developer Type

          
           Resource development permission control, that is, developers to whom the permissions to view, use, and delete themes are assigned.

           
            PERSONAL: Grant the development permission only to the individual who creates the asset.

            TEAM: Grant the development permission to a specified team.

name: Expressions for Dynamically Accessing Component Property Values
title: Expressions for Dynamically Accessing Component Property Values
text:
Expressions for Dynamically Accessing Component Property Values
 
 
  
  

  
   Dynamic variable parameters are used in scenarios where dynamic parameters need to be transferred during page orchestration. For example, if the initialization of a list page needs to call a service to query data and the service input parameter needs to transfer an ID contained in the page URL, you can use #Get[id] during service configuration to dynamically obtain the ID in the URL.

   
    
     
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Variable

       
        Description

      

     
     
      
       
        #Get[xxx]

       
        Obtained the parameter value transferred from the source page,

        for example, Nf.PageManager.open ("/demo/test/PersonSelect," { "task_id": "001"}).

        Use #Get[task_id] to return 001.

      

      
       
        #Row[xxx]

       
        Available in the list view component, indicating that the field data, for example, #Row[leavel_id], corresponding to the row list is obtained.

      

      
       
        #Sys[xxx]

       
        Obtained the values of variables including #Sys[utc]: provided by the system, or obtained the current UTC time.

        #Sys[now]: Obtained the current time. #Sys[localtime]: Obtained current local time.

        #Sys[username]: Obtained the current user name. #Sys[userinfo]: Obtained the information about the current user.

        #Sys[url]: Obtained the URL of the current page. #Sys[locale]: Obtained the language of the current system.

        #Sys[location]: Obtained the longitude and latitude of the current system.

      

      
       
        #Form[xxx]

       
        Obtained value of a component in a form. For example, #Form[formPanel1.textInput],formPanel1 indicates the ID of the formPanel component, and textInput indicates the ID of the dataField component.

      

      
       
        #ListForm[xxx]

       
        Obtained value of a component in a list form. For example, #ListForm[listForm1.template1.row1.text],listForm1 indicates the ID of the listForm component in the list form, and template1 indicates the form view template.

        row1 indicates the ID of the row component in the row layout, and text indicates the ID of the dataField component.

      

      
       
        #Encode[xxx]

       
        Returned empty string when the value of a parameter is null.

    #Row

    #Sys

    #Form

    #ListForm

name: Component Methods and Events Called Through JavaScript Scripts
title: Component Methods and Events Called Through JavaScript Scripts
text:
Component Methods and Events Called Through JavaScript Scripts
 
 
  
  

  
   MSPL2.0 provides 103 components. For details about the methods and events provided by each component, see the help document provided by the designer.

   For details about how to view a component, move the cursor to the component and click the API Doc link in the lower left corner of the floating box.

   

   The following uses the on method displayed for all components under Form > Data Field as an example.

   
    
     
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Parameter

       
        Description

      

     
     
      
       
        event

       
        Mandatory. Indicates the registration event to be added from the selected element.

      

      
       
        function

       
        Mandatory. Indicates the function that runs when an event occurs.

      

     
    
   

   The following parameters are received: One is the name of the event to be registered, and the other is the callback function to be triggered after the event occurs. If the parameters are used in JavaScript code, refer to the following information.

   //Use the C() method to transfer the component ID to obtain the component instance. Use the .on method to transfer the event name click and callback function function. When the component is clicked, the callback function is executed to record aaa.
C("id").on("click",function(){
  console.log('aaa')
})
C("id").on("change",function(){
  console.log('bbb')
})

    Nf.promptConfirm

    OK and Cancel buttons are displayed in the dialog box.

         Default value: OK

         String

        
         Text of the cancel button

         Default value: Cancel

         Function

        
         Callback of the confirm button

       

       
        
         no

        
         Function

        
         Callback of the cancel button

         Number

        
         (Optional) Waiting time (unit: ms) after which the dialog box is automatically closed

     Nf.promptConfirm({
  title:"prompt title",
  message:"prompt message",
  okText:"confirm",
  cancelText:"exit",
  yes: function () {

  },
  no:function(){

  }
});

text:
APIs Related to Data Acquisition and Submission
 
 
  
  

  
   The Spl.MessageProcessor. loadData API is used to obtain service data. (Ensure that you have obtained related permissions.)

   
    
     
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Property

       
        Type

       
        Description

      

     
     
      
       
        serviceId

       
        String

       
        Service ID

      

      
       
        data

       
        Object

       
        Indicates the submitted parameter.

      

      
       
        canUseWhenOffline

       
        Boolean

       
        Indicates whether offline data submission is allowed. The default value is true.

      

      
       
        showErrorMesisage

       
        Boolean

       
        Indicates whether to display error information. The default value is true.

      

      
       
        silent

       
        Boolean

       
        Indicates whether to submit data in silent mode. The value true indicates that data is submitted in silent mode and loading is not displayed. The default value is false.

      

      
       
        success

       
        Function

       
        Indicates that the callback is successful.

      

      
       
        error

       
        Function

       
        Indicates that the callback fails.

      

     
    
   

   Example:

   Spl.MessageProcessor.loadData({
The serviceId: '/adc-service/web/rest/v1/services/project_test/test/test_contact_tel_create', // Service ID exists.
  data: {
    contact_id: "wu_id",
    telephone: "119"
  },
  success:function(res){
    console.log(res)
  },
  error: function(error) { 
    console.log(error)
  },
  silent: true,
  showErrorMessage: true,
});
   The functions of the parameters of Spl.MessageProcessor. submitData used to submit service data are the same as those of the parameters of Spl.MessageProcessor. loadData.

name: Obtaining the Location Information
title: Obtaining the Location Information
text:
Obtaining the Location Information
 
 
  
  

  
   
    U.getLocation(callback, type, detail)

    
      
     
      
       When calling this API, you need to modify the value of the internationalization resource item whose Key is location_permission_detail to describe the specific usage scenario and purpose (such as providing the attendance service) of the location information. If you do not need such services, you can revoke this permission at any time. Your use of other services will not be affected.

       App developers should determine a proper API calling frequency based on the personal information protection policies, regulations, and standards, and the business scenarios and functions.

      

     

    

    
     
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Parameter

        
         Type

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         callback

        
         String

        
         Callback method name

       

       
        
         type

        
         String

        
         Type. The value can be network or gps (default value).

       

       
        
         detail

        
         String

        
         Details. The value of cityName can be transferred.

       

      
     
    

    Callback Parameters

    
     
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Parameter

        
         Description

        
         Example Value

       

      
      
       
        
         code

        
         Return result. The value can be 0 (success), -1 (obtaining the location failed), or -2 (obtaining the city name failed).

        
         0

       

       
        
         latitude

        
         Latitude

        
         xx.884208516537555

       

       
        
         longitude

        
         Longitude

        
         xx.87906437298003

       

       
        
         cityName

        
         City

        
         XX city

       

       
        
         errorMessage

        
         Error information

        
         get location error

       

      
     
    

    Example:

    U.getLocation(function(result){}, "gps");

U.getLocation(function(result){}, "network");

U.getLocation(function(result){}, "gps", "cityName");
// result: {"code":0,"cityName":"XX city","latitude":"xx.884208516537555","longitude":"xx.87906437298003"}
// result: {"code":-1,"errorMessage":"get location error"} 
// result: {"code":-2,"errorMessage":"get city name error"}

text:
Photo-Taking API
 
 
  
  

  
   
    U.takePhoto(options, callback)

    Used to switch to the native photo-taking page. You can add watermarks to the photos by configuring parameters.

    
      
     
      
       This function is supported on Android and HarmonyOS. The iOS version supports only simple photo taking.

       When calling this API, you need to modify Key to Value corresponding to camera_permission_detail in internationalization resources based on site requirements to describe the application scenario and purpose of the camera. For example, you can scan the QR code to add environment configuration information and take photos to record assets. If you do not need such services, you can revoke this permission at any time. Your use of other services will not be affected.

name: Anonymizing the Log Information
title: Anonymizing the Log Information
text:
Anonymizing the Log Information
 
 
  
  

  
   
    U.mask(message, maskRule) ⇒ String

    
     
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Parameter

        
         Type

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         message

        
         String

        
         Log information

       

       
        
         maskRule

        
         Object

        
         Anonymization rule configuration items

       

      
     
    

    Anonymization Rule Configuration Items (maskRule)

    
     
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Parameter

        
         Description

        
         Example Value

       

      
      
       
        
         type

        
         Anonymization rules. There are several built-in anonymization rules available.

        
         phone

       

       
        
         start

        
         The first several digits of log information are not anonymized.

        
         3

       

       
        
         end

        
         The last several digits of log information are not anonymized.

        
         3

       

       
        
         format

        
         Customized anonymization rule. Sample information with the same length must be provided. Anonymized digits are marked with asterisks (*).

        
         138*00**00**

       

      
     
    

    Example:

    // By default, characters in the even position are anonymized.
U.mask("13800000000"); // 1*8*0*0*0*0  

// Name. If there is only one character, it is anonymized. Otherwise, all characters except the first one are anonymized.
U.mask("Zhang San", { type: "name" }); // Zhang *

// Birthday. If the birthday contains less than or equal to four digits, all digits are anonymized. Otherwise, the digits following the first four digits are anonymized.
U.mask("1900-01-01", { type: "birthday" }); // 1900-**-**  

//Bank account. If the length is less than or equal to 10, all characters except the first and last ones are anonymized. If the length exceeds 12, the first six digits and the last four digits are retained.
U.mask("6200000000000000000", { type: "bankAccount" }); //620000*********0000  

// Email address. Both the emailbox name and address are anonymized.
U.mask("zhangsan@huawei.com", { type: "email" }); // ********@******.com  

// Phone number. Characters except the first three digits and last four digits are anonymized.
U.mask("13800000000", { type: "phone" }); // 138****0000  

// IPv4 address. The last segment is anonymized.
U.mask("127.0.0.1", { type: "ipv4" }); // 127.0.0.*  

// IPv6 address. The last 88 bits are anonymized.
U.mask("fe80:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000", { type: "ipv6" }); // fe80:0000:00**:*:*:***:****:****  

// ID card number. The last 12 characters are anonymized.
U.mask("320000000000000000", { type: "id" }); // 320000************  

// MAC address. The last four digits are anonymized.
U.mask("12-23-56-78-9A-7B-33", { type: "mac" }); // 12-23-56-78-9A-**-**  

// IMEI/IMSI. The last four digits are anonymized.
U.mask("869169030071234", { type: "imeiImsi" }); // 86916903007****  

// Common account. If the length is less than or equal to 1, all characters are anonymized. If the length is less than 8, only the last character is retained. If the length is greater than or equal to 8, the last four characters are retained and other characters are anonymized.
U.mask("defaultAdmin", { type: "accountId" }); // ********dmin  

// If the length is less than or equal to the sum of the values of start and end, all characters except the first and last ones are anonymized. Otherwise, characters at the first start positions and last end positions are retained.
U.mask("13800000000", { start: 4, end: 3 }); // 1380****000  

// Characters are anonymized according to the value of format.
U.mask("13800000000", { format: "0**0*00*000" }); // 1**0*00*000

name: Basic Form Orchestration
title: Basic Form Orchestration
text:
Basic Form Orchestration
 
 
  
  

  
   To display form element components, such as text boxes, some prerequisites need to be configured, including the model, query service, and update service of the form, form submission method, and form display method. The topic describes how to configure the prerequisites.

   
    Orchestration Procedure

    
     Create the components_form model corresponding to a form. The model fields must contain most data types, as shown in the following figure.
      

      

      

     Generate services and pages based on this model.
      

      

      

      

     Drag a Form Panel component to the component tree and set Id to formpanel.
      

      

      

     Drag a Hidden component under Data Fields.
      

      

      

     Set Id of the Hidden component to sid.
      

      

      

     Set Name of the Hidden component to sid.
      

      

      

     Set Value of the Hidden component to 1.
      

      

      
        
       
        sid matches the primary key sid in the model. Therefore, you can configure Value to locate the specific data in the model. For example, if sid is set to 1, subsequent operations on the current form are performed based on the data record whose primary key is 1 in the model.

       

      

      

     Set Require Submission to Yes for the Hidden component.
      

      

      
        
       
        The value of the Hidden component is involved in form data submission only when the property value is Yes.

       

      

      

     Drag a Service Button component under Button.
      

      

      

     Set Interface of the Service Button component to components_form_update.
      

      

      

     Set Success Message of the Service Button component to Data updated successfully!
      

      

      

     Set Text of the Service Button component to Update.
      

      

      

     Drag a Data Loader component under Form Panel.
      

      

      
        
       
        After the form data is updated, preview the form. The Data Loader component calls the interface in 14 to query the returned data.

       

      

      

     Set Interface of the Data Loader component to components_form_get.
      

      

      

     Set the parameters of the Data Loader component in the following figures.
      

      

      

      
        
       
        #Form[formpanel.sid] indicates the value of sid in the formpanel form. The value of sid for the Hidden component in the form can be transferred to the GET service as a parameter.

       

      

      

     After the preceding steps are performed, a basic form is created.
      

      

      

     To view the functions of a form element component, for example, Text Input, drag a Text Input component under Data Fields.
      

      

      

     Set Name of the Text Input component to name, which corresponds to the value of name for the Text component in the model.
      

      

      

      

     Set sid of the Hidden component to a data record in the model. In this example, set sid to 1.
      

      

      

     Preview the page.
      

      

      

     Enter a value in the text box and click Update. The form data has been updated to the data record whose sid is 1 in the model by the service.
      

      

      

     Cancel the preview and preview the page again. Click Data Loader. The form data is displayed.
      

      

      

    

   

   
    Common Issues

    None

title: APIs Related to Nf.PageManager
text:
APIs Related to Nf.PageManager
 
 
  
  

  
   Nf.PageManager.open

   NfPageOpen

   A page redirection function, which is used to open a page.

   Input parameters:

   page (string): Name of the target page, which ends with mspl.

   parameter (object): Parameters related to the target page

   config (object): Configuration of the target page

   
    
     
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Property

       
        Type/Value

       
        Meaning

      

     
     
      
       
        target

       
        String

       
        Whether the target page is an extended page of the current page or a new page.

      

      
       
        -

       
        _self

       
        Extended page

      

      
       
        -

       
        Others

       
        -

      

      
       
        history

       
        Number

       
        Whether to record the history of the target page

      

      
       
        -

       
        Nf.PageManager.History.RECORD

       
        The history of the target page is recorded.

      

      
       
        -

       
        Nf.PageManager.History.REPLACE

       
        The page history of the current page is replaced.

      

      
       
        -

       
        Nf.PageManager.History.NO_RECORD

       
        The history of the target page is not recorded.

      

      
       
        startPoint

       
        Boolean

       
        Whether the page is the start page. If it is, the rollback cannot be performed.

      

      
       
        -

       
        true

       
        The page is a start page.

      

      
       
        -

       
        false

       
        The page is not a start page.

      

      
       
        refresh

       
        Boolean

       
        Whether to refresh the page if the opened page exists.

      

      
       
        -

       
        true

       
        Refresh the page if the opened page exists.

      

      
       
        -

       
        false

       
        Do not refresh the page if the opened page exists.

      

     
    
   

   Example:

   Nf.PageReady(function(){
C("button").on("click",function(){
//The page history of the target page is not recorded.
Nf.PageManager.open("ignoreItemPageHistory_2.mspl","",
{history:Nf.PageManager.History.NO_RECORD});
});
});
   Nf.PageManager.getCurrentPage()

   CurrentPage()

   Used to obtain the object of the current page.

   Input parameters: none

   Example:

   var currentPage1 = CurrentPage();
var currentPage2 = Nf.PageManager.getCurrentPage();
   CurrentPage().parameters[key]

   Used to obtain the parameters transferred from the previous page to the current page.

   Input parameters:

   key (string): Key of a parameter

   Example:

   var taskId = CurrentPage().parameters["task_id"];
   Global

   backto_page()

   Used to return to the previous page.

   Input parameters: none

   Example:

   backto_page()

APIs Related to a Message Box
 
 
  
  

  
   Nf.promptConfirm

   This is a confirmation message box. It provides two buttons: one for confirmation and one for cancellation.

   Input parameters:

   option (object): Parameters of a message box, as listed in the following table.

   
    
     
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Property

        String

       
        (Optional) Text of the cancel button (with a default value)

        function

       
        Callback of the confirm button

        function

       
        Callback of the cancel button

   Nf.promptConfirm({
title:"prompt title",
message:"prompt message",
okText:"confirm",
cancelText:"exit",
yes:function(){
console.log("confirm is clicked");},
no:function(){
console.log("exit is clicked");
}
});
   Alternatively, use the default button and omit the title.

   Nf.promptConfirm({
message:"prompt message",
yes:function(){
console.log("confirm is clicked");
},
no:function(){
console.log("exit is clicked");
}

name: Mask-related APIs
title: Mask-related APIs
text:
Mask-related APIs
 
 
  
  

  
   NfLayout.showMask(message)

   Used to display the page mask. The page mask covers the entire page. As a result, all elements on the page cannot be clicked. This API is usually used to display the loading mask.

   Input parameters:

   message (string): Text displayed on the page mask

   Example:

   NfLayout.showMask(Nf.res("mask.processing"));

   NfLayout.loading(text,style,icon)

   Used to display the page loading mask. There is a dynamic loading circle.

   Input parameters:

   text (string): Displayed text

   style (string): Loading circle color

   
    
     
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Value

       
        Color Value

      

     
     
      
       
        spinner-calm (default value)

       
        #11c1f3

      

      
       
        spinner-stable

       
        #f8f8f8

      

      
       
        spinner-positive

       
        #387ef5

      

      
       
        spinner-light

       
        #ffffff

      

      
       
        spinner-balanced

       
        #33cd5f

      

      
       
        spinner-energized

       
        #ffc900

      

      
       
        spinner-royal

       
        #886aea

      

      
       
        spinner-dark

       
        #444444

      

     
    
   

   icon: String Pattern style of the loading circle

   
    
     
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Value

       
        Style

      

     
     
      
       
        spiral (default value)

       
        Circular vortex, rotating at a constant speed

      

      
       
        android

       
        Default pattern of Android, rotating at an inconstant speed

      

      
       
        ios

       
        Default pattern of iOS, scattering from the center

      

      
       
        ios-small

       
        Mini version of the default iOS loading style

      

      
       
        bubbles

       
        Rotating bubbles

      

      
       
        circles

       
        Rotating circles

      

      
       
        crescent

       
        Rotating semicircles

      

      
       
        dots

       
        Horizontal dots (three dots)

      

      
       
        lines

       
        Vertical line waves, similar to the shape of a common audio

      

      
       
        ripple

       
        Ripples

      

     
    
   

   Example:

   // Default
NfLayout.loading();
// Customized
NfLayout.loading("Loading Service...","spinner-energized","lines");

name: Spl.MessageProcessor.submitData
title: Spl.MessageProcessor.submitData
text:
Spl.MessageProcessor.submitData
 
 
  
  

  
   Used to submit service data.

   Input parameters:

   options (object): Parameters related to submitted service options

   
    
     
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Property

       
        Type

       
        Meaning

      

     
     
      
       
        serviceId

       
        String

       
        Service ID

      

      
       
        data

       
        Object

       
        Submitted parameter

      

      
       
        canUseWhenOffline

       
        Boolean

       
        Whether offline data submission is allowed. The default value is true.

      

      
       
        showErrorMessage

       
        Boolean

       
        Whether to display error information. The default value is true.

      

      
       
        silent

       
        Boolean

       
        Whether silent submission is enabled. The default value is false.

      

      
       
        actionType

       
        String

       
        Submission type. The default value is Update, indicating that the page form will be reloaded after the service request is completed. If the form does not need to be reloaded, you can manually set the value to Delete.

      

      
       
        pageBackWhenError

       
        Boolean

       
        Whether to return to the previous page when an error message is displayed. The default value is true.

      

      
       
        success

       
        Function

       
        Successful callback

      

      
       
        error

       
        Function

       
        Failed callback

      

      
       
        searchConfig

       
        Object

       
        Filter condition

      

      
       
        --contains

       
        Array

       
        Key value array for fuzzy match

      

      
       
        --or

       
        Array

       
        Key value array of the OR relationship

      

      
       
        --orderBy

       
        Object

       
        Sorting field in {"key":"asc"}. The value can be asc or desc.

      

      
       
        --range

       
        Array

       
        Key value array of the range filtering relationship

      

     
    
   

   Example:

   Spl.MessageProcessor.submitData({
serviceId: 'task_work_update',
data: {taskId:"CM-001"},
success:function(){
C("depart_btn").beSubmit=false;},
silent: true
});
   If canUseWhenOffline is set to false, the offline status is unavailable. If the value of this property is true (default or specified), the offline service must be configured as well. Otherwise, the obtained data is inaccurate. The configuration method is as follows: Open the mobilemarket_service_config_grid page in mobilemarket.app, and configure a service with the same name as serviceId and set the type to UPDATE. In addition, when the model field changes, data needs to be submitted to the cache. Otherwise, the GetList service is used to update fields during scheduled synchronization, with certain delay.

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: APIs Related to Data Acquisition and Submission

   Spl.MessageProcessor.loadData({
serviceId: 'task_work_get',
