name: Filter Panel
title: Filter Panel
text:
Filter Panel
 
 
  
  

  
   The Filter Panel component is used together with data viewing components (such as Table) to display data that meets the filter criteria.

   

   
    Properties

    

    

    
     
      
       Table 1 Properties
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Name

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Edit Panel Content

        
         Allows you to drag subcomponents to the filter panel on the displayed sub-canvas.

       

       
        
         Background Color

        
         Allows you to set the background color of the filter panel. A gradient color can be configured.

       

       
        
         Enable Vertical Scrollbar

        
         Specifies whether to display the vertical scrollbar.

       

       
        
         Enable Horizontal Scrollbar

        
         Specifies whether to display the horizontal scrollbar.

       

       
        
         Scrollbar Width

        
         Allows you to set the width of the scrollbar.

       

       
        
         Thumb Color

        
         Allows you to set the color of the scrollbar slider.

       

       
        
         Thumb Radius

        
         Allows you to set the corner radius of the scrollbar slider.

       

       
        
         Track Color

        
         Allows you to set the color of the scrollbar track.

       

       
        
         Track Radius

        
         Allows you to set the corner radius of the scrollbar track.

       

      
     
    

   

   
    APIs

    
     
      
       Table 2 APIs
      
      
       
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         API Name

        
         Description

        
         Parameter

        
         Example

       

      
      
       
        
         getValue

        
         Obtains the values of all input components in the filter panel.

        
         void

        
         S("compId").getValue()

       

       
        
         setValue

        
         Sets values for all input components in the filter panel.

        
         Object. The value of key must be the same as the Name field configured for the input component.

        
         S("compId").setValue({testKey: xxx,...})

       

       
        
         resetValue

        
         Resets the values of all input components in the filter panel to the initial values.

        
         void

        
         S("compId").resetValue()

       

      
     
    

    Configurable subcomponents

name: Iterator
title: Iterator
text:
Iterator
 
 
  
  

  
   The iterator iteratively renders components based on the data in data sources.

   

   
    Properties

    

    

    
     
      
       Table 1 Properties
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Name

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Edit Panel Content

        
         Allows you to drag subcomponents to the iterator on the displayed sub-canvas.

       

       
        
         Empty Message

        
         Prompt message displayed when the original data is empty.

       

       
        
         Column Size

        
         Allows you to set the number of columns displayed in each row of the iterator.

       

       
        
         Page Size

        
         Allows you to set the number of iteration items displayed on each page of the iterator.

       

       
        
         Pagination Or Carousel

        
         Allows you to switch between pagination and carousel display.

       

       
        
         Carousel Direction

        
         Allows you to set the carousel direction.

       

       
        
         Carousel Duration

        
         Allows you to set the carousel duration.

       

       
        
         Hover Pause

        
         Specifies whether to enable the hover pause function.

       

       
        
         Indicator Position

        
         Allows you to set the carousel indicator position.

       

       
        
         Indicator Default Style

        
         Allows you to set the width and height of the carousel indicator in the default state.

       

       
        
         Indicator Activation Style

        
         Allows you to set the width and height of the carousel indicator in the activated state.

       

       
        
         Fill Color

        
         Allows you to set the carousel indicator color.

       

       
        
         Item Width

        
         Allows you to set the width of the iteration item (available when the width is sufficient; otherwise, the width is adaptive).

       

       
        
         Item Height

        
         Allows you to set the height of the iteration item (available when the height is sufficient; otherwise, the height is adaptive).

       

       
        
         Column Spacing

        
         Allows you to set the spacing between columns of the iteration item (available when the width is sufficient; otherwise, the spacing is 0).

       

       
        
         Row Spacing

        
         Allows you to set the spacing between rows of the iteration item (available when the height is sufficient; otherwise, the spacing is 0).

       

      
     
    

   

   
    APIs

    
     
      
       Table 2 APIs
      
      
       
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         API Name

        
         Description

        
         Parameter

        
         Example

       

      
      
       
        
         getValue

        
         Obtains data from the iterator.

        
         -

        
         S("compId").getValue()

       

       
        
         setValue

        
         Sets data for the iterator.

        
         (Array)

        
         S("compId").setValue([{...}])

       

       
        
         reload

        
         Reloads data from the iterator.

        
         -

        
         S("compId").reload()

       

       
        
         registerEvent

        
         Registers the event of the subcomponent in the iterator.

        
         id: ID of the subcomponent in the iterator

         eventType: type of the subcomponent registration event in the iterator

         event: registration event response

        
         S("compId").registerEvent(id, eventType, event)

       

      
     
    

    Configurable components

        Component ID, which can be changed to a required value.

      

      
       
        Size

       
        The value includes width and height of the component. The unit is px.

      

      
       
        Position

       
        The value includes the horizontal coordinate and vertical coordinate of the component. The unit is px. The horizontal coordinate indicates the pixel distance between the upper left corner of the component and the left boundary of the page, and the vertical coordinate indicates the pixel distance between the upper left corner of the component and the upper boundary of the page.

      

      
       
        Rotate

       
        Rotation angle of the component with the center as the center point. The unit is degree (°).

      

     
    
   

   

   

   
    
     
      Table 2 Basic properties

name: About Network Operation Automation
title: About Network Operation Automation
text:
About Network Operation Automation
 
 
  
  

  
   Network O&M personnel, especially senior network O&M personnel, need to perform routine adjustments to network configurations. They need to modify scripts based on their understanding of network products and deliver the scripts to the network through devices or EMS clients. Application Development Center (ADC) provides network operation automation modules with the corresponding orchestration capabilities to standardize and automate routine network configuration change actions. This improves the efficiency of network configuration change actions and reduces network failures caused by manual operations.

   In the develop-state environment, the configuration of the network operation automation module includes the configuration items inside and outside the project.

   

   Basic concepts related to network operation automation are as follows:

   
    Command
     Commands are used by senior network O&M personnel to change routine network configurations. Commands are classified into the following types: general commands, diagnosis commands, proactive maintenance commands, and configuration commands. The execution of diagnosis, configuration, and proactive maintenance commands depends on OWS model APIs. Therefore, the three types of commands are used only in the OWS O&M automation domain. In other domains, general commands are used.

    Script
     Service personnel can compile commands to be sent to devices or EMS clients in Python scripts and associate the commands with scripts to directly execute scripts when commands are executed

    Application scenario
     When the asset development team needs to enable the interworking with devices or EMSs and perform operations such as querying and changing device information, network operation automation can be configured.

    Implementation principle
     The network operation automation module provides a command-related API. Service development personnel can call this API to transfer the login information of the target EMS and device so that the MCP probe can interwork with the target EMS and device. At the same time, the MCP probe sends the commands and returns the execution results to the service development personnel.

Managing APIs
 
 
  
  

  
   Configure APIs to interwork with different data sources, which means that you can obtain the EMS and device information from different systems.

   
    Context

    The APIs for querying the device and EMS authentication information, the device and EMS lists, and the device and EMS details have been imported to the system by default. The system can use the preceding APIs to call different integrated services to query the EMS and device information.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose General Settings > MCP Settings > Interface Management.

     On the displayed page, click Import, download the template, and set parameters.

           description

     Click Import.

Configuring a Command Whitelist
 
 
  
  

  
   Configure a command whitelist. Only commands in the whitelist can be delivered to devices.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     The NE type and vendor have been configured.

     The commands to be delivered have been configured.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose General Settings > MCP Settings > Command Whitelist.

     On the displayed page, click Create and set parameters.
      

      
       Figure 1 Configuring a command whitelist
       
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           NE Type

          
           The value of this parameter must be the same as that of the selected device in the command.

         

         
          
           NE Model

          
           The value of this parameter must be the same as that of the selected device in the command.

         

         
          
           Device Vendor

          
           The value of this parameter must be the same as that of the selected device in the command.

         

         
          
           Protocol

          
           The value of this parameter must be the same as that of the selected device in the command.

         

         
          
           Device Version

          
           The value of this parameter must be the same as that of the selected device in the command.

         

         
          
           Regular Expression

          
           Regular expression of the command that can be executed.

           Set this parameter based on site requirements.

           For example, the command to be executed is as follows:

           LST BTSRETSUBUNIT:IDTYPE=BYNAME,BTSNAME=${btsname},DEVICENO=${deviceno},SUBUNITNO=${subunitno};

           In this command, the regular expression is LST.*.

         

        
       
      

      

    

    
     Click OK.

name: Creating Network Operation Automation Modules
title: Creating Network Operation Automation Modules
text:
Creating Network Operation Automation Modules
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to create network operation automation modules in the created project.

   
    Prerequisites

    A project has been created.

   

   
    Context

    The project template provides a network automation template. You can create a project based on this template or using a blank template.

    
     When a project is created based on the network automation template, the new module automatically displays the menus required for network automation.

     When a project is created based on an existing project or using a blank template, you need to manually adjust the menus to be displayed.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Open a created project.
      

      If the new project does not contain modules, the Create Module dialog box will be displayed after you click the project name.

      

     Create a module.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Module name. The value can contain letters, digits, underscores (_), hyphens (-), and periods (.).

         

         
          
           Prefix

          
           Module prefix, which is used to distinguish different modules for easy search. The value can contain lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (_). The value is obtained from the Name value by default. A maximum of the first five characters can be retained.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Module description.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Create Module.

     (Optional) The Command and Script menus need to be displayed for network operation automation. If the new module does not contain these menus, click  in the lower-left corner to adjust the orchestration elements displayed on the left.

name: Configuring Network Operation Automation Scripts
title: Configuring Network Operation Automation Scripts
text:
Configuring Network Operation Automation Scripts
 
 
  
  

  
   To execute Python script commands, you need to upload the required script to ADC.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     The script file to be uploaded has been obtained.

     The network operation automation module has been created in the project.

    

   

   
    Context

    The system provides the following two types of scripts:

    
     Non-custom script: used for configuration, diagnosis, and preventive maintenance, and in some common scenarios.

     Custom script: used to convert existing non-REST commands to REST commands, and deliver the REST commands to devices without modifying the existing non-REST commands.
      
        
       
        In the same module of a project, only one custom script can be created.

       

      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the network operation automation module page, choose Script from the navigation pane.

     (Optional) Set command parameters.
      

      
       On the Script Management page, click Command Parameter.

       Click Add.

       In the displayed Add Command Parameter dialog box, select the command parameters to be added and click OK.
        

        

      

      

     Create non-custom and custom scripts.
      

      
       On the Script Management page, click Create.

       Configure parameters for a non-custom script.
        

        

        
         
          
           Table 1 Parameter description (for a non-custom script)
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Script Name

            
             Name of a script, which must be the same as the script file name

           

           
            
             Type

            
             Function type of a script

             
              Common

              Configuration

              Diagnosis

              Preventive maintenance

              Custom

             

             In this case, Type must be set to a value other than Custom.

           

           
            
             Script Type

            
             Script type, which can only be set to Python

           

           
            
             Risk Level

            
             Risk level of a script

             
              Low

              Medium

              High

              Critical

             

           

           
            
             Description

            
             Description of a script

           

           
            
             Insert Error Code

            
             Error code used in the script

             Click Insert Error Code. In the displayed dialog box, select the corresponding error code and click OK.

           

           
            
             Insert Command Parameter

            
             Command parameters used in the script

             Click Insert Command Parameter. In the displayed Command Parameter dialog box, select the corresponding command parameters and click OK.

           

           
            
             Script Content

            
             Script file content

           

          
         
        

       Configure parameters for a custom script.
        

        

        
         
          
           Table 2 Parameter description (for a custom script)
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Script Name

            
             Name of a custom script, which can only be set to Other_To_Rest

           

           
            
             Type

            
             Function type of a custom script

             
              Common

              Configuration

              Diagnosis

              Preventive maintenance

              Custom

             

             In this case, Type must be set to Custom.

           

           
            
             Script Type

            
             Type of a custom script, which can only be set to Python

           

           
            
             Risk Level

            
             Risk level of a custom script

             
              Low

              Medium

              High

              Critical

             

           

           
            
             Customized Project

            
             Project list corresponding to a custom script, that is, the projects in which this custom script is used

             Select one or more projects (including the project to which the custom script belongs) based on site requirements. If this parameter is not set, the custom script takes effect in the current project by default.

           

           
            
             Customize Priority

            
             Priority of a custom script. When a project has multiple custom scripts, the custom script with the highest priority takes effect.

             The value ranges from 1 to 10. A smaller value indicates a lower priority. If this parameter is not set, the custom script has the lowest priority by default.

           

           
            
             Description

            
             Description of a custom script

           

           
            
             Insert Error Code

            
             Error code used in a custom script

             Click Insert Error Code. In the displayed dialog box, select the corresponding error code and click OK.

           

           
            
             Insert Command Parameter

            
             Command parameters used in the script

             Click Insert Command Parameter. In the Command Parameter dialog box, select the corresponding command parameters and click OK.

           

           
            
             Script Content

            
             Content of a custom script

             The following methods can be used to customize scripts:

             
              channel.getUsername(): Obtains the user name of the peer device.

              channel.getPassword(): Obtains the password of the peer device.

              channel.sendForRest("GET", url, header, uriVariables, params, body, waitResultTime): Sends REST requests to the peer device.

              channel.waitForCallBackService(taskId, 15000): Waits for the callback result. If the callback result is not returned within 15 seconds, a timeout error message is reported.

             

           

          
         
        

       Click OK.

       (Optional) After the custom script is configured, access the runtime-state environment and choose Products and Services > Network Operation > Resource Management > Device. On the displayed page, modify the user name and password in the device credential corresponding to the existing non-REST command to ensure that the command can be sent to the peer device through the REST protocol.

      

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    
     
      
       Table 3 Operations after the configuration of network operation automation scripts
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Editing a script

        
         In the script list, locate the row that contains the target script, and click Edit in the Operation column to edit or view the script content.

       

       
        
         Deleting a script

        
         In the script list, locate the row that contains the target script, and click Delete in the Operation column to delete the script.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           If a script is referenced by a command instance, the script cannot be deleted. You need to remove the reference before deleting the script.

name: Creating Commands (Form Mode)
title: Creating Commands (Form Mode)
text:
Creating Commands (Form Mode)
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to create a command and command instance using a form.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     The network operation automation module has been created in the project.

     Devices and protocols have been configured.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the network operation automation page, choose Command from the navigation pane.

     On the displayed page, click Create and select Via form.

     On the displayed page, configure command parameters.
      

      
       
       
        
         
          Table 1 Parameter description
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Name

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Command Name

           
            Command name

          

          
           
            Command ID

           
            Unique ID of a command

            This parameter is automatically set based on the value of Command Name. If the command ID is the same as the name of another project module, the system automatically adds this project module name at the end of the command ID.

          

          
           
            Command Type

           
            Command type

            You can set this parameter to Common, Diagnosis, Preventive Maintenance, or Configuration based on site requirements. The last three types of commands can be used only in the OWS O&M automation domain and executed depending on some OWS model APIs. In other domains, you need to set this parameter to Common.

          

          
           
            Risk Level

           
            Risk level of a command

            
             Low

             Medium

             High

             Critical

            

          

          
           
            Time Window

           
            Time window for executing a command

            Example: If the command needs to be executed within 0 to 12 hours, set this parameter to 0~12.

          

          
           
            Description

           
            Description of a command

          

          
           
            Open Level

           
            Open level of a command

            
             Module: The command can only be used by a module.

             Project: When multiple modules exist in a project, the command can be called across modules.

             Public: The command is available in the system.

            

          

          
           
            Register as API

           
            After the command is registered with the API catalog, you can call it as an API and view it on the API Catalog page in the runtime state.

            This parameter is displayed only when Open Level is set to Public.

          

          
           
            API Catalog

           
            API catalog where the command is registered as a public API

            This parameter is displayed only when Register as API is enabled.

          

          
           
            API ShareScope

           
            Sharing scope of the API after the registration. If Open Level of the project to which the command belongs is set to Personal or Public, set API ShareScope to Private or Public. If Open Level of the project to which the command belongs is set to Team, set API ShareScope to Team or Public.

            
             Public: The API can be viewed by all users.

             Personal: The API can be viewed only by the creator.

             Team: The API can be viewed only by team members.

            

            This parameter is displayed only when Register as API is enabled.

          

          
           
            Input

           
            Input parameters of a command

          

          
           
            Output

           
            Output parameters of a command

          

         
        
       

      

      

     Click Next.

     In the command list area, create command details.
      

      
       Select a mode to configure the device information of the command instance based on site requirements.
        
         Exact match mode: Configure the exact device properties for the command. Before delivering a command, the system searches for the target device that exactly matches the device properties (such as the NE type and device vendor) in the command configuration.
          

          

          
           
           
            
             Table 2 Device parameters of a command instance (exact match mode)
            
            
             
             
            
            
             
              
               Name

              
               Description

             

            
            
             
              
               NE Type

              
               NE type, which can be selected only from the NE types added during command creation

             

             
              
               Device Vendor

              
               Vendor of a device

             

             
              
               NE Model

              
               Model of the NE associated with an NE type

             

             
              
               Protocol

              
               Protocol for connecting to the device

               Currently, the following protocols are supported: MML, MOSHELL, SFTP, SSH, TELNET, TL1, ONMML, and REST.

               
                 NOTICE: 
                
                 
                  MML, MOSHELL, TELNET, TL1, and ONMML are insecure. You are advised to use other secure protocols.

                  When a specified protocol is used to send commands or receive packets, the conditions of the protocol must be met. For details about the protocol requirements, see Protocol Restrictions on Network Operation Automation Commands.

                 

                

               

             

             
              
               Device Version

              
               Version of a device, which must be the same as the version configured on the device

             

            
           
          

         Condition matching mode: Configure device matching rules for commands. Before delivering a command, the system searches for the target device that matches the device property rules (such as the NE type and device vendor) in the command configuration.
          
            
           
            Commands configured in customized mode can be executed only after the collection probe is upgraded to 23.2.RC1.

           

          

          

          

          
           
            
             Table 3 Device parameters of a command instance (condition matching mode)
            
            
             
             
            
            
             
              
               Name

              
               Description

             

            
            
             
              
               Matching condition

              
               Matching condition of a device property

               
                is

                contains

                start with

                end with

                empty (only for Device Version)

               

             

             
              
               Value

              
               Value of a device property matching condition. For details about the meaning of each device property, see Table 2.

             

            
           
          

        

       Configure the main command.
        
         Configure the main command of a non-REST protocol.
          

          
           
           
            
             
              Table 4 Main command parameters of a command instance (non-REST protocol)
             
             
              
              
             
             
              
               
                Name

               
                Description

              

             
             
              
               
                Type

               
                Type of a command. The options are as follows:

                
                 Common: indicates that a single command is directly executed.

                

                
                 python: indicates that a Python script is executed.

                

                When Protocol is set to SFTP, Type is set to Common by default.

              

              
               
                python

               
                Python script corresponding to the main command. Click  on the right to create a script, or select an existing script and click  to edit it.

                This parameter is available only when Type is set to python.

              

              
               
                SFTP Command Type

               
                SFTP command type. The options are as follows:

                
                 ls

                 put

                

                This parameter is available only when Protocol is set to SFTP.

              

              
               
                Command

               
                Main command to be sent

                This parameter is available only when Type is set to Common.

                
                  NOTICE: 
                 
                  When Protocol is set to SFTP, the system supports only the following commands by default:

                  
                   ls ${filePath}

                   put ${fileName} ${dstPath} ${batchId}

                  

                 

                

              

              
               
                End Character

               
                End character for obtaining the result during command execution. If the end character is not obtained after the command is executed, the system continues to wait until the command times out.

                This parameter is available only when Type is set to Common.

              

              
               
                Read Result Time Out(1~120s)

               
                Timeout interval for command execution. The value ranges from 1 to 120, in seconds.

              

              
               
                Create Command Whitelist

               
                Determine whether to create a command whitelist.

                
                 Enabled: After a command is created, it is automatically added to the command whitelist.

                 Disabled: After a command is created, it will not be added to the command whitelist. If you need to execute the command in the future, manually add it to the whitelist.

                

                
                  NOTICE: 
                 
                  When Protocol is set to SFTP or the device information of a command instance is configured in condition matching mode, a command whitelist cannot be created.

                 

                

              

              
               
                Pre-executed Command

               
                Pre-processing commands executed prior to the main command

                This parameter is available only when Type is set to Common.

              

              
               
                Analysis Result Expression

               
                The command output is parsed using regular expressions and scripts, formatted, and displayed on the debug page as command output.

                
                 You can select only one parsing mode.

                

                
                 Before configuring a result analysis expression, you need to set at least one output parameter for the command to be created. The analysis result is included in the output parameter and is displayed in the response message on the debug page.

                

                
                 Rules for compiling scripts in the analysis result expression are as follows:
                  
                   The Ruby and Python scripts need to inherit RESULT_HANDLE_BASE and Result_Analyzer_Base, respectively.

                   params, an input parameter in JSON format, is written into the script (self parameter is also required for Python scripts). The analyze method in the base class for editing the command output needs to be re-written. You can compile a regular expression or extract fields and analyze the desired content.

                   The script execution result must be a character string.

                  

                

                This parameter is available only when Type is set to Common.

              

             
            
           

          

         Configure the main command of a REST protocol.
          

          

          
           
            
             Table 5 Main command parameters of a command instance (REST protocol)
            
            
             
             
            
            
             
              
               Name

              
               Description

             

            
            
             
              
               Type

              
               Type of a command. The options are as follows:

               
                Common: indicates that a single command is directly executed.

               

               
                python: indicates that a Python script is executed.

               

             

             
              
               Server Url

              
               Service address corresponding to the main command

               Format: Relative path of the service address without the IP address and port number, for example, /adc-intg/api/rest/v1/zzp/qq/qq_token_auth/hello.

             

             
              
               HTTP Method

              
               HTTP method for connecting to the service address

               
                GET

                POST

                PUT

                DELETE

                PATCH

               

             

             
              
               Content Type

              
               Type of the content sent to the service address when the main command is executed

               
                application/json

                text/plain

                form-data

                x-www-form-urlencoded

               

             

             
              
               python

              
               Python script corresponding to the main command. Click  on the right to create a script, or select an existing script and click  to edit it.

               This parameter is available only when Type is set to python.

               
                 NOTICE: 
                
                 In the Python script used by the main command of the REST protocol type, you can use either of the following methods to send REST messages:

                 
                  channel.sendForRest("POST", url, header, None, None, body, 0)

                  channel.sendForRest(header, None, None, body, 0)

                 

                 The difference between the two methods lies in input parameters. You can select either method based on site requirements.

                

               

             

             
              
               Input Param

              
               Input parameters sent to the service address when the main command is executed

               Click the Header/Path/Query or Body tab, and click Add Sibling Node to add required input parameters, including the name, Parameter Location, type, format, and Mandatory.

               This parameter is available only when Type is set to Common.

             

             
              
               Analysis Result Expression

              
               The command output is parsed using regular expressions and scripts, formatted, and displayed on the debug page as command output.

               
                You can select only one parsing mode.

               

               
                Before configuring a result analysis expression, you need to set at least one output parameter for the command to be created. The analysis result is included in the output parameter and is displayed in the response message on the debug page.

               

               
                Rules for compiling scripts in the analysis result expression are as follows:
                 
                  The Ruby and Python scripts need to inherit RESULT_HANDLE_BASE and Result_Analyzer_Base, respectively.

                  params, an input parameter in JSON format, is written into the script (self parameter is also required for Python scripts). The analyze method in the base class for editing the command output needs to be re-written. You can compile a regular expression or extract fields and analyze the desired content.

                  The script execution result must be a character string.

                 

               

               This parameter is available only when Type is set to Common.

             

            
           
          

        

       (Optional) Configure an anonymization rule for request messages. A regular expression is used to replace the matched character string with *** to anonymize the request command.

       (Optional) Configure an anonymization rule for response messages. A regular expression is used to replace the matched character string with *** to anonymize the command output.

       Click OK to save the settings.

      

      

     Click OK.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Creating Network Operation Automation Commands

name: Creating Commands (Canvas Mode)
title: Creating Commands (Canvas Mode)
text:
Creating Commands (Canvas Mode)
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to create a command and command instance using a canvas.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     The network operation automation module has been created in the project.

     Devices and protocols have been configured.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the network operation automation page, choose Command from the navigation pane.

     On the Command Management page, click Create and select Via canvas.

     In the displayed dialog box, configure basic command properties.
      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Basic command property parameters
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Command Name

          
           Command name

         

         
          
           Command ID

          
           Unique ID of a command. This parameter is automatically set based on the value of Command Name. If the command ID is the same as the name of another project module, the system automatically adds this project module name at the end of the command ID.

         

         
          
           Command Type

          
           Type of a command. You can set this parameter to Common, Diagnosis, Preventive Maintenance, or Configuration based on site requirements. The last three types of commands can be used only in the OWS O&M automation domain and executed depending on some OWS model APIs. In other domains, you need to set this parameter to Common.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Description of a command

         

         
          
           Risk Level

          
           Risk level of a command

           
            Low

            Medium

            High

            Critical

           

         

        
       
      

      

     Click OK to go to the command orchestration canvas.
      

      
       
       
         
        
         
          The command orchestration page consists of the command orchestration element area on the left and the command canvas display area on the right.

          The command orchestration element area on the left includes protocols, main commands, and advanced operations. You can drag and drop a command to the canvas area on the right.

          A complete command instance is displayed in the canvas area on the right. The command instance consists of seven orchestration elements by default.

          The toolbar on the canvas is described as follows:
           
            : Save a complete command.

            : Save the command data configured on the canvas in real time. The command data can be incomplete to facilitate subsequent configuration.

            : Cancel the previous operation.

            : Restore the default settings.

            : Debug commands.

             and : Zoom in and zoom out icons on the canvas.

            : Reset a command to its original position on the canvas.

            : Delete a selected icon or an added command instance.

            : Add a default command instance.

            : Copy the selected instance and its configurations.

            : Drag the canvas to move it.

           

         

        

       

      

      

     Configure basic properties of the command.
      

      
       Click the blank area on the canvas. The Properties > Basic Command Properties page is displayed on the right.

       Configure parameters of the command.
        

        
         
          
           Table 2 Parameter description
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Open Level

            
             Open level of a command

             
              Module: The command can only be used by a module.

              Project: When multiple modules exist in a project, the command can be called across modules.

              Public: The command is opened and can be called in the system.

             

           

           
            
             Register as Public API

            
             After the command is registered with the API catalog, you can call it as an API and view it on the API Catalog page in the runtime state.

             This parameter is displayed only when Open Level is set to Public.

           

           
            
             API Catalog

            
             API catalog where the command is registered as a public API.

             This parameter is displayed only when Register as Public API is enabled.

           

           
            
             API ShareScope

            
             Sharing scope of the API after the registration. If Open Level of the project to which the command belongs is set to Personal or Public, set API ShareScope to Private or Public. If Open Level of the project to which the command belongs is set to Team, set API ShareScope to Team or Public.

             
              Public: The API can be viewed by all users.

              Personal: The API can be viewed only by an individual.

              Team: The API can be viewed only by team members.

             

             This parameter is displayed only when Register as Public API is enabled.

           

           
            
             Risk Level

            
             Risk level of a command

             
              Low

              Medium

              High

              Critical

             

           

           
            
             Time Window

            
             Time window for executing a command

             Example: If the command needs to be executed within 0 to 12 hours, set this parameter to 0~12.

           

           
            
             Description

            
             Description of a command

           

          
         
        

       Click a blank area on the canvas to complete the configuration.

      

      

     (Optional) Set input parameters.
      

      
       Click the input icon.

       On the displayed page, set the input parameters.
        

       Click a blank area on the canvas to complete the configuration.

      

      

     Configure a meta device.
      

      
       Click the Meta Device icon.

       Set NE parameters in either of the following mode based on site requirements.
        
         Exact matching
          

          

         Condition Matching
          

          

        

      

      

     Check whether the protocol element needs to be replaced.
      

      
       To replace the canvas element, perform the following operations:
       
        Select the icon of the element to be replaced on the canvas, and then click  or Delete.

        Drag the element to be replaced from the left to the area where the element is deleted on the canvas. For details, see Figure 1. When the connection turns blue, release the pointer to replace the element.
         
          Figure 1 Replacing a canvas element
          
         

       

      

      

     Configure common commands or script commands.
      

      
       Configuring common commands
        
         Click the Common icon.

         Configure common command parameters.
          
           Common commands of non-REST protocols
            

            
             
              
               Table 3 Common command parameters (non-REST protocol)
              
              
               
               
              
              
               
                
                 Name

                
                 Description

               

              
              
               
                
                 SFTP Command Type

                
                 SFTP command type. The options are as follows:

                 
                  ls

                  put

                 

                 This parameter is displayed only when Protocol is set to SFTP.

               

               
                
                 Command

                
                 Main command to be sent

                 
                   NOTICE: 
                  
                   When Protocol is set to SFTP, the system supports only the following commands by default:

                   
                    ls ${filePath}

                    put ${fileName} ${dstPath} ${batchId}

                   

                  

                 

               

               
                
                 End Character

                
                 End mark for obtaining the result during command execution. If the end character is not obtained after the command is executed, the system continues to wait until the timeout.

               

               
                
                 Read Result Time Out(1~120s)

                
                 Timeout interval for command execution. The value ranges from 1 to 120, in seconds.

               

               
                
                 Create Command Whitelist

                
                 Determine whether to create a command whitelist.

                 
                  Enabled: After a command is created, it will be automatically added to the command whitelist.

                  Disabled: After a command is created, it will not be added to the command whitelist. If you need to execute the command in the future, manually add it to the whitelist.

                   When Protocol is set to SFTP or the device information of a command instance is configured in condition matching mode, a command whitelist cannot be created.

Debugging Network Operation Automation Commands
 
 
  
  

  
   Debug a configured command and enable the execution of the command script.

  

  
   
    Debugging Commands (Form Mode)
      On the command list page, debug commands to verify the correctness of the commands.

    Debugging Commands (Canvas Mode)
      On the command canvas page, debug commands to verify the correctness of the commands.

name: Debugging Commands (Form Mode)
title: Debugging Commands (Form Mode)
text:
Debugging Commands (Form Mode)
 
 
  
  

  
   On the command list page, debug commands to verify the correctness of the commands.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     Devices, protocols, and command whitelists have been configured.

     Commands have been delivered to the probe.

    

   

   
    Context

    There are two methods for debugging a command list:

    
     On the command list page, click Debug in the Operation column.

     On the command canvas, click  or Debug in the lower left corner of the canvas.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the network operation automation page, choose Command from the navigation pane.

     On the Command Management page, select a command and click Debug in the Operation column.

     On the displayed page, select the device to which the command is to be delivered for Device ID.
      

      

      
        
       
        If the device matches the command, the corresponding device and command information is loaded. Otherwise, the command information is empty.

       

      

      

     Click Test Config to check whether the basic configuration is correct. If the configuration is incorrect, restore the connection or modify the configuration as prompted.

     (Optional) Enter request parameters as required.

     Click Execute Command.

     In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

     (Optional) If Risk Level of the command is High or Critical, enter the confirm password of the current login user in the displayed dialog box and click OK.

     After the debugging is complete, view the command execution result in the Response Message area.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Debugging Network Operation Automation Commands

     On the command canvas, click  or Debug in the lower left corner of the canvas.

     On the displayed page, select a device ID. If the device matches the command, the corresponding device and command information is loaded.

title: Protocol Restrictions on Network Operation Automation Commands
text:
Protocol Restrictions on Network Operation Automation Commands
 
 
  
  

  
   When a specified protocol is used to send commands or receive packets, the conditions of the protocol must be met.

   
     
    
     MML, MOSHELL, TELNET, TL1, and ONMML are insecure. You are advised to use other secure protocols.

    

   

   
    
     
      Table 1 Restrictions on commands of different protocol types
     
     
      
      
      
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Protocol Type

       
        Restriction on the Content of the Sent Command

       
        Restriction on the Length of the Sent Command

       
        Restriction on the Length of the Received Packet

       
        Restriction on the Packet Reading Time

       
        Restriction on the Content of the Received Packet

      

     
     
      
       
        SSH

       
        Within the command whitelist

       
        Less than 100 KB

       
        Less than 2 MB

       
        Less than 120 seconds

       
        The reading of page-turning packets is supported.

        The page turning identifiers are ("---- More", "--More""----", "----", and "--").

      

      
       
        SFTP

       
        
         Within the command whitelist

         ls or put command

        

       
        Less than 100 KB

       
        Less than 2 MB

       
        Less than 120 seconds

       
        -

      

      
       
        MOSHELL

       
        Within the command whitelist

       
        Less than 100 KB

       
        Less than 2 MB

       
        Less than 120 seconds

       
        For details about the fields in the returned object after the packet content is received, see Table 2.

      

      
       
        Telnet

       
        
         Within the command whitelist

         Delete redundant spaces from the command. If the number of consecutive spaces is greater than 2, replace them with less than one.

        

       
        Less than 100 KB

       
        Less than 2 MB

       
        Less than 120 seconds

       
        The reading of page-turning packets is supported.

        The page turning identifiers are ("---- More", "--More""----", "----", and "--").

      

      
       
        MML

       
        
         Within the command whitelist

         Delete redundant spaces from the command. If the number of consecutive spaces is greater than 2, replace them with less than one.

        

       
        Less than 100 KB

       
        Less than 2 MB

       
        Less than 120 seconds

       
        For details about the fields in the returned object after the packet content is received, see Table 3.

      

      
       
        TL1

       
        Within the command whitelist

       
        Less than 100 KB

       
        Less than 2 MB

       
        Less than 120 seconds

       
        For details about the format of received packets, see Table 4.

        
         The following is an example of a received packet:
         IP CMD //Acknowledgement Message
<

EN=0 ENDESC=Success. //Error code description
   total_blocks=60   //Block Message
   block_number=1
   block_records=100

10.205.9.26	NA-0-1-2	11	0870ZYHj4938198sx	w15752475959	GM220-S	--	LOID	43494F5411E490D0	0870ZYHj4938198sx	--	V1.0.20.208

10.205.9.26	NA-0-1-4	20	0870ZYHi8457781im	87000650930	GM219-S	--	LOID	43494F54072BBC70	0870ZYHi8457781im	--	V1.6.11.052

...
10.205.9.26	NA-0-1-4	28	0870ZYHj5845043xi	87001937294	H2-3s	--	LOID	434D4443DF3F2E62	0870ZYHj5845043xi	--	V2.1.1.00.02

        REST

       
        Within the command whitelist

       
        Less than 100 KB

       
        Less than 2 MB

        The response information can be decompressed in gzip or deflate format.

      

     
    
   

   
    
    
     
      Table 2 Meanings of the fields returned after packets are received through commands of the MOSHELL protocol type
     
     
      
      
      
     
     
      
       
        Field

        The first line starts with IP, and the second line starts with <.

       
        -

      

      
       
        Response Message

       
        Yes

       
        Response message

       
        The first line starts with \n, and the second line starts with M.

       
        Packet blocks are separated by >, and packets end with a semicolon (;).

      

      
       
        Error code description

       
        No

       
        Status code description

       
        The EN and ENDESC fields are included.

       
        -

      

      
       
        Block Message

       
        No

       
        Packet block statistics

       
        total_blocks, blktag, and block_number are supported.

name: What Do I Do If Created EMSs or Devices Cannot Be Selected When Operations Are Performed on the Route Configuration Page in Runtime State?
title: What Do I Do If Created EMSs or Devices Cannot Be Selected When Operations Are Performed on the Route Configuration Page in Runtime State?
text:
What Do I Do If Created EMSs or Devices Cannot Be Selected When Operations Are Performed on the Route Configuration Page in Runtime State?
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Symptom

    When performing operations on the route configuration page in the runtime-state environment, you cannot select the created EMSs or devices.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The EMSs or devices obtained through the query interface is inconsistent with the created ones.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal in runtime environment.

     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

     Choose Products and Services > Network Operation > General Settings > Interface Management.

     On the Interface Management page, check whether the integration interface exists.
      

      
       If no integration interface exists, the system queries the data sources of network operation automation (MCP) by default when creating route configuration. In this case, go to the Products and Services > Network Operation > Resource Management > Device or Products and Services > Network Operation > Resource Management > EMS page and create the required device or EMS.

       If the CMDB or DIM integration interface exists, the system queries the corresponding data sources through the interface by default when creating route configuration. In this case, access the page (that is, a service customization page) corresponding to the interface to create the required device or EMS.
        

        

      

      

     If the fault persists, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

title: What Do I Do If a Command Fails to Be Debugged and Message "Not find command, suggest dispatch command and try again" Is Displayed?
text:
What Do I Do If a Command Fails to Be Debugged and Message "Not find command, suggest dispatch command and try again" Is Displayed?
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Symptom

    A command fails to be debugged, and the message "Not find command, suggest dispatch command and try again" is displayed.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The command is not delivered to the collection probe or microservice probe. As a result, the command fails to be executed.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal in runtime environment.

     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

     Choose Products and Services > Network Operation > Command Management.

     On the Command Management page, click Deliver.

     On the Select Probe page, select a probe record and click Deliver.
      

      

      

      

     Click OK.

     On the displayed page, click Query to view the task status. If the value of Status is Successful, the command is successfully delivered.

     Debug the command again. If the fault persists, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Common Troubleshooting Cases of Network Operation Automation

name: What Do I Do If a Command Fails to Be Debugged and Message "Dispatching command failed by Collection" Is Displayed?
title: What Do I Do If a Command Fails to Be Debugged and Message "Dispatching command failed by Collection" Is Displayed?
text:
What Do I Do If a Command Fails to Be Debugged and Message "Dispatching command failed by Collection" Is Displayed?
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Symptom

    A command fails to be debugged and the message "Dispatching command failed by Collection" is displayed.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The MCP probe is in Stopped state, and the MCP probe fails to be called during command debugging.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal in runtime environment.

     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click Data Service Management.

     Choose Products and Services > Data Cube > Data Access > Data Ingestion > Collector.

     In the collector list on the left, click the target collector. In the Probe Management area on the right, check whether the MCP probe is in Running state.
      

      

      

      
       If the MCP probe is in Running state, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

       If the MCP probe is in Stopped state, click  on the right of the probe to start it. After the startup is successful, debug the command again.

      

      

     Debug the command again. If the fault persists, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

    Symptom

    A command fails to be debugged and the message "Failed to get ems or device auth info, please check" is displayed.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The information (including model, vendor, and version) in the device is inconsistent with that configured in the command. As a result, the certificate of the protocol type cannot be obtained during command debugging.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal in runtime environment.

     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

     View the configuration information in the command instance.
      

      
       Choose Products and Services > Network Operation > Command Management.

       On the command list page, choose View > Via form on the right of a command.

       In the Command Instance List area, click Details on the right of a command instance.

       In the Command Information dialog box, view the configuration information about the command instance.
        

        

      

      

     View device configuration information.
      

      
       Choose Products and Services > Network Operation > Resource Management > Device.

       On the device list page, click the device name corresponding to the command.

       On the Edit Device page, view the device configuration information.
        

        

       Go back to the device list page and click Device Certificate on the right of the command.

       In the Device Certificate area, click Edit on the right of the corresponding certificate.

       In the Edit Certificate dialog box, view the certificate information of the device.
        

        

      

      

     Compare the device and device certificate information in the command instance in 3 with that in 4.
      

      
       If the information is consistent, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

       If the information is inconsistent, modify the inconsistent information, save the modification, and go to the next step.

      

      

     Debug the command again. If the fault persists, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

title: What Do I Do When Only Anonymized Command Input Parameters Can Be Viewed in Execution Logs?
text:
What Do I Do When Only Anonymized Command Input Parameters Can Be Viewed in Execution Logs?
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Symptom

    After a command is executed, only the command input parameters that have been anonymized can be viewed in the execution logs. As a result, valid information cannot be obtained.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    Assets may contain sensitive fields in input parameters. Therefore, the system desensitizes sensitive fields in input parameters by default.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal in runtime environment.

     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

     Choose Products and Services > Network Operation > General Settings > Sensitive Field Configuration.

     On the Sensitive Field Configuration page, enter the name of the sensitive field to be desensitized in the search box in the upper right corner.
      

      

      

      

     In the search result, click Delete on the right of the sensitive field configuration.

     Open the execution log file again and view the information about the command input parameters. If the fault persists, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Common Troubleshooting Cases of Network Operation Automation

text:
Configuring the Function Service (Preview)
 
 
  
  

  
   This chapter describes how to develop the function service. The permission for function service development is Function Development, and the corresponding role is StudioFaasDeveloper. If the developers do not have this permission, apply for it from the administrator.

  

  
   
    Introduction to Function Service
      This section describes functions provided by the function services.

    Configuring System Parameters of the Function Service
      You can create system parameters of the function service based on site requirements to facilitate subsequent service development and call.

    Managing the Dependency Package
      This section describes how to create a dependency package and how to configure a tenant-level or project-level dependency package.

    Configuring a Third-Party Image Repository
      The system provides the third-party image repository management capability to enable the interworking with a third-party image repository and verify certificates, so that dependency packages can be downloaded from an external repository.

    Configuring Dependency Upgrade
      The system provides a page for managing dependency upgrade and supports the update of dependencies of third-party components in batches.

    Configuring a Function Service Template
      The system provides a page for managing function service templates, including adding, deleting, modifying, querying, exporting, and importing the templates. Currently, function service templates support only tenant-level templates by default.

    Creating Python Function Service
      The function service allows you to develop functions using Python code.

    Online Editor User Guide
      When editing function code, you can create and edit files and folders in the way same as that of managing projects. You can use the inline editor to compile function code inline. If you upload a .zip package, the frontend decompresses the package and displays it. You can edit the code inline.

    Online Python Function Service Debugging
      After a function is created, you can debug it online.

    Local Debugging of a Python Function Service
      After creating a function, you can use PyCharm to locally test the Python function service.

    FAQs
      This section describes common issues that may occur during the function services.

   

   
    
     Parent topic: App Development
