name: Introduction to the Python Sandbox
title: Introduction to the Python Sandbox
text:
Introduction to the Python Sandbox
 
 
  
  

  
   The sandbox is implemented using the blacklist mode in Python 3.8, and using the whitelist mode in Python 3.9 or later.

   
    Python 3.8

    The sandbox is implemented in Python 3.8 using the blacklist mode. Some subclasses or functions that cannot be used by third-party software are list in Table 1.

    
     
     
      
       Table 1 Blacklist in Python 3.8
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         No.

        
         Third-Party Software Name

        
         Forbidden Subclass or Function

       

      
      
       
        
         1

        
         httplib2

        
         Http.request

       

       
        
         2

        
         multiprocessing

        
         Process, and Pool

       

       
        
         3

        
         os

        
         renames, system, fork, and popen

       

       
        
         4

        
         pycurl

        
         Curl

       

       
        
         5

        
         requests

        
         request, get, options, post, head, put, patch, and delete

       

       
        
         6

        
         subprocess

        
         run, check_call, getstatusoutput, getoutput, Popen, and call

       

       
        
         7

        
         threading

        
         Thread.start

       

       
        
         8

        
         urllib

        
         request.urlopen

       

       
        
         9

        
         urllib3

        
         PoolManager.urlopen

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Python3.9 or Later

    In Python 3.9 or later, sandboxes use the whitelist mode that is divided into two levels.

    
     The first level is the preset whitelists in the system which cannot be changed by users. The preset whitelists are listed in Table 2. 
      
       
       
        
         Table 2 Description of preset whitelists
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Whitelist Type

          
           Preset Whitelist

         

        
        
         
          
           Third-party software

          
           cycler,fonttools,kiwisolver,packaging,pillow,pyparsing,pyPDF2,six,joblib,scipy,threadpoolctl,pytz,numpy,et_xmlfile,filetype,pyasn1,openpyxl,xlrd3,xlwt,xlsxwriter,pandas,lxml,keyword,PIL,urllib,yaml,_yaml,math,cmath,fractions,statistics,gzip,csv,locale,trace,secrets,rsa,os,logging,sys,time, io, re, traceback, warnings, weakref, collections,itertools,linecache,collections.abc,string,threading,atexit,select,socket,pickle,struct,stat,queue,copy,types,copyreg,org,importlib,uuid,enum,platform,functools,_uuid,json,_json,codecs,__future__,ssl,_ssl,backports,ipaddress,operator,contextlib,_imp,builtins,http,email,abc,random,datetime,calendar,base64,binascii,quopri,uu,errno,brotli,hmac,_hashlib,_operator,hashlib,mimetypes,posixpath,winreg,zlib,chardet,OpenSSL,tempfile,zipfile,shutil,bz2,_compression,_bz2,lzma,_lzma,certifi,pathlib,fnmatch,ntpath,genericpath,nt,_collections_abc,_frozen_importlib,_frozen_importlib_external,typing,simplejson,bisect,idna,unicodedata,encodings,stringprep,decimal,_decimal,numbers,_bootlocale,pwd,resource,asyncio,concurrent,concurrent.futures,heapq,inspect,reprlib,_thread,contextvars,_contextvars,_asyncio,selectors,signal,pprint,gc,array,mmap,os.path,xlrd,defusedxml,xml,_elementtree,pyexpat,_codecs_cn,_multibytecodec,_csv

         

         
          
           Third-party software subclass

          
           getpid,makedirs,mkdir,umask,uname,_check_methods,setgid,setuid,seteuid,setreuid,urandom,putenv,walk,_walk,scandir,chdir,rename,listdir,getenv,altsep,curdir,pardir,sep,pathsep,linesep,defpath,name,path,devnull,fsencode,fsdecode,fdopen,access,chmod,close,closerange,environ,error,link,lseek,lstat,open,pipe,read,readlink,remove,replace,rmdir,times,times_result,uname_result,write,removedirs,renames,supports_bytes_environ,unlink,fstat,sendfile

         

         
          
           Readable file or directory

          
           /opt/mateuser/faas/python/function, /tmp, /etc/mime.types, and /var/tmp

         

        
       
      

    

    
     The second level is whitelist configured by the administrator on the Products and Services > Function Service > Sandbox Whitelist Configuration page in the runtime-state environment. The whitelist parameters are described in Table 3. 
      
       
       
        
         Table 3 Sandbox whitelist parameters
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           File white list

          
           Use commas (,) to separate files.

           Example: /etc,/var/tmp

         

         
          
           Lib white list

          
           Use commas (,) to separate third-party software systems.

           Example: xlrd,xlwt

         

         
          
           Subclass white list

          
           Use commas (,) to separate third-party software subclasses.

           Example: getenv,sendfile

         

         
          
           Faas IP address whitelist

          
           Use commas (,) to separate IP addresses. IPv4 addresses are supported.

           
             NOTE: 
            
             
              The IP addresses in the whitelist must be on the same network plane as those of the host machines where the FaaS container is located.

              After a tenant administrator configures an IP address whitelist for the FaaS function service, function service developers can access networks whose IP addresses are in the whitelist and use SDKs such as FTP, PyMySQL, and Redis to directly connect to middleware services built by developers. In this way, connections can be established and files and data can be transferred.

             

            

           

         

         
          
           Built-in white list

          
           Use commas (,) to separate system databases.

         

        
       
      

      
       During the configuration, the system prompts you to evaluate whether the class library is a high-risk function (identify the current high-risk function list by referring to Table 1) and whether the class library may bring injection risks. Customized whitelists are classified into three types: third-party software, third-party software subclasses, and readable files or directories.
       
        Third-party software refers to the third-party software that can be used by users, such as os and time.

        Third-party software subclasses refer to subclasses of third-party software, such as os.getenv and os.sendfile.

        A readable file or directory refers to a file or directory that can be accessed using user code, for example, /tmp and /var/tmp.

       

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Introduction to Function Service

name: Configuring System Parameters of the Function Service
title: Configuring System Parameters of the Function Service
text:
Configuring System Parameters of the Function Service
 
 
  
  

  
   You can create system parameters of the function service based on site requirements to facilitate subsequent service development and call.

   
    Prerequisites

    You have logged in to the GDE data zone portal as the administrator of the master tenant.

   

   
    Context

    Table 1 describes the system-level system parameters related to the function service.

    
     
     
      
       Table 1 System parameters related to the function service
      
      
       
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Name

        
         Category

        
         Encrypted

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         cseMaxInvokeTimes

        
         faas

        
         No

        
         (Optional) Maximum number of times that the function service calls the CSE interface.

         The value is an integer. The default value is 1000.

       

       
        
         maxInvokeTimes

        
         faas

        
         No

        
         Maximum number of times that the function service can be called to prevent DoS. This parameter is optional.

         The value is an integer. The default value is 300.

       

       
        
         concurrency

        
         faas

        
         No

        
         Number of concurrent tasks called by the function service. This parameter is optional.

         The default value is 50.

         The value ranges from 1 to 1000.

         
           NOTICE: 
          
           
            The function service runs tasks by dynamically creating pods. Each pod dynamically applies for resources. By default, the CPU is 0.1 U, and the memory size is defined during the function service orchestration. The default value is 128MB (the value can be 128MB, 256MB, 512MB, 1GB, or 4GB).

            The service personnel need to properly evaluate the memory and CPU resource requirements based on the memory size and number of concurrent services during the function service orchestration. If the number of concurrent services is too large and the memory and CPU resources are insufficient, new tasks cannot be started. In addition, the alarm whose ID is 5010 and name is Node CPU Usage Exceeds the Threshold is generated.

            You are advised to plan independent nodes for the function service during deployment and apply for CPU and memory resources based on the number of concurrent services and memory requirements. For example, if the number of concurrent services is 10 and the memory size is 128 MB, you need to apply for at least 1-U CPU and 1.5-GB memory resources.

           

          

         

       

       
        
         mesherListenPort

        
         faas

        
         No

        
         Listening port number of Mesher. This parameter is optional.

         The default value is 30101.

         The value ranges from 1 to 65535.

       

       
        
         deploy_mode

        
         faas

        
         No

        
         (Mandatory) ADC platform deployment mode.

         The default value is OP.

         The value can be HIS, HEC, or OP.

       

       
        
         new_deploy_mode_his

        
         faas

        
         No

        
         Whether to interwork with Mate through the open REST API.

         Set this parameter only when deploy_mode is set to HIS.

         The value can be true or other values.

       

       
        
         mate_dep_url_env

        
         faas

        
         No

        
         URL of the environment for interworking with Mate, which is provided by Mate.

         Set this parameter only when new_deploy_mode_his is set to true.

       

       
        
         mate_ak

        
         faas

        
         No

        
         AK required for interworking with Mate, which is provided by Mate.

         Set this parameter only when new_deploy_mode_his is set to true.

       

       
        
         mate_sk

        
         faas

        
         Yes

        
         SK required for interworking with Mate, which is provided by Mate.

         Set this parameter only when new_deploy_mode_his is set to true.

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration.

     Choose Products and Services > ADC System Management > Component Management > System Parameter Configuration.

     Click Create.

     Set the system parameters based on site requirements.
      

      Create system parameters in sequence by referring to Table 1. Optional parameters do not need to be created. The following uses the cseMaxInvokeTimes parameter to describe how to create a system parameter.

      

      

     Click OK.

name: Creating a Dependency Package
title: Creating a Dependency Package
text:
Creating a Dependency Package
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to create a dependency package.

   
    Context

    You can create dependency packages for open-source third-party software based on the following example for Python development. You can also create a dependency package based on the self-developed code by referring to the following example to implement code sharing and improve development efficiency in develop state.

    
      
     
      
       Ensure that dependency packages and code packages do not contain the same directory or file. Otherwise, errors may occur due to overwriting and combination.

       If the dependency package fails to be uploaded, check whether the dependency package contains non-Python files, such as CSV, tar.gz, PPT, and Excel files. If yes, delete them.

       The Python dependency package uploaded by the user varies depending on the system architecture. The dependency package needs to support dual architecture or can be uploaded again at the DR site after the DR switchover.

      

     

    

   

   
    Creating a Pure Python Code Dependency Package

    The pure Python third-party software can be used to create a dependency package without compilation. The following uses the open-source third-party software xlrd2.0.1 as an example to describe how to create a dependency package.

    
     Visit https://pypi.org/ and enter xlrd2.0.1 in the search box.
      

      

      

     Click the xlrd2.0.1 installation package.

     Click Download files on the left. The download page is displayed.
      

      

      

     Create the dependency package based on the .whl package.
      

      
       Download the .whl package and decompress it to obtain the xlrd folder.
        

       Compress the xlrd folder into a .zip file to obtain the dependency package. To distinguish versions, it is recommended that the package name contain the corresponding version.
        

      

      

     Prepare the package based on the package in other formats.
      

      This method is used when the open-source third-party software provides the installation package in .tar.gz or .zip format instead of the package in .whl format.

      
       Download the .tar.gz package and decompress it to obtain the xlrd folder.
        

       Compress the xlrd folder into a .zip file to obtain the dependency package. To distinguish versions, it is recommended that the package name contain the corresponding version.
        

      

      

    

   

   
    Creating a Dependency Package for Non-pure Python Code

    Some open-source third-party software contains C/C++ code and needs to be compiled. In addition, these components may depend on specific OSs (EulerOS, SUSE, and Arm). You are advised to obtain the .whl package of the Python version corresponding to the OS. The following uses the numpy1.20.2 package as an example to describe how to create a package.

    
     Visit https://pypi.org/ and enter numpy1.20.2 in the search box.
      

      
       Figure 1 Searching for the file
       
      

      
       
         
        
         
          Currently, only some .whl packages provided by the open-source third-party software are available, and the packages may be incompatible with the existing environment.

          If the .whl package cannot be obtained or the obtained .whl package is abnormal, contact Huawei engineers who release the corresponding dependency package.

          Currently, the dependency package version management capability is not provided. You can distinguish dependency package versions by dependency package name.

          If a dependency package is referenced across apps, you need to deploy the dependent apps during commissioning and running.

         

        

       

      

      

     Create a dependency package of the Python version for Linux (EulerOS or SUSE).
      

      
       Download the .whl package numpy-1.20.2-cp38-cp38-manylinux2010_x86_64.whl, decompress it, and obtain the numpy and num.libs folders.
        
         Figure 2 Downloading the file
         
        

       Compress the numpy and num.libs folders into a .zip file to obtain the dependency package. To distinguish versions, it is recommended that the package name contain the corresponding version.
        
         Figure 3 Packaging files
         
        

      

      

     Create the dependency package of the Python version corresponding to Arm.

name: Tenant-level Dependency Package Configuration
title: Tenant-level Dependency Package Configuration
text:
Tenant-level Dependency Package Configuration
 
 
  
  

  
   The dependency package management function of the function service enables users to configure tenant-level dependency packages.

   
    Prerequisites

    The permission for editing tenant-level dependency packages is Tenant Function Dependency Managing, and the corresponding role is StudioFaaSTenantAdmin. If you do not have the permission, apply for it from the administrator.

   

   
    Context

    Tenant-level dependency packages are uploaded by the tenant administrator. They are owned by the tenant system and can be used by all users and projects of the tenant. When managing dependency packages, tenant administrator needs to pay attention to the following:

    
     Tenant-level dependency packages can be manually created or batch imported

     The size of a single dependency package cannot exceed 50 MB. You can download a single dependency package.

     The total number of dependency packages in a batch cannot exceed 100, and the total package size cannot exceed 500 MB.
      The batch dependency package import function applies only to the batch exported dependency packages, no matter they are exported by this tenant or the others. For example, if tenant B wants to use the dependency packages created by tenant A, tenant B can create tenant-level dependency packages by exporting and importing them in batches. Tenant A exports the created dependency packages in batches. Tenant B obtains the dependency packages batch exported by tenant A. Then, tenant B only needs to batch import the dependency packages exported by tenant A.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the home page of the develop-state environment, choose General Settings > Function Orchestration > Function Service Dependency Management.

     Click Create.

     Configure tenant-level dependency package information by referring to Table 1.
      

      

      
       
       
        
        
         
          Table 1 Tenant-level dependency package parameters
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Parameter

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Name

           
            Name of a tenant-level dependency package.

          

          
           
            Version

           
            Version of the tenant-level dependency package.

          

          
           
            Language

           
            Running language of the tenant-level dependency package. You can select one of the following values:

            
             Python3.12

             Python3.11

             Python3.9

             Python3.8

            

            The implementation logic of sandboxes in Python 3.8 is different from that in Python 3.9 or later. For details about the differences, see Introduction to the Python Sandbox.

          

          
           
            OS Type

           
            Running environment of the tenant-level dependency package. You can select one of the following values:

            
             Euler-X86

             Suse-X86

             Euler-Aarch64

            

          

          
           
            Description

           
            Description of the tenant-level dependency package.

          

          
           
            Open Level

           
            Open level of the tenant-level dependency package. The default value is Tenant Level and cannot be changed.

          

          
           
            Package

           
            Other code dependency packages that the tenant-level dependency package depends on.

            Click Upload and select the required code dependency package.

            
              NOTICE: 
             
              This parameter needs to be set only when Interwork with Third-Party Image Repository is disabled. For details, see Configuring a Third-Party Image Repository.

             

            

          

          
           
            Source Address

           
            Open-source address corresponding to the dependency package. This parameter is optional.

          

         
        
       

      

      

     Click OK.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Operations

    After creating a tenant-level dependency package, you can perform operations described in the following table.

    
     
      
       Table 2 Operations after the tenant-level dependency package is created
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation

        
         Function Description

        
         Procedure

       

      
      
       
        
         Editing the dependency package

        
         Users can edit a created dependency package.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           After editing the dependency package, if the dependency package is used in the function service, you need to perform one-click deployment on the function service before debugging the function service.

          

         

        
         On the Function Service Dependency Management page, click Edit in the Operation column.

       

       
        
         Downloading the dependency package

        
         Users can download a single dependency package.

        
         On the Function Service Dependency Management page, click More > Download in the Operation column.

       

       
        
         Disabling the dependency package

        
         Only enabled dependency packages can be disabled.

        
         Method 1:

         
          On the Function Service Dependency Management page, click More > Deactive in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

         Method 2:

         
          On the Function Service Dependency Management page, select one or more enabled dependency packages.

          Click Batch Disable in the upper part of the page.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Enabling the dependency package

        
         Only disabled dependency packages can be enabled.

        
         Method 1:

         
          On the Function Service Dependency Management page, click More > Active in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

         Method 2:

         
          On the Function Service Dependency Management page, select one or more disabled dependency packages.

          Click Batch Enable in the upper part of the page.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Upgrading the dependency package

        
         Users can change the state of a dependency package from using to upgrading.

        
         On the Function Service Dependency Management page, choose More > Upgrade in the Operation column.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           If you need to add a code dependency package during the function service creation, the dependency packages in upgrading state cannot be selected.

          

         

       

       
        
         Using a dependency package

        
         Users can change the state of a dependency package from upgrading to using.

        
         On the Function Service Dependency Management page, choose More > use in the Operation column.

       

       
        
         Delete a dependency package

        
         Only disabled dependency packages can be deleted.

        
         
          On the Function Service Dependency Management page, click Delete in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Import dependency packages in batches

        
         Tenant-level dependency packages can be created by importing them in batches.

        
         
          On the Function Service Dependency Management page, click Batch Import above the list.

          Click Add and select the dependency package to be imported.
           The dependency packages are batch-exported packages.

          Click Save.

         

       

       
        
         Export dependency packages in batches

        
         Dependency packages can be exported in batches.

        
         
          On the Function Service Dependency Management page, select the dependency package to be exported.

          Click Batch Export in the upper part of the page.

         

       

       
        
         Exporting the dependency details of the function service

        
         The dependency details of the function service can be exported.

        
         
          On the Function Service Dependency Management page, select one or more dependency packages.

          Click Dependency List in the upper part of the page.

name: Project-Level Dependency Package Configuration
title: Project-Level Dependency Package Configuration
text:
Project-Level Dependency Package Configuration
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to configure a project-level dependency package.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment and accessed the Function Service page.

     The permission for editing project-level dependency packages is Function Dependency Managing, and the corresponding role is StudioFaasDeveloper. If you do not have the permission, apply for it from the administrator.

    

   

   
    Context

    Project-level dependency packages are for internal use only. Developers can upload dependency packages for Function Service in the project to use. When managing dependency packages, developers need to pay attention to the following:

    
     If dependency package A depends on dependency package B, you need to reference dependency package B when referencing dependency package A. Otherwise, the dependency package function is abnormal.

     A referenced dependency package cannot be directly deleted. You can view the referenced function in the dependency details. For example, if the dependency package is referenced by the Python1 function of the faas module of the proCode project, you need to remove the reference relationship between the Python1 function and the referenced package before deleting the dependency package.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Function Service.

name: Configuring a Third-Party Image Repository
title: Configuring a Third-Party Image Repository
text:
Configuring a Third-Party Image Repository
 
 
  
  

  
   The system provides the third-party image repository management capability to enable the interworking with a third-party image repository and verify certificates, so that dependency packages can be downloaded from an external repository.

   
    Prerequisites

    The permission for editing tenant-level dependency packages is Tenant Function Dependency Managing, and the corresponding role is StudioFaaSTenantAdmin. If you do not have the permission, apply for it from the administrator.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the home page of the develop-state environment, choose General Settings > Function Orchestration > Third-Party Image Repository Management.

     Click Modify Settings.

     Configure the third-party image repository information by referring to Table 1.
      

      

      
       
        
        
         
          Table 1 Parameters about the third-party image repository
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Parameter

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Interwork with Third-Party Image Repository

           
            Whether to interwork with a third-party image repository.

          

          
           
            Third-Party Image Repository Address

           
            Address of the third-party image repository. The value can be a domain name, an IPv4 address, or an IPv6 address.

            This parameter needs to be set only when Interwork with Third-Party Image Repository is enabled.

            
              NOTE: 
             
              The third-party image repository supports only the PYPI protocol. If the HTTP protocol is used, you need to ensure the security.

             

            

          

          
           
            Verification File

           
            Click Add and select the CRT certificate file to be verified.

            This parameter needs to be set only when Interwork with Third-Party Image Repository is enabled.

          

          
           
            Description

           
            Description of the third-party image repository. This parameter is optional.

            This parameter needs to be set only when Interwork with Third-Party Image Repository is enabled.

          

         
        
       

      

      

     Click OK.
      

      Certificate expired at is displayed under the certificate file.

      

     Click Test Connection to test whether the repository connection is normal.

name: Configuring Dependency Upgrade
title: Configuring Dependency Upgrade
text:
Configuring Dependency Upgrade
 
 
  
  

  
   The system provides a page for managing dependency upgrade and supports the update of dependencies of third-party components in batches.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment and have obtained the function developer permission. The permission for function development is Function Developing, and the corresponding role is StudioFaasDeveloper. If you do not have the permission, apply for it from the administrator.

     You have opened the Function Service menu.

    

   

   
    Context

    By default, only tenant-level dependency upgrade is supported.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Function Service.

     Choose Orchestration Resource > Dependency Relation Upgrade Mgmt under the function service.

     Click Add.

     Configure a dependency by referring to Table 1.
      

      

      
       
       
        
        
         
          Table 1 Parameters of a dependency
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Parameter

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Dependency Name

           
            Name of the dependency package for which a dependency needs to be configured. The options come from the dependency package names in Tenant-level Dependency Package Configuration.

          

          
           
            Version

           
            Version of the dependency package for which the dependency needs to be configured. The options come from the dependency package versions in Tenant-level Dependency Package Configuration.

          

          
           
            Operate Type

           
            Type of the operation for configuring the dependency. The options are as follows:

            
             Upgrade

             Add

             Delete

             Replace

            

          

          
           
            Replace Dependency Name

           
            Name of the dependency package to be replaced. The options come from the dependency package names in Tenant-level Dependency Package Configuration.

            This parameter is available when Operate Type is Replace.

          

          
           
            Upgrade Version

           
            Target version of the dependency package for which the dependency needs to be configured. The options come from the dependency package versions in Tenant-level Dependency Package Configuration.

            This parameter is available when Operate Type is Upgrade or Replace.

            
              NOTE: 
             
              When Operate Type is Upgrade, the target version must be later than the current dependency package version.

             

            

          

          
           
            Module Name

           
            Module for which the dependency needs to be configured. You can select multiple modules or leave this parameter blank.

            
              NOTE: 
             
              If this parameter is left blank, the meaning of this parameter varies according to the value of Operate Type.

              
               Upgrade: applies to all the function services that use the dependency package in the current project.

               Add: applies to all the function services in the current project.

               Delete: applies to all the function services that use the dependency package in the current project.

               Replace: applies to all the function services that use the dependency package in the current project.

              

             

            

          

         
        
       

      

      

     Click Confirm.

     (Optional) To create multiple dependencies, repeat 3 to 5. A maximum of 50 dependencies can be created.

     Click Confirm in the lower right corner of the page.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Operations

    After a dependency is created, you can perform the operations listed in the following table.

    
     
      
       Table 2 Operations after a dependency is created
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation

        
         Feature

        
         Procedure

       

      
      
       
        
         Editing the dependency

        
         Users can edit the created dependency.

        
         
          On the Dependency Upgrade page, click Edit in the Operation column.

          Edit the dependency by referring to Table 1.

          Click Confirm.

          (Optional) To edit multiple dependencies, repeat 1 to 3.

          Click Confirm in the lower right corner of the page.

         

       

       
        
         Deleting the dependency

        
         Users can delete the created dependency.

        
         
          On the Dependency Upgrade page, select one or more dependencies.

          Click Delete in the upper left corner of the page.

          Click Confirm in the lower right corner of the page.

         

       

       
        
         Exporting the dependencies

        
         Users can export the dependencies of all modules in the current project.

        
         
          On the Dependency Upgrade page, click Export Dependency Relation in the upper right corner of the page.

          Open the detail.csv file downloaded to the local PC to view the configured dependencies.

name: Configuring a Function Service Template
title: Configuring a Function Service Template
text:
Configuring a Function Service Template
 
 
  
  

  
   The system provides a page for managing function service templates, including adding, deleting, modifying, querying, exporting, and importing the templates. Currently, function service templates support only tenant-level templates by default.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment and have obtained the function developer permission. The permission for function development is Function Developing, and the corresponding role is StudioFaasDeveloper. If you do not have the permission, apply for it from the administrator.

     You have opened the Function Service menu.

    

   

   
    Context

    
     Function service templates are classified into custom and default templates. The default templates cannot be modified.

     Function service templates are used only for quickly creating functions and cannot be directly debugged.

     By default, the function service templates support only tenant-level templates. A tenant can create a maximum of 300 function service templates.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Function Service.

     Choose Orchestration Resource > Function Services Template Mgmt. The function template list page is displayed.

     Click Create.

     Configure information about the function service template.
      

      
       Configure basic template information, as shown in Table 1. 
        
         
         
          
           Table 1 Basic information about a function service template
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Template Name

            
             Name of the function service template. The value must contain 4 to 64 characters, start with a lowercase letter, and contain only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens (-).

           

           
            
             Entry Function

            
             The default value is index.handler, which cannot be edited.

           

           
            
             Execution Method

            
             Execution mode of the function service.

             
              Synchronize

              Asynchronize

             

             Default value: Asynchronize

           

           
            
             Programming Language

            
             Language supported by the function service. You can select one of the following values:

             
              Python3.12

              Python3.11

              Python3.9

              Python3.8

             

           

           
            
             Memory

            
             Evaluate the function memory based on the actual usage and set it to a proper value.

             
              128M

              256M

              512M

              1G

              4G

             

             
               NOTICE: 
              
               If the selected memory size is greater than 1 GB, contact the administrator to add the app for which the quota configuration is required to the app quota whitelist with Whitelist Configuration Item set to Procode Memory Quota. Otherwise, the app cannot run.

              

             

           

           
            
             Timeout Interval (s)

            
             Timeout interval of the function service, in seconds.

             
               NOTE: 
              
               
                The options of Timeout Interval (s) come from the system parameter configuration of the master tenant (system-level) or tenant user (tenant-level). Name of the system parameter is faas_time_out_config, Category is faas, and Value ranges from 15 to 7200.
                 
                  If Name is not set to faas_time_out_config for both the system-level and tenant-level parameters, the default options of Timeout Interval (s) are 120, 180, 240, and 300.

                  Once the tenant-level parameter is set, the values of the tenant-level parameter plus the default value (120, 180, 240, and 300) are used as the options of Timeout Interval (s).

                  If only the system-level parameter is set, the values of the system-level parameter plus the default value (120, 180, 240, and 300) are used as the options of Timeout Interval (s).

                 

                In the installation and upgrade packages, the following system parameter configuration items can be preset for the master tenant: faas_time_out_config for Name, faas for Category, and 120,180,240,300 for Value.

               

              

             

           

           
            
             Open Level

            
             Open level of the function service. You can select one of the following values:

             
              Module: indicates that the service can be used within a module.

              Project: indicates that the model can be used within a project. When there are multiple modules in the project, the model can also be used within the project modules.

              Public: indicates that the model is public and can be used within the system.

             

           

           
            
             Register with the API directory

            
             Whether the function service can be registered with the API catalog so that the function can be called as an API.

             This parameter is displayed only when Open Level is set to Public.

           

           
            
             API Catalog

            
             You can directly enter the registration directory path, for example, /catalog/subCatalog/domain, or directly register with an existing directory. After the registration is successful, you can view the information in the API center.

             This parameter is displayed only when Register with the API directory is enabled.

           

           
            
             Developer Type

            
             Resource development permission control, that is, developers who have the permission to view, use, and change (enable, disable, delete, edit, and import) resources.

             
              Personal: Grant the development permission only to the individual who creates the asset.

              Team: Grant the development permission to a specified team.

             

           

           
            
             Share Asset

            
             Whether resources can be shared, that is, whether to allow other users except individuals or teams to view, use, and export function service templates (excluding change operations). Resource sharing is a restricted disclosure of resource permissions. That is, only the resource usage permission is shared, and the resource change permission is not.

           

           
            
             Home Team

            
             Select a specified R&D team. The options come from Team Management.

             This parameter is available only when Developer Type is set to Team.

           

           
            
             Description

            
             Description of the function service.

           

          
         
        

       Set the input parameters, as shown in Figure 1.
        
         Figure 1 Input parameter configuration
         

         

        

        Subnodes can be added only to parameters of the object or array type. The validator varies according to the element type. For details, see Table 2.

        
         
         
          
           Table 2 Validator description
          
          
           
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Input Element Type

            
             Validator Type

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             object/array

            
             -

            
             -

           

           
            
             string

            
             Text

            
             Text validator type. The maximum length, forbidden characters, and regular expressions of text input can be verified.

           

           
            
             IP address

            
             The IP address format of the input parameter is verified.

           

           
            
             Phone number

            
             The format of the phone number of the input parameters is verified.

           

           
            
             Email

            
             The email address format (in the "x@y.z" format) and maximum length of the input parameters are verified.

           

           
            
             Alphabet

            
             The alphabet (only letters, digits, and underscores are allowed and the alphabet cannot start with a digit) and maximum length of the input parameter are verified.

           

           
            
             Date

            
             The date format of the input parameter is verified. The following date formats are supported:

             
              Date and time (yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss)

              Date (YYYY-MM-DD)

              Time (HH:mm:ss)

             

           

           
            
             Enum

            
             All values that can be entered are enumerated and the input parameters based on the values are verified. Enumerated values are separated with commas (,).

           

           
            
             integer

            
             
              int32

              int64

             

            
             Check whether the input parameter is a string of 32 or 64 characters.

           

           
            
             decimal

            
             
              double

              float

             

            
             Check whether the input parameter is of the integer or floating point type.

           

           
            
             boolean

            
             -

            
             The value can be true or false.

           

          
         
        

        
          
         
          
           The following preset formats are supported: fileToken, url, enum, password, staff, status, time and date. If Verification Type is set to FileToken, a file token is displayed when a service is used. During function debugging, the file token can be obtained after a file is uploaded.

           If you enable Register with the API directory when creating the function service template, the input parameters correspond to the request parameters of the API catalog.

          

         

        

       Set the output parameters.
        
         Figure 2 Output parameter configuration
         

         

        

        
          
         
          The output parameter configuration can be edited only when Execution Method is set to Synchronize.

         

        

       Configure the asynchronous processing result parameters.
        
         Figure 3 Configuring the asynchronous processing result parameters
         

         

        

        
          
         
          If you enable Register with the API directory when creating the function service template, the asynchronous processing result parameters corresponds to the output parameters of the API catalog.

         

        

       Click Save.
        After a function service template is created, the Edit Code tab page is automatically displayed.

      

      

     On the Edit Code tab page, configure the dependency package of the function service template.
      

      You can associate an uploaded dependency package with the function service.

      
       Click Add next to Code Dependency Package.

       Select the uploaded dependency package.
        
          
         
          The function service template dependency package come from tenant-level and project-level dependency packages. By default, no dependency package can be referenced.

          
           For project-level dependency packages, you need to add them on the Dependency Package Mgmt page. For details, see Project-Level Dependency Package Configuration.

           Tenant-level dependency packages need to be created by the administrator. For details, see Tenant-level Dependency Package Configuration.

          

         

        

       Click OK.

       Click Save.

      

      

     Compile the code of the function service template online.
      

      For details, see Online Editor User Guide.

      

     Download the code.
      

      Click Download Code to download the code of the function service template to the PC.

      

     Click the Configure Function tab to view and modify the configuration information of the function service template.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Operations

    After creating a function service template, you can perform the following operations.

    
     
      
       Table 3 Operations after a function service template is created
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation

        
         Function Description

        
         Procedure

       

      
      
       
        
         Viewing the function service template

        
         You can view the function service template based on filter criteria.

        
         On the Function Template List page, enter the template name, description, or select Disabled or Enabled to view the template.

       

       
        
         Editing the function service template

        
         You can edit a created function service template.

        
         On the Function Template List page, click the name of the template to be edited.

       

       
        
         Disabling the function service template

        
         Only enabled function service templates can be disabled.

        
         Method 1:

         On the Function Template List page, choose More > Disable in the Operation column.

name: Creating Python Function Service
title: Creating Python Function Service
text:
Creating Python Function Service
 
 
  
  

  
   The function service allows you to develop functions using Python code.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment and have obtained the function developer permission. The permission for function development is Function Developing, and the corresponding role is StudioFaasDeveloper. If you do not have the permission, apply for it from the administrator.

     You have opened the Function Service menu.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Function Service.

     Click .
      

      You can create functions in either of the following ways:

      
       Creating functions using a default template: Click Default Template.

       Creating functions using a customized template: Select the required template and click Custom Template.

      

      
        
       
        If functions are created based on a customized template, you can directly enter the function names or create functions after modifying the information in the customized template.

       

      

      

     Configure function information.
      

      
       Configure basic function information, as shown in Table 1. 
        
         
         
          
           Table 1 Basic information about a function
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Function

            
             Name of the function service. The value must contain 4 to 64 characters, start with a lowercase letter, and contain only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens (-).

           

           
            
             Entry Function

            
             The default value is index.handler, which cannot be edited.

           

           
            
             Execution Method

            
             Execution mode of the function service.

             
              Synchronize

              Asynchronize

             

             Default value: Asynchronize

           

           
            
             Programming Language

            
             Language supported by the function service. You can select one of the following values:

             
              Python3.12

              Python3.11

              Python3.9

              Python3.8

             

           

           
            
             Memory

            
             Evaluate the function memory based on the actual usage and set it to a proper value.

             
              128M

              256M

              512M

              1G

              4G

             

             
               NOTICE: 
              
               If the selected memory size is greater than 1 GB, contact the administrator to add the app for which the quota configuration is required to the app quota whitelist with Whitelist Configuration Item set to Procode Memory Quota. Otherwise, the app cannot run.

              

             

           

           
            
             Timeout Interval (s)

            
             Timeout interval of the function service, in seconds.

             
               NOTE: 
              
               
                The options of Timeout Interval (s) come from the system parameter configuration of the master tenant (system-level) or tenant user (tenant-level). Name of the system parameter is faas_time_out_config, Category is faas, and Value ranges from 15 to 7200.
                 
                  If Name is not set to faas_time_out_config for both the system-level and tenant-level parameters, the default options of Timeout Interval (s) are 120, 180, 240, and 300.

                  Once the tenant-level parameter is set, the values of the tenant-level parameter plus the default value (120, 180, 240, and 300) are used as the options of Timeout Interval (s).

                  If only the system-level parameter is set, the values of the system-level parameter plus the default value (120, 180, 240, and 300) are used as the options of Timeout Interval (s).

                 

                In the installation and upgrade packages, the following system parameter configuration items can be preset for the master tenant: faas_time_out_config for Name, faas for Category, and 120,180,240,300 for Value.

               

              

             

           

           
            
             Open Level

            
             Open level of the function service. You can select one of the following values:

             
              Module: indicates that the service can be used within a module.

              Project: indicates that the model can be used within a project. When there are multiple modules in the project, the model can also be used within the project modules.

              Public: indicates that the model is public and can be used within the system.

             

           

           
            
             Register with the API directory

            
             Whether the function service can be registered with the API catalog so that the function can be called as an API.

             This parameter is displayed only when Open Level is set to Public.

           

           
            
             API Catalog

            
             You can directly enter the registration directory path, for example, /catalog/subCatalog/domain, or directly register with an existing directory. After the registration is successful, you can view the information in the API center.

             This parameter is displayed only when Register with the API directory is enabled.

           

           
            
             Description

            
             Description of the function service.

           

          
         
        

       Set the input parameters, as shown in Figure 1.
        
         Figure 1 Input parameter configuration
         

         

        

        Subnodes can be added only to parameters of the object or array type. The validator varies according to the element type. For details, see Table 2.

        
         
         
          
           Table 2 Validator description
          
          
           
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Input Element Type

            
             Validator Type

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             object/array

            
             -

            
             -

           

           
            
             string

            
             Text

            
             Text validator type. The maximum length, forbidden characters, and regular expressions of text input can be verified.

           

           
            
             IP address

            
             The IP address format of the input parameter is verified.

           

           
            
             Phone number

            
             The format of the phone number of the input parameters is verified.

           

           
            
             Email

            
             The email address format (in the "x@y.z" format) and maximum length of the input parameters are verified.

           

           
            
             Alphabet

            
             The alphabet (only letters, digits, and underscores are allowed and the alphabet cannot start with a digit) and maximum length of the input parameter are verified.

           

           
            
             Date

            
             The date format of the input parameter is verified. The following date formats are supported:

             
              Date and time (yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss)

              Date (YYYY-MM-DD)

              Time (HH:mm:ss)

             

           

           
            
             Enum

            
             All values that can be entered are enumerated and the input parameters based on the values are verified. Enumerated values are separated with commas (,).

           

           
            
             integer

            
             
              int32

              int64

             

            
             Check whether the input parameter is a string of 32 or 64 characters.

           

           
            
             decimal

            
             
              double

              float

             

            
             Check whether the input parameter is of the integer or floating point type.

           

           
            
             boolean

            
             -

            
             The value can be true or false.

           

          
         
        

        
          
         
          
           The following preset formats are supported: fileToken, url, enum, password, staff, status, time and date. If Verification Type is set to FileToken, a file token is displayed when a service is used. During function debugging, the file token can be obtained after a file is uploaded.

           Desensitization policies can be configured for service input parameters. For details about the options in the drop-down list, see Configuring a Project Desensitization Policy. For function services, if multiple desensitization policies are configured for the same input parameter, only one desensitization policy is displayed.

           If you enable Register with the API directory when creating the function service template, the input parameters correspond to the request parameters of the API catalog.

          

         

        

       Set the output parameters.
        
         Figure 2 Output parameter configuration
         

         

        

        
          
         
          The output parameter configuration can be edited only when Execution Method is set to Synchronize.

         

        

       Configure the asynchronous processing result parameters.
        
         Figure 3 Configuring the asynchronous processing result parameters
         

         

        

        
          
         
          If you enable Register with the API directory when creating the function service template, the asynchronous processing result parameters corresponds to the output parameters of the API catalog.

         

        

       Click Save.
        After a function service is created, the Edit Code tab page is displayed.

      

      

     On the Edit Code tab page, configure the dependency package of the function service.
      

      You can associate an uploaded dependency package with the function service.

      
       Click Add next to Code Dependency Package.

       Select the uploaded dependency package.
        
          
         
          Function service dependency packages come from tenant-level and project-level dependency packages. By default, no dependency package can be referenced.

          
           For project-level dependency packages, you need to add them on the Dependency Package Mgmt page. For details, see Project-Level Dependency Package Configuration.

           Tenant-level dependency packages need to be created by the administrator. For details, see Tenant-level Dependency Package Configuration.

          

         

        

       Click OK.

       Click Save.

      

      

     Compile function code online.
      

      For details, see Online Editor User Guide.

      

     Test the function service online.
      

      For details, see Online Python Function Service Debugging.

      

     Download the code.
      

      Click Download Code to download the function code to the local PC.

      

     Click the Configure Function tab to view and modify the configuration information of the function service.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Operations

    After a function is created, you can perform the following operations:

    
     
      
       Table 3 Operations after function service creation
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation

        
         Function Description

        
         Procedure

       

      
      
       
        
         Viewing the function service

        
         You can view the function service based on filter criteria.

        
         On the Function List page, enter a function name and select Disabled or Enabled to view the function service.

       

       
        
         Debug a function service

        
         You can debug a function service.

        
         On the Function List page, click Debug in the Operation column. For details about the debugging process, see Online Python Function Service Debugging.

       

       
        
         Edit a function service

        
         You can edit a created function service.

        
         Method 1:

         On the Function List page, click the name of the function to be edited.

         Method 2:

         On the Function List page, click Edit in the Operation column.

       

       
        
         Disable a function service

        
         Only enabled function services can be disabled.

        
         Method 1:

         
          On the Function List page, click More > Deactive in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

         Method 2:

         
          On the Function List page, select one or more enabled functions.

          Click Batch Disable in the upper part of the page.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Enable a function service

        
         Only disabled function services can be enabled.

        
         Method 1:

         
          On the Function List page, click More > Active in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

         Method 2:

         
          On the Function List page, select one or more disabled functions.

          Click Batch Enable in the upper part of the page.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

       

       
        
         Delete a function service

        
         Only disabled function services can be deleted.

        
         Method 1:

         
          On the Function List page, click More > Delete in the Operation column.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

         

         Method 2:

         
          On the Function List page, select one or more disabled functions.

          Click Batch Delete in the upper part of the page.

          In the displayed dialog box, click OK.

name: Online Editor User Guide
title: Online Editor User Guide
text:
Online Editor User Guide
 
 
  
  

  
   When editing function code, you can create and edit files and folders in the way same as that of managing projects. You can use the inline editor to compile function code inline. If you upload a .zip package, the frontend decompresses the package and displays it. You can edit the code inline.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment and have obtained the function developer permission. The permission for function development is Function Developing, and the corresponding role is StudioFaasDeveloper. If you do not have the permission, apply for it from the administrator.

     You have opened the Function Service menu.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Function Service.

     Click the function service to be edited.

     Go to the Edit Online tab page and view the default preset file structure and code file.
      

      

      index.py is the call entry file of the function service, which is described as follows:

      
       event: user-defined input parameter, which is of the dict type

       context: task information when the function service is running, which is of the custom context data type. This parameter contains the following properties:
        
         function_uri: function running path. The format is "Project name/Module name/Function name".

         tracker_id: ID of the thread for creating a function service task

         username: user name called by the function service

         timeout: timeout duration for running the function service This parameter does not take effect when the Python function service is tested locally.

         memory: memory size limit for running the function service This parameter does not take effect when the Python function service is tested locally.

        

      

      

     Manage code files and file directories.
      

      
       On the Edit Online tab page, choose File to create a folder, create a file, or close all open file windows. The new file or folder is located in the root directory (at the same level as the my_module and index.py folders).
        

      

      
       Right-click a folder and choose a shortcut menu from the shortcut menu to create a file or folder, rename or delete the folder.
        

      

      
       Right-click a file and choose a shortcut menu from the shortcut menu to rename or delete the file.
        

       Right-click a file or folder and choose a shortcut menu from the shortcut menu to create, rename, or delete the file or folder.
        

      

      

     Edit the function code online.
      

      
       Edit Online tab page provides a preset code template, which can be directly run. You can use this template to develop function code. For details, see Function Service Development. You can call the SDK/API of the platform in the function code.

       Select Insert API to insert the required API into the code file for editing.
        

       Select Edit to undo the operation or restore the previous operation.
        

       Select Upload ZIP File, to develop function code offline and upload it as a .zip file.
        If the code is uploaded in .zip format, the frontend decompresses and displays the code and supports online editing and modification.

      

      

     Click Save.

Downloading the Local Debugging Tool
 
 
  
  

  
   The local debugging tools include the Pro Code CLI offline tool and Pro Code plugin installation package.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have logged in to the develop-state environment and have obtained the function developer permission. The permission for function development is Function Developing, and the corresponding role is StudioFaasDeveloper. If you do not have the permission, apply for it from the administrator.

      The tool version can be Python 3.9, Python 3.11, or Python 3.12. Python 3.12 is used by default.

      

     Click Download.

     Use the SHA256 hash value to verify the integrity of the tool.zip installation package.
      

      
       Open the CMD command line interface (CLI) on the local PC.

       Run the following command to check the SHA256 hash value of the tool.zip installation package:
        certutil -hashfile "D:\Downloads\tool.zip" SHA256

        In the preceding command, D:\Downloads\tool.zip indicates the local directory of the tool.zip installation package. Change it based on site requirements. After the command is executed, the verification value is displayed.

       Check whether the verification value in 5.b is the same as that on the local debugging tool download page in 2.
        If the verification values are the same, the integrity of the tool.zip installation package is not damaged. Otherwise, download the package again.

name: Installing the Pro Code CLI Offline Tool
title: Installing the Pro Code CLI Offline Tool
text:
Installing the Pro Code CLI Offline Tool
 
 
  
  

  
   You can use the Pro Code CLI offline tool to initialize a FaaS runtime environment locally so that you can use the breakpoint debugging function of PyCharm to implement local debugging.

   
    Prerequisites

    Node.js v18.x or later has been installed.

    
     To check the Node.js version, open the CMD window on the local PC and run the node -v command on the CLI.

     You can download Node.js from https://nodejs.org/en/download. If the installed Node.js version is too early, obtain the latest Node.js version with security hardening and install it.

     There is a version mapping between Node.js and npm. Ensure that the npm version matches the Node.js version based on the mapping provided in Nodejs Version Mapping to prevent version mismatch caused by manual npm upgrade.
      To check the npm version, open the CMD window on the local PC and run the npm -v command on the CLI.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     In the local debugging tool directory, press Shift, right-click the mouse, and select Open PowerShell Here or Open command window here from the shortcut menu.

     Run the following command to check the npm repository configuration:
      

      npm config edit

      
       In the displayed .npmrc file, check whether the file contains the following configuration information:
       no-proxy=.huawei.com
registry=https://cmc.centralrepo.rnd.huawei.com/npm
@adc:registry=https://cmc.centralrepo.rnd.huawei.com/artifactory/api/npm/product_npm/@adc/
strict-ssl=false
      

      If the file does not contain the information, add the information to the file, save the file, and close the file.

      

     Decompress the Pro Code CLI tool package on the local host.
      

      
       Figure 1 Decompressing the Pro Code CLI tool package on the local host
       
      

      

     Double-click the install.bat file to install the Pro Code CLI offline tool.
      

      
        
       
        To uninstall the old version, double-click the uninstall.bat file.

       

      

      

     After the installation window is closed, run the following command in the PowerShell window to check the version:
      

      adc -v

      
       If the correct version information is displayed, the installation is successful.
       C:\Users\procode>adc -v
24.0.9
      

      

     Run the following command to learn more about the command usage:
      

      
       adc help auth
       C:\Users\procode>adc help auth
Usage: Run auth [options]

authorization information

Options:
-ls | --list query authorized user environment // Query the list of environments in which the user is authorized.
-cf | --config <env...> login info config, IP:port, "accessID", "secretKey", "certPath" // Configure login information.
-ln | --login [trust] login with trust unauthorized certificate // Authorize the login.
  -lo | --logout           logout // Cancel authorization.
  -h, --help               display help for command

name: Logging In to PyCharm
title: Logging In to PyCharm
text:
Logging In to PyCharm
 
 
  
  

  
   PyCharm interworks with the Pro Code CLI tool to implement the login function.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     PyCharm of a version between 2020.2 and 2022.2 (professional or community edition) has been installed.

     Python 3.9.11 or later or Python 3.11.4 or later has been installed.

     The Pro Code CLI offline tool has been installed.

     The Pro Code plugin has been installed.

    

   

   
    Context

    Before logging in to PyCharm, you need to obtain the authorization, the HTTPS certificate, and CRL file of the machine-machine user.

    
     Create a machine-machine user.
      

      
       Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.

       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

       Choose Products and Services > Administration > Identity Authentication > Machine-Machine User Management.

       Click Create Machine-Machine User.

       Set Authentication Type to Basic and Select Human-machine User to a user with the FaaS development permission for the new user.

       Click Submit.

       A dialog box is displayed, indicating that the key is created successfully. Record the new values of AccessId and Secretkey for future use.

       Select I have confirmed to save the Basic secret key.

       Click OK.

      

      

     Apply for a certificate from the certificate issuing department.

     Open the applied certificate on the local PC and switch to the Details tab page to view the certificate details.
      

      Pay attention to the certificate validity period. When the certificate is about to expire, apply for a new certificate.

      

      

      

     Find the CRL Distribution Points field and view and record the URL in the Value column.
      

      

      

      

     Enter the URL recorded in 4 in the address box of the browser to directly download the CRL file.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Open PyCharm.

     Click Create New Project.

     Choose Location and select a project folder.
      

      

      

     Configure the project interpreter.
      

      There are two types of project interpreters. Select one based on site requirements.

      
       New interpreters: To use them, select New Environment using Virtualenv, and then set Location and Base interpreter.
        

       (Recommended) Existing interpreters: To use them, select Existing interpreter, and then set Interpreter.
        

      

      

     Right-click the project directory on the left and choose Adc Assistant > Login Setting.
      

      

      

     Configure login information.
      

      

      Where:

      
       Environment Configuration corresponds to the IP address and port number of the ADC environment.

       AcessId corresponds to the value of AccessId recorded after the machine-machine account is created in 1.

       Secretkey corresponds to the value of Secretkey recorded after the machine-machine account is created in 1.

       Certificate: indicates the certificate that the customer applies for from the certificate issuing department.

       CRL: CRL file downloaded in 5.
        
          
         
          The local debugging tool supports only CRL verification. If no CRL file is uploaded, the server certificate revocation verification cannot be performed, and login risks exist.

         

        

      

      

     Click Login.

     (Optional) If no CRL file is uploaded, the following dialog box is displayed. Click Confirm.
      

      

      

     After the login is successful, the following dialog box is displayed. Click Confirm.
      

      

      
        
       
        
         To log in to another environment, open the login page again and configure the login information.

         If the certificate is about to expire, you need to apply for a new one from the certificate issuing department. When configuring login information, you need to select the new certificate.
