name: Creating a Local Python Project
title: Creating a Local Python Project
text:
Creating a Local Python Project
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to create a local Python project.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     PyCharm of a version between 2020.2 and 2022.2 (professional or community edition) has been installed.

     Python 3.9.11 or later or Python 3.11.4 or later has been installed.

     The Pro Code CLI offline tool has been installed.

     The Pro Code plugin has been installed.

    

   

   
    Context

    PyCharm plugin interworks with CLI commands to create local functions, manage function metadata, upload function code, and pull function code. After a local Python project is created, the following directories are involved:

   

   
    ${DIR}/app/function/code: directory where you compile Python code. The entry file is index.py.

    ${DIR}/app/function/lib: directory where the dependency package associated with the cloud function service is downloaded after the function is pulled.

    ${DIR}/app/function/${functionName}.json: file where the function service metadata information is stored. parameters in the file can be customized.

    ${DIR}/app/faas_local_debug_temp/logs/function/adc-faas-python-function.log: file where the function service logs are stored.

    ${DIR}/app/faas_local_debug_temp/logs/runtime/adc-faas-python-runtime.log: file where the run logs of function service are stored.

    ${DIR}/app/faas_local_debug_temp/run_temp: temporary file directory of the function service.

   

   
     
    
     ${DIR} indicates a project directory. Change it based on site requirements.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Open the PyCharm that has been authenticated.

     Create a function service.
      

      
       Right-click the project directory on the left and choose Adc Assistant > Code Sync > Function Creation.
        

       Go to the ADC page for configuring the environment during PyCharm login.
        
         If you have not logged in to ADC, go to the ADC login page.

         If you have logged in to ADC, go to the runtime-state ADC page.

        

       Create a function service by referring to Creating Python Function Service.

      

      

     Manage function metadata.
      

      
       Right-click the project directory on the left and choose Adc Assistant > Code Sync > Function Metadata Management.

       Go to the ADC page for configuring the environment during PyCharm login.
        
         If you have not logged in to ADC, go to the ADC login page.

         If you have logged in to ADC, go to the runtime- state ADC page.

        

       Manage function metadata by referring to Creating Python Function Service.

      

      

     Pull the function service code.
      

      
       Right-click the project directory on the left and choose Adc Assistant > Code Sync > Function Code Pulling.
        

      

      
       On the displayed page, enter the project name, module name, and function name of the function service created on ADC.

       Click Pull.
        After the pull is successful, the following dialog box is displayed.

        

        
          
         
          If the corresponding function code already exists in the current folder, a message is displayed, asking you whether to pull the function code again. If yes, the app in the current project is deleted and the latest code is pulled.

         

        

       Click Confirm.

       Right-click the project directory on the left and choose Reload from Disk.
        

       Check whether the app folder exists in the current local project directory. If yes, you can perform local commissioning in the project.
        

      

      

     Upload function code.
      

      
       Right-click the project directory on the left and choose Adc Assistant > Code Sync > Function Code Upload.

      

      
       On the displayed page, enter the project name, module name, and function name of the function service created on ADC.

       Click Push.
        After the upload is successful, the following dialog box is displayed.

        

       Click Confirm.

       Check whether the function service code on the ADC page is synchronized with the code of the current local project.
        

        

      

      

     Mark the faas_engine directory and its subdirectories as Sources Root.

name: Installing the Python Third-Party Components
title: Installing the Python Third-Party Components
text:
Installing the Python Third-Party Components
 
 
  
  

  
   Before debugging a local Python project, you need to install the Python third-party component.

   
    Prerequisites

    A local Python project has been created.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Configure the PIP source.
      

      
       Create the C:\Users\${username}\pip directory in local drive C.

       Create the pip.ini file in the preceding directory.

       Configure the pip.ini file.
        [global]
# Huawei PIP source is used as an example. Replace it as required.
timeout = 60
index-url = https://mirrors.huaweicloud.com/repository/pypi/simple
trusted-host = mirrors.huaweicloud.com

      

      

     Open the CMD command line interface (CLI) on the local PC.

     Install third-party components.
      

      Method 1: If you select an existing interpreter when creating a local Python project, perform the following operations:

      
       Run the following command to go to the ${PYTHONDIR}\Scripts directory:
        cd ${PYTHONDIR}\Scripts

        
          
         
          ${PYTHONDIR} indicates the Python installation directory, for example, c:\python3.9.2\Scripts. Replace it with the actual directory.

         

        

       Run the following command to install the third-party component requests:
        .\pip3.exe install requests==2.28.1

        
          
         
          The third-party component requests is used as an example. If other third-party components are used in the code, install them in the same way. In this method, you need to install the third-party component only once.

         

        

      

      Method 2: If you select a new interpreter when creating a local Python project, perform the following operations:

      
       Run the following command to go to the ${DIR}\venv\Scripts directory:
        cd ${DIR}\venv\Scripts

        
          
         
          ${DIR} indicates the project directory, for example, D:\05-python-projects\leetcode\pycharm-test. Replace it with the actual directory.

         

        

       Run the following command to install the third-party component requests:
        .\pip3.exe install requests==2.28.1

        
          
         
          The third-party component requests is used as an example. If other third-party components are used in the code, install them in the same way. In this method, you need to install the third-party component each time you use it.

         

        

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Local Debugging of a Python Function Service

Debugging a Local Python Project

    Context

    The Python sandbox function cannot be debugged in a local Python project.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Open the PyCharm that has been authenticated.

     Compile your Python code in the ${DIR}/app directory.
      

      
        
       
        ${DIR} indicates a project directory. Change it based on site requirements.

       

      

      

     (Optional) Compile the ${functionName}.json file.
      

      The faas.json file is used as an example. You can configure parameters as required.

      

      

     After compiling the code, run the framework process in the ${DIR}/app/parent/__main__.py directory, and then run your code.
      

      

      
        
       
        When a local Python project is debugged, the values of tracker_id and username in the context directory in the index.py file are the mock data used for local debugging instead of the actual running data.

       

      

      

     View logs in the adc-faas-python-function.log and adc-faas-python-runtime.log files.
      

      The log files are stored in the ${DIR}/app/faas_local_debug_temp/logs/function and ${DIR}/app/faas_local_debug_temp/logs/runtime directories.

name: What Can I Do If the Function Service Sandbox Does Not Contain the File Whitelist?
title: What Can I Do If the Function Service Sandbox Does Not Contain the File Whitelist?
text:
What Can I Do If the Function Service Sandbox Does Not Contain the File Whitelist?
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Symptom

    After ADC is upgraded from 24.5.6 to 24.5.9 or a later version, if the multi-thread function or rmtree method is used for changing the security sandbox, an error message is displayed due to sandbox permission restrictions. In this case, you can choose Products and Services > Log Management > FaaS Task Run Log in the runtime-state environment to view the log details of the corresponding function service. Information similar to the following figure is displayed in the function service log.

    
     The following error is reported when the multi-thread function is used.
      
       Python 3.9:
        You don't have access to the file: /opt/mateinfo/python/python3.9/lib/python3.9/threading.py

       Python 3.11:
        You don't have access to the file: /opt/mateinfo/python/python3.11/lib/python3.11/threading.py

      

    

    
     The following error is reported when the rmtree method is used.
      [2023-11-02 01:33:57.000]-[6542fc7c0d8e542a]-[2004]-[INFO]-[FBBMalaysisIPMANFaaS]-[FBBMalaysisIPMANFaaS]-[FAAS]-[fbb_malaysis_ipman scri pt_generation]-[adc_loggerwrite:113]-[Function-Execution]-[-[]-[]-[(ERROR] (ed20f3e3] You don't have access to the file: Undo Shutdown Route OL D PE1.] 

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The file whitelist is not added due to sandbox permission restrictions.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.

     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

     Choose Products and Services > Function Service > Sandbox Whitelist Configuration.

     Click  on the right of Config Information to configure file whitelists.
      

      
       Python 3.9 is used as an example. Configure the information based on the actual Python version.
       
        If the error is reported because the multi-thread function is used, enter /opt/mateinfo/python/python3.9/lib in the File white list text box.
         

         

        If the error is reported because the rmtree method is used, enter /opt/mateinfo/python/python3.9/lib in the File white list text box.

       

      

      

     Click Submit.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: FAQs

name: What Can I Do If the Memory of the Function Service Exceeds the Upper Limit?
title: What Can I Do If the Memory of the Function Service Exceeds the Upper Limit?
text:
What Can I Do If the Memory of the Function Service Exceeds the Upper Limit?
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Symptom

    After ADC is upgraded from 24.5.6 to 24.5.9 or a later version, if you run the function service directly, the error message shown in the following figure is displayed because Memory is set to 4G for the function service in the project in 24.5.6.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    When Memory is set to 4G for the function service, the app is not added to the app quota whitelist.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.

     Click the user account in the upper right corner, and choose Switch Tenant to switch to the master tenant.

     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

     Choose Products and Services > App O&M Management > App Quota Configuration.

     In the navigation pane, choose App Quota Whitelist.

     On the displayed page, click Create.

     Configure the app whitelist.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Whitelist Configuration Item

          
           Name of the app configuration item for which a whitelist is to be configured Select Procode Memory Quota.

         

         
          
           Tenant ID

          
           ID of the tenant corresponding to the app quota whitelist Select ID of the tenant under which the function service runs.

         

         
          
           App Scope

          
           Apps that the app quota whitelist applies to. Use commas (,) to separate multiple values. Enter the name of the app whose memory is 4 GB.

         

         
          
           Memory Quota (GB)

          
           Maximum memory that can be occupied by a specified app of a specified tenant when the function service is used. The value ranges from 1 to 20, in GB.

           Set this parameter to 4.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click OK.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: FAQs

name: Local Debugging Pro Code Plugin Login to ADC Times Out
title: Local Debugging Pro Code Plugin Login to ADC Times Out
text:
Local Debugging Pro Code Plugin Login to ADC Times Out
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Symptom

    By default, the local debugging Pro Code plugin does not support the network proxy configuration. As a result, the Pro Code plugin cannot be used to log in to ADC when the network proxy needs to be configured.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    No network proxy is configured for the local debugging Pro Code plugin.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Obtain the installation directory of adc-faas-cli.
      

      
       Open the CMD command line interface (CLI) on the local PC.

       Run the npm root -g command to obtain the installation directory of the NPM dependency package.

      

      The following information is displayed:

      C:\Users\user>npm root -g 
D:\DevelopKit\npm\node_global\node_modules 
      D:\DevelopKit\npm\node_global\node_modules indicates the installation directory of the NPM dependency package. The following uses this directory as an example. By default, adc-faas-cli is installed under the installation directory of the NPM dependency package. Therefore, the installation directory of adc-faas-cli is D:\DevelopKit\npm\node_global\node_modules\adc-faas-cli.

      

     Install node-global-proxy.
      

      
       Open the CMD CLI on the local PC.

       Run the following command to go to the adc-faas-cli installation directory:
        cd D:\DevelopKit\npm\node_global\node_modules\adc-faas-cli

       Run the following command to install node-global-proxy:
        npm install node-global-proxy --save

      

      

     Add the proxy configuration code.
      

      
       Open and edit the api.js file in the local directory.
        The api.js file is stored in the api directory of the adc-faas-cli installation directory. The D:\DevelopKit\npm\node_global\node_modules\adc-faas-cli\api directory is used as an example. Replace it with the actual directory.

       Add the following code to line 9 in the api.js file:
        import proxy from 'node-global-proxy'
        

       Add the following user proxy information to lines 54 and 92 in the api.js file.
        let user_proxy = proxy.default
user_proxy.setConfig({http: "http://usernanme:password@proxy"});
user_proxy.start(); 
        Replace username with the user name for logging in to the network proxy, password with the password of the user for logging in to the network proxy, and proxy with the network proxy address.

        
          
         
          If the value of username, password, or proxy contains special characters, such as *$%, you need to use URLencode to convert the special characters.

         

        

        

       Save the file.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: FAQs

name: Project Quality Assessment
title: Project Quality Assessment
text:
Project Quality Assessment
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes how to assess the project quality and rectify problems based on the assessment result.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     A project has been orchestrated.

     (Optional) If the AI quality detection capability needs to be enabled, ensure that you have completed the following operations:
      
       Contact the master tenant, set the system-level parameter global_aqm_ai_detection_enabled to true, and set Enabling Policy of the current tenant to Enable in the tenant-level Copilot configuration.

       Contact the tenant administrator and set the tenant-level parameter aqm_ai_detection_enabled to true.

      

    

   

   
    Context

    Currently, the system supports the check of project source files, models, services, and pages in terms of security, efficiency, and maintainability.

    The quality check capability varies according to the deployment solution.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Quality check
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Deployment Scenario

        
         Quality Check Capability

       

      
      
       
        
         Stack only

        
         In stack mode, the quality check can only be performed locally.

       

       
        
         Cloud

        
         In cloud mode, the quality check can be performed on the cloud.

       

       
        
         Stack Online

        
         In Stack Online mode, the quality check can be performed locally and on the cloud.

       

      
     
    

    You can choose General Settings > Quality Evaluation Rule Management to view the available check items.

    In addition, the standard check items that can be directly scanned by the current system are only part of the overall development specifications. Developers can learn more about the development specifications in App Development Specifications.

    The scoring rules for quality check are as follows: By default, the full score is 100 points. Three points are deducted for a critical problem, one point for a warning problem, and 0.1 point for a suggestion problem. If a critical problem is found, points will be deducted based on the full score of 80 points. When the score drops to 50 points, no more deduction is performed. That is, the lowest score displayed in the quality check is 50 points.

    If the score is lower than 80 points, the app quality does not meet the requirements and the app cannot be released.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Access the created project and click Quality Check at the bottom.

     Expand the check box at the bottom of the page and start the check. When the percentage reaches 100%, the check is complete.
      

      

      

      

     If an exception occurs during the check, confirm the result. You can click a rule name to view the rule details and solution.
      

      Take the rule Service validator check as an example. If the message "xxx: The input field of the service does not config a validator" is displayed in the details, configure a validator for the input parameter of the service. For details, see Configuring the Element Validator.

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Project Quality Evaluation and Issue Management

name: Describing the Deployment Capabilities
title: Describing the Deployment Capabilities
text:
Describing the Deployment Capabilities
 
 
  
  

  
   To ensure that developers can debug apps in a timely manner during app orchestration, the system supports triggering app deployment in the develop-state environment.

   
    App deployment allows you to quickly package the current project as an app and deploy the app in the runtime-state environment.

    During development and design in the develop-state environment, you can use the app deployment function to quickly deploy an app. After the app is deployed, you can debug services in the develop-state environment.

    If the configuration in the development state is updated and needs to be debugged again, you need to deploy it again to debug the updated content.

   

   You can trigger app deployment in the develop-state environment in either of the following ways:

   
    One-click deployment: Apps can be quickly deployed to the runtime-state environment corresponding to the current develop-state environment based on the current configuration.

    Customized deployment: You can customize deployment information, such as the running environment for deployment.

    Hot deployment: After the hot deployment mode is enabled, when the configuration in the develop-state environment changes, the deployment is automatically initiated. The deployment can be completed without being perceived by developers, optimizing developers' debugging experience.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: App Deployment Through a Develop-State Menu Entry

parent.name: App Deployment Through a Develop-State Menu Entry

name: One-Click Deployment
title: One-Click Deployment
text:
One-Click Deployment
 
 
  
  

  
   One-click deployment allows you to package the current project into an app and install it in the runtime-state environment.

   
    Prerequisites

    A project has been created.

   

   
    Context

    One-click deployment is performed based on the default configuration. If developers modify the configuration with hot deployment disabled for a project, they need to perform one-click deployment in a timely manner before debugging the project.

    For example, if hot deployment is not enabled for a developer's project and the input parameter configuration of the service is modified, the developer needs to perform one-click deployment before debugging the project.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Go to the created project, click  in the upper right corner, and select One-Click Deployment.

     The system automatically packages and deploys the project. After the deployment is complete, view the notification in the upper right corner.
      

      If an exception occurs during the deployment, locate the fault based on the exception information. View the detailed installation logs on the Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager page in the runtime-state environment.

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: App Deployment Through a Develop-State Menu Entry

parent.name: App Deployment Through a Develop-State Menu Entry

name: Custom Deployment
title: Custom Deployment
text:
Custom Deployment
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    A project has been created.

   

   
    Context

    Custom deployment supports the following modes:

    
     Package a project into an app and select information such as the remote deployment environment and included global assets.

     Deploy past packaged apps in the local asset library. After the current project is packaged into an app (for details, see Packaging a Project into an App), the app is stored in the local asset library. You can deploy this app in the library.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Go to the created project, click  in the upper right corner, and select Custom Deployment.

     (App packaging and deployment) In the displayed dialog box, click the Package and Deploy App tab and set basic project information.
      

      

      

      
       Target Environment: If the remote deployment is configured, you can select a runtime-state environment for deployment. You can select multiple environments and deploy the app in them at the same time. For details about remote deployment capabilities and configuration methods, see Configuring Remote Deployment.
        
          
         
          When you select a remote environment for deployment, note that if assets contain data orchestration or API Fabric orchestration elements, you need to manually set the deployment distribution mode to GDE App Manager in the Deployment Configuration dialog box.

         

        

       Included Global Assets: Add global assets to the project package.

       Dependency: If the dependency has been configured during project configuration, the dependency is automatically obtained. If the dependency is not set, you can add it here.

       Bind Developer Role: If this function is enabled, all permissions configured on the Permission page of the project are assigned to the StudioDeveloper role by default, facilitating debugging and verification for developers.

      

      

     (Deploying an existing app) In the displayed dialog box, click the Deploy Local App tab and set deployment information.
      

      

      

      
       Version: Select an option from the drop-down list. If there is no option in the drop-down list, the current project has not been packaged. In this case, package the project first. For details, see Packaging a Project into an App.

       Target Environment: If the remote deployment is configured, you can select a runtime-state environment for deployment. You can select multiple environments and deploy the app in them at the same time. If a role control whitelist is configured for the environment, the access is allowed only when the current user has the permission of the corresponding role. Environments on which the current user has the access permission are displayed here.

      

      

     After the configuration is complete, click Deploy. The system automatically packages and deploys the project. When the deployment is successful, a notification is displayed.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After the deployment is complete, view the installation logs on the Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager page in the runtime-state environment.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: App Deployment Through a Develop-State Menu Entry

parent.name: App Deployment Through a Develop-State Menu Entry

name: Hot Deployment
title: Hot Deployment
text:
Hot Deployment
 
 
  
  

  
   You can set whether to enable hot deployment through deployment configuration.

   
    Context

    Currently, the develop state is separated from the runtime state. After development, you need to package the elements and deploy them to the runtime state for debugging. Currently, the deployment of 50 element instances is completed within 1 minute. Some services have thousands of element instances. The deployment duration may reach 5 minutes, which is inconvenient for development and debugging.

    Hot deployment is to incrementally deploy elements orchestrated in the develop-state environment to the runtime-state environment in real time. Developers do not need to manually perform one-click deployment, which facilitates quick debugging.

    
      
     
      During process orchestration, only the hot deployment setting of process charts and process definitions (including creating, modifying, deleting, copying, enabling, and disabling processes) can be saved.

     

    

    When creating a project, you can determine whether to enable hot deployment. If you need to modify the configuration after the project creation, change the parameter value through deployment configuration.

   

   
     
    
     If an app fails to pass the quality assessment and code check, and birth certificates, registration certificates, and health certificates of the assets released to the runtime-state environment need to be verified, hot deployment to the runtime-state environment has security risks. In this case, you need to ensure that the risks are acceptable before enabling hot deployment.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Open to the created project, click  in the upper right corner, and choose Deployment Configuration.

     In the displayed dialog box, configure the deployment.
      

      

      

      

     Click OK.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: App Deployment Through a Develop-State Menu Entry

parent.name: App Deployment Through a Develop-State Menu Entry

name: Configuring the Deployment Distribution Mode
title: Configuring the Deployment Distribution Mode
text:
Configuring the Deployment Distribution Mode
 
 
  
  

  
   You can set the default distribution mode for app deployment mode through deployment configuration.

   
    Context

    The deployment distribution mode is used by the backend during app deployment. The selected distribution mode takes effect during app deployment.

    
     ADC App Manager is usually used to develop app distribution modes in ADC. It can also be used to orchestrate elements such as external access, API integration, common settings, network services, processes, robot automation, and network automation.

     GDE App Manager calls AppManager in the backend to install apps. It can also be used when orchestration elements including data orchestration and API integration are involved.

     Auto: If the orchestration elements of data orchestration and API integration are included and AppManager has been deployed in the current system, the asset is deployed based on the process of GDE App Manager. If the orchestration elements (for example, external access, API integration, common settings, network service, robot automation, and network automation) in ADC are detected, ADC App Manager can be used. This mode is not supported for remote deployment.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Open to the created project, click  in the upper right corner, and choose Deployment Configuration.

     In the displayed dialog box, configure the deployment.
      

      

      

      

     Click OK.

name: Packaging a Project into an App
title: Packaging a Project into an App
text:
Packaging a Project into an App
 
 
  
  

  
   An app is an entity that can be directly run in the runtime-state environment. You can package an app into a project and compile the project into an entity for running in the runtime-state environment.

   
    Context

    The app package name extension is .gpk. After a project is packaged into an app, the content in the generated app file cannot be modified.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Open the created project, click , and select App from the Packaged Into list.

     In the displayed dialog box, set the basic packaging information.
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Version

          
           
            The version format is fixed to n.n.n, where n is a number. Other version number formats are invalid.

            By default, the version starts from 0.0.1. Each time a packaging task is executed, the version increases.

            You can manually change the version of an app package and package the app package of an earlier version. For example, if you package apps of 0.0.1 and 0.0.2 and then package the app of 0.0.1, the assets in the local asset library are updated to the newly packaged assets of 0.0.1.

           

         

         
          
           Version Type

          
           You can set this parameter to Beta Version or Official Version for distinguishing.

         

         
          
           Asset Catalog

          
           Type of a service. Available values are asset catalogs in the asset library. For details about how to add an asset catalog, see Managing Labels.

         

         
          
           Submit Changes

          
           Whether to enable the function of submitting change records to record version changes. This parameter is not displayed by default. It is displayed only for tenants who have enabled the remote repository and whitelist.

         

         
          
           Version Change Reason

          
           Version change reason. This parameter is displayed only when Submit Changes is enabled.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Advanced Settings to view detailed settings.
      

      
       
       
        
         
          Table 2 Parameter description
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Name

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Sharing Scope

           
            Sharing scope, that is, the members who can view, package, and upload the asset on the Asset Management page. Set this parameter based on the sharing scope of the project.

            
             Public: All users can view and upload this asset.

             Personal: Only the creator can view and upload this asset.

             Team: Only team members can view and upload this asset.

             Restricted Public: All users can view this asset, but only the team or creator of the asset can upload the asset.

            

          

          
           
            Encrypt

           
            Specifies whether to encrypt the app package. If yes, the Password field is displayed. Set the encryption password.

            For an encrypted app package, you need to enter the password for decryption during project import and app installation. The corresponding operations can be performed only after the decryption is successful.

          

          
           
            Asset Listing Business Area

           
            Service domain of the asset to be deployed. The options in the drop-down list are the configurations on the Asset Management > Service Domain page. For details about how to add a service domain, see Managing Labels.

          

          
           
            Tag

           
            Used to classify assets so that specific assets can be quickly found. A label can contain a maximum of 20 characters and cannot contain \/:*?"'<>|(). Non-compliant labels will be deleted.

          

          
           
            Signature Certificate

           
            Signature certificate of the app package. The options in the drop-down list come from the value of Signature Certificate on the page displayed after you choose Products and Services > Administration > Password and Key > Asset Certificate Management.

          

          
           
            Prohibit Uninstallation

           
            After this function is enabled, the app cannot be uninstalled after being installed on the Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager in the runtime-state environment. This prevents the app from being deleted by mistake.

          

         
        
       

      

      

     Set the global assets contained in the project. Tenant-level global assets can be imported and packaged. Apps generated after global assets are packaged can be deployed in the runtime-state environment.
      

      
       Click Add.

       In the displayed dialog box, query and select the global asset to be added.
        

        

        
          
         
          According to the EOS date management of assets, you are advised not to use assets that are about to expire or have expired.

         

        

       Click OK.

      

      

     Add the project that the current project depends on. Dependent apps are verified only when runtime-state packages are imported. If the dependency is configured in the project, the configured dependency is automatically displayed during packaging.
      

      

      

      

     Click Package. After the packaging is complete, click Download.

    

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    
     After a project is packaged into an app, the app asset is stored in the local asset library by default and can be downloaded. On the home page of the develop state system, choose Asset Management > Asset Library and click the Local Assets tab.
      
       Figure 1 Local assets
       
      

     Click  and select Packaging History to view the packaging history and download or delete historical versions.
      If you select Delete Cascading Asset when performing the deletion operation, the assets stored in the local asset library will also be deleted.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Manually Packaging Projects into Assets

    When packaging a project package, you can set Read-only. If it is enabled, you cannot modify the project package when importing the project package to the environment again.

     In the displayed dialog box, set the basic packaging information.
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description

           Version Type

          
           You can set this parameter to Beta Version or Official Version.

         

         
          
           Asset Catalog

          
           Type of a service. Available values are asset catalogs in the asset library. For details about how to add an asset catalog, see Managing Labels.

         

         
          
           Submit Changes

          
           Whether to enable the function of submitting change records to record version changes. This parameter is not displayed by default. It is displayed only for tenants who have enabled the remote repository and whitelist.

         

         
          
           Version Change Reason

          
           Version change reason. This parameter is displayed only when Submit Changes is enabled.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Advanced Settings.
      

      

      
       
        
         Table 2 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Sharing Scope

          
           Sharing scope, that is, the members who can view, package, and upload the asset on the Asset Management page. Set this parameter based on the sharing scope of the project.

           
            Public: All users can view and upload this asset.

            Personal: Only the creator can view and upload this asset.

            Team: Only team members can view and upload this asset.

            Restricted Public: All users can view this asset, but only the team or creator of the asset can upload the asset.

           

         

         
          
           Tag

          
           Used to classify assets so that specific assets can be quickly found. A label can contain a maximum of 20 characters and cannot contain \/:*?"'<>|(). Non-compliant labels will be deleted.

         

         
          
           Signature Certificate

          
           Signature certificate of the app package. The options in the drop-down list come from the value of Signature Certificate on the page displayed after you choose Products and Services > Administration > Password and Key > Asset Certificate Management.

           Specifies whether to encrypt the project package. If yes, the Password field is displayed. Set the encryption password.

           Read-only

          
           When this function is enabled and the project package is imported to the development environment again, the project package cannot be modified.

     Set the global assets contained in the project. Tenant-level global assets can be packaged and downloaded.
      

      
       Click Add.

       In the displayed dialog box, query and select the global asset to be added.
        

        

        
          
         
          According to the EOS date management of assets, you are advised not to use assets that are about to expire or have expired.

         

        

       Click OK.

      

      

     Add the project that the current project depends on. Dependent apps are verified only when runtime-state packages are imported. If the dependency is configured in the project, the configured dependency is automatically displayed during packaging.
      

      

      

      

      

     Click Package. After the packaging is complete, click Download.

name: Packaging a Project into a Service Components (for Replication)
title: Packaging a Project into a Service Components (for Replication)
text:
Packaging a Project into a Service Components (for Replication)
 
 
  
  

  
   Service components (for replication) are used to copy orchestration elements between projects when developers export orchestration elements in the develop-state environment and import them to another project.

   
    Prerequisites

    A project or module has been created, and orchestration elements have been created.

   

   
    Context

    Packaging a project into a service component (for replication) is used to package only the selected component elements, that is, incremental packaging. The file name extension is .gdk.

    Currently, packaging a project into a service component (for replication) supports the following engines: basic orchestration, UI orchestration, process orchestration, interface integration orchestration, network operation automation orchestration, and RPA orchestration.

    After you obtain the service component package, import it in the develop-state environment. The elements that do not exist in the incremental package are not deleted. That is, only the added or changed elements are imported.

    For example, if orchestration element A has been configured in the current project and needs to be copied to another project, export orchestration element A and import it to another project.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access the created project, click , and select Service Component(Copy) from the Packed Into list.

     In the displayed window, set basic packaging information and click Next.

     Click Add, select the element to be added, and click Add again.
      

      
       Figure 1 Selecting an element
       
      

      

     To add multiple types of elements, repeat 3.

     After the elements are added, click Package.

     After the packaging is complete, click Download to obtain the incremental deployment package.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    Click  in the upper right corner of the project and module to be incrementally imported, select Import Component, and upload the downloaded .gdk package to import the exported component to other projects or modules.

    
     Figure 2 Importing a component
     
    

    In the scenario where hot deployment is enabled, after a component is imported, the deployment starts and the new component is deployed in the runtime-state environment.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Manually Packaging Projects into Assets

name: Packaging a Project into a Service Components (for Running)
title: Packaging a Project into a Service Components (for Running)
text:
Packaging a Project into a Service Components (for Running)
 
 
  
  

  
   Service components (for running) are full runtime-state app packages and can be loaded and packaged by other apps as subcomponents.

   
    Prerequisites

    A project or module has been created, and orchestration elements have been created.

   

   
    Context

    Package element instances in the current project into service components that can run. Different from apps, the service components can be loaded by or packaged with other apps. The service components can be used in the following engines: basic, UI, process, API integration, network operation automation, and RPA orchestration engines.

    The difference between packaging into a service component (for running) and packaging as a service component (for replication) is that the former is to package all orchestration elements in the entire project and use the packaged full .gdk package in the runtime-state environment as a service component.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access the created project, click , and select Service Component(Run) from the Packed Into list.

     In the displayed dialog box, set the basic packaging information.

     Expand Advanced Settings.
      

      

      

      

     Click Package.

     After the packaging is complete, click Download to obtain the incremental deployment package.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Manually Packaging Projects into Assets

name: Packaging a Project into an Upgrade Package
title: Packaging a Project into an Upgrade Package
text:
Packaging a Project into an Upgrade Package
 
 
  
  

  
   An upgrade package, also called a patch package, is an incremental package of modules and elements.

   
    Prerequisites

    An app has been packaged.

   

   
    Context

    You can package a project into an upgrade package. Upgrade packages, also called patch packages, can be created to incrementally package modules and elements. Custom assets and data import or export patches are supported for incremental upgrade.

    For example, if the versions 0.0.1 and 0.0.2 have been provided for an app and you want to use a patch package instead of a full package to upgrade the version 0.0.1 running in the runtime-state environment, you can package the app into an upgrade package.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Typical app upgrade packages
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Operation in Develop State

        
         Operation in Runtime State

        
         Version Change in Runtime State

       

      
      
       
        
         Package the app (version: 0.0.1) for the first time.

        
         Install an app in runtime state.

        
         0.0.1

       

       
        
         Package the app (version: 0.0.2) for the second time.

        
         Do not perform any operation. Do not install the full version of 0.0.2.

        
         None

       

       
        
         Package the upgrade package 0.0.3 and set the target app version to 0.0.2.

        
         Install the upgrade package.

        
         Changed to 0.0.2

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Open the created project, click , and select the upgrade package from the Packaged Into list.
      

      In the displayed dialog box, set the basic packaging information.

      
       
        
         Table 2 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Sharing Scope

          
           Sharing scope, that is, the members who can view, package, and upload the asset on the Asset Management page. Set this parameter based on the sharing scope of the project.

           
            Public: All users can view and upload this asset.

            Personal: Only the creator can view and upload this asset.

            Team: Only team members can view and upload this asset.

            Restricted Public: All users can view this asset, but only the team or creator of the asset can upload the asset.

           

         

         
          
           Patch version

          
           The system provides a default version based on the number of packaging times. You can customize the version. The new version must be greater than or equal to the default value. The value of this parameter does not affect the version after upgrade.

         

         
          
           Baseline App version

          
           Source version of the upgrade. Obtain the data from the packaged historical version. If the app is not packaged, no data is available. If this parameter is set, the upgrade version in the runtime-state environment can be deployed only when the current version in the runtime-state environment is in this version.

         

         
          
           Target App version

          
           Version to which the upgrade is performed. Obtain the data from the packaged historical version. If the app is not packaged, no data is available. If the value of Target App version is the same as that of Baseline App version, the version remains unchanged after upgrade.

         

         
          
           Tag

          
           Used to classify assets so that specific assets can be quickly found. A label can contain a maximum of 20 characters and cannot contain \/:*?"'<>|(). Non-compliant labels will be deleted.

         

         
          
           Signature Certificate

          
           Signature certificate of the app package. The options in the drop-down list come from the value of Signature Certificate on the page displayed after you choose Products and Services > Administration > Password and Key > Asset Certificate Management.

         

         
          
           Asset Listing Business Area

          
           Service domain of the asset to be deployed. The options in the drop-down list are the configurations on the Asset Management > Service Domain page. For details about how to add a service domain, see Managing Labels.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Description of the upgrade package.

         

         
          
           Submit Changes

          
           Whether to enable the function of submitting change records to record version changes. This parameter is not displayed by default. It is displayed only for tenants who have enabled the remote repository and whitelist.

         

         
          
           Version Change Reason

          
           Version change reason. This parameter is displayed only when Submit Changes is enabled.

         

        
       
      

      

     In the Elements area, select the upgrade package element. You can click Add Without Comparison or Add After Comparison.
      

      
       Add assets without comparison. Select an element, a module, or the element to be deleted, and click Add Without Comparison.
        
         Element: Select and package elements based on the orchestration element granularity.
          
           Figure 1 Selecting an element
           
          

          
            
           
            When adding an upgrade package whose Element Type is set to Process, if the elements on which the process depends are changed, you need to add the corresponding depended elements. Generally, a process depends on the following elements: model, service, page, permission, and internationalization.

           

          

         Module: Packages are selected based on the module granularity. After the module granularity is selected, you do not need to select elements in this module.
          
           Figure 2 Selecting a module
           
          

         To-be-deleted element: Select a specified module and element type, and then enter the name of the element to be deleted.
          
           Figure 3 Element to be deleted
           
          

          Figure 4 shows the style after selection

          
           Figure 4 Selecting upgrade elements
           
          

        

       Add assets after comparison. Compare the baseline app to be upgraded with the current project to identify the elements to be added.
        Click Add After Comparison. In the displayed dialog box, compare assets and determine the assets to be selected based on the comparison result.

      

      

     (Optional) Select the global asset to be added.
      

      
       Click Add.

       In the displayed dialog box, query and select the global asset to be added.
        

        

        
          
         
          According to the EOS date management of assets, you are advised not to use assets that are about to expire or have expired.

         

        

       Click OK.

      

      

     Click Package.

     Click Download to download the upgrade package to a local directory.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    In the runtime-state environment, choose Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager to install patches for apps that have been running the baseline version and upgrade the apps to the target version.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Manually Packaging Projects into Assets

name: Configuring the Project Template Scenario Directory
title: Configuring the Project Template Scenario Directory
text:
Configuring the Project Template Scenario Directory
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    Project template scenario directory, which is a category of project templates. Developers can classify scenarios based on service requirements and manage project templates by category.

    Currently, project directories can be configured in an Excel file and imported to the system for scenario directory management.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management and click Create Project. The scenario directory is displayed on the left.

     Click  to go to the page for uploading a scenario. Download the template and fill in the template.
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Template description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Scene ID

          
           Mandatory. The value can contain a maximum of 45 characters.

           Unique ID of a scenario. If the ID already exists, the existing scenario information is overwritten.

         

         
          
           Scene Name (Chinese)

          
           Mandatory. Scenario name displayed in the Chinese environment. The value can contain a maximum of 100 characters.

         

         
          
           Scene Name (English)

          
           Mandatory. Scenario name displayed in the English environment. The value can contain a maximum of 100 characters.

         

         
          
           Scene Description (Chinese)

          
           Scenario description displayed in the Chinese environment. The value can contain a maximum of 1000 characters.

         

         
          
           Scene Description (English)

          
           Scenario description displayed in the English environment. The value can contain a maximum of 1000 characters.

         

         
          
           Parent Scene ID

          
           Parent scenario ID.

           A maximum of two cascading layers are supported. The parent scenario data must be imported before the sub-scenario data.

         

        
       
      

      Figure 1 shows an example of template settings.

      
       Figure 1 Scenario directory example
       
      

      

     After filling in the template, click Add, upload the template, and click OK.

     Check the new data in the scenario directory.
      

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Managing Project Templates

name: Packaging a Project into a Template
title: Packaging a Project into a Template
text:
Packaging a Project into a Template
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    
     The project template scenario directory has been configured.

     You have created projects and modules that need to be preset in the template.

    

   

   
    Context

    You can release a created project or module as a project template. When you create a project, the content preset in the current project template is displayed by default.

    When releasing a project template, you can specify the scenario directory to which the project template is to be released.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access the project to be released as a template, click , and select Project Template from the Packaged Into list.

     In the displayed dialog box, set the basic packaging information.

     Click Advanced Settings and set other template parameters.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Sharing Scope

          
           Sharing scope, that is, the members who can view, package, and upload the asset on the Asset Management page. Set this parameter based on the sharing scope of the project.

           
            Personal: Only the creator can view and upload this asset.

            Team: Only team members can view and upload this asset.

            Restricted Public: All users can view this asset, but only the team or creator that the asset belongs to can upload the asset.

           

         

         
          
           Asset Listing Business Area

          
           Service domain of the asset to be deployed. The options in the drop-down list are the configurations on the Asset Management > Service Domain page. For details about how to add a service domain, see Managing Labels.

         

         
          
           Tag

          
           Used to classify assets so that specific assets can be quickly found. A label can contain a maximum of 20 characters and cannot contain \/:*?"'<>|(). Non-compliant labels will be deleted.

         

         
          
           Signature Certificate

          
           Signature certificate of the app package. The options in the drop-down list come from the value of Signature Certificate on the page displayed after you choose Products and Services > Administration > Password and Key > Asset Certificate Management.

         

         
          
           Display Sequence

          
           Used to define the position where the project template is displayed when you select a template during project creation. A smaller value indicates a higher position. If the values are the same, the project templates are displayed in ascending order by ID. If this parameter is not set, the default value 100 is used.

           Value range: an integer from 1 to 10000

         

         
          
           Template Scenario

          
           Select the default template scenario provided by the system or a customized template scenario from the drop-down list.

         

         
          
           Background Page URL

          
           Background page after a project is created based on this template. The project page is displayed when no orchestration element tab pages are opened.

           The value must be an absolute path starting with / in the domain. It can contain a maximum of 300 characters, including two consecutive digits, letters, and the following special characters: +&@#/%?=~-_|!:,.;

           Source of the background page. Generally, the background page is developed by developers. You can configure the URL of a background page to reference the page as the background page. To ensure that the background page can be packaged and released with the project template, you need to package the project for developing the background page as an executable service component, that is, select Service Component(Run) from Packaged Into drop-down list, and load the component to the global asset.

           For example, if a page whose project name is page, module name is page, and page name is page_background is used as the background page, the URL is /adc-web/ui/standalone/index.html#/spl2/page/page/page_background.

         

         
          
           Welcome Page URL

          
           Welcome page of the project page after a project is created based on the template. The configuration restrictions are the same as those of Background Page URL.

           If the welcome page is configured, the Welcome tab page is displayed after you use this template to create a project. Content in the welcome page is displayed on this tab page.

         

         
          
           Preview Image

          
           Enables users to understand the template. Multiple images can be provided.

         

         
          
           Submit Changes

          
           Whether to enable the function of submitting change records to record version changes. This parameter is not displayed by default. It is displayed only for tenants who have enabled the remote repository and whitelist.

         

         
          
           Version Change Reason

          
           Version change reason. This parameter is displayed only when Submit Changes is enabled.

         

        
       
      

      

     (Optional) Configure the multi-language template description.
      

      

      

      

     (Optional) Perform this step when the background page and welcome page are configured. Click Add, enter Service Component in the search box, select the packaged service components, and click OK.
      

      

      

      
        
       
        
         The asset page is generated after being packaged as a service component (running). It provides the orchestrated background page and welcome page.

         You cannot select the service components packaged from the current project, that is, the development background page or welcome page and template must belong to different projects.

         When the global asset is packaged after being loaded, the system deploys the service component to the runtime-state environment. When this project template is used during project creation, the background page and welcome page can directly call the pages that have been deployed in the runtime-state environment to display the pages.

         When a project template is imported to the asset library as a file, the global assets contained in the project template are automatically imported to the asset library, and the service components contained in the project template are automatically installed in the runtime-state environment.

        

       

      

      

     (Optional) Configure the dependency between project templates. The dependency needs to be configured only when the project depends on other projects. For example, if the current project depends on the system project, you can configure the dependency. If the current project does not depend on any project, you do not need to configure the dependency.
      

      
       Figure 1 Dependency
       
      

      

     Click Package. After the packaging is complete, click Close or Download.
      

      After the packaging, the project template is added to the selected template scenario. Developers can select the corresponding scenario and project template when creating a project.

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    After the project template is packaged, it is uploaded to the asset library. You can view the asset library by clicking Local Assets on the Asset Management > Asset Library page of the develop-state environment. For details about how to deploy assets, view asset history, as well as download and delete assets, see Tenant Asset Management.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Managing Project Templates

text:
Configuring Remote Deployment
 
 
  
  

  
   Through remote deployment, apps in the current system can be deployed in multiple remote systems. This section describes how to perform remote app deployment.
