name: Introduction to Remote Deployment
title: Introduction to Remote Deployment
text:
Introduction to Remote Deployment
 
 
  
  

  
   Apps must be developed in the develop-state environment of ADC and debugged and run in the runtime state. ADC allows you to deploy apps developed in a develop-state environment in multiple runtime-state environments.

   For example, after developing an app in the develop-state environment, you can deploy it in runtime-state environment 1 for testing. After the test is complete, you can deploy the app in runtime-state environment 2 for production.

   This way ensures normal running of the production environment and ensured and improves app release efficiency.

   

   This feature requires multiple environments to interwork. You need to configure this feature in the involved runtime-state environments and develop-state environment before using it.

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Configuring Remote Deployment

name: Configuring a Machine-Machine Account (in the Runtime-State Environment)
title: Configuring a Machine-Machine Account (in the Runtime-State Environment)
text:
Configuring a Machine-Machine Account (in the Runtime-State Environment)
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    Remote deployment requires authorization of the runtime-state environment. Therefore, you need to configure a machine-machine account used for authentication and authorization. When multiple remote runtime-state environments are required, the machine-machine account must obtain the authentication and authorization of each environment.

    A machine-machine role adc-remote-app-manager is preset in the system. You need to create a machine-machine account and associate it with this preset role for authenticating the environment configured with remote deployment.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as an administrator (for example, admin).

     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

     Choose Products and Services > Administration > Identity Authentication > Machine-Machine User Management.

     Click Create Machine-Machine User.

     Set machine-machine user information.
      

      
       Figure 1 Parameters for creating a machine-machine user
       
      

      
       
        
         
          Table 1 Parameters for creating a machine-machine user
         
         
          
          
         
         
          
           
            Parameter

           
            Description

          

         
         
          
           
            Machine-Machine User Account

           
            Machine-machine user account under a service tenant, which is used for login. The value can contain 6 to 64 characters, including only digits, letters, and underscores (_).

          

          
           
            Authentication Type

           
            The value can be AK/SK or Basic. Either authentication mode will work.

          

          
           
            Select Human-Machine User

           
            Human-machine user associated with the machine-machine user. You can select an option as required. This parameter is optional.

          

          
           
            Description

           
            Description of the machine-machine user. The value can contain 0 to 512 characters.

          

         
        
       

       
         
        
         
          Record the new machine-machine user account and AK/SK information or basic key information. The system displays the information only once.

          AK: unique identifier associated with the private access key. The AK and private access key are used together to encrypt the request signature.

          SK: private access key that works with AK to obtain an encrypted signature for a request, identify the sender, and prevent the request from being modified.

          An AK identifies a user, and an SK is used to calculate a signature.

         

        

       

      

      

     Click Submit. The system displays the Creation Success dialog box. Record the AK/SK or basic key information.
      

      
       Figure 2 AK/SK information
       
      

      

     Assign a role to the machine-machine user.
      

      
        
       
        
         In the non-RSM scenario (only the admin administrator is preset), you do not need to switch to another user.

         In the RSM scenario (the admin, secadmin, and secauditor users are preset), the admin user does not have the permission to manage roles or bind IP addresses. You need to switch to the secadmin user and then perform operations in 7 and 8.

        

       

      

      
       
        Click the machine-machine user to be associated with a role, and then click the Machine-Machine User Authorization tab.

        Click Machine-Machine Role. On the displayed page, select roles for the machine-machine user as required. For example, you can select adc-remote-app-manager.
         

         

        Click Associate.

       

      

      

     Optional: Create an IP address association policy and associate it with the machine-machine user.
      

      
        
       
        
         Authentication mode of an IP address access control policy:
          
           If a whitelist is configured to allow the access from a specified IP address or IP address segment, IP addresses not in the whitelist cannot be used for access.

           If a blacklist is configured to reject the access from a specified IP address or IP address segment, IP addresses not in the blacklist can be used for access.

           If there is no configuration data, IP addresses are not restricted.

          

         By default, the system presets the default IP address control policy for machine-machine users in basic authentication mode. However, the IP addresses that need to be authorized for remote deployment are not included in the default IP address control policy of the tenant. In actual configuration, you need to associate the IP address access control policy as planned to cater to different authentication modes.
          
           For the basic authentication mode, if you do not modify the IP address authentication policy, the authentication fails. You can delete the default authentication policy. Specifically, IP addresses are not restricted. Alternatively, you can add a proper IP address and associate it to enhance security.

           For the AK/SK authentication mode, there is no default IP address control policy. Therefore, IP addresses will not be verified and will pass the authentication. You can add a proper IP address and associate it to enhance security.

          

        

       

      

      
       Choose Products and Services > Administration > Security Center > IP Access Control Policy Configuration.

       Click Create IP Access Control Policy.

       Set the parameters on the displayed page based on site requirements. The following table lists all parameters for you to configure an IP address control policy. After the configuration is complete, click Submit.
        

        

        
         
          
           
            Table 2 Parameters for creating an IP address access control policy
           
           
            
            
           
           
            
             
              Parameter

             
              Description

            

           
           
            
             
              IP Address Type

             
              IP address types that can be configured in an IP address access control policy are as follows:

              
               IP address: You can configure a specific IP address, for example, 10.10.x.x.

               IP address range: You can configure the start IP address and end IP address of a network segment, for example, 10.x.x.0 and 10.x.x.255.

               IP address segment: You can configure an IP segment in IP address/mask format, for example, 10.x.x.0/16.

               IP geolocation: You can enter the geographical location of an IP address. During access authentication, the system determines whether the access using the IP address in the IP address segment corresponding to the geographical location associated in the access control policy.

              

            

            
             
              IP Address

             
              This parameter is mandatory when IP Address Type is set to IP address.

              The system supports IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

            

            
             
              IP Address Segment

             
              This parameter is mandatory when IP Address Type is set to IP address segment.

              The system supports IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

            

            
             
              IP Geolocation

             
              This parameter is mandatory when IP Address Type is set to IP geolocation.

              You can set the geographical location in the IP address access control policy based on site requirements.

            

            
             
              Start IP Address

             
              When IP Address Type is set to IP address range, you need to set Start IP Address and End IP Address.

              The system supports IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, and the start IP address must be smaller than the end IP address.

            

            
             
              End IP Address

            

            
             
              Control Type

             
              The control types of an IP address access control policy are as follows:

              
               Allow: The configured IP address is allowed to access the system.

               Reject: The configured IP address is rejected to access the system.

              

            

            
             
              Effective Type

             
              The effective types of an IP address access control policy are as follows:

              
               Effective after user association: When a user is associated with a configured IP address access control policy, the policy takes effect for the user.

               Globally effective: If a user is not associated with any IP address access control policy, the preset global policy takes effect for the user. If Globally effective is selected, users for whom the preset global policy is not configured cannot log in to the system.
                
                  NOTE: 
                 
                  The IP address access control policy whose Effective Type is Globally effective does not take effect for machine-machine users.

                 

                

              

            

            
             
              Client Type

             
              Client type supported by the system to which the access is controlled. The options are as follows:

              
               All: web and mobile devices

               Web

               Mobile

              

            

           
          
         

        

        
         
           
          
           When the whitelist is used for IP address access control, the allowed IP address segment must contain the IP address of the node where adc-studio-project-mgt is located. You can obtain the node installation plan from the installation personnel or GDE Kernel.

          

         

        

       Choose Products and Services > Administration > Identity Authentication > Machine-Machine User Management. On the displayed page, click the created machine-machine user, and then click the IP Access Control Policy tab.

       Click IP Access Control Policy and select the configured IP address policy as required.

       Click Associate.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Configuring Remote Deployment

name: Managing the Runtime-State Environment Information (in the Develop-State Environment)
title: Managing the Runtime-State Environment Information (in the Develop-State Environment)
text:
Managing the Runtime-State Environment Information (in the Develop-State Environment)
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Prerequisites

    You have obtained the machine-machine account information of the runtime-state environment.

   

   
    Context

    If remote deployment is required and you need to deploy an app in multiple runtime-state environments, configure runtime-state environment information in the develop-state environment first.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as an administrator (for example, admin) of a tenant and choose Development State Studio to go to the develop-state environment.

     Choose General Settings > Environment Management.

     On the displayed page, click Create.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Environment Name

          
           Environment name based on which developers identify the remote deployment environment during deployment. The environment name must be clear.

           The value must start with a letter and can contain only letters, digits, underscores (_), hyphens (-), and periods (.). A maximum of 50 characters are allowed.

         

         
          
           Description

          
           Environment description.

         

         
          
           Deploy Environment Address

          
           Address for accessing the runtime-state environment where the app is deployed. The format is "https://IP address:Port number/" or "https://{Domain name}/".

           Set this parameter to the access address of the runtime-state environment that the machine-machine account in Configuring a Machine-Machine Account (in the Runtime-State Environment) belongs to.

         

         
          
           Environment Type

          
           Environment type, for example, alpha, beta, and product.

         

         
          
           Public

          
           Reserved field.

         

         
          
           Enable the reverse proxy

          
           Enable this function when the reverse proxy is configured on the LB in the develop-state environment for interworking.

         

         
          
           Authentication Type

          
           Authentication type, which must be the same as that of the machine-machine account created in Configuring a Machine-Machine Account (in the Runtime-State Environment).

           
            Basic

            AK/SK

           

         

         
          
           Authentication Identity

          
           Authentication identity of the machine-machine account, which is obtained when the machine-machine account is created in Configuring a Machine-Machine Account (in the Runtime-State Environment).

           
            If Authentication Type is set to Basic, set this parameter to the value of AccessId of the basic key.

            If Authentication Type is set to AK/SK, set this parameter to the value of Accesskey of the AK/SK key.

           

         

         
          
           Authentication Credential

          
           Authentication credential of the machine-machine account, which is obtained when the machine-machine account is created in Configuring a Machine-Machine Account (in the Runtime-State Environment).

           If Authentication Type is set to Basic or AK/SK, the value of this parameter is the same as that of Secretkey.

         

         
          
           Use Auto Environment

          
           Automation environment, which is used in the automatic test scenario of the ADC Mate CI/CD tool chain to simulate human-machine interaction and perform deployment verification by using an automatic pipeline. Therefore, this environment is usually configured as the frontend access address of the automatic test and verification environment.

           For details about the automation function, see Function Test.

         

         
          
           Web Auth Type

          
           This parameter is displayed when Use Auto Environment is enabled.

           Currently, only SSO is supported.

         

         
          
           User Access Address

          
           This parameter is displayed when Use Auto Environment is enabled.

           Set this parameter to the frontend access address in the automatic test scenario.

         

         
          
           User Name

          
           This parameter is displayed when Use Auto Environment is enabled.

           Set this parameter to the user name used for the automatic test.

         

         
          
           User Password

          
           This parameter is displayed when Use Auto Environment is enabled.

           Set this parameter to the password of the user used for the automatic test.

         

         
          
           Whitelist of Roles That Can Access the Environment

          
           Role whitelist, which is used to control the environment access permission.

           
            If this parameter is not set, the user roles are not controlled.

            If a role is configured, only users associated with the whitelist role have the permission to access the environment.

           

         

        
       
      

      

     Click OK to save the settings.

    

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Configuring Remote Deployment

name: Configuring Interworking Between Network Nodes (in the Develop-State Environment)
title: Configuring Interworking Between Network Nodes (in the Develop-State Environment)
text:
Configuring Interworking Between Network Nodes (in the Develop-State Environment)
 
 
  
  

  
   
     
    
     The operations described in this section need to be performed by delivery personnel or O&M personnel.

    

   

   If the network between the docker node (adc-studio-project-mgt) where the develop-state project is managed and the docker node where the LB of the runtime-state environment is deployed is disconnected, remote deployment cannot be performed. In this case, you need to configure the network interworking.

   Determine the network connection mode based on the actual network conditions.

   
    Method 1: Bind the docker node where the project is managed to the host machine with a public IP address, for example, the maccrt01 node. This operation must be performed at the IaaS layer. Contact the IaaS administrator to perform this operation or perform this operation by referring to the IaaS guide. This method is preferred. If this method cannot be used, use method 2.

    Method 2: If the LB nodes in the develop-state environment and runtime-state environment can communicate with each other, configure the reverse proxy on the LB node in the develop-state environment. You do not need to manually configure this item. When you set the runtime-state environment information, enable the reverse proxy function. For details, see Managing the Runtime-State Environment Information (in the Develop-State Environment).

    Method 3: In the public and private network scenarios, if the address of the deployment environment is a public network address, perform the following steps:
     
      On the Environment Management page, turn on the Enable the reverse proxy switch. For details, see Managing the Runtime-State Environment Information (in the Develop-State Environment).

      Log in to the lb-service node and run the following command to access the docker container where the lb-service node is deployed:
       Run the following command to check the container ID:

       docker ps | grep lb-service

       Run the following command to access the container:

       docker exec -it Container ID bash

       

      Modify the environment configuration file.
       vi /usr/local/NSP/etc/nginx/vhosts/route_adc_{Tenant ID}_env.config

       Replace {Tenant ID} with the actual tenant ID, for example, 1002.

       In the opened file, edit the configuration file and save it.

        location /adc-remote-install/tenant_1002/{env_name}/ {
    rewrite /adc-remote-install/tenant_1002/{env_name}/(.*) /$1 break;
    proxy_pass {lb_external_ip};
}
       {env_name} indicates the environment name configured in Managing the Runtime-State Environment Information (in the Develop-State Environment).

       Set {lb_external_ip} to the value of lb_external_url in the lb-cfg-configmap configuration item, as shown in the following figure.

name: Commissioning a Remotely Deployed App (in Develop State)
title: Commissioning a Remotely Deployed App (in Develop State)
text:
Commissioning a Remotely Deployed App (in Develop State)
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    After developing an app in the develop-state environment, a developer can remotely deploy the app in different environments for testing and releasing.

    
      
     
      Data orchestration-related apps strongly depend on data sources. Therefore, during remote deployment, ensure that the corresponding data source has been configured in the remote environment. This restriction does not apply to other orchestration scenarios.

     

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the develop-state environment as a developer.

     Go to the created project, click  in the upper right corner, and select Custom Deployment.

     Click Advanced Settings. In the Select Running Environment drop-down list, select a configured remote deployment environment.
      

      

      

      
        
       
        When you select a remote environment for deployment, note that if assets contain data orchestration or API Fabric orchestration elements, you need to manually set the deployment distribution mode to GDE App Manager in the Deployment Configuration dialog box.

       

      

      

     Click Deploy.

     Confirm the settings as prompted and click OK.

     In this dialog box, the system installs the app and logs the operations. After the message "Deploy successfully." is displayed, click Close.

     After the deployment is complete, access the remote running environment to check the app.

    

   

   
    Handling Exceptions

    If the remote deployment fails and the following information is displayed, check the authentication configuration by performing the operations in 8.

    [2021-10-19 12:03:06]-[INFO]-[adc-studio-project] Project packaging task starts. Task ID: 844ecf4f-30d4-11ec-bcbf-0255ac12002a
...
[2021-10-19 12:03:10]-[ERROR]-[adc-studio-project] Failed to install the app.
[2021-10-19 12:03:13]-[ERROR]-[adc-studio-project] Failed to obtain the authentication information.
   

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Configuring Remote Deployment

name: Introducing Project Database Sharding
title: Introducing Project Database Sharding
text:
Introducing Project Database Sharding
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Introduction to Database Sharding

    Sharding is a method for distributing a single dataset across multiple databases, which can then be stored on multiple machines. This allows for larger datasets to be split in smaller chunks and stored in multiple data nodes, increasing the total storage capacity of the system. By default, the system supports app database sharding. Developers need to configure the service domain of a project and create data sources for the service domain to implement database sharding.

    
     Figure 1 Database sharding diagram
     
    

   

   
    Database Sharding Configuration

    Database sharding configuration includes project configuration in develop state and data source configuration on the management plane.

    
     
      
       Table 1 Database sharding configuration
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Configuration Item

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         (Mandatory) Configure Service Domain for the project.

        
         This parameter is set by the developer in the develop-state environment.

       

       
        
         (Optional) Configure the database.

        
         This parameter is set by the administrator on the management plane.

       

       
        
         (Mandatory) Configure extra data sources for tenants.

        
         This parameter is set by the administrator on the management plane.

       

       
        
         (Optional) Configure the elastic model database sharding feature.

        
         This parameter is set after the installation to support elastic model data synchronization.

       

      
     
    

   

   
    Database Sharding Constraints

    If a project has been deployed and a data model instance has been created in the runtime state, database sharding will not be triggered when the project is deployed again. The database sharding status cannot be changed after deployment.

    In the debugging phase, developers can uninstall apps without retaining data during uninstallation. After the uninstallation is complete, developers can deploy the apps again to implement database sharding.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Database Sharding

name: Configuring Project Database Sharding (Develop State)
title: Configuring Project Database Sharding (Develop State)
text:
Configuring Project Database Sharding (Develop State)
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    ADC supports project-level database sharding. You can configure database sharding for a project and create a project database instance to a specified database.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the Studio in the develop state as a developer.

     Choose Project Management.

     Configure a service domain.
      

      
       On the top menu bar, choose General Settings > Service Domain Management.

       Click Create and set parameters.
        
         Figure 1 Creating a service domain
         
        

       Click OK.

      

      

     Configure the service domain to which the project belongs. The Service Domain field can be set during or after the project creation. The following steps describe how to configure a service domain after project creation. For details about how to create a project, see Creating a Project.
      

      
       On the Project Management page, click  the card of a created project.
        
         Figure 2 Configuring a project
        

        

       On the Project Settings tab page, click Edit on the right of Project Information to configure the service domain, for example, FM.
        
         Figure 3 Configuring a service domain
        

        

       Click OK to save the service domain settings.

name: Configuring a Data Source for Database Sharding (Management Zone)
title: Configuring a Data Source for Database Sharding (Management Zone)
text:
Configuring a Data Source for Database Sharding (Management Zone)
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    In an actual environment, the data source for database sharding is configured by the master administrator on the management zone.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.

     Click the user account in the upper right corner, and choose Switch Tenant to switch to the master tenant.

     Configure a data source. Each tenant has a default tenant database. If no extra database is available in the debugging phase, the default tenant database can be used for service verification.
      

      If extra data sources need to be added, you need to configure them using the TSM API for creating or updating external data sources, and specify the service configuration for the corresponding tenant using the service broker template.

      After configuring the database specified by the tenant, you can view the database on the Products and Services > ADC System Management > Component Management > DB Configuration page.

      

     Configure the extra data source for the tenant. Choose Products and Services > ADC System Management > Tenant Extra Data Sources Management. Click Create.

     Click Create and configure extra data sources of the tenant.
      

      
       Figure 1 Configuring extra data sources for the tenant
       

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters for configuring extra data sources for the tenant
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Tenant ID

          
           ID of the tenant who uses the extra data source.

         

         
          
           Data Source Type

          
           Type of the extra data source.

           
            DB: database

            ES: Elasticsearch

           

         

         
          
           Data Source Configuration Name

          
           Name of the extra data source configuration.

           
            When Data Source Type is set to DB, the data source configuration name is the value of Name on the DB Configuration page.

            When Data Source Type is set to ES, the data source configuration name is the value of Name on the ES Configuration page.

           

         

         
          
           Configuration Detail

          
           Database schema ID of the extra data source.

           This parameter is displayed only when Data Source Type is set to DB.

         

         
          
           Configure Label

          
           Label of the extra data source.

           Click Add and configure the label name and value of the extra data source.

           
            Label: label name of the extra data source.
             
              In the database sharding scenario, set this parameter to division_domain.

              In other scenarios, set this parameter based on site requirements.

             

            Tag Value: label value of the extra data source.
             
              In the database sharding scenario, the value of division_domain must be set to the service domain name for association in the project.
               
                 NOTICE: 
                
                 When Data Source Type is set to ES, do not set division_domain to DEFAULT. Otherwise, the preset data source configuration for the Elasticsearch shard may be affected.

                

               

              In other scenarios, set this parameter based on site requirements.

             

           

         

         
          
           Whether to Enable

          
           After the configuration, determine whether to enable the extra data source configuration for the tenant.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click OK.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Database Sharding

name: Debugging Database Sharding
title: Debugging Database Sharding
text:
Debugging Database Sharding
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    After database sharding is deployed, you need to check whether new data is generated in the secondary database. Users are unaware of database sharding. They need to view the database sharding result in the back-end database.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Deploy an app. In an environment where the develop-state system and runtime-state system is co-deployed, you can install the app in one-click mode in the develop-state system. If an independent test environment in the runtime-state environment is provided, export the app package in the develop-state environment, access the runtime-state environment, choose Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager, and install the app.

     Add data to the model of the app based on the actual configuration of this app.

     (R&D personnel) Check the database sharding result based on back-end data. The following uses the GaussDB database as an example to describe how to view the data result.
      

      
       Log in to the node as the sshusr user, switch to the root user, and run the following command to switch to the gtsgsdba user:
        su - gtsgsdba -s /bin/bash

       Connect to the database on the current host as the administrator.
        zsql / as sysdba -q

       Query data.
        SQL> SELECT USERNAME , ACCOUNT_STATUS FROM ADM_USERS;
USERNAME                                                         ACCOUNT_STATUS 
---------------------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------
SYS                                                              OPEN                                       MATEINFO_2001                                                    OPEN       
MATEINFO_PORTAL_2001                                             OPEN
MATEINFO_2000                                                    OPEN
PROJECT001                                                     OPEN     
......
31 rows fetched.
SQL> alter session set current_schema=PROJECT001;
Succeed.
//PROJECT001 indicates the database schema ID configured in the extra data source.
SQL> select * from adm_tables where TABLE_NAME LIKE '%MODULE_NAME%';
//Check whether the instance table of the corresponding model data is generated.

      

      

    

   

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Database Sharding

name: Configuring the Elastic Model Database Sharding Feature
title: Configuring the Elastic Model Database Sharding Feature
text:
Configuring the Elastic Model Database Sharding Feature
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    After the configuration is complete based on Configuring a Data Source for Database Sharding (Management Zone) and Configuring Project Database Sharding (Develop State), the basic sharding feature of data models can be implemented.

    In the current service scenario, after a data model is created in the schema of database sharding, the data model needs to synchronize the elastic model data. For example, in the FM service domain, after the database sharding feature is configured, data model A created in the database sharding schema needs to be synchronized to elastic model B.

    
     In the MySQL database, this feature can be used by default. No additional configuration is required.

     In the GaussDB database, you need to modify the configuration of the corresponding data source node.

    

    The elastic model–based database sharding feature has the following restrictions:

    
     Currently, only GaussDB and MySQL databases are supported.

     The GaussDB database sharding supports only database nodes installed using GKit as external data sources.

     The newly connected database must communicate with the system network to which ADC is to be connected.

     The version of the newly connected external GaussDB database must be Gauss100 OLTP 1.3.0 or later.

     A maximum of 10 external database sources can be configured. Only the scenarios where both the master and slave databases are GaussDB or MySQL databases are supported.

     Before you install adc-zenith-trigger on the server where the external GaussDB database is located, install third-party components, for example, ADC-rhm and adc-mgt-init jre1.8 or later.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Use GKit to expand the capacity of the GaussDB node, and install the adc-zenith-trigger plugin on the GaussDB node.

     After the installation and before the startup, manually modify the external data source configuration.
      

      
       Log in to the node as the sshusr user and switch to the root user.

       Modify the /opt/adc-zenith-trigger/mateinfo/cfg/mateinfo_logicrep.properties file, and add configuration information in the format of DB_LINK_ID=Database name. The database name is the name of the database added in 3. You can view the database name after choosing Products and Services > ADC System Management > Component Management > DB Configuration.
        DB_LINK_ID=newdb01

       Log in to the GDE management zone portal as the installation user of the external data source service.

       Choose Maintenance > Instance Deployment > K8s Application Deployment.

       Search for adc-zenith-trigger. In the Operation column of the located record, click Stop. After the plugin is stopped, click Start.

       If there are multiple nodes, perform the preceding operations on each node. To upgrade or redeploy the adc-zenith-trigger plugin, perform the preceding steps again.

      

      

    

   

   
    Result Commissioning

name: Introduction to Customized Apps
title: Introduction to Customized Apps
text:
Introduction to Customized Apps
 
 
  
  

  
   When an app is running on the live network, the released baseline app is customized for different tenants or sites due to differences and changes between sites and service requirements. As a result, the app mixes baseline and customized contents together, making the version management difficult. With the expansion of services, the problem will become more serious. These hinder service deployment and expansion. The pain points are:

   
    During an upgrade, the services or features of a general app will overwrite the app customized for a site. The changes must be sorted out manually and incorporated to the target app. This is time-consuming and error-prone. (This poses high skills requirements for the upgrade personnel.)

    The apps are not well protected, and customized services are mixed in the baseline apps. Therefore, it is difficult for the service personnel to determine the customized contents. The upgrade risk is high.

   

   To resolve preceding problems, the system provides the configuration and development function for customized apps to separate the baseline contents from customized contents, implementing efficient customization. Before customization, developers are advised to analyze possible customization features and plan customization. Figure 1 shows the customization capabilities. The customization capabilities are described as follows:

   
    A project to be customized is called a baseline project.

    A baseline project can be customized into multiple projects. For example, if the baseline project needs to be used to deliver multiple projects such as A, B, C, and D, you need to perform customization for multiple times to obtain corresponding customized projects.

    When a baseline project is customized in a project, all customized orchestration elements are placed in only one project for management.

    In a customized project, you can customize orchestration elements in the baseline project, and add orchestration elements.

    Elements in a baseline project can be customized in a project only after being configured to customizable.

   

   
    Figure 1 Customized project diagram
    
   

   
    The baseline model mod_a needs to be customized at a site and is customized as mod_a' in the customized project. The running effect is that the customized model mod_a' takes effect.

    The baseline model mod_b can be ignored in the customized project because it does not need to be customized at a site. The running effect is that the baseline model mod_b takes effect.

    The baseline service service_a needs to be customized at a site and is customized as service_a' in the customized project. The running effect is that the customized service service_a' takes effect.

    The baseline service service_b can be ignored in the customized project because it does not need to be customized at a site. The running effect is that the service_b takes effect.

    To add a requirement at a site, you can add models and services to the customized module or add a module. The new orchestration elements also take effect during running.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Customized Apps

name: Customizing Services
title: Customizing Services
text:
Customizing Services
 
 
  
  

  
   The system supports customization of services in apps so that existing assets can be reused to meet personalized requirements.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     A baseline project exists and the service is customizable.

     A project and a module have been created, and they are customizable.

    

   

   
    Context

    Assume that a developed app is provided for different projects. In different projects, most pages, logic, and functions of the app can be reused. Only some pages and logic need to be customized. In some cases, output parameters need to be converted while other content can be reused. In this scenario, you can customize a service.

    Services can be customized in either of the following ways:

    
     Override: Completely clear the existing service configuration, which is similar to creating a service to replace the original one.

     Extend: Customize the original service by adding parameters, validators, and translators to the original service.

    

    When configuring a service, you need to set whether the service can be customized. Only services whose Customizable is set to Yes can be customized.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Choose Project Management.

     Select the customized project and module you have created.

     Choose Service.

     Click  to create a service.
      

      

      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Name

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Creation Mode

          
           
            Common Service: Add a new service.

            Customized Service: Customize an existing service. If the current module is not a customized module, you cannot switch to the Customized Service tab page.

           

         

         
          
           CustomizationMode

          
           
            Override: Create a service to replace the original service, instead of customizing a service based on the original service.

            Extend: Customize the original service by adding parameters, validators, and translators to the original service.

           

         

         
          
           Service Name

          
           Name of the customization service to be created

         

         
          
           Customization Priority

          
           When an original service is customized for multiple times, the system sorts the customized services in descending order based on the value of this parameter and runs the one with the highest priority.

           When a service is customized in the same project, the customization priority must be unique.

         

         
          
           Baseline Service

          
           Service that needs to be customized and overwritten

         

         
          
           (Displayed when CustomizationMode is set to Override)

           Copy From Baseline

          
           In Override mode, developers can copy services from the baseline version and then modify and customize the copied services.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click OK.

     (Overwriting) In the scenario where a customized service is created in overwriting mode, configure the service based on service requirements. The configuration method is similar to that of creating a service. For details, see Configuring Services.

     (Extension) In the scenario where a customized service is created in extension mode, perform the following extension operations:
      

      
       Add parameters. Select a parent node and click Child Node to add a child node under the parent node. The child node is used to add specific fields to a specific project.

       Customize validators and translators for existing fields. Select the parameters for which you want to extend the validator or translator. In the Extended Information area on the right, click Add on the right of the validator or translator.
        
          
         
          For details about the validator, see Configuring the Element Validator. For details about the translator, see Configuring the Element Translator. Translators and validators of the script type cannot be configured for new fields.

         

        

        

        

      

      

     Click OK.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    The following describes the actual running effect after a service is customized and deployed in the runtime-state environment:

    Assume that service A' is customized based on service A which is in an app and is called through pages, the system determines that service A is customized during calling of service A and executes service A' if there is only one customized service A'.

    If there are multiple customized services, the one with the highest priority will be executed first.

name: Data Model Interworking
title: Data Model Interworking
text:
Data Model Interworking
 
 
  
  

  
   Data processing is classified into online transaction processing (OLTP) and online analytical processing (OLAP). OLTP is a main app of the traditional relational database. It is used for processing basic and routine transactions, such as bank transactions. OLAP is a main app in data warehouse system. It supports complex analysis, focuses on the decision-making support, and provides query results that are easy to understand.

   Currently, the app data in ADC belongs to the OLTP class while the data of the data services belongs to the OLAP class.

   Based on the data model interworking, OLTP models in ADC can be quickly converted to the OLAP models for data analysis, or OLAP data can be loaded to ADC for data display.

   
    Enabling Interworking Through the JDBC Driver

    The JDBC driver can be used to directly interwork the data in the ADC model with DataFactory, which optimizes the file-based data interworking mode.

    

   

   
    Enabling Interworking Through File Dumping and Loading

    ADC can be interworked with DataFactory through file dumping and loading.

    
     Figure 1 Data dumping
     
    

    In the data dumping mode, data is dumped from ADC and flows to DataFactory for loading.

    
     Figure 2 Data loading
     
    

    In the data loading mode, data is extracted from DataFactory and flows to ADC for loading.

    Data in data models, elastic models, and proxy models can be dumped and loaded.

   

   
    Querying Data Using Yacht

    Unidirectional query from ADC to DataFactory is implemented through service orchestration. This mode supports only data query and does not support data addition or modification.

Load General Work
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Description

    The Load General Work operator is used to load data to ADC models.

   

   
    Application Scenarios and Constraints

          fmtTime(#flow.startDataTime#,"yyyyMM00000000") when Data Granularity is set to Month

          fmtTime(#flow.startDataTime#,"yyyyMMdd000000") when Data Granularity is set to Day

The quotation marks are not displayed after the loading node loads data.

Extract General Work
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Description

    The Extract General Work operator is used to obtain data from ADC models.

   

   
    Application Scenarios and Constraints

    
     To extract data from an ADC model, use the Extract General Work operator.

     The operator can be used only in the integrated orchestration scenario.

     For data sources supported by this operator, see Relationship Between Operators and Data Sources.

    

   

   
    Parameter Description

    
     
      
       Table 1 Parameter description for Extract General Work
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Parameter

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Model Name

        
         Specifies the name of a model. Select the name of a model generated on the Model page of ADC from the drop-down list.

       

       
        
         Data Granularity

        
         Specifies the dump period configured in the task for dumping data from ADC to DataFactory, that is, the interval at which data is generated.

       

       
        
         Data Time Baseline

        
         Specifies the data time baseline.

         
          fmtTime(#flow.startDataTime#,"yyyyMM00000000") when Data Granularity is set to Month

          fmtTime(#flow.startDataTime#,"yyyyMMdd000000") when Data Granularity is set to Day

          fmtTime(#flow.startDataTime#,"yyyyMMddHH0000") when Data Granularity is set to Hour

         

       

       
        
         Data Range

        
         Specifies the time range of the data extraction.

         
          If the data start time is 20210425180000, the data range is [-1,1], and the data granularity is hour, the actual data extraction time is 2021-04-25 17:00:00, 2021-04-25 18:00:00, and 2021-04-25 19:00:00.

          If the data start time is 20210425000000, the data range is [-1,1], and the data granularity is day, the actual data extraction time is 2021-04-24 00:00:00, 2021-04-25 00:00:00, and 2021-04-26 00:00:00.

          If the data start time is 20210400000000, the data range is [-1,1], and the data granularity is month, the actual data extraction time is 2021-03-01 00:00:00, 2021-04-01 00:00:00, and 2021-05-01 00:00:00.

         

       

       
        
         Auto Match File Header

        
         Specifies whether the column name in the file header can be matched based on the entered name.

         
           NOTE: 
          
           For example, if the column names of the first row in the extraction file are aa|bb|cc, you can set the input name to bb, cc, and aa in the text extraction. The flow automatically matches the column names based on the input names and extracts data.

          

         

       

      
     
    

    
     
      
       Table 2 Parameters on the Columns tab page
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Parameter

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         Input Name

        
         Specifies an actual field name in the extracted file.

       

       
        
         Output Name

        
         Specifies the field name passed to the downstream operators.

       

       
        
         Output Flag

        
         Specifies whether to generate the field.

       

       
        
         Data Type

        
         Specifies the data type of the extracted field.

       

       
        
         Description

        
         Describes the extracted field.

       

       
        
         Format

        
         Specifies the date format of the extracted field. This parameter is configurable when Data Type is set to datetime.

       

       
        
         Min Value

        
         Specifies the minimum value of the extracted field. This parameter is configurable when Check is set to Modify or Discard.

       

       
        
         Max Value

        
         Specifies the maximum value of the extracted field. This parameter is configurable when Check is set to Modify or Discard.

       

       
        
         Default Value

         Is Null

        
         Specifies whether the extracted field can be null. This parameter is configurable when Check is set to Modify or Discard.

name: Introduction to the Model JDBC Driver
title: Introduction to the Model JDBC Driver
text:
Introduction to the Model JDBC Driver
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Usage Scenarios

    Orchestration models provide standards-based drivers for JDBC, enabling developers to access model data in scenarios such as integration of data orchestration.

   

   
    Authentication Mode

    The model driver uses the GAM machine-machine account for authentication. User name corresponds to the value of AccessId in the machine-machine account, and the password corresponds to the value of Secretkey in the machine-machine account.

   

   
    Supported Syntax

    Table 1 lists the syntax supported by the model driver.

    
     
     
      
       Table 1 Description of the model driver syntax
      
      
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Syntax Type

        
         Supported Capability

       

      
      
       
        
         DDL

        
         Not supported

       

       
        
         DCL

        
         Not supported

       

       
        
         DQL

        
         The supported syntax is basically the same as that of the model TQL. For details, see TQL Syntax Reference.

         Differences with TQL syntax in JDBC:

         
          JDBC query statements support specifying the general job model in the format of "App name.Model name".

          JDBC query statements support using question marks (?) as a placeholder for TQL parameters.

          The JDBC query statement does not restrict the value of limit. However, for the elastic model, if the value of limit exceeds 10000 or the value is not specified, the limitation can only start from 0. That is, offset cannot be specified.

         

       

       
        
         DML

        
         INSERT clause

        
         INSERT INTO [ schema_name. ]table_name (column_name [ , ... ]) VALUES (expression [ , ... ])

         
          schema_name: project name, which can be left empty.

          table_name: model name

          column_name: model property name

          expression: Only specific values such as character strings, digits, and Boolean values or placeholders such as question marks (?) are supported.

         

       

       
        
         UPDATE clause

        
         UPDATE [schema_name.]table_name SET {[column_name= expression] [ , ... ]} [ WHERE condition ]

         
          schema_name: project name, which can be left empty.

          table_name: model name

          column_name: model property name

          expression: Only specific values such as character strings, digits, and Boolean values or placeholders such as question marks (?) are supported.

          condition: expression that returns a result of the Boolean type. (The left value supports only id, keycode, and primary key. For the comparison operator, this value can only be equals. Only one data record can be operated at a time.)

         

       

       
        
         DELETE clause

        
         DELETE FROM [ schema_name. ]table_name [ WHERE condition ] [ LIMIT [ start, ] count ]

         
          schema_name: project name, which can be left empty.

          table_name: model name

          column_name: model property name

          condition: expression that returns a result of the Boolean type. (The left value supports only id, keycode, and primary key. For the comparison operator, this value can only be equals. Only one data record can be operated at a time.)

         

       

       
        
         Function

        
         The supported functions are the same as those of the TQL syntax.

       

      
     
    

    
      
     
      
       Data Definition Language (DDL) is used to define or change the structure, data type, links, and constraints of tables. It is usually used to create tables.

       Data Control Language (DCL) is a database control language used to set or change the permissions of database users or roles, including grant, deny, and revoke statements.

       Data Query Language (DQL) is used to query table records in a database.

       Data manipulation language (DML) uses INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE commands as the core to manipulate the running data of database objects.

      

     

    

   

   
    
    Connection Parameters

    Table 2 lists the available connection parameters of the driver.

    
     
     
      
       Table 2 Description of connection parameters
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Connection Parameter

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         user

        
         Database user, that is, the value of AccessId in the GAM machine-machine account

       

       
        
         password

        
         Database user password, that is, the value of Secretkey in the GAM machine-machine account

       

       
        
         trustServerCertificate

        
         Whether it is a trusted server certificate, that is, whether the server certificate verification can be skipped. The default value is false. If this parameter is set to false, trustStore and trustStorePassword must be set.

       

       
        
         trustStore

        
         Path of the truststore certificate file

       

       
        
         trustStorePassword

        
         Password of the truststore certificate file

       

       
        
         crl

        
         Path of the revoked certificate configuration file

       

       
        
         transportTimeout

        
         Client transmission timeout configuration, that is, the time when data can be read and transmitted by the ResultSet method of the client. The unit is millisecond. The default value is 300000.

text:
Configuring the Interworking Between DataFactory and Model JDBC Driver
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Obtaining the JDBC Driver Package of a Model

    
     To download the package from the runtime-state page, perform the following steps:
     
      Log in to the runtime-state environment as the admin user of a tenant.

      Choose Model Management > Model JDBC Driver Download.

      Click Download to obtain the JDBC driver package in ZIP format of the model.

      Decompress the ZIP package to obtain the JAR driver package.

     

    

   

   
    Uploading the Model JDBC Driver Package to BDI

    Upload the JDBC driver package by referring to Manually Uploading the Data Source Driver Package.

   

   
    Configuring Model Data Sources

    
     Configure a machine-machine account.
      

      
       In the runtime-state environment, choose Products and Services > Administration > Identity Authentication > Machine-Machine User Management.

       Click Create Machine-Machine User, and set Authentication Type to Basic.

       Click Submit. After the submission, the values of AccessId and Secretkey are displayed. The system displays them only once. Keep them secure.

      

      

     Authorize a machine-machine user.
      

      
        
       
        
         In the non-RSM scenario (only the admin administrator is preset), you do not need to switch to another user.

         In the RSM scenario (the admin, secadmin, and secauditor users are preset), the admin user does not have the permission to manage roles or bind IP addresses. You need to switch to the secadmin user and then perform operations.

        

       

      

      
       
        Click the created machine-machine user.

        Click the Machine-Machine User Authorization tab.

        Click Machine-Machine Role. In the displayed Machine-Machine Role dialog box, select adc-model-jdbc.

        Click Associate.

       

      

      

     Configure the model data sources.
      

      
       Log in to the GDE data zone portal as a user with the StudioDeveloper role.
        When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click Development State Studio. 

        When the portal is displayed in menu mode, choose Products and Services > Development State Studio on the home page.

       On the Project Management page, search for the name of the created project, and click the search result to access the details page of the data orchestration project.

       Choose Data Source > Data Source Configuration > Database and click Create.
        

        

        
         
          
           Table 1 Database parameters
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Name

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Database Type

            
             MySql

           

           
            
             Driver Name

            
             Select com.huawei.mateinfo.sdk.model.jdbc.client.ModelDriver from the drop-down list.

           

           
            
             JDBC Connection Description Character String

            
             Click  and set this parameter. The page automatically combines the entered IP address/domain name and port number based on the selected driver to form a complete address.

             
              Lightweight ETL scenario:
               
                IP address/Domain name: adc-model-ui.{App namespace}.svc.cluster.local. Log in to the management zone portal to obtain the app namespace, as shown in Figure 1. For example, if obtained namespace is kube-system, enter adc-model-ui.kube-system.svc.cluster.local after combination.
                 
                  Figure 1 Namespace
                  
                 

                Port: 18443

               

              Batch processing (FusionInsight) scenario: Set the IP address/domain name and port to the IP address and port of the DMZ LB node. In this case, ensure that the FusionInsight data plane can communicate with the DMZ LB node.

             

           

           
            
             Character Set

            
             UTF-8

           

           
            
             User Name

            
             Account of a machine-machine user

           

           
            
             Password

            
             Secret key of the machine-machine user

           

           
            
             Extended Information

            
             Access ID of the machine-machine user

             
              Name: Set it to AccessId.

              Value: Set it to the value of AccessId.

             

           

          
         
        

       Click Save.

       When the message "Data source created. An available driver exists. Do you want to associate the data source with the driver?" is displayed, click Yes and associate the JDBC driver.

      

      

    

   

   
    Configuring BDI JDBC Extraction Parameters

    Access a DataFactory project, choose Data Process on the left, choose Light ETL > Data Flow, create a data flow, select the Extract JDBC operator, and double-click this operator to configure extraction parameters. For details, see Extract JDBC under Data Orchestration.

    Note:

    
     The BDI MySQL data source does not support the database mode. Set Physical Model to a value in the format of "ADC app name.ADC model name".

     If there is a query on more than 10,000 data records at a time for the elastic model, the offset cannot be specified. The default threshold of data records in a BDI task shard is 2 million. If more than 2 million data records need to be extracted, the BDI shard parameter value needs to be adjusted so that the extraction task can be executed in one shard.

    

    

    

   

   
    Configuring BDI JDBC Loading Parameters

    Select the Load JDBC operator and double-click this operator to configure loading parameters. For details, see Load JDBC under Data Orchestration.

    Note:

    
     General job models do not support automatic table creation.

     Data loading mode cannot be set to Replace for general job models.

     The BDI MySQL data source does not support the database mode. Set Physical Model to a value in the format of "ADC app name.ADC model name".
      
        
       
        If an app name contains periods (.), use `` to enclose the app name, for example, `model.app.name`.table_name.

       

      

    

    

    

   

   
    Configuring the JDBC Transmission Timeout Interval of a Model

    The JDBC transmission timeout interval of the current model is restricted. If the transmission timeout interval exceeds the threshold, the connection is disconnected. In scenarios where BDI processes a large amount of data and takes a long time, the timeout interval needs to be adjusted separately.

    The default transmission timeout interval of the JBDC client is 5 minutes, and the maximum value is 1 hour. The default transmission timeout interval of the JDBC server is 32 minutes, and the maximum value is 62 minutes. The unit configured on the WebUI is millisecond. Generally, the transmission timeout interval of the server needs to be greater than that of the client.

    Client timeout interval configuration

    For details, see Connection Parameters.

    

    Server timeout interval configuration

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the operations administrator. Click the user account in the upper right corner, and choose Switch Tenant to switch to the master tenant.

     Choose Products and Services > ADC System Management > Component Management > System Parameter Configuration.

     Check whether the configuration item whose Category is model and Name is async-request-timeout exists. If the configuration item does not exist, create it. The unit of Value is millisecond and the value ranges from 60000 (1 minute) to 3720000 (62 minutes). Click OK.
      

      

      

      

     Restart the adc-model microservice.

name: Configuring the Yacht Data Query Node

text:
Configuring the Yacht Data Query Node
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Context

    The application scenario of DataService Query under Platform Services is different from that of Get, GetList, and TQLQuery under Model Operations.

    

    

    
      
     
      This node is not displayed by default. To display this node, set integration_yacht to true at the master level.

     

    

    This node is used for data exchanges between ADC and Data Cube. The following query modes are supported:

    
     TQL mode: Data can be queried using TQL syntax or TQL scripts. For details about the syntax and examples, see TQL Syntax Reference.
      An example is as follows.

      select * from #table where name = $name and age > $age limit #start,#limit order by #orders #asc_desc

     Yacht SQL mode: The SQL editor for Yacht service is provided to edit SQL statements for accessing Data Cube data through Yacht, implementing flexible development of data access functions. For details about the SQL syntax supported by Yacht, see SQL Syntax of the Yacht Service.
      Before configuring this item, you are advised to prepare a runtime-state environment where Yacht has been installed and understand the data source to be queried under Products and Services > Data Cube > Data Opening > SQL Editor.

      

      

      An example of Yacht SQL statements is as follows:

      yacht_sql: select * from #table where name = ? and age > ? order by #orders #asc_desc limit #start,#limit

    

    Take the preceding statement as an example. You need to set the input parameters listed in the following table in the service.

    
     
     
      
       Table 1 Input parameters for DataService Query
      
      
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Parameter

        
         Description

       

      
      
       
        
         table

        
         Table name. If the table name has been specified in the SQL statement, for example, select * from cfg.BAT_IMP_RELATION_D, you do not need to set the table name again.

         If no table name is specified in the SQL statement, you need to transfer the table name using a parameter. For example, if select * from #table is used, you need to transfer the specified table name using a parameter.

       

       
        
         start

        
         Start row number of the query

       

       
        
         limit

        
         Number of query records

       

       
        
         orders

        
         Field to be sorted. Multiple fields are supported. Use commas (,) to separate them.

       

       
        
         asc_desc

        
         Sorting mode of the field to be sorted. The options are true (ascending order) and false (descending order).

       

       
        
         yacht_database

        
         Yacht data source for the specified query. By default, if this parameter is not transferred, the query data source is physical-MetaOne. That is, you do not need to specify this parameter when querying physical-MetaOne.

         To query other data sources, such as data in physical-MONITOR_PT, transfer this parameter and specify the data source.

       

       
        
         Other parameters

        
         Parameter used as the query input, for example, a field in a data table

       

      
     
    

    The following uses the Yacht SQL mode as an example to describe how to configure the DataService Query service.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Create a service using a blank template.

     Configure service input parameters.
      

      
       Click the blank area in the canvas and click  on the right to expand the service property configuration window.

       Select the text box on the left of Input and click Subnode to add parameters to the root node. For details about the parameters, see Table 1.

       Click OK to save the settings.

      

      

     Configure the DataService Query node.
      

      
       Drag DataService Query from the left pane.

       Select the DataService Query node and click  in property box on the right.

       In the displayed dialog box, set basic information.
        

        

       In the Query Condition area, compile SQL statements.
        

        

       Click OK to save the node property configuration.

      

      

     Click  to save the service configuration.

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    The debugging of the Yacht DataService Query depends on the deployment of the Yacht service in the runtime-state environment. Otherwise, the debugging cannot be performed.

    
     After the configuration is complete, click , select APP, package as an app, and download the app package.

     In the runtime-state environment where the Yacht service is deployed, switch to the master tenant, choose Products and Services > ADC System Management > Component Management > System Parameter Configuration, and configure the Yacht parameter.
      

      
       
        
         Table 2 Yacht parameter
        
        
         
         
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Category

          
           Parameter Name

          
           Default Value

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           adc-service

          
           integration_yacht_db_address

          
           None

          
           Yacht SQL execution link address

           
            If a unique link address is used globally, set this parameter to the link address.

            If different link addresses need to be defined for multiple tenants, specify the tenant address and default address in the format {"Tenant ID":"Link address 1","default":"Link address 2"}.
             Example: {"2000":"BBB","default":"CCC"}

           

         

        
       
      

      

     Switch to the service tenant, choose Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager, and deploy the installation package.

     In the runtime-state environment, call the configured service for debugging and verification.

text:
Tenant Asset Management
 
 
  
  

  
   This document describes how users under a tenant manage assets in the ADC develop-state environment.

  

  
   
    Viewing Asset Details
      On the Asset Management page, you can view the asset information such as apps, APIs, and templates.

    Managing Labels
      The following labels are available on the Asset Management page: Service Domain, Asset Type/Asset Catalog, and Technology Category.

    Subscribing to an Asset
      GDE Store is used to put away and share assets. Developers can download required assets from GDE Store and share their apps within GDE Store.

    Uploading Assets to the Asset Management Page
      Developers can use the asset upload function to upload personal assets to the Asset Management page. The personal assets are displayed on the Local Assets page.

    Putting Away Assets to the Asset Management Page
      Developers can put away assets through a pipeline or using the asset management page.

    Deploying Assets to the Customer Asset Library
      This section describes the parameters to be configured and operations to be performed by developers to deploy assets to the customer asset library.

    Approving an Asset
      This section describes the permissions required for developers to approve tickets on the asset management page and the ticket approval process.

    Viewing the Vulnerability Information
      In the scenario where an asset service is interworked with GDE Store, you can view the vulnerability information of the asset. Asset vulnerability information provided by GDE Store is displayed on the Asset Management page.

    Viewing the Asset Dependency Analysis
      The information tree service enables developers to view the list of projects and apps synchronized from the local asset library or the Project Management page. It also allows them to parse elements in the project, and view the project element structure and project dependencies.

    Viewing Asset Difference Comparison Results
      When multiple developers develop an app at the same time, the asset library provides a tool for comparing app differences.

   

   
    
     Parent topic: Release and Verification

Viewing Asset Details
 
 
  
  

  
   On the Asset Management page, you can view the asset information such as apps, APIs, and templates.

   The login user has the permission to view the following assets:

   
    Personal assets

    Assets of the user's team

    Assets shared by other users or teams

    API assets scanned during system initialization

   

   
    Context

    Asset sources are as follows:

    Local assets

    
     Assets uploaded on the Asset Management page. These assets are displayed on the Local Assets tab page. For details, see Uploading Assets to the Asset Management Page.

     Packaged apps, project files, templates, and service components, and saved card assets. These assets are displayed on the Local Assets tab page.

    

    Putaway assets

    
     Assets pulled from GDE Store. For details, see Subscribing to an Asset.

     Assets that are put away through the pipeline, studio, and asset management. These assets are displayed on the Putaway Assets tab page. For details, see Putting Away Assets to the Asset Management Page.

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.
      

      
       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click Development State Studio. 

       When the portal is displayed in menu mode, choose Products and Services > Development State Studio.

      

      

     On the menu bar of the home page, choose Asset Management > Asset Library.

Managing Labels
 
 
  
  

  
   The following labels are available on the Asset Management page: Service Domain, Asset Type/Asset Catalog, and Technology Category.

   
    Context

    
     
      
       
       
       
       
      
      
       
        
         Label

        
         Customizable

        
         Description

        
         Applicable Scenario

       

      
      
       
        
         Service Domain

        
         Some labels can be customized.

        
         Labels in the Custom directory can be customized. These labels are used to categorize customized domains for tenant asset management.

        
         When you put away assets from the ADC pipeline to the asset management module, select labels from the Custom directory when you configure Domain.

       

       
        
         Asset Type/Asset Catalog

        
         
          Types of assets that have been put away cannot be customized.

          Catalogs of local assets can be customized.

         

        
         
          Labels of putaway assets: Asset type labels obtained from GDE Store are synchronized to the Asset Type directory.

          Customizable labels in local assets: Labels in the Custom directory are customized categories of domains in tenant asset management and can be customized by users.

         

        
         
          When packaging assets in the ADC develop-state environment, you can select the corresponding asset catalog. After the assets are packaged, the assets of the specified type are displayed on the Asset Management page.

          When you put away assets from the ADC pipeline to the asset management module, you can select labels from the Putaway Assets directory when configuring Asset Type.

         

       

       
        
         Technology Category

        
         A category cannot be customized but can be associated with an asset catalog.

        
         You can associate a label with a specific technology category in the Asset Catalog area.

        
         An asset catalog can be associated with different technical categories. For example, if an asset catalog is associated only with a project package, this asset catalog can be selected only when the project package is packaged.

       

       
        
         Customized Label

        
         Customized category.

        
         
          Customized label added during project creation.

          Asset label added by a developer during asset putaway.

         

        
         An asset category can be defined by users.

       

      
     
    

   

  

  
   
    Managing Service Domain Labels
      Based on service domains, rights- and domain-based isolation can be implemented for putaway assets in the customer asset library. The service domain labels of local assets are customized.

    Managing Asset Catalog Labels
      When the asset type label of assets that have been put away are synchronized from GDE Store, only the asset catalog label of local assets can be customized by users.The asset catalog label can be customized by users.

    Associating Technical Category Label
      Technical category labels cannot be customized and can be associated with asset catalog labels of local assets.

    Selecting Assets by Category Label
      When viewing assets on the Asset Management page, you can select a label to filter assets of the target category.
