text:
Managing Service Domain Labels
 
 
  
  

  
   Based on service domains, rights- and domain-based isolation can be implemented for putaway assets in the customer asset library. The service domain labels of local assets are customized.

   
    Prerequisites

    Log in to the GDE data zone portal as a system administrator.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.
      

      
       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click Development State Studio. 

       When the portal is displayed in menu mode, choose Products and Services > Development State Studio.

      

      

     On the menu bar of the home page, choose Asset Management > Asset Library.

     Manage the service domain labels of putaway assets.
      

      
       Click the Putaway Assets tab.

       Click  under Service Domain. The Business Domain Management page is displayed.

       Add a service domain label for a putaway asset. For details about the parameters, see Table 1.
        
         Click  on the right of a service domain to add a same-level service domain.

         Click  on the right of a service domain to add a service domain at the lower level.

        

        
         
         
          
           Table 1 Description of service domain properties
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Domain ID

            
             Customized service domain name, which is mandatory.

           

           
            
             Domain Internationalization

            
             Internationalization configuration item of the customized service domain name, which is mandatory. Click Add Language. Both Chinese and English must be configured.

           

          
         
        

        
         Figure 1 Adding a service domain for a putaway asset
         

        

       Click Save.

      

      

     Manage service domain labels of local assets.
      

      
       Click the Local Assets tab.

       Click  on the right of a customized directory under Service Domain. The Edit Service Domain page is displayed.

       Add a service domain label for a local asset. For details about the parameters, see Table 2.
        
         Click  on the right of a service domain to add a same-level service domain.

         Click  on the right of a service domain to add a service domain at the lower level.

        

        
         
         
          
           Table 2 Description of service domain properties
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Parameter

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             Domain ID

            
             Customized service domain name, which is mandatory.

           

           
            
             Domain Internationalization

            
             Internationalization configuration item of the customized service domain name, which is mandatory. Click Add. Both Chinese and English must be configured.

           

          
         
        

        
         Figure 2 Adding a service domain for a local asset
         

        

       Click Save.

      

      

    

   

   
    Follow-up Procedure

    
     Modifying service domain labels
      
       Modify the service domain labels of putaway assets.
        Click  on the right of a domain property and modify service domain parameters for a putaway asset.

       Modify service domain labels of local assets.
        For the service domain parameters of a local asset, only the Domain Internationalization parameter can be modified. The Domain ID parameter cannot be modified. Click Edit in the Operation column of the Domain Internationalization parameter to modify it.

      

     Deleting service domain labels
      Click  on the right of the service domain to be deleted to delete it.

      
        
       
        If the service domain to be deleted contains sub-domains, these sub-domains will also be deleted once the service domain is deleted.

       

      

     Adjusting the sequence of service domains
      
       Adjust the service domain sequence of putaway assets.
        Click  on the right of a required service domain to adjust the sequence.

       Adjusting the service domain sequence of local assets
        Select a required service domain, and hold down the left mouse button and drag it to a proper position.

      

     Adding a domain administrator
      
        
       
        When adding a service domain for local assets, you do not need to configure the domain administrator.

       

      

      In the Domain Administrator area, select the user name to be added from the drop-down list and click Add. Alternatively, you can click  and search for the user to be added in the displayed Select User dialog box.

name: Subscribing to an Asset
title: Subscribing to an Asset
text:
Subscribing to an Asset
 
 
  
  

  
   GDE Store is used to put away and share assets. Developers can download required assets from GDE Store and share their apps within GDE Store.

   After ADC is interworked with GDE Store, you can obtain assets from remote or local GDE Store for asset management.

   

   
     
    
     Before subscribing to an asset, you need to be bound with the domain administrator permission of the service domain to which the asset belongs. For details, see Managing Service Domain Labels.

    

   

  

  
   
    Subscribing to Assets from the Remote GDE Store
      The Asset Management page allows you to subscribe to assets from a remote GDE Store.

    Subscribing to Assets from the Local GDE Store
      The Asset Management page allows you to subscribe to assets from the local GDE Store.

   

   
    
     Parent topic: Tenant Asset Management

name: Subscribing to Assets from the Remote GDE Store
title: Subscribing to Assets from the Remote GDE Store
text:
Subscribing to Assets from the Remote GDE Store
 
 
  
  

  
   The Asset Management page allows you to subscribe to assets from a remote GDE Store.

   
    Prerequisites

    The user has been granted the permission to access the remote GDE Store. For details about the configurations, see Data Zone Configuration > Data Zone Configuration (default Tenant) > Application Asset Management > GDE Store Configuration > Remote Access to GDE Store in GDE x.x.x Product Documentation.

    You have the domain administrator permission of the service domain to access the assets that have been put away.

    You have the administrator permission of the service domain that the assets to be subscribed belong to.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.
      

      
       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click Development State Studio. 

       When the portal is displayed in menu mode, choose Products and Services > Development State Studio on the home page.

      

      

     On the menu bar of the home page, choose Asset Management > Asset Library.

     Click the Putaway Assets tab.

     Click Subscribe from GDE Store in the upper right corner of the page.

     Click the desired asset.
      

      

      

      

     On the displayed asset details page, click Obtain.
      

      

      

      

     Go back to the Asset Management page, and view the obtained asset.
      

      Assets are displayed in the Putaway Assets and Local Assets tab pages.

      
        
       
        
         A domain administrator can subscribe to assets only in the service domain that the domain administrator belongs to.
          For example, if the operator is the domain administrator of the Inspection service domain, the service domain to which the asset test0606 belongs is Inspection.

         If a domain administrator is associated with multiple service domains and the service domain of a subscribed asset is A, you cannot switch the service domain when subscribing to the same asset of a later version.
          For example, the version of the subscribed asset test0606 is 0.0.1, and the service domain is xxx. When you need to subscribe to asset test0606 whose version is 0.0.2, you cannot switch the service domain of the asset of that version.

        

       

      

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Subscribing to an Asset

name: Subscribing to Assets from the Local GDE Store
title: Subscribing to Assets from the Local GDE Store
text:
Subscribing to Assets from the Local GDE Store
 
 
  
  

  
   The Asset Management page allows you to subscribe to assets from the local GDE Store.

   
    Prerequisites

    The user has been granted the permission to access the local GDE Store. For details about the configurations, see Data Zone Configuration > Data Zone Configuration (default Tenant) > Application Asset Management > GDE Store Configuration > Local Access to GDE Store in GDE x.x.x Product Documentation.

    You have the administrator permission of the service domain that the assets to be subscribed belong to.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.
      

      
       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click Development State Studio. 

       When the portal is displayed in menu mode, choose Products and Services > Development State Studio on the home page.

      

      

     On the menu bar of the home page, choose Asset Management > Asset Library.

     Click the Local Assets tab.

     Click Subscribe from GDE Store in the upper right corner of the page to access the local GDE Store of ADC.
      

      
        
       
        
         If you subscribe to an asset on the GDE Store asset subscription page from the Local Assets page, the asset is displayed only on the Local Assets page.

         If you click View More in the Latest Recommendations or Popular Templates area on the home page of the develop-state environment, the asset is displayed only on the Local Assets page.

        

       

      

      

     Click the card of the asset to be subscribed.

     On the asset details page, click Subscribe.
      

      

      

     Enter the asset subscription information. The following table describes the parameters.
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameter configuration description
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Asset Name

          
           Name of the asset to be subscribed to.

         

         
          
           Version Number

          
           Asset version.

         

         
          
           Dev. Team

          
           Developer team that an asset belongs to.

         

         
          
           Service Domain

          
           Service domain that an asset belongs to.

         

         
          
           Location

          
           Country where the asset is used.

         

         
          
           Region

          
           Region where the asset is used.

         

         
          
           Whether to Install

          
           
             NOTE: 
            
             Select this option only when asset type is set to APP.

            

           

           
            Yes: Push the asset to AppManager and install it.

            No: Push the asset to AppManager but do not install it.

           

         

         
          
           Application Reason

          
           User-defined reason for applying for asset subscription. This parameter is mandatory.

           The value contains 5 to 250 characters and can contain the following special characters: -_, .:{}.

         

        
       
      

      

     Click OK.
      

      After the process is approved, the asset is displayed on the Local Assets page under Asset Management.

name: Uploading Assets to the Asset Management Page
title: Uploading Assets to the Asset Management Page
text:
Uploading Assets to the Asset Management Page
 
 
  
  

  
   Developers can use the asset upload function to upload personal assets to the Asset Management page. The personal assets are displayed on the Local Assets page.

   
    Prerequisites

    The assets to be uploaded are available.

   

   
    Context

    You can click Upload Asset to upload assets for tenant asset management. When the latest version of an asset is uploaded, the old version is overwritten. For example, when the version 1.0.1 is uploaded to the system where the version 1.0.0 exists, the version 1.0.0 will be deleted.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.
      

      
       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click Development State Studio. 

       When the portal is displayed in menu mode, choose Products and Services > Development State Studio on the home page.

      

      

     On the menu bar of the home page, choose Asset Management > Asset Library.

     Click the Local Assets tab.

     (Optional) For API assets, click Download API Template in the upper right corner to configure the template based on rules.

     Click Upload Asset in the upper right corner.

     In the displayed dialog box, enter the information about the asset to be uploaded.
      

      
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters for uploading assets
        
        
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Upload File

          
           Asset files in .gdk, .gpk, .zip, or .yaml format can be uploaded.

           
             NOTE: 
            
             
              The size of an NAIE-S asset package cannot exceed 3 GB and that of a non-NAIE-S asset package cannot exceed 200 MB. This principle applies to all of the preceding asset package types.

              For API assets, upload the configured API template.

              Only one file can be uploaded. If multiple .gdk or .gpk files need to be uploaded, compress them into a ZIP file and upload the file.

              Only one .yaml file less than 1 MB can be uploaded. After the upload is successful, the domain service directory and name in the file are displayed. For the domain service imported through files, the first-level directory is Custom, and only the Custom directory and its subdirectories are displayed in the tree.

             

            

           

         

         
          
           Developer Type

          
           Ownership permission of an asset.

           
            Personal: The uploaded asset belongs to the developer.

            Team: You need to select the team to which the asset belongs.

            Public: All users can view the asset.

           

         

         
          
           Share Asset

           
             NOTE: 
            
             This parameter is displayed when Developer Type is set to Personal or Team.

            

           

          
           Whether an asset is public.

           
            When this parameter is enabled:
             
              When Developer Type is set to Personal, the asset is only visible to the individual.

              When Developer Type is set to Team, the asset is only visible to the members of the team.

             

            When this parameter is disabled:
             
              Developer Type is set to Personal, the asset is only visible to the individual developer.

              If Developer Type is set to Team, the asset is visible only to members of the team to which the developer belongs.

             

           

         

        
       
      

      

     Click OK to view the information summary.
      

      

      

     Click OK.
      

      On the Local Assets page, view the uploaded assets.

name: Putting Away Assets Through the Pipeline
title: Putting Away Assets Through the Pipeline
text:
Putting Away Assets Through the Pipeline
 
 
  
  

  
   Package the projects that are edited online and put away them to the Asset Management page.

   
    Prerequisites

    On the Products and Services > Administration > Pipeline Configuration page, you have set Pipeline Submission Mode to Put Away.

   

   
    Context

    After projects are packaged and put away on the Asset Management page of ADC, users under a tenant share the assets on the Asset Management page.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Access the created project and choose CI/CD Tool Chain > Pipeline from the lower left corner.
      

      
       Figure 1 Accessing the Pipeline page from the CI/CD Tool Chain menu
       

      

      

     Package app assets. (Putting away an app asset is used as an example.)
      

      
       On the App Pipeline tab page, click Deliver.
        If you need to package project files, templates, and service component assets, switch to the corresponding pipeline tab page and click Deliver.

        

       In the displayed dialog box, select the environment where the app is to be deployed, enter the user name and password of the current GDE data zone, and click OK.
        
         Figure 2 Setting the login information
         

        

       Package a project into an app. For details, see Packaging a Project into an App.
        

       Click Pack to start the pipeline. Go to the pipeline building page and wait until the pipeline building is complete.
        

      

      

     On the pipeline building page, click Put away in asset library to go to the putaway page. Set putaway parameters as prompted. For details about the parameters and page display, see Putaway Page.
      

      
        
       
        When assets with the same name, same technology category, and different versions are put away, the service domain of the new asset must be the same as that of the old asset and cannot be modified. For example, if the old app asset test whose version is 1.0 has been put away, when the new app asset test whose version is 2.0 is put away, the service domain must be the same as that of the old app asset and cannot be modified.

       

      

      

     (Optional) After setting the parameters, click Preview to preview the settings.

     Click OK to go to the putaway process.

     After the putaway configuration is complete, the asset is in Putaway approving state and displayed under Local Assets on the Asset Management page. The asset can be put away only after the administrator approves it on the Asset Management > Asset Approval > Release Ticket Mgmt page.
      

      After the approval is complete, the asset is displayed under Putaway Assets on the Asset Management page. For details about how to approve an asset, see Approving an Asset Putaway Ticket.

name: Deploying Assets to the Customer Asset Library
title: Deploying Assets to the Customer Asset Library
text:
Deploying Assets to the Customer Asset Library
 
 
  
  

  
   This section describes the parameters to be configured and operations to be performed by developers to deploy assets to the customer asset library.

  

  
   
    Configuring the Production Environment
      Before asset deployment, you need to create a production environment and configure it.

    Deploying an Asset
      Streamline the one-click distribution capability of assets that have been put away in the customer asset library from the customer asset library to the runtime-state environment.

   

   
    
     Parent topic: Tenant Asset Management

name: Configuring the Production Environment
title: Configuring the Production Environment
text:
Configuring the Production Environment
 
 
  
  

  
   Before asset deployment, you need to create a production environment and configure it.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     To create a production environment, you need to have permissions of one of the following roles:
      
       System administrators in Develop State role

       AssetOperationsAdmin role that has been bound to a user you have created. For details about how to bind the role to the created user, see Associating Users with Roles.

       Approval administrator role that is created by users and has the permission to approve asset putaway and removal

      

    

   

   
    The maximum number of distribution environments is 50.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Create a machine-machine user and associate the user with a role.
      

      
       Create a machine-machine user. For details, see Creating a Machine-Machine User.

       Click the created machine-machine user, choose Machine-Machine User Authorization > Associate Machine-Machine Role, select the machine-machine role mr_appmanager_visitor, and click Associate.
        

      

      

     Create a production environment.
      

      
       Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.
        
         When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click Development State Studio. 

         When the portal is displayed in menu mode, choose Products and Services > Development State Studio.

        

       On the menu bar of the home page, choose Asset Management > Asset Production Environment.

       Click Add Production Environment and enter the environment information based on site requirements.
        
          
         
          The environment address is in the format of "IP address:Port". Enter the IP address, port, AK, and SK for accessing the environment when creating a machine-machine user created on 1.

         

        

        

       Click OK.

      

      

     Add configuration to LB in the develop-state environment.
      

      
       Log in to each node of LB as the sshusr user, and run the following command to switch to the root user.
        su - root

       Run the following command to check the LB container ID:
        docker ps | grep lb

       Run the following command to access the LB container:
        docker exec -it ${LB container ID} bash

       Run the following command to go to the Nginx configuration file directory:
        cd /usr/local/NSP/etc/nginx/vhosts/

       Add the configuration file route_asset_XXX.config.
        Run the vi route_asset_XXX.config command to generate a configuration file and write environment information into the configuration file. The following is an example:

        
          
         
          Replace XXX with the environment name.

          The distribution environment address is in the format of IP address:Port or Domain name. Enter the access address of the environment to be interconnected, that is, the URL entered when the environment is added. Enter the environment name (name in English is recommended) defined when the environment is added. The environment name in the configuration file must be the same as that in the actual environment.

         

        

        location /Environment name/gam/v1/auth/tokens {
    rewrite /Environment name/(.*) /$1 break;
    proxy_pass https://IP address of the distribution environment;
}
location /Environment name/apm/plat/v2/packages {
    rewrite /Environment name/(.*) /$1 break;
    proxy_pass https://IP address of the distribution environment;
}

       Press Esc to exit the editing mode, and enter :wq! to save the configuration.

       Run the following command to make the configuration take effect:
        /usr/local/NSP/sbin/nginx -s reload

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Deploying Assets to the Customer Asset Library

name: Deploying an Asset
title: Deploying an Asset
text:
Deploying an Asset
 
 
  
  

  
   Streamline the one-click distribution capability of assets that have been put away in the customer asset library from the customer asset library to the runtime-state environment.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     The production environment has been created and configured, and the network between the asset library production environment and the customer asset library environment is connected.

     Type Of Technology of the asset to be deployed is App.

     To deploy assets that have been put away, the following requirements must be met:
      
       You have the administrator permission of the service domain to which the assets to be deployed belong.

       The system administrator of the develop-state environment has been bound to the permissions of the O&M administrator role AssetMaintenanceAdmin.

      

     The following requirements must be met when local assets are deployed:
      The system administrator of the develop-state environment has been bound to the permissions of the O&M administrator role AssetMaintenanceAdmin.

     Select the environment to be deployed and enter the application reason.
      

      

      

      

     Click OK.

     (Optional) If the asset EOS check function is enabled (that is, eos_check_enable in the unified_orchestration category is set to true) and the asset is about to reach its EOS date or has reached its EOS date, click OK in the displayed Asset Expiration Reminder dialog box.

    Approving an Asset Putaway Ticket
      The tenant asset management system allows you to quickly release verified assets and use asset release application, approval, and control processes.

    Approving an Asset Deployment Ticket
      The tenant asset management system allows you to allocate asset deployment tickets to different reviewers.

name: Approving an Asset Subscription Ticket
title: Approving an Asset Subscription Ticket
text:
Approving an Asset Subscription Ticket
 
 
  
  

  
   The tenant asset management system allows you to subscribe to assets from GDE Store in both remote and local modes. You can query the assets, which are subscribed from the local GDE Store, in the local App Store of GDE Store or on the Asset Management page.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have the administrator permission of the service domain to which the assets belong. (The tickets of these assets are to be approved.)

     To approve asset subscription tickets, you need to have permissions of one of the following roles:
      
       System administrators in Develop State role

       AssetOperationsAdmin role that has been bound to a user you have created. For details about how to bind the role to the created user, see Associating Users with Roles.

       Approval administrator role that is created by users and has the permission to approve asset subscription tickets

      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     On the Asset Management page, view tickets.
      

      
       Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.
        
         When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click Development State Studio. 

         When the portal is displayed in menu mode, choose Products and Services > Development State Studio on the home page.

        

       On the menu bar of the home page, choose Asset Management > Asset Approval.

       In the navigation pane, choose Subscription Ticket Mgmt.

       Click the ticket number to go to the ticket details page. The current approval status is Pass.
        

        

      

      

     View the asset subscription ticket in local GDE Store.
      

      
       Click an asset card. On the App Info page, click View Order.
        

       Access the asset subscription ticket details page to view the approval status and the current approver.
        
          
         
          Subscription tickets are stored only for two years. If there are 50,000 tickets, the system automatically deletes them even if they are stored for less than two years. The originally stored tickets and the tickets in the Approved or Rejected status are cleared first.

         

        

      

      

     View the ticket approval result.
      

      
       When the approval status is Approved, check the task status of the ticket. 
        
         
          
           Table 1 Ticket task status and scenario description
          
          
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Task Status

            
             Scenario

           

          
          
           
            
             Successful

            
             Indicates that the asset is automatically downloaded from GDE Store to the tenant asset management module and pushed to GDE AppManager. The asset can be automatically installed on GDE AppManager.

           

           
            
             Failed

            
             Failed to automatically download assets from App Store of GDE Store to the tenant asset management module.

           

           
            
             Failed to push approved assets to GDE AppManager.

           

           
            
             Failed to automatically install the asset on GDE AppManager.

           

          
         
        

      

      
       If the approval status is Rejected, the app is rejected on the approval page of GDE Store. If you need to subscribe to the asset, submit a subscription ticket again.

       If the approval status is Canceled, the ticket has been manually canceled on the My Orders page of GDE Store. After the ticket is canceled, you can submit it again.

      

      

     In the local App Store of GDE Store, click an asset whose ticket task has been successfully executed, and click View Order to go to the asset that has been downloaded to the tenant asset management module.
      

      

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Approving an Asset

name: Approving an Asset Putaway Ticket
title: Approving an Asset Putaway Ticket
text:
Approving an Asset Putaway Ticket
 
 
  
  

  
   The tenant asset management system allows you to quickly release verified assets and use asset release application, approval, and control processes.

   
    Context

    After the developer completes asset development and testing, the asset release process and channel are provided to put away assets from the develop-state environment to the developer asset library.

   

   
    Prerequisites

    
     You have the administrator permission of the service domain to which the assets belong. (The tickets of these assets are to be approved.)

     To approve asset putaway and removal tickets, you need to have permissions of one of the following roles:
      
       System administrators in Develop State role

       AssetOperationsAdmin role that has been bound to a user you have created. For details about how to bind the role to the created user, see Associating Users with Roles.

       Approval administrator role that is created by users and has the permission to approve asset putaway tickets

      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.
      

      
       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click Development State Studio. 

       When the portal is displayed in menu mode, choose Products and Services > Development State Studio on the home page.

      

      

     Approve the asset putaway ticket.
      

      
       On the menu bar of the home page, choose Asset Management > Asset Approval.

       In the navigation pane, choose Release Ticket Mgmt.
        
          
         
          A domain administrator can view all tickets in the relevant domain, and tickets submitted by the domain administrator.

          Common users can view only the tickets submitted by themselves.

         

        

       Click the number of the ticket to be approved. The Release Ticket Mgmt page is displayed.
        
         Click Approve in the upper right corner, enter the approval comments, and click OK. The asset in the ticket is successfully put away.

        

        
         Click Reject in the upper right corner, enter the approval comments, and click OK. The asset putaway application in the ticket is rejected.

        

      

      

     Remove an asset.
      

      
       On the menu bar of the home page, choose Asset Management > Asset Library.

       Click the Putaway Assets tab.

       Click the asset to be removed. The asset details page is displayed.

       Click Remove. When an asset is removed, an approved asset removal ticket is automatically generated.
        

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Approving an Asset

name: Approving an Asset Deployment Ticket
title: Approving an Asset Deployment Ticket
text:
Approving an Asset Deployment Ticket
 
 
  
  

  
   The tenant asset management system allows you to allocate asset deployment tickets to different reviewers.

   
    Prerequisites

    
     The system administrator of the develop-state environment has been bound to the permissions of the O&M administrator role AssetMaintenanceAdmin.

     The asset deployment ticket viewing permission is described as follows:
      
       Historical tickets that are upgraded to the latest version and have no service domain can be viewed by all users.

       Asset deployment tickets whose source is Tenant asset service do not have service domains and can be viewed by all users.

       Asset deployment tickets whose source is Customer asset library and that have service domains can be viewed by the domain administrator and develop-state system administrator.

      

    

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.
      

      
       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click Development State Studio. 

       When the portal is displayed in menu mode, choose Products and Services > Development State Studio on the home page.

      

      

     On the menu bar of the home page, choose Asset Management > Asset Approval.

     In the navigation pane, choose Deployment Ticket Mgmt.

     In the ticket list, click the number of the ticket to be approved to view the ticket details.

     Enter the approval comment and approve the ticket.
      

      
        
       
        The domain administrator can view all deployment applications in the service domain but cannot approve them.

       

      

      

     View the ticket approval result.
      

      
       On the ticket details page, view the task information and execution status of the ticket. After the ticket is approved, the corresponding asset is automatically deployed.

       The task status is not associated with the approval status. If a single task fails to be deployed, the task can be retried.
        For example, if the deployment application is approved but Task Status is Failed, the task can be retried.

       After the asset is successfully deployed, view the deployment state of the target app on the App List page of the GDE App Manager page.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Approving an Asset

name: Viewing the Asset Dependency Analysis
title: Viewing the Asset Dependency Analysis
text:
Viewing the Asset Dependency Analysis
 
 
  
  

  
   The information tree service enables developers to view the list of projects and apps synchronized from the local asset library or the Project Management page. It also allows them to parse elements in the project, and view the project element structure and project dependencies.

   
    Context

    After interworking with the information tree service, the asset services provide the project list information, which is displayed on the Asset Management > Asset Dependency Analysis page.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.
      

      
       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click Development State Studio. 

       When the portal is displayed in menu mode, choose Products and Services > Development State Studio.

      

      

     On the menu bar of the home page, choose Asset Management > Asset Dependency Analysis.

     View the project list.
      

      
       In the project list, projects and apps can be synchronized from the local asset library or the Project Management page.

       Data in the project list can be displayed on multiple pages. By default, 20 records are displayed. The number of records displayed on each page can be 10, 20, 50, or 100.

       Move the pointer over the project name to view the project information, including Project Name, Version, Type, and Source.

       In the search box below the project list, enter a project name and click . All projects that meet the search criteria are displayed.
        
          
         
          Fuzzy search is supported. A maximum of 64 characters can be entered. By default, the search box is left blank, indicating that all projects are displayed.

         

        

      

      
       Figure 1 Viewing the project list
       
      

      

     Parse the project.
      

      
       Click a project whose indicator is gray in the project list to trigger project parsing.

       For a project that has been successfully parsed, click Reparse on the right of the page to trigger project parsing again.
        
          
         
          
           You can parse up to 10 projects at once. If more than 10 projects are being parsed, the message "The number of running tasks exceeds the maximum number." is displayed.

           Project and app packages with a maximum size of 200 MB can be parsed.

          

         

        

      

      

     View the parsing result of the project.
      

      
       Select a project that has been successfully parsed in the project list and view the project element structure on the Element Structure tab page on the right.
        
         Figure 2 Viewing the element structure
         
        

       Click  or  next to a module, or click Expand/Collapse All to collapse or expand subnodes.

       Move the pointer over an element. The current element and its upstream elements are highlighted, and the element details card is displayed. Elements can be zoomed in or out by scrolling the mouse wheel.

       Click View All in the upper right corner of the page to view the project element list.
        
         Figure 3 Viewing all elements
         
        

       On the Element List page, select a module or element type, enter an element name, and click  to filter the desired element.

       On the Element List page, click View Element Reference Relationships in the Operation column

       On the Element Reference Diagram page, click the icon in front of an element to view its upstream and reference elements.
        
         Figure 4 Viewing elements involved in an element reference relationship
         
        

       On the Element Reference Diagram page, hover the pointer over a relationship line between elements to view the element reference relationship.
        
         Figure 5 Viewing element reference relationships
         
        

      

      

     Select a project that has been successfully parsed in the project list and view the project dependency on the Single-Project Dependency tab page on the right.
      

      
       Downstream dependencies of the current project: The current project is highlighted and the project has only downstream dependencies.
        
         Figure 6 Downstream dependencies of a single project
         
        

       Upstream dependencies of the current project: The current project is highlighted and the project has only upstream dependencies.
        
         Figure 7 Upstream dependencies of a single project
         
        

       Upstream and downstream dependencies of the current project: The current project is highlighted and the three-layer relationships between the current project (at the center) and its upstream and downstream dependencies are displayed. The downstream projects that are depended on are displayed on the left. The upstream dependent projects are displayed on the right.
        
         Figure 8 Upstream and downstream dependencies of a single project
         
        

       Switching to the benchmark project: The three-layer upstream and downstream dependencies of the project after the switching are displayed. When you select a project, the dependencies of the project are highlighted.
        
         Figure 9 Switching to the benchmark project
         
        

      

      

     Select a project that has been successfully parsed in the project list and view the project dependency on the Multi-Project Dependency tab page on the right.
      

      
       The current project does not depend on other projects. In this case, the Project Dependency tab page has only one root node and does not have other subnodes.
        
         Figure 10 Current project depending on none projects
         
        

       The current project depends on another project, but the dependent project is not parsed.
        
         Figure 11 No parsing of the other projects on which the current project depends
         
        

        

       The current project depends on another project, and that project is present in the current develop-state environment.
        
         Figure 12 Project on which the current project depends found in the develop-state environment
         
        

      

      

     Click Export All to export all the project dependencies to the local PC in an Excel file.

     View the link relationship of a project dependency.
      

      
       Double-click the solid line of a dependency. The Link Relationship page is displayed.

       View the element dependency, including the project and module names, and element type.
        
         Figure 13 Viewing the link relationship of a project dependency
         
        

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Tenant Asset Management

name: Viewing Asset Difference Comparison Results
title: Viewing Asset Difference Comparison Results
text:
Viewing Asset Difference Comparison Results
 
 
  
  

  
   When multiple developers develop an app at the same time, the asset library provides a tool for comparing app differences.

   
    Prerequisites

    You have signed the asset development disclaimer.

   

   
    Context

    When multiple developers develop an app at the same time, the element modification records cannot be viewed. If multiple developers modify the same element, the content may be overwritten.

    App packages and project packages can be compared.

   

   
    Procedure

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.
      

      
       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click Development State Studio. 

       When the portal is displayed in menu mode, choose Products and Services > Development State Studio.

      

      

     On the menu bar of the home page, choose Asset Management > Asset Comparison Tool.
      

      
       Figure 1 Asset Comparison Tool
       
      

      

     Configure the assets to be compared by referring to Table 1.
      

      
       
       
        
         Table 1 Parameters of the asset comparison tool
        
        
         
         
         
        
        
         
          
           Area

          
           Parameter

          
           Description

         

        
        
         
          
           Source Asset

          
           Asset Source

          
           
            Local upload: Upload a local asset package (only in GDK, GPK, or ZIP format) as the source asset for comparison.

            Local asset library: Upload an asset in the local asset library as the source asset for comparison.

           

         

         
          
           Asset Upload

          
           This parameter is displayed only when Local upload is selected for Asset Source.

           Click Add and upload a local asset package (only in GDK, GPK, or ZIP format).

         

         
          
           Asset Password

          
           This parameter is displayed only when the asset package uploaded from the local PC is password-protected.

           Enter the correct password and click . After the pre-check is passed, the values of Asset Type, Asset Name, and Asset Version are automatically filled in.

         

         
          
           Asset Type

          
           
            When Local upload is selected for Asset Source, this parameter is automatically filled in after an asset package is successfully uploaded.

            When Local asset library is selected for Asset Source, select an asset type from the drop-down list. The options are App and Project Package.

           

         

         
          
           Asset Name

          
           
            When Local upload is selected for Asset Source, this parameter is automatically filled in after an asset package is successfully uploaded.

            When Local asset library is selected for Asset Source, select an asset name from the drop-down list.

           

         

         
          
           Asset Version

          
           
            When Local upload is selected for Asset Source, this parameter is automatically filled in after an asset package is successfully uploaded.

            When Local asset library is selected for Asset Source, select an asset version from the drop-down list.

           

         

         
          
           Asset to Be Compared

          
           Asset Source

          
           
            Local upload: Upload a local asset package (only in GDK, GPK, or ZIP format) as the target asset for comparison.

            Local asset library: Upload an asset in the local asset library as the target asset for comparison.

           

           
             NOTE: 
            
             Asset Source of the target asset does not need to be the same as that of the source asset.

            

           

         

         
          
           Asset Upload

          
           This parameter is displayed only when Local upload is selected for Asset Source. The type of the uploaded asset must be the same as the value of Asset Type of the source asset.

           Click Add and upload a local asset package (only in GDK, GPK, or ZIP format).

         

         
          
           Asset Password

          
           This parameter is displayed only when the asset package uploaded from the local PC is password-protected.

           Enter the correct password and click . After the pre-check is passed, the values of Asset Type, Asset Name, and Asset Version are automatically filled in.

         

         
          
           Asset Type

          
           
            When Local asset library is selected for Asset Source, only options of Asset Type of the source asset are displayed in the drop-down list.

            When Local upload is selected for Asset Source, this parameter is automatically filled in after an asset package is successfully uploaded.

           

         

         
          
           Asset Name

          
           
            When Local asset library is selected for Asset Source, select an asset name from the drop-down list.

            When Local upload is selected for Asset Source, this parameter is automatically filled in after an asset package is successfully uploaded.

           

         

         
          
           Asset Version

          
           
            When Local asset library is selected for Asset Source, select an asset version from the drop-down list.

            When Local upload is selected for Asset Source, this parameter is automatically filled in after an asset package is successfully uploaded.

           

         

        
       
      

      

     Click Compare.
      

      The asset comparison page is displayed, as shown in Figure 2.

      
        
       
        
         For ADC engine models, model dump, model loading, model archiving, model permissions, model pipelines, triggers, services (including scripts), data import or export, pages (including scripts), Mateline pages, Mateline scripts, processes, events, event listening, manifest.json, common functions, commands, data visualization screens, cards, inbound/outbound REST APIs, and inbound/outbound SOAP APIs, change types and modification details can be displayed.

         Difference details are not displayed for global assets included in the project package, other JSON files in the asset package, and other ADC elements except the preceding ones, such as permissions, internationalization, and custom assets.

         For other elements, such as DataFactory and AI, of a non-ADC engine, difference details are not displayed.

         The manifest.json file of an ADC engine can display the difference details from the following dimensions: name, asset type, project name, and version.

        

       

      

      
       Figure 2 Asset Comparison Result
       
      

      

     If the comparison result contains an element whose Change Type is Modification, click Details in the Operation column.
      

      
       Figure 3 Asset comparison result details
       
      

      

     Click View in the Operation column to view the asset differences.
      

      
       Figure 4 Asset comparison result

      Figure 1 Basic information and asset putaway information
      
     

     
      
       
        Table 1 Parameters in the Basic Info and Putaway Info areas
       
       
        
        
       
       
        
         
          Parameter

         
          Description

        

       
       
        
         
          Asset Name

         
          Name displayed on GDE Store, which can be modified only when the asset is put away for the first time.

        

        
         
          Putaway Version

         
          Version of the asset that is successfully packaged.

        

        
         
          Technical Support

         
          Set this parameter based on the actual service content. A maximum of five lines are allowed, and each line contains a maximum of 300 characters.

          An example is as follows:

          Service time: 9:00-18:00

          Service content: hotline support, remote services, on-site maintenance, and training services

          Service hotline: 12345678

          Service email: xx@xx.com

        

        
         
          Developer Type

         
          This parameter is displayed by default and cannot be modified.

        

        
         
          Developer Info

         
          This parameter is displayed by default and cannot be modified.

        

        
         
          Asset Type

         
          Asset category. You can select only one option.

        

        
         
          Business Domain

         
          There are sub-business domains under the business domain. You can select only one option.

        

        
         
          Deployment Mode

         
          Asset delivery type. You can select only one option.

          
           SaaS: online app software deployed on cloud-based infrastructure resources

           License: app software or BuildingBlock that can be used only after being downloaded and deployed

           API: API service of the software system deployed on cloud-based infrastructure resources

          

        

        
         
          Custom Label

         
          List of asset labels added by a developer. Multiple labels are separated with commas (,). Each label contains a maximum of 64 characters. A maximum of 16 labels are supported.

        

       
      
     

     
      Figure 2 Asset description

          Parameter

         
          Description

          Asset icon. Only one image in JPG, PNG, or JPEG format is supported. The size of a single image must be less than 50 KB, and the recommended size is 64 px x 64 px to 90 px x 90 px.

        

        
         
          background Image

         
          Only one image in JPG, PNG, or JPEG format is supported. The size of a single image must be less than 200 KB and the recommended size is 310 px x 120 px.

        

        
         
          Homepage Image

         
          Only one image in JPG, PNG, or JPEG format is supported. The size of a single image must be less than 500 KB and the recommended size is 660 px x 430 px.

        

        
         
          Introduction

         
          A maximum of 100 characters are supported. This parameter is mandatory.

        

        
         
          Asset Description

         
          Asset description.

        

        
         
          Dev Tutorial

         
          Asset development tutorial.

        

        
         
          Sample

         
          Asset sample description.

        

        
         
          Help Document

         
          Only one ZIP file can be uploaded. The total file size cannot exceed 100 MB.

        

        
         
          Open Source Software Statement

         
          You need to truthfully state the open source software usage of the asset in Open Source Software Statement. If no open source software is used, select N/A. The .zip format is supported, and the size cannot exceed 20 MB.

        

       
      
     

     
      Figure 3 Offering information
      
     

     
      
       
        Table 3 Parameters in the Offering Information area
       
       
        
        
       
       
        
         
          Parameter

         
          Description

        

       
       
        
         
          Main Image

         
          Images in JPG, PNG, JPEG, or GIF format are supported. A maximum of five files can be uploaded. The size of each file must be less than 5 MB. The recommended size is 800 px x 600 px. This parameter is mandatory.

        

        
         
          Highlight

         
          Offering highlight. Each highlight occupies a line. A maximum of five highlights can be added. Each highlight can contain a maximum of 100 characters.

        

        
         
          Customer Case

         
          Successful customer cases of the released version. If a success case is provided, describe it in detail rather than fill in only one success case name.

        

        
         
          Content Agreement

         
          Product service agreement, which contains a maximum of 200,000 characters. This parameter is mandatory.

        

        
         
          Copyright

         
          Only one ZIP file can be uploaded. The total file size cannot exceed 100 MB.

        

       
      
     

     
      Figure 4 Version update
      
     

     
      
       
        Table 4 Parameters in the Explanation of version update area
       
       
        
        
       
       
        
         
          Parameter

         
          Description

          Asset putaway description.

        

        
         
          Add Images

         
          A maximum of five files in JPG, PNG, or JPEG format can be uploaded, and the size of each file cannot exceed 500 KB.

title: TQL Syntax Reference
text:
TQL Syntax Reference
 
 
  
  

  
   This document describes the TQL syntax and usage reference in ADC.

   
     
    
     
      The TQL syntax and capabilities of ADC 2.X versions are slightly different from those of ADC 1.X versions. The syntax of ADC 2.X versions described in this document applies to assets added to ADC 2.X versions. TQL statements in assets imported by apps of ADC 1.X versions and TQL statements executed by calling compatible APIs of ADC 1.X versions can retain the TQL syntax of ADC 1.X versions.

      When a TQL statement constructed by a developer is used, it must be protected against TQL injection.

     

    

   

  

  
   
    TQL Overview

    TQL Statements Used for Model Data Query

   

   
    
     Parent topic: SCRIPT interface

name: TQL Overview
title: TQL Overview
text:
TQL Overview
 
 
  
  

  
   Top Query Language (TQL) is a unified query language of ADC. TQL statements can be considered as SQL statements of relational databases, but their syntax and capabilities are different. For example, TQL statements used in the model data query scenario are written based on the model concept (such as the model name and property name). Such statements cannot be used to determine the control value on a page. The functions and capabilities of TQL statements vary with the application scenarios. But, when the same semantics are to be expressed, the writing of TQL statements is the same.

  

  
   
    Basic TQL Concepts

    Common TQL Reserved Words

    Differences Between TQL and TEL Statements

   

   
    
     Parent topic: TQL Syntax Reference

name: Basic TQL Concepts
title: Basic TQL Concepts
text:
Basic TQL Concepts
 
 
  
  

  
   This topic describes the basic concepts of TQL based on the comparison with SQL and model data query scenarios.

   
    
    Identifier

    An identifier is used to refer to a specific object. The object is determined by the specific scenario and its position in the TQL statement. For example, in the model data query scenario, the identifiers may be the model name and property name, which correspond to the table name and field name in the SQL statement, respectively.

    Identifiers are case sensitive. In most cases, an identifier must start with a letter which can be followed by letters, digits, and underscores (_). If special characters such as spaces are required in an identifier, enclose the special characters with double quotation marks (""). For details, see Quotation Mark.

    An identifier can be separated by dots (.), which is commonly used in scenarios where a field in a table is referenced by a table name or alias. A maximum of two dots are supported, that is, the identifier is divided into three parts. When you use a dot (.) to separate an identifier, if you need to use double quotation marks (""), place the dot (.) outside the double quotation marks (""), for example, "book"."author".

   

   
    
    Constant

    A Constant refers to a fixed value, character string, and or specific value (such as null).

    Numeric constants include decimal integers and decimals, for example, 100 and 3.14.

    A string constant must start and end with a single quotation mark ('). The content quoted in the single quotation mark is a string. For details, see Quotation Mark.

   

   
    Value Variable

    A value variable is similar to a placeholder in a precompiled SQL statement, and variables can also be used in TQL statements to implement the same function as placeholders. Value variables are used to replace constants in TQL statements. The values of these variables can be transferred through parameters.

    A value variable starts with a dollar sign ($) or a dollar sign and an exclamation mark ($!), which are followed by a variable name. A variable name is case sensitive and must start with a letter, which is followed by letters, digits, and underscores (_), for example, $name and $! author.

    If a variable starts with a dollar sign and an exclamation mark ($!), the expression that contains the variable is invalid when the variable is left empty (the logical expression with the smallest logic unit is deleted from the TQL statement).

    Null: indicates that if no value is transferred for a variable or the variable value is null, an empty string, empty array, or empty object, the variable value is null.

   

   
    Function

    A function encapsulates the data processing logic to implement specific functions. After a function is executed, the corresponding result is returned. Available functions vary with the application scenarios. Functions with the same name may have different semantics and usage in different scenarios.

    For details about the usage and examples, see TQL Functions.

   

   
    Operator and Operand

    When writing TQL statements, you can use operators to process operands. Operators can be used to process one or more operands and can be placed before, after, or between operands. After the processing is complete, the processing result is returned. Operands can be identifiers, constants, variables, functions, and other expressions. The operators and operands that can be used vary with scenarios.

    For details about the usage and examples, see Operators and Expressions.

   

   
    Expression

    Consisting of operators and operands, an expression is a formula that expresses the logical meaning of one or more data processing operations. Expressions can be combined using operators to form more complex processing logic expressions.

    For details about the usage and examples, see Operators and Expressions.

   

   
    
    Quotation Mark

    Different quotation marks in TQL statements have different meanings. The following quotation marks can be used in TQL statements:

    
     Double quotation marks ("") are used to indicate identifiers. For details, see Identifier. If double quotation marks ("") need to be used in an identifier, add a backslash (\) in front of the double quotation marks ("") for escape. For example, "username" indicates the identifier username. This identifier does not need to be escaped because it does not contain quotation marks (""). "identifier with \"double quote\"" indicates the identifier identifier with "double quote". You need to use backslashes (\) to escape the double quotation marks ("") in TQL statements because this identifier contains double quotation marks ("").

     Single quotation marks (') are used to indicate a string constant. For details, see Constant. If single quotation marks (') need to be used in a character string, add a backslash (\) in front of the single quotation marks (\) for escape. For example, 'ADC' and '123' indicate the ADC and 123 character strings, respectively. These character strings do not need to be escaped because they do not contain single quotation marks ('). 'You\'re welcome.' indicates the character string You're welcome. You need to use a backslash (\) to escape the single quotation mark (') in TQL statements because this character string contains a single quotation mark (').

    

   

   
    Reserved Words

    Reserved words have special meanings in TQL statements. For example, if reserved words are used as identifiers, the TQL statement syntax may fail to be parsed. You cannot use reserved words as identifiers in TQL statements. The reserved words vary with the application scenarios of TQL statements. Common TQL Reserved Words describes the reserved words in each scenario. For details about the usage of reserved words in other scenarios, see the corresponding topics.

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: TQL Overview

name: Common TQL Reserved Words
title: Common TQL Reserved Words
text:
Common TQL Reserved Words
 
 
  
  

  
   The reserved words described in this topic are those used in all ADC scenarios. The details are as follows:

   ALL, ALTER, ANALYZE, AND, ANY, AS, ASC, BETWEEN, BY, CASE, CHAR, CHECK, CLUSTER, COMPRESS, CONNECT, CONTAINS, CREATE, DATE, DECIMAL, DEFAULT, DELETE, DESC, DISTINCT, DROP, ELSE, EMPTY, END, ENDS, EQUAL, EXCLUSIVE, EXISTS, FALSE, FIRST, FLOAT, FOR, FROM, FULL, GRANT, GREATER, GROUP, HAVING, IDENTIFIED, IGNORE, IN, INDEX, INNER, INSERT, INTEGER, INTERSECT, INTO, IS, JOIN, LAST, LEFT, LESS, LIKE, LIMIT, LOCK, LONG, MINUS, MODE, NOCOMPRESS, NOT, NOWAIT, NULL, NULLS, NUMBER, OF, ON, OPTION, OR, ORDER, OUTER, OVER, PARTITION, PCTFREE, PRIOR, PUBLIC, RAW, RENAME, RESOURCE, REVOKE, RIGHT, SELECT, SET, SHARE, SIZE, SMALLINT, START, STARTS, SYNONYM, TABLE, THAN, THEN, TO, TRIGGER, TRUE, TRUNCATE, UNION, UPDATE, USING, UNIQUE, VALUES, VARCHAR, VIEW, WHEN, WHERE, WITH
   
     
    
     The reserved words are case insensitive.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: TQL Overview

name: Differences Between TQL and TEL Statements
title: Differences Between TQL and TEL Statements
text:
Differences Between TQL and TEL Statements
 
 
  
  

  
   The main functions and application scenarios of TQL and TEL statements are different. In a specific scenario, only either of them is used. For details, see the development guide for the specific scenario. For example, TQL statements instead of TEL statements are used for model data query.

   
    TQL statements are used for query.
     TQL statements are used to query data that meets the specified conditions from the existing data based on the criteria specified in TQL statements. A typical scenario is as follows: During model data query, TQL statements are used to specify query conditions and further calculate the query result (such as grouping and aggregation).

    TEL statements are used for the expression calculation.
     TEL statements are used to calculate the given data based on the expressions specified in TEL statements to obtain the calculation result.

   

   Other differences are as follows:

   
    Variables can be used in TQL statements but cannot be used in TEL statements.
     TQL statements are used in the scenario where a trigger is triggered by a business logic (for example, the business side calls a service or an API of a model). You can use a variable as a placeholder in a TQL statement, and the calling party transfers a specific value to obtain a complete TQL statement for execution.

     However, TEL statements are generally used when data is changed (for example, the model data is changed). Therefore, a parameter (that is, an identifier in a TEL statement) calculated by a TEL statement comes from the context of the TEL statements (for example, model data that is actually changed). Additional values don not need to and cannot be transferred through mechanisms, such as variables.

   

   TQL statement examples in the model data query scenario:

   author = 'Tom' -- Data filtering TQL statement, which is used to query the data whose author is Tom
select title from book where author = 'Tom' and nationality = $nationality -- Complete TQL statement, which is used to query the book whose author is Tom and the author's nationality is transferred by a variable
select author, count(1) as count from book group by author -- Complete TQL statement, which is used to collect statistics on the number of works of each author
   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: TQL Overview

TQL Statements Used for Model Data Query
 
 
  
  

  
   TQL statements can be used to limit the condition of operations such as querying, updating, and deleting model data in some service model operations and some APIs of model data operations. The TQL statement query capability varies with the underlying data storage mode of each model. This topic mainly describes TQL statements used for data model and data source model query. A few TQL statement capabilities support the elastic models and have some special functions, which are described in Introduction to the Elastic Model TQL Statements.
