name: 02020303 An App with the Same Name as an Installed App Exists and the UUIDs in the Two App Packages Are Different
title: 02020303 An App with the Same Name as an Installed App Exists and the UUIDs in the Two App Packages Are Different
text:
02020303 An App with the Same Name as an Installed App Exists and the UUIDs in the Two App Packages Are Different
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An app fails to be installed. The system displays a message indicating that a project or app package with the same name as an installed app exists and the UUIDs in the two app packages are different. The error code is 02020303.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    During app installation, the system verifies the app:

    
     If an app with the same name and UUID as an installed app exists and the version verification requirements are met, the installed app will be updated.

     If an app with the same name but different UUID as an installed app exist, the system displays a message indicating that the installation fails and an error message is displayed. The causes of this scenario are different. Developers need to select a solution based on the specific cause:
      
       Cause 1: A developer creates apps with the same name in different environments. As a result, the UUIDs of the apps are different. In this case, the two apps are different. The developer expects to deploy the two apps normally, that is, importing the current app without affecting the original one.

       Cause 2: A human error occurs when the developer manually packages the orchestration element file. As a result, the UUIDs during the two packaging are different. In this case, the developer expects that the latest packaged app can be properly deployed and that the existing app of the old version can be uninstalled or overwritten, that is, the app of the old version is uninstalled and then the app of the new version is installed, or the app of the old version is overwritten by deploying the app of the new version.

      

    

   

   
    Solution

    To locate and rectify the fault for cause 1, perform the following steps:

    
     Select the required mode based on site requirements and change the name of the app package.
      

      
       (Recommended) Method 1: Rename a cloned project on the develop-state page.
        
         Go to the Project Management page in the develop-state environment and find the project corresponding to the current app.

         Click  to clone the project, and rename the project.

         Go to the details page of the new project and repackage the app.

        

       Method 2: Change the value of name in the manifest.json file in the app package.
        
         Decompress the app package on the local PC and change the value of name in the manifest.json file to a globally unique name.

         Package the app again based on the rules.

        

      

      

     Reinstall the new app package.

    

    

    To locate and rectify the fault for cause 2, perform the following steps:

    
     Change the name of the app package or uninstall the existing app package with the same name as the faulty one.
      

      
       (Recommended) Method 1: Manually change the UUID in the app package to be the same as the UUID of the installed app in the system.
        
         Decompress the app package on the local PC and change the value of uuid in the manifest.json file to be the same as the UUID of the installed app in the system.

         Package the app again based on the rules.

        

       Method 2: Manually uninstall the app with the same name as the faulty one in the system and click Data Clear to delete the service data of that app.
        
          
         
          Uninstalling an app is a high-risk operation. Evaluate the risks before performing this operation.

         

        

      

      

     Reinstall the app package.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: App Orchestration

name: 02020332 The App on Which the App to Be Installed Depends Does Not Exist
title: 02020332 The App on Which the App to Be Installed Depends Does Not Exist
text:
02020332 The App on Which the App to Be Installed Depends Does Not Exist
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An app fails to be installed. The system displays a message indicating that the app on which the app to be installed depends does not exist. The error code is 02020332.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The app on which the app to be installed depends is not installed or fails to be installed.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Obtain the name of the app on which the app to be installed depends based on the error information and obtain the corresponding app package.
      

      For example, if the error information contains "The app [NBIAlarm] on which the app [ToB_PLIO] depends does not exist", the app to be installed is ToB_PLIO and the app on which the app depends is NBIAlarm.

      

     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

     Choose Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager.

     Choose App Manager > App List to check whether the app on which the app to be installed depend has been installed.
      

      
       If no, import the obtained app and install it.

       If yes, check whether the app is successfully installed. If the installation fails, locate, analyze, and rectify the fault based on the installation error information.

      

      

     After the app on which the app to be installed depends is installed successfully installed, reinstall the app package.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: App Orchestration

name: 03010001 Number of Tasks Created by a User on a Single Node Exceeds the Upper Limit
title: 03010001 Number of Tasks Created by a User on a Single Node Exceeds the Upper Limit
text:
03010001 Number of Tasks Created by a User on a Single Node Exceeds the Upper Limit
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An app fails to be installed. The system displays a message indicating that the number of tasks created by a user on a single node exceeds the upper limit. The error code is 03010001.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The number of concurrent app package import tasks created by a user exceeds the maximum number of tasks on a single node (5 by default, indicating that a single user can install a maximum of five apps on a single node concurrently).

   

   
    Solution

    
     Contact the tenant administrator to determine whether to change the maximum number of tasks on a single node.
      

      
       If the current maximum number of tasks on a single node meets the requirements in most application scenarios, you do not need to change the number. In this case, the user can go to 3 after the ongoing installation task is complete.

       If the user needs to import more than five apps concurrently frequently, change the maximum number of tasks on a single node after evaluation. In this case, go to 2 and 3.

      

      

     Change the maximum number as the tenant administrator.
      

      
       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

       Choose Products and Services > Administration > System Settings.

       In the search area, enter import-concurrency-user-limit in the name search box and set the category to app-io.
        
         If the search result is not empty, click Edit in the Operation column on the right of the parameter and change Value based on site requirements.
          

          

         If the search result is empty, click Create and set parameters based on site requirements.
          

          

        

       Click OK.

      

      

     Reinstall the app package.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: App Orchestration

name: 03010464 Failed to Execute the App Package Import Task
title: 03010464 Failed to Execute the App Package Import Task
text:
03010464 Failed to Execute the App Package Import Task
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An app fails to be installed. The system displays a message indicating that the import task fails to be executed. The error code is 03010464.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    Orchestration elements such as models, services, pages, commands, and internationalization elements fail to be imported.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Locate, analyze, and rectify the fault based on the error log information.
      

      
       View all error information in front of the message "failed to do import task", and analyze and handle the orchestration element errors one by one.

       After all orchestration element errors are handled, reinstall the app package.

      

      

     If the fault persists, contact Huawei technical support to locate and rectify the fault.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: App Orchestration

name: 03010478 An Error Occurred During App Installation
title: 03010478 An Error Occurred During App Installation
text:
03010478 An Error Occurred During App Installation
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    On the App Management page in the runtime-state environment, an error occurred during app installation. The error code is 03010478.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The administrator has disabled the app installation function in the App Management area.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Check whether the GDE App Manager menu exists.
      

      
       Log in to the GDE data zone portal.

       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

       On the menu bar, check whether the Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager menu exists.
        
         Yes: Go to 2.

         No: Go to 3.

        

      

      

     Install apps on the GDE App Manager page.
      

      
       Access the GDE App Manager page and choose App Manager > App List from the navigation pane.

       Click Import and select the asset package of the app to be installed.

       Click OK.

       On the App List page, select the app to be installed and click Install.
        

        

      

      

     Contact the administrator to enable the installation function in the App Management area.
      

      
       Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.

       Click the user account in the upper right corner, and choose Switch Tenant to switch to the master tenant.

       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

       Choose Products and Services > ADC App Development Management > App Release Configuration.

       In the navigation pane, click the Tenant Configuration tab.

       Select the tenant to be configured from the Tenant drop-down list.

       In the App Management area, disable Mask the Installation Function.
        

        

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: App Orchestration

title: 03010479 An Error Occurred During Installation File Downloading

     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

     Choose Products and Services > ADC App Development Management > App Release Configuration.

     In the navigation pane, click the Tenant Configuration tab.

     Select the tenant to be configured from the Tenant drop-down list.

     In the App Management area, disable Mask the Download Button on the Installation Log List Page.

name: 03020455 Version of the App Installation Package Must Be Later Than or Equal to That of the Existing App in the System
title: 03020455 Version of the App Installation Package Must Be Later Than or Equal to That of the Existing App in the System
text:
03020455 Version of the App Installation Package Must Be Later Than or Equal to That of the Existing App in the System
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An app fails to be installed. The system displays a message indicating that the version of the app installation package must be later than or equal to that of the existing app in the system. The error code is 03020455.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    An app package of a later version has been installed in the system, and the version of the newly imported app package is earlier than that of the app package in the system.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Select the required handling method.
      

      
       (Recommended) Method 1: Enable the function of importing apps of earlier versions.
        
         Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the current tenant administrator.

         When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

         Choose Products and Services > Administration > System Settings.

         In the search area, enter allow_lower_version_app in the name search box and set the category to adc-app-mgt.
          
           If the search result is not empty, click Edit in the Operation column on the right of the parameter and change Value to true.
            

            

           If the search result is empty, click Create and set related parameters.
            

            

          

         Click OK.

        

       Method 2: Uninstall the app package of the later version and delete the corresponding data.
        
          
         
          Uninstalling apps and deleting app data are high-risk operations. Evaluate the risks before performing these operations.

         

        

      

      

     Reinstall the app package.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: App Orchestration

name: 03020461 An App of a Later Version Whose Data Is Not Cleared Exists
title: 03020461 An App of a Later Version Whose Data Is Not Cleared Exists
text:
03020461 An App of a Later Version Whose Data Is Not Cleared Exists
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An app fails to be installed. The system displays a message indicating that there is an app of a later version whose data is not cleared. The error code is 03020461.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The app package of a later version has been uninstalled, but Reserve data is selected during the uninstallation. As a result, the app data of the later version still exists in the system, and the app of an earlier version fails to be installed.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Select the required handling method.
      

      
       (Recommended) Method 1: Enable the function of importing apps of earlier versions.
        
         Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the current tenant administrator.

         When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

         Choose Products and Services > Administration > System Settings.

         In the search area, enter allow_lower_version_app in the name search box and set the category to adc-app-mgt.
          
           If the search result is not empty, click Edit in the Operation column on the right of the parameter and change Value to true.
            

            

           If the search result is empty, click Create and set related parameters.
            

            

          

         Click OK.

        

       Method 2: Delete the app data of a later version.
        
          
         
          Deleting app data is high-risk operations. Evaluate the risks before performing the operation.

         

        

        
         Delete the app data of the later version on the App Management page.
          
           Choose Products and Services > Administration > Assets > App Management.

           Click Data Clear. Uninstalled apps with data reserved are displayed on the page.

           Select the app whose data is to be deleted and click Clear.

          

         Delete the app data of the later version on the GDE App Manager page.
          
           Choose Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager.

           Click the Data Clearance tab. Uninstalled apps with data reserved are displayed on the page.

           Select the app whose data is to be deleted and click Clear Data.

          

        

      

      

     Reinstall the app package.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: App Orchestration

name: 03060209 Assets with Installation Engine Category Containing Non-ADC Engines Are Not Supported
title: 03060209 Assets with Installation Engine Category Containing Non-ADC Engines Are Not Supported

03060209 Assets with Installation Engine Category Containing Non-ADC Engines Are Not Supported
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An app fails to be installed. The system displays a message indicating that assets with installation engine category containing non-ADC engines are not supported. The error code is 03060209.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The app package contains non-ADC orchestration elements, for example, elements related to data orchestration (elements of the data_orchestration type).

     Click the user account in the upper right corner, and choose Switch Tenant to switch to the service tenant.

name: 07020320 An Error Occurred During Project Deletion
title: 07020320 An Error Occurred During Project Deletion
text:
07020320 An Error Occurred During Project Deletion
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An error occurred when a project is deleted from the Project Management page in the develop-state environment. The error code is 07020320.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The current user does not have the permission to delete the target project.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Check whether the target project is no longer used.
      

      
       Yes: Go to 2.

       No: Retain the project and ignore the error.

      

      

     Contact the owner of the target project to delete the project.
      

      
       Go to the develop-state page and choose Project Management.

       Search for the project to be deleted in the search box.

       In the search result, view the owner of the project and contact the owner to delete the target project.

      

      

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: App Orchestration

name: 07050306 Failed to Obtain the Element Instance List
title: 07050306 Failed to Obtain the Element Instance List
text:
07050306 Failed to Obtain the Element Instance List
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An app fails to be packaged. The system displays a message indicating that the element instance list fails to be obtained. The error code is 07050306.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The microservice corresponding to the element instance is abnormal.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Obtain the name of the abnormal microservice based on the error details in the error information. For example, if the message "Invocation of service adc-studio-mcp.CommandPackageRpcService.queryElements occurred an error" is displayed in the error details, the name of the abnormal microservice is adc-studio-mcp.

     Check whether the stack status of the microservice is normal.
      

      
       Log in to the GDE management zone portal as the service installation user.

       Choose Maintenance > Instance Deployment > TOSCA Stack Deployment.

       Enter the microservice name in the search box and click the search icon.

       View the stack status in the search result.
        
         If the stack status is abnormal, perform the following operations to restart the stack:
          
           Choose More > Stop in the row of the stack.

           After the stack is stopped, choose More > Start in the row of the stack.
            If the stack status is normal after the restart, go to 3. If the stack status is abnormal after the restart, contact Huawei technical support to locate and rectify the fault.

          

         If the stack status is normal, contact Huawei technical support to locate and rectify the fault.

        

      

      

     Reinstall the app package.

name: 09100006 Failed to Obtain Authentication Information
title: 09100006 Failed to Obtain Authentication Information
text:
09100006 Failed to Obtain Authentication Information
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    A project fails to be deployed in one-click mode. The system displays a message indicating that the authentication information fails to be obtained. The error code is 09100006.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    During remote project deployment, the configured environment authentication information is incorrect. As a result, the remote deployment environment fails to be authenticated.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Obtain the name of the remote deployment environment based on the description in the error information. For example, if the message "App install to remote environment failed" is displayed in the error description, the name of the remote deployment environment is remote.

     In the remote deployment environment, check whether the machine-machine user account information is correct.
      

      
       Log in to the GDE data zone portal corresponding to the remote deployment environment as the tenant administrator.

       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

       Choose Products and Services > Administration > Identity Authentication > Machine-Machine User Management.

       Enter the machine-machine user account used for remote deployment environment authentication in the search box and click the search icon.

       In the search result, check whether the machine-machine user account is correctly configured, and obtain the correct authentication information of the account based on the following information:
        
         Check whether the machine-machine user account is associated with the adc-remote-app-manager role. If yes, go to the Machine-Machine User Authorization tab page on the machine-machine user details page and bind the role with the account.

         Check whether the IP address control policy is enabled for the machine-machine user account. If yes, ensure that the IP address of the remote deployment environment is included in the IP address control policy.

         Obtain the machine-machine user account, authentication type, and AK/SK information. The AK/SK information is displayed only once when the machine-machine account is created. Ensure that the correct AK/SK information is saved during the creation.

        

      

      

     In the develop-state environment, check whether the authentication information is correctly configured.
      

      
       Log in to the GDE data zone portal corresponding to the develop-state environment as the tenant administrator.

       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

       Choose Development State Studio.

       Select General Settings > Environment Management.

       Enter the name of the remote deployment environment in the search box and click the search icon.

       In the search result, click Edit in the Operation column of the remote deployment environment.

       Check the authentication configuration information and modify it as needed to ensure that the information is consistent with that on the remote deployment environment.

      

      

     Deploy the project again in one-click mode.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: App Orchestration

name: 00640012 Insufficient Service Execution Permission
title: 00640012 Insufficient Service Execution Permission
text:
00640012 Insufficient Service Execution Permission
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    A service fails to be called and the system displays a message indicating that the service execution permission is insufficient. The error code is 00640012.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The user or service does not meet the permission verification requirements of the called service.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Obtain the names of the project, module, and service based on the service URI in the error information. The service URI is in the format of "[/{Project name}/{Module name}/{Service name}]".
      

      For example, the message "/tetError/tetError/teterror_qqqww_create" in the error information indicates that the teterror_qqww_create service in the tetError module of the tetError project fails to be called.

      

     Go to the develop-state page and choose Project Management.

     On the project list page, click the project corresponding to the service that fails to be called.

     In the navigation pane, choose Service. In the service list, click the service that fails to be called.

     In the canvas area, click the entry node of that service and check the value of Permission Control Mode in the Basic Information area of the Service tab page on the right.
      

      

      

      
       If Permission Control Mode is set to Logged-in, check whether Page Access in the Basic Information area of the Service tab page on the right is enabled.
        
         If Page Access is disabled, enable it.

         If Page Access is enabled, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

        

       If Permission Control Mode is set to Logged-in and Authorized and Permission items has been configured, contact the administrator to grant the permission items to the role of the user who fails to call the service.

       If Permission Control Mode is set to Customized Service, check whether the return result contains {"result":true} after the custom service is called and perform corresponding operations based on the return result.
        
         If the return result contains {"result":true}, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

         If the return result does not contain {"result":true}, check the logic of the custom service, determine the conditions for which the return result contains {"result":true}, and use the conditions to call the service for which the error is reported again.

        

       If Permission Control Mode is set to Legacy Permission, perform the following operations to associate the service with the compatible permission item:
        
         In the navigation pane, choose Permission.

         Click the Permission Compatibility tab and click Create.

         Configure compatible permission items and click Create.
          

          

          Configure parameters as follows:

          
           Name: Set it to the name of the service that fails to be called.

           Type: Set it to service.

           Permission Path: Set it to the permission path of an existing permission item or customize the permission path as required.

           Resource Operation: Set it to invokeService.

          

         Contact the administrator to grant the permission items created in 5.c to the role of the user who fails to call the service.

        

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Service and Model Orchestration

name: 00610009 Service Call Times Exceeds the Maximum
title: 00610009 Service Call Times Exceeds the Maximum
text:
00610009 Service Call Times Exceeds the Maximum
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    A service fails to be called and the system displays a message indicating that service call times exceeds the maximum. The error code is 00610009.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The service is called cyclically or service call times exceeds the maximum.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Obtain the names of the project, module, and service based on the service URI in the error information. The service URI is in the format of "[/{Project name}/{Module name}/{Service name}]".
      

      For example, the message "/tetError/tetError/teterror_qqqww_create" in the error description indicates that the teterror_qqww_create service in the tetError module of the tetError project reports the error.

      

     Check whether a cyclic call exists in the logic of the service for which the error is reported.
      

      
       Go to the develop-state page and choose Project Management.

       On the project list page, click the project corresponding to the service for which the error is reported.

       In the navigation pane, choose Service. In the service list, click the service for which the error is reported.

       Check whether a cyclic call exists in the logic of the service.
        
         Yes: Modify the service logic and save the modification.

         No: Go to 3.

        

      

      

     Check whether the service for which the error is reported is cyclically called.
      

      
       Obtain the trace ID on the right of the error code.

       Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.

       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click App O&M Management.

       Choose Products and Services > App O&M Management > Log Viewing.

       In the Filter Condition area, set Trace ID. Equal to. Trace ID obtained in 3.a and click OK.

       In the search result, view the corresponding log information to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault. If the fault persists, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Service and Model Orchestration

name: 00640149 Services Related to a Legacy Asset Cannot Be Found in the Runtime-State Environment
title: 00640149 Services Related to a Legacy Asset Cannot Be Found in the Runtime-State Environment
text:
00640149 Services Related to a Legacy Asset Cannot Be Found in the Runtime-State Environment
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    Services related to a legacy asset fail to be called and the system displays a message indicating that services related to a legacy asset cannot be found in the runtime-site environment. The error code is 00640149.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    A non-legacy asset is called in four-segment mode (format: app.service.xxx.xxx) or the runtime-state environment does not contain the services related to the legacy asset.

   

   
    Solution

    
     View the names of the project and module that the service belongs to.
      

      
       Obtain the service name based on the service URI in the error information. The last segment of the four segments in the service URI is the service name.
        For example, app.service.unkown.khl_test_csv_get_list in the error information indicates that the error is reported by the khl_test_csv_get_list service.

       On the develop-state page, click  in the upper right corner.

       In the search area, enter the name of the service for which the error is reported and press Enter.

       Click the All Projects tab and view the names of the project and module that the faulty service belongs to.
        
         If the search result is empty, the service does not exist. In this case, access the page designer and check whether the called service is correct.

         If the search result is not empty, the service exists. In this case, check the names of the project and module that the faulty service belongs to and go to 2.
          

          

        

      

      

     Check whether the called service is a service related to the legacy asset.
      

      
       Go to the develop-state page and choose Project Management.

       On the project list page, click the project corresponding to the service that fails to be called.

       In the navigation pane, choose Service. Click  in the upper right corner of the service list.

       Enter the name of the service that fails to be called in the search box and click the search icon.

       In the search result, check whether the service name contains Legacy Asset.
        
         Yes: The called service is a service related to the legacy asset. In this case, go to 3.

         No: The called service is not a service related to the legacy asset. In this case, change the service call mode in the script as follows and save the modification.
          var request = {};
var response = ServiceInvoker.post("url",request);

        

      

      

     Check whether the legacy asset to which the called service belongs can be found in the runtime-state environment.
      

      
       Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.

       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click App O&M Management.

       Choose Products and Services > App O&M Management > App Debugging > Service Debugging.

       Select Service from the service type drop-down list and click  in the text box in the upper left corner.

       In the displayed Search for Service dialog box, set the names of the project, module, and service, and click Search.
        
         If the service can be found, the legacy asset to which the called service belongs exists. In this case, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

         If the service cannot be found, the legacy asset to which the called service belongs does not exist. In this case, go to 4.

        

      

      

     Install the legacy asset to which the called service belongs.
      

      
       Obtain files related to the legacy asset to which the called service belongs.

       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

       Choose Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager.

       In the navigation pane, choose App Manager > App List and click Import.

       Click Select File to upload the legacy asset file and click OK.

       In the app list, select the name of the uploaded legacy asset and click Install.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Service and Model Orchestration

name: 01000001 Failed to Compile the JavaScript Script into a Class
title: 01000001 Failed to Compile the JavaScript Script into a Class
text:
01000001 Failed to Compile the JavaScript Script into a Class
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    A script fails to be saved after being compiled in a service, and the system displays a message indicating that the JavaScript script fails to be compiled into a class. The error code is 01000001.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    Syntax errors exist in the script.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Check whether the content marked with red wavy lines in the service script is correct.
      

      
       Examples of common syntax errors are as follows:
       
        Incorrect syntax keyword
         

        Incorrect JSON definition format
         

        Incorrect constant name
         

        Too much data in the script
         

         

       

      

      

     Modify the service script based on the syntax errors found in 1 and save the modification.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Service and Model Orchestration

name: 06010012 Value of Script Quota JS Command Exceeds the Threshold
title: 06010012 Value of Script Quota JS Command Exceeds the Threshold
text:
06010012 Value of Script Quota JS Command Exceeds the Threshold
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    A service fails to be called, and the system displays a message indicating that the value of script quota JS Command exceeds the threshold. The error code is 06010012.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The number of commands in the service script exceeds the value of the quota JS Command.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Obtain the names of the project, module, and script in which the number of commands exceeds the threshold based on the script URI in the error information. The service URI is in the format of "[/{Project name}/{Module name}/{Script name}]".
      

      For example, the message "/test_pcq_js1/test_pcq_js1/pcqjs1_InstructionsExceeds" in the error information indicates that the pcqjs1_InstructionsExceeds script in the test_pcq_js1 module of the test_pcq_js1 project is the script in which the number of commands exceeds the threshold.

      

     Check the number of commands in the script in which the number of commands exceeds the limit.
      

      
       Go to the develop-state page and choose Project Management.

       On the project list page, click the project corresponding to the script in which the number of commands exceeds the threshold.

       In the navigation pane, choose Service > Orchestration Resources > Script Management.

       Enter the name of the script in which the number of commands exceeds the threshold in the search box and click the search icon.

       In the search result, click Edit on the right of the script.

       Check the commands in the script and modify the script to ensure that the number of JavaScript commands in the script is less than the threshold.

       Click OK.

      

      

     (Optional) If the number of JavaScript commands in the script cannot be lower than the threshold, contact the administrator to modify the corresponding app quota.
      

      
        
       
        This operation may affect other users under the same tenant. Therefore, exercise caution when performing this operation.

       

      

      
       Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.

       Click the user account in the upper right corner, and choose Switch Tenant to switch to the master tenant.

       When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

       Choose Products and Services > App O&M Management > App Quota Configuration.

       Use either of the following methods to modify the configuration of the quota JS Command:
        
         Modify the configuration of the quota JS Command at the tenant level by increasing the maximum number of JavaScript commands under the current tenant.
          
           In the navigation pane, click the Tenant Configuration tab.

           Select the tenant to be configured from the Tenant drop-down list.

           In the JS Engine area, click Modify on the right of JS Command Quota.

           In the displayed Edit JS Command Quota dialog box, change the values of Max JS Commands and Policy Mode based on site requirements.
            

            

           Click OK.

          

         Configure the JavaScript command quantity quota whitelist so that the current tenant is not restricted by the configuration of JS Command Quota when using the corresponding app.
          
           In the navigation pane, choose App Quota Whitelist.

           Click Create.

           Configure the app quota whitelist based on site requirements.
            

            

            Configure parameters as follows:

            
             Whitelist Configuration Item: Set it to JS Command Quota.

             Tenant ID: Select the tenant to which the current user belongs based on site requirements.

             App Scope: Set it to the name of the project to which the script containing excessive commands belongs.

            

           Click OK.

          

        

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Service and Model Orchestration

          Text

          Text

         
          The maximum length of the text is greater than or equal to 16 characters.

          Integer

         
          -

        

        
         
          Reference

         
          Text

         
          -

name: 04001000 Ticket ID or the Value of TicketId Does Not Exist
title: 04001000 Ticket ID or the Value of TicketId Does Not Exist
text:
04001000 Ticket ID or the Value of TicketId Does Not Exist
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An error occurs when the delete_ticket, deleteProcessInstance, and batch_delete_ticket services are called to delete tickets in the develop-state environment. The error code is 04001000.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The ticket information does not exist in the quick ticket query table or the ticket data is incomplete.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Go to the develop-state page and choose Project Management.

     Search for Bpm in the search box and access the process_runtime module of the BPM project.

     In the navigation pane, choose Service.

     In the service list, open and run the process_runtime_ticket_basicinfo_get service, transfer the ticket ID or the value of TicketId in the error information, and check whether a value is returned.
      

      
       If a value is returned, the ticket exists in the quick query table. In this case, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

       If no value is returned, the ticket does not exist in the quick query table. In this case, go to 5.

      

      

      

      

     Check whether redundant data of the ticket exists in the process model.
      

      
       Go to the develop-state page and choose Project Management.

       On the project list page, click the project corresponding to the process for which the error is reported.

       In the navigation pane, choose Business Process.

       On the Business Process page, locate the process in the error information and click Edit in the Operation column.

       The following uses TroubleTicket as an example to describe how to view and record the data model corresponding to the process.
        

        

       In the navigation pane, choose Service.

       In the service list, open and run the ${data_model_name}_get service to check whether the ticket contains redundant data.
        
         ${data_model_name} indicates the data model name recorded in 5.e. Enter the ticket ID or the value of TicketId in the error information in the orderid text box and check whether the id parameter has a return value.
         
          If so, redundant ticket data exists in the process model. In this case, go to 5.h.

          If not, redundant ticket data does not exist in the process model. In this case, ignore the error.

         

        

        

        

       In the service list, open and run the ${data_model_name}_batch_delete service to delete data.
        ${data_model_name} is the data model name recorded in 5.e, and id is the value of id in the return value in 5.g.

        

        

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Process Orchestration

name: 08001002 Ticket Is Not in running State
title: 08001002 Ticket Is Not in running State
text:
08001002 Ticket Is Not in running State
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An error is reported when a user associates, cancels, escalates, transfers, or handles a ticket in the runtime-state environment. The error code is 08001002.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The target ticket is in Canceled, Completed, or Suspended state.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Go to the develop-state page and choose Project Management.

     Search for Bpm in the search box and access the process_runtime module of the BPM project.

     In the navigation pane, choose Service.

     Open and run the process_runtime_ticket_basicinfo_get service, transfer the ticket ID in the error information, and check the ticket status in the return result.
      

      
       If the ticket is not in running state, the preceding ticket operations are unavailable. In this case, ignore the error.

       If the ticket is in running state, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.
        

        

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Process Orchestration

name: 09001001 Process Definition Does Not Exist
title: 09001001 Process Definition Does Not Exist
text:
09001001 Process Definition Does Not Exist
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An error is reported when a ticket-related operation is performed in the runtime-state environment. The error code is 09001001.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    Process definition does not exist.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal.

     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

     Choose Products and Services > Administration > Process Management > Process Configuration.

     Enter the process name in the error information in the Process Name search box and click the search icon.
      

      
       If no data is found, the process definition does not exist. In this case, go to 5.

       If any data is found, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

      

      

     Check whether the GDE App Manager menu exists.
      

      
       On the menu bar, check whether the Products and Services > Administration > Assets > GDE App Manager menu exists.
       
        Yes: Go to 6.

        No: Contact Huawei technical support.

       

      

      

     Install apps on the GDE App Manager page.
      

      
       Access the GDE App Manager page and choose App Manager > App List from the navigation pane.

       Click Import and select the asset package of the app to be installed.

       Click OK.

       On the App List page, select the app to be installed and click Install.
        

        

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Process Orchestration

name: 08001010 Tickets to Be Associated Do Not Exist
title: 08001010 Tickets to Be Associated Do Not Exist
text:
08001010 Tickets to Be Associated Do Not Exist
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An error is reported when the ticket_accociate_create service is called to associate tickets in the develop-state environment. The error code is 08001010.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The source tickets do not exist.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Go to the develop-state page and choose Project Management.

     Search for Bpm in the search box and access the process_runtime module of the BPM project.

     In the navigation pane, choose Service.

     Open and run the process_runtime_ticket_basicinfo_get service, transfer the ticket instance ID in the error information to orderid, and check whether a value is returned.
      

      

      
       
       
        No: The source ticket does not exist. Select another ticket for association.

        Yes: Contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

       

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Process Orchestration

name: 04200002 Process Is Not Activated
title: 04200002 Process Is Not Activated
text:
04200002 Process Is Not Activated
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An error is reported when a ticket-related operation is performed in the runtime-state environment. The error code is 04200002.

    

    

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The process for which the ticket is created is not activated.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal.

     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

     Choose Products and Services > Administration > Process Management > Process Configuration.

     Enter the process name in the error information in the Process Name search box and click the search icon.

     In the search result, click Enable in the Operation column.

     Click OK.

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Process Orchestration

name: 02000002 Traffic Is Limited During Ticket Creation
title: 02000002 Traffic Is Limited During Ticket Creation
text:
02000002 Traffic Is Limited During Ticket Creation
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An error is reported on the ticket creation page in the runtime-state environment or when the develop-state system calls an API to create a ticket. The error code is 02000002.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    The number of ticket creation requests per second on a single node exceeds the upper limit.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal as the admin user.

     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

     Choose Products and Services > Administration > System Settings.

     Enter create_rate_limit in the search box and click the search icon.
      

      
       If the configuration shown in the following figure exists, click Edit in the Operation column and configure the parameters by referring to Table 1.

       If the configuration shown in the following figure does not exist, click Create and configure traffic limit parameters by referring to Table 1.
        

        

        
         
         
          
           Table 1 BPM traffic limit parameters
          
          
           
           
           
           
           
          
          
           
            
             Category

            
             Parameter

            
             Encrypted

            
             Default Value

            
             Description

           

          
          
           
            
             adc-bpm

            
             api_order_create_rate_limit

            
             No

            
             20

            
             Traffic limit parameter for creating tickets for an automated process.

             Value range: [1,100]

             If the value is out of the range, the default value is used. A maximum of 20 concurrent ticket creation requests can be sent per second.

             
               NOTICE: 
              
               
                When the adc-bpm service stack deployed in the x86-based system with dual-core CPU and 2 GB memory is used, you are advised to set this parameter to 20. If you want to set this parameter to the maximum value, the system specifications must be greater than 10-core CPU and 10 GB memory.

                In lightweight scenarios, only 30% of the traffic control configuration takes effect and the value is rounded up. For example, if this parameter is set to 15, the value 5 takes effect.

               

              

             

           

           
            
             bus_order_create_rate_limit

            
             No

            
             10

            
             Traffic limit parameter for creating tickets for a non-automated process.

             Value range: [1,50]

             If the value is out of the range, the default value is used. A maximum of 10 concurrent ticket creation requests can be sent per second.

             
               NOTICE: 
              
               
                When the adc-bpm service stack deployed in the x86-based system with dual-core CPU and 2 GB memory is used, you are advised to set this parameter to 10. If you want to set this parameter to the maximum value, the system specifications must be greater than 10-core CPU and 10 GB memory.

                In lightweight scenarios, only 30% of the traffic control configuration takes effect and the value is rounded up. For example, if this parameter is set to 15, the value 5 takes effect.

               

              

             

           

          
         
        

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Process Orchestration

name: 04400002 System Users Cannot Call APIs
title: 04400002 System Users Cannot Call APIs
text:
04400002 System Users Cannot Call APIs
 
 
  
  

  
   
    Error Description

    An error is reported when system users call the BPM microservice APIs. The error code is 04400002.

   

   
    Possible Causes

    System users cannot call APIs.

   

   
    Solution

    
     Log in to the GDE data zone portal.

     When the portal is displayed in shortcut mode, choose Common Management, and click GDE Common Configuration. 

     Choose Products and Services > API Catalog.

     Open the APIs under Bpm.
      

      

      

      

     Search for the API mentioned in the error information under Bpm.
      

      
       If the API is displayed under Bpm, the API cannot be called by system users. In this case, use another user to call the API.

       If the API is not displayed under Bpm, contact Huawei technical support to locate, analyze, and rectify the fault.

      

      

    

   

  

  
   
    
     Parent topic: Process Orchestration
